# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared (expose localhost to the **public** internet).
- **Tailscale** — WireGuard mesh VPN (tailnet-only, the opposite of the tunnel tools). Helper CLI: `tsnet`. Picker: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`, `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`.
- **Agent sounds** — audio notifications on agent Stop/Notification hooks. See `docs/tools/agent-sounds.md`.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
- **`agent-warmup`** — Tyro CLI that drives a real interactive Claude TUI at a scheduled time through an existing Herdr session (preferred) or tmux, with uv-first daemon bootstrap and safe fallback. See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
- **`raid-perm-check`** — read-only auditor for a group+ACL-shared data mount (`summary`/`orphans`/`groups`/`units`/`user`/`all`, default `/mnt/raid`). Catches the two silent breakages: orphaned uid/gid after an account is deleted, and a stale `systemd --user` manager whose frozen groups make timers hit EACCES on paths your shell reads fine. Never modifies — prints the fix. See `docs/sysadmin/shared-storage-permissions.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`ytmv`** — download YouTube music videos for **old MP3 players**: mp3 + sidecar `.lrc` + ID3v2.3/USLT lyrics, or mp4 with soft/burned-in subtitles. Subcommands `get` / `lyrics` / `tag` / `doctor`; `ytmv help` is the complete setup/cookie-safety guide and `doctor --cookies` explicitly tests a configured source. Public downloads use packaged EJS + managed Node 22+ cookie-free first (doctor flags legacy Node 20/16). Compatibility profiles (`safe`, `cjk-big5`, `cjk-gbk`, `ipod`, `modern`) are re-appliable offline via `ytmv tag`. Needs ffmpeg (`installMediaTools`); `--burn-subs` needs the keg-only `ffmpeg-full`. No `tv` channel by design. See `docs/tools/ytmv.md`.
- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
- **`herdr-grep`** — search visible or retained content across panes in the current, one named, or all running local Herdr sessions; reports exact session/workspace/tab/pane coordinates, supports `--json`, and `--pick` pipes matches to fzf then exact-focuses/attaches the selection. Inside Herdr, `prefix+Alt+F` opens a visible-content picker (Alt+S = scrollback, Alt+V = visible). Remote use runs the CLI through SSH. See `docs/tools/herdr.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, binary-matched global skill from `herdr --skill`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with three metadata pickers (`tv herdr-agent-panes`, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`) plus `herdr-grep` for pane-content search. See `docs/tools/herdr.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~50 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `tailnet`, `ssh-config`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`,
`kill-process`, `services`, `sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`,
`mac-apps`/`linux-apps`, the agent trio (`agent-panes`, `agent-sessions`,
`agent-wakeup`, dual tmux/Herdr with stable agent-session scheduling) and the `herdr-*` family. Full reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` opens the action menu. There is **no `prefix + e`** —
  that alias was removed, and `prefix + E` is "break every pane into its own
  window", so do not guess it. `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools.
  Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).


ARGUMENTS: Read-only, very thorough exploration. Locate dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl and related translate CLI tap trust, package installation, shell completion, default dev tool lists, bootstrap/apply scripts, and docs. Determine where the current dev-cli repository's actual binary/repo name should be added. Do not edit.

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	}
32	
33	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
34	func (a *App) Load() error {
35		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
36		if err != nil {
37			return err
38		}
39		a.Cfg = cfg
40		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
41		if a.Out == nil {
42			a.Out = os.Stdout
43		}
44		if a.Err == nil {
45			a.Err = os.Stderr
46		}
47		return nil
48	}
49	
50	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
51	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
52	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
53		if a.noRuntime {
54			return runtime.None{}
55		}
56		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
57		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
58			backend = a.runtimeOverride
59		}
60		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
61		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
62			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
63		}
64		return rt
65	}
66	
67	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
68	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
69		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
70	}
71	
72	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
73	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
74		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
75	}
76	
77	// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
78	// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
79	// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
80	// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
81	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
82		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
83	}
84	
85	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
86	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }

18	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
19	
20	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
21	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
22	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
23	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
24	
25	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
26	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
27	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`

29	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
30	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
31		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
32	}
33	
34	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
35	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
36	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
37	// descriptors.
38	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
39		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
40	
41		root := &cobra.Command{
42			Use:           "dev",
43			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
44			Long:          rootLong,
45			Version:       Version,
46			SilenceUsage:  true,
47			SilenceErrors: true,
48			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
49			// exists to answer.
50			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
51				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
52					out, err := skill.Render()
53					if err != nil {
54						return err
55					}
56					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
57					return nil
58				}
59				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
60				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
61				if interactive() {
62					return runTUI(app)
63				}
64				return runList(app, listOptions{})
65			},
66			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
67				return app.Load()
68			},
69		}

112	func Execute() int {

10	// zshInit and friends define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to leave
11	// the user *inside* the checkout.
12	//
13	// A process can never change its parent's working directory, so dev prints a
14	// `cd <path>` directive on stdout and the wrapper evaluates it. This is the
15	// same mechanism try-cli uses, and it is why `dev` is a shell function rather
16	// than only a binary.
17	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
18	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
19	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
20	dev() {
21	  local __dev_out __dev_status
22	  __dev_out="$(command %[1]s "$@")"
23	  __dev_status=$?
24	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ "${__dev_out#cd }" != "$__dev_out" ]; then
25	    eval "$__dev_out"
26	  elif [ -n "$__dev_out" ]; then
27	    printf '%%s\n' "$__dev_out"
28	  fi
29	  return $__dev_status
30	}
31	`

34	#   dev shell-init fish | source
35	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
36	function dev
37	    set -l __dev_out (command %[1]s $argv)
38	    set -l __dev_status $status
39	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and string match -q 'cd *' -- "$__dev_out"
40	        eval $__dev_out
41	    else if test -n "$__dev_out"
42	        printf '%%s\n' $__dev_out
43	    end
44	    return $__dev_status
45	end
46	`

55	"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
56	directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
57	working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.
58	
59	Add to your shell rc file:
60	
61	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
62	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,

50	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
51	
52	The `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism spans **6 surfaces that must move together** — devtools install, `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml`, `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`, `dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl` hooks, `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` (+ its `modify_package.json`), and `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`'s producers API. Exact contents: [workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md) § Status icon mechanics; why it leaks: [workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md).
53	
54	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (writes parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears). The workmux hook entries are **unconditional** — the `agentSounds` prompt gates only the notify.sh / peon-ping entries in the same file. `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux) stay distinct tools.

58	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` agent skill (restored on every `chezmoi apply`; see [agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md)). **Load the skill** for the template and disambiguation table.

66	
67	## Chezmoi templating conventions
68	
69	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask whether the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` (`darwin`/`linux`) / `.chezmoi.arch` (`arm64`/`amd64`) / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for **user-role choices only**, and its values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts. `.profile` is still the right knob for desktop-vs-headless.
70	
71	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
72	
73	Predicate table, examples, the `macos_intel` migration: [chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
74	
75	## Hard repo invariants
76	
77	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
78	
79	YAML / TOML / JSON syntax and template rendering are not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (`codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is only a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
80	
81	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
82	
83	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
84	
85	**Hard rules**:
86	
87	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
88	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
89	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
90	
91	The ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be last before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions`/`syntax-highlighting`/`history-substring-search` MUST be excluded (double-init flicker). [bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
92	
93	### Three-tier user-local override layer
94	
95	User overrides live in **six** untracked files, all in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). Default target: shared; drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
96	
97	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl` — `managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc`. Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
98	
99	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
100	
101	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
102	
103	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templates + 2 first-seed files: [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
104	
105	**Hard rules**:
106	
107	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
108	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/`, `dot_config/opencode/`, `dot_cursor/`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
109	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
110	- The `minimal` bundle forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without an explicit request.
111	- New vim-touched file → follow the gate-it-or-not flow in [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md) → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table there.
112	
113	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
114	
115	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
116	
117	**Hard rules**:
118	
119	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
120	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
121	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a *single* tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it genuinely needs a newer one (`python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5`). It MUST detect the install style and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (silent no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors when it isn't a formula). The dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and the role. See [uv-bootstrap](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
122	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`, or the install guard short-circuits and entry-point shims are never written (silently missing `jupyter` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit command: [uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
123	- New upgrade category: [upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) § Adding a new category. Tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise → do nothing, generic `upgrade` picks it up.
124	- **Probe `brew` by output, never exit status** — `[[ -n "$(brew --prefix 2>/dev/null)" ]]`. A stub `brew` passes `command -v brew` and returns 0 with empty output for *every* subcommand: `brew bundle` silently installs nothing and `community.general.homebrew` dies on `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`. [ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md](pitfalls/ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md)
125	
126	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
127	
128	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
129	
130	**Hard rules**:
131	
132	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
133	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
134	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
135	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
136	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
137	
138	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**: `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top → set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag → `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"` and branch on its return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason` → run privileged commands via `sudo_run …` (or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible).
139	
140	For **non-interactive** injection (`scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH), `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (0600) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty` — **never** read that variable directly, always go through the helper. Full API + state + cleanup model: [sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
141	
142	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
143	
144	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
145	
146	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked; hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let the template win.
147	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (`chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`), so ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for those.
148	- **`--branch BRANCH` is a no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS your editor working tree): they warn and run against the working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
149	- **Install-only by design.** `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
150	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
151	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint; anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without an explicit request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
152	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse. `just fleet-status` is the **pre-flight readiness probe** (13 states; always exits 0 — use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates; `fleet-status-quick` skips the remote `git fetch`). `just fleet-apply-status` is a **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`, run during/after, pairing with `fleet-apply-tail`/`-watch`/`-kill`. State meanings incl. `toml-mismatch`: [fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md).
153	- **`fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving** (auto-seed / exit 0 with a hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
154	
155	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
156	
157	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes the current target contents to stdin and expects the new contents on stdout. Used wherever a *foreign writer* also owns part of the file — `~/.claude/settings.json`, editor `settings.json`, the agent CLI configs, `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`, `~/.gitconfig` (preserves the `[credential]` blocks `gh auth setup-git` injects). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it overwrites the script with the live file.
158	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches the contents after (`~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json`, editor `keybindings.json`). Refresh the baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"` — `chezmoi add` strips the prefix and `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
159	
160	Per-file case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). The three agent CLI overlays, incl. the Claude hook merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland) without ping-ponging: [agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
161	
162	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
163	
164	The popup menu (`prefix + Space` / `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two tmux quirks force that: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) instead of clamped — the `devtools` role auto-upgrades Debian/Ubuntu past it — and `display-menu` does **not** paginate, so a menu taller than the terminal is suppressed entirely, with no error anywhere.
165	
166	**Hard rules**:
167	
168	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
169	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
170	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
171	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
172	
173	Full story incl. the red herrings: `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`, `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
174	
175	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
176	
177	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
178	
179	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps. **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
180	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
181	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
182	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
183	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
184	
185	Full breakdown / themes / keybindings / troubleshooting: [](docs/tools/tmux/).
186	
187	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
188	
189	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` sets `default_mode "locked"` on purpose — all keys pass through to inner apps, `Ctrl+G` unlocks Zellij's own. Do **not** change it. Fresh box → pick the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" preset. [keyboard-shortcuts.md](docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)
190

```text
1	# dev
2	
3	A thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
4	
5	It exists to stop four things collapsing into one:
6	
7	```
8	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
9	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
10	herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
11	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
12	```
13	
14	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
15	only what git cannot answer — a task's **state**, **owner** and **next
16	action** — as one TOML file per task.
17	
18	## The problem
19	
20	When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
21	working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
22	So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
23	defeats the point of having one.
24	
25	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
26	the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
27	
28	Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
29	the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
30	expected.
31	
32	```
33	$ dev ls
34	   TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
35	🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
36	🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
37	❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
38	```
39	
40	## Install
41	
42	```bash
43	make install     # builds, installs to ~/.local/bin, installs the agent skill
44	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
45	```
46	
47	Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
48	
49	```bash
50	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
51	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
52	```
53	
54	The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
55	working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
56	directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
57	
58	```bash
59	dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
60	```
61	
62	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
63	degrade cleanly when absent.
64	
65	## The lifecycle
66	
67	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
70	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
71	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
72	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
73	
74	```bash
75	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
76	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
77	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
78	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
79	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
80	dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
81	```
82	
83	### A task does not have to mean a worktree
84	
85	Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
86	
87	```bash
88	# No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
89	dev repo open api
90	
91	# Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
92	dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct
93	
94	# Use a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout, but no linked worktree.
95	dev start api --task "small feature" --branch-only --base main
96	
97	# Default: independent branch + worktree, provisioned and runtime-opened.
98	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
99	```
100	
101	Direct work can be parked WARM and resumed, but cannot go COLD because the
102	canonical checkout cannot be removed. `dev done` on a clean direct task needs
103	no `--ff` or `--pr`: the work is already on its destination branch.
104	
105	Start direct for one change stream, then create a normal worktree task later
106	when real parallelism appears. A new worktree starts from committed HEAD; dirty
107	main changes are deliberately not smuggled into it, so checkpoint first when
108	the parallel task depends on them.
109	
110	### The dashboard
111	
112	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens three lists, switched with `tab`:
113	
114	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
115	- **REPOS** — every repository under the scan roots, with its branch, dirty
116	  state, worktree count and per-state task tally, sorted so anything in flight
117	  is at the top. What do I have here.
118	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through the authenticated `gh` and `glab`
119	  CLIs, marked when a local clone exists. What can I open or clone.
120	
121	TASKS and REPOS come from the same code paths as `dev ls` and `dev repo list`,
122	so they cannot disagree. The repo list matters on day one: with forty repositories and
123	no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just be empty.
124	
125	Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
126	
127	```
128	j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
129	g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
130	/          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
131	```
132	
133	`enter` opens the selected row in the runtime. In TASKS, `p` parks and prompts
134	for the next action and `c` edits it. In REPOS, `enter` is pure ad-hoc open,
135	`s` starts an isolated worktree task, and `d` starts a tracked direct task on
136	the current branch. That makes the branch/worktree cost an explicit choice,
137	not something every task silently pays.
138	
139	**External tools are configured, not fixed.** They run through your shell in
140	the selected row's checkout; the dashboard suspends and redraws when they exit:
141	
142	```toml
143	[[tui.tools]]
144	key  = "L"
145	name = "lazygit"
146	run  = "lazygit"
147	
148	[[tui.tools]]
149	key  = "V"
150	name = "nvim"
151	run  = "nvim ."
152	
153	[[tui.tools]]
154	key  = "B"
155	name = "vibe"
156	run  = "vibe"
157	interactive = true     # load + evaluate aliases/functions after shell rc
158	
159	[[tui.tools]]
160	key  = "P"
161	name = "plans here"
162	run  = "claude-plans-here"
163	interactive = true
164	```
165	
166	`dev config init` writes the defaults out in full rather than leaving them
167	implicit, and `dev tui tools` shows what is bound here and whether each one is
168	actually installed — bindings for missing programs are not offered. A tool
169	cannot take a key the dashboard already uses; dev reports the clash on load.
170	
171	REMOTE loads lazily, so dashboard startup never waits on the network. A private
172	15-minute XDG cache makes later switches instant; `r` refreshes both forges.
173	`/` searches provider, owner/name and description; enter opens a local clone,
174	and `c` confirms before cloning an absent repo into `project_root`. The same
175	inventory is available without the full-screen UI via `dev repo remote [query]`;
176	`--cached` is its instant/offline form.
177	REPOS has an explicit LIVE column (`herdr:working`, `herdr:idle`, …); its
178	detail pane includes the workspace handle. `H` opens the selected repo's
179	one-year activity heatmap and `e` edits config. Returning from the editor, or
180	pressing `r`, reparses config and reloads data/tool bindings without restarting
181	the TUI; a runtime-backend change is reported as requiring restart.
182	
183	REPOS includes `LATEST`, defined as the newest dirty-file mtime, commit time, or
184	task update. Columns and default ordering are config:
185	
186	```toml
187	[tui.repos]
188	columns = ["repo", "branch", "git", "live", "latest", "worktrees", "tasks"]
189	sort = "activity"       # activity | latest | name | git | tasks
190	reverse = false
191	```
192	
193	In REPOS, `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses it. The configured order returns on
194	reload. Local repo probes run with bounded parallelism, and the alternate screen
195	appears before they finish; the measured serial 56-repo path was ~4.2s, while
196	startup now immediately shows loading and fills rows in the background.
197	
198	See `dev help tui` for the full key map.
199	
200	Going cold is safe because **the branch is the identity and the directory is a
201	cache**. `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, and `dev resume`
202	rebuilds the checkout from `origin/<branch>`. Once that holds, the local
203	filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished worktrees.
204	
205	## Rich Git state
206	
207	Every inventory surface uses the same compact, starship-like status:
208	
209	```text
210	⇕⇡3⇣2 =1 +4 !2 ?3
211	```
212	
213	- `⇡` / `⇣` / `⇕` — ahead, behind, diverged
214	- `=` — conflicted paths
215	- `+` — staged paths
216	- `!` — unstaged paths
217	- `?` — untracked paths
218	
219	`dev status` and the TUI detail pane also show the unique changed-path total
220	and type breakdown (added / modified / deleted / renamed). A path staged and
221	then modified again is one changed path, while correctly appearing in both the
222	staged and unstaged categories. JSON output exposes all counts separately.
223	
224	## Worktree ownership
225	
226	Three mechanisms create git worktrees. `dev` takes one position so nobody has
227	to improvise:
228	
229	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
230	|---|---|---|---|
231	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until `dev done` / `dev sweep` |
232	| Turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | dies with the turn |
233	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add`, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
234	
235	**Might you come back tomorrow → `dev`. Dies with this agent turn → Claude
236	Code native.**
237	
238	`dev` does not delegate placement to herdr because the path policy has to hold
239	on machines without herdr. It creates the checkout with plain git and asks
240	herdr only to *open* it — which still surfaces it in the sidebar grouped under
241	its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
242	
243	`dev` refuses to create a worktree inside a repository: a checkout nested in
244	another checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second
245	copy of the tree.
246	
247	### Provisioning
248	
249	A worktree is a clean checkout — no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`.
250	Without provisioning, every new one starts broken. `dev` copies the gitignored
251	files you list, optionally symlinks heavy directories, and runs a setup
252	command detected from the lockfiles:
253	
254	```toml
255	[worktree]
256	include     = [".env", ".env.local"]   # only files that are ALSO gitignored
257	link        = []                       # opt-in; sharing node_modules is risky
258	post_create = "auto"                   # uv.lock → uv sync, package-lock.json → npm ci, …
259	```
260	
261	**Copy or reinstall?** Reinstalling is always correct but can take minutes;
262	copying is fast but only sound for dependency trees carrying no absolute paths.
263	That is a per-ecosystem fact, not a preference, so dev knows it:
264	
265	```toml
266	[worktree]
267	strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip
268	
269	[worktree.strategies]
270	node = "copy"               # node_modules copies soundly
271	```
272	
273	Asking to copy a virtualenv is refused with the reason — it bakes its own
274	absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg` and `bin/activate` — and narrowed back to
275	reinstalling rather than silently producing a broken checkout.
276	
277	`dev wt plan` shows exactly what a new worktree of a repository would get:
278	which project types were detected, which tools are missing, and every file and
279	command involved. `dev wt plan --write` seeds a `<repo>/.dev.toml` from it, so
280	a project can commit its own setup and every machine provisions the same way.
281	
282	```
283	$ dev wt plan
284	PROJECT  MANAGER  FROM               DEPENDENCIES  TOOL
285	node     npm      package-lock.json  node_modules  installed
286	python   uv       uv.lock            .venv         installed
287	
288	   ACTION    WHAT          WHY
289	✓  copy      .env          gitignored, so the checkout would not have it
290	✓  copy-dir  node_modules  npm dependencies, copied instead of reinstalling
291	✓  run       uv sync       uv.lock detected
292	```
293	
294	## Other things it does
295	
296	```bash
297	dev repo list                  # every repo under the scan roots, with status
298	dev repo clone owner/name -c Web   # clone into the right place, via gh or glab
299	dev repo sync --all            # fetch + prune, and report what moved
300	
301	dev try redis-streams          # dated scratch directory for an experiment
302	dev graduate redis-streams -c Infra --remote   # promote it into a real project
303	
304	dev gitignore                  # .gitignore from GitHub's templates + the rest
305	dev adopt                      # import existing worktrees/sessions as tasks
306	
307	dev stats --heatmap            # where the time actually went
308	dev help worktrees             # quick-reference pages for the workflow
309	```
310	
311	`dev stats` draws a contribution-style heatmap from two sources: a sampler
312	watching live agent sessions (the only way to count time spent reading and
313	debugging), and git history (which backfills the past and survives losing the
314	database). WakaTime can be imported alongside for editor time.
315	
316	```bash
317	dev stats backfill                          # seed all repos from git history
318	dev stats backfill --repo api               # seed only one repo
319	dev stats sample --interval 5m              # from cron, every five minutes
320	dev stats import-wakatime                   # optional
321	dev stats path                              # durable SQLite location
322	dev stats clear --repo api                  # guarded selective deletion
323	```
324	
325	In the TUI, select a repo and press `H`. If it has no data, `b` backfills only
326	that repo and refreshes the panel; `r` merely rereads existing stats data.
327	
328	Stats are **data**, not cache: session samples and WakaTime imports may not be
329	reconstructible. They live at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and clearing them
330	requires a scope plus confirmation (`--repo`, `--source`, or `--all`).
331	Regenerable data lives separately:
332	
333	```bash
334	dev cache list
335	dev cache path
336	dev cache clear remote
337	dev cache clear gitignore
338	dev cache clear all
339	```
340	
341	Those remove only `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/{remotes.json,gitignore/}` and never touch
342	`stats.db`.
343	
344	## Bootstrapping an existing machine
345	
346	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use: `dev` discovers repositories
347	wherever `scan_roots` point and never requires a particular physical layout.
348	When you want a recursive audit or a curated navigation layer, bootstrap is the
349	explicit path:
350	
351	```bash
352	dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work                    # recursive report, no changes
353	dev bootstrap ~/code --json                       # machine-readable inventory
354	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects           # plan a flat symlink catalog
355	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --apply   # create only the ready links
356	dev bootstrap ~/old --move ~/Projects             # plan physical moves
357	```
358	
359	The scanner classifies canonical checkouts, linked worktrees, bare repositories
360	and symlink aliases, deduplicating by Git common-directory identity rather than
361	path.
362	
363	**A symlink index is the default recommendation.** It gives a flat,
364	metadata-aware navigation root while every physical repository stays exactly
365	where it was. Put the index first in `scan_roots` and that alias becomes the UI;
366	normal discovery follows direct repo symlinks and deduplicates index + physical
367	paths.
368	
369	Physical move exists, but refuses dirty repos, linked worktrees anywhere in the
370	clone, live sessions, a current shell inside, aliases that would break,
371	occupied destinations and cross-filesystem renames. A plan with any blocked row
372	moves nothing. `--config-out` writes a fresh config for the resulting root
373	without silently rewriting the user's current one. See `dev help bootstrap`.
374	
375	## Adopting work in flight
376	
377	There is nothing to migrate. `dev` discovers repositories wherever your scan
378	roots point and **never moves, renames or deletes anything** you already have.
379	`dev config init` probes the conventional locations — `~/Documents/Program`,
380	`~/src`, `~/code`, a `GHQ_ROOT`, and so on — counts the repositories in each,
381	and writes only the ones that exist:
382	
383	```
384	$ dev config init
385	wrote ~/.config/dev/config.toml
386	
387	Detected:
388	ROOT                 REPOS  ROLE
389	~/Documents/Program  40     scan root, new projects land here
390	~/src                16     scan root
391	```
392	
393	Repositories are discovered; *tasks* are not. `dev adopt` finds the work
394	already in flight — linked worktrees from any tool, live runtime sessions, and
395	local branches ahead of the default branch — and offers to record it. It skips
396	branches already merged, and the turn-scoped worktrees an agent harness cleans
397	up itself:
398	
399	```bash
400	dev adopt            # report only
401	dev adopt --apply    # record as tasks; nothing on disk changes
402	```
403	
404	A worktree you already have somewhere else keeps working exactly as it did —
405	`dev` records the path git reports rather than relocating it. Full detail in
406	`dev help adopting`.
407	
408	## .gitignore
409	
410	```bash
411	dev gitignore                 # detect the languages from the repo's files
412	dev gitignore python node     # or say so explicitly
413	dev gitignore --offline       # cached and bundled templates only
414	```
415	
416	Language sections come from [GitHub's templates](https://github.com/github/gitignore),
417	fetched once and cached. On top of those it adds what no language template
418	covers: the host platform's junk files, editor state, local env files, and the
419	directories coding-agent harnesses create — an agent's linked worktree left
420	untracked makes every `git status` in the main checkout unreadable.
421	
422	Everything it writes goes inside a delimited block, so re-running updates that
423	block and leaves rules you added by hand alone.
424	
425	## Configuration
426	
427	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml`. Write a commented starter with
428	`dev config init`; see the effective settings with `dev config show`; open the
429	actual file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` with either form:
430	
431	```bash
432	dev edit
433	dev config edit
434	DEV_EDITOR=unused dev edit --editor "code --wait"   # explicit override
435	```
436	
437	If the file does not exist, `edit` generates the machine-detected starter first
438	rather than opening an empty file. Resolution is `--editor` → `$VISUAL` →
439	`$EDITOR` → `nvim` → `vim` → `vi`.
440	
441	Every path is configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine —
442	a faster volume, a different naming convention:
443	
444	```toml
445	[paths]
446	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries"]
447	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
448	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
449	state_dir     = "~/.local/share/dev"        # point at a git repo to sync it
450	```
451	
452	Template variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`,
453	`host`, `date`. Filters: `|slug` (`feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`), `|lower`,
454	`|base`. A typo in a variable name fails at load, not as a directory literally
455	named `{{rep}}`.
456	
457	A flat project layout is already first-class — it needs no migration and no
458	special mode:
459	
460	```toml
461	[paths]
462	scan_roots   = ["~/code"]
463	project_root = "~/code"       # repo new/clone/graduate land at ~/code/<repo>
464	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/wt"
465	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}--{{branch|slug}}"
466	```
467	
468	Omit `--category` and canonical repos stay flat. Categories are metadata the
469	user may choose, never a directory structure dev imposes.
470	
471	## Multiple machines
472	
473	Do not sync worktrees or runtime state. Sync branches, and let the remote be
474	the handoff boundary:
475	
476	```bash
477	dev park --cold --push      # on the machine holding the work
478	dev resume <task> --fetch   # on the machine picking it up
479	```
480	
481	`dev` records an owner host per task and refuses to resume someone else's
482	without `--force`. Two machines committing to one branch is the reliable way
483	to produce a conflict here; the ownership check prevents it.
484	
485	For a cross-machine view, `dev ls --json` is a stable contract:
486	
487	```bash
488	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="hot")'
489	```
490	
491	## The agent skill
492	
493	`dev` ships the agent skill that documents it, embedded in the binary — the
494	same pattern `herdr --skill` uses. A skill vendored separately drifts from the
495	tool it describes, and an agent reading a stale command list is worse than one
496	reading none.
497	
498	```bash
499	dev skill install    # → ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills
500	dev --skill          # print it, for a dotfiles installer to sync
501	dev skill sync       # regenerate the command reference from the command tree
502	dev skill sync --check   # fail if it has drifted — wire into CI
503	```
504	
505	The skill defers to the companion `git-workflow` skill for commit conventions,
506	SemVer and branch naming rather than restating them. It owns what is new: the
507	worktree ownership rule, the task lifecycle, and how `dev` and herdr divide
508	responsibility.
509	
510	## Development
511	
512	```bash
513	make          # fmt, vet, test, build
514	make test
515	make e2e      # drives the real binary through a full lifecycle in a sandbox
516	make skill-check
517	```
518	
519	Tests build throwaway repositories under `t.TempDir()` via
520	`internal/gitx/gittest`, and the runtime adapters share one contract suite that
521	skips backends not installed on the machine — so the suite is meaningful in CI
522	(where only the null backend exists) and locally (where herdr and tmux do).
523
```

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	}
32	
33	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
34	func (a *App) Load() error {
35		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
36		if err != nil {
37			return err
38		}
39		a.Cfg = cfg
40		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
41		if a.Out == nil {
42			a.Out = os.Stdout
43		}
44		if a.Err == nil {
45			a.Err = os.Stderr
46		}
47		return nil
48	}
49	
50	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
51	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
52	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
53		if a.noRuntime {
54			return runtime.None{}
55		}
56		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
57		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
58			backend = a.runtimeOverride
59		}
60		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
61		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
62			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
63		}
64		return rt
65	}
66	
67	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
68	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
69		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
70	}
71	
72	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
73	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
74		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
75	}
76	
77	// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
78	// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
79	// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
80	// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
81	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
82		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
83	}
84	
85	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
86	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
87

1	# TODO
2	
3	Priority `P1` (next) … `P4` (someday); effort `S` / `M` / `L`.
4	
5	## Active
6	
7	### P2 · M — Incremental local repo snapshot
8	The TUI now renders immediately and probes repositories in the background with
9	bounded concurrency, reducing perceived startup latency. A 56-repo refresh
10	still takes roughly three seconds because status + latest commit remain live Git
11	queries. If inventories grow into the hundreds, persist a short-lived snapshot
12	and stream changed rows into the model; keep `r` as the explicit live refresh.
13	
14	### P2 · M — Multi-host aggregation
15	`dev ls --all` fanning out over ssh to the machines in a configured host list,
16	merging their `dev ls --json`. The JSON contract is already stable and the
17	`owner` field already identifies which machine holds a task, so this is
18	plumbing rather than design. Today the same thing works by hand:
19	
20	```bash
21	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="hot")'
22	```
23	
24	### P3 · S — Television / fzf channel
25	A `tv` channel over `dev ls --json` for fuzzy-picking a task, and an `fzf`
26	fallback. Navigation by metadata rather than by remembering a path is the point
27	of the tool; the TUI covers it, but a picker composes better with other tools.
28	
29	### P3 · S — `dev stats` per-repo heatmap
30	`--repo X` currently filters the totals and the combined grid. A dedicated
31	per-repo grid, several stacked, would answer "which project did I move to in
32	March" better than the aggregate does.
33	
34	### P4 · M — Raycast extension
35	`dev ls` and `dev resume` from the launcher. Wants the JSON contract and a
36	stable binary path; nothing else new.
37	
38	## Deliberately not doing
39	
40	### Installing dependencies
41	`dev doctor` reports what is missing and what degrades; it will not install
42	anything. This is the one place where being glue matters most: git, herdr,
43	tmux, gh, glab, lazygit and yazi are all installed by a package manager the
44	user already has opinions about (brew, apt, mise, nix, chezmoi), and a tool
45	that shells out to one of them is guessing. `doctor` naming the missing binary
46	is enough — the user knows how they install things on that machine.
47	
48	Reconsider only if `doctor` grows a case where the *right* command is
49	unambiguous and the user has asked for it.
50	
51	### A second git database
52	Anything derivable from git is derived live, every run. The registry holds
53	state, owner, next action and a note — nothing else. The moment it caches a
54	branch name or an ahead/behind count, it can disagree with git, and a tool that
55	disagrees with git about git is worse than no tool.
56	
57	### Syncing runtime state between machines
58	Each host runs its own multiplexer. What crosses machines is branches, through
59	the remote, plus the task registry if `state_dir` is a git repo. Syncing
60	sessions would mean reconciling two live terminal states, which is a much
61	harder problem than the one this tool has.
62	
63	### Owning the worktree path on machines with herdr
64	`herdr worktree create` would be less code, but the path policy has to hold
65	where herdr is not installed. dev creates the checkout with git and asks herdr
66	only to open it. See `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/worktree-ownership.md`.
67	
68	## Done

70	- Task lifecycle: `start` / `park` / `resume` / `done` / `sweep`.
71	- Worktree ownership rule, path templates, provisioning, per-repo `.dev.toml`.
72	- Runtime adapters: herdr, tmux, none, behind one contract suite.
73	- Repo discovery and gh/glab-backed clone, create, sync.
74	- `try` and `graduate`.
75	- Activity stats: sampler, git backfill, WakaTime import, heatmap.
76	- Interactive TASKS / REPOS / REMOTE dashboard with vim navigation, lazy

78	- Explicit configurable TUI tools, including interactive shell aliases/functions,
