```text
1	# dev
2	
3	A thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
4	
5	It exists to stop four things collapsing into one:
6	
7	```
8	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
9	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
10	herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
11	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
12	```
13	
14	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
15	only what git cannot answer — a task's **state**, **owner** and **next
16	action** — as one TOML file per task.
17	
18	## The problem
19	
20	When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
21	working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
22	So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
23	defeats the point of having one.
24	
25	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
26	the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
27	
28	Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
29	the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
30	expected.
31	
32	```
33	$ dev ls
34	   TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
35	🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
36	🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
37	❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
38	```
39	
40	## Install
41	
42	```bash
43	make install     # builds, installs to ~/.local/bin, installs the agent skill
44	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
45	```
46	
47	Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
48	
49	```bash
50	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
51	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
52	```
53	
54	The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
55	working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
56	directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
57	
58	```bash
59	dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
60	```
61	
62	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
63	degrade cleanly when absent.
64	
65	## The lifecycle
66	
67	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
70	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
71	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
72	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
73	
74	```bash
75	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
76	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
77	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
78	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
79	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
80	dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
81	```
82	
83	### A task does not have to mean a worktree
84	
85	Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
86	
87	```bash
88	# No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
89	dev repo open api
90	
91	# Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
92	dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct
93	
94	# Use a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout, but no linked worktree.
95	dev start api --task "small feature" --branch-only --base main
96	
97	# Default: independent branch + worktree, provisioned and runtime-opened.
98	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
99	```
100	
101	Direct work can be parked WARM and resumed, but cannot go COLD because the
102	canonical checkout cannot be removed. `dev done` on a clean direct task needs
103	no `--ff` or `--pr`: the work is already on its destination branch.
104	
105	Start direct for one change stream, then create a normal worktree task later
106	when real parallelism appears. A new worktree starts from committed HEAD; dirty
107	main changes are deliberately not smuggled into it, so checkpoint first when
108	the parallel task depends on them.
109	
110	### The dashboard
111	
112	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens three lists, switched with `tab`:
113	
114	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
115	- **REPOS** — every repository under the scan roots, with its branch, dirty
116	  state, worktree count and per-state task tally, sorted so anything in flight
117	  is at the top. What do I have here.
118	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through the authenticated `gh` and `glab`
119	  CLIs, marked when a local clone exists. What can I open or clone.
120	
121	TASKS and REPOS come from the same code paths as `dev ls` and `dev repo list`,
122	so they cannot disagree. The repo list matters on day one: with forty repositories and
123	no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just be empty.
124	
125	Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
126	
127	```
128	j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
129	g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
130	/          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
131	```
132	
133	`enter` opens the selected row in the runtime. In TASKS, `p` parks and prompts
134	for the next action and `c` edits it. In REPOS, `enter` is pure ad-hoc open,
135	`s` starts an isolated worktree task, and `d` starts a tracked direct task on
136	the current branch. That makes the branch/worktree cost an explicit choice,
137	not something every task silently pays.
138	
139	**External tools are configured, not fixed.** They run through your shell in
140	the selected row's checkout; the dashboard suspends and redraws when they exit:
141	
142	```toml
143	[[tui.tools]]
144	key  = "L"
145	name = "lazygit"
146	run  = "lazygit"
147	
148	[[tui.tools]]
149	key  = "V"
150	name = "nvim"
151	run  = "nvim ."
152	
153	[[tui.tools]]
154	key  = "B"
155	name = "vibe"
156	run  = "vibe"
157	interactive = true     # load + evaluate aliases/functions after shell rc
158	
159	[[tui.tools]]
160	key  = "P"
161	name = "plans here"
162	run  = "claude-plans-here"
163	interactive = true
164	```
165	
166	`dev config init` writes the defaults out in full rather than leaving them
167	implicit, and `dev tui tools` shows what is bound here and whether each one is
168	actually installed — bindings for missing programs are not offered. A tool
169	cannot take a key the dashboard already uses; dev reports the clash on load.
170	
171	REMOTE loads lazily, so dashboard startup never waits on the network. A private
172	15-minute XDG cache makes later switches instant; `r` refreshes both forges.
173	`/` searches provider, owner/name and description; enter opens a local clone,
174	and `c` confirms before cloning an absent repo into `project_root`. The same
175	inventory is available without the full-screen UI via `dev repo remote [query]`;
176	`--cached` is its instant/offline form.
177	REPOS has an explicit LIVE column (`herdr:working`, `herdr:idle`, …); its
178	detail pane includes the workspace handle. `H` opens the selected repo's
179	one-year activity heatmap and `e` edits config. Returning from the editor, or
180	pressing `r`, reparses config and reloads data/tool bindings without restarting
181	the TUI; a runtime-backend change is reported as requiring restart.
182	
183	REPOS includes `LATEST`, defined as the newest dirty-file mtime, commit time, or
184	task update. Columns and default ordering are config:
185	
186	```toml
187	[tui.repos]
188	columns = ["repo", "branch", "git", "live", "latest", "worktrees", "tasks"]
189	sort = "activity"       # activity | latest | name | git | tasks
190	reverse = false
191	```
192	
193	In REPOS, `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses it. The configured order returns on
194	reload. Local repo probes run with bounded parallelism, and the alternate screen
195	appears before they finish; the measured serial 56-repo path was ~4.2s, while
196	startup now immediately shows loading and fills rows in the background.
197	
198	See `dev help tui` for the full key map.
199	
200	Going cold is safe because **the branch is the identity and the directory is a
201	cache**. `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, and `dev resume`
202	rebuilds the checkout from `origin/<branch>`. Once that holds, the local
203	filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished worktrees.
204	
205	## Rich Git state
206	
207	Every inventory surface uses the same compact, starship-like status:
208	
209	```text
210	⇕⇡3⇣2 =1 +4 !2 ?3
211	```
212	
213	- `⇡` / `⇣` / `⇕` — ahead, behind, diverged
214	- `=` — conflicted paths
215	- `+` — staged paths
216	- `!` — unstaged paths
217	- `?` — untracked paths
218	
219	`dev status` and the TUI detail pane also show the unique changed-path total
220	and type breakdown (added / modified / deleted / renamed). A path staged and
221	then modified again is one changed path, while correctly appearing in both the
222	staged and unstaged categories. JSON output exposes all counts separately.
223	
224	## Worktree ownership
225	
226	Three mechanisms create git worktrees. `dev` takes one position so nobody has
227	to improvise:
228	
229	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
230	|---|---|---|---|
231	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until `dev done` / `dev sweep` |
232	| Turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | dies with the turn |
233	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add`, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
234	
235	**Might you come back tomorrow → `dev`. Dies with this agent turn → Claude
236	Code native.**
237	
238	`dev` does not delegate placement to herdr because the path policy has to hold
239	on machines without herdr. It creates the checkout with plain git and asks
240	herdr only to *open* it — which still surfaces it in the sidebar grouped under
241	its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
242	
243	`dev` refuses to create a worktree inside a repository: a checkout nested in
244	another checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second
245	copy of the tree.
246	
247	### Provisioning
248	
249	A worktree is a clean checkout — no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`.
250	Without provisioning, every new one starts broken. `dev` copies the gitignored
251	files you list, optionally symlinks heavy directories, and runs a setup
252	command detected from the lockfiles:
253	
254	```toml
255	[worktree]
256	include     = [".env", ".env.local"]   # only files that are ALSO gitignored
257	link        = []                       # opt-in; sharing node_modules is risky
258	post_create = "auto"                   # uv.lock → uv sync, package-lock.json → npm ci, …
259	```
260	
261	**Copy or reinstall?** Reinstalling is always correct but can take minutes;
262	copying is fast but only sound for dependency trees carrying no absolute paths.
263	That is a per-ecosystem fact, not a preference, so dev knows it:
264	
265	```toml
266	[worktree]
267	strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip
268	
269	[worktree.strategies]
270	node = "copy"               # node_modules copies soundly
271	```
272	
273	Asking to copy a virtualenv is refused with the reason — it bakes its own
274	absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg` and `bin/activate` — and narrowed back to
275	reinstalling rather than silently producing a broken checkout.
276	
277	`dev wt plan` shows exactly what a new worktree of a repository would get:
278	which project types were detected, which tools are missing, and every file and
279	command involved. `dev wt plan --write` seeds a `<repo>/.dev.toml` from it, so
280	a project can commit its own setup and every machine provisions the same way.
281	
282	```
283	$ dev wt plan
284	PROJECT  MANAGER  FROM               DEPENDENCIES  TOOL
285	node     npm      package-lock.json  node_modules  installed
286	python   uv       uv.lock            .venv         installed
287	
288	   ACTION    WHAT          WHY
289	✓  copy      .env          gitignored, so the checkout would not have it
290	✓  copy-dir  node_modules  npm dependencies, copied instead of reinstalling
291	✓  run       uv sync       uv.lock detected
292	```
293	
294	## Other things it does
295	
296	```bash
297	dev repo list                  # every repo under the scan roots, with status
298	dev repo clone owner/name -c Web   # clone into the right place, via gh or glab
299	dev repo sync --all            # fetch + prune, and report what moved
300	
301	dev try redis-streams          # dated scratch directory for an experiment
302	dev graduate redis-streams -c Infra --remote   # promote it into a real project
303	
304	dev gitignore                  # .gitignore from GitHub's templates + the rest
305	dev adopt                      # import existing worktrees/sessions as tasks
306	
307	dev stats --heatmap            # where the time actually went
308	dev help worktrees             # quick-reference pages for the workflow
309	```
310	
311	`dev stats` draws a contribution-style heatmap from two sources: a sampler
312	watching live agent sessions (the only way to count time spent reading and
313	debugging), and git history (which backfills the past and survives losing the
314	database). WakaTime can be imported alongside for editor time.
315	
316	```bash
317	dev stats backfill                          # seed all repos from git history
318	dev stats backfill --repo api               # seed only one repo
319	dev stats sample --interval 5m              # from cron, every five minutes
320	dev stats import-wakatime                   # optional
321	dev stats path                              # durable SQLite location
322	dev stats clear --repo api                  # guarded selective deletion
323	```
324	
325	In the TUI, select a repo and press `H`. If it has no data, `b` backfills only
326	that repo and refreshes the panel; `r` merely rereads existing stats data.
327	
328	Stats are **data**, not cache: session samples and WakaTime imports may not be
329	reconstructible. They live at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and clearing them
330	requires a scope plus confirmation (`--repo`, `--source`, or `--all`).
331	Regenerable data lives separately:
332	
333	```bash
334	dev cache list
335	dev cache path
336	dev cache clear remote
337	dev cache clear gitignore
338	dev cache clear all
339	```
340	
341	Those remove only `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/{remotes.json,gitignore/}` and never touch
342	`stats.db`.
343	
344	## Bootstrapping an existing machine
345	
346	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use: `dev` discovers repositories
347	wherever `scan_roots` point and never requires a particular physical layout.
348	When you want a recursive audit or a curated navigation layer, bootstrap is the
349	explicit path:
350	
351	```bash
352	dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work                    # recursive report, no changes
353	dev bootstrap ~/code --json                       # machine-readable inventory
354	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects           # plan a flat symlink catalog
355	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --apply   # create only the ready links
356	dev bootstrap ~/old --move ~/Projects             # plan physical moves
357	```
358	
359	The scanner classifies canonical checkouts, linked worktrees, bare repositories
360	and symlink aliases, deduplicating by Git common-directory identity rather than
361	path.
362	
363	**A symlink index is the default recommendation.** It gives a flat,
364	metadata-aware navigation root while every physical repository stays exactly
365	where it was. Put the index first in `scan_roots` and that alias becomes the UI;
366	normal discovery follows direct repo symlinks and deduplicates index + physical
367	paths.
368	
369	Physical move exists, but refuses dirty repos, linked worktrees anywhere in the
370	clone, live sessions, a current shell inside, aliases that would break,
371	occupied destinations and cross-filesystem renames. A plan with any blocked row
372	moves nothing. `--config-out` writes a fresh config for the resulting root
373	without silently rewriting the user's current one. See `dev help bootstrap`.
374	
375	## Adopting work in flight
376	
377	There is nothing to migrate. `dev` discovers repositories wherever your scan
378	roots point and **never moves, renames or deletes anything** you already have.
379	`dev config init` probes the conventional locations — `~/Documents/Program`,
380	`~/src`, `~/code`, a `GHQ_ROOT`, and so on — counts the repositories in each,
381	and writes only the ones that exist:
382	
383	```
384	$ dev config init
385	wrote ~/.config/dev/config.toml
386	
387	Detected:
388	ROOT                 REPOS  ROLE
389	~/Documents/Program  40     scan root, new projects land here
390	~/src                16     scan root
391	```
392	
393	Repositories are discovered; *tasks* are not. `dev adopt` finds the work
394	already in flight — linked worktrees from any tool, live runtime sessions, and
395	local branches ahead of the default branch — and offers to record it. It skips
396	branches already merged, and the turn-scoped worktrees an agent harness cleans
397	up itself:
398	
399	```bash
400	dev adopt            # report only
401	dev adopt --apply    # record as tasks; nothing on disk changes
402	```
403	
404	A worktree you already have somewhere else keeps working exactly as it did —
405	`dev` records the path git reports rather than relocating it. Full detail in
406	`dev help adopting`.
407	
408	## .gitignore
409	
410	```bash
411	dev gitignore                 # detect the languages from the repo's files
412	dev gitignore python node     # or say so explicitly
413	dev gitignore --offline       # cached and bundled templates only
414	```
415	
416	Language sections come from [GitHub's templates](https://github.com/github/gitignore),
417	fetched once and cached. On top of those it adds what no language template
418	covers: the host platform's junk files, editor state, local env files, and the
419	directories coding-agent harnesses create — an agent's linked worktree left
420	untracked makes every `git status` in the main checkout unreadable.
421	
422	Everything it writes goes inside a delimited block, so re-running updates that
423	block and leaves rules you added by hand alone.
424	
425	## Configuration
426	
427	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml`. Write a commented starter with
428	`dev config init`; see the effective settings with `dev config show`; open the
429	actual file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` with either form:
430	
431	```bash
432	dev edit
433	dev config edit
434	DEV_EDITOR=unused dev edit --editor "code --wait"   # explicit override
435	```
436	
437	If the file does not exist, `edit` generates the machine-detected starter first
438	rather than opening an empty file. Resolution is `--editor` → `$VISUAL` →
439	`$EDITOR` → `nvim` → `vim` → `vi`.
440	
441	Every path is configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine —
442	a faster volume, a different naming convention:
443	
444	```toml
445	[paths]
446	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries"]
447	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
448	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
449	state_dir     = "~/.local/share/dev"        # point at a git repo to sync it
450	```
451	
452	Template variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`,
453	`host`, `date`. Filters: `|slug` (`feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`), `|lower`,
454	`|base`. A typo in a variable name fails at load, not as a directory literally
455	named `{{rep}}`.
456	
457	A flat project layout is already first-class — it needs no migration and no
458	special mode:
459	
460	```toml
461	[paths]
462	scan_roots   = ["~/code"]
463	project_root = "~/code"       # repo new/clone/graduate land at ~/code/<repo>
464	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/wt"
465	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}--{{branch|slug}}"
466	```
467	
468	Omit `--category` and canonical repos stay flat. Categories are metadata the
469	user may choose, never a directory structure dev imposes.
470	
471	## Multiple machines
472	
473	Do not sync worktrees or runtime state. Sync branches, and let the remote be
474	the handoff boundary:
475	
476	```bash
477	dev park --cold --push      # on the machine holding the work
478	dev resume <task> --fetch   # on the machine picking it up
479	```
480	
481	`dev` records an owner host per task and refuses to resume someone else's
482	without `--force`. Two machines committing to one branch is the reliable way
483	to produce a conflict here; the ownership check prevents it.
484	
485	For a cross-machine view, `dev ls --json` is a stable contract:
486	
487	```bash
488	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="hot")'
489	```
490	
491	## The agent skill
492	
493	`dev` ships the agent skill that documents it, embedded in the binary — the
494	same pattern `herdr --skill` uses. A skill vendored separately drifts from the
495	tool it describes, and an agent reading a stale command list is worse than one
496	reading none.
497	
498	```bash
499	dev skill install    # → ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills
500	dev --skill          # print it, for a dotfiles installer to sync
501	dev skill sync       # regenerate the command reference from the command tree
502	dev skill sync --check   # fail if it has drifted — wire into CI
503	```
504	
505	The skill defers to the companion `git-workflow` skill for commit conventions,
506	SemVer and branch naming rather than restating them. It owns what is new: the
507	worktree ownership rule, the task lifecycle, and how `dev` and herdr divide
508	responsibility.
509	
510	## Development
511	
512	```bash
513	make          # fmt, vet, test, build
514	make test
515	make e2e      # drives the real binary through a full lifecycle in a sandbox
516	make skill-check
517	```
518	
519	Tests build throwaway repositories under `t.TempDir()` via
520	`internal/gitx/gittest`, and the runtime adapters share one contract suite that
521	skips backends not installed on the machine — so the suite is meaningful in CI
522	(where only the null backend exists) and locally (where herdr and tmux do).
523
```
</details></tool-use>

23	// harness runs dev commands against an isolated HOME, config and scan root.
24	type harness struct {
25		t          *testing.T
26		home       string
27		configPath string
28		scanRoot   string
29		wtRoot     string
30		repo       *gittest.Repo
31	}
32	
33	func newHarness(t *testing.T) *harness {
34		t.Helper()
35		home := t.TempDir()
36		scanRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Program")
37		wtRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Worktrees")
38		if err := os.MkdirAll(scanRoot, 0o755); err != nil {
39			t.Fatal(err)
40		}
41	
42		// A repo inside the scan root, so `dev` discovers it the way it would in
43		// real use rather than via an absolute path.
44		r := gittest.New(t)
45		dest := filepath.Join(scanRoot, "demo")
46		if err := os.Rename(r.Root, dest); err != nil {
47			t.Fatal(err)
48		}
49		r.Root = dest
50	
51		// Isolate every path dev touches from the developer's real machine.
52		t.Setenv("HOME", home)
53		t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".local", "share"))
54		t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".config"))
55		t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".cache"))
56	
57		configPath := filepath.Join(home, "config.toml")
58		cfg := "" +
59			"[paths]\n" +
60			"scan_roots = [\"" + scanRoot + "\"]\n" +
61			"project_root = \"" + scanRoot + "\"\n" +
62			"tries_root = \"" + filepath.Join(home, "tries") + "\"\n" +
63			"worktree_root = \"" + wtRoot + "\"\n" +
64			"state_dir = \"" + filepath.Join(home, "state") + "\"\n" +
65			"\n[runtime]\nbackend = \"none\"\n" +
66			"\n[worktree]\ninclude = [\".env\"]\npost_create = []\n"
67		if err := os.WriteFile(configPath, []byte(cfg), 0o644); err != nil {
68			t.Fatal(err)
69		}
70		return &harness{t: t, home: home, configPath: configPath, scanRoot: scanRoot, wtRoot: wtRoot, repo: r}
71	}
72	
73	// run executes one dev invocation, capturing its output. Commands write
74	// through App, so the writers passed to NewRootCommandWithIO are all that is
75	// needed — no file-descriptor juggling.
76	func (h *harness) run(args ...string) (string, string, error) {
77		h.t.Helper()
78		var out, errBuf bytes.Buffer
79		root := cli.NewRootCommandWithIO(&out, &errBuf)
80		root.SetArgs(append([]string{"--config", h.configPath}, args...))
81		err := root.Execute()
82		return out.String(), errBuf.String(), err
83	}
84	
85	func (h *harness) mustRun(args ...string) string {
86		h.t.Helper()
87		out, errOut, err := h.run(args...)
88		if err != nil {
89			h.t.Fatalf("dev %s: %v\nstderr: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), err, errOut)
90		}
91		return out
92	}

94	func TestLifecycleEndToEnd(t *testing.T) {
95		h := newHarness(t)
96	
97		// An empty inventory should tell the user how to start, not print nothing.
98		out := h.mustRun("ls")
99		if !strings.Contains(out, "No tasks yet") {
100			t.Errorf("empty ls output: %q", out)
101		}
102	
103		// start: branch + worktree + task entry.
104		out = h.mustRun("start", "demo", "--task", "auth", "--branch", "feat/auth", "--base", "main")
105		if !strings.Contains(out, "feat/auth") {
106			t.Fatalf("start output: %q", out)
107		}
108		wtPath := filepath.Join(h.wtRoot, "demo", "feat-auth")
109		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(wtPath, "README.md")); err != nil {
110			t.Fatalf("worktree should exist at the templated path: %v", err)
111		}
112	
113		// The task appears in the inventory as hot.
114		out = h.mustRun("ls")
115		if !strings.Contains(out, "auth") || !strings.Contains(out, "HOT") {
116			t.Errorf("ls after start: %q", out)
117		}
118	
119		// JSON is a stable contract for other tools.
120		out = h.mustRun("ls", "--json")
121		var rows []map[string]any
122		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(out), &rows); err != nil {
123			t.Fatalf("ls --json is not valid JSON: %v\n%s", err, out)
124		}
125		if len(rows) != 1 {
126			t.Fatalf("want 1 row, got %d", len(rows))
127		}
128		if rows[0]["branch"] != "feat/auth" || rows[0]["state"] != "hot" {
129			t.Errorf("json row: %+v", rows[0])
130		}
131	
132		// park: records the next action, closes the session, keeps the worktree.
133		out = h.mustRun("park", "feat/auth", "--next", "add the regression test")
134		if !strings.Contains(out, "WARM") {
135			t.Errorf("park output: %q", out)
136		}
137		out = h.mustRun("ls")
138		if !strings.Contains(out, "WARM") || !strings.Contains(out, "add the regression test") {
139			t.Errorf("ls after park: %q", out)
140		}
141		if _, err := os.Stat(wtPath); err != nil {
142			t.Error("a warm task keeps its worktree")
143		}
144	
145		// resume: back to hot.
146		out = h.mustRun("resume", "auth")
147		if !strings.Contains(out, "feat/auth") {
148			t.Errorf("resume output: %q", out)
149		}
150		out = h.mustRun("ls")
151		if !strings.Contains(out, "HOT") {
152			t.Errorf("ls after resume: %q", out)
153		}
154	
155		// Commit something on the branch so there is work to integrate.
156		h.repo.GitIn(wtPath, "config", "user.email", "dev@example.test")
157		h.repo.GitIn(wtPath, "config", "user.name", "dev test")
158		os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(wtPath, "auth.go"), []byte("package auth\n"), 0o644)
159		h.repo.GitIn(wtPath, "add", "auth.go")
160		h.repo.GitIn(wtPath, "commit", "-m", "feat: add auth")
161	
162		// done --ff: rebase and fast-forward, then clean up.
163		out = h.mustRun("done", "auth", "--ff")
164		if !strings.Contains(out, "merged into main") {
165			t.Fatalf("done output: %q", out)
166		}
167		if _, err := os.Stat(wtPath); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
168			t.Error("done should remove the worktree")
169		}
170		// The commit is on main, and the history stayed linear.
171		if _, err := gitx.Run(gittest.Ctx(), h.repo.Root, "cat-file", "-e", "main:auth.go"); err != nil {
172			t.Error("the branch's commit should be on main")
173		}
174		merges, _ := gitx.Run(gittest.Ctx(), h.repo.Root, "log", "--merges", "--oneline")
175		if merges != "" {
176			t.Errorf("--ff must not create a merge commit, got:\n%s", merges)
177		}
178		// The branch survives by default: merged is not always finished.
179		if !gitx.BranchExists(gittest.Ctx(), h.repo.Root, "feat/auth") {
180			t.Error("the branch should survive without --delete-branch")
181		}
182	
183		// sweep reaps the done entry.
184		out = h.mustRun("sweep")
185		if !strings.Contains(out, "reap") {
186			t.Errorf("sweep should offer to reap a done task: %q", out)
187		}
188	}

282			t.Fatalf("graduated project should exist at %s: %v", dest, err)
283		}
284		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(triesRoot, tryName)); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
285			t.Error("the try directory should have been moved, not copied")
286		}
287		// The date prefix is dropped, and it is a repo with history.
288		if _, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(gittest.Ctx(), dest); err != nil {
289			t.Errorf("a graduated project should have a commit: %v", err)
290		}
291	}

398	func TestAdoptReportsThenApplies(t *testing.T) {
399		h := newHarness(t)
400	
401		// A branch ahead of main, which is exactly the unfinished work adopt is for.
402		h.repo.Branch("feat/in-flight")
403		h.repo.Commit("wip.txt", "half done\n", "feat: in flight")
404		h.repo.Git("switch", "main")
405	
406		out := h.mustRun("adopt")
407		if !strings.Contains(out, "feat/in-flight") {
408			t.Fatalf("adopt should find the unmerged branch:\n%s", out)
409		}
410		if !strings.Contains(out, "--apply") {
411			t.Error("reporting run should say how to act on it")
412		}
413		// Reporting must not have created anything.
414		if ls := h.mustRun("ls"); !strings.Contains(ls, "No tasks yet") {
415			t.Errorf("adopt without --apply must create nothing, got:\n%s", ls)
416		}
417	
418		h.mustRun("adopt", "--apply", "--yes")
419		ls := h.mustRun("ls")
420		if !strings.Contains(ls, "feat/in-flight") {
421			t.Errorf("adopted task should appear in the inventory:\n%s", ls)
422		}
423	
424		// Adopting twice must not duplicate.
425		out = h.mustRun("adopt")
426		if strings.Contains(out, "feat/in-flight") {
427			t.Errorf("an already-tracked branch should not be offered again:\n%s", out)
428		}
429	}

530		root.SetArgs([]string{"--config", generated, "repo", "list", "--long"})
531		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
532			t.Fatal(err)
533		}
534		if !strings.Contains(listed.String(), config.Contract(filepath.Join(index, "demo"))) {
535			t.Errorf("repo list should retain the index path:\n%s", listed.String())
536		}
537	}

1	# TODO
2	
3	Priority `P1` (next) … `P4` (someday); effort `S` / `M` / `L`.
4	
5	## Active
6	
7	### P2 · M — Incremental local repo snapshot
8	The TUI now renders immediately and probes repositories in the background with
9	bounded concurrency, reducing perceived startup latency. A 56-repo refresh
10	still takes roughly three seconds because status + latest commit remain live Git
11	queries. If inventories grow into the hundreds, persist a short-lived snapshot
12	and stream changed rows into the model; keep `r` as the explicit live refresh.
13	
14	### P2 · M — Multi-host aggregation
15	`dev ls --all` fanning out over ssh to the machines in a configured host list,
16	merging their `dev ls --json`. The JSON contract is already stable and the
17	`owner` field already identifies which machine holds a task, so this is
18	plumbing rather than design. Today the same thing works by hand:
19	
20	```bash
21	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="hot")'
22	```
23	
24	### P3 · S — Television / fzf channel
25	A `tv` channel over `dev ls --json` for fuzzy-picking a task, and an `fzf`
26	fallback. Navigation by metadata rather than by remembering a path is the point
27	of the tool; the TUI covers it, but a picker composes better with other tools.
28	
29	### P3 · S — `dev stats` per-repo heatmap
30	`--repo X` currently filters the totals and the combined grid. A dedicated
31	per-repo grid, several stacked, would answer "which project did I move to in
32	March" better than the aggregate does.
33	
34	### P4 · M — Raycast extension
35	`dev ls` and `dev resume` from the launcher. Wants the JSON contract and a
36	stable binary path; nothing else new.
37	
38	## Deliberately not doing
39	
40	### Installing dependencies
41	`dev doctor` reports what is missing and what degrades; it will not install
42	anything. This is the one place where being glue matters most: git, herdr,
43	tmux, gh, glab, lazygit and yazi are all installed by a package manager the
44	user already has opinions about (brew, apt, mise, nix, chezmoi), and a tool
45	that shells out to one of them is guessing. `doctor` naming the missing binary
46	is enough — the user knows how they install things on that machine.
47	
48	Reconsider only if `doctor` grows a case where the *right* command is
49	unambiguous and the user has asked for it.
50	
51	### A second git database
52	Anything derivable from git is derived live, every run. The registry holds
53	state, owner, next action and a note — nothing else. The moment it caches a
54	branch name or an ahead/behind count, it can disagree with git, and a tool that
55	disagrees with git about git is worse than no tool.
56	
57	### Syncing runtime state between machines
58	Each host runs its own multiplexer. What crosses machines is branches, through
59	the remote, plus the task registry if `state_dir` is a git repo. Syncing
60	sessions would mean reconciling two live terminal states, which is a much
61	harder problem than the one this tool has.
62	
63	### Owning the worktree path on machines with herdr
64	`herdr worktree create` would be less code, but the path policy has to hold
65	where herdr is not installed. dev creates the checkout with git and asks herdr
66	only to open it. See `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/worktree-ownership.md`.
67

72	- Runtime adapters: herdr, tmux, none, behind one contract suite.
73	- Repo discovery and gh/glab-backed clone, create, sync.
74	- `try` and `graduate`.
75	- Activity stats: sampler, git backfill, WakaTime import, heatmap.
76	- Interactive TASKS / REPOS / REMOTE dashboard with vim navigation, lazy
77	  gh/glab inventory, private XDG cache, local-clone matching and confirmed clone.
78	- Explicit configurable TUI tools, including interactive shell aliases/functions,

83	  building a non-destructive symlink index, or planning guarded atomic moves.

```text
1	# dev
2	
3	A thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
4	
5	It exists to stop four things collapsing into one:
6	
7	```
8	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
9	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
10	herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
11	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
12	```
13	
14	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
15	only what git cannot answer — a task's **state**, **owner** and **next
16	action** — as one TOML file per task.
17	
18	## The problem
19	
20	When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
21	working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
22	So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
23	defeats the point of having one.
24	
25	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
26	the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
27	
28	Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
29	the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
30	expected.
31	
32	```
33	$ dev ls
34	   TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
35	🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
36	🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
37	❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
38	```
39	
40	## Install
41	
42	```bash
43	make install     # builds, installs to ~/.local/bin, installs the agent skill
44	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
45	```
46	
47	Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
48	
49	```bash
50	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
51	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
52	```
53	
54	The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
55	working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
56	directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
57	
58	```bash
59	dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
60	```
61	
62	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
63	degrade cleanly when absent.
64	
65	## The lifecycle
66	
67	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
70	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
71	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
72	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
73	
74	```bash
75	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
76	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
77	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
78	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
79	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
80	dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
81	```
82	
83	### A task does not have to mean a worktree
84	
85	Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
86	
87	```bash
88	# No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
89	dev repo open api
90	
91	# Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
92	dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct
93	
94	# Use a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout, but no linked worktree.
95	dev start api --task "small feature" --branch-only --base main
96	
97	# Default: independent branch + worktree, provisioned and runtime-opened.
98	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
99	```
100	
101	Direct work can be parked WARM and resumed, but cannot go COLD because the
102	canonical checkout cannot be removed. `dev done` on a clean direct task needs
103	no `--ff` or `--pr`: the work is already on its destination branch.
104	
105	Start direct for one change stream, then create a normal worktree task later
106	when real parallelism appears. A new worktree starts from committed HEAD; dirty
107	main changes are deliberately not smuggled into it, so checkpoint first when
108	the parallel task depends on them.
109	
110	### The dashboard
111	
112	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens three lists, switched with `tab`:
113	
114	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
115	- **REPOS** — every repository under the scan roots, with its branch, dirty
116	  state, worktree count and per-state task tally, sorted so anything in flight
117	  is at the top. What do I have here.
118	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through the authenticated `gh` and `glab`
119	  CLIs, marked when a local clone exists. What can I open or clone.
120
```
</details></tool-use>

<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./README.md`

```text
400	dev adopt            # report only
401	dev adopt --apply    # record as tasks; nothing on disk changes
402	```
403	
404	A worktree you already have somewhere else keeps working exactly as it did —
405	`dev` records the path git reports rather than relocating it. Full detail in
406	`dev help adopting`.
407	
408	## .gitignore
409	
410	```bash
411	dev gitignore                 # detect the languages from the repo's files
412	dev gitignore python node     # or say so explicitly
413	dev gitignore --offline       # cached and bundled templates only
414	```
415	
416	Language sections come from [GitHub's templates](https://github.com/github/gitignore),
417	fetched once and cached. On top of those it adds what no language template
418	covers: the host platform's junk files, editor state, local env files, and the
419	directories coding-agent harnesses create — an agent's linked worktree left
420	untracked makes every `git status` in the main checkout unreadable.
421	
422	Everything it writes goes inside a delimited block, so re-running updates that
423	block and leaves rules you added by hand alone.
424	
425	## Configuration
426	
427	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml`. Write a commented starter with
428	`dev config init`; see the effective settings with `dev config show`; open the
429	actual file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` with either form:
430	
431	```bash
432	dev edit
433	dev config edit
434	DEV_EDITOR=unused dev edit --editor "code --wait"   # explicit override
435	```
436	
437	If the file does not exist, `edit` generates the machine-detected starter first
438	rather than opening an empty file. Resolution is `--editor` → `$VISUAL` →
439	`$EDITOR` → `nvim` → `vim` → `vi`.
440	
441	Every path is configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine —
442	a faster volume, a different naming convention:
443	
444	```toml
445	[paths]
446	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries"]
447	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
448	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
449	state_dir     = "~/.local/share/dev"        # point at a git repo to sync it
450	```
451	
452	Template variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`,
453	`host`, `date`. Filters: `|slug` (`feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`), `|lower`,
454	`|base`. A typo in a variable name fails at load, not as a directory literally
455	named `{{rep}}`.
456	
457	A flat project layout is already first-class — it needs no migration and no
458	special mode:
459	
460	```toml
461	[paths]
462	scan_roots   = ["~/code"]
463	project_root = "~/code"       # repo new/clone/graduate land at ~/code/<repo>
464	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/wt"
465	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}--{{branch|slug}}"
466	```
467	
468	Omit `--category` and canonical repos stay flat. Categories are metadata the
469	user may choose, never a directory structure dev imposes.
470	
471	## Multiple machines
472	
473	Do not sync worktrees or runtime state. Sync branches, and let the remote be
474	the handoff boundary:
475	
476	```bash
477	dev park --cold --push      # on the machine holding the work
478	dev resume <task> --fetch   # on the machine picking it up
479	```
480	
481	`dev` records an owner host per task and refuses to resume someone else's
482	without `--force`. Two machines committing to one branch is the reliable way
483	to produce a conflict here; the ownership check prevents it.
484	
485	For a cross-machine view, `dev ls --json` is a stable contract:
486	
487	```bash
488	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="hot")'
489	```
490	
491	## The agent skill
492	
493	`dev` ships the agent skill that documents it, embedded in the binary — the
494	same pattern `herdr --skill` uses. A skill vendored separately drifts from the
495	tool it describes, and an agent reading a stale command list is worse than one
496	reading none.
497	
498	```bash
499	dev skill install    # → ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills
500	dev --skill          # print it, for a dotfiles installer to sync
501	dev skill sync       # regenerate the command reference from the command tree
502	dev skill sync --check   # fail if it has drifted — wire into CI
503	```
504	
505	The skill defers to the companion `git-workflow` skill for commit conventions,
506	SemVer and branch naming rather than restating them. It owns what is new: the
507	worktree ownership rule, the task lifecycle, and how `dev` and herdr divide
508	responsibility.
509	
510	## Development
511	
512	```bash
513	make          # fmt, vet, test, build
514	make test
515	make e2e      # drives the real binary through a full lifecycle in a sandbox
516	make skill-check
517	```
518	
519	Tests build throwaway repositories under `t.TempDir()` via
520	`internal/gitx/gittest`, and the runtime adapters share one contract suite that
521	skips backends not installed on the machine — so the suite is meaningful in CI
522	(where only the null backend exists) and locally (where herdr and tmux do).
523
```
</details></tool-use>

12		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
13	)
14	
15	type checkStatus int
16	
17	const (
18		checkOK checkStatus = iota
19		checkWarn
20		checkFail
21	)
22	
23	func (s checkStatus) icon() string {
24		switch s {
25		case checkOK:
26			return "✓"
27		case checkWarn:
28			return "!"
29		}
30		return "✗"
31	}
32	
33	type check struct {
34		name   string
35		status checkStatus
36		detail string
37	}
38	
39	func newDoctorCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
40		return &cobra.Command{
41			Use:   "doctor",
42			Short: "Check dependencies, paths and runtime backends",
43			Long: `Report what dev can and cannot do on this machine.
44	
45	Only git is required. Everything else — a multiplexer, a forge CLI — enables
46	extra behaviour and degrades cleanly when missing, so a warning here is not a
47	problem to fix unless you want that capability.`,
48			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
49			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
50				return runDoctor(app)
51			},
52		}
53	}
54	
55	func runDoctor(app *App) error {
56		ctx := ctxOf()
57		var checks []check
58	
59		// Required.
60		if v, err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "--version").Output(); err == nil {
61			checks = append(checks, check{"git", checkOK, strings.TrimSpace(string(v))})
62		} else {
63			checks = append(checks, check{"git", checkFail, "not found — dev cannot work without it"})
64		}
65	
66		// Runtime backends.
67		active := app.Runtime().Name()
68		for _, rt := range runtime.All() {
69			name := rt.Name()
70			detail := "not available"
71			st := checkWarn
72			if rt.Available() {
73				st, detail = checkOK, "available"
74				if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil && len(sessions) > 0 {
75					detail = fmt.Sprintf("available, %d live session(s)", len(sessions))
76				}
77			}
78			if name == "none" {
79				st, detail = checkOK, "always available (prints a cd directive)"
80			}
81			if name == active {
82				detail += "  ← selected"
83			}
84			checks = append(checks, check{"runtime/" + name, st, detail})
85		}
86	
87		// Optional forge CLIs.
88		for _, f := range []struct{ bin, purpose string }{
89			{"gh", "GitHub: clone, create, PRs"},
90			{"glab", "GitLab: clone, create, MRs"},
91		} {
92			if path, err := exec.LookPath(f.bin); err == nil {
93				checks = append(checks, check{f.bin, checkOK, path + " — " + f.purpose})
94			} else {
95				checks = append(checks, check{f.bin, checkWarn, "not found — " + f.purpose + " unavailable"})
96			}
97		}
98	
99		// Shell integration: without the wrapper, `dev resume` prints a path
100		// instead of moving the user, which looks broken if unexplained.
101		if os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_INIT") == "1" {
102			checks = append(checks, check{"shell wrapper", checkOK, "active"})
103		} else {
104			checks = append(checks, check{"shell wrapper", checkWarn,
105				`not detected — add: eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"`})
106		}
107	
108		// Paths.
109		cfgSrc := app.Cfg.Source
110		if cfgSrc == "" {
111			cfgSrc = "built-in defaults (no config.toml)"
112		}
113		checks = append(checks, check{"config", checkOK, cfgSrc})
114		stateStatus, stateDetail := pathCheck(app.Cfg.StateDir())
115		checks = append(checks, check{"state dir", stateStatus, stateDetail})
116	
117		for _, root := range app.Cfg.ScanRoots() {
118			st, detail := pathCheck(root)
119			if st != checkOK {
120				detail = "missing — no repos will be discovered here"
121				st = checkWarn
122			}
123			checks = append(checks, check{"scan root", st, config.Contract(root) + " — " + detail})
124		}
125	
126		wtRoot := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.WorktreeRoot)
127		sample, err := app.Cfg.WorktreePathFor("example", "/repo/example", "feat/demo", "")
128		if err != nil {
129			checks = append(checks, check{"worktree path", checkFail, err.Error()})
130		} else {
131			checks = append(checks, check{"worktree path", checkOK,
132				config.Contract(sample) + fmt.Sprintf("  (root %s, %s)", config.Contract(wtRoot), writableNote(wtRoot))})
133		}
134	
135		// Render.
136		failures := 0
137		for _, c := range checks {
138			if c.status == checkFail {
139				failures++
140			}
141			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %-16s %s\n", c.status.icon(), c.name, c.detail)
142		}
143		if failures > 0 {
144			return fmt.Errorf("%d required check(s) failed", failures)
145		}
146		return nil
147	}
148	
149	func pathCheck(p string) (checkStatus, string) {
150		info, err := os.Stat(p)
151		switch {
152		case err == nil && info.IsDir():
153			return checkOK, config.Contract(p)
154		case os.IsNotExist(err):
155			return checkWarn, config.Contract(p) + " (will be created on first use)"
156		case err != nil:
157			return checkFail, err.Error()
158		default:
159			return checkFail, config.Contract(p) + " is not a directory"
160		}
161	}
162	
163	// writableNote reports whether dev could actually create a worktree under the
164	// configured root, walking up to the nearest existing ancestor. A root on an
165	// unmounted volume or a read-only mount is the failure this catches early,
166	// before a `dev wt create` gets halfway through.
167	func writableNote(root string) string {
168		dir := root
169		for {
170			if info, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil {
171				if !info.IsDir() {
172					return "not a directory"
173				}
174				if dirWritable(dir) {
175					return "writable"
176				}
177				return "NOT WRITABLE"
178			}
179			parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
180			if parent == dir {
181				return "unreachable"
182			}
183			dir = parent
184		}
185	}
186	
187	// dirWritable probes by creating and removing a temp file. There is no
188	// portable stdlib permission check, and the mode bits alone would lie about
189	// read-only mounts and ACLs.
190	func dirWritable(dir string) bool {
191		f, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, ".dev-write-probe-*")
192		if err != nil {
193			return false
194		}
195		name := f.Name()
196		f.Close()
197		os.Remove(name)
198		return true
199	}
200

109	// generateCommandReference renders the whole command tree as markdown. This is
110	// the single source of truth for what the skill tells an agent dev can do.
111	func generateCommandReference(root *cobra.Command) string {
112		var b strings.Builder
113		b.WriteString("<!-- generated by `dev skill sync`; do not edit by hand -->\n\n")
114		writeCommand(&b, root, 0)
115		return b.String()

118	func writeCommand(b *strings.Builder, c *cobra.Command, depth int) {
119		if c.Hidden || c.Name() == "no-help" || c.Name() == "completion" {
120			return
121		}
122		if depth > 0 {
123			fmt.Fprintf(b, "### `%s`\n\n%s\n\n", c.CommandPath(), firstLine(c.Short))
124			if usage := c.UseLine(); usage != "" {
125				fmt.Fprintf(b, "```\n%s\n```\n\n", usage)
126			}
127			if flags := renderFlags(c); flags != "" {
128				b.WriteString(flags)
129				b.WriteString("\n")
130			}
131		}
132		for _, sub := range c.Commands() {
133			writeCommand(b, sub, depth+1)
134		}
135	}
136	
137	func renderFlags(c *cobra.Command) string {
138		var b strings.Builder
139		c.LocalNonPersistentFlags().VisitAll(func(f *pflag.Flag) {
140			if f.Hidden {
141				return
142			}
143			name := "--" + f.Name
144			if f.Shorthand != "" {
145				name = "-" + f.Shorthand + ", " + name
146			}
147			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` — %s\n", name, f.Usage)
148		})
149		return b.String()
150	}
151	
152	func firstLine(s string) string {
153		if i := strings.IndexByte(s, '\n'); i >= 0 {
154			return s[:i]
155		}
156		return s
157	}

```text
270	- Adopting a machine that already has repos, worktrees and sessions.
271	- Recursively scanning, indexing, or physically reorganising existing repos.
272	- Configuring a flat repo/worktree layout or generating config for one.
273	
274	## When NOT to use it
275	
276	- **Commit messages, SemVer, branch naming, PR-vs-main tiering** — that is the
277	  `git-workflow` skill. This one links to it rather than restating it.
278	- **Driving herdr panes and agents directly** — that is the `herdr` skill.
279	- A single `git add` + `git commit` needs no tooling at all.
280	
281	## Reference files
282	
283	- `references/bootstrap.md` — read before scanning or organising an existing
284	  machine; includes the non-destructive index default and move safety gates.
285	- `references/worktree-ownership.md` — who owns which worktree, and how a
286	  worktree gets a working environment. Read before creating one.
287	- `references/task-lifecycle.md` — HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, when to park, and how
288	  work moves between machines.
289	- `references/runtime-herdr.md` — how `dev` and herdr divide responsibility,
290	  and the sidebar configuration that makes task state visible.
291	- `references/commands.md` — the full command reference, generated from the
292	  binary by `dev skill sync` so it cannot drift.
293	
294	## Gotchas
295	
296	- **`dev` is a shell function, not just a binary.** Commands that move you into
297	  a checkout print a `cd` directive for the wrapper installed by
298	  `eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"`. Without it they print a path and do not move
299	  you — that is not a bug.
300	- **A worktree is a clean checkout.** It has no `node_modules`, no `.venv` and
301	  none of the gitignored env files. `dev` provisions it; `--no-provision`
302	  skips that and leaves you to it.
303	- **Only gitignored files are copied into a worktree.** Listing a *tracked*
304	  file in `worktree.include` does nothing, because git already put it there on
305	  the correct branch — and copying it would overwrite that version.
306	- **Removing a worktree never deletes the branch.** Those are separate
307	  decisions; conflating them is how work gets lost.
308	- **`dev done` defaults to reporting.** With neither `--ff` nor `--pr` it
309	  explains the options and changes nothing.
310	- **The stats sampler must be scheduled.** `dev stats` is empty until
311	  `dev stats backfill` runs once and `dev stats sample` runs periodically.
312
```

```text
1	// Package skill embeds and installs dev's agent skill.
2	//
3	// The binary is the authority for its own skill, the same way `herdr --skill`
4	// is: a skill vendored separately drifts from the tool it documents, and an
5	// agent reading a stale command list is worse than one reading none. Embedding
6	// means the skill shipped is always the skill this build implements.
7	package skill
8	
9	import (
10		"embed"
11		"fmt"
12		"io/fs"
13		"os"
14		"path/filepath"
15		"strings"
16	)
17	
18	//go:embed all:dev-cli
19	var files embed.FS
20	
21	// Name is the skill's directory and frontmatter name.
22	//
23	// Deliberately not "dev", matching the binary: a skill is selected by its name
24	// and description, and "dev" describes nothing. The binary is typed dozens of
25	// times a day and should stay short; the skill is read by an agent deciding
26	// whether it is relevant, and should say what it covers.
27	const Name = "dev-cli"
28	
29	// Render returns the SKILL.md body.
30	func Render() (string, error) {
31		b, err := files.ReadFile("dev-cli/SKILL.md")
32		if err != nil {
33			return "", fmt.Errorf("bundled skill is missing: %w", err)
34		}
35		return string(b), nil
36	}
37	
38	// Files walks the embedded skill tree, yielding relative paths and contents.
39	func Files() (map[string][]byte, error) {
40		out := map[string][]byte{}
41		err := fs.WalkDir(files, "dev-cli", func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
42			if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
43				return err
44			}
45			b, err := files.ReadFile(p)
46			if err != nil {
47				return err
48			}
49			out[strings.TrimPrefix(p, "dev-cli/")] = b
50			return nil
51		})
52		return out, err
53	}
54	
55	// InstallResult reports what an install changed.
56	type InstallResult struct {
57		Dir     string
58		Written []string
59		Skipped []string
60		Links   []string
61	}
62	
63	// DefaultDir is where the skill is installed: the shared agent skills
64	// directory, which Claude Code, Codex and others all read.
65	func DefaultDir() string {
66		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
67		return filepath.Join(home, ".agents", "skills", Name)
68	}
69	
70	// LinkDirs are the tool-specific directories that get a symlink back to the
71	// shared install, matching the layout these tools already use.
72	func LinkDirs() []string {
73		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
74		return []string{filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "skills")}
75	}
76	
77	// Install writes the embedded skill to dir and links it into the per-tool
78	// skill directories. Writes are content-compared first, so re-running is a
79	// no-op and does not churn mtimes that other tools watch.
80	func Install(dir string, link bool) (InstallResult, error) {
81		res := InstallResult{Dir: dir}
82		all, err := Files()
83		if err != nil {
84			return res, err
85		}
86		if len(all) == 0 {
87			return res, fmt.Errorf("no skill files are embedded in this build")
88		}
89	
90		for rel, content := range all {
91			dst := filepath.Join(dir, rel)
92			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o755); err != nil {
93				return res, err
94			}
95			if existing, err := os.ReadFile(dst); err == nil && string(existing) == string(content) {
96				res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, rel)
97				continue
98			}
99			if err := os.WriteFile(dst, content, 0o644); err != nil {
100				return res, fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", dst, err)
101			}
102			res.Written = append(res.Written, rel)
103		}
104	
105		if !link {
106			return res, nil
107		}
108		for _, base := range LinkDirs() {
109			if _, err := os.Stat(base); err != nil {
110				continue // that tool is not installed here
111			}
112			target := filepath.Join(base, Name)
113			if existing, err := os.Readlink(target); err == nil {
114				if resolveLink(base, existing) == dir {
115					continue // already correct
116				}
117				os.Remove(target)
118			} else if _, err := os.Stat(target); err == nil {
119				// A real directory, not our symlink: never clobber it.
120				continue
121			}
122			if err := os.Symlink(dir, target); err != nil {
123				return res, fmt.Errorf("link %s: %w", target, err)
124			}
125			res.Links = append(res.Links, target)
126		}
127		return res, nil
128	}
129	
130	func resolveLink(base, link string) string {
131		if filepath.IsAbs(link) {
132			return filepath.Clean(link)
133		}
134		return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(base, link))
135	}
136

109	// generateCommandReference renders the whole command tree as markdown. This is
110	// the single source of truth for what the skill tells an agent dev can do.
111	func generateCommandReference(root *cobra.Command) string {
112		var b strings.Builder
113		b.WriteString("<!-- generated by `dev skill sync`; do not edit by hand -->\n\n")
114		writeCommand(&b, root, 0)
115		return b.String()
116	}
117	
118	func writeCommand(b *strings.Builder, c *cobra.Command, depth int) {
119		if c.Hidden || c.Name() == "no-help" || c.Name() == "completion" {
120			return
121		}
122		if depth > 0 {
123			fmt.Fprintf(b, "### `%s`\n\n%s\n\n", c.CommandPath(), firstLine(c.Short))
124			if usage := c.UseLine(); usage != "" {
125				fmt.Fprintf(b, "```\n%s\n```\n\n", usage)
126			}
127			if flags := renderFlags(c); flags != "" {
128				b.WriteString(flags)
129				b.WriteString("\n")
130			}
131		}
132		for _, sub := range c.Commands() {
133			writeCommand(b, sub, depth+1)
134		}
135	}
136	
137	func renderFlags(c *cobra.Command) string {
138		var b strings.Builder
139		c.LocalNonPersistentFlags().VisitAll(func(f *pflag.Flag) {
140			if f.Hidden {
141				return
142			}
143			name := "--" + f.Name
144			if f.Shorthand != "" {
145				name = "-" + f.Shorthand + ", " + name
146			}
147			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` — %s\n", name, f.Usage)
148		})
149		return b.String()
150	}
151	
152	func firstLine(s string) string {
153		if i := strings.IndexByte(s, '\n'); i >= 0 {
154			return s[:i]
155		}
156		return s
157	}

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"os"
7		"path/filepath"
8		"strings"
9	)
10	
11	// Markers delimit the generated block inside the skill's command reference,
12	// so the hand-written parts of that file survive a regeneration.
13	const (
14		genBegin = "<!-- BEGIN GENERATED COMMANDS -->"
15		genEnd   = "<!-- END GENERATED COMMANDS -->"
16	)
17	
18	// commandReferencePath is the file `dev skill sync` maintains, relative to the
19	// repository root. Sync only makes sense when run from a checkout of dev
20	// itself — the installed binary's copy is embedded and immutable.
21	const commandReferencePath = "internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md"
22	
23	// syncCommandReference writes the generated block into the skill source, or
24	// reports drift when check is set.
25	func syncCommandReference(app *App, generated string, check bool) error {
26		path, err := findSkillSource()
27		if err != nil {
28			return err
29		}
30		current, err := os.ReadFile(path)
31		if err != nil {
32			return fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
33		}
34		updated, err := replaceBlock(string(current), generated)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38	
39		if string(current) == updated {
40			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "command reference is current (%s)\n", commandReferencePath)
41			return nil
42		}
43		if check {
44			return errors.New("the skill's command reference is out of date — run `dev skill sync`")
45		}
46		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(updated), 0o644); err != nil {
47			return err
48		}
49		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "updated %s\n", commandReferencePath)
50		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "rebuild dev so the embedded copy matches: go build ./cmd/dev")
51		return nil
52	}
53	
54	// replaceBlock swaps the content between the generated markers.
55	func replaceBlock(doc, generated string) (string, error) {
56		start := strings.Index(doc, genBegin)
57		end := strings.Index(doc, genEnd)
58		if start < 0 || end < 0 || end < start {
59			return "", fmt.Errorf("missing the %s / %s markers", genBegin, genEnd)
60		}
61		return doc[:start+len(genBegin)] + "\n\n" + generated + doc[end:], nil
62	}
63	
64	// findSkillSource walks up from the working directory looking for dev's own
65	// checkout, so `dev skill sync` works from anywhere inside it.
66	func findSkillSource() (string, error) {
67		dir, err := os.Getwd()
68		if err != nil {
69			return "", err
70		}
71		for {
72			candidate := filepath.Join(dir, commandReferencePath)
73			if _, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil {
74				return candidate, nil
75			}
76			parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
77			if parent == dir {
78				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s not found — run `dev skill sync` from a checkout of dev-cli itself",
79					commandReferencePath)
80			}
81			dir = parent
82		}
83	}

5		"os"
6	
7		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
8	)
9	
10	// zshInit and friends define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to leave
11	// the user *inside* the checkout.
12	//
13	// A process can never change its parent's working directory, so dev prints a
14	// `cd <path>` directive on stdout and the wrapper evaluates it. This is the
15	// same mechanism try-cli uses, and it is why `dev` is a shell function rather
16	// than only a binary.
17	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
18	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
19	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
20	dev() {
21	  local __dev_out __dev_status
22	  __dev_out="$(command %[1]s "$@")"
23	  __dev_status=$?
24	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ "${__dev_out#cd }" != "$__dev_out" ]; then
25	    eval "$__dev_out"
26	  elif [ -n "$__dev_out" ]; then
27	    printf '%%s\n' "$__dev_out"
28	  fi
29	  return $__dev_status
30	}
31	`
32	
33	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
34	#   dev shell-init fish | source
35	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
36	function dev
37	    set -l __dev_out (command %[1]s $argv)
38	    set -l __dev_status $status
39	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and string match -q 'cd *' -- "$__dev_out"
40	        eval $__dev_out
41	    else if test -n "$__dev_out"
42	        printf '%%s\n' $__dev_out
43	    end
44	    return $__dev_status
45	end
46	`
47	
48	func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
49		cmd := &cobra.Command{
50			Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
51			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
52			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
53	
54	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
55	"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
56	directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
57	working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.
58	
59	Add to your shell rc file:
60	
61	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
62	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
63			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
64			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
65			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
66				self, err := os.Executable()
67				if err != nil || self == "" {
68					self = "dev"
69				}
70				switch args[0] {
71				case "bash", "zsh":
72					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
73				case "fish":
74					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
75				default:
76					return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
77				}
78				return nil
79			},
80		}
81		// Completion is a sibling concern but belongs to the same "wire dev into
82		// my shell" moment, so it hangs off this command.
83		cmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
84			Use:       "completion <bash|zsh|fish>",
85			Short:     "Print shell completions",
86			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
87			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
88			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
89				root := cmd.Root()
90				switch args[0] {
91				case "bash":
92					return root.GenBashCompletionV2(app.Out, true)
93				case "zsh":
94					return root.GenZshCompletion(app.Out)
95				case "fish":
96					return root.GenFishCompletion(app.Out, true)
97				}
98				return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q", args[0])
99			},
100		})
101		return cmd
102	}

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"os"

7		"path/filepath"

9	
10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
11		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
12		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
13	)
14	
15	type checkStatus int
16	
17	const (
18		checkOK checkStatus = iota
19		checkWarn
20		checkFail
21	)
22	
23	func (s checkStatus) icon() string {
24		switch s {
25		case checkOK:
26			return "✓"
27		case checkWarn:
28			return "!"
29		}
30		return "✗"
31	}
32	
33	type check struct {
34		name   string
35		status checkStatus
36		detail string
37	}
38	
39	func newDoctorCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
40		return &cobra.Command{
41			Use:   "doctor",
42			Short: "Check dependencies, paths and runtime backends",
43			Long: `Report what dev can and cannot do on this machine.
44	
45	Only git is required. Everything else — a multiplexer, a forge CLI — enables
46	extra behaviour and degrades cleanly when missing, so a warning here is not a
47	problem to fix unless you want that capability.`,
48			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
49			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
50				return runDoctor(app)
51			},
52		}
53	}
54	
55	func runDoctor(app *App) error {
56		ctx := ctxOf()
57		var checks []check
58	
59		// Required.
60		if v, err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "--version").Output(); err == nil {
61			checks = append(checks, check{"git", checkOK, strings.TrimSpace(string(v))})
62		} else {
63			checks = append(checks, check{"git", checkFail, "not found — dev cannot work without it"})
64		}
65	
66		// Runtime backends.
67		active := app.Runtime().Name()
68		for _, rt := range runtime.All() {
69			name := rt.Name()
70			detail := "not available"
71			st := checkWarn
72			if rt.Available() {
73				st, detail = checkOK, "available"
74				if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil && len(sessions) > 0 {
75					detail = fmt.Sprintf("available, %d live session(s)", len(sessions))
76				}
77			}
78			if name == "none" {
79				st, detail = checkOK, "always available (prints a cd directive)"
80			}
81			if name == active {
82				detail += "  ← selected"
83			}
84			checks = append(checks, check{"runtime/" + name, st, detail})
85		}
86	
87		// Optional forge CLIs.
88		for _, f := range []struct{ bin, purpose string }{
89			{"gh", "GitHub: clone, create, PRs"},
90			{"glab", "GitLab: clone, create, MRs"},
91		} {
92			if path, err := exec.LookPath(f.bin); err == nil {
93				checks = append(checks, check{f.bin, checkOK, path + " — " + f.purpose})
94			} else {
95				checks = append(checks, check{f.bin, checkWarn, "not found — " + f.purpose + " unavailable"})
96			}
97		}
98	
99		// Shell integration: without the wrapper, `dev resume` prints a path
100		// instead of moving the user, which looks broken if unexplained.
101		if os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_INIT") == "1" {
102			checks = append(checks, check{"shell wrapper", checkOK, "active"})
103		} else {
104			checks = append(checks, check{"shell wrapper", checkWarn,
105				`not detected — add: eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"`})
106		}
107	
108		// Paths.
109		cfgSrc := app.Cfg.Source
110		if cfgSrc == "" {
111			cfgSrc = "built-in defaults (no config.toml)"
112		}
113		checks = append(checks, check{"config", checkOK, cfgSrc})
114		stateStatus, stateDetail := pathCheck(app.Cfg.StateDir())
115		checks = append(checks, check{"state dir", stateStatus, stateDetail})
116	
117		for _, root := range app.Cfg.ScanRoots() {
118			st, detail := pathCheck(root)
119			if st != checkOK {
120				detail = "missing — no repos will be discovered here"
121				st = checkWarn
122			}
123			checks = append(checks, check{"scan root", st, config.Contract(root) + " — " + detail})
124		}
125	
126		wtRoot := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.WorktreeRoot)
127		sample, err := app.Cfg.WorktreePathFor("example", "/repo/example", "feat/demo", "")
128		if err != nil {
129			checks = append(checks, check{"worktree path", checkFail, err.Error()})
130		} else {
131			checks = append(checks, check{"worktree path", checkOK,
132				config.Contract(sample) + fmt.Sprintf("  (root %s, %s)", config.Contract(wtRoot), writableNote(wtRoot))})
133		}
134	
135		// Render.
136		failures := 0
137		for _, c := range checks {
138			if c.status == checkFail {
139				failures++
140			}
141			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %-16s %s\n", c.status.icon(), c.name, c.detail)
142		}
143		if failures > 0 {
144			return fmt.Errorf("%d required check(s) failed", failures)
145		}
146		return nil
147	}
148	
149	func pathCheck(p string) (checkStatus, string) {
150		info, err := os.Stat(p)
151		switch {
152		case err == nil && info.IsDir():
153			return checkOK, config.Contract(p)
154		case os.IsNotExist(err):
155			return checkWarn, config.Contract(p) + " (will be created on first use)"
156		case err != nil:
157			return checkFail, err.Error()
158		default:
159			return checkFail, config.Contract(p) + " is not a directory"
160		}
161	}
162	
163	// writableNote reports whether dev could actually create a worktree under the
164	// configured root, walking up to the nearest existing ancestor. A root on an
165	// unmounted volume or a read-only mount is the failure this catches early,
166	// before a `dev wt create` gets halfway through.
167	func writableNote(root string) string {
168		dir := root
169		for {
170			if info, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil {
171				if !info.IsDir() {
172					return "not a directory"
173				}
174				if dirWritable(dir) {
175					return "writable"
176				}
177				return "NOT WRITABLE"
178			}
179			parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
180			if parent == dir {
181				return "unreachable"
182			}
183			dir = parent
184		}
185	}
186	
187	// dirWritable probes by creating and removing a temp file. There is no
188	// portable stdlib permission check, and the mode bits alone would lie about
189	// read-only mounts and ACLs.
190	func dirWritable(dir string) bool {
191		f, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, ".dev-write-probe-*")
192		if err != nil {
193			return false
194		}
195		name := f.Name()
196		f.Close()
197		os.Remove(name)
198		return true
199	}
200
