```text
1	# `bootstrap.sh` — first-touch entry for a new machine
2	
3	The repo's one-liner installer:
4	
5	```bash
6	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash
7	```
8	
9	does just three things (the script itself is ~75 lines, mostly logging):
10	
11	1. **Install [`uv`](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv)** if missing (Astral's
12	   installer → `~/.local/bin/uv`).
13	2. **Reattach stdin to `/dev/tty`** so [`questionary`](https://github.com/tmbo/questionary)
14	   prompts inside `dotfiles_init.py` can read keystrokes (otherwise the curl
15	   pipe would steal stdin and the wrapper would silently fall back to
16	   non-interactive stubs).
17	3. **`exec uv run --script <URL>`** — fetches
18	   [`scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`](../../scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py)
19	   over HTTPS, resolves its PEP 723 inline deps (`questionary`, `rich`, `tyro`)
20	   into an ephemeral venv, runs it. No global pip install, no `pyproject.toml`.
21	
22	`bootstrap.sh` is in [`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiignore.tmpl) — `chezmoi
23	apply` does **not** deploy it to `$HOME/bootstrap.sh`.
24	
25	## "It's been 5 minutes and there's no output — is it stuck?"
26	
27	Most likely the wrapper is downloading something silently. Three layers can
28	each take 30 s – several minutes on a slow / throttled network with **zero
29	visible output**:
30	
31	| Layer | What's happening | How to confirm |
32	|---|---|---|
33	| `curl https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh \| sh` | Downloading the `uv` binary tarball from GitHub Releases | `pgrep -af 'uv\|curl\|install.sh'` |
34	| `uv run --script <URL>` (deps stage) | Resolving + downloading `questionary`/`rich`/`tyro` wheels from PyPI; building any sdists | `lsof -p $(pgrep -f dotfiles_init) -i \| head` |
35	| `chezmoi init` (after prompts) | `git clone` the dotfiles repo (~MBs of submodules, agent skills, etc.) over HTTPS / SSH | `pgrep -af 'git\|chezmoi'` |
36	
37	### Diagnose without killing the run
38	
39	In **another shell** on the same machine:
40	
41	```bash
42	# 1) see the full process tree under bootstrap
43	echo "=== process tree ==="
44	pgrep -af 'bootstrap|dotfiles_init|uv|chezmoi|ansible|brew|apt|git'
45	
46	# 2) what is the leaf doing right now?
47	LEAF=$(pgrep -f 'dotfiles_init|chezmoi|ansible' | tail -1)
48	[ -n "$LEAF" ] && {
49	  ps -p "$LEAF" -o pid,ppid,etime,stat,command
50	  lsof -p "$LEAF" 2>/dev/null -i | head -10        # network sockets
51	  lsof -p "$LEAF" 2>/dev/null -p "$LEAF" | grep REG | tail -10  # files being read
52	}
53	
54	# 3) which remote is slow?
55	for url in https://astral.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com \
56	           https://pypi.org https://github.com https://get.chezmoi.io; do
57	  printf '%-40s ' "$url"
58	  curl -fsS --max-time 5 -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code}  %{time_total}s\n' "$url" \
59	    || echo 'TIMEOUT/FAIL'
60	done
61	```
62	
63	Common patterns:
64	
65	- **`curl` to `astral.sh` taking >30 s** → GFW; set `https_proxy` (see below).
66	- **`uv` process exists but has no TCP socket** → resolver is CPU-bound on a
67	  big sdist build (rare for these three deps; usually means a transitive
68	  pulled in something heavy). Wait it out or run with `DOTFILES_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE=1`.
69	- **`git-remote-https` / `git-remote-ssh` child** → `chezmoi init` is cloning;
70	  GFW slowness is normal here.
71	- **Python process in `select()` with no children** → it's waiting for
72	  keyboard input. The TTY reattach failed; kill and re-run from a real
73	  terminal (not over a non-PTY SSH session).
74	
75	### Verbose mode
76	
77	Re-run with progress output everywhere:
78	
79	```bash
80	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh \
81	  | DOTFILES_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE=1 bash
82	```
83	
84	That sets `set -x` in `bootstrap.sh`, prints timestamped stage logs, and adds
85	`uv run --verbose` so you see every wheel download / venv operation.
86	
87	## Skipping `bootstrap.sh` entirely (recommended on slow networks)
88	
89	Once you've cloned the repo locally, you don't need the curl-piped bootstrap
90	at all — call the wrapper script directly via the `just` recipe:
91	
92	```bash
93	git clone https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles ~/.local/share/chezmoi
94	cd ~/.local/share/chezmoi
95	
96	just bootstrap-local                 # interactive (same as bootstrap.sh)
97	just bootstrap-local-verbose         # shows uv resolver progress
98	
99	# Pass through args after `--`:
100	just bootstrap-local -- --yes --bundle minimal     # non-interactive
101	just bootstrap-local -- doctor                     # schema parity check
102	just bootstrap-local -- list-bundles               # see all bundles
103	```
104	
105	Advantages:
106	
107	- **No `raw.githubusercontent.com` round-trip** for the wrapper script (only
108	  the deps still need PyPI, and PyPI is mirrorable; see below).
109	- **No `/dev/tty` re-exec gymnastics** — you're already in a real shell.
110	- **You can `git pull` and re-run** to test wrapper changes without re-running
111	  the curl pipeline.
112	- **You can `git checkout <branch>`** and run a feature branch's wrapper
113	  before merging.
114	
115	The only thing `bootstrap.sh` does that `just bootstrap-local` doesn't is
116	auto-installing `uv`. If `uv` is missing on the new host, install it once:
117	
118	```bash
119	curl -fsSL https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
120	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
121	```
122	
123	then `just bootstrap-local`.
124	
125	## Behind GFW / corporate proxy
126	
127	Three layers each need separate proxy/mirror config. The cheapest setup is a
128	local SOCKS/HTTP proxy (clash, v2ray, etc.) listening on `127.0.0.1:7890`:
129	
130	```bash
131	# (1) shell layer — curl, git, uv installer
132	export https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:7890
133	export http_proxy=$https_proxy
134	export all_proxy=socks5://127.0.0.1:7890
135	export no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1
136	
137	# (2) git layer — chezmoi init clones via git
138	git config --global http.https://github.com.proxy "$https_proxy"
139	# (or globally: git config --global http.proxy "$https_proxy")
140	
141	# (3) uv / PyPI layer — switch index instead of routing through proxy
142	export UV_INDEX_URL=https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple
143	# Tencent / Aliyun mirrors also work:
144	#   https://mirrors.cloud.tencent.com/pypi/simple
145	#   https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/
146	```
147	
148	If `raw.githubusercontent.com` itself is the bottleneck (the very first
149	`curl` in the bootstrap pipeline), point at a mirror:
150	
151	```bash
152	# ghproxy.com proxies *.githubusercontent.com transparently
153	export DOTFILES_RAW_URL="https://ghproxy.com/https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles"
154	export DOTFILES_REF=main
155	
156	curl -fsSL "${DOTFILES_RAW_URL}/${DOTFILES_REF}/bootstrap.sh" | bash
157	```
158	
159	`bootstrap.sh` itself respects `DOTFILES_RAW_URL` / `DOTFILES_REF` when
160	constructing the inner script URL, so the inner `uv run --script` will also
161	go through the mirror.
162	
163	> **Caveat — jsdelivr / cdn.statically.io** style CDNs use a different URL
164	> scheme (`/gh/owner/repo@ref/path`) and will not work as a drop-in
165	> `DOTFILES_RAW_URL`. Stick with `ghproxy.com`-style transparent proxies, or
166	> just clone locally and use `just bootstrap-local`.
167	
168	## Why bootstrap edits `~/.bashrc` and then `apply` undoes it
169	
170	Step 7 of `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` appends this to `~/.bashrc`:
171	
172	```bash
173	# Added by chezmoi bootstrap - ~/.local/bin for uv, mise, chezmoi
174	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
175	```
176	
177	and a later `chezmoi diff` shows it being **removed** again (red on the left side = "on the machine now, apply will delete it" — see [cheatsheet → Reading `chezmoi diff`](cheatsheet.md#reading-chezmoi-diff--which-side-is-which)). **This is expected, and nothing is lost.**
178	
179	The script is `run_once_**before**_`, so it runs before chezmoi has written a single dotfile. `chezmoi`, `uv` and `mise` all live in `~/.local/bin`, and the append is a shim for exactly that pre-apply window — it keeps them reachable if you open a bash shell before apply finishes, or if apply dies half-way. Once apply writes `~/.bashrc` from `dot_bashrc.tmpl` the shim is superseded: the managed `~/.bashrc` sources `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell`, and [`dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl) already exports `PATH="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin:$HOME/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` for **both** shells (the in-script comment claiming "dotfiles only wire this up in zsh" is stale — `00_exports.sh` predates it).
180

`dev-cli` does **not use Tyro**. It is a Go CLI built with **Cobra v1.10.2**. There is no Python package manifest, Tyro import, or Tyro lock/version evidence in the project.

The only Tyro references are in `.specstory` history concerning the broader request or a different `agent-warmup` tool. No Tyro API/version can be inferred for `dev-cli`.

## Existing completion exposure

There are currently **two completion command paths**.

### Explicit nested command

`/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/internal/cli/shell.go`

Symbol: `newShellInitCmd`

It adds:

```text
dev shell-init completion <bash|zsh|fish>
```

The dispatch uses Cobra’s native APIs:

- `root.GenBashCompletionV2(app.Out, true)`
- `root.GenZshCompletion(app.Out)`
- `root.GenFishCompletion(app.Out, true)`

This implementation has existed since the initial commit `f3af72e`.

### Cobra’s automatic top-level command

Cobra v1.10.2 calls `InitDefaultCompletionCmd()` during `ExecuteC()`. The root does not set `CompletionOptions.DisableDefaultCmd` and does not define its own top-level command named `completion`.

Therefore Cobra also exposes:

```text
dev completion bash
dev completion zsh
dev completion fish
dev completion powershell
```

Cobra’s automatic command also supplies `--no-descriptions` where enabled. For Bash, Zsh, and Fish, it largely duplicates the nested generator.

Relevant upstream API implementation:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/go/pkg/mod/github.com/spf13/cobra@v1.10.2/completions.go`
  - `CompletionOptions`
  - `InitDefaultCompletionCmd`
  - hidden `__complete` command
- `/Users/david/.local/share/go/pkg/mod/github.com/spf13/cobra@v1.10.2/bash_completionsV2.go`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/go/pkg/mod/github.com/spf13/cobra@v1.10.2/zsh_completions.go`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/go/pkg/mod/github.com/spf13/cobra@v1.10.2/fish_completions.go`

The generated scripts register against the command name `dev` and invoke the current command token through hidden `__complete`. This is compatible in principle with the `dev()` shell wrapper rather than requiring direct invocation of the executable.

## Current completion depth

Project code has no use of:

- `ValidArgsFunction`
- `RegisterFlagCompletionFunc`
- `MarkFlagFilename` or `MarkFlagDirname`
- `NoFileCompletions`
- project-configured `CompletionOptions`

Static `ValidArgs` occur only in:

- `/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/internal/cli/shell.go`
  - `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`
- `/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/internal/cli/cache.go`
  - `remote`, `gitignore`, `all`

Consequently, current completion covers:

- Commands and subcommands
- Command aliases
- Flag names
- Boolean flags
- Those small static positional lists

It does not supply semantic values for task names, repositories, branches, help topics, languages, states, runtime backends, or similar flag values. Cobra’s default filename completion can therefore appear for many leaf-command arguments that are not actually paths.

Because root `PersistentPreRunE` is inherited, completion generation and tab-time `dev __complete ...` both run `App.Load()`. Missing configuration is accepted; malformed configuration can prevent completion. Unknown-key warnings go to stderr rather than candidate stdout.

## Shell integration

`/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/internal/cli/shell.go`

Relevant symbols:

Current commands:

```text

dev shell-init fish
```

Behavior:

- Bash and Zsh receive the same POSIX `dev()` function.
- Fish receives a Fish function.
- The wrapper captures executable output.
- A successful `cd ...` directive is evaluated in the parent shell.
- Other multiline output is printed.

61	## Completion Categories
62	
63	Tools fall into four categories:
64	
65	### A. Self-generating (`tool completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tool`)
66	
67	Most modern CLI tools can output their own completion script. **Auto-generated for both shells** by the `chezmoi apply` hook (`run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl` → `scripts/generate_completions.sh`); see [Generating Completions After Fresh Install](#generating-completions-after-fresh-install) for opt-out + manual rerun.
68	
69	| Tool | Command |
70	|------|---------|
71	| `uv` | `uv generate-shell-completion zsh` |
72	| `mise` | `mise completion zsh` |
73	| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi completion zsh` |
74	| `just` | `just --completions zsh` |
75	| `bat` | `bat --completion zsh` |
76	| `delta` | `delta --generate-completion zsh` |
77	| `starship` | `starship completions zsh` |
78	| `rg` | `rg --generate complete-zsh` |
79	| `fd` | `fd --gen-completions zsh` |
80	| `zellij` | `zellij setup --generate-completion zsh` |
81	| `sesh` | `sesh completion zsh` |
82	| `pueue` | `pueue completions zsh` |
83	| `docker` | `docker completion zsh` |
84	| `gh` | `gh completion -s zsh` |
85	| `opencode` | `opencode completion zsh` |
86	| `bw` | `bw completion --shell zsh` |
87	
88	**Usage pattern:**
89	
90	```bash
91	# Generate once (or after upgrade)
92	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc
93	uv generate-shell-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_uv
94	mise completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_mise
95	```
96	
97	### B. Pre-bundled (no action needed)
98	
99	Completions ship with the package or via the `zsh-completions` community plugin.
100	
101	| Tool | Source |
102	|------|--------|
103	| `eza` | Homebrew formula installs `_eza` into site-functions |
104	| `git` | oh-my-zsh `git` plugin |
105	| `yazi` | Ships `_yazi` in release assets (also in zsh-completions) |
106	| `lazygit` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
107	| `btop` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
108	| Many others | `zsh-completions` plugin covers 184 tools |
109	
110	### C. Eval/source at startup (shell integration)
111	
112	These tools inject completions as part of broader shell integration. Most live in the POSIX `dot_config/shell/` layer (sourced by both zsh and bash); zsh-only ones live in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`.
113	
114	| Tool | Where | How | Cached? |
115	|------|-------|-----|---------|
116	| `fzf` | `dot_config/shell/10_fzf.sh` | `eval "$(fzf --zsh)"` (zsh) / `eval "$(fzf --bash)"` (bash) | — |
117	| `zoxide` | `dot_config/shell/20_zoxide.sh` | `eval "$(zoxide init <shell>)"` | — |
118	| `direnv` | `dot_config/shell/30_direnv.sh` | `eval "$(direnv hook <shell>)"` | — |
119	| `marimo` | `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh` | `_MARIMO_COMPLETE=<shell>_source marimo` | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/{zsh,bash}/marimo_completion.{zsh,bash}` — refresh via `marimo-update-completion` |
120	| `thefuck` | `dot_config/shell/27_thefuck.sh` | `thefuck --alias` | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/{zsh,bash}/thefuck_alias.{zsh,bash}` — refresh via `thefuck-update-completion` |
121	| `try-cli` | `dot_config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh` | `ruby try.rb init` (zsh-only) | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/zsh/try_init.zsh` — refresh via `try-update-completion` |
122	
123	> **Cached entries** auto-invalidate when the tool's binary mtime is newer than the cache file (`[ "$(command -v <tool>)" -nt "$cache" ]`) — catches `mise install <NEW>`, `brew upgrade`, `uv tool upgrade`. Manual refresh helpers handle edge cases: gem-only upgrades that don't bump the ruby binary, in-place tool replacements, or cache corruption. The pattern mirrors `dot_config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` (the canonical example).
124	
125	### D. No completion support
126	
127	`claude`, `gemini`, `agy`/`agyc` (Antigravity CLI), `btop`, `lazygit` -- no generation command available.
128	
129	### E. Python tools via `shtab` / `tyro` / `click` / `argcomplete`
130	
131	Python CLI frameworks can generate completions. Pick by what your script uses:
132	
133	- **[tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/)** (this repo's `mi-router` + every `scripts/fleet/*.py` and `scripts/mlf/*.py` subcommand): `<tool> --tyro-write-completion zsh <path>`. Native flag — auto-added when you call `tyro.cli(...)`. tyro emits `#compdef <full-binary-path>` for zsh, so post-process the first line to the short name (see `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` for the canonical pattern). Bash output already binds `basename`, no fixup needed.
134	- **[shtab](https://github.com/iterative/shtab)**: `shtab --shell=zsh my_module.parser > ~/.zfunc/_my_tool`. Decorate-an-`argparse.ArgumentParser` style; works for both shells.
135	- **argcomplete**: `register-python-argcomplete tool_name` (eval-at-startup style, category C). Requires the script to call `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` before `parse_args()`. Cross-shell.
136	- **click** (used by `marimo`, `thefuck`, `mlflow`, `litellm`, etc.): `_TOOL_COMPLETE=zsh_source tool > ~/.zfunc/_tool`. The completion script may include side effects (aliases / functions) — if so, treat as category C and cache via `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>`. See the canonical pattern at `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh`.
137	
138	> **TAB display itself**, not just completion data: see [`oh-my-zsh-plugins.md`](oh-my-zsh-plugins.md) "TAB display upgrades — alternatives evaluated" for fzf-tab (recommended) and rejected alternatives (zsh-autocomplete / carapace-bin / inshellisense).

Guard with `command -v`, **not** `$+commands` / a PATH test — the target is a function, so those never see it |
162	| `herdr-grep` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_herdr-grep` | argparse | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/59_herdr_grep_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/59_herdr_grep_completion.bash`; `--session` candidates come from `herdr-grep --list-sessions`; `--pick` pipes filtered matches into fzf and focuses/attaches the selection |
163	| `ytmv` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_ytmv` + `scripts/ytmv/*.py` | hand-rolled umbrella + tyro subs | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/60_ytmv_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/60_ytmv_completion.bash`; completes `help <leaf>` and `doctor --cookies`; `--profile` candidates come from `ytmv doctor --list-profiles`; enum flags (`--id3-version`, `--lrc-encoding`, `--lyrics`, …) complete their allowed values |

165	| `aiblock` | `scripts/aiblock.py` | questionary (interactive TUI) | — (no CLI args) | (not needed) |
166	
167	**Dynamic candidates wired up:**
168	
169	- `fleet` host names — `_fleet_hosts_one` / `_fleet_hosts_csv` shell out to `fleet hosts --list`. Used for the positional `fleet hosts NAME`, `fleet chezmoi diff HOST`, `fleet chezmoi tail HOST`, and the `--hosts=foo,bar,baz` CSV flag everywhere.
170	- `pqsum -g <GROUP>` — `_pqsum` shells out to `pueue status --json | jq '.groups | keys[]'`.
171	- `mlf` ids (run-id, experiment-id, model-name) — **not** auto-completed (would round-trip MLflow tracking server, possibly auth-required). Use `tv mlflow` for fuzzy id picking instead.
172	- `yth` video ids — **not** auto-completed (opaque 11-char ids; enumerating the whole history on every TAB is wasteful). Use `tv yth` or `yth search <query>` instead.
173	- `wake` host names — `_wake` shells out to `wake --list-names` (reads `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`), same pattern as `_fleet_hosts_one`.
174	- `appsrc which <name>` / `appsrc size <name>` — `_appsrc_names` shells out to `appsrc scan --list-names` (installed GUI app names) and adds `_command_names -e` / `compgen -c` (PATH commands), so both a GUI app name and a shell command complete. Same shell-out pattern as `_wake` / `_fleet_hosts_one`.
175	- `herdr-grep --session <name>` — both completion files shell out to `herdr-grep --list-sessions`, which reads the local Herdr session registry and returns sorted running names. Errors are silent so TAB still works when no Herdr server is running.
176	- `raid-perm-check user <name>` — `_raid_perm_check_users` reads `getent passwd` filtered to uid ≥ 1000 (real accounts, not system users). The optional trailing `ROOT` argument completes from `findmnt -rno TARGET` minus the kernel pseudo-filesystems, falling back to plain directory completion.
177	
178	**Adding a new in-house CLI** (decision flow):
179	
180	1. **Does it use tyro?** → Use Strategy A. Mirror `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh`. Add a `<tool>-update-completion` helper to `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. Don't forget to rewrite `#compdef` in zsh post-gen.
181	2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
182	   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
183	   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).
184	3. **Hand-rolled / shell script** → Strategy B hand-written. One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers.
185	4. **Update this table + `docs/shells/aliases.md`** in the same commit (per the cross-file maintenance rule in `CLAUDE.md`).
186	
187	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
188	
189	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
190	
191	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
192	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
193	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
194	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
195	
196	### What we DO track
197	
198	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
199	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
200	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
201	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
202	
203	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
204	
205	**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).
206	
207	The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
208	
209	Output paths:
210	- **zsh**: `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` — lazy-loaded by compinit on first TAB (in `$fpath` via `dot_zshrc.tmpl:68`).
211	- **bash**: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` — lazy-loaded by bash-completion v2 on first TAB.
212	
213	### Manual rerun
214	
215	```bash
216	just completions-refresh                              # force regen all (--force)
217	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh --force          # same, no `just`
218	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh                  # mtime-checked (same as the chezmoi hook)
219	```
220	
221	Use `just completions-refresh` after a tool upgrade outside the chezmoi flow (e.g. `cargo install <tool>`), or to recover from a corrupted completion file.
222	
223	### Opt out
224	
225	```bash
226	export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1   # in ~/.shellrc.adhoc; suppresses the chezmoi-apply hook
227	```
228	
229	Existing completion files stay as-is; you can still run `just completions-refresh` manually.
230	
231	### Add a new tool to the auto-gen inventory
232	
233	Edit the `regen <tool> "<zsh-args>" "<bash-args>"` block in `scripts/generate_completions.sh`. The arguments are whatever follows the tool name to produce the per-shell completion script — check `<tool> completion --help` or `<tool> --help | grep -i complet`. Examples already in the script cover click (`_TOOL_COMPLETE=`), clap (`--generate complete-<shell>`), tyro (`--tyro-write-completion <shell>`-equivalent), cobra (`completion <shell>`), and ad-hoc styles (`--completions <shell>`).
234	
235	### What about tools NOT in the auto-gen inventory?
236	
237	- **`sesh` / `tv` / `worktrunk`**: shell-startup mtime check (each tool has its own `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>.zsh` file that runs the version check on every shell start — these tools are typically `cargo install`-ed outside chezmoi, so they need the per-startup probe to catch user upgrades).
238	- **`bw` / `marimo` / `thefuck` / `try-cli`**: cached eval at startup (their completion script has side effects beyond `compdef`, so the file is `source`'d into the running shell rather than autoloaded).
239	- **`mi-router`**: tyro self-gen, lives in `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` (not the bulk script — has its own `#compdef` rewrite for tyro's full-path output quirk).
240	- **`fleet` / `mlf` / `pqsum` / `x` / `dotcfg`**: hand-written completion in `dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-54_*_completion.*` (in-house CLIs without a built-in completion generator). `dotcfg`'s `--set` key list mirrors the PROMPTS table in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`. `agent-warmup` moved to the Tyro self-generation pattern above.
241	
242	## Priority / Override Order
243	
244	When the same `_tool` file exists in multiple fpath directories, the **first match wins**:
245	
246	```
247	1. ~/.zfunc/                                    (highest - your overrides)
248	2. ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/
249	3. ~/.docker/completions/
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Repo architecture & install flow
2	
3	How `chezmoi apply` deploys configs and triggers ansible / brew on this machine.
4	
5	> **See also**: [`tool-managers.md`](tool-managers.md) — once you've read this architecture overview, that doc maps every tool in the repo to its concrete install mechanism (manager-by-manager catalog + A–Z tool index + decision tree for adding new tools). And [`upgrades.md`](upgrades.md) for the upgrade-side companion.
6	
7	## Layout
8	
9	```
10	chezmoi repo/
11	├── dot_* files               → ~/.* (config files)
12	├── dot_ansible/              → ~/.ansible/ (ansible playbooks)
13	├── run_once_before_*.tmpl    → bootstrap (runs once)
14	└── run_onchange_after_*.tmpl → ansible (runs on changes)
15	```
16	
17	## Install order
18	
19	1. **Bootstrap** (`run_once_before`) — installs Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, ansible, mise.
20	2. **`chezmoi apply`** — deploys config files + ansible playbooks.
21	3. **Ansible** (`run_onchange_after`) — runs on fresh install + when roles change.
22	4. **Brew bundle** (`run_onchange_after`) — installs GUI apps when enabled.
23	
24	## Auto-run scripts
25	
26	| Script | Behavior |
27	|--------|----------|
28	| `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` | Installs Homebrew (macOS and Linux), uv, mise, ansible |
29	| `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` | Runs ansible with all tags |
30	| `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl` | Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps`, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps`) |
31	
32	The onchange script includes SHA256 hashes of all role files. It runs on **fresh install** (no previous hash state) and on **updates** (any role's `tasks/main.yml` or `defaults/main.yml` changes).
33	
34	To force re-run all scripts:
35	
36	```bash
37	chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=scriptState
38	chezmoi apply
39	```
40	
41	See [sudo-session.md](sudo-session.md) for the shared sudo cache used by all three run-scripts.
42	
43	## Externals (`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`)
44	
45	Upstream git repos / single-file downloads that used to be cloned by Ansible are declared in `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` at the repo root. chezmoi fetches them during `chezmoi apply` and re-pulls weekly (`refreshPeriod = "168h"`):
46	
47	- oh-my-zsh core + 4 custom plugins (`zsh-autosuggestions`, `zsh-syntax-highlighting`, `zsh-completions`, `zsh-vi-mode` — last one conditional on chezmoi `enableVimMode`, see [vim-mode.md](vim-mode.md))
48	- TPM (tmux plugin manager, `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm`)
49	- fzf git source (Linux only, `~/.fzf`; apt version lacks `--zsh`)
50	- toolkami.rb (`~/.local/share/toolkami/toolkami.rb`)
51	
52	```bash
53	chezmoi apply                          # normal: pull if older than 168h
54	chezmoi apply --refresh-externals      # force: pull every external now
55	```
56	
57	Ansible retains only the post-clone steps externals can't do:
58	
59	- `zsh` role — install `zsh` package + change login shell.
60	- `devtools` role — run `tpm/bin/install_plugins` once (sentinel: `~/.tmux/plugins/.ansible-installed`).
61	- `lazyvim_deps` role — run `~/.fzf/install --bin` (idempotent via `creates:`).
62	
63	**When to add an entry here vs Ansible**: use `.chezmoiexternal` when the content is a plain clone / single file and the only conditional is `.chezmoi.os`. Keep things in Ansible when they need arch / `noRoot` / `armv7l` logic, dynamic version paths, or `become: true`. Full schema notes: [chezmoi-prefixes.md → Companion file: `.chezmoiexternal.<format>`](../tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md#companion-file-chezmoiexternalformat).
64	
65	## Ansible vs Homebrew
66	
67	**Primary tool: Ansible** — manages CLI tools and system dependencies cross-platform.
68	
69	| Tool | Role | When to Use |
70	|------|------|-------------|
71	| **Ansible** | CLI tools, system packages | Always (apt/brew formulas) |
72	| **Brewfile** | macOS GUI apps (casks), App Store | Optional (opt-in) |
73	| **Linuxbrew** | Linux packages not in apt | Always installed on Linux |
74	
75	Bootstrap installs Homebrew on both macOS and Linux. Ansible roles use `community.general.homebrew` for macOS formulas. Brewfile manages casks (GUI apps) and mas (App Store) separately. On Linux, Ansible uses apt; Linuxbrew is available for newer packages.
76	
77	Deeper comparison of Linux package sources (apt / snap / Linuxbrew / GitHub binaries) and the policy ansible roles follow: [docs/linux-package-sources.md](../linux-package-sources.md).
78	
79	## Ansible usage
80	
81	Ansible playbooks run automatically via `chezmoi apply` when playbook files change. For manual runs, use `~/.ansible/`:
82	
83	```bash
84	cd ~/.ansible
85	
86	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml                    # Full setup (macOS)
87	ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml                    # Full setup (Linux)
88	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --tags "neovim"    # Specific tags only
89	ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml --skip-tags "sudo" # Skip sudo tasks
90	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --check            # Dry run
91	```
92	
93	After modifying playbooks/roles, syntax check:
94	
95	```bash
96	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/base.yml
97	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/macos.yml
98	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml
99	```
100	
101	Or use `just ansible-syntax-check`.
102

59	
60	## Quick Setup
61	
62	### Interactive (recommended)
63	
64	```bash
65	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash
66	```
67	
68	Installs [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (if missing) and launches `dotfiles-init` — a Python wrapper that groups the ~19 chezmoi prompts into a clean multi-select UI, offers pre-set bundles (`personal-mac` / `work-mac` / `server-linux` / `cloud-vm` / `minimal`), checks SSH keys, then calls real `chezmoi init` with your answers pre-filled. Full docs: [`scripts/init/README.md`](scripts/init/README.md).
69	
70	On first-run or slow networks the `uv` resolver can sit silently for a few minutes — use the verbose form to see timestamped progress + `uv --verbose` resolver output + `set -x`:
71	
72	```bash
73	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | DOTFILES_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE=1 bash
74	```
75	
76	Pass extra args through to the wrapper via `bash -s --` (e.g. run the schema-parity checker instead of the default `init`):
77	
78	```bash
79	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash -s -- doctor
80	```
81	
82	Behind GFW? Set `DOTFILES_RAW_URL` / `DOTFILES_REF` to point at a mirror, or use the non-interactive path below.
83	
84	### Non-interactive (direct chezmoi)
85	
86	```bash
87	# Installs chezmoi to ~/.local/bin and walks through the raw prompts one-by-one.
88	# Uses HTTPS to avoid SSH key setup on fresh machines.
89	export GITHUB_USERNAME=daviddwlee84
90	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin" init --apply "https://github.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git"
91	
92	# After install, switch the chezmoi source repo to SSH (so future `chezmoi update` uses your SSH key):
93	#   chezmoi cd
94	#   git remote set-url origin git@github.com:$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git
95	#   exit
96	```
97	
98	This automatically:
99	
100	1. Bootstraps Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, mise, ansible
101	2. Deploys all config files
102	3. Runs ansible playbooks (git, ripgrep, fd, neovim, etc.)
103	4. Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` is enabled, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps` / `installGamingApps` is enabled)
104	
105	#### Sudo password injection (when chezmoi can't open `/dev/tty`)
106	
107	Some Linux environments — notably **CentOS 7 + AD/LDAP user with high UID** where `pam_systemd` never created `/run/user/<UID>/` — leave the chezmoi-spawned bootstrap script unable to open `/dev/tty`, so the shared sudo helper can't prompt and Linuxbrew aborts with `Insufficient permissions to install Homebrew to "/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew"`. The fix is to pre-stage the password via `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (the same env-var [`fleet_apply`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md) uses over SSH).
108	
109	The repo ships [`scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh`](scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh) to handle the prompt → 0600 tmpfile → export → run → `shred` dance:
110	
111	```bash
112	# First time (chezmoi not installed yet):
113	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin"   # install chezmoi only
114	bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles/main/scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh) \
```
</details></tool-use>

121		}

3	import (

9	
10	// zshInit and friends define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to leave
11	// the user *inside* the checkout.
12	//
13	// A process can never change its parent's working directory, so dev prints a
14	// `cd <path>` directive on stdout and the wrapper evaluates it. This is the
15	// same mechanism try-cli uses, and it is why `dev` is a shell function rather
16	// than only a binary.
17	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
18	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
19	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
20	dev() {
21	  local __dev_out __dev_status
22	  __dev_out="$(command %[1]s "$@")"
23	  __dev_status=$?
24	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ "${__dev_out#cd }" != "$__dev_out" ]; then
25	    eval "$__dev_out"
26	  elif [ -n "$__dev_out" ]; then
27	    printf '%%s\n' "$__dev_out"
28	  fi
29	  return $__dev_status
30	}
31	`
32	
33	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
34	#   dev shell-init fish | source
35	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
36	function dev
37	    set -l __dev_out (command %[1]s $argv)
38	    set -l __dev_status $status
39	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and string match -q 'cd *' -- "$__dev_out"
40	        eval $__dev_out
41	    else if test -n "$__dev_out"
42	        printf '%%s\n' $__dev_out
43	    end
44	    return $__dev_status
45	end
46	`
47	
48	func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
49		cmd := &cobra.Command{
50			Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
51			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
52			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
53	
54	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
55	"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
56	directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
57	working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.
58	
59	Add to your shell rc file:
60	
61	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
62	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
63			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
64			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
65			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
66				self, err := os.Executable()
67				if err != nil || self == "" {
68					self = "dev"
69				}
70				switch args[0] {
71				case "bash", "zsh":
72					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
73				case "fish":
74					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
75				default:
76					return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
77				}
78				return nil
79			},
80		}
81		// Completion is a sibling concern but belongs to the same "wire dev into
82		// my shell" moment, so it hangs off this command.
83		cmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
84			Use:       "completion <bash|zsh|fish>",
85			Short:     "Print shell completions",
86			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
87			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
88			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
89				root := cmd.Root()
90				switch args[0] {
91				case "bash":
92					return root.GenBashCompletionV2(app.Out, true)
93				case "zsh":
94					return root.GenZshCompletion(app.Out)
95				case "fish":
96					return root.GenFishCompletion(app.Out, true)
97				}
98				return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q", args[0])
99			},
100		})
101		return cmd
102	}

```text
1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	}
32	
33	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
34	func (a *App) Load() error {
35		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
36		if err != nil {
37			return err
38		}
39		a.Cfg = cfg
40		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
41		if a.Out == nil {
42			a.Out = os.Stdout
43		}
44		if a.Err == nil {
45			a.Err = os.Stderr
46		}
47		return nil
48	}
49	
50	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
51	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
52	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
53		if a.noRuntime {
54			return runtime.None{}
55		}
56		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
57		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
58			backend = a.runtimeOverride
59		}
60		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
61		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
62			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
63		}
64		return rt
65	}
66	
67	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
68	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
69		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
70	}
71	
72	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
73	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
74		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
75	}
76	
77	// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
78	// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
79	// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
80	// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
81	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
82		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
83	}
84	
85	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
86	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
87
```

+# ============================================================================
+# Category: go — `go install <pkg>@latest` for each tool in
+# dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/defaults/main.yml
+# ============================================================================
+cat_go() {
+  # Resolve go via mise shim first, then system PATH.
+  local go_cmd=""
+  if [[ -x "$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims/go" ]]; then
+    go_cmd="$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims/go"
+  elif command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    go_cmd="go"
+  else
+    warn "go not found (Go not installed via mise?) — skipping"
+    return $SKIP_RC
+  fi
+
+  # Parse the tools list from defaults YAML — lines `  - name: <pkg>@<ver>`.
+  # Same hand-rolled awk parser as cat_dotnet.
+  local defaults_file="$_REPO_ROOT/dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/defaults/main.yml"
+  local tools=()
+  if [[ -f "$defaults_file" ]]; then
+    while IFS= read -r line; do
+      tools+=("$line")
+    done < <(awk '
+            /^go_tools:/ { in_list=1; next }
+            in_list && /^[^ ]/ { in_list=0 }
+            in_list && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*name:/ {
+                sub(/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*name:[[:space:]]*/, "")
+                gsub(/["'"'"']/, "")
+                print
+            }
+        ' "$defaults_file")
+  fi
+
+  if [[ ${#tools[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
+    warn "no go tools to upgrade — skipping"
+    return $SKIP_RC
+  fi
+
+  # Install into ~/.local/bin (the blessed dir), not ~/go/bin or the mise
+  # toolchain dir. Upgrade = re-install at @latest regardless of the version
+  # pinned in defaults (install-vs-upgrade split — defaults pin for fresh
+  # installs, this moves them forward). See docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md.
+  export GOBIN="$HOME/.local/bin"
+
+  local any_fail=0
+  for t in "${tools[@]}"; do
+    # Strip any @version pin (module paths never contain '@') and go to @latest.
+    local pkg="${t%@*}"
+    info "Upgrading go tool: $pkg@latest"
+    _run "$go_cmd" install "$pkg@latest" || any_fail=1
+  done
+  return "$any_fail"
+}
+
 # ============================================================================
 # Category: dotnet — upgrade each tool in dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml
 # ============================================================================

1	# TODO
2	
3	Priority `P1` (next) … `P4` (someday); effort `S` / `M` / `L`.
4	
5	## Active
6	
7	### P2 · M — Incremental local repo snapshot
8	The TUI now renders immediately and probes repositories in the background with
9	bounded concurrency, reducing perceived startup latency. A 56-repo refresh
10	still takes roughly three seconds because status + latest commit remain live Git
11	queries. If inventories grow into the hundreds, persist a short-lived snapshot
12	and stream changed rows into the model; keep `r` as the explicit live refresh.
13	
14	### P2 · M — Multi-host aggregation
15	`dev ls --all` fanning out over ssh to the machines in a configured host list,
16	merging their `dev ls --json`. The JSON contract is already stable and the
17	`owner` field already identifies which machine holds a task, so this is
18	plumbing rather than design. Today the same thing works by hand:
19	
20	```bash
21	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="hot")'
22	```
23	
24	### P3 · S — Television / fzf channel
25	A `tv` channel over `dev ls --json` for fuzzy-picking a task, and an `fzf`
26	fallback. Navigation by metadata rather than by remembering a path is the point
27	of the tool; the TUI covers it, but a picker composes better with other tools.
28	
29	### P3 · S — `dev stats` per-repo heatmap
30	`--repo X` currently filters the totals and the combined grid. A dedicated
31	per-repo grid, several stacked, would answer "which project did I move to in
32	March" better than the aggregate does.
33	
34	### P4 · M — Raycast extension
35	`dev ls` and `dev resume` from the launcher. Wants the JSON contract and a
36	stable binary path; nothing else new.
37	
38	## Deliberately not doing
39	
40	### Installing dependencies
41	`dev doctor` reports what is missing and what degrades; it will not install
42	anything. This is the one place where being glue matters most: git, herdr,
43	tmux, gh, glab, lazygit and yazi are all installed by a package manager the
44	user already has opinions about (brew, apt, mise, nix, chezmoi), and a tool
45	that shells out to one of them is guessing. `doctor` naming the missing binary
46	is enough — the user knows how they install things on that machine.
47	
48	Reconsider only if `doctor` grows a case where the *right* command is
49	unambiguous and the user has asked for it.
50	
51	### A second git database
52	Anything derivable from git is derived live, every run. The registry holds
53	state, owner, next action and a note — nothing else. The moment it caches a
54	branch name or an ahead/behind count, it can disagree with git, and a tool that
55	disagrees with git about git is worse than no tool.
56	
57	### Syncing runtime state between machines
58	Each host runs its own multiplexer. What crosses machines is branches, through
59	the remote, plus the task registry if `state_dir` is a git repo. Syncing
60	sessions would mean reconciling two live terminal states, which is a much
61	harder problem than the one this tool has.
62	
63	### Owning the worktree path on machines with herdr
64	`herdr worktree create` would be less code, but the path policy has to hold
65	where herdr is not installed. dev creates the checkout with git and asks herdr
66	only to open it. See `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/worktree-ownership.md`.
67	
68	## Done
69	
70	- Task lifecycle: `start` / `park` / `resume` / `done` / `sweep`.
71	- Worktree ownership rule, path templates, provisioning, per-repo `.dev.toml`.
72	- Runtime adapters: herdr, tmux, none, behind one contract suite.
73	- Repo discovery and gh/glab-backed clone, create, sync.
74	- `try` and `graduate`.
75	- Activity stats: sampler, git backfill, WakaTime import, heatmap.
76	- Interactive TASKS / REPOS / REMOTE dashboard with vim navigation, lazy
77	  gh/glab inventory, private XDG cache, local-clone matching and confirmed clone.
78	- Explicit configurable TUI tools, including interactive shell aliases/functions,
79	  with lazygit / yazi / editor / shell defaults.
80	- `dev gitignore`, from GitHub's templates plus the sections no template has.
81	- `dev adopt`, to import existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches.
82	- `dev bootstrap`, recursively classifying existing repos/worktrees/bare hubs,
83	  building a non-destructive symlink index, or planning guarded atomic moves.
84	- Symlink catalogs as first-class scan roots, deduplicated with physical paths.
85	- `dev config init` / `dev edit`, generating and opening config from the
86	  machine's detected layout; TUI edit + live config/data/tool reload.
87	- Explicit direct / branch-only / worktree task modes, including direct-main
88	  lifecycle and ad-hoc repo open with no task.
89	- Rich starship-like Git status counts plus unique-path/type breakdown.
90	- Latest repo activity from dirty-file mtime, commit, or task update; configurable
91	  REPOS columns and activity/latest/name/git/tasks sorting.
92	- Immediate TUI render with bounded-parallel repo probes (serial path measured
93	  4.2s); background rows replace the initial loading state.
94	- Explicit Herdr/tmux LIVE repo status and selected-repo heatmap overlay in TUI,
95	  including `b` single-repo backfill.
96	- XDG `stats path/clear` and regenerable `cache list/path/clear` with stats data
97	  deliberately kept out of cache semantics.

4	
5	# =============================================================================
6	# macOS - all via Homebrew
7	# =============================================================================
8	
9	- name: Tap diffnav formula (macOS)
10	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
11	  community.general.homebrew_tap:
12	    name: dlvhdr/formulae
13	    state: present
14	
15	- name: Tap raine/workmux formula (macOS)
16	  # workmux is a tmux + git-worktree orchestrator with first-class agent
17	  # status icons (🤖 working / 💬 waiting / ✅ done) rendered into the tmux
18	  # window list. Coexists with worktrunk (`wt`); see docs/tools/workmux.md
19	  # for the wt-vs-wm split.
20	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
21	  community.general.homebrew_tap:
22	    name: raine/workmux
23	    state: present
24	
25	# Homebrew 6.0 added a formula-trust security gate: `brew install` refuses to
26	# load formulae from third-party taps until the tap is explicitly trusted
27	# ("Error: Refusing to load formula <tap>/<formula> from untrusted tap"). The
28	# homebrew_tap module has no trust parameter, so trust via `brew trust`.
29	# Idempotent + back-compatible: older Homebrew has no trust concept, so
30	# `tap-info` won't contain "Untrusted" and the trust task no-ops (no version
31	# gate needed). Keep this loop in sync with the third-party taps above — add any
32	# new third-party tap here too. See pitfalls/homebrew-6-refuses-untrusted-tap-formula.md
33	- name: Check trust state of third-party taps (macOS, Homebrew >= 6.0 formula-trust gate)
34	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
35	  ansible.builtin.command: "brew tap-info {{ item }}"
36	  loop:
37	    - dlvhdr/formulae
38	    - raine/workmux
39	  register: devtools_tap_info
40	  changed_when: false
41	  failed_when: false
42	
43	- name: Trust untrusted third-party taps (macOS)
44	  when:
45	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
46	    - "'Untrusted' in item.stdout"
47	  ansible.builtin.command: "brew trust {{ item.item }}"
48	  loop: "{{ devtools_tap_info.results }}"
49	  loop_control:
50	    label: "{{ item.item }}"
51	  changed_when: true
52	
53	- name: Install developer CLI tools (macOS)
54	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
55	  community.general.homebrew:

/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md:888:### 15. ya pkg (Yazi plugins)
/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md:892:> **`ya` and `yazi` are a matched pair.** Every upstream release asset ships both binaries; installing only `yazi` yields a host that can never acquire a plugin, and yazi then refuses to start at all (`Failed to load plugin from …/duckdb.yazi/main.lua`). The `devtools` role installs and probes for both. See [pitfalls/yazi-lua-runtime-failed-plugin-main-lua.md](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/yazi-lua-runtime-failed-plugin-main-lua.md).

1	# 37_worktrunk.sh - Worktrunk (`wt`) shell integration (shared bash + zsh).
2	# https://worktrunk.dev — github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk
3	#
4	# Backend half of the split: shell-init wrapper (so `wt switch` can change
5	# the parent shell's $PWD) + the `wtcd` fzf picker. Zsh-only half lives in
6	# dot_config/zsh/tools/37_worktrunk.zsh (clap-based completion generation
7	# into ~/.zfunc/_wt).
8	#
9	# Companion config: ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml (managed by chezmoi at
10	# dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml). Aliases like `wt sw` / `wt cc` live
11	# THERE, not here — keep this file focused on shell-level integration only.
12	
13	# Skip silently if not installed (Linux ansible install can fail offline)
14	command -v wt &>/dev/null || return 0
15	
16	# ── Shell integration: cd-wrapping `wt` function ───────────────────────────
17	#
18	# `wt switch` needs to change the parent shell's $PWD, which a normal binary
19	# can't do. Worktrunk solves this by writing a directive file that a wrapper
20	# shell function reads and `cd`s to. We eval that wrapper at shell startup
21	# rather than running `wt config shell install` (which edits ~/.zshrc with a
22	# block chezmoi would fight over).
23	#
24	# Same pattern as starship / zoxide / direnv elsewhere. The `2>/dev/null`
25	# swallows the error if wt doesn't support the requested shell (e.g. bash
26	# wrapper not yet implemented in upstream) — the binary itself still works,
27	# users just lose the cd-on-switch wrapper.
28	if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
29	    eval "$(wt config shell init zsh 2>/dev/null)"
30	elif [ -n "$BASH_VERSION" ]; then
31	    eval "$(wt config shell init bash 2>/dev/null)"
32	fi
33	
34	# ── Tiny shell-side conveniences (NOT duplicating wt's own aliases) ────────
35	#
36	# `wt`'s own aliases (sw / ls / rm / cc / oc) are defined in
37	# ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml so they work from any shell + the
38	# interactive picker. Anything below is shell niceness that wt's alias
39	# system can't express.
40	
41	# `wtcd` — jump to a worktree path WITHOUT switching tmux/sesh session.
42	# Useful when you want to peek at sibling worktree files (open in nvim split,
43	# scp, etc.) without disturbing the current pane's session context.
44	function wtcd() {
45	    local target
46	    target=$(wt list --format=json 2>/dev/null \
47	        | jq -r '.worktrees[].path' \
48	        | fzf-tmux -p 60%,40% --prompt='wt cd ❯ ' --header='Pick a worktree to cd into') \
49	        || return
50	    [ -n "$target" ] && cd -- "$target"
51	}
52
```

```text
1	# 37_worktrunk.zsh - Worktrunk (`wt`) zsh-only completion generation.
2	# Shell-init wrapper + wtcd function live in dot_config/shell/37_worktrunk.sh
3	# (shared bash + zsh). This file only handles ~/.zfunc/_wt completion regen,
4	# which is zsh-specific.
5	# https://worktrunk.dev — github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk
6	
7	# Skip silently if not installed
8	command -v wt &>/dev/null || return 0
9	
10	# ── Completion ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
11	#
12	# macOS (Homebrew): `_wt` ships in /opt/homebrew/share/zsh/site-functions/
13	# and is picked up automatically by compinit — nothing to do here.
14	#
15	# Linux (ansible drops the bare binary into ~/.local/bin/) has no system
16	# completion path, so dump clap's auto-generated zsh completer into
17	# ~/.zfunc/_wt (already on $fpath via dot_zshrc.tmpl). Same pattern as sesh /
18	# television. Regenerate when wt's version changes.
19	#
20	# Worktrunk doesn't expose a `wt completion zsh` subcommand — clap's dynamic
21	# completer is invoked via `COMPLETE=zsh wt` (with no args). Output is a
22	# self-contained `#compdef wt` script that handles further completion
23	# requests by re-invoking the binary with COMPLETE+_CLAP_COMPLETE_INDEX set.
24	if [[ -d ~/.zfunc ]] && [[ ! -f /opt/homebrew/share/zsh/site-functions/_wt ]] \
25	                    && [[ ! -f /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_wt ]]; then
26	    local _wt_ver="$(wt --version 2>/dev/null)"
27	    if [[ ! -f ~/.zfunc/_wt ]] || ! grep -q "${_wt_ver}" ~/.zfunc/_wt 2>/dev/null; then
28	        {
29	            print -r -- "# Auto-generated by 37_worktrunk.zsh for ${_wt_ver}"
30	            COMPLETE=zsh wt 2>/dev/null
31	        } > ~/.zfunc/_wt
32	    fi
33	fi
34
```
</details></tool-use>
