1	# 24_herdr.sh - herdr workspace layout helpers (shared backend; bash 4+ / zsh).
2	# https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr
3	#
4	# herdr-native analogs of the sesh/tmux helpers in 22_sesh.sh. herdr's model is
5	# Workspace -> Tab -> Pane (tmux is Session -> Window -> Pane), and its CLI
6	# (`herdr workspace|tab|pane|agent …`) is the scripting surface that replaces
7	# `tmux new-session/split-window`.
8	#
9	# Backend that powers the user-facing commands and their aliases:
10	#   herdr-vibe / hvibe  — parametric multi-agent pack in a new workspace
11	#                         (N agent panes + lazygit tab + nvim tab)
12	#   herdr-code / hcode  — repo-scoped single-agent layout
13	#                         (nvim | agent split + btop monitor tab)
14	#
15	# REUSE: the *pure* (multiplexer-agnostic) helpers from 22_sesh.sh are reused
16	# verbatim — `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_wrap_agent` (specstory
17	# wrapping), `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` (shell|kill|restart post-exit behavior).
18	# 22_sesh.sh sorts before this file, so they are defined by the time hvibe/hcode
19	# run. Only the tmux calls are swapped for `herdr …` CLI calls.
20	#
21	# Bash baseline: 4+ (same array-slicing idiom as svibe; no `local -A`).
22	
23	# Skip entirely if herdr isn't installed (it's a trial tool, not on every host).
24	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
25	
26	# ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
27	
28	# Echo the workspace_id of an existing workspace whose label == $1 (else empty).
29	# Used for idempotency: re-running hvibe/hcode in a repo focuses the existing
30	# workspace instead of stacking duplicates (mirrors svibe's has-session check).
31	function _herdr_ws_by_label() {
32	    herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null \
33	        | jq -r --arg l "$1" '.result.workspaces[]? | select(.label==$l) | .workspace_id' 2>/dev/null \
34	        | head -1
35	}
36	
37	# Compose the shell command for one agent pane: specstory-wrap then on-exit-wrap.
38	# $1=agent  $2=specstory_mode(auto|never)  $3=on_exit(shell|kill|restart)
39	function _herdr_agent_cmd() {
40	    local inner
41	    inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$2")
42	    _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$3" "${1:-agent}"
43	}
44	
45	# Create a labeled tab in workspace $1 (cwd $2, label $3) and run command $4 in
46	# its root pane. `tab create` returns the new pane id at .result.root_pane.
47	# $1=workspace_id  $2=cwd  $3=label  $4=command
48	function _herdr_tool_tab() {
49	    local pane
50	    pane=$(herdr tab create --workspace "$1" --cwd "$2" --label "$3" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
51	        | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
52	    [ -n "$pane" ] && herdr pane run "$pane" "$4" >/dev/null 2>&1
53	}
54	
55	# Absolutize + validate a `-p/--path DIR` argument in THIS shell. Echoes the
56	# canonical (symlink-resolved) path; on a non-directory, echoes nothing and
57	# returns 1 after a message on stderr.
58	#
59	# LOAD-BEARING for every `--cwd` below: herdr resolves a *relative* `--cwd`
60	# against the SERVER's launch directory (wherever `herdr server` was started),
61	# not the caller's cwd — and on a miss it silently falls back to $HOME, so
62	# `hhere -p ../sibling` opens a workspace at `~` with no error anywhere. tmux
63	# resolves `new-session -c` client-side, which is why the sesh originals
64	# (shere/svibe/scode) never needed this.
65	# See pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md.
66	#
67	# `CDPATH=''` + `--` + `>/dev/null` keep a CDPATH hit from silently retargeting
68	# the cd or echoing the resolved dir into the capture.
69	# $1=dir  $2=caller name (for the error message)
70	function _herdr_abs_dir() {
71	    local abs
72	    abs=$(CDPATH=''; cd -- "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
73	    if [ -z "$abs" ]; then
74	        echo "${2:-herdr}: --path is not a directory: $1" >&2
75	        return 1
76	    fi
77	    printf '%s\n' "$abs"
78	}
79	
80	# Resolve the target herdr session for hvibe/hcode from an optional --session
81	# value. Echoes "<name><TAB><socket_override_or_empty>". The socket field is
82	# non-empty ONLY when the caller must override HERDR_SOCKET_PATH (explicit
83	# --session); empty means "use the ambient/default socket untouched". Returns 1
84	# (with a message) when an explicit --session names a session that isn't running.
85	#
86	# A herdr server hosts multiple named sessions (default + `herdr --session NAME`),
87	# each with its own socket. The CLI has no --session flag on subcommands; the
88	# only lever is the HERDR_SOCKET_PATH env var (verified). `session list --json`
89	# is the authoritative name -> socket_path resolver.
90	function _herdr_session_target() {
91	    local want="$1" js line running socket nm
92	    js=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null)
93	    if [ -n "$want" ]; then
94	        line=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
95	            | jq -r --arg n "$want" '.sessions[] | select(.name==$n) | "\(.running)\t\(.socket_path)"' 2>/dev/null \
96	            | head -1)
97	        if [ -z "$line" ]; then
98	            echo "session '$want' not found. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
99	            return 1
100	        fi
101	        running=${line%%$'\t'*}
102	        socket=${line#*$'\t'}
103	        if [ "$running" != "true" ]; then
104	            echo "session '$want' is not running. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
105	            return 1
106	        fi
107	        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$want" "$socket"
108	        return 0
109	    fi
110	    # No explicit --session: inside herdr use the ambient session (no override);
111	    # outside, fall back to the default session. Only the NAME matters here (for
112	    # the attach path) — socket stays empty so the ambient socket is left as-is.
113	    if [ -n "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" ]; then
114	        nm=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
115	            | jq -r --arg s "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" '.sessions[] | select(.socket_path==$s) | .name' 2>/dev/null \
116	            | head -1)
117	        printf '%s\t\n' "${nm:-default}"
118	    else
119	        printf 'default\t\n'
120	    fi
121	}
122	
123	# When hvibe/hcode run from OUTSIDE herdr, bring up a client attached to the
124	# session so the just-created/focused workspace is actually visible — the
125	# `herdr workspace focus` calls only move an ALREADY-attached client. Inside
126	# herdr (HERDR_ENV set) those focus calls already switched the live client, so
127	# there is nothing to do. Runs the client as a child (no exec), mirroring
128	# svibe's `tmux attach-session`. $1=session_name (default: "default").
129	function _herdr_attach_if_outside() {
130	    [ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ] && return 0
131	    local session="${1:-default}"
132	    if [ "$session" = "default" ]; then
133	        herdr
134	    else
135	        herdr session attach "$session"
136	    fi
137	}
138	
139	# ── hvibe: parametric multi-agent pack ──────────────────────────────────────
140	#
141	# A herdr "vibe" workspace: tab "agents" with N agent panes (side-by-side
142	# splits by default), tab "git" (lazygit), tab "edit" (nvim). Built directly
143	# with herdr CLI calls so pane count stays parametric.
144	#
145	# Workspace label: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (idempotent — re-running focuses it).
146	# Refuses outside a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo).
147	#
148	# Each agent pane is specstory-wrapped (known providers) and on-exit-wrapped,
149	# exactly like `svibe` — the wrapping helpers are shared, only the layout calls
150	# differ. herdr auto-detects agent state per pane, so all N agents surface
151	# individually in the sidebar even when they share the "agents" tab.
152	#
153	# Two modes for choosing agents (same as svibe):
154	#   Homogeneous (positional):  hvibe 3 codex        → 3 panes all codex
155	#   Heterogeneous (--agents):  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode
156	#
157	# --tab-per-agent puts each agent in its OWN tab (own rolled-up state dot in the
158	# sidebar) instead of side-by-side splits — better for many agents, since herdr
159	# has no even-out-splits command.
160	#
161	# Usage:
162	#   hvibe                                       # auto N × claude (specstory)
163	#   hvibe 2                                     # 2× claude
164	#   hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× specstory run codex
165	#   hvibe 2 opencode                            # 2× opencode (raw)
166	#   hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
167	#   hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
168	#   hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude, no md auto-save
169	#   hvibe --on-exit restart 2 codex             # auto-respawn loop
170	#   hvibe -p ~/repo 2 claude                    # explicit path
171	#   hvibe --no-attach 2 claude                  # create in background
172	function herdr-vibe() {
173	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hvibe: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
174	
175	    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto" session_arg=""
176	    local n_agents=0 n_agents_set=0 agent_cli="claude" agents_csv="" tab_per_agent=0
177	    local min_width="${HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
178	    # Stagger between pane launches so agents that share a global resource at
179	    # cold start (opencode's single SQLite DB + WAL pragma) don't race. Set 0
180	    # to launch all at once. Same rationale as svibe's SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER.
181	    local launch_stagger="${HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER:-0.25}"
182	
183	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
184	        case "$1" in
185	            -p|--path)       target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
186	            --on-exit)       on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
187	            --agents)        agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
188	            --session)       session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
189	            --min-width)     min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
190	            --tab-per-agent) tab_per_agent=1; shift ;;
191	            --no-specstory)  specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
192	            --specstory)     specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
193	            --no-attach)     no_attach=1; shift ;;
194	            -h|--help)
195	                cat <<'EOF'
196	hvibe — herdr multi-agent pack (herdr analog of svibe)
197	
198	Usage:
199	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
200	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [--session NAME] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
201	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
202	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [--session NAME] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]
203	
204	Builds a new herdr workspace `vibe/<repo>`:
205	  tab "agents" — N agent panes (side-by-side splits; each auto-detected in
206	                 the sidebar). --tab-per-agent → one tab per agent instead.
207	  tab "git"    — lazygit (falls back to `git status`)
208	  tab "edit"   — nvim
209	Idempotent: re-running in the same repo focuses the existing workspace.
210	Requires:  a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into one).
211	
212	Attach behavior: run from OUTSIDE herdr → attaches a client to the session so
213	the new workspace is visible; run from INSIDE herdr → just focuses it.
214	--no-attach builds in the background either way.
215	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: the current session
216	when inside herdr, else the default session). Start a session first with
217	`herdr --session NAME`.
218	
219	Two modes for choosing agents:
220	  Homogeneous:    hvibe 3 codex → 3 panes all codex
221	  Heterogeneous:  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode  (list length = panes)
222	
223	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
224	  antigravity / claude / codex / cursor / deepseek / droid / gemini
225	                                            → `specstory run <agent>`
226	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
227	
228	--on-exit MODE (per pane, on Ctrl+C / clean exit):
229	  shell (default) — drop to a shell with a re-run hint
230	  kill            — let the pane close
231	  restart         — auto-respawn in a loop
232	
233	--min-width COLS (default $HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80) auto-picks N when omitted:
234	  N = clamp(term_width / min-width, 1, 6)
235	$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER (seconds, default 0.25) delays each pane launch.
236	
237	Examples:
238	  hvibe                                       # auto N × claude
239	  hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× codex
240	  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
241	  hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
242	  hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude
243	EOF
244	                return 0 ;;
245	            -*)              echo "hvibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
246	            *)               break ;;
247	        esac
248	    done
249	
250	    if ! [[ "$min_width" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( min_width < 1 )); then
251	        echo "hvibe: --min-width must be a positive integer (got: $min_width)" >&2
252	        return 1
253	    fi
254	    if ! [[ "$launch_stagger" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
255	        echo "hvibe: HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER must be a non-negative number (got: $launch_stagger)" >&2
256	        return 1
257	    fi
258	
259	    local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"
260	
261	    # Build the agents array (same two paths as svibe; mixing is rejected).
262	    local -a agents
263	    agents=()
264	    if [ -n "$agents_csv" ]; then
265	        if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
266	            echo "hvibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
267	            return 1
268	        fi
269	        local tok
270	        while IFS= read -r tok; do
271	            tok="${tok## }"; tok="${tok%% }"
272	            [ -n "$tok" ] && agents+=( "$tok" )
273	        done < <(printf '%s\n' "$agents_csv" | tr ',' '\n')
274	        if [ "${#agents[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
275	            echo "hvibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
276	            return 1
277	        fi
278	    else
279	        if [ $# -gt 0 ] && [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
280	            n_agents="$1"; n_agents_set=1; shift
281	        fi
282	        [ $# -gt 0 ] && agent_cli="$1"
283	        # Auto-pick N from terminal width. Clamp [1,6] (lower than svibe's 12:
284	        # herdr right-splits nest, so many panes get cramped — use
285	        # --tab-per-agent for more).
286	        if [ "$n_agents_set" -eq 0 ]; then
287	            n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
288	            (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
289	            (( n_agents > 6 )) && n_agents=6
290	        fi
291	        local k
292	        for (( k = 0; k < n_agents; k++ )); do agents+=( "$agent_cli" ); done
293	    fi
294	
295	    case "$on_exit" in
296	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
297	        *) echo "hvibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
298	    esac
299	
300	    # Resolve git root (required, like svibe). `-p DIR` is absolutized first so
301	    # a bad path reports itself instead of masquerading as "not a git repo".
302	    local repo_root
303	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
304	        target=$(_herdr_abs_dir "$target" hvibe) || return 1
305	        repo_root=$(cd -- "$target" >/dev/null 2>&1 && _sesh_git_root)
306	    else
307	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
308	    fi
309	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
310	        echo "hvibe: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo." >&2
311	        return 1
312	    fi
313	
314	    # Fail-fast: every agent CLI must exist in PATH.
315	    local a missing=""
316	    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
317	        command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing $a"
318	    done
319	    if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
320	        echo "hvibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH:$missing" >&2
321	        echo "       Available: claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini (install as needed)." >&2
322	        return 1
323	    fi
324	
325	    local repo label
326	    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
327	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/$repo")
328	
329	    # Resolve the target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
330	    # A non-empty sess_sock means an explicit --session override — scope it with
331	    # `local -x` so child `herdr` calls see it but the user's shell is untouched.
332	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
333	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
334	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
335	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
336	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
337	
338	    # Idempotent: focus an existing workspace instead of duplicating.
339	    local existing
340	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
341	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
342	        echo "hvibe: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
343	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
344	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
345	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
346	        fi
347	        return 0
348	    fi
349	
350	    # Create the workspace; capture the initial pane/tab (become the first agent).
351	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
352	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
353	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
354	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
355	    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')
356	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ] || [ -z "$t0" ]; then
357	        echo "hvibe: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
358	        return 1
359	    fi
360	
361	    local first_agent="${agents[@]:0:1}"
362	    if [ "$tab_per_agent" -eq 1 ]; then
363	        # One tab per agent. Initial tab hosts the first agent (labeled by it).
364	        herdr tab rename "$t0" "$first_agent" >/dev/null 2>&1
365	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
366	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
367	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
368	            _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" "$a" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")"
369	        done
370	    else
371	        # Side-by-side splits in one "agents" tab. Thread `prev` so each new pane
372	        # splits off the previous one → predictable left-to-right columns.
373	        herdr tab rename "$t0" agents >/dev/null 2>&1
374	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
375	        # Even columns: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so set each
376	        # split's ratio explicitly. --ratio is the fraction KEPT by the pane
377	        # being split (the left one); the new pane gets the rest. Splitting the
378	        # rightmost pane on step m (of N-1) with ratio 1/(N-m+1) leaves every
379	        # finalized column at 1/N width.
380	        local n_total="${#agents[@]}" prev="$p0" np m=1 ratio
381	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
382	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
383	            ratio=$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.4f\", 1/($n_total-$m+1)}")
384	            np=$(herdr pane split "$prev" --direction right --ratio "$ratio" --cwd "$repo_root" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
385	                | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
386	            if [ -n "$np" ]; then
387	                herdr pane run "$np" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
388	                prev="$np"
389	            fi
390	            m=$((m+1))
391	        done
392	    fi
393	
394	    # git + edit tabs (same on-exit treatment as the agents).
395	    local git_inner git_label
396	    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then git_inner="lazygit"; else git_inner="git status"; fi
397	    git_label="${git_inner%% *}"
398	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" git  "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$git_inner" "$on_exit" "$git_label")"
399	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" edit "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")"
400	
401	    # Focus the workspace + agents tab unless --no-attach.
402	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
403	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
404	        herdr tab focus "$t0" >/dev/null 2>&1
405	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
406	    fi
407	}
408	
409	# ── hcode: repo-scoped single-agent layout ──────────────────────────────────
410	#
411	# herdr analog of `scode`. Workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
412	#   tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
413	#   tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top fallback)
414	# Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
415	#
416	# Usage:
417	#   hcode                     # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
418	#   hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
419	#   hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
420	#   hcode --no-specstory claude
421	#   hcode --on-exit kill claude
422	#   hcode -p ~/work/foo
423	function herdr-code() {
424	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hcode: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
425	
426	    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto" session_arg=""
427	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
428	        case "$1" in
429	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
430	            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
431	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
432	            --session)      session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
433	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
434	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
435	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
436	            --agents)
437	                echo "hcode: --agents is hvibe-only (hcode is single-agent)." >&2
438	                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: hvibe --agents '$2'" >&2
439	                return 1 ;;
440	            -h|--help)
441	                cat <<'EOF'
442	hcode — herdr single-agent coding layout (herdr analog of scode)
443	
444	Usage: hcode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
445	             [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [AGENT]
446	
447	Builds a new herdr workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
448	  tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
449	  tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top)
450	Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
451	
452	Attach behavior: run from OUTSIDE herdr → attaches a client to the session;
453	run from INSIDE herdr → just focuses. --no-attach builds in the background.
454	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: current session when
455	inside herdr, else the default session; start one with `herdr --session NAME`).
456	
457	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
458	  antigravity / claude / codex / cursor / deepseek / droid / gemini
459	                                            → `specstory run <agent>`
460	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
461	
462	--on-exit MODE (per pane): shell (default) | kill | restart
463	
464	Examples:
465	  hcode                     # default agent (specstory → claude)
466	  hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
467	  hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
468	  hcode --on-exit kill claude
469	EOF
470	                return 0 ;;
471	            -*)             echo "hcode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
472	            *)              [ -z "$agent" ] && agent="$1"; shift ;;
473	        esac
474	    done
475	
476	    case "$on_exit" in
477	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
478	        *) echo "hcode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
479	    esac
480	
481	    local repo_root
482	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
483	        target=$(_herdr_abs_dir "$target" hcode) || return 1
484	        repo_root=$(cd -- "$target" >/dev/null 2>&1 && _sesh_git_root)
485	    else
486	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
487	    fi
488	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
489	        echo "hcode: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or use hvibe in any dir." >&2
490	        return 1
491	    fi
492	
493	    if [ -n "$agent" ] && ! command -v "$agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
494	        echo "hcode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
495	        return 1
496	    fi
497	
498	    local repo label
499	    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
500	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/$repo")
501	
502	    # Resolve target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
503	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
504	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
505	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
506	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
507	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
508	
509	    local existing
510	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
511	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
512	        echo "hcode: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
513	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
514	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
515	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
516	        fi
517	        return 0
518	    fi
519	
520	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
521	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
522	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
523	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')

557	# ── hhere: plain "open a workspace here + attach" ────────────────────────────

561	# attach a client when run from outside herdr. NO git requirement and NO agent
562	# layout — just a shell in the workspace root pane. This fills the gap where

565	# layer, so without this you'd launch herdr, create a space (opens at $HOME),
566	# then cd manually.
567	#

570	#   hhere npm run dev              # bare args → run as the root-pane command

572	#   hhere -p ~/proj                # explicit path, plain shell

578	#

580	# treatment stays with hcode/hvibe; hhere is deliberately lightweight.
581	#
582	# Idempotent per label (bare basename of the dir, matching herdr's own native
583	# auto-label convention). Caveat: herdr auto-relabels a workspace to the root
584	# pane's LIVE cwd basename after a `cd` in tab 1 (see docs/tools/herdr.md § cwd
585	# & workspace-naming), so the reuse is best-effort — if the label has drifted, a
586	# re-run creates a fresh workspace (arguably correct: you're elsewhere now).
587	#
588	# Usage:
589	#   hhere [--path DIR] [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
590	function herdr-here() {
591	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hhere: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }

602	hhere — open a plain herdr workspace here + attach (herdr analog of shere)
603	
604	Usage: hhere [--path DIR] [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
605	
606	Creates a herdr workspace at DIR (default $PWD), focuses it, and — when run
607	from OUTSIDE herdr — attaches a client so it is visible. No git repo required
608	and no agent layout: just a shell in the workspace root pane. For agent
609	layouts use hcode (single-agent) or hvibe (multi-agent).
610	
611	Smart argument handling:
612	  hhere                        # plain shell at $PWD
613	  hhere npm run dev            # bare args → run as the root-pane command
614	  hhere -c "npm run dev"       # explicit --command flag
615	  hhere -p ~/proj              # explicit path, plain shell
616	  hhere -p ../sibling          # relative paths resolve against YOUR shell
617	  hhere -p ~/proj npm run dev  # explicit path + command
618	
619	--path DIR is resolved (and symlink-canonicalized) here, in your shell, before
620	it reaches herdr — a DIR that does not exist is a hard error, not a silent

628	                return 0 ;;

673	    [ -n "$cmd" ] && herdr pane run "$p0" "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1

677	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"

679	}

681	# ── hroot: like hhere but at the git-root ────────────────────────────────────
682	#
683	# herdr analog of `sroot` (sesh-root). Same as hhere except the target resolves
684	# to the current git top-level (falls back to $PWD outside a repo). Thin wrapper
685	# over herdr-here so there is one code path; -p is not accepted (the root IS the
686	# path), everything else (-c / bare command / --session / --no-attach) passes

688	#
689	# Usage:
690	#   hroot                          # plain shell at git-root (else $PWD)
691	#   hroot npm run dev              # + run a command
692	#   hroot -c "npm run dev"         # explicit --command flag
693	function herdr-root() {
694	    case "$1" in
695	        -h|--help)
696	            cat <<'EOF'
697	hroot — open a plain herdr workspace at the git-root + attach (analog of sroot)
698	
699	Usage: hroot [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
700	
701	Like hhere, but the workspace opens at the current git top-level (falls back to
702	$PWD outside a repo). All flags except --path pass through to hhere.
703	
704	  hroot                # plain shell at git-root (else $PWD)
705	  hroot npm run dev    # + run a command
706	EOF
707	            return 0 ;;
708	        -p|--path)
709	            echo "hroot: --path is not accepted (root is derived from git). Use hhere -p DIR." >&2

712	    local root
713	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
714	    herdr-here -p "$root" "$@"

717	# ── Review-pending flag (mark-unread / ⭐) ───────────────────────────────────

21	# ── Manual marker cleanup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
22	#
23	# The `working` (🤖) status workmux sets is *sticky* — it never auto-clears
24	# on its own. `waiting` (💬) and `done` (✅) auto-clear when you focus the
25	# window, but `working` only goes away when:
26	#   1. The agent's plugin/hook explicitly calls `workmux set-window-status done`
27	#      (Claude Stop / OpenCode session.idle), OR
28	#   2. `workmux sidebar` is running and detects 10s of pane silence
29	#      (interrupted-agent detection), OR
30	#   3. You manually clear it.
31	#
32	# Path #1 fails when the agent is killed before its Stop/idle handler fires
33	# (Ctrl+C, terminal crash, OOM). Path #2 requires keeping a sidebar pane open.
34	# `wmclear` is the manual escape hatch.
35	#
36	# Without arg: clears the marker for the current tmux window.
37	# With arg:    `wmclear 5` clears window 5 in the current session.
38	# Pass `--all` to nuke every workmux marker in the current session.
39	function wmclear() {
40	    if [[ "$1" == "--all" ]]; then
41	        # Walk every window in the current session and unset the user-var.
42	        # Original zsh code used `windows=("${(@f)$(...)}")` to split command
43	        # output on newlines; the `while IFS= read -r` loop below is the
44	        # portable equivalent (works in bash + zsh).
45	        local sess
46	        sess=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
47	        local -a windows
48	        windows=()
49	        local w
50	        while IFS= read -r w; do
51	            [ -n "$w" ] && windows+=( "$w" )
52	        done < <(tmux list-windows -t "$sess" -F '#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null)
53	        for w in "${windows[@]}"; do
54	            tmux set-option -w -t "${sess}:${w}" -u '@workmux_status' 2>/dev/null
55	        done
56	        echo "Cleared @workmux_status on ${#windows[@]} windows in session $sess"
57	        return 0
58	    fi
59	
60	    if [[ -n "$1" ]]; then
61	        # Specific window: use workmux's own clear command (handles agent
62	        # state too, not just the tmux user-var)
63	        local sess win
64	        sess=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
65	        win="$1"
66	        tmux set-option -w -t "${sess}:${win}" -u '@workmux_status' 2>/dev/null
67	        echo "Cleared @workmux_status on ${sess}:${win}"
68	        return 0
69	    fi
70	
71	    # Current window: prefer workmux's clear so it also resets agent state
72	    workmux set-window-status clear 2>/dev/null
73	}

75	# ── Sidebar daemon convenience ─────────────────────────────────────────────

98	# OMB's autosuggestions / syntax-highlighting / history-substring-search
99	# plugins are excluded in dot_config/bash/01_omb_plugins.bash because
100	# ble.sh provides better native versions.
101	# Presence-gated so plain-bash (no OMB installed) still works.
102	if [ -r "$HOME/.oh-my-bash/oh-my-bash.sh" ]; then
103	    export OSH="$HOME/.oh-my-bash"
104	    : "${OSH_THEME:=""}"  # empty = no OMB theme; starship takes over
105	    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
106	    source "$OSH/oh-my-bash.sh"
107	fi
108	
109	# 7. ============================================================
110	# Shared POSIX layer — env vars (PATH, GFW mirrors, GOPATH, BUN_INSTALL,
111	# PNPM_HOME), tool init wrappers (starship/mise/zoxide/direnv/thefuck),
112	# POSIX aliases. Same dir is sourced by ~/.zshrc.
113	# starship init bash is here, AFTER ble.sh source but BEFORE ble-attach.
114	load_modular_dir "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell" sh
115	
116	# 8. ============================================================
117	# atuin (history sync) — `--disable-up-arrow` is mandatory when
118	# ble.sh is loaded; ble.sh's history navigation owns the up arrow.
119	# Ctrl+R still opens atuin's TUI (no conflict).
120	# Alt+R is also bound to atuin via dot_config/shell/15_atuin.sh
121	# (cross-shell parity with zsh; deferred-bind via PROMPT_COMMAND
122	# because __atuin_history is defined by THIS init below, after
123	# 15_atuin.sh has already been sourced by load_modular_dir).
124	if command -v atuin >/dev/null 2>&1; then
125	    eval "$(atuin init bash --disable-up-arrow)"
126	fi
127	
128	# 9. ============================================================
129	# Load secrets (not tracked by chezmoi). Two-layer pattern mirrors zsh:
130	#   9a. ~/.shellrc.secrets — shared POSIX layer, sourced by BOTH shells.
131	#       Canonical home for API keys / tokens that both shells need.
132	#   9b. ~/.config/bash/secrets.sh — bash-only secrets, layered on top so
133	#       it can use bash-only syntax and overrides shared on conflict.
134	# Both run BEFORE ble-attach so vars are available to ble.sh / starship.
```

Idempotent per dir-basename. `-p DIR` is absolutized in-shell (relative paths OK; a non-directory is a hard error — herdr resolves a relative `--cwd` server-side and would silently open `$HOME`). 7	#   Ctrl+/     toggle preview panel (shows tldr or --help)
8	#
9	# The invocation for tools that need arguments has a trailing space,
10	# so pressing Enter pastes e.g. "rg " — cursor lands after the space,
11	# ready for you to type your arguments.
12	
13	_TOOLS_DOC="${HOME}/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md"
14	
15	# Bail silently if the data file hasn't been deployed yet or fzf is missing
16	[[ -f "$_TOOLS_DOC" ]] || return 0

18	
19	# Parse the markdown tables into "INVOCATION<TAB>DESCRIPTION" lines.
20	# Tab separator preserves the trailing space in invocations like "rg ".
21	_tools_list() {
22	    awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
23	      inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
24	      desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/,"",desc)
25	      printf "%s\t%s\n", inv, desc
26	    }' "$_TOOLS_DOC"
27	}
28	
29	# ZLE widget: opens fzf picker, pastes selected invocation to the shell command line.
30	tools-picker() {
31	    {
32	        exec </dev/tty
33	        exec <&1
34	
35	        local selected

37	            _tools_list | fzf \
38	                --ansi \
39	                --border \
40	                --prompt ' tools  ' \
41	                --header 'Enter: paste  Ctrl+E: execute  Ctrl+/: preview' \
42	                --delimiter=$'\t' \
43	                --with-nth=1,2 \
44	                --preview 'tool=$(printf "%s" {1} | awk "{print \$1}" | sed "s/ *$//"); (command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1 && tldr "$tool" 2>/dev/null) || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50' \
45	                --preview-window='right:55%:wrap:hidden' \
46	                --bind='ctrl-/:toggle-preview' \
47	                --bind='ctrl-e:execute(eval $(printf "%s" {1} | awk "{print \$1}"))+abort'
48	        )
49

52	
53	        # Extract the invocation (field 1 before the tab), preserving trailing space

# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared (expose localhost to the **public** internet).
- **Tailscale** — WireGuard mesh VPN (tailnet-only, the opposite of the tunnel tools). Helper CLI: `tsnet`. Picker: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`, `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`.
- **Agent sounds** — audio notifications on agent Stop/Notification hooks. See `docs/tools/agent-sounds.md`.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
- **`agent-warmup`** — Tyro CLI that drives a real interactive Claude TUI at a scheduled time through an existing Herdr session (preferred) or tmux, with uv-first daemon bootstrap and safe fallback. See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
- **`raid-perm-check`** — read-only auditor for a group+ACL-shared data mount (`summary`/`orphans`/`groups`/`units`/`user`/`all`, default `/mnt/raid`). Catches the two silent breakages: orphaned uid/gid after an account is deleted, and a stale `systemd --user` manager whose frozen groups make timers hit EACCES on paths your shell reads fine. Never modifies — prints the fix. See `docs/sysadmin/shared-storage-permissions.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`ytmv`** — download YouTube music videos for **old MP3 players**: mp3 + sidecar `.lrc` + ID3v2.3/USLT lyrics, or mp4 with soft/burned-in subtitles. Subcommands `get` / `lyrics` / `tag` / `doctor`; `ytmv help` is the complete setup/cookie-safety guide and `doctor --cookies` explicitly tests a configured source. Public downloads use packaged EJS + managed Node 22+ cookie-free first (doctor flags legacy Node 20/16). Compatibility profiles (`safe`, `cjk-big5`, `cjk-gbk`, `ipod`, `modern`) are re-appliable offline via `ytmv tag`. Needs ffmpeg (`installMediaTools`); `--burn-subs` needs the keg-only `ffmpeg-full`. No `tv` channel by design. See `docs/tools/ytmv.md`.
- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
- **`herdr-grep`** — search visible or retained content across panes in the current, one named, or all running local Herdr sessions; reports exact session/workspace/tab/pane coordinates, supports `--json`, and `--pick` pipes matches to fzf then exact-focuses/attaches the selection. Inside Herdr, `prefix+Alt+F` opens a visible-content picker (Alt+S = scrollback, Alt+V = visible). Remote use runs the CLI through SSH. See `docs/tools/herdr.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, binary-matched global skill from `herdr --skill`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with three metadata pickers (`tv herdr-agent-panes`, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`) plus `herdr-grep` for pane-content search. See `docs/tools/herdr.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~50 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `tailnet`, `ssh-config`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`,
`kill-process`, `services`, `sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`,
`mac-apps`/`linux-apps`, the agent trio (`agent-panes`, `agent-sessions`,
`agent-wakeup`, dual tmux/Herdr with stable agent-session scheduling) and the `herdr-*` family. Full reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` opens the action menu. There is **no `prefix + e`** —
  that alias was removed, and `prefix + E` is "break every pane into its own
  window", so do not guess it. `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools.
  Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end smoke test: drives the real binary through a full task lifecycle
3	# in a throwaway HOME, with the runtime backend pinned to "none" so no
4	# multiplexer is touched.
5	set -euo pipefail
6	
7	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
8	BIN="${BIN:-$ROOT/dev}"
9	
10	# Always rebuild. The Go build cache makes this nearly free, and testing a
11	# stale binary against fresh assertions is worse than not testing at all.
12	echo "building $BIN"
13	(cd "$ROOT" && go build -o "$BIN" ./cmd/dev)
14	
15	SANDBOX="$(mktemp -d)"
16	trap 'rm -rf "$SANDBOX"' EXIT
17	
18	export HOME="$SANDBOX/home"
19	export XDG_DATA_HOME="$HOME/.local/share"
20	export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"
21	mkdir -p "$HOME/Program"
22	
23	# A local "remote" so the push and cold-park paths are exercised for real.
24	git init --bare --quiet --initial-branch=main "$SANDBOX/origin.git"
25	
26	cat > "$SANDBOX/config.toml" <<CONFIG
27	[paths]
28	scan_roots    = ["$HOME/Program"]
29	project_root  = "$HOME/Program"
30	tries_root    = "$HOME/tries"
31	worktree_root = "$HOME/Worktrees"
32	state_dir     = "$HOME/state"
33	
34	[runtime]
35	backend = "none"
36	
37	[worktree]
38	include     = [".env"]
39	post_create = []
40	CONFIG
41	
42	dev() { "$BIN" --config "$SANDBOX/config.toml" "$@"; }
43	
44	step() { printf '\n\033[1m▸ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
45	fail() { printf '\033[31m✗ %s\033[0m\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
46	ok()   { printf '  \033[32m✓\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
47	
48	step "doctor"
49	dev doctor
50	
51	step "create a repo with a gitignored env file"
52	REPO="$HOME/Program/demo"
53	git init --quiet --initial-branch=main "$REPO"
54	git -C "$REPO" config user.email dev@example.test
55	git -C "$REPO" config user.name  "dev e2e"
56	printf '# demo\n'  > "$REPO/README.md"
57	printf '.env\n'    > "$REPO/.gitignore"

 `./README.md`

```text
1	# dev
2	
3	A thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
4	
5	It exists to stop four things collapsing into one:
6	
7	```
8	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
9	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
10	herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
11	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
12	```
13	
14	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
15	only what git cannot answer — a task's **state**, **owner** and **next
16	action** — as one TOML file per task.
17	
18	## The problem
19	
20	When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
21	working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
22	So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
23	defeats the point of having one.
24	
25	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
26	the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
27	
28	Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
29	the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
30	expected.
31	
32	```
33	$ dev ls
34	   TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
35	🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
36	🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
37	❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
38	```
39	
40	## Install
41	
42	```bash
43	make install     # builds, installs to ~/.local/bin, installs the agent skill
44	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
45	```
46	
47	Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
48	
49	```bash
50	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
51	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
52	```
53	
54	The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
55	working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
56	directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
57	
58	```bash
59	dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
60	```
61	
62	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
63	degrade cleanly when absent.
64	
65	## The lifecycle
66	
67	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
70	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
71	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
72	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
73	
74	```bash
75	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
76	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
77	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
78	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
79	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
80	dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
81	```
82	
83	### A task does not have to mean a worktree
84	
85	Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
86	
87	```bash
88	# No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
89	dev repo open api
90	
91	# Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
92	dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct
93	
94	# Use a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout, but no linked worktree.
95	dev start api --task "small feature" --branch-only --base main
96	
97	# Default: independent branch + worktree, provisioned and runtime-opened.
98	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
99	```
100	
101	Direct work can be parked WARM and resumed, but cannot go COLD because the
102	canonical checkout cannot be removed. `dev done` on a clean direct task needs
103	no `--ff` or `--pr`: the work is already on its destination branch.
104	
105	Start direct for one change stream, then create a normal worktree task later
106	when real parallelism appears. A new worktree starts from committed HEAD; dirty
107	main changes are deliberately not smuggled into it, so checkpoint first when
108	the parallel task depends on them.
109	
110	### The dashboard
111	
112	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens three lists, switched with `tab`:
113	
114	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
115	- **REPOS** — every repository under the scan roots, with its branch, dirty
116	  state, worktree count and per-state task tally, sorted so anything in flight
117	  is at the top. What do I have here.
118	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through the authenticated `gh` and `glab`
119	  CLIs, marked when a local clone exists. What can I open or clone.
120	
121	TASKS and REPOS come from the same code paths as `dev ls` and `dev repo list`,
122	so they cannot disagree. The repo list matters on day one: with forty repositories and
123	no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just be empty.
124	
125	Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
126	
127	```
128	j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
129	g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
130	/          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
131	```
132	
133	`enter` opens the selected row in the runtime. In TASKS, `p` parks and prompts
134	for the next action and `c` edits it. In REPOS, `enter` is pure ad-hoc open,
135	`s` starts an isolated worktree task, and `d` starts a tracked direct task on
136	the current branch. That makes the branch/worktree cost an explicit choice,
137	not something every task silently pays.
138	
139	**External tools are configured, not fixed.** They run through your shell in
140	the selected row's checkout; the dashboard suspends and redraws when they exit:
141	
142	```toml
143	[[tui.tools]]
144	key  = "L"
145	name = "lazygit"
146	run  = "lazygit"
147	
148	[[tui.tools]]
149	key  = "V"
150	name = "nvim"
151	run  = "nvim ."
152	
153	[[tui.tools]]
154	key  = "B"
155	name = "vibe"
156	run  = "vibe"
157	interactive = true     # load + evaluate aliases/functions after shell rc
158	
159	[[tui.tools]]
160	key  = "P"
161	name = "plans here"
162	run  = "claude-plans-here"
163	interactive = true
164	```
165	
166	`dev config init` writes the defaults out in full rather than leaving them
167	implicit, and `dev tui tools` shows what is bound here and whether each one is
168	actually installed — bindings for missing programs are not offered. A tool
169	cannot take a key the dashboard already uses; dev reports the clash on load.
170	
171	REMOTE loads lazily, so dashboard startup never waits on the network. A private
172	15-minute XDG cache makes later switches instant; `r` refreshes both forges.
173	`/` searches provider, owner/name and description; enter opens a local clone,
174	and `c` confirms before cloning an absent repo into `project_root`. The same
175	inventory is available without the full-screen UI via `dev repo remote [query]`;
176	`--cached` is its instant/offline form.
177	REPOS has an explicit LIVE column (`herdr:working`, `herdr:idle`, …); its
178	detail pane includes the workspace handle. `H` opens the selected repo's
179	one-year activity heatmap and `e` edits config. Returning from the editor, or
180	pressing `r`, reparses config and reloads data/tool bindings without restarting
181	the TUI; a runtime-backend change is reported as requiring restart.
182	
183	REPOS includes `LATEST`, defined as the newest dirty-file mtime, commit time, or
184	task update. Columns and default ordering are config:
185	
186	```toml
187	[tui.repos]
188	columns = ["repo", "branch", "git", "live", "latest", "worktrees", "tasks"]
189	sort = "activity"       # activity | latest | name | git | tasks
190	reverse = false
191	```
192	
193	In REPOS, `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses it. The configured order returns on
194	reload. Local repo probes run with bounded parallelism, and the alternate screen
195	appears before they finish; the measured serial 56-repo path was ~4.2s, while
196	startup now immediately shows loading and fills rows in the background.
197	
198	See `dev help tui` for the full key map.
199	
200	Going cold is safe because **the branch is the identity and the directory is a
201	cache**. `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, and `dev resume`
202	rebuilds the checkout from `origin/<branch>`. Once that holds, the local
203	filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished worktrees.
204	
205	## Rich Git state
206	
207	Every inventory surface uses the same compact, starship-like status:
208	
209	```text
210	⇕⇡3⇣2 =1 +4 !2 ?3
211	```
212	
213	- `⇡` / `⇣` / `⇕` — ahead, behind, diverged
214	- `=` — conflicted paths
215	- `+` — staged paths
216	- `!` — unstaged paths
217	- `?` — untracked paths
218	
219	`dev status` and the TUI detail pane also show the unique changed-path total
220	and type breakdown (added / modified / deleted / renamed). A path staged and
221	then modified again is one changed path, while correctly appearing in both the
222	staged and unstaged categories. JSON output exposes all counts separately.
223	
224	## Worktree ownership
225	
226	Three mechanisms create git worktrees. `dev` takes one position so nobody has
227	to improvise:
228	
229	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
230	|---|---|---|---|
231	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until `dev done` / `dev sweep` |
232	| Turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | dies with the turn |
233	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add`, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
234	
235	**Might you come back tomorrow → `dev`. Dies with this agent turn → Claude
236	Code native.**
237	
238	`dev` does not delegate placement to herdr because the path policy has to hold
239	on machines without herdr. It creates the checkout with plain git and asks
240	herdr only to *open* it — which still surfaces it in the sidebar grouped under
241	its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
242	
243	`dev` refuses to create a worktree inside a repository: a checkout nested in
244	another checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second
245	copy of the tree.
246	
247	### Provisioning
248	
249	A worktree is a clean checkout — no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`.
250	Without provisioning, every new one starts broken. `dev` copies the gitignored
251	files you list, optionally symlinks heavy directories, and runs a setup
252	command detected from the lockfiles:
253	
254	```toml
255	[worktree]
256	include     = [".env", ".env.local"]   # only files that are ALSO gitignored
257	link        = []                       # opt-in; sharing node_modules is risky
258	post_create = "auto"                   # uv.lock → uv sync, package-lock.json → npm ci, …
259	```
260	
261	**Copy or reinstall?** Reinstalling is always correct but can take minutes;
262	copying is fast but only sound for dependency trees carrying no absolute paths.
263	That is a per-ecosystem fact, not a preference, so dev knows it:
264	
265	```toml
266	[worktree]
267	strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip
268	
269	[worktree.strategies]
270	node = "copy"               # node_modules copies soundly
271	```
272	
273	Asking to copy a virtualenv is refused with the reason — it bakes its own
274	absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg` and `bin/activate` — and narrowed back to
275	reinstalling rather than silently producing a broken checkout.
276	
277	`dev wt plan` shows exactly what a new worktree of a repository would get:
278	which project types were detected, which tools are missing, and every file and
279	command involved. `dev wt plan --write` seeds a `<repo>/.dev.toml` from it, so
280	a project can commit its own setup and every machine provisions the same way.
281	
282	```
283	$ dev wt plan
284	PROJECT  MANAGER  FROM               DEPENDENCIES  TOOL
285	node     npm      package-lock.json  node_modules  installed
286	python   uv       uv.lock            .venv         installed
287	
288	   ACTION    WHAT          WHY
289	✓  copy      .env          gitignored, so the checkout would not have it
290	✓  copy-dir  node_modules  npm dependencies, copied instead of reinstalling
291	✓  run       uv sync       uv.lock detected
292	```
293	
294	## Other things it does
295	
296	```bash
297	dev repo list                  # every repo under the scan roots, with status
298	dev repo clone owner/name -c Web   # clone into the right place, via gh or glab
299	dev repo sync --all            # fetch + prune, and report what moved
300	
301	dev try redis-streams          # dated scratch directory for an experiment
302	dev graduate redis-streams -c Infra --remote   # promote it into a real project
303	
304	dev gitignore                  # .gitignore from GitHub's templates + the rest
305	dev adopt                      # import existing worktrees/sessions as tasks
306	
307	dev stats --heatmap            # where the time actually went
308	dev help worktrees             # quick-reference pages for the workflow
309	```
310	
311	`dev stats` draws a contribution-style heatmap from two sources: a sampler
312	watching live agent sessions (the only way to count time spent reading and
313	debugging), and git history (which backfills the past and survives losing the
314	database). WakaTime can be imported alongside for editor time.
315	
316	```bash
317	dev stats backfill                          # seed all repos from git history
318	dev stats backfill --repo api               # seed only one repo
319	dev stats sample --interval 5m              # from cron, every five minutes
320	dev stats import-wakatime                   # optional
321	dev stats path                              # durable SQLite location
322	dev stats clear --repo api                  # guarded selective deletion
323	```
324	
325	In the TUI, select a repo and press `H`. If it has no data, `b` backfills only
326	that repo and refreshes the panel; `r` merely rereads existing stats data.
327	
328	Stats are **data**, not cache: session samples and WakaTime imports may not be
329	reconstructible. They live at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and clearing them
330	requires a scope plus confirmation (`--repo`, `--source`, or `--all`).
331	Regenerable data lives separately:
332	
333	```bash
334	dev cache list
335	dev cache path
336	dev cache clear remote
337	dev cache clear gitignore
338	dev cache clear all
339	```
340	
341	Those remove only `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/{remotes.json,gitignore/}` and never touch
342	`stats.db`.
343	
344	## Bootstrapping an existing machine
345	
346	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use: `dev` discovers repositories
347	wherever `scan_roots` point and never requires a particular physical layout.
348	When you want a recursive audit or a curated navigation layer, bootstrap is the
349	explicit path:
350	
351	```bash
352	dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work                    # recursive report, no changes
353	dev bootstrap ~/code --json                       # machine-readable inventory
354	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects           # plan a flat symlink catalog
355	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --apply   # create only the ready links
356	dev bootstrap ~/old --move ~/Projects             # plan physical moves
357	```
358	
359	The scanner classifies canonical checkouts, linked worktrees, bare repositories
360	and symlink aliases, deduplicating by Git common-directory identity rather than
361	path.
362	
363	**A symlink index is the default recommendation.** It gives a flat,
364	metadata-aware navigation root while every physical repository stays exactly
365	where it was. Put the index first in `scan_roots` and that alias becomes the UI;
366	normal discovery follows direct repo symlinks and deduplicates index + physical
367	paths.
368	
369	Physical move exists, but refuses dirty repos, linked worktrees anywhere in the
370	clone, live sessions, a current shell inside, aliases that would break,
371	occupied destinations and cross-filesystem renames. A plan with any blocked row
372	moves nothing. `--config-out` writes a fresh config for the resulting root
373	without silently rewriting the user's current one. See `dev help bootstrap`.
374	
375	## Adopting work in flight
376	
377	There is nothing to migrate. `dev` discovers repositories wherever your scan
378	roots point and **never moves, renames or deletes anything** you already have.
379	`dev config init` probes the conventional locations — `~/Documents/Program`,
380	`~/src`, `~/code`, a `GHQ_ROOT`, and so on — counts the repositories in each,
381	and writes only the ones that exist:
382	
383	```
384	$ dev config init
385	wrote ~/.config/dev/config.toml
386	
387	Detected:
388	ROOT                 REPOS  ROLE
389	~/Documents/Program  40     scan root, new projects land here
390	~/src                16     scan root
391	```
392	
393	Repositories are discovered; *tasks* are not. `dev adopt` finds the work
394	already in flight — linked worktrees from any tool, live runtime sessions, and
395	local branches ahead of the default branch — and offers to record it. It skips
396	branches already merged, and the turn-scoped worktrees an agent harness cleans
397	up itself:
398	
399	```bash
400	dev adopt            # report only
401	dev adopt --apply    # record as tasks; nothing on disk changes
402	```
403	
404	A worktree you already have somewhere else keeps working exactly as it did —
405	`dev` records the path git reports rather than relocating it. Full detail in
406	`dev help adopting`.
407	
408	## .gitignore
409	
410	```bash
411	dev gitignore                 # detect the languages from the repo's files
412	dev gitignore python node     # or say so explicitly
413	dev gitignore --offline       # cached and bundled templates only
414	```
415	
416	Language sections come from [GitHub's templates](https://github.com/github/gitignore),
417	fetched once and cached. On top of those it adds what no language template
418	covers: the host platform's junk files, editor state, local env files, and the
419	directories coding-agent harnesses create — an agent's linked worktree left
420	untracked makes every `git status` in the main checkout unreadable.
421	
422	Everything it writes goes inside a delimited block, so re-running updates that
423	block and leaves rules you added by hand alone.
424	
425	## Configuration
426	
427	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml`. Write a commented starter with
428	`dev config init`; see the effective settings with `dev config show`; open the
429	actual file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` with either form:
430	
431	```bash
432	dev edit
433	dev config edit
434	DEV_EDITOR=unused dev edit --editor "code --wait"   # explicit override
435	```
436	
437	If the file does not exist, `edit` generates the machine-detected starter first
438	rather than opening an empty file. Resolution is `--editor` → `$VISUAL` →
439	`$EDITOR` → `nvim` → `vim` → `vi`.
440	
441	Every path is configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine —
442	a faster volume, a different naming convention:
443	
444	```toml
445	[paths]
446	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries"]
447	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
448	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
449	state_dir     = "~/.local/share/dev"        # point at a git repo to sync it
450	```
451	
452	Template variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`,
453	`host`, `date`. Filters: `|slug` (`feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`), `|lower`,
454	`|base`. A typo in a variable name fails at load, not as a directory literally
455	named `{{rep}}`.
456	
457	A flat project layout is already first-class — it needs no migration and no
458	special mode:
459	
460	```toml
461	[paths]
462	scan_roots   = ["~/code"]
463	project_root = "~/code"       # repo new/clone/graduate land at ~/code/<repo>
464	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/wt"
465	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}--{{branch|slug}}"
466	```
467	
468	Omit `--category` and canonical repos stay flat. Categories are metadata the
469	user may choose, never a directory structure dev imposes.
470	
471	## Multiple machines
472	
473	Do not sync worktrees or runtime state. Sync branches, and let the remote be
474	the handoff boundary:
475	
476	```bash
477	dev park --cold --push      # on the machine holding the work
478	dev resume <task> --fetch   # on the machine picking it up
479	```
480	
481	`dev` records an owner host per task and refuses to resume someone else's
482	without `--force`. Two machines committing to one branch is the reliable way
483	to produce a conflict here; the ownership check prevents it.
484	
485	For a cross-machine view, `dev ls --json` is a stable contract:
486	
487	```bash
488	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="hot")'
489	```
490	
491	## The agent skill
492	
493	`dev` ships the agent skill that documents it, embedded in the binary — the
494	same pattern `herdr --skill` uses. A skill vendored separately drifts from the
495	tool it describes, and an agent reading a stale command list is worse than one
496	reading none.
497	
498	```bash
499	dev skill install    # → ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills
500	dev --skill          # print it, for a dotfiles installer to sync
501	dev skill sync       # regenerate the command reference from the command tree
502	dev skill sync --check   # fail if it has drifted — wire into CI
503	```
504	
505	The skill defers to the companion `git-workflow` skill for commit conventions,
506	SemVer and branch naming rather than restating them. It owns what is new: the
507	worktree ownership rule, the task lifecycle, and how `dev` and herdr divide
508	responsibility.
509	
510	## Development
511	
512	```bash
513	make          # fmt, vet, test, build
514	make test
515	make e2e      # drives the real binary through a full lifecycle in a sandbox
516	make skill-check
517	```
518	
519	Tests build throwaway repositories under `t.TempDir()` via
520	`internal/gitx/gittest`, and the runtime adapters share one contract suite that
521	skips backends not installed on the machine — so the suite is meaningful in CI
522	(where only the null backend exists) and locally (where herdr and tmux do).
523
```
