```text
66	
67	## Chezmoi templating conventions
68	
69	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask whether the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` (`darwin`/`linux`) / `.chezmoi.arch` (`arm64`/`amd64`) / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for **user-role choices only**, and its values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts. `.profile` is still the right knob for desktop-vs-headless.
70	
71	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
72	
73	Predicate table, examples, the `macos_intel` migration: [chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
74	
75	## Hard repo invariants
76	
77	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
78	
79	YAML / TOML / JSON syntax and template rendering are not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (`codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is only a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
80	
81	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
82	
83	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
84	
85	**Hard rules**:
86	
87	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
88	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
89	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
90	
91	The ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be last before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions`/`syntax-highlighting`/`history-substring-search` MUST be excluded (double-init flicker). [bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
92	
93	### Three-tier user-local override layer
94	
95	User overrides live in **six** untracked files, all in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). Default target: shared; drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
96	
97	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl` — `managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc`. Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
98	
99	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
100	
101	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
102	
103	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templates + 2 first-seed files: [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
104	
105	**Hard rules**:
106	
107	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
108	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/`, `dot_config/opencode/`, `dot_cursor/`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
109	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
110	- The `minimal` bundle forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without an explicit request.
111	- New vim-touched file → follow the gate-it-or-not flow in [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md) → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table there.
112	
113	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
114	
115	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
116	
117	**Hard rules**:
118	
119	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
120	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
121	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a *single* tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it genuinely needs a newer one (`python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5`). It MUST detect the install style and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (silent no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors when it isn't a formula). The dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and the role. See [uv-bootstrap](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
122	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`, or the install guard short-circuits and entry-point shims are never written (silently missing `jupyter` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit command: [uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
123	- New upgrade category: [upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) § Adding a new category. Tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise → do nothing, generic `upgrade` picks it up.
124	- **Probe `brew` by output, never exit status** — `[[ -n "$(brew --prefix 2>/dev/null)" ]]`. A stub `brew` passes `command -v brew` and returns 0 with empty output for *every* subcommand: `brew bundle` silently installs nothing and `community.general.homebrew` dies on `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`. [ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md](pitfalls/ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md)
125	
126	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
127	
128	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
129	
130	**Hard rules**:
131	
132	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
133	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
134	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
135	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
136	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
137	
138	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**: `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top → set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag → `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"` and branch on its return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason` → run privileged commands via `sudo_run …` (or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible).
139	
140	For **non-interactive** injection (`scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH), `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (0600) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty` — **never** read that variable directly, always go through the helper. Full API + state + cleanup model: [sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
141	
142	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
143	
144	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
145	
146	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked; hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let the template win.
147	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (`chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`), so ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for those.
148	- **`--branch BRANCH` is a no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS your editor working tree): they warn and run against the working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
149	- **Install-only by design.** `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
150	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
151	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint; anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without an explicit request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
152	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse. `just fleet-status` is the **pre-flight readiness probe** (13 states; always exits 0 — use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates; `fleet-status-quick` skips the remote `git fetch`). `just fleet-apply-status` is a **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`, run during/after, pairing with `fleet-apply-tail`/`-watch`/`-kill`. State meanings incl. `toml-mismatch`: [fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md).
153	- **`fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving** (auto-seed / exit 0 with a hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
154	
155	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
156	
157	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes the current target contents to stdin and expects the new contents on stdout. Used wherever a *foreign writer* also owns part of the file — `~/.claude/settings.json`, editor `settings.json`, the agent CLI configs, `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`, `~/.gitconfig` (preserves the `[credential]` blocks `gh auth setup-git` injects). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it overwrites the script with the live file.
158	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches the contents after (`~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json`, editor `keybindings.json`). Refresh the baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"` — `chezmoi add` strips the prefix and `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
159	
160	Per-file case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). The three agent CLI overlays, incl. the Claude hook merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland) without ping-ponging: [agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
161	
162	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
163	
164	The popup menu (`prefix + Space` / `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two tmux quirks force that: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) instead of clamped — the `devtools` role auto-upgrades Debian/Ubuntu past it — and `display-menu` does **not** paginate, so a menu taller than the terminal is suppressed entirely, with no error anywhere.
165	
166	**Hard rules**:
167	
168	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
169	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
170	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
171	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
172	
173	Full story incl. the red herrings: `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`, `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
174	
175	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
176	
177	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
178	
179	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps. **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
180	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
181	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
182	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
183	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
184	
185	Full breakdown / themes / keybindings / troubleshooting: [](docs/tools/tmux/).
186	
187	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
188	
189	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` sets `default_mode "locked"` on purpose — all keys pass through to inner apps, `Ctrl+G` unlocks Zellij's own. Do **not** change it. Fresh box → pick the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" preset. [keyboard-shortcuts.md](docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)
190
```

```text
40	**Three-tier file placement** for new shell helpers:
41	
42	| Tier | Dir | When |

50	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
51	
52	The `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism spans **6 surfaces that must move together** — devtools install, `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml`, `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`, `dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl` hooks, `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` (+ its `modify_package.json`), and `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`'s producers API. Exact contents: [workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md) § Status icon mechanics; why it leaks: [workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md).
53	
54	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (writes parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears). The workmux hook entries are **unconditional** — the `agentSounds` prompt gates only the notify.sh / peon-ping entries in the same file. `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux) stay distinct tools.
55	
56	### Long-term backlog + past pitfalls → use the `project-knowledge-harness` skill
57	
58	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` agent skill (restored on every `chezmoi apply`; see [agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md)). **Load the skill** for the template and disambiguation table.
59	
60	**Fallback rules**, so this still binds when the skill can't be loaded:
61	
62	- Three repo-root surfaces, all chezmoi-ignored, all NOT auto-redacted: [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) (tags `P1`/`P2`/`P3`/`P?` × `S`/`M`/`L`/`XL`), [`backlog/`](backlog/README.md) (notes for `P?` / `[L]` / `[XL]` / multi-option), [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/README.md) (debugged traps — **title by symptom, not root cause**, verbatim error messages, never paraphrase).
63	- Capture triggers — future work: "maybe later", "nice to have", "工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來". Pitfalls: >~15 min debugging, not googleable, non-obvious fix, silent failure.
64	- Do **not** spawn `ROADMAP.md` / `IDEAS.md` / `LESSONS.md` / `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`. Three surfaces, always.
65	- A pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant below when it recurs across machines, silently corrupts state, or has a non-obvious workaround. Link back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md`.
66	
67	## Chezmoi templating conventions
68	
69	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask whether the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` (`darwin`/`linux`) / `.chezmoi.arch` (`arm64`/`amd64`) / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for **user-role choices only**, and its values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts. `.profile` is still the right knob for desktop-vs-headless.
70	
71	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
72	
73	Predicate table, examples, the `macos_intel` migration: [chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
74	
75	## Hard repo invariants
76	
77	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
78	
79	YAML / TOML / JSON syntax and template rendering are not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (`codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is only a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
80	
81	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
82	
83	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
84	
85	**Hard rules**:
86	
87	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
88	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
89	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
90	
91	The ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be last before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions`/`syntax-highlighting`/`history-substring-search` MUST be excluded (double-init flicker). [bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
92	
93	### Three-tier user-local override layer
94	
95	User overrides live in **six** untracked files, all in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). Default target: shared; drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
96	
97	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl` — `managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc`. Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
98	
99	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
100	
101	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
102	
103	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templates + 2 first-seed files: [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
104	
105	**Hard rules**:
106	
107	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
108	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/`, `dot_config/opencode/`, `dot_cursor/`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
109	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
110	- The `minimal` bundle forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without an explicit request.
111	- New vim-touched file → follow the gate-it-or-not flow in [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md) → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table there.
112	
113	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
114	
115	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
116	
117	**Hard rules**:
118	
119	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
120	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
121	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a *single* tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it genuinely needs a newer one (`python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5`). It MUST detect the install style and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (silent no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors when it isn't a formula). The dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and the role. See [uv-bootstrap](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
122	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`, or the install guard short-circuits and entry-point shims are never written (silently missing `jupyter` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit command: [uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
123	- New upgrade category: [upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) § Adding a new category. Tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise → do nothing, generic `upgrade` picks it up.
124	- **Probe `brew` by output, never exit status** — `[[ -n "$(brew --prefix 2>/dev/null)" ]]`. A stub `brew` passes `command -v brew` and returns 0 with empty output for *every* subcommand: `brew bundle` silently installs nothing and `community.general.homebrew` dies on `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`. [ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md](pitfalls/ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md)
125	
126	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
127	
128	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
129	
130	**Hard rules**:
131	
132	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
133	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
134	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
135	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
136	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
137	
138	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**: `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top → set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag → `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"` and branch on its return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason` → run privileged commands via `sudo_run …` (or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible).
139	
140	For **non-interactive** injection (`scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH), `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (0600) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty` — **never** read that variable directly, always go through the helper. Full API + state + cleanup model: [sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
141	
142	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
143	
144	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
145	
146	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked; hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let the template win.
147	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (`chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`), so ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for those.
148	- **`--branch BRANCH` is a no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS your editor working tree): they warn and run against the working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
149	- **Install-only by design.** `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
150	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
151	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint; anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without an explicit request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
152	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse. `just fleet-status` is the **pre-flight readiness probe** (13 states; always exits 0 — use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates; `fleet-status-quick` skips the remote `git fetch`). `just fleet-apply-status` is a **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`, run during/after, pairing with `fleet-apply-tail`/`-watch`/`-kill`. State meanings incl. `toml-mismatch`: [fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md).
153	- **`fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving** (auto-seed / exit 0 with a hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
154	
155	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
156	
157	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes the current target contents to stdin and expects the new contents on stdout. Used wherever a *foreign writer* also owns part of the file — `~/.claude/settings.json`, editor `settings.json`, the agent CLI configs, `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`, `~/.gitconfig` (preserves the `[credential]` blocks `gh auth setup-git` injects). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it overwrites the script with the live file.
158	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches the contents after (`~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json`, editor `keybindings.json`). Refresh the baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"` — `chezmoi add` strips the prefix and `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
159	
160	Per-file case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). The three agent CLI overlays, incl. the Claude hook merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland) without ping-ponging: [agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
161	
162	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
163	
164	The popup menu (`prefix + Space` / `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two tmux quirks force that: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) instead of clamped — the `devtools` role auto-upgrades Debian/Ubuntu past it — and `display-menu` does **not** paginate, so a menu taller than the terminal is suppressed entirely, with no error anywhere.
165	
166	**Hard rules**:
167	
168	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
169	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
170	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
171	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
172	
173	Full story incl. the red herrings: `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`, `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
174	
175	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
176	
177	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
178	
179	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps. **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
180	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
181	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
182	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
183	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
184	
185	Full breakdown / themes / keybindings / troubleshooting: [](docs/tools/tmux/).
186	
187	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
188	
189	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` sets `default_mode "locked"` on purpose — all keys pass through to inner apps, `Ctrl+G` unlocks Zellij's own. Do **not** change it. Fresh box → pick the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" preset. [keyboard-shortcuts.md](docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)
```

```text
64				return runList(app, listOptions{})

111	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
112	func Execute() int {
113		root := NewRootCommand()
114		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
115			msg := err.Error()
116			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
117			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
118				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
119			}
120			return 1
121		}
122		return 0
123	}
```

```text
1	package cli

3	import (

8	)
9	
10	// zshInit and friends define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to leave
11	// the user *inside* the checkout.
12	//
13	// A process can never change its parent's working directory, so dev prints a
14	// `cd <path>` directive on stdout and the wrapper evaluates it. This is the
15	// same mechanism try-cli uses, and it is why `dev` is a shell function rather
16	// than only a binary.
17	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
18	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
19	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
20	dev() {
21	  local __dev_out __dev_status
22	  __dev_out="$(command %[1]s "$@")"
23	  __dev_status=$?
24	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ "${__dev_out#cd }" != "$__dev_out" ]; then
25	    eval "$__dev_out"
26	  elif [ -n "$__dev_out" ]; then
27	    printf '%%s\n' "$__dev_out"
28	  fi
29	  return $__dev_status
30	}
31	`
32	
33	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
34	#   dev shell-init fish | source
35	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
36	function dev
37	    set -l __dev_out (command %[1]s $argv)
38	    set -l __dev_status $status
39	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and string match -q 'cd *' -- "$__dev_out"
40	        eval $__dev_out
41	    else if test -n "$__dev_out"
42	        printf '%%s\n' $__dev_out
43	    end
44	    return $__dev_status
45	end
46	`
47	
48	func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
49		cmd := &cobra.Command{
50			Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
51			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
52			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
53	
54	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
55	"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
56	directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
57	working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.
58	
59	Add to your shell rc file:
60	
61	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
62	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
63			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
64			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
65			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
66				self, err := os.Executable()
67				if err != nil || self == "" {
68					self = "dev"
69				}
70				switch args[0] {
71				case "bash", "zsh":
72					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
73				case "fish":
74					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
75				default:
76					return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
77				}
78				return nil
79			},
80		}
81		// Completion is a sibling concern but belongs to the same "wire dev into
82		// my shell" moment, so it hangs off this command.
83		cmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
84			Use:       "completion <bash|zsh|fish>",
85			Short:     "Print shell completions",
86			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
87			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
88			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
89				root := cmd.Root()
90				switch args[0] {
91				case "bash":
92					return root.GenBashCompletionV2(app.Out, true)
93				case "zsh":
94					return root.GenZshCompletion(app.Out)
95				case "fish":
96					return root.GenFishCompletion(app.Out, true)
97				}
98				return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q", args[0])
99			},
100		})
101		return cmd
102	}
```

```text
359					Repo: repoName, Seconds: seconds, ActiveDays: days,

425	// collectRepos builds the repository view: what exists, plus how much of it is
426	// in flight.
427	func collectRepos(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime) ([]tui.RepoRow, error) {
428		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
429		if err != nil {
430			return nil, err
431		}
432		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
433		if err != nil {
434			return nil, err
435		}
436		byRepo := map[string][]*task.Task{}
437		for _, t := range tasks {
438			byRepo[t.RepoPath] = append(byRepo[t.RepoPath], t)
439		}
440		sessions, _ := rt.List(ctx)
441	
442		out := make([]tui.RepoRow, len(repos))
443		// Each repo needs status, worktree and remote subprocesses. Serialising
444		// ~3*56 git processes was the measured 4.2s startup bottleneck; eight
445		// workers brings that down without forking hundreds at once.
446		sem := make(chan struct{}, 8)
447		var wg sync.WaitGroup
448		for i, r := range repos {
449			wg.Add(1)
450			go func(i int, r repo.Repo) {
451				defer wg.Done()
452				sem <- struct{}{}
453				defer func() { <-sem }()
454	
455				row := tui.RepoRow{Repo: r}
456				row.Tasks = append(row.Tasks, byRepo[r.Path]...)
457				if r.RealPath != "" && r.RealPath != r.Path {
458					row.Tasks = append(row.Tasks, byRepo[r.RealPath]...)
459				}
460				if !r.Bare {
461					row.Status, _ = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
462					if row.Status.LatestChange.After(row.LastActivity) {
463						row.LastActivity = row.Status.LatestChange
464					}
465					// A normal clone stores one administrative directory per
466					// linked worktree. Reading it avoids spawning another git
467					// process for almost every repo in the main inventory.
468					if entries, err := os.ReadDir(filepath.Join(r.CommonDir, "worktrees")); err == nil {
469						for _, entry := range entries {
470							if entry.IsDir() {
471								row.Worktrees++
472							}
473						}
474					}
475					row.RemoteForge, row.RemoteName = forge.IdentityFromURL(gitx.RemoteFromConfig(r.CommonDir, "origin"))
476					if unix, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, r.Path); err == nil && unix > 0 {
477						commitTime := time.Unix(unix, 0)
478						if commitTime.After(row.LastActivity) {
479							row.LastActivity = commitTime
480						}
481					}
482				}
483				for _, tracked := range row.Tasks {
484					if tracked.Updated.After(row.LastActivity) {
485						row.LastActivity = tracked.Updated
486					}
487				}
488				for _, session := range sessions {
489					if session.Covers(r.Path) || (r.RealPath != "" && session.Covers(r.RealPath)) {
490						row.Live = true
491						row.Runtime, row.RuntimeHandle, row.RuntimeStatus =
492							rt.Name(), session.Handle, session.AgentStatus
493						break
494					}
495				}
496				out[i] = row
497			}(i, r)
498		}
499		wg.Wait()
500		return out, ctx.Err()
501	}
502	
503	// externalTools resolves the configured tool bindings.
504	//
505	// Configurable rather than fixed because which program you reach for is
506	// personal, and because the useful ones are often your own scripts and
507	// aliases, not just the well-known tools.
508	func externalTools(app *App) []tui.Tool {
509		var out []tui.Tool
510		for _, t := range app.Cfg.EffectiveTools() {
511			run := t.Run
512			name := t.Name
513			if name == "" {
514				name = firstWord(run)
515			}
516			command := []string{shellPath(), "-c", run}
517			if t.Interactive {
518				// The command string passed to shell -lic is parsed before some
519				// shells finish loading aliases. Parse only eval "$1" up front,
520				// then evaluate the configured command after rc loading, so both
521				// aliases (vibe) and functions (claude-plans-here) work.
522				command = []string{shellPath(), "-lic", `eval "$1"`, "dev-tui-tool", run}
523			}
524			out = append(out, tui.Tool{
525				Key: t.Key, Name: name, Command: command,
526				Available: commandRunnable(run, t.Interactive),
527			})
528		}
529		return out
530	}
531	
532	// commandRunnable resolves the command's first word on PATH, expanding a
533	// leading environment variable so "$EDITOR ." checks the editor itself.
534	func commandRunnable(run string, interactive bool) func() bool {
535		// Availability is stable for the lifetime of one dashboard. In particular,
536		// probing an interactive alias starts a login shell; doing that on every
537		// render would turn a 60fps UI into a shell-launch benchmark.
538		var once sync.Once
539		available := false
540		return func() bool {
541			once.Do(func() { available = checkCommandRunnable(run, interactive) })
542			return available
543		}
544	}
545	
546	func checkCommandRunnable(run string, interactive bool) bool {
547		word := firstWord(run)
548		if strings.HasPrefix(word, "$") {
549			word = os.Getenv(strings.TrimPrefix(word, "$"))
550			if word == "" {
551				return false
552			}
553			word = firstWord(word)
554		}
555		if word == "" {
556			return false
557		}
558		if interactive {
559			// Ask the configured shell after it loads its rc files; LookPath
560			// cannot see aliases or functions.
561			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
562			defer cancel()
563			probe := exec.CommandContext(ctx, shellPath(), "-lic",
564				`command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1`, "dev-tool-probe", word)
565			return probe.Run() == nil
566		}
567		if filepath.IsAbs(word) {
568			_, err := os.Stat(word)
569			return err == nil
570		}
571		_, err := exec.LookPath(word)
572		return err == nil
573	}
574	
575	func firstWord(s string) string {
576		f := strings.Fields(s)
577		if len(f) == 0 {
578			return ""
579		}
580		return f[0]
581	}
582	
583	func shellPath() string {
584		if s := os.Getenv("SHELL"); s != "" {
585			return s
586		}
587		return "/bin/sh"
588	}
589	
590	// remoteCachePath is private because the inventory can contain names and URLs
591	// of private repositories.
592	func remoteCachePath() string {
593		return filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "remotes.json")
594	}
595	
596	// cachedRemoteRows reads only the private JSON cache — no repository scan or
597	// subprocess — so it is safe on the startup path. Local clone markers are
598	// filled when the background local inventory arrives.
599	func cachedRemoteRows(app *App) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool) {
600		cache, ok := forge.LoadCache(remoteCachePath(), app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration)
601		if !ok {
602			return nil, false
603		}
604		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(cache.Repos))
605		for _, rr := range cache.Repos {
606			out = append(out, tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr})
607		}
608		return out, true
609	}
610	
611	// cachedRemotesForRepoRows uses the local repo data the dashboard already
612	// collected, avoiding another process-spawning scan on startup.
613	func cachedRemotesForRepoRows(app *App, locals []tui.RepoRow) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool) {
614		cache, ok := forge.LoadCache(remoteCachePath(), app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration)
615		if !ok {
616			return nil, false
617		}
618		byRemote := map[string]tui.RepoRow{}
619		for _, r := range locals {
620			if r.RemoteForge != forge.Unknown && r.RemoteName != "" {
621				byRemote[string(r.RemoteForge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(r.RemoteName)] = r
622			}
623		}
624		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(cache.Repos))
625		for _, rr := range cache.Repos {
626			row := tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr}
627			if local, ok := byRemote[string(rr.Forge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(rr.FullName)]; ok {
628				row.LocalPath, row.LocalName = local.Repo.Path, local.Repo.Display()
629			}
630			out = append(out, row)
631		}
632		return out, true
633	}
634	
635	// cachedRemotes returns a fresh, already-local-matched cache for instant TUI
636	// navigation. Local paths are recomputed rather than cached because clones can
637	// move independently of the forge inventory.
638	func cachedRemotes(ctx context.Context, app *App) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool) {
639		cache, ok := forge.LoadCache(remoteCachePath(), app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration)
640		if !ok {
641			return nil, false
642		}
643		return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, cache.Repos), true
644	}
645	
646	// collectRemotes aggregates gh and glab, caches the normalised response, then
647	// marks remotes that already have a checkout under the configured scan roots.
648	// Calls run concurrently so one slow forge does not serialise the other.
649	func collectRemotes(ctx context.Context, app *App, limit int) ([]tui.RemoteRow, error) {
650		if limit <= 0 {
651			limit = app.Cfg.Forge.RemoteLimit
652		}
653		type result struct {
654			repos []forge.RemoteRepo
655			err   error
656		}
657		ch := make(chan result, len(forge.All()))
658		var wg sync.WaitGroup
659		available := 0
660		for _, f := range forge.All() {
661			if !f.Available() {
662				continue
663			}
664			available++
665			wg.Add(1)
666			go func(f forge.Forge) {
667				defer wg.Done()
668				r, err := f.ListRepos(ctx, limit)
669				ch <- result{repos: r, err: err}
670			}(f)
671		}
672		wg.Wait()
673		close(ch)
674		if available == 0 {
675			return nil, fmt.Errorf("neither gh nor glab is installed")
676		}
677	
678		var (
679			remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo
680			errs        []error
681		)
682		for res := range ch {
683			if res.err != nil {
684				errs = append(errs, res.err)
685			}
686			remoteRepos = append(remoteRepos, res.repos...)
687		}
688		// Cache partial results too. They are exactly what was observed, and a
689		// partial list is more useful on the next switch than another six-second
690		// wait merely to rediscover the same provider failure.
691		if len(remoteRepos) > 0 && limit >= app.Cfg.Forge.RemoteLimit {
692			_ = forge.SaveCache(remoteCachePath(), remoteRepos)
693		}
694		return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, remoteRepos), errors.Join(errs...)
695	}
696	
697	func matchRemoteLocals(ctx context.Context, app *App, remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo) []tui.RemoteRow {
698		locals, _ := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
699		localByRemote := map[string]repo.Repo{}
700		for _, r := range locals {
701			if r.Bare {
702				continue
703			}
704			kind, name := forge.IdentityFromURL(gitx.RemoteFromConfig(r.CommonDir, "origin"))
705			if kind != forge.Unknown && name != "" {
706				localByRemote[string(kind)+"/"+strings.ToLower(name)] = r
707			}
708		}
709		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(remoteRepos))
710		for _, rr := range remoteRepos {
711			row := tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr}
712			if local, ok := localByRemote[string(rr.Forge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(rr.FullName)]; ok {
713				row.LocalPath, row.LocalName = local.Path, local.Display()
714			}
715			out = append(out, row)
716		}
717		return out
718	}
719
```

```text
76	func (h *harness) run(args ...string) (string, string, error) {

78		var out, errBuf bytes.Buffer
79		root := cli.NewRootCommandWithIO(&out, &errBuf)
80		root.SetArgs(append([]string{"--config", h.configPath}, args...))

103		// start: branch + worktree + task entry.
104		out = h.mustRun("start", "demo", "--task", "auth", "--branch", "feat/auth", "--base", "main")
105		if !strings.Contains(out, "feat/auth") {
106			t.Fatalf("start output: %q", out)
107		}
108		wtPath := filepath.Join(h.wtRoot, "demo", "feat-auth")
109		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(wtPath, "README.md")); err != nil {
110			t.Fatalf("worktree should exist at the templated path: %v", err)
111		}
112	
113		// The task appears in the inventory as hot.
114		out = h.mustRun("ls")
115		if !strings.Contains(out, "auth") || !strings.Contains(out, "HOT") {
116			t.Errorf("ls after start: %q", out)
117		}
118	
119		// JSON is a stable contract for other tools.
120		out = h.mustRun("ls", "--json")
121		var rows []map[string]any
122		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(out), &rows); err != nil {
123			t.Fatalf("ls --json is not valid JSON: %v\n%s", err, out)
124		}
125		if len(rows) != 1 {
126			t.Fatalf("want 1 row, got %d", len(rows))
127		}
128		if rows[0]["branch"] != "feat/auth" || rows[0]["state"] != "hot" {
129			t.Errorf("json row: %+v", rows[0])
130		}
131	
132		// park: records the next action, closes the session, keeps the worktree.
133		out = h.mustRun("park", "feat/auth", "--next", "add the regression test")
134		if !strings.Contains(out, "WARM") {
135			t.Errorf("park output: %q", out)
136		}
137		out = h.mustRun("ls")
138		if !strings.Contains(out, "WARM") || !strings.Contains(out, "add the regression test") {
139			t.Errorf("ls after park: %q", out)
140		}
141		if _, err := os.Stat(wtPath); err != nil {
142			t.Error("a warm task keeps its worktree")
143		}
144	
145		// resume: back to hot.
146		out = h.mustRun("resume", "auth")
147		if !strings.Contains(out, "feat/auth") {
148			t.Errorf("resume output: %q", out)
149		}
150		out = h.mustRun("ls")
151		if !strings.Contains(out, "HOT") {
152			t.Errorf("ls after resume: %q", out)
153		}
154	
155		// Commit something on the branch so there is work to integrate.
156		h.repo.GitIn(wtPath, "config", "user.email", "dev@example.test")
157		h.repo.GitIn(wtPath, "config", "user.name", "dev test")
158		os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(wtPath, "auth.go"), []byte("package auth\n"), 0o644)
159		h.repo.GitIn(wtPath, "add", "auth.go")
160		h.repo.GitIn(wtPath, "commit", "-m", "feat: add auth")
161	
162		// done --ff: rebase and fast-forward, then clean up.
163		out = h.mustRun("done", "auth", "--ff")
164		if !strings.Contains(out, "merged into main") {
165			t.Fatalf("done output: %q", out)
166		}
167		if _, err := os.Stat(wtPath); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
168			t.Error("done should remove the worktree")
169		}
170		// The commit is on main, and the history stayed linear.
171		if _, err := gitx.Run(gittest.Ctx(), h.repo.Root, "cat-file", "-e", "main:auth.go"); err != nil {
172			t.Error("the branch's commit should be on main")
173		}
174		merges, _ := gitx.Run(gittest.Ctx(), h.repo.Root, "log", "--merges", "--oneline")
175		if merges != "" {
176			t.Errorf("--ff must not create a merge commit, got:\n%s", merges)
177		}
178		// The branch survives by default: merged is not always finished.
179		if !gitx.BranchExists(gittest.Ctx(), h.repo.Root, "feat/auth") {
180			t.Error("the branch should survive without --delete-branch")
181		}
182	
183		// sweep reaps the done entry.
184		out = h.mustRun("sweep")
185		if !strings.Contains(out, "reap") {
186			t.Errorf("sweep should offer to reap a done task: %q", out)
187		}
188	}

251	func TestTryAndGraduate(t *testing.T) {
252		h := newHarness(t)
253	
254		out := h.mustRun("try", "redis-streams")
255		if !strings.Contains(out, "redis-streams") {
256			t.Fatalf("try output: %q", out)
257		}
258		triesRoot := filepath.Join(h.home, "tries")
259		entries, _ := os.ReadDir(triesRoot)
260		if len(entries) != 1 {
261			t.Fatalf("want one try directory, got %d", len(entries))
262		}
263		tryName := entries[0].Name()
264		if !strings.HasSuffix(tryName, "-redis-streams") || len(tryName) < 21 {
265			t.Errorf("a try should be date-prefixed, got %q", tryName)
266		}
267	
268		// A second `try` with the same name reuses the existing directory rather
269		// than creating a near-duplicate.
270		h.mustRun("try", "redis-streams")
271		entries, _ = os.ReadDir(triesRoot)
272		if len(entries) != 1 {
273			t.Errorf("try should reuse an existing match, got %d directories", len(entries))
274		}
275	
276		out = h.mustRun("graduate", "redis-streams", "--category", "Infra")
277		if !strings.Contains(out, "is now a project") {
278			t.Fatalf("graduate output: %q", out)
279		}
280		dest := filepath.Join(h.scanRoot, "Infra", "redis-streams")
281		if _, err := os.Stat(dest); err != nil {
282			t.Fatalf("graduated project should exist at %s: %v", dest, err)
283		}
284		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(triesRoot, tryName)); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
285			t.Error("the try directory should have been moved, not copied")
286		}
287		// The date prefix is dropped, and it is a repo with history.
288		if _, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(gittest.Ctx(), dest); err != nil {
289			t.Errorf("a graduated project should have a commit: %v", err)
290		}
291	}

398	func TestAdoptReportsThenApplies(t *testing.T) {
399		h := newHarness(t)
400	
401		// A branch ahead of main, which is exactly the unfinished work adopt is for.
402		h.repo.Branch("feat/in-flight")
403		h.repo.Commit("wip.txt", "half done\n", "feat: in flight")
404		h.repo.Git("switch", "main")
405	
406		out := h.mustRun("adopt")
407		if !strings.Contains(out, "feat/in-flight") {
408			t.Fatalf("adopt should find the unmerged branch:\n%s", out)
409		}
410		if !strings.Contains(out, "--apply") {
411			t.Error("reporting run should say how to act on it")
412		}
413		// Reporting must not have created anything.
414		if ls := h.mustRun("ls"); !strings.Contains(ls, "No tasks yet") {
415			t.Errorf("adopt without --apply must create nothing, got:\n%s", ls)
416		}
417	
418		h.mustRun("adopt", "--apply", "--yes")
419		ls := h.mustRun("ls")
420		if !strings.Contains(ls, "feat/in-flight") {
421			t.Errorf("adopted task should appear in the inventory:\n%s", ls)
422		}
423	
424		// Adopting twice must not duplicate.
425		out = h.mustRun("adopt")
426		if strings.Contains(out, "feat/in-flight") {
427			t.Errorf("an already-tracked branch should not be offered again:\n%s", out)
428		}
429	}

508		info, err := os.Lstat(link)

510			t.Fatalf("want a symlink at %s: %+v %v", link, info, err)
511		}

514		}

523			t.Errorf("the index is navigation, not where physical new repos should land:\n%s", body)
524		}

526		// The normal repo inventory follows direct repo symlinks, so the catalog is
527		// a real navigation layer rather than a set of links dev itself ignores.
528		var listed bytes.Buffer
529		root := cli.NewRootCommandWithIO(&listed, io.Discard)
530		root.SetArgs([]string{"--config", generated, "repo", "list", "--long"})
531		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
532			t.Fatal(err)
533		}
534		if !strings.Contains(listed.String(), config.Contract(filepath.Join(index, "demo"))) {
535			t.Errorf("repo list should retain the index path:\n%s", listed.String())
536		}
537	}
```

The key product defect is confirmed: the generated POSIX/fish functions always capture `command dev "$@"` in command substitution, so the wrapped bare command no longer owns a terminal on stdout and cannot launch the dashboard. The coherent fix is to make wrappers bypass capture for ordinary output-producing invocations and capture only successful directory-directive candidates, while preserving exit status and stderr; tests need a real shell/PTY-facing seam rather than merely asserting wrapper text contains `cd`. Completion should be consolidated on Cobra’s conventional top-level command so Homebrew, dotfiles, and manual users invoke exactly one stable interface.

```text
1	package task
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"io/fs"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"regexp"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	
14		"github.com/BurntSushi/toml"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}
```

```text
1	package gitx
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"strings"
6	)
7	
8	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
9	type Worktree struct {
10		Path string
11		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
12		Head string
13		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
14		Branch   string
15		Detached bool
16		Bare     bool
17		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
18		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
19		Locked         bool
20		LockedReason   string
21		Prunable       bool
22		PrunableReason string
23		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
24		Main bool
25	}
26	
27	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
28	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
29	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
30		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
31		if err != nil {
32			return nil, err
33		}
34		var (
35			list []Worktree
36			cur  *Worktree
37		)
38		flush := func() {
39			if cur != nil {
40				list = append(list, *cur)
41				cur = nil
42			}
43		}
44		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
45			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
46				flush()
47				continue
48			}
49			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
50			switch key {
51			case "worktree":
52				flush()
53				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
54			case "HEAD":
55				if cur != nil {
56					cur.Head = val
57				}
58			case "branch":
59				if cur != nil {
60					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
61				}
62			case "detached":
63				if cur != nil {
64					cur.Detached = true
65				}
66			case "bare":
67				if cur != nil {
68					cur.Bare = true
69				}
70			case "locked":
71				if cur != nil {
72					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
73				}
74			case "prunable":
75				if cur != nil {
76					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
77				}
78			}
79		}
80		flush()
81		return list, nil
82	}
83	
84	// WorktreeFor finds the worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git refuses to
85	// check the same branch out twice, so at most one can match.
86	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
87		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
88		if err != nil {
89			return Worktree{}, false, err
90		}
91		for _, w := range list {
92			if w.Branch == branch {
93				return w, true, nil
94			}
95		}
96		return Worktree{}, false, nil
97	}
98	
99	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
100	//
101	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
102	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
103	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
104	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
105	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
106		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
107		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
108		if exists {
109			args = append(args, path, branch)
110		} else {
111			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
112			if base != "" {
113				args = append(args, base)
114			}
115		}
116		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
117		return err
118	}
119	
120	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
121	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
122	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
123		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
124		if force {
125			args = append(args, "--force")
126		}
127		args = append(args, path)
128		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
129		return err
130	}
131	
132	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
133	// were deleted behind git's back.
134	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
135		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
136		return err
137	}
138	
139	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
140	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
141		if branch == "" {
142			return false
143		}
144		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
145		return err == nil
146	}
147	
148	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
149	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
150		if ref == "" {
151			return false
152		}
153		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
154		return err == nil
155	}
```

```text
1	// Package help serves the git-workflow quick-reference pages dev bundles.
2	//
3	// These exist because the hard part of this workflow is not running the
4	// commands, it is remembering which one applies. A page you can reach in one
5	// keystroke from the terminal you are already in beats a bookmark.
6	package help
7	
8	import (
9		"embed"
10		"fmt"
11		"io/fs"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	)
15	
16	//go:embed all:topics
17	var topics embed.FS
18	
19	// Topic is one reference page.
20	type Topic struct {
21		Name    string
22		Title   string
23		Summary string
24		Body    string
25	}
26	
27	// List returns every topic, sorted by name.
28	func List() ([]Topic, error) {
29		entries, err := fs.ReadDir(topics, "topics")
30		if err != nil {
31			return nil, err
32		}
33		var out []Topic
34		for _, e := range entries {
35			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".md") {
36				continue
37			}
38			t, err := load(strings.TrimSuffix(e.Name(), ".md"))
39			if err != nil {
40				continue
41			}
42			out = append(out, t)
43		}
44		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name < out[j].Name })
45		return out, nil
46	}
47	
48	// Get returns one topic by exact name, or by unique prefix.
49	func Get(name string) (Topic, error) {
50		if t, err := load(name); err == nil {
51			return t, nil
52		}
53		all, err := List()
54		if err != nil {
55			return Topic{}, err
56		}
57		var hits []Topic
58		for _, t := range all {
59			if strings.HasPrefix(t.Name, name) || strings.Contains(t.Name, name) {
60				hits = append(hits, t)
61			}
62		}
63		switch len(hits) {
64		case 1:
65			return hits[0], nil
66		case 0:
67			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("no help topic %q; run `dev help` to list them", name)
68		default:
69			names := make([]string, len(hits))
70			for i, t := range hits {
71				names[i] = t.Name
72			}
73			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("%q matches several topics: %s", name, strings.Join(names, ", "))
74		}
75	}
76	
77	func load(name string) (Topic, error) {
78		b, err := topics.ReadFile("topics/" + name + ".md")
79		if err != nil {
80			return Topic{}, err
81		}
82		body := string(b)
83		t := Topic{Name: name, Body: body}
84		// The first heading is the title; the first paragraph after it is the
85		// summary shown in the index.
86		for _, line := range strings.Split(body, "\n") {
87			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
88			switch {
89			case t.Title == "" && strings.HasPrefix(line, "# "):
90				t.Title = strings.TrimPrefix(line, "# ")
91			case t.Title != "" && t.Summary == "" && line != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(line, "#"):
92				// A page may open with a blockquote or a list; the marker is
93				// formatting, not part of the one-line summary.
94				t.Summary = strings.TrimLeft(line, ">-* ")
95				return t, nil
96			}
97		}
98		return t, nil
99	}
```
