1	// Package ignore assembles .gitignore files from GitHub's published templates
2	// plus the entries that every repository on a given machine wants but no
3	// language template includes.
4	//
5	// The split matters: a Python template says nothing about .DS_Store, and
6	// nothing at all about the worktree directories an agent harness creates —
7	// which, left untracked, show up as noise in every status.
8	package ignore
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"embed"
13		"fmt"
14		"io"
15		"net/http"
16		"os"
17		"path/filepath"
18		"sort"
19		"strings"
20		"time"
21	)
22	
23	//go:embed all:templates
24	var bundled embed.FS
25	
26	// TemplateAPI is GitHub's public gitignore endpoint. It needs no
27	// authentication, which is what lets this work before `gh auth login`.
28	const TemplateAPI = "https://api.github.com/gitignore/templates"
29	
30	// Source records where a section's content came from, so the generated file
31	// can say so honestly.
32	type Source string
33	
34	const (
35		// SourceRemote is GitHub's template API.
36		SourceRemote Source = "github"
37		// SourceCache is a previously fetched template on disk.
38		SourceCache Source = "cache"
39		// SourceBundled is a template compiled into the binary.
40		SourceBundled Source = "bundled"
41	)
42	
43	// Section is one named block of the generated file.
44	type Section struct {
45		Name   string
46		Body   string
47		Source Source
48	}
49	
50	// Fetcher resolves template names to content, preferring the network and
51	// falling back through the cache to the bundled copies.
52	type Fetcher struct {
53		CacheDir string
54		Client   *http.Client
55		// Offline skips the network entirely.
56		Offline bool
57		// BaseURL overrides the template endpoint; empty means TemplateAPI.
58		BaseURL string
59	}
60	
61	// NewFetcher returns a fetcher caching under dir.
62	func NewFetcher(cacheDir string) *Fetcher {
63		return &Fetcher{
64			CacheDir: cacheDir,
65			Client:   &http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second},
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// Get resolves one template by name, case-insensitively ("python", "Python",
70	// "PYTHON" all work, because nobody remembers GitHub's capitalisation).
71	func (f *Fetcher) Get(ctx context.Context, name string) (Section, error) {
72		canonical := Canonical(name)
73	
74		if !f.Offline {
75			body, err := f.fetch(ctx, canonical)
76			if err == nil {
77				f.writeCache(canonical, body)
78				return Section{Name: canonical, Body: body, Source: SourceRemote}, nil
79			}
80		}
81		if body, ok := f.readCache(canonical); ok {
82			return Section{Name: canonical, Body: body, Source: SourceCache}, nil
83		}
84		if body, ok := bundledTemplate(canonical); ok {
85			return Section{Name: canonical, Body: body, Source: SourceBundled}, nil
86		}
87		return Section{}, fmt.Errorf("no gitignore template for %q (offline, and no cached or bundled copy);"+
88			" available offline: %s", name, strings.Join(BundledNames(), ", "))
89	}
90	
91	// Canonical normalises a template name to GitHub's own capitalisation where
92	// it is known, and otherwise title-cases the input.
93	func Canonical(name string) string {
94		lower := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(name))
95		if c, ok := knownNames[lower]; ok {
96			return c
97		}
98		if lower == "" {
99			return ""
100		}
101		return strings.ToUpper(lower[:1]) + lower[1:]
102	}
103	
104	// knownNames maps the spellings people type to GitHub's file names. Only the
105	// cases where they differ need an entry.
106	var knownNames = map[string]string{
107		"python": "Python", "node": "Node", "nodejs": "Node", "js": "Node",
108		"javascript": "Node", "typescript": "Node", "ts": "Node",
109		"go": "Go", "golang": "Go", "rust": "Rust", "java": "Java",
110		"ruby": "Ruby", "elixir": "Elixir", "c": "C", "c++": "C++", "cpp": "C++",
111		"swift": "Swift", "kotlin": "Kotlin", "scala": "Scala", "haskell": "Haskell",
112		"r": "R", "julia": "Julia", "dart": "Dart", "flutter": "Dart",
113		"terraform": "Terraform", "unity": "Unity", "godot": "Godot",
114		"tex": "TeX", "latex": "TeX", "zig": "Zig", "lua": "Lua", "perl": "Perl",
115		"php": "Composer", "laravel": "Laravel", "rails": "Rails",
116		"android": "Android", "objective-c": "Objective-C", "objc": "Objective-C",
117		"csharp": "VisualStudio", "c#": "VisualStudio", "dotnet": "VisualStudio",
118	}
119	
120	func (f *Fetcher) fetch(ctx context.Context, name string) (string, error) {
121		base := f.BaseURL
122		if base == "" {
123			base = TemplateAPI
124		}
125		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, base+"/"+name, nil)
126		if err != nil {
127			return "", err
128		}
129		req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/vnd.github.raw")
130		client := f.Client
131		if client == nil {
132			client = http.DefaultClient
133		}
134		resp, err := client.Do(req)
135		if err != nil {
136			return "", err
137		}
138		defer resp.Body.Close()
139		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
140			return "", fmt.Errorf("github returned %s for %s", resp.Status, name)
141		}
142		body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20))
143		if err != nil {
144			return "", err
145		}
146		// The raw media type returns the file itself; if a proxy ignored the
147		// Accept header we would get JSON, which is not a usable gitignore.
148		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(string(body)), "{") {
149			return "", fmt.Errorf("unexpected JSON response for %s", name)
150		}
151		return strings.TrimRight(string(body), "\n"), nil
152	}
153	
154	func (f *Fetcher) cachePath(name string) string {
155		if f.CacheDir == "" {
156			return ""
157		}
158		return filepath.Join(f.CacheDir, name+".gitignore")
159	}
160	
161	func (f *Fetcher) readCache(name string) (string, bool) {
162		p := f.cachePath(name)
163		if p == "" {
164			return "", false
165		}
166		b, err := os.ReadFile(p)
167		if err != nil {
168			return "", false
169		}
170		return strings.TrimRight(string(b), "\n"), true
171	}
172	
173	func (f *Fetcher) writeCache(name, body string) {
174		p := f.cachePath(name)
175		if p == "" {
176			return
177		}
178		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p), 0o755); err != nil {
179			return // caching is an optimisation; failing to cache is not an error
180		}
181		_ = os.WriteFile(p, []byte(body+"\n"), 0o644)
182	}
183	
184	func bundledTemplate(name string) (string, bool) {
185		b, err := bundled.ReadFile("templates/" + name + ".gitignore")
186		if err != nil {
187			return "", false
188		}
189		return strings.TrimRight(string(b), "\n"), true
190	}
191	
192	// BundledNames lists the templates available with no network at all.
193	func BundledNames() []string {
194		entries, err := bundled.ReadDir("templates")
195		if err != nil {
196			return nil
197		}
198		var out []string
199		for _, e := range entries {
200			out = append(out, strings.TrimSuffix(e.Name(), ".gitignore"))
201		}
202		sort.Strings(out)
203		return out
204	}
205

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	}
32	
33	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
34	func (a *App) Load() error {
35		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
36		if err != nil {
37			return err
38		}
39		a.Cfg = cfg
40		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
41		if a.Out == nil {
42			a.Out = os.Stdout
43		}
44		if a.Err == nil {
45			a.Err = os.Stderr
46		}
47		return nil
48	}
49	
50	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
51	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
52	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
53		if a.noRuntime {
54			return runtime.None{}
55		}
56		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
57		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
58			backend = a.runtimeOverride
59		}
60		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
61		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
62			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
63		}
64		return rt
65	}
66	
67	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
68	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
69		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
70	}
71	
72	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
73	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
74		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
75	}
76	
77	// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
78	// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
79	// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
80	// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
81	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
82		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
83	}
84	
85	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
86	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
87

302				for _, r := range targets {

305					}
306					note := ""
307					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, r.Path, "fetch", "--prune", "--quiet", "origin"); err != nil {
308						note = "fetch failed (no remote?)"
309					}
310					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
311					if err != nil {
312						continue
313					}
314					if note == "" {
315						switch {
316						case st.Behind > 0 && st.Ahead > 0:
317							note = "diverged — rebase or merge explicitly"
318						case st.Behind > 0 && !st.Dirty():
319							note = "behind — git pull --ff-only"
320						case st.Behind > 0:
321							note = "behind, and dirty — commit first"
322						case st.Ahead > 0:
323							note = "unpushed commits"
324						}
325					}
326					t.Add(truncate(r.Name, 28), truncate(st.Branch, 24), st.Summary(), note)
327				}
328				t.Render(app.Out)
329				return nil
330			},
331		}

333		return cmd

336	// repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.
337	func repoNameFromRef(ref string) string {
338		ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")
339		if i := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:"); i >= 0 {
340			return ref[i+1:]
341		}
342		return ref
343	}
344	
345	func contractAll(paths []string) []string {
346		out := make([]string, len(paths))
347		for i, p := range paths {
348			out[i] = config.Contract(p)
349		}
350		return out
351	}

195		}
196		f := cmd.Flags()
197		f.StringVarP(&name, "task", "t", "", "human name for this change stream")
198		f.StringVarP(&branch, "branch", "b", "", "branch name (default: feat/<task-slug>)")
199		f.StringVar(&base, "base", "", "ref a new branch starts from (default: repo default branch)")
200		f.StringVar(&next, "next", "", "the first next action to record")
201		f.BoolVar(&direct, "direct", false, "track work on the currently checked-out branch; create no branch/worktree")
202		f.BoolVar(&branchOnly, "branch-only", false, "create/switch a branch in the canonical checkout; no worktree")
203		f.BoolVar(&noWorktree, "no-worktree", false, "deprecated alias for --branch-only")
204		_ = f.MarkDeprecated("no-worktree", "use --branch-only (or --direct to stay on main)")
205		f.BoolVar(&noProvision, "no-provision", false, "skip dependency install and ignored-file copying")
206		f.BoolVar(&focus, "focus", false, "focus the new runtime session")
207		return cmd
208	}
209	
210	// checkoutOf is where a task's code lives right now.
211	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
212		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
213			return t.WorktreePath
214		}
215		return t.RepoPath
216	}
217	
218	// annotate pushes the task's state and next action into the runtime as
219	// display-only metadata, so a sidebar can show why a session is open without
220	// anyone having to ask dev.
221	//
222	// For herdr this lands as workspace metadata tokens. A token only renders if
223	// the sidebar row layout in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g.
224	//
225	//	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
226	//	rows = [["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"], ["branch", "git_status"], ["$next"]]
227	//
228	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds and shows nothing,
229	// which is why dev never treats a failure here as an error.
230	func annotate(app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, t *task.Task) {
231		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
232			return
233		}
234		kv := map[string]string{
235			"stage": t.State.Label(),
236			"next":  t.Next,
237		}
238		if err := rt.Annotate(ctxOf(), t.RuntimeHandle, kv); err != nil {
239			app.warnf("could not annotate the runtime session: %v", err)
240		}
241	}
242	
243	func reportProvision(app *App, res *wt.CreateResult) {
244		p := res.Provision
245		if n := len(p.Copied); n > 0 {
246			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   copied    %d gitignored file(s): %s\n", n, strings.Join(p.Copied, ", "))
247		}
248		if n := len(p.Linked); n > 0 {
249			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   linked    %s\n", strings.Join(p.Linked, ", "))
250		}
251		for _, e := range p.Failures {
252			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   warning   %v\n", e)
253		}
254	}

15	func newParkCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
16		var (
17			next   string
18			note   string
19			wip    bool
20			push   bool
21			cold   bool
22			keepRT bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "park [task]",
26			Short: "Stop working on a task without losing the thread",
27			Long: `Park the current task (or the one named) so its runtime session can close.
28	
29	Parking is the missing move that makes a crowded sidebar shrink. It records
30	what to do next, optionally checkpoints uncommitted work, and closes the
31	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
32	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.
33	
34	  warm (default)  worktree and branch stay; session closes. Back within days.
35	  cold (--cold)   work is committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstruct
36	                  it anywhere later with dev resume.
37	
38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
41			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
42			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
43				ctx := ctxOf()
44				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
45				if err != nil {
46					return err
47				}
48	
49				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
50				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
51					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
52						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
53				}
54				target := task.Warm
55				if cold {
56					target = task.Cold
57				}
58				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
59	
60				if next != "" {
61					t.Next = next
62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69	
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97	
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114	
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}
124	
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes
133					// the task reconstructible rather than lost.
134					t.WorktreePath = ""
135				}
136				if cold && mode == task.ModeBranch {
137					// Free the canonical checkout for other work. The branch remains
138					// local + remote and resume switches back to it.
139					base := t.Base
140					if base == "" {
141						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
142					}
143					if base == "" {
144						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but its base branch is unknown")
145					}
146					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
147						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
148							base, err)
149					}
150				}
151	
152				t.State = target
153				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
154				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
155					return err
156				}
157				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
158				if t.Next != "" {
159					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
160				}
161				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
162				return nil
163			},
164		}
165		f := cmd.Flags()
166		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
167		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
168		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
169		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
170		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
171		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
172		return cmd
173	}
174	
175	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
176	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
177		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
178			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
179		}
180		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
181		return nil
182	}
183	
184	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
185	// directory when no argument is given.
186	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
187		if len(args) == 1 {
188			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
189		}
190		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
191		if err != nil {
192			return nil, err
193		}
194		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
195		if err != nil {
196			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
197				config.Contract(cwd))
198		}
199		return t, nil
200	}

14	func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			noProvision bool
17			fetch       bool
18			force       bool
19		)
20		cmd := &cobra.Command{
21			Use:   "resume <task>",
22			Short: "Pick a task back up, rebuilding whatever is missing",
23			Long: `Make a parked task hot again.
24	
25	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
26	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
27	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
28	identity.
29	
30	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
33			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
34			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
35				ctx := ctxOf()
36				t, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
37				if err != nil {
38					return err
39				}
40	
41				host := config.Hostname()
42				if !t.OwnedBy(host) && !force {
43					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is owned by %s.\n"+
44						"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
45						t.ID, t.Owner)
46				}
47	
48				if fetch {
49					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "fetch", "--prune", "origin"); err != nil {
50						app.warnf("fetch failed: %v", err)
51					}
52				}
53	
54				rt := app.Runtime()
55				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
56				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
57	
58				switch mode {
59				case task.ModeWorktree:
60					_, statErr := os.Stat(checkout)
61					// Rebuild the worktree when it is gone — the cold-to-hot path.
62					if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
63						base := t.Base
64						// Prefer the published branch: a cold task's work lives on
65						// the remote, and a stale local ref could drop it.
66						if remote := "origin/" + t.Branch; gitx.RefExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, remote) {
67							base = remote
68						}
69						m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
70						res, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
71							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, RepoName: t.Repo, Branch: t.Branch,
72							Base: base, Label: t.Title(), NoProvision: noProvision,
73						})
74						if err != nil {
75							var exists *wt.ErrExists
76							if asError(err, &exists) {
77								t.WorktreePath = exists.Path
78							} else {
79								return err
80							}
81						} else {
82							t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = res.Path, res.RuntimeHandle
83							reportProvision(app, res)
84							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebuilt    %s\n", config.Contract(res.Path))
85						}
86						checkout = t.WorktreePath
87					}
88	
89				case task.ModeBranch:
90					checkout = t.RepoPath
91					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
92					if err != nil {
93						return err
94					}
95					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
96						if st.Dirty() {
97							return fmt.Errorf("cannot switch the canonical checkout from %s to %s: %s",
98								st.Branch, t.Branch, st.Breakdown())
99						}
100						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "switch", t.Branch); err != nil {
101							return err
102						}
103					}
104	
105				case task.ModeDirect:
106					checkout = t.RepoPath
107					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
108					if err != nil {
109						return err
110					}
111					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
112						return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s tracks %s, but the canonical checkout is on %s; "+
113							"switch back explicitly or start a worktree task", t.Title(), t.Branch, st.Branch)
114					}
115				}
116				if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
117					handle, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, checkout, t.Title())
118					if err != nil {
119						app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
120					}
121					if rt.Name() != "none" {
122						t.RuntimeHandle = handle
123					}
124				}
125	
126				t.State = task.Hot
127				t.Owner = host
128				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
129					return err
130				}
131				annotate(app, rt, t)
132	
133				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s  %s on %s (%s)\n",
134					task.Hot.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, mode)
135				if t.Next != "" {
136					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   next      %s\n", t.Next)
137				}
138				if t.AgentSession != "" {
139					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   agent     %s (resumable)\n", t.AgentSession)
140				}
141				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout); err == nil {
142					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   git       %s\n", st.Summary())
143					if st.Behind > 0 {
144						app.warnf("branch is %d behind upstream — `git pull --ff-only` before you start", st.Behind)
145					}
146				}
147				if rt.Name() == "none" {
148					app.cdDirective(checkout)
149				}
150				return nil
151			},
152		}
153		f := cmd.Flags()
154		f.BoolVar(&noProvision, "no-provision", false, "skip dependency install when rebuilding a worktree")
155		f.BoolVar(&fetch, "fetch", true, "fetch from origin first")
156		f.BoolVar(&force, "force", false, "take ownership of a task owned by another machine")
157		return cmd
158	}

16	func newDoneCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
17		var (
18			ff           bool
19			pr           bool
20			deleteBranch bool
21			keepWorktree bool
22			push         bool
23		)

27			Long: `Finish a task: integrate the branch, then remove what it leaves behind.
28	
29	Two integration modes, matching the two shapes a branch's history takes:
30	
31	  --ff    rebase onto the base and fast-forward it. Use when the branch's
32	          commits are worth keeping in the base's history.
33	  --pr    push and open a pull/merge request with gh or glab, leaving the
34	          merge to review and CI. Use when someone (or something) should look
35	          at it first.
36	
37	With neither, dev only reports what it would do.
38	
39	Cleanup is deliberately conservative: the worktree is removed, the task entry
40	is marked done, and the branch is deleted only with --delete-branch. A merged
41	branch that still has unpushed commits is never deleted.`,
42			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
43			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
44				ctx := ctxOf()
45				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
46				if err != nil {
47					return err
48				}
49				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
50				if _, err := os.Stat(checkout); err != nil {
51					return fmt.Errorf("%s no longer exists — resume the task first", config.Contract(checkout))
52				}
53	
54				st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
55				if err != nil {
56					return err
57				}
58				if st.Dirty() {
59					return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes: %s.\n"+
60						"Commit them, or park the task with --wip, before finishing it",
61						config.Contract(checkout), st.Breakdown())
62				}
63	
64				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
65				if mode == task.ModeDirect {
66					if ff || pr || deleteBranch || keepWorktree {
67						return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s is already on %s; it has no branch/worktree to integrate. "+
68							"Run `dev done` without --ff/--pr/--delete-branch/--keep-worktree", t.Title(), t.Branch)
69					}
70					if push {
71						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
72							return err
73						}
74					}
75					rt := app.Runtime()
76					if t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
77						if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
78							app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
79						}
80						t.RuntimeHandle = ""
81					}
82					t.State = task.Done
83					if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
84						return err
85					}
86					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s completed directly on %s\n", task.Done.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Branch)
87					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   no branch or worktree was created or removed")
88					return nil
89				}
90	
91				base := t.Base
92				if base == "" {
93					base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
94				}
95				if base == "" {
96					return fmt.Errorf("cannot determine the base branch for %s — pass --base when starting a task", t.Repo)
97				}
98	
99				switch {
100				case ff && pr:
101					return fmt.Errorf("--ff and --pr are alternatives; pick one")
102				case pr:
103					if err := openPR(ctx, app, t, checkout, base); err != nil {
104						return err
105					}

107					// so state and cleanup stay untouched.
108					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nThe branch is under review — run `dev done --ff` or `dev sweep` after it merges.")
109					return nil
110				case ff:
111					if err := fastForward(ctx, app, t, checkout, base); err != nil {
112						return err
113					}
114				default:
115					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s on %s (base %s, %s)\n", t.Title(), t.Branch, base, st.Summary())
116					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing done. Choose an integration mode:")
117					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "  dev done --ff    rebase onto "+base+" and fast-forward it")
118					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "  dev done --pr    push and open a pull request")
119					return nil
120				}
121	
122				if push {

124						app.warnf("could not push %s: %v", base, err)
125					} else {

127					}
128				}
129	
130				rt := app.Runtime()
131				if t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
132					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
133						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
134					}
135					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
136				}
137				if t.WorktreePath != "" && !keepWorktree {
138					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
139					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath}); err != nil {

141					} else {
142						t.WorktreePath = ""
143					}
144				}
145				if deleteBranch {
146					if err := deleteMergedBranch(ctx, app, t.RepoPath, t.Branch, base); err != nil {
147						app.warnf("%v", err)
148					}
149				}
150	
151				t.State = task.Done
152				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
153					return err
154				}
155				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s merged into %s\n", task.Done.Icon(), t.Title(), base)
156				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   the task entry stays until `dev sweep --apply` reaps it\n")
157				return nil
158			},
159		}
160		f := cmd.Flags()
161		f.BoolVar(&ff, "ff", false, "rebase onto the base and fast-forward it")
162		f.BoolVar(&pr, "pr", false, "push and open a pull/merge request instead of merging locally")
163		f.BoolVar(&keepWorktree, "keep-worktree", false, "keep the worktree checkout")
164		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the resulting branch (direct mode pushes its current branch)")
165		// Off by default: a branch is cheap to keep and expensive to recreate, and
166		// "merged" is not always "finished" — work often continues on a branch
167		// after its first integration.
168		f.BoolVar(&deleteBranch, "delete-branch", false, "delete the branch once its commits are in the base")
169		return cmd
170	}
171	
172	func directPushHint(push bool) string {
173		if push {
174			return " --push"
175		}
176		return ""
177	}
178	
179	// fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
180	// forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
181	//
182	// merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
183	// branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
184	// a merge commit the user did not ask for.
185	func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
186		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
187		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
188			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
189				"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
190				err, config.Contract(checkout))
191		}
192		// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
193		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
194		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
195			return err
196		}
197		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
198			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
199				"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
200		}
201		return nil
202	}
203	
204	// deleteMergedBranch removes a branch only when git agrees its commits are already
205	// contained in the base — the check that makes cleanup safe.
206	func deleteMergedBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, repoPath, branch, base string) error {
207		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", branch, base); err != nil {
208			return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)
209		}
210		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "branch", "-d", branch); err != nil {
211			return fmt.Errorf("could not delete %s: %w", branch, err)
212		}
213		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   deleted    branch %s\n", branch)
214		return nil
215	}
216	
217	// openPR pushes the branch and asks the forge CLI to open a pull/merge
218	// request. When no forge CLI is available dev prints the push result and the
219	// URL to open by hand, rather than failing: the branch being published is the
220	// part that actually matters.
221	func openPR(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
222		if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
223			return err
224		}
225		kind := forge.Detect(ctx, t.RepoPath)
226		f, err := forge.For(kind)
227		if err != nil || !f.Available() {
228			app.warnf("no forge CLI for this remote — the branch is pushed; open the request in your browser")
229			return nil
230		}
231		url, err := f.CreatePR(ctx, checkout, forge.PRRequest{
232			Base: base, Head: t.Branch, Fill: true,
233		})
234		if err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		if url != "" {
238			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   opened     %s\n", url)
239		}
240		return nil
241	}

425	// renderPlan prints a provisioning plan as a table plus its warnings.
426	func renderPlan(app *App, plan wt.Plan, repoPath string) {
427		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n\n", config.Contract(repoPath))
428	
429		if len(plan.Ecosystems) == 0 {
430			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No project type detected — only gitignored files will be carried over.")
431		} else {
432			t := NewTable("PROJECT", "MANAGER", "FROM", "DEPENDENCIES", "TOOL")
433			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
434				deps := "—"
435				if len(e.DepDirs) > 0 {
436					deps = strings.Join(e.DepDirs, ", ")
437				} else {
438					deps = "global cache"
439				}
440				tool := "installed"
441				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
442					tool = "MISSING: " + e.Tool
443				}
444				t.Add(e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, deps, tool)
445			}
446			t.Render(app.Out)
447		}
448	
449		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
450		if len(plan.Steps) == 0 {
451			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to provision.")
452		} else {
453			st := NewTable("", "ACTION", "WHAT", "WHY")
454			for _, s := range plan.Steps {
455				mark := "✓"
456				if s.Skipped {
457					mark = "·"
458				}
459				st.Add(mark, string(s.Kind), truncate(s.What, 34), s.Why)
460			}
461			st.Render(app.Out)
462		}
463	
464		for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
465			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\nwarning: %s\n", w)
466		}
467		if plan.Empty() {
468			fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "\nNothing would run. If a new worktree comes up broken, add what it needs to "+
469				"worktree.post_create, or commit a .dev.toml with `dev wt plan --write`.")
470		}
471	}
472	
473	// writeRepoTemplate seeds a .dev.toml from the detected plan.
474	//
475	// Committing it is what makes a project's worktree setup reproducible: the
476	// next machine, and the next person, get the same one without having to
477	// rediscover it.
478	func writeRepoTemplate(app *App, repoPath string, plan wt.Plan, set wt.Settings) error {
479		path := filepath.Join(repoPath, wt.OverrideFilename)
480		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
481			return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists — edit it directly", config.Contract(path))
482		}
483	
484		var b strings.Builder

500			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%q", inc)

502		b.WriteString("]\n\n")

504		if len(plan.Ecosystems) > 0 {

517			b.WriteString("#   link       share one directory between checkouts (fastest, risky)\n")

14	
15	func newGitignoreCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
16		var (
17			stdout    bool
18			offline   bool
19			noOS      bool
20			noEditors bool
21			noAgents  bool
22			noEnv     bool
23			list      bool
24		)
25		cmd := &cobra.Command{
26			Use:     "gitignore [language...]",
27			Aliases: []string{"ignore"},
28			Short:   "Write a .gitignore from GitHub's templates plus the entries every repo needs",
29			Long: `Compose a .gitignore for this repository.
30	
31	Language sections come from GitHub's published templates, fetched once and
32	cached. On top of those, dev adds the entries no language template covers but
33	almost every repository wants: the host platform's junk files, editor state,
34	local env files, and the directories coding-agent harnesses create — a
35	harness's linked worktree left untracked makes every git status in the main
36	checkout unreadable.
37	
38	With no language argument, the languages are inferred from the files present.
39	
40	Everything dev writes goes inside a delimited block, so re-running updates that
41	block and leaves rules you added by hand alone.
42	
43	  dev gitignore                 # detect from the repo's files
44	  dev gitignore python node     # explicit
45	  dev gitignore --stdout        # preview without writing
46	  dev gitignore --no-agents     # skip the harness section`,
47			Args: cobra.ArbitraryArgs,
48			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
49				ctx := ctxOf()
50	
51				if list {
52					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Available without a network:")
53					for _, n := range ignore.BundledNames() {
54						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s\n", n)
55					}
56					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nAny name from https://github.com/github/gitignore works online.")
57					return nil
58				}
59	
60				// Operate on the repository root, not wherever the shell happens
61				// to be: a .gitignore in a subdirectory only covers that subtree.
62				cwd, err := os.Getwd()
63				if err != nil {
64					return err
65				}
66				target := cwd
67				if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd); err == nil {
68					target = g.Root
69				} else if !stdout {
70					return fmt.Errorf("%s is not a git repository (use --stdout to preview anyway)",
71						config.Contract(cwd))
72				}
73	
74				names := args
75				if len(names) == 0 {
76					names = ignore.Detect(target)
77					if len(names) == 0 {
78						app.warnf("no language detected in %s — writing only the common sections",
79							config.Contract(target))
80					} else {
81						fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "detected: %s\n", strings.Join(names, ", "))
82					}
83				}
84	
85				fetcher := ignore.NewFetcher(filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "gitignore"))
86				fetcher.Offline = offline
87	
88				var sections []ignore.Section
89				for _, n := range names {
90					s, err := fetcher.Get(ctx, n)
91					if err != nil {
92						// One unknown language must not lose the rest of the file.
93						app.warnf("%v", err)
94						continue
95					}
96					sections = append(sections, s)
97				}
98	
99				extras := ignore.DefaultExtras()
100				extras.OS = !noOS
101				extras.Editors = !noEditors
102				extras.Agents = !noAgents
103				extras.Env = !noEnv
104	
105				block := ignore.Compose(sections, extras)
106				if stdout {
107					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, block)
108					return nil
109				}
110	
111				path := filepath.Join(target, ".gitignore")
112				existing, _ := os.ReadFile(path)
113				updated := ignore.Merge(string(existing), block)
114				if string(existing) == updated {
115					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s is already up to date\n", config.Contract(path))
116					return nil
117				}
118				if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(updated), 0o644); err != nil {
119					return err
120				}
121	
122				verb := "wrote"
123				if ignore.HasManagedBlock(string(existing)) {
124					verb = "updated the managed block in"
125				} else if len(existing) > 0 {
126					verb = "appended a managed block to"
127				}
128				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s\n", verb, config.Contract(path))
129				for _, s := range sections {
130					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %-14s %s\n", s.Name, s.Source)
131				}
132				return nil
133			},
134		}
135		f := cmd.Flags()
136		f.BoolVar(&stdout, "stdout", false, "print instead of writing the file")
137		f.BoolVar(&offline, "offline", false, "use only cached and bundled templates")
138		f.BoolVar(&list, "list", false, "list the templates available offline")
139		f.BoolVar(&noOS, "no-os", false, "omit the host platform's junk files")
140		f.BoolVar(&noEditors, "no-editors", false, "omit editor and IDE state")
141		f.BoolVar(&noAgents, "no-agents", false, "omit coding-agent harness directories")
142		f.BoolVar(&noEnv, "no-env", false, "omit local env and secret files")
143		return cmd
144	}

269	// parseSince accepts a relative window ("30d", "6mo", "1y") or an absolute
270	// date. Relative is what people actually type; absolute is what scripts want.
271	func parseSince(s string, now time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
272		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
273		if s == "" {
274			return now.AddDate(-1, 0, 0), nil
275		}
276		if d, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", s, time.Local); err == nil {
277			return d, nil
278		}
279		var n int
280		var unit string
281		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(s, "%d%s", &n, &unit); err != nil || n <= 0 {
282			return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot parse --since %q: want 30d, 6mo, 1y or YYYY-MM-DD", s)
283		}
284		switch strings.ToLower(unit) {
285		case "d", "day", "days":
286			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n), nil
287		case "w", "week", "weeks":
288			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n*7), nil
289		case "mo", "month", "months":
290			return now.AddDate(0, -n, 0), nil
291		case "y", "yr", "year", "years":
292			return now.AddDate(-n, 0, 0), nil
293		}
294		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown unit %q in --since: want d, w, mo or y", unit)
295	}

327	    dev stats clear --source git

329	    dev stats clear --all

331	Use "dev cache clear" for regenerable forge/gitignore caches instead.`,
332			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
333			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
334				if all && (repo != "" || len(sources) > 0) {
335					return fmt.Errorf("--all cannot be combined with --repo or --source")
336				}
337				if !all && repo == "" && len(sources) == 0 {
338					return fmt.Errorf("choose --repo, --source, or --all; stats data is not treated as disposable cache")
339				}
340				var parsed []stats.Source
341				for _, source := range sources {
342					s := stats.Source(strings.ToLower(source))
343					switch s {
344					case stats.SourceSession, stats.SourceGit, stats.SourceWakaTime:
345						parsed = append(parsed, s)
346					default:
347						return fmt.Errorf("unknown source %q: want session, git or wakatime", source)
348					}
349				}
350				description := "all activity data"
351				if !all {
352					var parts []string
353					if repo != "" {
354						parts = append(parts, "repo="+repo)
355					}
356					if len(parsed) > 0 {
357						parts = append(parts, "source="+strings.Join(sources, ","))
358					}
359					description = strings.Join(parts, " ")
360				}
361				if !yes {
362					in := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
363					if !confirm(app, in, "delete "+description+" from stats.db") {
364						fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "not changed")
365						return nil
366					}
367				}
368				store, err := stats.Open(stats.Path(app.Cfg.StateDir()))
369				if err != nil {
370					return err
371				}
372				defer store.Close()
373				q := stats.ClearQuery{}
374				if !all {
375					q.Repo, q.Sources = repo, parsed
376				}
377				n, err := store.Clear(q)
378				if err != nil {
379					return err
380				}
381				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "deleted %d activity row(s) from %s\n", n,
382					config.Contract(stats.Path(app.Cfg.StateDir())))
383				return nil
384			},
385		}
386		f := cmd.Flags()
387		f.BoolVar(&all, "all", false, "delete all activity and collector checkpoints")
388		f.StringVarP(&repo, "repo", "r", "", "delete this exact repository name")
389		f.StringSliceVar(&sources, "source", nil, "delete these sources: session, git, wakatime")
390		f.BoolVarP(&yes, "yes", "y", false, "do not prompt")
391		return cmd
392	}

105	        non-interactive | "")

126	# --- Adopt pre-flight (macOS only, OPT-IN)
127	# Casks installed manually (drag .app into /Applications) are invisible to brew
128	# until "adopted". `brew install --cask --adopt <name>` writes Caskroom
129	# metadata in-place so subsequent `brew bundle` runs skip the cask.
130	#
131	# Why opt-in (CHEZMOI_BREW_ADOPT_PREFLIGHT=1 to enable):
132	#
133	#   1. **Version-strict**: `--adopt` compares SHA256 of /Applications/Foo.app
134	#      against the SHA256 brew's formula expects. If your manually-installed
135	#      version differs by even a single byte (different download date, vendor
136	#      auto-update, etc.) brew raises "no installed App to adopt" and falls
137	#      back to a full download. In a typical real-world `Brewfile.darwin`
138	#      with 20+ casks, the hit rate observed was ~40% — the rest re-download
139	#      anyway, defeating the point.
140	#
141	#   2. **Password storm**: each `brew install --cask --adopt` invocation
142	#      internally calls `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` / `sudo xattr` / similar.
143	#      Our `sudo_session_warm_cache` warms the TTY timestamp but brew's
144	#      internal sudo invocations don't always reuse it (brew may `sudo -k`
145	#      before pkg installs, or use a different timestamp_type). Result:
146	#      one `Password:` prompt per pkg-based cask, often with multi-second
147	#      gaps where the user has to babysit the terminal.
148	#
149	#   3. **`--adopt` doesn't skip download**: brew calls `fetch_artifacts`
150	#      BEFORE `install_artifacts` (where --adopt branches), so casks whose
151	#      `.app` isn't present (or whose SHA mismatches) still get downloaded.
152	#      Even our filesystem pre-filter only catches the first case.
153	#
154	#   4. **Mac App Store conflicts**: if you have Tailscale (or others) from
155	#      the App Store, the brew cask version's pkg installer pops up an
156	#      interactive "already installed via Mac App Store" dialog mid-apply.
157	#      We detect this via `mas list` when opt-in is enabled.
158	#
159	# When useful:
160	#   - You're setting up a NEW mac, have just manually dragged some `.app`s
161	#     into /Applications/ from vendor DMGs, AND those apps happen to be the
162	#     CURRENT brew-formula versions (rare in practice). Most users should
163	#     leave this off and let `brew bundle` install everything fresh on
164	#     first apply — slower one-time download cost but no password storm and
165	#     no version-mismatch failures.
166	#
167	# To enable: `export CHEZMOI_BREW_ADOPT_PREFLIGHT=1` in ~/.shellrc.adhoc.
168	adopt_existing_casks() {
169	    local file="$1"
170	    [[ -f "$file" ]] || return 0
171	    [[ -n "$(brew --prefix 2>/dev/null)" ]] || return 0
172	
173	    # Resolve Caskroom path once (arm64 vs intel).
174	    local caskroom=""
175	    if [[ -d /opt/homebrew/Caskroom ]]; then
176	        caskroom=/opt/homebrew/Caskroom
177	    elif [[ -d /usr/local/Caskroom ]]; then
178	        caskroom=/usr/local/Caskroom
179	    fi
180	
181	    # Snapshot /Applications/ once (lowercased, newline-separated). Avoids
182	    # forking ls/find per cask. Falls back to empty string if dir missing.
183	    local apps_lc=""
184	    if [[ -d /Applications ]]; then
185	        apps_lc="$(/bin/ls -1 /Applications 2>/dev/null | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
186	    fi
187	
188	    # Snapshot mas-installed App Store apps (lowercased). Used to skip
189	    # casks whose app the user has via App Store — adopting them would
190	    # trigger a "Mac App Store Install Detected" dialog mid-apply.
191	    # `mas list` format: "<id>  <Name>  (<version>)"
192	    local mas_lc=""
193	    if command -v mas >/dev/null 2>&1; then
194	        mas_lc="$(mas list 2>/dev/null | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
195	    fi
196	
197	    # Heuristic: does /Applications/ have an .app whose name matches this
198	    # cask? Tries a handful of candidate spellings derived from the cask
199	    # short-name. Misses on weird capitalization (chatgpt → ChatGPT.app works
200	    # because case-insensitive; aerospace → AeroSpace.app works too).
201	    _has_app_for_cask() {
202	        local short="$1"
203	        local stem="${short%-app}"
204	        stem="${stem%-desktop}"
205	        local candidates=(
206	            "${short}.app"
207	            "${stem}.app"
208	            "${short//-/ }.app"
209	            "${stem//-/ }.app"
210	            "${short//-/}.app"
211	            "${stem//-/}.app"
212	        )
213	        local c c_lc
214	        for c in "${candidates[@]}"; do
215	            c_lc="$(printf '%s' "$c" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
216	            if printf '%s\n' "$apps_lc" | grep -qFx -- "$c_lc"; then
217	                return 0
218	            fi
219	        done
220	        return 1
221	    }
222	
223	    # Heuristic: is this cask's app already installed via Mac App Store?
224	    # Matches the cask stem against `mas list` output (case-insensitive).
225	    # False positives possible (substring match) but the cost of a false
226	    # positive is just "we don't try to adopt" — cheap.
227	    _is_mas_installed() {
228	        [[ -z "$mas_lc" ]] && return 1
229	        local short="$1"
230	        local stem="${short%-app}"
231	        stem="${stem%-desktop}"
232	        # Replace dashes with spaces for the search term (App Store names
233	        # generally have spaces, e.g. "Tailscale" or "The Unarchiver").
234	        local search="${stem//-/ }"
235	        printf '%s\n' "$mas_lc" | grep -qF -- "$search" && return 0
236	        return 1
237	    }
238	
239	    local cask_list
240	    cask_list="$(brew bundle list --casks --file="$file" 2>/dev/null)" || return 0
241	    [[ -n "$cask_list" ]] || return 0
242	
243	    # Three-stage filter:
244	    #   - drop already-tracked (cheap filesystem check)
245	    #   - drop casks whose .app isn't in /Applications/ (no point — brew would
246	    #     download anyway)
247	    #   - drop casks already installed via Mac App Store (would trigger the
248	    #     "already installed via Mac App Store" pkg-installer dialog)
249	    local needs_adopt=() already=0 not_present=0 mas_conflict=0 cask short
250	    while IFS= read -r cask; do
251	        [[ -n "$cask" ]] || continue
252	        short="${cask##*/}"
253	        if [[ -n "$caskroom" && -d "$caskroom/$short" ]]; then
254	            already=$(( already + 1 ))
255	            continue
256	        fi
257	        if ! _has_app_for_cask "$short"; then
258	            not_present=$(( not_present + 1 ))
259	            continue
260	        fi
261	        if _is_mas_installed "$short"; then
262	            mas_conflict=$(( mas_conflict + 1 ))
263	            info "  skipping $short — also installed via Mac App Store (mas)"
264	            continue
265	        fi
266	        needs_adopt+=("$cask")

268	
269	    local total=${#needs_adopt[@]}
270	    if (( total == 0 )); then
271	        info "Adopt pre-flight: $already tracked, $not_present not in /Applications/, $mas_conflict mas-conflict, nothing to adopt"
272	        return 0
273	    fi
274	
275	    info "Adopt pre-flight: $already tracked, $not_present not in /Applications/, $mas_conflict mas-conflict, attempting --adopt on $total cask(s)..."
276	
277	    local adopted=0 failed=0 idx=0 err
278	    local err_file
279	    err_file="$(mktemp -t cz_adopt_err.XXXXXX)"
280	    for cask in "${needs_adopt[@]}"; do
281	        idx=$(( idx + 1 ))
282	        short="${cask##*/}"

285	        # (google-drive, etc.) shell out to `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` from a
286	        # subshell that doesn't always inherit our controlling TTY. Best-effort:

293	        else

298	                    || head -n1 "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)"

300	                info "    ✗ adopt failed: $short — ${err}"
301	            else
302	                info "    ✗ adopt failed (no brew stderr captured): $short"
303	            fi
304	        fi
305	    done
306	    rm -f "$err_file"
307	
308	    info "Adopt pre-flight done: $adopted adopted, $already tracked, $not_present absent, $mas_conflict mas-conflict, $failed adopt-failed"
309	}
310	
311	# Gated on CHEZMOI_BREW_ADOPT_PREFLIGHT=1 (opt-in). See block comment above
312	# for the trade-offs that made this opt-in.
313	if [[ "${CHEZMOI_BREW_ADOPT_PREFLIGHT:-0}" = "1" ]]; then

317	{{ end -}}
318	
319	# Run brew bundle up to N times. Subsequent attempts only retry items that
320	# failed (already-installed packages are skipped quickly). This papers over
321	# transient GitHub CDN / HTTP/2 errors that commonly hit large cask lists.
322	# Between attempts we wipe Homebrew's `.incomplete*` lockfiles so a previously

325	BUNDLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS="${BUNDLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS:-2}"
326	clear_brew_download_locks() {
327	    local cache_dir
328	    cache_dir="$(brew --cache 2>/dev/null)/downloads"

331	    find "$cache_dir" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.incomplete*' -print -delete 2>/dev/null \
332	        | head -20 \

334	}

336	trust_bundle_taps() {

339	    [[ -f "$file" ]] || return 0
340	    taps="$(brew bundle list --taps --file="$file" 2>/dev/null || true)"

343	    while IFS= read -r tap; do
344	        [[ -n "$tap" ]] || continue
345	        if ! brew tap | grep -qFx -- "$tap"; then
346	            if ! brew tap "$tap"; then
347	                warn "Could not tap $tap before brew bundle; brew bundle will retry normally"

352	        info_out="$(brew tap-info "$tap" 2>/dev/null || true)"

360	run_bundle_with_retry() {

379	    return 0

2	# Regenerate shell completion files for upstream CLIs.
3	#
4	# Usage:
5	#   scripts/generate_completions.sh [--force] [--quiet] [--help]
6	#
7	# Modes:
8	#   default   Skip tools whose completion file is already newer than the binary
9	#             (binary-mtime check — same idiom as 95_bitwarden.zsh / 47_mi_router.sh).
10	#   --force   Regenerate every tool's completion regardless of mtime.
11	#   --quiet   Suppress per-tool progress; still print final summary.
12	#
13	# Output paths (lazy-autoload conventions):
14	#   zsh:  ~/.zfunc/_<tool>                                              (in fpath via dot_zshrc.tmpl:68)
15	#   bash: ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>
16	#         (auto-loaded on first TAB by bash-completion v2)
17	#
18	# Tools NOT handled here (covered elsewhere — don't double-up):
19	#   sesh, tv, worktrunk        → shell-startup mtime check (dot_config/zsh/tools/{22_sesh,12_television,37_worktrunk}.zsh)
20	#   bw                         → cached eval at startup    (dot_config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh)
21	#   marimo, thefuck, try-cli   → cached eval at startup    (dot_config/shell/{29_marimo,27_thefuck}.sh + dot_config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh)
22	#   mi-router                  → tyro self-gen at startup  (dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh)
23	#   fleet, mlf, pqsum, x       → hand-written eager-load   (dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-49_*_completion.*)
24	#

27	#   - `just completions-refresh`                                          (manual, --force)
28	#

30	# Full design: docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md "How autocomplete works" + Section A.
31	
32	set -euo pipefail

34	force=0

39	    --quiet) quiet=1 ;;

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Regenerate shell completion files for upstream CLIs after every `chezmoi
3	# apply`. Detects tools whose binaries were upgraded since the last completion
4	# generation (binary mtime > completion file mtime → regen).
5	#
6	# `run_after_*` (not `run_onchange_after_*`): we want to detect tools that

2	# https://worktrunk.dev — github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk
3	#
4	# Backend half of the split: shell-init wrapper (so `wt switch` can change
5	# the parent shell's $PWD) + the `wtcd` fzf picker. Zsh-only half lives in
6	# dot_config/zsh/tools/37_worktrunk.zsh (clap-based completion generation
7	# into ~/.zfunc/_wt).

9	# Companion config: ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml (managed by chezmoi at
10	# dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml). Aliases like `wt sw` / `wt cc` live
11	# THERE, not here — keep this file focused on shell-level integration only.
12	
13	# Skip silently if not installed (Linux ansible install can fail offline)
14	command -v wt &>/dev/null || return 0
15	
16	# ── Shell integration: cd-wrapping `wt` function ───────────────────────────
17	#
18	# `wt switch` needs to change the parent shell's $PWD, which a normal binary
19	# can't do. Worktrunk solves this by writing a directive file that a wrapper
20	# shell function reads and `cd`s to. We eval that wrapper at shell startup
21	# rather than running `wt config shell install` (which edits ~/.zshrc with a
22	# block chezmoi would fight over).
23	#
24	# Same pattern as starship / zoxide / direnv elsewhere. The `2>/dev/null`
25	# swallows the error if wt doesn't support the requested shell (e.g. bash
26	# wrapper not yet implemented in upstream) — the binary itself still works,
27	# users just lose the cd-on-switch wrapper.
28	if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
29	    eval "$(wt config shell init zsh 2>/dev/null)"
30	elif [ -n "$BASH_VERSION" ]; then
31	    eval "$(wt config shell init bash 2>/dev/null)"
32	fi
33	
34	# ── Tiny shell-side conveniences (NOT duplicating wt's own aliases) ────────
35	#
36	# `wt`'s own aliases (sw / ls / rm / cc / oc) are defined in
37	# ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml so they work from any shell + the
38	# interactive picker. Anything below is shell niceness that wt's alias
39	# system can't express.
40	
41	# `wtcd` — jump to a worktree path WITHOUT switching tmux/sesh session.
42	# Useful when you want to peek at sibling worktree files (open in nvim split,
43	# scp, etc.) without disturbing the current pane's session context.
44	function wtcd() {
45	    local target
46	    target=$(wt list --format=json 2>/dev/null \
47	        | jq -r '.worktrees[].path' \
48	        | fzf-tmux -p 60%,40% --prompt='wt cd ❯ ' --header='Pick a worktree to cd into') \
49	        || return
50	    [ -n "$target" ] && cd -- "$target"
51	}

34	# (dot_config/shell/02_legacy_tools.sh) and scripts/upgrade_tools.sh cat_go. The
35	# `creates:` guard makes this install-only + idempotent — version bumps go
36	# through `just upgrade-go` (scripts/upgrade_tools.sh cat_go), never a re-apply.
37	#
38	# macOS is EXCLUDED: those tools (currently just `translate`) install via Homebrew
39	# (dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl → daviddwlee84/tap), so this go path is
40	# Linux-only — otherwise both mechanisms fight over the binary and ~/.local/bin
41	# shadows brew. cat_go() has the mirror gate. Revisit if a future go tool needs macOS.
42	- name: Install Go CLI tools via go install (Linux; macOS uses Homebrew)
43	  when:
44	    - (go_bindir.stdout | default('') | trim) != ""
45	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] != 'Darwin'
46	  ansible.builtin.command: "go install {{ item.name }}"
47	  args:
48	    creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/{{ item.binary }}"
49	  loop: "{{ go_tools }}"
50	  loop_control:
51	    label: "{{ item.name }}"
52	  environment:
53	    GOBIN: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
54	    GOPATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/share/go"
55	    PATH: "{{ (go_bindir.stdout | trim) }}:{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
56

```text
1	# Zsh & Bash Completions
2	
3	How tab completions are organized in this dotfiles project — for both upstream tools and in-house CLIs (`fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `mi-router`, `x`).
4	
5	## How autocomplete works (mechanics)
6	
7	Tab completion is the same idea on both shells but the plumbing differs.
8	
9	### zsh — `compinit` + `fpath` + autoload `_<tool>` functions
10	
11	1. **`compinit`** scans every directory in `$fpath` for files starting with `_` and registers them as completion candidates. Run by oh-my-zsh once at startup.
12	2. **`$fpath`** is zsh's function search path. Order in this repo (`dot_zshrc.tmpl:67-70`):
13	   ```
14	   ~/.zfunc                                             ← user-generated (this repo's lazy autoload target)
15	   ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/     ← community (184 tools)
16	   ~/.docker/completions/                               ← Docker-shipped
17	   $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/           ← Homebrew-managed
18	   ```
19	3. **The first line of each file** matters: `#compdef <name>` tells zsh which command to bind to. If you write `#compdef fleet`, then `fleet<TAB>` invokes the file's `_fleet` function.
20	4. **Autoload vs eager-load**: a file in `$fpath` is *parsed* the first time the user actually TABs the command (lazy). Files sourced explicitly at startup (e.g. via `load_modular_dir` in this repo) call `compdef _<func> <cmd>` directly — parsed eagerly, no need to be in `$fpath`.
21	5. **`_arguments` DSL** (zsh-only) lets you describe options + positional args declaratively: `'--hosts=[help text]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv'` defines the flag, hint, and a custom completer function. See `dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh`.
22	
23	### bash — `bash-completion v2` + `complete -F` + `COMPREPLY`
24	
25	1. **bash-completion v2** is sourced at shell startup by `dot_config/bash/03_completion.bash`. It auto-loads completion files on first TAB.
26	2. **The user dir** is `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/` — drop a file named after the command (e.g. `mi-router`) here and v2 lazy-loads it on TAB.
27	3. **`complete -F _func cmd`** registers a bash function as the completer for `cmd`. The function reads `$COMP_WORDS` / `$COMP_CWORD` and writes candidates to `$COMPREPLY`.
28	4. **`_init_completion` + `compgen`** are bash-completion v2 helpers — `_init_completion` populates `cur`/`prev`/`words`/`cword`; `compgen -W "list" -- "$cur"` filters a wordlist by the current prefix.
29	5. **Eager vs lazy** mirrors zsh: a file in the user dir is lazy; a file sourced via `load_modular_dir` (this repo's `dot_config/bash/`) calls `complete -F` immediately.
30	
31	### Three generation strategies in this repo
32	
33	| Strategy | Where the file lives | Trigger | Best for |
34	|---|---|---|---|
35	| **A. Lazy autoload** | zsh `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` / bash `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` | First TAB on the command | Tools that ship `--print-completion <shell>` or similar (tyro, click, clap-derive — including this repo's `mi-router`) |
36	| **B. Eager-load at startup** | `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<tool>_completion.bash` | Sourced via `load_modular_dir` after compinit / bash-completion v2 init | Hand-written completion (this repo's `fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `x`) |
37	| **C. Cached eval at startup** | `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>` | Sourced via shell `init` script (`dot_config/shell/<NN>_<tool>.sh`) | Slow generators whose output has side effects beyond `compdef` (e.g. `thefuck --alias` outputs an `alias` line — needs to land in the running shell's namespace, not just a deferred `_<tool>` function) |
38	
39	Cache invalidation in classes A and C uses **binary-mtime check**:
40	```sh
41	[ ! -f "$cache" ] || [ "$(command -v <tool>)" -nt "$cache" ]  # → regenerate
42	```
43	This catches `brew upgrade`, `uv tool upgrade`, `mise install <NEW>` — anything that bumps the binary's mtime. Manual `<tool>-update-completion` helpers (in `dot_config/{shell,zsh}/10_aliases.zsh`) cover edge cases (gem-only upgrades, in-place replacements, cache corruption).
44	
45	## Architecture
46	
47	```
48	compinit runs once (inside oh-my-zsh.sh)
49	        │
50	        ├── ~/.zfunc/                          ← user-generated completions (NOT tracked by chezmoi)
51	        ├── ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/       ← community completions (184 files, cloned by ansible)
52	        │     └── zsh-completions/src/
53	        ├── ~/.docker/completions/             ← Docker-shipped completions
54	        ├── $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/        ← Homebrew-managed completions (via `brew completions link`)
55	        │     └── site-functions/
56	        └── $ZSH/completions/                  ← oh-my-zsh built-in completions
57	```
58	
59	All `fpath` additions are in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` **before** `source "$ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh"`, so `compinit` runs exactly once and picks up everything.

61	## Completion Categories
62	
63	Tools fall into four categories:
64	
65	### A. Self-generating (`tool completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tool`)
66

70	|------|---------|
71	| `uv` | `uv generate-shell-completion zsh` |

73	| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi completion zsh` |

130	
131	Python CLI frameworks can generate completions. Pick by what your script uses:
132	
133	- **[tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/)** (this repo's `mi-router` + every `scripts/fleet/*.py` and `scripts/mlf/*.py` subcommand): `<tool> --tyro-write-completion zsh <path>`. 135	- **argcomplete**: `register-python-argcomplete tool_name` (eval-at-startup style, category C). Requires the script to call `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` before `parse_args()`. Cross-shell.
136	- **click** (used by `marimo`, `thefuck`, `mlflow`, `litellm`, etc.): `_TOOL_COMPLETE=zsh_source tool > ~/.zfunc/_tool`. The completion script may include side effects (aliases / functions) — if so, treat as category C and cache via `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>`. See the canonical pattern at `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh`.

138	> **TAB display itself**, not just completion data: see [`oh-my-zsh-plugins.md`](oh-my-zsh-plugins.md) "TAB display upgrades — alternatives evaluated" for fzf-tab (recommended) and rejected alternatives (zsh-autocomplete / carapace-bin / inshellisense).

186	
187	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
188	
189	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
190	
191	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
192	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
193	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
194	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
195	
196	### What we DO track
197	
198	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
199	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
200	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
201	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
202	
203	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
204	
205	**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).
206	
207	The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
208	
209	Output paths:
210	- **zsh**: `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` — lazy-loaded by compinit on first TAB (in `$fpath` via `dot_zshrc.tmpl:68`).
211	- **bash**: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` — lazy-loaded by bash-completion v2 on first TAB.
212	
213	### Manual rerun
214	
215	```bash
216	just completions-refresh                              # force regen all (--force)
217	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh --force          # same, no `just`
218	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh                  # mtime-checked (same as the chezmoi hook)
219	```
220	
221	Use `just completions-refresh` after a tool upgrade outside the chezmoi flow (e.g. `cargo install <tool>`), or to recover from a corrupted completion file.
222	
223	### Opt out
224	
225	```bash
226	export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1   # in ~/.shellrc.adhoc; suppresses the chezmoi-apply hook
227	```
228	
229	Existing completion files stay as-is; you can still run `just completions-refresh` manually.
230	
231	### Add a new tool to the auto-gen inventory
232	
233	Edit the `regen <tool> "<zsh-args>" "<bash-args>"` block in `scripts/generate_completions.sh`. The arguments are whatever follows the tool name to produce the per-shell completion script — check `<tool> completion --help` or `<tool> --help | grep -i complet`. Examples already in the script cover click (`_TOOL_COMPLETE=`), clap (`--generate complete-<shell>`), tyro (`--tyro-write-completion <shell>`-equivalent), cobra (`completion <shell>`), and ad-hoc styles (`--completions <shell>`).
234	
235	### What about tools NOT in the auto-gen inventory?
236	
237	- **`sesh` / `tv` / `worktrunk`**: shell-startup mtime check (each tool has its own `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>.zsh` file that runs the version check on every shell start — these tools are typically `cargo install`-ed outside chezmoi, so they need the per-startup probe to catch user upgrades).
238	- **`bw` / `marimo` / `thefuck` / `try-cli`**: cached eval at startup (their completion script has side effects beyond `compdef`, so the file is `source`'d into the running shell rather than autoloaded).
239	- **`mi-router`**: tyro self-gen, lives in `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` (not the bulk script — has its own `#compdef` rewrite for tyro's full-path output quirk).
240	- **`fleet` / `mlf` / `pqsum` / `x` / `dotcfg`**: hand-written completion in `dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-54_*_completion.*` (in-house CLIs without a built-in completion generator). `dotcfg`'s `--set` key list mirrors the PROMPTS table in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`. `agent-warmup` moved to the Tyro self-generation pattern above.
241	
242	## Priority / Override Order
243	
244	When the same `_tool` file exists in multiple fpath directories, the **first match wins**:
245	
246	```
247	1. ~/.zfunc/                                    (highest - your overrides)
248	2. ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/
249	3. ~/.docker/completions/
250	4. $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/   (Homebrew-managed)
251	5. /usr/share/zsh/*/functions/                  (system, lowest)
252	```
253	
254	Current `dot_zshrc.tmpl` order:
255	
256	```zsh
257	fpath+=~/.zfunc                     # appended (lowest of custom)
258	fpath=(zsh-completions/src $fpath)  # prepended (higher than ~/.zfunc)
259	fpath=(~/.docker/completions $fpath) # prepended (highest of custom)
260	```
261	
262	If you want `~/.zfunc/` to override community completions, change to prepend:
263	
264	```zsh
265	fpath=(~/.zfunc $fpath)  # prepend instead of append
266	```
267	
268	## FAQ
269	
270	**Q: Should I generate completions for tools that `zsh-completions` already covers?**
271	A: Only if you want the latest version. The community plugin may lag behind. For fast-moving tools (uv, mise), generating your own is worthwhile.
272	
273	**Q: A completion file throws errors after I uninstall a tool. What do I do?**
274	A: Remove the file: `rm ~/.zfunc/_toolname`. Stale `_tool` files in fpath are harmless (silently ignored) unless they have syntax errors.
275	
276	**Q: How do I debug completion issues?**
277	A: Run `echo $fpath | tr ' ' '\n'` to see all fpath entries. Use `which _toolname` to see which completion file is being used. Force rebuild with `rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit`.
278
```

40	
41	The script runs categories in the canonical `ALL_CATEGORIES` order regardless of CLI arg order — dependencies between categories are real (see [§ Run order](#run-order)).
42	
43	## Category matrix
44	
45	| Category | What actually happens |
46	| --- | --- |
47	| `externals` | `chezmoi upgrade` (the chezmoi binary itself) + `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals` (force-refresh the 168h externals: oh-my-zsh, TPM, toolkami.rb, fzf). First because a chezmoi version bump may change how later steps behave. |
48	| `brew` | `brew update` → `brew upgrade` → `brew upgrade --cask --greedy` → `brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile` *without* `--no-upgrade` → `Brewfile.{darwin,linux}` → `brew cleanup`. macOS pre-warms the shared sudo session via [`scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`](../../scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) so cask pkg installers that shell out to `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` find a live ticket. |
49	| `mise` | `mise self-update --yes` + `mise upgrade` (honours the version constraints in `~/.config/mise/config.toml`). `self-update` warns, rather than fails, when mise was installed via brew/apt. |
50	| `uv` | Detects install style by binary path (Homebrew vs curl-installer) and dispatches to the right channel: `brew upgrade uv` for Homebrew/Linuxbrew installs, `uv self update` for the standalone curl installer. Then `uv tool upgrade --all`. Covers every tool listed in [`python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml) and [`llm_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/llm_tools/defaults/main.yml). The `python_uv_tools` ansible role does the same dispatch automatically when uv is below `min_uv_version` — see [`docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`](uv-bootstrap.md). |
51	| `npm` | `npm -g update`, falling back to `mise exec -- npm -g update` when `npm` is not directly on PATH (same detection as [`js_cli_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/js_cli_tools/tasks/main.yml) / [`bitwarden`](../../dot_ansible/roles/bitwarden/tasks/main.yml)). |
52	| `cargo` | If absent, bootstraps the `cargo-update` crate, then `cargo install-update -a`. Covers pueue (Linux) plus any future entries in [`rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml). |
53	| `go` | Parses tool names from [`go_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/defaults/main.yml) and runs `go install <pkg>@latest` per entry (strips the pinned version), installing into `~/.local/bin` via `GOBIN`. Resolves go via the mise shim; `SKIPPED` when Go is absent (`installExtraRuntimes=false`). **macOS is skipped entirely** — its go tools (currently just `translate`) are Homebrew-managed via `daviddwlee84/tap`, so upgrade them with `brew upgrade` (`just upgrade-brew`). |
54	| `dotnet` | Parses tool names from [`dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml) and runs `dotnet tool update --global <name>` per tool (via the mise dotnet shim). Falls back to `dotnet tool list --global` if parsing finds nothing. |
55	| `gem` | `gem update --system` + `gem update` via the mise ruby shim. |
56	| `flatpak` | `flatpak update --user --noninteractive --assumeyes` for user-scope Flathub apps (Discord et al. when `discordChannel=flatpak` — see [`docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md`](../playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md)). Skipped when `flatpak` is absent OR when no user-scope apps are installed. System-scope (`flatpak update --system`) is intentionally NOT covered — it requires `sudo` and is rare in this repo's flow; run manually if needed. |
57	| `warp` | **Linux only.** `sudo apt-get update` + `sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade -y warp-terminal` via the shared sudo session. macOS Warp is handled by `cat_brew` (cask `warp` + `--greedy`); this category short-circuits with `SKIPPED` on Darwin. The on-disk binary is replaced but the running Warp process is **not** restarted — quit + relaunch Warp to load the new version. The in-app `warp_finish_update <token>` graceful-restart only works from inside a live Warp session (Warp-injected shell function, not on `$PATH` otherwise) — see [`docs/tools/warp.md`](../tools/warp.md) for the full mechanism. |
58	| `agents` | Re-runs the official `curl \| bash` installers for **tools already present** only — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Ollama (Linux), llmfit (Linux), RTK. Bootstrap list mirrors [`coding_agents`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml). |
59	| `atuin` | macOS: `brew upgrade atuin` (no-op when atuin was installed via the upstream installer rather than brew). Linux: re-runs `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://setup.atuin.sh \| env ATUIN_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 sh` so the upstream installer drops the new binary into `~/.atuin/bin/` while leaving PATH wiring to [`dot_config/shell/15_atuin.sh`](../../dot_config/shell/15_atuin.sh). Skipped with `SKIPPED` if `atuin` is not on PATH. The local SQLite history (`~/.local/share/atuin/`) and config (`~/.config/atuin/config.toml`) are untouched. |
60	| `herdr` | **Only from outside herdr, and only for a self-managed install.** `herdr update --handoff` — the live path that replaces the server without killing pane processes, so coding agents running in panes survive. `SKIPPED` when the binary came from brew/mise/Nix (upstream *disables* `herdr update` there; this repo installs the GitHub-release binary on **both** platforms precisely so the handoff stays available — the message tells you to re-run `chezmoi apply` to migrate) and `SKIPPED` with instructions when `HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID` show you are inside a pane. After a successful update, the category refreshes `~/.agents/skills/herdr/SKILL.md` from that exact binary's `herdr --skill` output, then reports stale agent integrations without auto-reinstalling them. See [`docs/tools/herdr.md`](../tools/herdr.md) and [`pitfalls/herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md). |
61	| `plugins` | `nvim --headless "+Lazy! sync" +qa` → `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/bin/update_plugins all` → refresh installed `claude-hud` via [`claude_hud_sync.py`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/files/claude_hud_sync.py) → `pre-commit autoupdate` (on the dotfiles repo root) → `tldr --update` → `gh extension upgrade --all`. Each step is guarded on the relevant binary being present. |
62	| `yazi-plugins` | `ya pkg upgrade` — bumps Yazi plugins (`piper.yazi`, …) declared in [`dot_config/yazi/package.toml`](../../dot_config/yazi/package.toml) to their latest upstream revs. `SKIPPED` when `ya` or the lockfile is absent. Install-only `chezmoi apply` pins the committed revs via `ya pkg install`; after upgrading, copy the regenerated `~/.config/yazi/package.toml` back into the chezmoi source to persist the new revs. See [`docs/tools/office-viewers.md`](../tools/office-viewers.md). |
