310	- **Linux audit framework** (optional, Linux only, `installAuditd=true`): [`auditd`](docs/sysadmin/auditd.md) + baseline rule set (identity / sudoers / sshd_config / privileged-exec watches), plus `audit-*` shell helpers and `tv sessions` / `tv sudo-history` / `tv audit-events` Television channels for the routine "who did what on this server" queries. Full guide: [docs/sysadmin/](docs/sysadmin/README.md); ansible role: [docs/playbooks/auditd.md](docs/playbooks/auditd.md)
311	- **Homelab hardware monitoring** (optional, Linux/physical only, `installHomelabTools=true`): hardware-monitoring CLIs ([lm-sensors, smartmontools, ipmitool, nvme-cli, storcli](docs/sysadmin/hardware.md)) installed only when the matching hardware is detected, plus the `hw-*` shell helper family (`hw-fans`, `hw-temps`, `hw-raid`, `hw-smart`, `hw-status` …) for the "is this server's hardware healthy?" sweep. Full guide: [docs/sysadmin/hardware.md](docs/sysadmin/hardware.md)
312	- **Wake-on-LAN** (optional, Linux/physical only, `installWakeOnLan=true`): arm a box's wired NIC to power on remotely from a [magic packet](docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md), persisted across reboots via a `wol@<iface>` systemd unit; send from any machine with the `wake` CLI (`wake <host>`) or `wakeonlan`. Wake-from-full-shutdown also needs a one-time BIOS change (Power On By PCI-E on, ErP off). Full guide: [docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md](docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md)
313	- **Media / AV tools** (optional, `installMediaTools=true`): [ffmpeg](docs/tools/ffmpeg.md), [ImageMagick](docs/tools/imagemagick.md), [exiftool](docs/tools/exiftool.md), [libvips](docs/tools/libvips.md). Plus three zsh helpers (`compress-video`, `extract-audio`, `to-wav16k`) at [`dot_config/zsh/tools/29_media.zsh`](dot_config/zsh/tools/29_media.zsh). Also satisfies `vhs`'s runtime ffmpeg dep.
314	- **System audio & media control** (cross-platform): `sys*` shell helpers — `sysvol` / `sysmute` (built-in, always available) and `sysplay` / `sysnow` (with `installMediaControl=true`, which adds `nowplaying-cli`/`switchaudio-osx` on macOS and `playerctl` on Linux). Enables remote one-key mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`. See [docs/tools/media-control.md](docs/tools/media-control.md).
315	- **.NET tools** (optional): .NET SDK via mise + `azure-cost-cli` (Azure cost analysis); see [docs/tools/dotnet-tools.md](docs/tools/dotnet-tools.md)
316	- **Docker**: OrbStack (macOS) or Docker Engine (Linux)
317	- **Cargo tools**: pueue (process queue manager), [`recon`](https://github.com/gavraz/recon) (Claude Code tmux dashboard — see [agent pane discovery](docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md))
318	- **GUI Apps** (macOS): general terminals, editors, browsers, network tools, and utilities via Brewfile when `installBrewApps=true`, including developer apps like `dbeaver-community` and `superset` (Apple Silicon only); AI desktop apps via Brewfile when `installAiDesktopApps=true` (`claude`, `chatgpt`, `opencode-desktop`, `antigravity`, `codex-app` on Apple Silicon only, `codeisland` notch HUD for coding-agent activity, and `ollama-app` only when `installLlmTools=true`); Steam via Brewfile when `installGamingApps=true`; Tailscale (desktop app **and** `tailscale` CLI) via Homebrew Cask `tailscale-app` — the cask's pkg also installs a `/usr/local/bin/tailscale` wrapper into the app, so there is no separate `tailscale` formula on macOS.
319	
320	### Bootstrap (installed before ansible)
321	
322	- **Homebrew** (macOS): Package manager for macOS
323	- **uv**: Python package manager for ansible
324	- **mise**: Runtime manager for Node.js and Rust (pins versions from `~/.config/mise/config.toml`; upgrade with `just upgrade-mise`, see [Keeping tools up-to-date](#keeping-tools-up-to-date))
325	- **Dev tools**: bat, bats, gh, glab, diffnav, git-delta, git-graph, eza, tldr, [glow](docs/tools/glow.md), [gum](docs/tools/gum.md), [vhs](docs/tools/vhs.md), [freeze](docs/tools/freeze.md), thefuck, zoxide, direnv, yazi, superfile, tmux+tpm, sesh, worktrunk ([workflow playbook](docs/tools/worktrunk.md)), workmux ([playbook](docs/tools/workmux.md)), zellij, btop, htop, taplo, television, pandoc, [doxx](docs/tools/office-viewers.md), libreoffice, witr, figlet, toilet, lolcat, [fastfetch](https://github.com/fastfetch-cli/fastfetch) ([SSH login banner](docs/zsh/motd.md))
326	- **Log viewers**: tailspin (`tspin`), lnav, grc, ccze (Linux only — no Homebrew formula) — plus `catl`/`lessl`/`logtail` zsh wrappers and a `tv logs` Television channel ([docs](docs/tools/log-tools.md))
327	- **GUI Apps on Linux** (`gui_apps` tag on `ubuntu_desktop`): [`gui_apps_linux`](dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) bundles Alacritty (cargo, absolute-path launcher so GNOME does not hide it when `~/.cargo/bin` is absent from the session PATH), AppImageLauncher (PPA with `.deb` fallback, Lite variant for noRoot), VSCode (Microsoft apt repo), Cursor (`.deb`), Google Chrome (`.deb`, x86_64 only — Ubuntu ships no Chromium `.deb`, only a snap shim), Discord (Flatpak default or `.deb`), optional Steam via Valve apt repo when `installGamingApps=true`, Zen Browser (managed AppImage outside AppImageLauncher's watched dirs + stable `.desktop` ID), and `libfuse2` for AppImage compatibility. The role also repairs a disabled GNOME Super key and removes stale user launchers that duplicate a packaged Clash Verge. macOS equivalents ship via [`Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`](dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl) (Arc + Discord + optional Steam casks there). See [docs/tools/appimage.md](docs/tools/appimage.md) for AppImageLauncher install paths, `ail-cli` usage, and Ubuntu 24.04 AppArmor gotchas.
328	- **niri** (optional, `installNiri=true`, `ubuntu_desktop` only): [niri](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri) scrollable-tiling Wayland compositor built from source via the [`niri`](dot_ansible/roles/niri/tasks/main.yml) ansible role (binary → `/usr/local/bin`, GDM session + systemd user units, NVIDIA VRAM application-profile when an NVIDIA GPU is present). Starter config at [`dot_config/niri/config.kdl`](dot_config/niri/config.kdl). Full guide: [docs/playbooks/niri.md](docs/playbooks/niri.md).
329	- **AeroSpace** (macOS, with `installBrewApps=true`): [AeroSpace](https://github.com/nikitabobko/AeroSpace) tiling window manager (cask in [`Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`](dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl)). Config is chezmoi-managed at the XDG path [`~/.config/aerospace/aerospace.toml`](dot_config/aerospace/aerospace.toml) (legacy `~/.aerospace.toml` is auto-removed via `.chezmoiremove` to avoid AeroSpace's both-configs-present error). macOS counterpart to niri on Linux — keybinds (alt + hjkl/arrows, `alt+enter` terminal) are aligned.
330	- **Starship**: Cross-shell prompt (replaces oh-my-zsh theme)

361	## Keeping tools up-to-date
362	
363	`chezmoi apply` is deliberately **install-only** — ansible roles mostly use
364	`state: present` / `creates:` idempotency so re-applying never silently bumps
365	every tool on your machine. For explicit upgrades, use the dedicated entry
366	points (see [`docs/this_repo/upgrades.md`](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) for the full matrix):
367	
368	```bash
369	just upgrade-all          # externals + brew + mise + uv + npm + cargo + go + dotnet + gem + agents + plugins
370	just upgrade-dry-run      # preview without executing
371	
372	# Per category (compose as you like):
373	just upgrade-brew         # formulas + casks (--greedy) + Brewfile (no --no-upgrade) + cleanup
374	just upgrade-mise         # mise self-update + `mise upgrade`
375	just upgrade-uv           # uv itself (auto-dispatches: brew vs self update) + `uv tool upgrade --all` (apprise, mlflow, sqlit-tui, ...)
376	just upgrade-npm          # global npm packages (Bitwarden CLI, readability-cli, ...)
377	just upgrade-cargo        # cargo install-update -a (bootstraps cargo-update)
378	just upgrade-go           # go install <pkg>@latest per go_tools entry (Linux only; on macOS translate → brew)
379	just upgrade-dotnet       # .NET global tools (azure-cost-cli, ...)
380	just upgrade-gem          # Ruby gems (try-cli, tmuxinator, ...)
381	just upgrade-agents       # re-runs install.sh for Claude Code / OpenCode / Cursor CLI / Ollama / llmfit / RTK
382	just upgrade-plugins      # LazyVim :Lazy sync + TPM + claude-hud + pre-commit autoupdate + tldr + gh extensions
383	just upgrade-externals    # chezmoi upgrade + chezmoi apply --refresh-externals
384	```
385	
386	Underlying script: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) —
387	best-effort, prints a `SUCCESS / SKIPPED / FAILED` summary at the end. Full

230	// initCompleteCmd adds a special hidden command that can be used to request custom completions.
231	func (c *Command) initCompleteCmd(args []string) {
232		completeCmd := &Command{
233			Use:                   fmt.Sprintf("%s [command-line]", ShellCompRequestCmd),
234			Aliases:               []string{ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd},
235			DisableFlagsInUseLine: true,
236			Hidden:                true,

238			Args:                  MinimumNArgs(1),
239			Short:                 "Request shell completion choices for the specified command-line",
240			Long: fmt.Sprintf("%[2]s is a special command that is used by the shell completion logic\n%[1]s",
241				"to request completion choices for the specified command-line.", ShellCompRequestCmd),
242			Run: func(cmd *Command, args []string) {
243				finalCmd, completions, directive, err := cmd.getCompletions(args)
244				if err != nil {
245					CompErrorln(err.Error())
246					// Keep going for multiple reasons:
247					// 1- There could be some valid completions even though there was an error
248					// 2- Even without completions, we need to print the directive
249				}
250	
251				noDescriptions := cmd.CalledAs() == ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
252				if !noDescriptions {
253					if doDescriptions, err := strconv.ParseBool(getEnvConfig(cmd, configEnvVarSuffixDescriptions)); err == nil {
254						noDescriptions = !doDescriptions
255					}
256				}
257				noActiveHelp := GetActiveHelpConfig(finalCmd) == activeHelpGlobalDisable
258				out := finalCmd.OutOrStdout()
259				for _, comp := range completions {
260					if noActiveHelp && strings.HasPrefix(comp, activeHelpMarker) {
261						// Remove all activeHelp entries if it's disabled.
262						continue
263					}
264					if noDescriptions {
265						// Remove any description that may be included following a tab character.
266						comp = strings.SplitN(comp, "\t", 2)[0]
267					}
268	
269					// Make sure we only write the first line to the output.
270					// This is needed if a description contains a linebreak.
271					// Otherwise the shell scripts will interpret the other lines as new flags
272					// and could therefore provide a wrong completion.
273					comp = strings.SplitN(comp, "\n", 2)[0]
274	
275					// Finally trim the completion.  This is especially important to get rid
276					// of a trailing tab when there are no description following it.
277					// For example, a sub-command without a description should not be completed
278					// with a tab at the end (or else zsh will show a -- following it
279					// although there is no description).
280					comp = strings.TrimSpace(comp)
281	
282					// Print each possible completion to the output for the completion script to consume.
283					fmt.Fprintln(out, comp)
284				}
285	
286				// As the last printout, print the completion directive for the completion script to parse.
287				// The directive integer must be that last character following a single colon (:).
288				// The completion script expects :<directive>
289				fmt.Fprintf(out, ":%d\n", directive)
290	
291				// Print some helpful info to stderr for the user to understand.
292				// Output from stderr must be ignored by the completion script.
293				fmt.Fprintf(finalCmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Completion ended with directive: %s\n", directive.string())
294			},
295		}

## Recommended implementation

Use one public completion interface, `dev completion <shell>`, backed by Cobra’s standard top-level completion command. Remove the undocumented duplicate `dev shell-init completion ...`. Add a focused local semantic-completion layer, make shell integration preserve the original stdout TTY, publish a source-based Homebrew formula, and only then pin the released version in dotfiles.

Defaults:

- Initial release: `v0.1.0`
- Formula: `dev-cli`
- Installed executable: `dev`
- License: MIT, pending explicit confirmation
- Repository visibility: public, required for unauthenticated Homebrew source downloads
- Homebrew build: source archive with explicit `internal/cli.Version=v#{version}` ldflag
- Release automation: a small tag-triggered GitHub Release workflow, not GoReleaser or cross-repository automation

## Existing-state safeguards

- `/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew` contains unrelated SpecStory changes. Do not stage them with the feature.
- `/usr/local/Homebrew/Library/Taps/daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap` is clean on `main`; create a feature branch before editing.
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi` has unrelated Copilot proxy changes. Create a feature branch and stage only the dev integration paths, or first let the user finish those changes. Never include them in the integration commit.
- `daviddwlee84/dev-cli` currently returns 404 and the local product repository has no configured remote. Repository creation is therefore part of the release sequence, not an assumed prerequisite.

## Phase 1: Prepare `dev-cli`

### 1. Preserve TUI behavior through the shell wrapper

Update `newShellInitCmd`, `posixInit`, `fishInit`, and `App.cdDirective`.

Use a secure per-invocation directive file:

1. The generated bash/zsh/fish function creates a `mktemp` file.
2. It invokes the absolute `dev` executable directly, with stdout and stderr untouched, setting `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` only for that child.
3. `App.cdDirective` writes the shell-quoted `cd ...` directive to that file when the variable is present; without the wrapper, it retains the current stdout behavior.
4. After the executable exits, the wrapper:
   - reads and evaluates exactly one `cd ` directive only on exit status zero;
   - removes the temporary file;
   - returns the original executable status.
5. Keep `DEV_SHELL_INIT=1` for the existing doctor check.

This avoids command substitution around the actual CLI process. Consequently:

- bare `dev` still sees stdin/stdout as TTYs and opens the dashboard;
- explicit `dev tui` can own the terminal;
- `dev ls | grep ...` still sees a pipe and uses normal pipe semantics;
- directory-changing commands still update the parent shell;
- stderr is streamed immediately rather than buffered.

Add tests for:

- normal stdout and stderr passing through the wrapper;
- non-zero status preservation;
- successful directory changes for bash and zsh;
- fish generation and behavior when fish is available;
- `cdDirective` separation from ordinary stdout;
- a PTY/manual smoke showing sourced wrapper plus bare `dev` opens the TUI and `q` exits cleanly.

### 2. Consolidate completion commands

Retain Cobra’s standard top-level command:

```text
dev completion bash
dev completion zsh
dev completion fish
```

Cobra may continue exposing PowerShell as it already does; the supported installation/documentation scope remains bash, zsh, and fish.

Remove the nested command created in `newShellInitCmd`:

```text
dev shell-init completion ...
```

It is undocumented and should not become a second compatibility surface. Regenerate the embedded command reference with `make skill-sync`, then verify it with `make skill-check`.

### 3. Add focused semantic completion

Create `/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/internal/cli/completion.go` for reusable Cobra callbacks.

Because Cobra’s `__complete` path does not call `PersistentPreRunE`, introduce a completion-specific lazy loader that:

- calls `App.Load()` when needed;
- honors parsed persistent flags, especially `--config`;
- returns no candidates on configuration or discovery errors;
- emits no user-facing errors during tab completion;
- performs no writes, runtime operations, status collection, or network access.

Implement this scope:

- **Tasks:** `park`, `resume`, and `done`
  - use `Store.List`;
  - return stable task IDs as values;
  - include title, state, repo, and branch as tab-separated descriptions.
- **Repositories:** `start`, `repo open`, `repo sync`, and applicable `--repo` flags under `wt` and `stats`
  - use `repo.Discover`;
  - return `Repo.Display()` with contracted path descriptions.
- **Worktrees:** `wt open` and `wt rm`
  - resolve the current or parsed `--repo`;
  - use `gitx.Worktrees`;
  - omit detached entries;
  - omit the main checkout for `wt rm`.
- **Embedded values:**
  - `help [topic]` from `help.List`;
  - `gitignore [language...]` from `ignore.BundledNames`.
- **Finite flag values:**
  - root `--runtime`: `herdr`, `tmux`, `none`;
  - `stats --source` and `stats clear --source`: `session`, `git`, `wakatime`;
  - retain existing static shell/cache argument completion.

Return `cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp` for domain values. Leave genuine path arguments, such as provisioning paths, to filesystem/directory completion.

Do not query `gh`, `glab`, remote repository inventories, Git status, or network-backed gitignore names on every tab press.

### 4. Versioning, licensing, release preparation

Pending MIT confirmation:

- add a project-level `LICENSE`;
- update the install section in `README.md` with:
  - `brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli`;
  - the manual `go install ...@version` route;
  - completion generation commands;
  - shell-init setup;
  - `dev skill install` as an explicit optional post-install step, not a formula side effect.
- change the Makefile version assignment so `VERSION=v0.1.0 make build` can override `git describe`;
- add a test that an injected `cli.Version` appears through `dev --version`.

Add a minimal `/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/.github/workflows/release.yml`:

- trigger only on `v*` tags;
- grant `contents: write`;
- run formatting/vet/tests and build with the tag explicitly injected as `internal/cli.Version`;
- assert `dev --version` matches the tag;
- create a GitHub Release with generated notes and no binary artifacts.

This supports source-formula releases without introducing GoReleaser or a PAT-driven tap updater.

### 5. Product validation

Run before any push:

```bash
gofmt -l .
go vet ./...
go test -race ./...
make skill-sync
make skill-check
./scripts/e2e.sh
VERSION=v0.1.0 make build
./dev --version
./dev completion zsh
./dev completion bash
./dev completion fish
```

Also exercise `__complete` directly in tests to prove task, repository, worktree, help-topic, gitignore, and enum candidates work even though `PersistentPreRunE` is skipped.

- source generated bash and zsh wrappers;
- run a `runtime=none` command that emits a directory directive and assert `$PWD` changes;
- verify ordinary output is not buffered or swallowed;
- run bare `dev` in a real terminal and confirm the TUI starts.

## Phase 2: Publish the first product release

### Gate A: repository and license decisions

Ask the user to confirm:

37	    set -l __dev_out (command %[1]s $argv)
38	    set -l __dev_status $status
39	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and string match -q 'cd *' -- "$__dev_out"
40	        eval $__dev_out
41	    else if test -n "$__dev_out"
42	        printf '%%s\n' $__dev_out
43	    end
44	    return $__dev_status
45	end

56	directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
57	working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.

2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in

4	package cli

17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	}
32	
33	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
34	func (a *App) Load() error {
35		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
36		if err != nil {
37			return err
38		}
39		a.Cfg = cfg
40		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
41		if a.Out == nil {
42			a.Out = os.Stdout
43		}
44		if a.Err == nil {
45			a.Err = os.Stderr
46		}
47		return nil
48	}
49	
50	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
51	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
52	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
53		if a.noRuntime {
54			return runtime.None{}
55		}
56		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
57		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
58			backend = a.runtimeOverride
59		}
60		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
61		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
62			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
63		}
64		return rt
65	}
66	
67	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
68	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
69		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
70	}
71	
72	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
73	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
74		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
75	}
76	
77	// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by

79	// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
80	// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
81	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
82		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))

29	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.

34	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
35	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
36	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
37	// descriptors.

40	
41		root := &cobra.Command{

43			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
44			Long:          rootLong,
45			Version:       Version,
46			SilenceUsage:  true,
47			SilenceErrors: true,
48			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
49			// exists to answer.

58				}
59				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
60				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
61				if interactive() {
62					return runTUI(app)
63				}
64				return runList(app, listOptions{})
65			},
66			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
67				return app.Load()
68			},
69		}
70	
71		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
72		pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
73		pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux or none")

111	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
112	func Execute() int {
113		root := NewRootCommand()
114		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
115			msg := err.Error()
116			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.

118				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
119			}
120			return 1
121		}
122		return 0
123	}

33	func newHarness(t *testing.T) *harness {

54		t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".config"))
55		t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".cache"))

2	# Regenerate shell completion files for upstream CLIs.
3	#
4	# Usage:

6	#
7	# Modes:
8	#   default   Skip tools whose completion file is already newer than the binary
9	#             (binary-mtime check — same idiom as 95_bitwarden.zsh / 47_mi_router.sh).
10	#   --force   Regenerate every tool's completion regardless of mtime.
11	#   --quiet   Suppress per-tool progress; still print final summary.
12	#
13	# Output paths (lazy-autoload conventions):
14	#   zsh:  ~/.zfunc/_<tool>                                              (in fpath via dot_zshrc.tmpl:68)
15	#   bash: ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>
16	#         (auto-loaded on first TAB by bash-completion v2)
17	#
18	# Tools NOT handled here (covered elsewhere — don't double-up):
19	#   sesh, tv, worktrunk        → shell-startup mtime check (dot_config/zsh/tools/{22_sesh,12_television,37_worktrunk}.zsh)
20	#   bw                         → cached eval at startup    (dot_config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh)
21	#   marimo, thefuck, try-cli   → cached eval at startup    (dot_config/shell/{29_marimo,27_thefuck}.sh + dot_config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh)
22	#   mi-router                  → tyro self-gen at startup  (dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh)
23	#   fleet, mlf, pqsum, x       → hand-written eager-load   (dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-49_*_completion.*)
24	#
25	# Invoked from:
26	#   - .chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl   (every chezmoi apply, no --force)
27	#   - `just completions-refresh`                                          (manual, --force)
28	#
29	# Skip from chezmoi apply: export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1
30	# Full design: docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md "How autocomplete works" + Section A.
31	
32	set -euo pipefail
33	
34	force=0
35	quiet=0
36	for a in "$@"; do
37	  case "$a" in
38	    --force) force=1 ;;
39	    --quiet) quiet=1 ;;
40	    -h | --help)
41	      sed -n '2,30p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \?//'
42	      exit 0
43	      ;;
44	    *)
45	      echo "generate_completions: unknown arg: $a" >&2
46	      exit 2
47	      ;;
48	  esac

53	
54	mkdir -p "$ZFUNC" "$BASHDIR"

56	n_z_regen=0

59	n_b_skip=0
60	n_missing=0

62	# regen <tool> <zsh-args> <bash-args>
63	# Uses word-splitting on $zargs / $bargs deliberately (the upstream completion
64	# subcommands are 1-3 words, no quoting needed).
65	regen() {
66	  local tool="$1" zargs="$2" bargs="$3"
67	  local bin
68	  if ! bin="$(command -v "$tool" 2>/dev/null)"; then
69	    n_missing=$((n_missing + 1))
70	    return 0
71	  fi
72	  local zfile="${ZFUNC}/_${tool}"
73	  local bfile="${BASHDIR}/${tool}"
74	
75	  # zsh
76	  if [ "$force" = 1 ] || [ ! -f "$zfile" ] || [ "$bin" -nt "$zfile" ]; then
77	    # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # word-split intentional
78	    if "$tool" $zargs >"$zfile.tmp" 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$zfile.tmp" ]; then
79	      mv "$zfile.tmp" "$zfile"
80	      n_z_regen=$((n_z_regen + 1))
81	      [ "$quiet" = 0 ] && printf '  zsh   %-10s → %s\n' "$tool" "$zfile"
82	    else
83	      rm -f "$zfile.tmp"
84	    fi
85	  else
86	    n_z_skip=$((n_z_skip + 1))
87	  fi
88

106	  return 0

1	# 37_worktrunk.sh - Worktrunk (`wt`) shell integration (shared bash + zsh).
2	# https://worktrunk.dev — github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk
3	#
4	# Backend half of the split: shell-init wrapper (so `wt switch` can change
5	# the parent shell's $PWD) + the `wtcd` fzf picker. Zsh-only half lives in
6	# dot_config/zsh/tools/37_worktrunk.zsh (clap-based completion generation
7	# into ~/.zfunc/_wt).
8	#
9	# Companion config: ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml (managed by chezmoi at
10	# dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml). Aliases like `wt sw` / `wt cc` live
11	# THERE, not here — keep this file focused on shell-level integration only.
12	
13	# Skip silently if not installed (Linux ansible install can fail offline)
14	command -v wt &>/dev/null || return 0
15	
16	# ── Shell integration: cd-wrapping `wt` function ───────────────────────────
17	#
18	# `wt switch` needs to change the parent shell's $PWD, which a normal binary
19	# can't do. Worktrunk solves this by writing a directive file that a wrapper
20	# shell function reads and `cd`s to. We eval that wrapper at shell startup
21	# rather than running `wt config shell install` (which edits ~/.zshrc with a
22	# block chezmoi would fight over).
23	#
24	# Same pattern as starship / zoxide / direnv elsewhere. The `2>/dev/null`
25	# swallows the error if wt doesn't support the requested shell (e.g. bash
26	# wrapper not yet implemented in upstream) — the binary itself still works,
27	# users just lose the cd-on-switch wrapper.
28	if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
29	    eval "$(wt config shell init zsh 2>/dev/null)"
30	elif [ -n "$BASH_VERSION" ]; then
31	    eval "$(wt config shell init bash 2>/dev/null)"
32	fi
33	
34	# ── Tiny shell-side conveniences (NOT duplicating wt's own aliases) ────────
35	#
36	# `wt`'s own aliases (sw / ls / rm / cc / oc) are defined in
37	# ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml so they work from any shell + the
38	# interactive picker. Anything below is shell niceness that wt's alias
39	# system can't express.
40	
41	# `wtcd` — jump to a worktree path WITHOUT switching tmux/sesh session.
42	# Useful when you want to peek at sibling worktree files (open in nvim split,
43	# scp, etc.) without disturbing the current pane's session context.
44	function wtcd() {
45	    local target
46	    target=$(wt list --format=json 2>/dev/null \
47	        | jq -r '.worktrees[].path' \
48	        | fzf-tmux -p 60%,40% --prompt='wt cd ❯ ' --header='Pick a worktree to cd into') \
49	        || return
50	    [ -n "$target" ] && cd -- "$target"
51	}
52

15	func newParkCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
16		var (
17			next   string
18			note   string
19			wip    bool
20			push   bool
21			cold   bool
22			keepRT bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "park [task]",
26			Short: "Stop working on a task without losing the thread",
27			Long: `Park the current task (or the one named) so its runtime session can close.
28	
29	Parking is the missing move that makes a crowded sidebar shrink. It records
30	what to do next, optionally checkpoints uncommitted work, and closes the
31	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
32	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.
33	
34	  warm (default)  worktree and branch stay; session closes. Back within days.
35	  cold (--cold)   work is committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstruct
36	                  it anywhere later with dev resume.
37	
38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
41			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
42			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
43				ctx := ctxOf()
44				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
45				if err != nil {
46					return err
47				}
48	
49				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
50				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
51					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
52						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
53				}
54				target := task.Warm
55				if cold {
56					target = task.Cold
57				}
58				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
59	
60				if next != "" {
61					t.Next = next
62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69	
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97	
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114	
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}
124	
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes
133					// the task reconstructible rather than lost.
134					t.WorktreePath = ""
135				}
136				if cold && mode == task.ModeBranch {
137					// Free the canonical checkout for other work. The branch remains
138					// local + remote and resume switches back to it.
139					base := t.Base
140					if base == "" {
141						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
142					}
143					if base == "" {
144						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but its base branch is unknown")
145					}
146					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
147						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
148							base, err)
149					}
150				}
151	
152				t.State = target
153				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
154				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
155					return err
156				}
157				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
158				if t.Next != "" {
159					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
160				}
161				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
162				return nil
163			},
164		}
165		f := cmd.Flags()
166		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
167		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
168		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
169		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
170		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
171		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
172		return cmd
173	}

175	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
176	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
177		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
178			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
179		}
180		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
181		return nil
182	}
183	
184	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
185	// directory when no argument is given.
186	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
187		if len(args) == 1 {
188			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
189		}
190		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
191		if err != nil {
192			return nil, err
193		}
194		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
195		if err != nil {
196			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
197				config.Contract(cwd))
198		}
199		return t, nil
200	}

14	func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			noProvision bool
17			fetch       bool
18			force       bool
19		)
20		cmd := &cobra.Command{
21			Use:   "resume <task>",
22			Short: "Pick a task back up, rebuilding whatever is missing",
23			Long: `Make a parked task hot again.
24	
25	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
26	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
27	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
28	identity.
29	
30	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
33			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
34			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
35				ctx := ctxOf()
36				t, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
37				if err != nil {
38					return err
39				}
40	
41				host := config.Hostname()
42				if !t.OwnedBy(host) && !force {
43					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is owned by %s.\n"+
44						"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
45						t.ID, t.Owner)
46				}
47	
48				if fetch {
49					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "fetch", "--prune", "origin"); err != nil {
50						app.warnf("fetch failed: %v", err)
51					}
52				}
53	
54				rt := app.Runtime()
55				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
56				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
57	
58				switch mode {
59				case task.ModeWorktree:
60					_, statErr := os.Stat(checkout)
61					// Rebuild the worktree when it is gone — the cold-to-hot path.
62					if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
63						base := t.Base
64						// Prefer the published branch: a cold task's work lives on
65						// the remote, and a stale local ref could drop it.
66						if remote := "origin/" + t.Branch; gitx.RefExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, remote) {
67							base = remote
68						}
69						m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
70						res, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
71							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, RepoName: t.Repo, Branch: t.Branch,
72							Base: base, Label: t.Title(), NoProvision: noProvision,
73						})
74						if err != nil {
75							var exists *wt.ErrExists
76							if asError(err, &exists) {
77								t.WorktreePath = exists.Path
78							} else {
79								return err
80							}
81						} else {
82							t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = res.Path, res.RuntimeHandle
83							reportProvision(app, res)
84							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebuilt    %s\n", config.Contract(res.Path))
85						}
86						checkout = t.WorktreePath
87					}
88	
89				case task.ModeBranch:
90					checkout = t.RepoPath
91					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
92					if err != nil {
93						return err
94					}
95					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
96						if st.Dirty() {
97							return fmt.Errorf("cannot switch the canonical checkout from %s to %s: %s",
98								st.Branch, t.Branch, st.Breakdown())
99						}
100						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "switch", t.Branch); err != nil {
101							return err
102						}
103					}
104	
105				case task.ModeDirect:
106					checkout = t.RepoPath
107					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
108					if err != nil {
109						return err
110					}
111					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
112						return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s tracks %s, but the canonical checkout is on %s; "+
113							"switch back explicitly or start a worktree task", t.Title(), t.Branch, st.Branch)
114					}
115				}
116				if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
117					handle, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, checkout, t.Title())
118					if err != nil {
119						app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
120					}
121					if rt.Name() != "none" {
122						t.RuntimeHandle = handle
123					}
124				}
125	
126				t.State = task.Hot
127				t.Owner = host
128				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
129					return err
130				}
131				annotate(app, rt, t)
132	
133				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s  %s on %s (%s)\n",
134					task.Hot.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, mode)
135				if t.Next != "" {
136					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   next      %s\n", t.Next)
137				}
138				if t.AgentSession != "" {
139					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   agent     %s (resumable)\n", t.AgentSession)
140				}
141				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout); err == nil {
142					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   git       %s\n", st.Summary())
143					if st.Behind > 0 {
144						app.warnf("branch is %d behind upstream — `git pull --ff-only` before you start", st.Behind)
145					}
146				}
147				if rt.Name() == "none" {
148					app.cdDirective(checkout)
149				}
150				return nil
151			},

154		f.BoolVar(&noProvision, "no-provision", false, "skip dependency install when rebuilding a worktree")
155		f.BoolVar(&fetch, "fetch", true, "fetch from origin first")
156		f.BoolVar(&force, "force", false, "take ownership of a task owned by another machine")
157		return cmd
158	}

29	Two integration modes, matching the two shapes a branch's history takes:

31	  --ff    rebase onto the base and fast-forward it. Use when the branch's

1	package task
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"io/fs"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"regexp"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	
14		"github.com/BurntSushi/toml"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}

21		Name string

23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).

1	// Package help serves the git-workflow quick-reference pages dev bundles.
2	//
3	// These exist because the hard part of this workflow is not running the
4	// commands, it is remembering which one applies. A page you can reach in one
5	// keystroke from the terminal you are already in beats a bookmark.
6	package help
7	
8	import (
9		"embed"
10		"fmt"
11		"io/fs"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	)
15	
16	//go:embed all:topics
17	var topics embed.FS
18	
19	// Topic is one reference page.
20	type Topic struct {
21		Name    string
22		Title   string
23		Summary string
24		Body    string
25	}
26	
27	// List returns every topic, sorted by name.
28	func List() ([]Topic, error) {
29		entries, err := fs.ReadDir(topics, "topics")
30		if err != nil {
31			return nil, err
32		}
33		var out []Topic
34		for _, e := range entries {
35			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".md") {
36				continue
37			}
38			t, err := load(strings.TrimSuffix(e.Name(), ".md"))
39			if err != nil {
40				continue
41			}
42			out = append(out, t)
43		}
44		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name < out[j].Name })
45		return out, nil
46	}
47	
48	// Get returns one topic by exact name, or by unique prefix.
49	func Get(name string) (Topic, error) {
50		if t, err := load(name); err == nil {
51			return t, nil
52		}
53		all, err := List()
54		if err != nil {
55			return Topic{}, err
56		}
57		var hits []Topic
58		for _, t := range all {
59			if strings.HasPrefix(t.Name, name) || strings.Contains(t.Name, name) {
60				hits = append(hits, t)
61			}
62		}
63		switch len(hits) {
64		case 1:
65			return hits[0], nil
66		case 0:
67			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("no help topic %q; run `dev help` to list them", name)
68		default:
69			names := make([]string, len(hits))
70			for i, t := range hits {
71				names[i] = t.Name
72			}
73			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("%q matches several topics: %s", name, strings.Join(names, ", "))
74		}
75	}
76	
77	func load(name string) (Topic, error) {
78		b, err := topics.ReadFile("topics/" + name + ".md")
79		if err != nil {
80			return Topic{}, err
81		}
82		body := string(b)
83		t := Topic{Name: name, Body: body}
84		// The first heading is the title; the first paragraph after it is the
85		// summary shown in the index.
86		for _, line := range strings.Split(body, "\n") {
87			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
88			switch {
89			case t.Title == "" && strings.HasPrefix(line, "# "):
90				t.Title = strings.TrimPrefix(line, "# ")
91			case t.Title != "" && t.Summary == "" && line != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(line, "#"):
92				// A page may open with a blockquote or a list; the marker is
93				// formatting, not part of the one-line summary.
94				t.Summary = strings.TrimLeft(line, ">-* ")
95				return t, nil
96			}
97		}
98		return t, nil
99	}

1	// Package ignore assembles .gitignore files from GitHub's published templates
2	// plus the entries that every repository on a given machine wants but no
3	// language template includes.
4	//
5	// The split matters: a Python template says nothing about .DS_Store, and
6	// nothing at all about the worktree directories an agent harness creates —
7	// which, left untracked, show up as noise in every status.
8	package ignore
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"embed"
13		"fmt"
14		"io"
15		"net/http"
16		"os"
17		"path/filepath"
18		"sort"
19		"strings"
20		"time"
21	)
22	
23	//go:embed all:templates
24	var bundled embed.FS
25	
26	// TemplateAPI is GitHub's public gitignore endpoint. It needs no
27	// authentication, which is what lets this work before `gh auth login`.
28	const TemplateAPI = "https://api.github.com/gitignore/templates"
29	
30	// Source records where a section's content came from, so the generated file
31	// can say so honestly.
32	type Source string
33	
34	const (
35		// SourceRemote is GitHub's template API.
36		SourceRemote Source = "github"
37		// SourceCache is a previously fetched template on disk.
38		SourceCache Source = "cache"
39		// SourceBundled is a template compiled into the binary.
40		SourceBundled Source = "bundled"
41	)
42	
43	// Section is one named block of the generated file.
44	type Section struct {
45		Name   string
46		Body   string
47		Source Source
48	}
49	
50	// Fetcher resolves template names to content, preferring the network and
51	// falling back through the cache to the bundled copies.
52	type Fetcher struct {
53		CacheDir string
54		Client   *http.Client
55		// Offline skips the network entirely.
56		Offline bool
57		// BaseURL overrides the template endpoint; empty means TemplateAPI.
58		BaseURL string
59	}
60	
61	// NewFetcher returns a fetcher caching under dir.
62	func NewFetcher(cacheDir string) *Fetcher {
63		return &Fetcher{
64			CacheDir: cacheDir,
65			Client:   &http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second},
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// Get resolves one template by name, case-insensitively ("python", "Python",
70	// "PYTHON" all work, because nobody remembers GitHub's capitalisation).
71	func (f *Fetcher) Get(ctx context.Context, name string) (Section, error) {
72		canonical := Canonical(name)
73	
74		if !f.Offline {
75			body, err := f.fetch(ctx, canonical)
76			if err == nil {
77				f.writeCache(canonical, body)
78				return Section{Name: canonical, Body: body, Source: SourceRemote}, nil
79			}
80		}
81		if body, ok := f.readCache(canonical); ok {
82			return Section{Name: canonical, Body: body, Source: SourceCache}, nil
83		}
84		if body, ok := bundledTemplate(canonical); ok {
85			return Section{Name: canonical, Body: body, Source: SourceBundled}, nil
86		}
87		return Section{}, fmt.Errorf("no gitignore template for %q (offline, and no cached or bundled copy);"+
88			" available offline: %s", name, strings.Join(BundledNames(), ", "))
89	}
90	
91	// Canonical normalises a template name to GitHub's own capitalisation where
92	// it is known, and otherwise title-cases the input.
93	func Canonical(name string) string {
94		lower := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(name))
95		if c, ok := knownNames[lower]; ok {
96			return c
97		}
98		if lower == "" {
99			return ""
100		}
101		return strings.ToUpper(lower[:1]) + lower[1:]
102	}
103	
104	// knownNames maps the spellings people type to GitHub's file names. Only the
105	// cases where they differ need an entry.
106	var knownNames = map[string]string{

108		"javascript": "Node", "typescript": "Node", "ts": "Node",
109		"go": "Go", "golang": "Go", "rust": "Rust", "java": "Java",
110		"ruby": "Ruby", "elixir": "Elixir", "c": "C", "c++": "C++", "cpp": "C++",
111		"swift": "Swift", "kotlin": "Kotlin", "scala": "Scala", "haskell": "Haskell",
112		"r": "R", "julia": "Julia", "dart": "Dart", "flutter": "Dart",
113		"terraform": "Terraform", "unity": "Unity", "godot": "Godot",
114		"tex": "TeX", "latex": "TeX", "zig": "Zig", "lua": "Lua", "perl": "Perl",
115		"php": "Composer", "laravel": "Laravel", "rails": "Rails",
116		"android": "Android", "objective-c": "Objective-C", "objc": "Objective-C",
117		"csharp": "VisualStudio", "c#": "VisualStudio", "dotnet": "VisualStudio",
118	}
119	
120	func (f *Fetcher) fetch(ctx context.Context, name string) (string, error) {
121		base := f.BaseURL
122		if base == "" {
123			base = TemplateAPI
124		}
125		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, base+"/"+name, nil)
126		if err != nil {
127			return "", err
128		}
129		req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/vnd.github.raw")
130		client := f.Client
131		if client == nil {
132			client = http.DefaultClient
133		}
134		resp, err := client.Do(req)
135		if err != nil {
136			return "", err
137		}
138		defer resp.Body.Close()
139		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
140			return "", fmt.Errorf("github returned %s for %s", resp.Status, name)

Base directory for this skill: /Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/.claude/skills/agent-history-hygiene

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `probe-specstory-redaction.py`   | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?"   |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

## Core invariants

1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
   history back.

## When to use this skill

Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:

- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
  chat history".
- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.

## When NOT to use

- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
  skip this skill entirely.
- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).

## Integration with existing infrastructure

This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
already has. It does not duplicate:

- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
  config the wrapper expects to find.
- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a
  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo
  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via
  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details
  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).

What this skill **adds**:

- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
  current transcript among many" problem.
- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
  committing.

## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene

Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
chat/plan artifacts.

```bash
# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh

# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
git add path/to/feature/file.ts
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.

# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
  exit 1
}

# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
git commit -m "feat: ..."
```

## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project

For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
installed. Runs once per repo.

```bash
cd /path/to/new/project
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit

# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
pre-commit run --all-files
```

What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:

1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`
   keeps it current everywhere.
2. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
3. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
4. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
   one-line patch if missing.
5. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.

Migrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed
`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):

```bash
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
```

removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
(idempotent; safe to re-run).

## Workflow C: post-leak remediation

When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
committed / pushed a secret":

1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
   become worth discussing.
4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.

## Gotchas

- **SpecStory >= 2.4.0 already redacts on write — plan around it, not
  against it.** Since
  [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) shipped in
  v2.4.0 (2026-07-20), the CLI redacts secrets via the
  [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset **by
  default**, covering both local markdown and cloud sync, writing
  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`. Measured coverage is 36 of 54 class/context pairs;
  15 are ours alone (every webhook rule, plus every custom key in prose
  context — betterleaks catches many classes only in `KEY=value` form via its
  entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule). So: **keep this layer, but never
  rewrite what SpecStory already cleaned.** `redact_secrets.py` writes the
  same `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` sentinel and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so
  a cleaned transcript is left untouched and pre-commit stops demanding a
  re-`git add`. Full matrix + knobs in
  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md).
  Only `[redaction] enabled` is configurable upstream — the PR's
  `extra_patterns` did not survive the Betterleaks rewrite, so repo-specific
  rules stay our job. For SpecStory older than 2.4.0 (or with redaction
  disabled), run `redact_secrets.py --fix --legacy`.
- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
  syntax everywhere.
- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
  `find-session.sh`.
- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
  agent artifacts, not after.
- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
  empty fields signal absence).

- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.

- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.

- **`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`**
  Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers, by
  synthesizing a Claude Code session and rendering it twice (with and without
  `--no-redact-secrets`). Prints a coverage matrix and the residual set our
  layer must still handle. Exit 30 when specstory isn't installed.

- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--migrate] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the current
  repo, wire the hook to the installed skill's redactor, then run
  `pre-commit install`. Audits
  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
  (warns, never silently edits).

## Bundled assets

- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
  regex.
- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
  standard hygiene hooks.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
  agent artifact dirs.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — the redactor, published to consuming repos
  as the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook (root
  `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`). Writes `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`, the sentinel
  SpecStory also writes natively; `--legacy` writes the pre-2.4.0
  placeholders instead. Release procedure in
  `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.

## Reference files

- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.
  Read when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.
- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),
  allowlist design, sync procedure for the bundled redactor. Read
  when tuning rules or debugging unexpected pre-commit failures.
- [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md)
  — what SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts on its own, measured per secret class and
  per context, plus the upstream PRs, config knobs, and why our layer is still
  load-bearing. Read before changing anything about redaction placeholders.
- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) —
  rotate-first runbook for "I committed / pushed a secret". Read
  **before** any `git filter-repo` / `git push --force` action.

## Tests

The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:

```bash
make test-skill
```

- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.
- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git
  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are
  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.
- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).
- `test_specstory_coverage.py` — locks in that SpecStory still redacts by
  default and still writes `[REDACTED:<label>]`; skips without the CLI.

The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each
regression the suite locks in.

## Related skills

- [`project-knowledge-harness`](../project-knowledge-harness/SKILL.md)
  — complementary memory harness (TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/) that
  references `.claude/plans/` as "ephemeral agent scratchpads". This
  skill fills the gap: those scratchpads belong in git, not ignored.
