 `./README.md`

```text
1	# dev
2	
3	A thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
4	
5	It exists to stop four things collapsing into one:
6	
7	```
8	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
9	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
10	herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
11	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
12	```
13	
14	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
15	only what git cannot answer — a task's **state**, **owner** and **next
16	action** — as one TOML file per task.
17	
18	## The problem
19	
20	When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
21	working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
22	So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
23	defeats the point of having one.
24	
25	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
26	the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
27	
28	Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
29	the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
30	expected.
31	
32	```
33	$ dev ls
34	   TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
35	🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
36	🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
37	❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
38	```
39	
40	## Install
41	
42	```bash
43	make install     # builds, installs to ~/.local/bin, installs the agent skill
44	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
45	```
46	
47	Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
48	
49	```bash
50	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
51	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
52	```
53	
54	The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
55	working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
56	directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
57	
58	```bash
59	dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
60	```
61	
62	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
63	degrade cleanly when absent.
64	
65	## The lifecycle
66	
67	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
70	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
71	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
72	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
73	
74	```bash
75	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
76	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
77	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
78	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
79	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
80	dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
81	```
82	
83	### A task does not have to mean a worktree
84	
85	Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
```
</details></tool-use>

2	# End-to-end smoke test: drives the real binary through a full task lifecycle
3	# in a throwaway HOME, with the runtime backend pinned to "none" so no
4	# multiplexer is touched.
5	set -euo pipefail
6	
7	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
8	BIN="${BIN:-$ROOT/dev}"
9	
10	# Always rebuild. The Go build cache makes this nearly free, and testing a
11	# stale binary against fresh assertions is worse than not testing at all.
12	echo "building $BIN"
13	(cd "$ROOT" && go build -o "$BIN" ./cmd/dev)
14	
15	SANDBOX="$(mktemp -d)"
16	trap 'rm -rf "$SANDBOX"' EXIT
17	
18	export HOME="$SANDBOX/home"
19	export XDG_DATA_HOME="$HOME/.local/share"
20	export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"
21	mkdir -p "$HOME/Program"
22	
23	# A local "remote" so the push and cold-park paths are exercised for real.
24	git init --bare --quiet --initial-branch=main "$SANDBOX/origin.git"
25	
26	cat > "$SANDBOX/config.toml" <<CONFIG
27	[paths]
28	scan_roots    = ["$HOME/Program"]
29	project_root  = "$HOME/Program"
30	tries_root    = "$HOME/tries"
31	worktree_root = "$HOME/Worktrees"
32	state_dir     = "$HOME/state"
33	
34	[runtime]
35	backend = "none"
36	
37	[worktree]
38	include     = [".env"]
39	post_create = []
40	CONFIG
41	
42	dev() { "$BIN" --config "$SANDBOX/config.toml" "$@"; }
43	
44	step() { printf '\n\033[1m▸ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
45	fail() { printf '\033[31m✗ %s\033[0m\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
46	ok()   { printf '  \033[32m✓\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
47	
48	step "doctor"
49	dev doctor
50	
51	step "create a repo with a gitignored env file"
52	REPO="$HOME/Program/demo"
53	git init --quiet --initial-branch=main "$REPO"
54	git -C "$REPO" config user.email dev@example.test
55	git -C "$REPO" config user.name  "dev e2e"
56	printf '# demo\n'  > "$REPO/README.md"
57	printf '.env\n'    > "$REPO/.gitignore"
58	printf 'TOKEN=x\n' > "$REPO/.env"
59	git -C "$REPO" add README.md .gitignore
60	git -C "$REPO" commit --quiet -m "chore: initial commit"
61	git -C "$REPO" remote add origin "$SANDBOX/origin.git"
62	git -C "$REPO" push --quiet -u origin main
63	ok "demo repo created and pushed"
64	
65	step "repo list"
66	dev repo list | grep -q demo || fail "demo not discovered"

2	# Regenerate shell completion files for upstream CLIs after every `chezmoi
3	# apply`. Detects tools whose binaries were upgraded since the last completion
4	# generation (binary mtime > completion file mtime → regen).
5	#
6	# `run_after_*` (not `run_onchange_after_*`): we want to detect tools that
7	# ansible / brew / mise / uv upgraded BETWEEN applies. Onchange would only fire
8	# when this script's content changes — that misses every package upgrade.
9	# Cost when nothing changed: ~50ms (presence checks + 28 stat calls).
10	#
11	# Tools handled (the "self-generating" set from docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md
12	# Section A): chezmoi, mise, uv, just, starship, gh, docker, rg, fd, bat,
13	# delta, zellij, pueue, opencode.

15	# Tools handled elsewhere (don't double-up):
16	#   sesh, tv, worktrunk        → shell-startup mtime check
17	#   bw, marimo, thefuck, try   → cached eval at startup
18	#   mi-router                  → tyro self-gen at startup
19	#   fleet, mlf, pqsum, x       → hand-written eager-load
20	#
21	# Manual rerun (--force regenerates all even if cache fresh):
22	#   just completions-refresh
23	#   bash {{ .chezmoi.sourceDir }}/scripts/generate_completions.sh --force
24	#
25	# Skip this hook (cache files stay as they are):
26	#   export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1
27	
28	set -e
29	
30	[ "${CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN:-0}" = "1" ] && exit 0
31	
32	generator="{{ .chezmoi.sourceDir }}/scripts/generate_completions.sh"
33	[ -x "$generator" ] || {
34	    echo "completions: generator not found at $generator (skipping)" >&2
35	    exit 0
36	}
37	
38	bash "$generator" --quiet
39

```markdown
# Context

`dev-cli` 目前只能從 source 以 `make install` 安裝；沒有公開 GitHub repo/tag、Homebrew formula、release 流程或已部署的 completion。CLI 實際是 Go/Cobra（不是 Tyro），而 Cobra 已自動提供 `dev completion <shell>`，但專案又另有未文件化的 `dev shell-init completion ...`，且兩者都沒有被 package manager 安裝或測試。現有 shell wrapper 以 command substitution 捕捉整段 stdout，會讓裸跑 `dev` 看不到 stdout TTY、從 TUI 退化成 plain list。

目標是把 `dev-cli` 以 public MIT 專案從 `v0.1.0` 開始發布；macOS 可用 `brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli` 安裝 executable `dev` 並立即取得 bash/zsh/fish completion，Linux 則沿用 dotfiles 的版本鎖定 `go_tools`。同時把 `dev` 納入 dotfiles 的預設開發工具、completion cache、shell directory-change integration 與工具文件，而且不讓 Formula 在安裝期寫入使用者的 agent skill 目錄。

# Implementation plan

## 1. 先在 `dev-cli` 收斂 shell integration 與 completion

- 在 `internal/cli/shell.go` 與 `internal/cli/app.go` 改寫 bash/zsh/fish wrapper：
  - 每次呼叫建立權限受限的暫存檔，透過 `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` 傳給真正的 `dev` process；binary 的 stdout/stderr 直接連到原 terminal，不再包在 `$()` 內。
  - `App.cdDirective` 在該環境變數存在時只把「原始目錄路徑」寫入檔案；wrapper 成功執行後讀取路徑並以 `cd -- "$path"` 切換，不 `eval` 檔案內容；未載入 wrapper 時保留目前輸出 shell-quoted `cd ...` 的行為。
  - 保留 `DEV_SHELL_INIT=1`、child exit status、即時 stdout/stderr、pipe 行為與可靠 cleanup；確認裸 `dev`/`dev tui` 仍看到真實 TTY。
- 移除 `newShellInitCmd` 下重複且未文件化的 `shell-init completion` 子命令；唯一公開介面採 Cobra 慣例：`dev completion bash|zsh|fish`（Cobra 現有 PowerShell 可保留，但本次安裝範圍為三種 shell）。
- 新增 `internal/cli/completion.go`，以可重用的 `ValidArgsFunction` / `RegisterFlagCompletionFunc` 接到既有 command constructors：
  - task：`park`、`resume`、`done`，重用 `internal/task.Store.List`，以穩定 task ID 為值並提供 title/state/repo/branch 描述；
  - repo：`start`、`repo open/sync` 與適用的 `--repo`，重用 `internal/repo.Discover`、`Repo.Display`、`resolveRepoRef`；
  - worktree：`wt open/rm`，重用 `repoContext`、`internal/gitx.Worktrees`，排除 detached，且 `rm` 排除 main checkout；
  - embedded/enum：`help` 重用 `internal/help.List`、`gitignore` 重用 `internal/ignore.BundledNames`，以及 `--runtime`、stats `--source` 等有限值；domain 值回傳 `ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp`，真正的 path arguments 維持 filesystem completion。
  - completion 只讀本機 config/task/repo/worktree/embedded data；不在每次 Tab 查 forge/network、collect runtime/status 或寫入 cache。
- 修正 `internal/cli/root.go` 的 completion 載入時機：hidden `cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd` 進入 root `PersistentPreRunE` 時，目標 command 的 persistent flags（尤其 `--config`）尚未由 `getCompletions` parse，因此先略過一般 `App.Load`，由 dynamic callback 在 flags parse 後 lazy-load。載入/探索失敗時靜默回傳無 dynamic candidates，仍保留 Cobra 的 command/flag 靜態 completion；執行 `dev completion <shell>` 產生腳本時也不依賴使用者 config。
- 在 `internal/cli/cli_test.go`（必要時拆出 focused test file）使用既有 `NewRootCommandWithIO` harness 測試：三種 script generation、移除 duplicate path、直接呼叫 `__complete` 的 task/repo/worktree/help/gitignore/enum candidates、`--config` 生效、壞 config 仍能補 command/flag、NoFileComp directive；另以 subprocess shell tests 驗證 wrapper 的 stdout/stderr、exit status、directory change、cleanup 與 TTY-preserving 行為。
- 跑 `make skill-sync` 更新 `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`，再以 `make skill-check` 防止 command tree drift。

## 2. 準備 public `v0.1.0` source release

- 新增專案層 MIT `LICENSE`。
- 更新 `README.md`：Homebrew 與版本化 `go install` 安裝、`dev completion bash|zsh|fish` 手動產生方式、shell-init、以及明確 opt-in 的 `dev skill install`；說明 Formula 不會修改 `~/.agents/skills`。
- 將 `Makefile` 的 `VERSION` 改為可由 `VERSION=v0.1.0 make build` 覆寫，並測試 injected `internal/cli.Version` 會由 `dev --version` 顯示；Homebrew source archive 沒有 `.git`，不能依賴 `git describe`。
- 新增最小 `.github/workflows/release.yml`：只在 `v*` tag 觸發，執行 format/vet/test/skill-check/E2E、以 tag 注入版本並 assert `dev --version`，成功後用 GitHub CLI 建立 generated-notes Release；不加入 GoReleaser、binary matrix 或跨 repo PAT automation，Formula 仍沿用 `translate` 的 source-build 慣例。
- 本地全部驗證通過後，另行確認再建立 public `github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli`、設定 `origin`、推 branch/PR。合併後再次確認，才在 exact merged commit 建立並 push immutable `v0.1.0` tag；若有錯誤發布新版本，不移動既有 tag。下載公開 archive 並計算 SHA-256，供 formula 使用。

## 3. 在既有 `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap` 加 Formula

- 先在 `/usr/local/Homebrew/Library/Taps/daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap` 建 feature branch，再新增 `Formula/dev-cli.rb`，沿用 `Formula/translate.rb`：
  - class `DevCli`、public homepage/tag archive URL、實測 SHA-256、MIT、`head` main、`depends_on "go" => :build`；
  - 直接 `go build` `./cmd/dev` 到 `bin/"dev"`，以 `-X github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/cli.Version=v#{version}` 注入版本；絕不呼叫會執行 `dev skill install` 的 `make install`；
  - 使用 Homebrew 官方 Cobra 形式 `generate_completions_from_executable(bin/"dev", shell_parameter_format: :cobra)`，自動安裝 bash/zsh/fish completion；
  - test block 驗證 `--version`、`--help` 與 completion script 可生成。
- 更新 tap `README.md` 的安裝與人工升版順序（publish immutable tag → checksum → bump URL/SHA → lint/install/test → publish tap），保持與 `translate` 一樣不需要 cross-repo secret。
- formula 本地 build-from-source、audit、test 與 completion keg 檢查通過後，另行確認才 push/merge tap；再從 published tap 做 fresh install 驗證。

## 4. Formula 公開可用後再接入 chezmoi dotfiles

- `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl`：保留既有單一 `tap "daviddwlee84/tap"`，在 `translate` 旁新增 Darwin 的 `brew "daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli"`；沿用現有 `trust_bundle_taps`，不新增 trust task，也不改 brew-bundle 的 profile/global skip semantics。
- `dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/defaults/main.yml`：新增 `github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli@v0.1.0` / binary `dev`，讓既有 role 在 Linux 安裝到 `~/.local/bin`、macOS 避免 shadow Homebrew；同步修正只提 `translate` 的註解/升級說明，不另改 playbook wiring。
- `scripts/generate_completions.sh`：新增 `regen dev "completion zsh" "completion bash"`。Homebrew completion 讓一般 brew 使用者安裝後立即可用；chezmoi cache 同時涵蓋 Linux 並統一兩平台。同步更新 `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl` 與 completion 文件的既有 drift：加入目前漏列的 `translate` 與新 `dev`，總數 16、兩 shell stat checks 32。
- 新增 `dot_config/shell/39_dev.sh`，沿用 `dot_config/shell/37_worktrunk.sh`：`dev` 不存在即靜默 return，依 `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION` 執行 `command dev shell-init <shell>`，不依 `$SHELL`、不加 primary-shell gate；只有第 1 步的 TTY-safe wrapper 完成後才啟用。Fish 由 Homebrew 自動 completion 與手動 shell-init command 支援，不塞進目前只共享 bash/zsh 的 layer。

## Approved Plan:
# Context

`dev-cli` 目前只能從 source 以 `make install` 安裝；沒有公開 GitHub repo/tag、Homebrew formula、release 流程或已部署的 completion。CLI 實際是 Go/Cobra（不是 Tyro），而 Cobra 已自動提供 `dev completion <shell>`，但專案又另有未文件化的 `dev shell-init completion ...`，且兩者都沒有被 package manager 安裝或測試。現有 shell wrapper 以 command substitution 捕捉整段 stdout，會讓裸跑 `dev` 看不到 stdout TTY、從 TUI 退化成 plain list。

目標是把 `dev-cli` 以 public MIT 專案從 `v0.1.0` 開始發布；macOS 可用 `brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli` 安裝 executable `dev` 並立即取得 bash/zsh/fish completion，Linux 則沿用 dotfiles 的版本鎖定 `go_tools`。同時把 `dev` 納入 dotfiles 的預設開發工具、completion cache、shell directory-change integration 與工具文件，而且不讓 Formula 在安裝期寫入使用者的 agent skill 目錄。

# Implementation plan

## 1. 先在 `dev-cli` 收斂 shell integration 與 completion

- 在 `internal/cli/shell.go` 與 `internal/cli/app.go` 改寫 bash/zsh/fish wrapper：
  - 每次呼叫建立權限受限的暫存檔，透過 `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` 傳給真正的 `dev` process；binary 的 stdout/stderr 直接連到原 terminal，不再包在 `$()` 內。
  - `App.cdDirective` 在該環境變數存在時只把「原始目錄路徑」寫入檔案；wrapper 成功執行後讀取路徑並以 `cd -- "$path"` 切換，不 `eval` 檔案內容；未載入 wrapper 時保留目前輸出 shell-quoted `cd ...` 的行為。
  - 保留 `DEV_SHELL_INIT=1`、child exit status、即時 stdout/stderr、pipe 行為與可靠 cleanup；確認裸 `dev`/`dev tui` 仍看到真實 TTY。
- 移除 `newShellInitCmd` 下重複且未文件化的 `shell-init completion` 子命令；唯一公開介面採 Cobra 慣例：`dev completion bash|zsh|fish`（Cobra 現有 PowerShell 可保留，但本次安裝範圍為三種 shell）。
- 新增 `internal/cli/completion.go`，以可重用的 `ValidArgsFunction` / `RegisterFlagCompletionFunc` 接到既有 command constructors：
  - task：`park`、`resume`、`done`，重用 `internal/task.Store.List`，以穩定 task ID 為值並提供 title/state/repo/branch 描述；
  - repo：`start`、`repo open/sync` 與適用的 `--repo`，重用 `internal/repo.Discover`、`Repo.Display`、`resolveRepoRef`；
  - worktree：`wt open/rm`，重用 `repoContext`、`internal/gitx.Worktrees`，排除 detached，且 `rm` 排除 main checkout；
  - embedded/enum：`help` 重用 `internal/help.List`、`gitignore` 重用 `internal/ignore.BundledNames`，以及 `--runtime`、stats `--source` 等有限值；domain 值回傳 `ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp`，真正的 path arguments 維持 filesystem completion。
  - completion 只讀本機 config/task/repo/worktree/embedded data；不在每次 Tab 查 forge/network、collect runtime/status 或寫入 cache。
- 修正 `internal/cli/root.go` 的 completion 載入時機：hidden `cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd` 進入 root `PersistentPreRunE` 時，目標 command 的 persistent flags（尤其 `--config`）尚未由 `getCompletions` parse，因此先略過一般 `App.Load`，由 dynamic callback 在 flags parse 後 lazy-load。載入/探索失敗時靜默回傳無 dynamic candidates，仍保留 Cobra 的 command/flag 靜態 completion；執行 `dev completion <shell>` 產生腳本時也不依賴使用者 config。
- 在 `internal/cli/cli_test.go`（必要時拆出 focused test file）使用既有 `NewRootCommandWithIO` harness 測試：三種 script generation、移除 duplicate path、直接呼叫 `__complete` 的 task/repo/worktree/help/gitignore/enum candidates、`--config` 生效、壞 config 仍能補 command/flag、NoFileComp directive；另以 subprocess shell tests 驗證 wrapper 的 stdout/stderr、exit status、directory change、cleanup 與 TTY-preserving 行為。
- 跑 `make skill-sync` 更新 `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`，再以 `make skill-check` 防止 command tree drift。

## 2. 準備 public `v0.1.0` source release

- 新增專案層 MIT `LICENSE`。
- 更新 `README.md`：Homebrew 與版本化 `go install` 安裝、`dev completion bash|zsh|fish` 手動產生方式、shell-init、以及明確 opt-in 的 `dev skill install`；說明 Formula 不會修改 `~/.agents/skills`。
- 將 `Makefile` 的 `VERSION` 改為可由 `VERSION=v0.1.0 make build` 覆寫，並測試 injected `internal/cli.Version` 會由 `dev --version` 顯示；Homebrew source archive 沒有 `.git`，不能依賴 `git describe`。
- 新增最小 `.github/workflows/release.yml`：只在 `v*` tag 觸發，執行 format/vet/test/skill-check/E2E、以 tag 注入版本並 assert `dev --version`，成功後用 GitHub CLI 建立 generated-notes Release；不加入 GoReleaser、binary matrix 或跨 repo PAT automation，Formula 仍沿用 `translate` 的 source-build 慣例。
- 本地全部驗證通過後，另行確認再建立 public `github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli`、設定 `origin`、推 branch/PR。合併後再次確認，才在 exact merged commit 建立並 push immutable `v0.1.0` tag；若有錯誤發布新版本，不移動既有 tag。下載公開 archive 並計算 SHA-256，供 formula 使用。

## 3. 在既有 `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap` 加 Formula

- 先在 `/usr/local/Homebrew/Library/Taps/daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap` 建 feature branch，再新增 `Formula/dev-cli.rb`，沿用 `Formula/translate.rb`：
  - class `DevCli`、public homepage/tag archive URL、實測 SHA-256、MIT、`head` main、`depends_on "go" => :build`；
  - 直接 `go build` `./cmd/dev` 到 `bin/"dev"`，以 `-X github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/cli.Version=v#{version}` 注入版本；絕不呼叫會執行 `dev skill install` 的 `make install`；
  - 使用 Homebrew 官方 Cobra 形式 `generate_completions_from_executable(bin/"dev", shell_parameter_format: :cobra)`，自動安裝 bash/zsh/fish completion；
  - test block 驗證 `--version`、`--help` 與 completion script 可生成。
- 更新 tap `README.md` 的安裝與人工升版順序（publish immutable tag → checksum → bump URL/SHA → lint/install/test → publish tap），保持與 `translate` 一樣不需要 cross-repo secret。
- formula 本地 build-from-source、audit、test 與 completion keg 檢查通過後，另行確認才 push/merge tap；再從 published tap 做 fresh install 驗證。

```text
# worktrunk shell integration for zsh
#
# Completions require zsh's completion system (compinit). If completions don't work:
#   autoload -Uz compinit && compinit  # add before this line in .zshrc

# Only initialize if wt is available (in PATH or via WORKTRUNK_BIN)
if command -v wt >/dev/null 2>&1 || [[ -n "${WORKTRUNK_BIN:-}" ]]; then

    # Override wt command with split directive passing.
    # Creates two temp files: one for cd (raw path) and one for exec (shell).
    # WORKTRUNK_BIN can override the binary path (for testing dev builds).
    wt() {
        local use_source=false
        local -a args

        for arg in "$@"; do
            if [[ "$arg" == "--source" ]]; then use_source=true; else args+=("$arg"); fi
        done

        # Completion mode: call binary directly, no directive files needed.
        # This check MUST be here (not in the binary) because clap's completion
        # handler runs before argument parsing.
        if [[ -n "${COMPLETE:-}" ]]; then
            command "${WORKTRUNK_BIN:-wt}" "${args[@]}"
            return
        fi

        local cd_file exec_file exit_code=0
        cd_file="$(mktemp)"
        exec_file="$(mktemp)"

        # --source: use cargo run (builds from source)
        if [[ "$use_source" == true ]]; then
            WORKTRUNK_DIRECTIVE_CD_FILE="$cd_file" WORKTRUNK_DIRECTIVE_EXEC_FILE="$exec_file" \
                cargo run --bin wt --quiet -- "${args[@]}" || exit_code=$?
        else
            WORKTRUNK_DIRECTIVE_CD_FILE="$cd_file" WORKTRUNK_DIRECTIVE_EXEC_FILE="$exec_file" \
                command "${WORKTRUNK_BIN:-wt}" "${args[@]}" || exit_code=$?
        fi

        # cd file holds a raw path (no shell escaping needed)
        if [[ -s "$cd_file" ]]; then
            cd -- "$(<"$cd_file")"
            local cd_exit=$?
            if [[ $exit_code -eq 0 ]]; then
                exit_code=$cd_exit
            fi
        fi

        # exec file holds arbitrary shell (e.g. from --execute)
        if [[ -s "$exec_file" ]]; then
            source "$exec_file"
            local src_exit=$?
            if [[ $exit_code -eq 0 ]]; then
                exit_code=$src_exit
            fi
        fi

        rm -f "$cd_file" "$exec_file"
        return "$exit_code"
    }

    # Lazy completions - generate on first TAB, then delegate to clap's completer
    _wt_lazy_complete() {
        # Generate completions function once (check if clap's function exists)
        if ! (( $+functions[_clap_dynamic_completer_wt] )); then
            # Use `command` to bypass the shell function and call the binary directly.
            # Without this, `wt` would call the shell function which evals
            # the completion script internally but doesn't re-emit it.
            #
            # The -V flag creates an unsorted group, preserving our recency-based
            # ordering instead of zsh's default alphabetical sort.
            # Note: _describe's -V does NOT take an argument - it just sets a flag.
            # The _describe function internally passes -o nosort to compadd.
            # TODO(clap): Ideally clap_complete would preserve ordering natively.
            # See: https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues/5752
            eval "$(COMPLETE=zsh command "${WORKTRUNK_BIN:-wt}" 2>/dev/null | sed "s/_describe 'values'/_describe -V 'values'/")" || return
        fi
        _clap_dynamic_completer_wt "$@"
    }

    # Register completion (silently skip if compinit hasn't run yet).
    # We don't warn here because this script runs on every shell startup - users
    # shouldn't see warnings every time they open a terminal. Instead, `wt config
    # shell install` detects missing compinit and shows a one-time advisory.
    if (( $+functions[compdef] )); then
        compdef _wt_lazy_complete wt
        # Single-column display keeps descriptions visually associated with each branch.
        # Users can override: zstyle ':completion:*:wt:*' list-max ''
        zstyle ':completion:*:wt:*' list-max 1
        # Prevent grouping branches with identical descriptions (same timestamp) on one line.
        # Without this, "release  main  -- + 12m" instead of separate lines per branch.
        zstyle ':completion:*:*:wt:*' list-grouped false
    fi
fi
```

1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123	
124		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
125		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
126	}
127	
128	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}
141	
142	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}

1	package gitx

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"strings"
6	)
7	
8	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
9	type Worktree struct {
10		Path string
11		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
12		Head string
13		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
14		Branch   string
15		Detached bool
16		Bare     bool
17		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
18		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
19		Locked         bool
20		LockedReason   string
21		Prunable       bool
22		PrunableReason string
23		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
24		Main bool
25	}
26	
27	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
28	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
29	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
30		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
31		if err != nil {
32			return nil, err
33		}
34		var (
35			list []Worktree
36			cur  *Worktree
37		)
38		flush := func() {
39			if cur != nil {
40				list = append(list, *cur)
41				cur = nil
42			}
43		}
44		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
45			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
46				flush()
47				continue
48			}
49			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
50			switch key {
51			case "worktree":
52				flush()
53				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
54			case "HEAD":
55				if cur != nil {
56					cur.Head = val
57				}
58			case "branch":
59				if cur != nil {
60					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
61				}
62			case "detached":
63				if cur != nil {
64					cur.Detached = true
65				}
66			case "bare":
67				if cur != nil {
68					cur.Bare = true
69				}
70			case "locked":
71				if cur != nil {
72					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
73				}
74			case "prunable":
75				if cur != nil {
76					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
77				}
78			}
79		}
80		flush()
81		return list, nil
82	}
83	
84	// WorktreeFor finds the worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git refuses to
85	// check the same branch out twice, so at most one can match.
86	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
87		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
88		if err != nil {
89			return Worktree{}, false, err
90		}
91		for _, w := range list {
92			if w.Branch == branch {
93				return w, true, nil
94			}
95		}
96		return Worktree{}, false, nil
97	}
98	
99	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
100	//
101	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
102	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
103	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
104	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
105	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
106		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
107		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
108		if exists {
109			args = append(args, path, branch)
110		} else {
111			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
112			if base != "" {
113				args = append(args, base)
114			}
115		}
116		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
117		return err
118	}
119	
120	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
121	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
122	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
123		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
124		if force {
125			args = append(args, "--force")
126		}
127		args = append(args, path)
128		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
129		return err
130	}
131	
132	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
133	// were deleted behind git's back.
134	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
135		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
136		return err
137	}
138	
139	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
140	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
141		if branch == "" {
142			return false
143		}
144		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
145		return err == nil
146	}
147	
148	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
149	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
150		if ref == "" {
151			return false
152		}
153		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
154		return err == nil
155	}

15	func newGitignoreCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

17			stdout    bool

20			noEditors bool
21			noAgents  bool
22			noEnv     bool

28			Short:   "Write a .gitignore from GitHub's templates plus the entries every repo needs",
29			Long: `Compose a .gitignore for this repository.
30	
31	Language sections come from GitHub's published templates, fetched once and
32	cached. On top of those, dev adds the entries no language template covers but
33	almost every repository wants: the host platform's junk files, editor state,
34	local env files, and the directories coding-agent harnesses create — a
35	harness's linked worktree left untracked makes every git status in the main
36	checkout unreadable.
37	
38	With no language argument, the languages are inferred from the files present.
39	
40	Everything dev writes goes inside a delimited block, so re-running updates that
41	block and leaves rules you added by hand alone.
42	
43	  dev gitignore                 # detect from the repo's files
44	  dev gitignore python node     # explicit
45	  dev gitignore --stdout        # preview without writing
46	  dev gitignore --no-agents     # skip the harness section`,
47			Args: cobra.ArbitraryArgs,
48			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
49				ctx := ctxOf()
50	
51				if list {
52					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Available without a network:")
53					for _, n := range ignore.BundledNames() {
54						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s\n", n)
55					}
56					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nAny name from https://github.com/github/gitignore works online.")
57					return nil
58				}
59	
60				// Operate on the repository root, not wherever the shell happens
61				// to be: a .gitignore in a subdirectory only covers that subtree.
62				cwd, err := os.Getwd()
63				if err != nil {
64					return err
65				}
66				target := cwd
67				if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd); err == nil {
68					target = g.Root
69				} else if !stdout {
70					return fmt.Errorf("%s is not a git repository (use --stdout to preview anyway)",
71						config.Contract(cwd))
72				}
73	
74				names := args
75				if len(names) == 0 {
76					names = ignore.Detect(target)
77					if len(names) == 0 {
78						app.warnf("no language detected in %s — writing only the common sections",
79							config.Contract(target))
80					} else {
81						fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "detected: %s\n", strings.Join(names, ", "))
82					}
83				}
84	
85				fetcher := ignore.NewFetcher(filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "gitignore"))
86				fetcher.Offline = offline
87	
88				var sections []ignore.Section
89				for _, n := range names {
90					s, err := fetcher.Get(ctx, n)
91					if err != nil {
92						// One unknown language must not lose the rest of the file.
93						app.warnf("%v", err)
94						continue
95					}
96					sections = append(sections, s)
97				}
98	
99				extras := ignore.DefaultExtras()
100				extras.OS = !noOS
101				extras.Editors = !noEditors
102				extras.Agents = !noAgents
103				extras.Env = !noEnv
104	
105				block := ignore.Compose(sections, extras)
106				if stdout {
107					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, block)
108					return nil
109				}
110	
111				path := filepath.Join(target, ".gitignore")
112				existing, _ := os.ReadFile(path)
113				updated := ignore.Merge(string(existing), block)
114				if string(existing) == updated {
115					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s is already up to date\n", config.Contract(path))
116					return nil
117				}
118				if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(updated), 0o644); err != nil {
119					return err
120				}
121	
122				verb := "wrote"
123				if ignore.HasManagedBlock(string(existing)) {
124					verb = "updated the managed block in"
125				} else if len(existing) > 0 {
126					verb = "appended a managed block to"
127				}
128				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s\n", verb, config.Contract(path))
129				for _, s := range sections {
130					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %-14s %s\n", s.Name, s.Source)
131				}
132				return nil
133			},
134		}
135		f := cmd.Flags()
136		f.BoolVar(&stdout, "stdout", false, "print instead of writing the file")
137		f.BoolVar(&offline, "offline", false, "use only cached and bundled templates")
138		f.BoolVar(&list, "list", false, "list the templates available offline")

142		f.BoolVar(&noEnv, "no-env", false, "omit local env and secret files")
143		return cmd

18	func newStartCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

29		)
30		cmd := &cobra.Command{
31			Use:   "start [repo]",
32			Short: "Track work directly, on a canonical branch, or in an isolated worktree",
33			Long: `Start a tracked change stream in one of three explicit modes:
34	
35	  default        create a branch + linked worktree, provision it, open a
36	                 runtime session, and record the task. Safest for work that
37	                 may be interrupted or run in parallel.
38	  --branch-only  create/switch a branch in the canonical checkout, with no
39	                 worktree. Lighter, but that checkout cannot host another
40	                 branch concurrently.
41	  --direct       track the branch already checked out in the canonical repo —
42	                 usually main — without creating either a branch or worktree.
43	                 Best for one-session ad-hoc changes.
44	
45	For untracked ad-hoc navigation, use "dev repo open" or press Enter in the
46	TUI's REPOS view; that opens the project without creating any task at all.
47	
48	With no repo argument, the repository containing the current directory is used.
49	Always pass --base for an unattended branch/worktree task.`,
50			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
51			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
52				ctx := ctxOf()
53				if direct && (branchOnly || noWorktree) {
54					return errors.New("--direct and --branch-only are different modes; pick one")
55				}
56				branchOnly = branchOnly || noWorktree
57	
58				// Resolve the repository: an explicit argument, else the cwd.
59				var repoPath, repoName, category string
60				if len(args) == 1 {
61					r, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), args[0])
62					if err != nil {
63						return err
64					}
65					repoPath, repoName, category = r.Path, r.Name, r.Category
66				} else {
67					cwd, err := os.Getwd()
68					if err != nil {
69						return err

72					if err != nil {
73						return fmt.Errorf("no repo argument and %s is not a git repository", config.Contract(cwd))
74					}
75					repoPath, repoName = g.MainRoot, g.Name
76				}
77	
78				if name == "" {
79					if branch != "" && !direct {
80						name = branch
81					} else {
82						return errors.New("give the work a name: dev start <repo> --task <name>")
83					}
84				}
85	
86				mode := task.ModeWorktree
87				switch {
88				case direct:
89					mode = task.ModeDirect

91					if err != nil {
92						return err
93					}

95						return errors.New("--direct needs a named branch; this checkout has detached HEAD")
96					}

package cli

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/help"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/ignore"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/repo"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

var noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp

// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
// persistent flags (notably --config).
func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
	if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
		return true
	}
	for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
		if cur.Name() == "completion" {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// loadCompletion prepares local completion providers after Cobra has parsed the
// command line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break
// command and flag completion entirely.
func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
	if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
		a.completionLoadAttempted = true
		a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
	}
	return a.completionLoadErr == nil
}

func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
	return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
		for _, t := range tasks {
			description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
			out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
		}
		return out, noFileCompletion
	}
}

func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
	return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
		if err != nil {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
		for _, r := range repos {
			out = addCompletion(out, r.Display(), config.Contract(r.Path), toComplete)
		}
		return out, noFileCompletion
	}
}

func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
	return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
		repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
		for _, wt := range worktrees {
			if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
				continue
			}
			description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
			if wt.Main {
				description += " (main checkout)"
			}
			out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
		}
		return out, noFileCompletion
	}
}

func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
	if len(args) > 0 {
		return nil, noFileCompletion
	}
	topics, err := help.List()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, noFileCompletion
	}
	out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
	for _, topic := range topics {
		out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
	}
	return out, noFileCompletion
}

func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
	names := ignore.BundledNames()
	out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
	for _, name := range names {
		out = addCompletion(out, name, "bundled template", toComplete)
	}
	return out, noFileCompletion
}

func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
	return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
		out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
		for _, value := range values {
			out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
		}
		return out, noFileCompletion
	}
}

func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
	if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}

func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
	description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
	needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
	if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
		return out
	}
	if description != "" {
		value += "\t" + description
	}
	return append(out, value)
}

185	func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
186		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
187		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
188			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+

190				err, config.Contract(checkout))
191		}
192		// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
193		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
194		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
195			return err
196		}
197		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
198			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
199				"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
200		}
201		return nil
202	}

205	// contained in the base — the check that makes cleanup safe.
206	func deleteMergedBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, repoPath, branch, base string) error {
207		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", branch, base); err != nil {
208			return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)
209		}
210		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "branch", "-d", branch); err != nil {
211			return fmt.Errorf("could not delete %s: %w", branch, err)
212		}
213		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   deleted    branch %s\n", branch)
214		return nil
215	}

217	// openPR pushes the branch and asks the forge CLI to open a pull/merge
218	// request. When no forge CLI is available dev prints the push result and the
219	// URL to open by hand, rather than failing: the branch being published is the
220	// part that actually matters.
221	func openPR(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
222		if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
223			return err
224		}

226		f, err := forge.For(kind)

228			app.warnf("no forge CLI for this remote — the branch is pushed; open the request in your browser")
229			return nil
230		}
231		url, err := f.CreatePR(ctx, checkout, forge.PRRequest{
232			Base: base, Head: t.Branch, Fill: true,
233		})
234		if err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		if url != "" {
238			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   opened     %s\n", url)
239		}
240		return nil
241	}

package cli_test

import (
	"bytes"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/cli"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"

func (h *harness) runRaw(args ...string) (string, string, error) {
	h.t.Helper()
	var out, errBuf bytes.Buffer
	root := cli.NewRootCommandWithIO(&out, &errBuf)
	root.SetArgs(args)
	err := root.Execute()
	return out.String(), errBuf.String(), err
}

func TestCompletionScriptsUseThePublicCommand(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness(t)
	for shell, marker := range map[string]string{
		"bash": "__start_dev",
		"zsh":  "#compdef dev",
		"fish": "complete -c dev",
	} {
		out := h.mustRun("completion", shell)
		if !strings.Contains(out, marker) {
			t.Errorf("dev completion %s missing %q", shell, marker)
		}
	}

	if _, _, err := h.run("shell-init", "completion", "zsh"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("the duplicate shell-init completion command should not exist")
	}
}

func TestDynamicCompletionUsesParsedConfig(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness(t)
	h.mustRun("start", "demo", "--task", "auth", "--branch", "feat/auth", "--base", "main")

	id := task.MakeID("demo", "feat/auth")
	out, errOut, err := h.runRaw("__complete", "resume", "--config", h.configPath, "auth")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("complete task: %v\nstderr: %s", err, errOut)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(out, id+"\t") || !strings.Contains(out, "hot · auth · demo · feat/auth") {
		t.Errorf("task completion did not use --config state:\n%s", out)
	}
	if !strings.HasSuffix(out, ":4\n") {
		t.Errorf("task completion should disable file completion:\n%s", out)
	}

	out, errOut, err = h.runRaw("__complete", "start", "--config", h.configPath, "dem")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("complete repo: %v\nstderr: %s", err, errOut)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(out, "demo\t") {
		t.Errorf("repo completion did not discover demo:\n%s", out)
	}

	out, errOut, err = h.runRaw(
		"__complete", "wt", "open", "--config", h.configPath, "--repo", "demo", "feat",
	)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("complete worktree: %v\nstderr: %s", err, errOut)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(out, "feat/auth\t") {
		t.Errorf("worktree completion missing linked branch:\n%s", out)
	}

	out, errOut, err = h.runRaw(
		"__complete", "wt", "rm", "--config", h.configPath, "--repo", "demo", "",
	)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("complete removable worktree: %v\nstderr: %s", err, errOut)
	}
	if strings.Contains(out, "main\t") || !strings.Contains(out, "feat/auth\t") {
		t.Errorf("remove completion should exclude main and include linked worktrees:\n%s", out)
	}
}

func TestCompletionSurvivesInvalidConfig(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness(t)
	bad := filepath.Join(h.home, "bad.toml")
	if err := os.WriteFile(bad, []byte("not = [valid"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	out, errOut, err := h.runRaw("__complete", "--config", bad, "r")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("static completion should survive invalid config: %v\nstderr: %s", err, errOut)
	}
	for _, want := range []string{"repo\t", "resume\t"} {
		if !strings.Contains(out, want) {
			t.Errorf("static completion missing %q with invalid config:\n%s", want, out)
		}
	}

	out, errOut, err = h.runRaw("__complete", "resume", "--config", bad, "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("dynamic completion should degrade quietly: %v\nstderr: %s", err, errOut)
	}
	if out != ":4\n" {
		t.Errorf("invalid config should yield no task candidates, got %q", out)
	}

	out, errOut, err = h.runRaw("--config", bad, "completion", "zsh")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("script generation should not load config: %v\nstderr: %s", err, errOut)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(out, "#compdef dev") {
		t.Error("zsh completion script was not generated")
	}
}

func TestEmbeddedAndFixedCompletions(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness(t)
	cases := []struct {
		args []string
		want string
	}{
		{[]string{"__complete", "help", "park"}, "parking\t"},
		{[]string{"__complete", "gitignore", "py"}, "Python\tbundled template"},
		{[]string{"__complete", "--runtime", "t"}, "tmux"},
		{[]string{"__complete", "stats", "--source", "w"}, "wakatime"},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		out, errOut, err := h.runRaw(tc.args...)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%v: %v\nstderr: %s", tc.args, err, errOut)
		}
		if !strings.Contains(out, tc.want) || !strings.HasSuffix(out, ":4\n") {
			t.Errorf("%v: want %q and no-file directive, got:\n%s", tc.args, tc.want, out)
		}
	}
}

func TestInjectedVersionIsReported(t *testing.T) {
	original := cli.Version
	cli.Version = "v0.1.0"
	t.Cleanup(func() { cli.Version = original })

	h := newHarness(t)
	out := h.mustRun("--version")
	if !strings.Contains(out, "v0.1.0") {
		t.Errorf("version output did not contain injected version: %q", out)
	}
}

package cli

import (

func TestCDDirectiveUsesPrivateFile(t *testing.T) {
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "directive")
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, nil, 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Setenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE", path)

	var out, errOut bytes.Buffer
	app := &App{Out: &out, Err: &errOut}
	dir := "/tmp/a directory"
	app.cdDirective(dir)

	body, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if string(body) != dir {
		t.Errorf("directive file = %q, want raw path %q", body, dir)
	}
	if out.Len() != 0 || errOut.Len() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("file transport should not write streams: stdout=%q stderr=%q", out.String(), errOut.String())
	}
}

func TestCDDirectiveFallsBackToPrintableCommand(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE", "")
	var out bytes.Buffer
	app := &App{Out: &out, Err: &bytes.Buffer{}}
	app.cdDirective("/tmp/a directory")
	if out.String() != "cd '/tmp/a directory'\n" {
		t.Errorf("fallback directive = %q", out.String())
	}
}

dev __complete
if [ -n "$(find "$TMPDIR" -name 'dev-cd.*' -print -quit)" ]; then

else

	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("run wrapper: %v\nstdout:\n%s\nstderr:\n%s", err, stdout.String(), stderr.String())
	}
	for _, want := range []string{
		"streamed stdout\n", "stream_status=0\n", "fail_status=7\n",
		"cd_status=0\n", "pwd=" + target + "\n", "completion-direct\n", "leaked=no\n",
	} {
		if !strings.Contains(stdout.String(), want) {
			t.Errorf("stdout missing %q:\n%s", want, stdout.String())
		}
	}
	if !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "streamed stderr\n") {
		t.Errorf("stderr was not passed through:\n%s", stderr.String())
	}
}

func writeFakeDev(t *testing.T) (path, tmp, target string) {
	t.Helper()
	root := t.TempDir()
	tmp = filepath.Join(root, "tmp")
	target = filepath.Join(root, "target with spaces")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(tmp, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(target, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	path = filepath.Join(root, "fake dev")
	body := `#!/bin/sh
case "${1:-}" in
  stream)
    printf 'streamed stdout\n'
    printf 'streamed stderr\n' >&2
    ;;
  fail)
    exit 7
    ;;
  cd)
    printf '%s' "$2" > "$DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"
    ;;
  __complete|__completeNoDesc)
    if [ -n "${DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE:-}" ]; then
      printf 'completion-wrapped\n'
    else
      printf 'completion-direct\n'
    fi
    ;;
esac
`
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return path, tmp, target
}

```

```yaml
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: true

      - name: Validate release tag
        shell: bash
        run: |
          [[ "$VERSION" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([.-][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]

      - name: Configure git
        run: |
          git config --global user.email "ci@example.test"
          git config --global user.name "ci"
          git config --global init.defaultBranch main

      - run: gofmt -l . | tee /dev/stderr | (! read)
      - run: go vet ./...
      - run: go test -race ./...
      - run: make skill-check
      - run: ./scripts/e2e.sh

      - name: Build tagged version
        run: |
          make build
          test "$(./dev --version)" = "dev version $VERSION"

      - name: Create GitHub release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if ! gh release view "$VERSION" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release create "$VERSION" --verify-tag --generate-notes --title "$VERSION"
          fi

```

_**Agent - sidechain (2026-08-27 16:41:30Z)**_

`high effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`. If the Agent tool is not available in your current tool set, do not error — perform each angle (and each verification) yourself, sequentially, in this context.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

173	 # dev
174	 
175	 A thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
176	 
177	 It exists to stop four things collapsing into one:
178	 
179	 ```
180	 git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
181	 git worktree    a disposable local checkout
182	 herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
183	 dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
184	 ```
185	 
186	 Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
187	 only what git cannot answer — a task's **state**, **owner** and **next
188	 action** — as one TOML file per task.
189	 
190	 ## The problem
191	 
192	 When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
193	 working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
194	 So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
195	 defeats the point of having one.
196	 
197	 The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
198	 the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
199	 
200	 Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
201	 the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
202	 expected.
203	 
204	 ```
205	 $ dev ls
206	    TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
207	 🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
208	 🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
209	 ❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
210	 ```
211	 
212	 ## Install
213	 
214	+### Homebrew (macOS)
215	+
216	 ```bash
217	-make install     # builds, installs to ~/.local/bin, installs the agent skill
218	+brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli
219	 dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
220	 ```
221	 
222	-Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
223	+The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
224	+does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.
225	+
226	+### Go or source
227	+
228	+```bash
229	+go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@v0.1.0
230	+# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
231	+```
232	+
233	+For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
234	+them:
235	 
236	 ```bash
237	-eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
238	+mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
239	+dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
240	+dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
241	+dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
242	+```
243	+
244	+Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
245	+worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
246	+a forge or the network.
247	+
248	+Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
249	+
250	+```bash
251	+eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
252	+eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
253	 dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
254	 ```
255	 
256	-The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
257	-working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
258	-directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
259	+A child process cannot change its parent's working directory, so the wrapper
260	+passes directory changes back through a private file while leaving normal
261	+stdout/stderr connected to the terminal. That preserves the interactive TUI and
262	+normal pipe behavior.
263	+
264	+The agent skill is an explicit, optional post-install step:
265	 
266	 ```bash
267	+dev skill install
268	 dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
269	 ```
270	 
271	-Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
272	-degrade cleanly when absent.
273	+Only **git** is required at runtime. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each
274	+enable more and degrade cleanly when absent.
275	 
276	 ## The lifecycle
277	 
278	 | State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
279	 |---|---|---|---|
280	 | 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
281	 | 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
282	 | ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
283	 | ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
284	 
285	 ```bash
286	 dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
287	 dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
288	 dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
289	 dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
290	 dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
291	 dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
292	 ```
293	 
294	 ### A task does not have to mean a worktree
295	 
296	 Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
297	 
298	 ```bash
299	 # No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
300	 dev repo open api
301	 
302	 # Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
303	 dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct
304	 
305	 # Use a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout, but no linked worktree.
306	 dev start api --task "small feature" --branch-only --base main
307	 
308	 # Default: independent branch + worktree, provisioned and runtime-opened.
309	 dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
310	 ```
311	 
312	 Direct work can be parked WARM and resumed, but cannot go COLD because the
313	 canonical checkout cannot be removed. `dev done` on a clean direct task needs
314	 no `--ff` or `--pr`: the work is already on its destination branch.
315	 
316	 Start direct for one change stream, then create a normal worktree task later
317	 when real parallelism appears. A new worktree starts from committed HEAD; dirty
318	 main changes are deliberately not smuggled into it, so checkpoint first when
319	 the parallel task depends on them.
320	 
321	 ### The dashboard
322	 
323	 Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens three lists, switched with `tab`:
324	 
325	 - **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
326	 - **REPOS** — every repository under the scan roots, with its branch, dirty
327	   state, worktree count and per-state task tally, sorted so anything in flight
328	   is at the top. What do I have here.
329	 - **REMOTE** — repositories visible through the authenticated `gh` and `glab`
330	   CLIs, marked when a local clone exists. What can I open or clone.
331	 
332	 TASKS and REPOS come from the same code paths as `dev ls` and `dev repo list`,
333	 so they cannot disagree. The repo list matters on day one: with forty repositories and
334	 no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just be empty.
335	 
336	 Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
337	 
338	 ```
339	 j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
340	 g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
341	 /          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
342	 ```
343	 
344	 `enter` opens the selected row in the runtime. In TASKS, `p` parks and prompts
345	 for the next action and `c` edits it. In REPOS, `enter` is pure ad-hoc open,
346	 `s` starts an isolated worktree task, and `d` starts a tracked direct task on
347	 the current branch. That makes the branch/worktree cost an explicit choice,
348	 not something every task silently pays.
349	 
350	 **External tools are configured, not fixed.** They run through your shell in
351	 the selected row's checkout; the dashboard suspends and redraws when they exit:
352	 
353	 ```toml
354	 [[tui.tools]]
355	diff --git a/internal/cli/app.go b/internal/cli/app.go
356	index df9ae39..0064e3e 100644
357	--- a/internal/cli/app.go
358	+++ b/internal/cli/app.go
359	@@ -1,86 +1,98 @@
360	 // Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
361	 // flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
362	 // config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
363	 package cli
364	 
365	 import (
366	 	"context"
367	 	"fmt"
368	 	"io"
369	 	"os"
370	 
371	 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
372	 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
373	 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
374	 )
375	 
376	 // App is the state shared by every command.
377	 type App struct {
378	 	Cfg   config.Config
379	 	Tasks *task.Store
380	 
381	 	Out io.Writer
382	 	Err io.Writer
383	 
384	 	// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
385	 	configPath string
386	 	// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
387	 	runtimeOverride string
388	 	// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
389	 	noRuntime bool
390	+
391	+	// Completion requests parse the target command's persistent flags after the
392	+	// root pre-run hook. These fields let completion callbacks load once, at the

398	 // Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
399	 func (a *App) Load() error {
400	 	cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
401	 	if err != nil {
402	 		return err
403	 	}
404	 	a.Cfg = cfg
405	 	a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
406	 	if a.Out == nil {
407	 		a.Out = os.Stdout
408	 	}
409	 	if a.Err == nil {
410	 		a.Err = os.Stderr
411	 	}
412	 	return nil
413	 }

415	 // Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
416	 // --runtime and --no-runtime.
417	 func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
418	 	if a.noRuntime {
419	 		return runtime.None{}
420	 	}
421	 	backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
422	 	if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
423	 		backend = a.runtimeOverride
424	 	}
425	 	rt := runtime.Select(backend)
426	 	if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
427	 		return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
428	 	}
429	 	return rt
430	 }

558	 // fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
559	 // forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
560	 //
561	 // merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
562	 // branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
563	 // a merge commit the user did not ask for.
564	 func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
565	 	fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
566	 	if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
567	 		return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
568	 			"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
569	 			err, config.Contract(checkout))
570	 	}
571	 	// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
572	 	fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
573	 	if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
574	 		return err
575	 	}
576	 	if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
577	 		return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
578	 			"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
579	 	}
580	 	return nil
581	 }
582	 
583	 // deleteMergedBranch removes a branch only when git agrees its commits are already
584	 // contained in the base — the check that makes cleanup safe.
585	 func deleteMergedBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, repoPath, branch, base string) error {
586	 	if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", branch, base); err != nil {
587	 		return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)
588	 	}
589	 	if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "branch", "-d", branch); err != nil {
590	 		return fmt.Errorf("could not delete %s: %w", branch, err)
591	 	}
592	 	fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   deleted    branch %s\n", branch)
593	 	return nil
594	 }

596	 // openPR pushes the branch and asks the forge CLI to open a pull/merge
597	 // request. When no forge CLI is available dev prints the push result and the
598	 // URL to open by hand, rather than failing: the branch being published is the
599	 // part that actually matters.
600	 func openPR(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
601	 	if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
602	 		return err
603	 	}
604	 	kind := forge.Detect(ctx, t.RepoPath)
605	 	f, err := forge.For(kind)
606	 	if err != nil || !f.Available() {
607	 		app.warnf("no forge CLI for this remote — the branch is pushed; open the request in your browser")
608	 		return nil
609	 	}
610	 	url, err := f.CreatePR(ctx, checkout, forge.PRRequest{
611	 		Base: base, Head: t.Branch, Fill: true,
612	 	})
613	 	if err != nil {
614	 		return err
615	 	}
616	 	if url != "" {
617	 		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   opened     %s\n", url)
618	 	}
619	 	return nil
620	 }

857	 // resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
858	 // directory when no argument is given.
859	 func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
860	 	if len(args) == 1 {
861	 		return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
862	 	}
863	 	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
864	 	if err != nil {
865	 		return nil, err
866	 	}
867	 	t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
868	 	if err != nil {
869	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
870	 			config.Contract(cwd))
871	 	}
872	 	return t, nil
873	 }

1447	-// zshInit and friends define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to leave
1448	-// the user *inside* the checkout.
1449	-//
1450	-// A process can never change its parent's working directory, so dev prints a
1451	-// `cd <path>` directive on stdout and the wrapper evaluates it. This is the
1452	-// same mechanism try-cli uses, and it is why `dev` is a shell function rather
1453	-// than only a binary.
1454	+// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
1455	+// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
1456	+// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
1457	+// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
1458	 const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
1459	 #   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
1460	 export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
1461	 dev() {
1462	-  local __dev_out __dev_status
1463	-  __dev_out="$(command %[1]s "$@")"
1464	+  case "${1:-}" in
1465	+    __complete|__completeNoDesc)
1466	+      command %[1]s "$@"
1467	+      return $?
1468	+      ;;
1469	+  esac
1470	+
1471	+  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
1472	+  __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX")" || return 1
1473	+  DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE="$__dev_cd_file" command %[1]s "$@"
1474	   __dev_status=$?
1475	-  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ "${__dev_out#cd }" != "$__dev_out" ]; then
1476	-    eval "$__dev_out"
1477	-  elif [ -n "$__dev_out" ]; then
1478	-    printf '%%s\n' "$__dev_out"
1479	+  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
1480	+    IFS= read -r __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
1481	+    if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
1482	+      builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
1483	+      __dev_status=$?
1484	+    fi
1485	   fi
1486	+  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
1487	   return $__dev_status
1488	 }
1489	 `

1491	 const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
1492	 #   dev shell-init fish | source
1493	 set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
1494	 function dev
1495	-    set -l __dev_out (command %[1]s $argv)
1496	+    if test (count $argv) -gt 0; and contains -- $argv[1] __complete __completeNoDesc
1497	+        command %[1]s $argv
1498	+        return $status
1499	+    end
1500	+
1501	+    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
1502	+    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
1503	+    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX")
1504	+    or return 1
1505	+    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE $__dev_cd_file
1506	+    command %[1]s $argv
1507	     set -l __dev_status $status
1508	-    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and string match -q 'cd *' -- "$__dev_out"
1509	-        eval $__dev_out
1510	-    else if test -n "$__dev_out"
1511	-        printf '%%s\n' $__dev_out
1512	+    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
1513	+        read -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
1514	+        if test -n "$__dev_dir"
1515	+            builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
1516	+            set __dev_status $status
1517	+        end
1518	     end
1519	+    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
1520	     return $__dev_status
1521	 end
1522	 `
