1524	 func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
1525	 	cmd := &cobra.Command{
1526	 		Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
1527	 		Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
1528	 		Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
1529	 
1530	 dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
1531	 "none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
1532	 directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
1533	 working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.
1534	 
1535	 Add to your shell rc file:
1536	 
1537	     eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
1538	     dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
1539	 		Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
1540	 		ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
1541	 		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
1542	 			self, err := os.Executable()
1543	 			if err != nil || self == "" {
1544	 				self = "dev"
1545	 			}
1546	 			switch args[0] {
1547	 			case "bash", "zsh":
1548	 				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
1549	 			case "fish":
1550	 				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
1551	 			default:
1552	 				return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
1553	 			}
1554	 			return nil
1555	 		},
1556	 	}

1668	 // checkoutOf is where a task's code lives right now.
1669	 func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
1670	 	if t.WorktreePath != "" {
1671	 		return t.WorktreePath
1672	 	}
1673	 	return t.RepoPath

1676	 // annotate pushes the task's state and next action into the runtime as
1677	 // display-only metadata, so a sidebar can show why a session is open without
1678	 // anyone having to ask dev.
1679	 //
1680	 // For herdr this lands as workspace metadata tokens. A token only renders if
1681	 // the sidebar row layout in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g.
1682	 //
1683	 //	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
1684	 //	rows = [["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"], ["branch", "git_status"], ["$next"]]
1685	 //
1686	 // Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds and shows nothing,
1687	 // which is why dev never treats a failure here as an error.
1688	 func annotate(app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, t *task.Task) {
1689	 	if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
1690	 		return
1691	 	}
1692	 	kv := map[string]string{
1693	 		"stage": t.State.Label(),
1694	 		"next":  t.Next,
1695	 	}
1696	 	if err := rt.Annotate(ctxOf(), t.RuntimeHandle, kv); err != nil {
1697	 		app.warnf("could not annotate the runtime session: %v", err)
1698	 	}
1699	 }

1701	 func reportProvision(app *App, res *wt.CreateResult) {
1702	 	p := res.Provision
1703	 	if n := len(p.Copied); n > 0 {
1704	 		fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   copied    %d gitignored file(s): %s\n", n, strings.Join(p.Copied, ", "))
1705	 	}
1706	 	if n := len(p.Linked); n > 0 {
1707	 		fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   linked    %s\n", strings.Join(p.Linked, ", "))
1708	 	}
1709	 	for _, e := range p.Failures {
1710	 		fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   warning   %v\n", e)
1711	 	}
1712	 }

1958	 // parseSince accepts a relative window ("30d", "6mo", "1y") or an absolute
1959	 // date. Relative is what people actually type; absolute is what scripts want.
1960	 func parseSince(s string, now time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
1961	 	s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
1962	 	if s == "" {
1963	 		return now.AddDate(-1, 0, 0), nil
1964	 	}
1965	 	if d, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", s, time.Local); err == nil {
1966	 		return d, nil
1967	 	}
1968	 	var n int
1969	 	var unit string
1970	 	if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(s, "%d%s", &n, &unit); err != nil || n <= 0 {
1971	 		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot parse --since %q: want 30d, 6mo, 1y or YYYY-MM-DD", s)
1972	 	}
1973	 	switch strings.ToLower(unit) {
1974	 	case "d", "day", "days":
1975	 		return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n), nil
1976	 	case "w", "week", "weeks":
1977	 		return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n*7), nil
1978	 	case "mo", "month", "months":
1979	 		return now.AddDate(0, -n, 0), nil
1980	 	case "y", "yr", "year", "years":
1981	 		return now.AddDate(-n, 0, 0), nil
1982	 	}
1983	 	return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown unit %q in --since: want d, w, mo or y", unit)
1984	 }

14	
15	var noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
16	
17	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
18	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
19	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
20	// persistent flags (notably --config).
21	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
22		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
23			return true
24		}
25		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
26			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
27				return true
28			}
29		}
30		return false
31	}
32	
33	// loadCompletion prepares local completion providers after Cobra has parsed the
34	// command line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break
35	// command and flag completion entirely.
36	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
37		if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
38			a.completionLoadAttempted = true
39			a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
40		}
41		return a.completionLoadErr == nil
42	}
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
46			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
47				return nil, noFileCompletion
48			}
49			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
54			for _, t := range tasks {
55				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
56				out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
57			}
58			return out, noFileCompletion
59		}
60	}
61	
62	func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
63		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
64			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
65				return nil, noFileCompletion
66			}
67			repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
68			if err != nil {
69				return nil, noFileCompletion
70			}
71			out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
72			for _, r := range repos {
73				out = addCompletion(out, r.Display(), config.Contract(r.Path), toComplete)
74			}
75			return out, noFileCompletion
76		}
77	}
78	
79	func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
80		return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
81			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
82				return nil, noFileCompletion
83			}
84			repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
85			repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
86			if err != nil {
87				return nil, noFileCompletion
88			}
89			worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
90			if err != nil {
91				return nil, noFileCompletion
92			}
93			out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
94			for _, wt := range worktrees {
95				if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
96					continue
97				}
98				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
99				if wt.Main {
100					description += " (main checkout)"
101				}
102				out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
103			}
104			return out, noFileCompletion
105		}
106	}
107	
108	func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
109		if len(args) > 0 {
110			return nil, noFileCompletion
111		}
112		topics, err := help.List()
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, noFileCompletion
115		}
116		out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
117		for _, topic := range topics {
118			out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
119		}
120		return out, noFileCompletion
121	}
122	
123	func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
124		names := ignore.BundledNames()
125		out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
126		for _, name := range names {
127			out = addCompletion(out, name, "bundled template", toComplete)
128		}
129		return out, noFileCompletion
130	}
131	
132	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
133		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
134			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
135			for _, value := range values {
136				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
137			}
138			return out, noFileCompletion
139		}
140	}
141	
142	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
143		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
144			panic(err)
145		}
146	}
147	
148	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
149		description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
150		needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
151		if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
152			return out
153		}
154		if description != "" {
155			value += "\t" + description
156		}
157		return append(out, value)
158	}

 ```bash

+mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions

+
+Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
+worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
+a forge or the network.

+Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:

+```bash
+eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh

-The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's

 // Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
 // flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
 // config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
 package cli
 
 import (
 	"context"
 	"fmt"
 	"io"
 	"os"
 
 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
 )
 
 // App is the state shared by every command.
 type App struct {
 	Cfg   config.Config
 	Tasks *task.Store
 
 	Out io.Writer
 	Err io.Writer
 
 	// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
 	configPath string
 	// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
 	runtimeOverride string
 	// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
 	noRuntime bool
+
+	// Completion requests parse the target command's persistent flags after the
+	// root pre-run hook. These fields let completion callbacks load once, at the
+	// correct time, while treating an invalid config as no dynamic candidates.
+	completionLoadAttempted bool
+	completionLoadErr       error
 }
 
 // Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
 func (a *App) Load() error {
 	cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
 	if err != nil {
 		return err
 	}
 	a.Cfg = cfg
 	a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
 	if a.Out == nil {
 		a.Out = os.Stdout
 	}
 	if a.Err == nil {
 		a.Err = os.Stderr
 	}
 	return nil
 }
 
 // Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
 // --runtime and --no-runtime.
 func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
 	if a.noRuntime {
 		return runtime.None{}
 	}
 	backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
 	if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
 		backend = a.runtimeOverride
 	}
 	rt := runtime.Select(backend)

15	var noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
16	
17	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
18	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
19	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
20	// persistent flags (notably --config).
21	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
22		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
23			return true
24		}
25		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
26			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
27				return true
28			}
29		}
30		return false
31	}
32	
33	// loadCompletion prepares local completion providers after Cobra has parsed the
34	// command line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break
35	// command and flag completion entirely.
36	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
37		if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
38			a.completionLoadAttempted = true
39			a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
40		}
41		return a.completionLoadErr == nil
42	}
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
46			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
47				return nil, noFileCompletion
48			}
49			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
54			for _, t := range tasks {
55				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
56				out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
57			}
58			return out, noFileCompletion
59		}
60	}

63		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {

148	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
149		description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
150		needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
151		if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
152			return out
153		}
154		if description != "" {
155			value += "\t" + description
156		}
157		return append(out, value)
158	}

140	func writeFakeDev(t *testing.T) (path, tmp, target string) {
141		t.Helper()
142		root := t.TempDir()
143		tmp = filepath.Join(root, "tmp")
144		target = filepath.Join(root, "target with spaces")
145		if err := os.MkdirAll(tmp, 0o755); err != nil {
146			t.Fatal(err)
147		}
148		if err := os.MkdirAll(target, 0o755); err != nil {
149			t.Fatal(err)
150		}
151		path = filepath.Join(root, "fake dev")
152		body := `#!/bin/sh
153	case "${1:-}" in
154	  stream)
155	    printf 'streamed stdout\n'
156	    printf 'streamed stderr\n' >&2
157	    ;;
158	  fail)
159	    exit 7
160	    ;;
161	  cd)
162	    printf '%s' "$2" > "$DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"
163	    ;;
164	  __complete|__completeNoDesc)
165	    if [ -n "${DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE:-}" ]; then
166	      printf 'completion-wrapped\n'
167	    else
168	      printf 'completion-direct\n'
169	    fi
170	    ;;
171	esac
172	`
173		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o755); err != nil {
174			t.Fatal(err)
175		}
176		return path, tmp, target
177	}

14	
15	var noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
16	
17	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
18	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
19	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
20	// persistent flags (notably --config).
21	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
22		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
23			return true
24		}
25		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
26			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
27				return true
28			}
29		}
30		return false
31	}
32	
33	// loadCompletion prepares local completion providers after Cobra has parsed the
34	// command line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break
35	// command and flag completion entirely.
36	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
37		if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
38			a.completionLoadAttempted = true
39			a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
40		}
41		return a.completionLoadErr == nil
42	}
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
46			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
47				return nil, noFileCompletion
48			}
49			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
54			for _, t := range tasks {
55				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
56				out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
57			}
58			return out, noFileCompletion
59		}
60	}
61	
62	func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
63		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
64			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
65				return nil, noFileCompletion
66			}
67			repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
68			if err != nil {
69				return nil, noFileCompletion
70			}
71			out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
72			for _, r := range repos {
73				out = addCompletion(out, r.Display(), config.Contract(r.Path), toComplete)
74			}
75			return out, noFileCompletion
76		}
77	}
78	
79	func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
80		return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
81			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
82				return nil, noFileCompletion
83			}
84			repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
85			repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
86			if err != nil {
87				return nil, noFileCompletion
88			}
89			worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
90			if err != nil {
91				return nil, noFileCompletion
92			}
93			out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
94			for _, wt := range worktrees {
95				if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
96					continue
97				}
98				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
99				if wt.Main {
100					description += " (main checkout)"
101				}
102				out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
103			}
104			return out, noFileCompletion
105		}
106	}
107	
108	func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
109		if len(args) > 0 {
110			return nil, noFileCompletion
111		}
112		topics, err := help.List()
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, noFileCompletion
115		}
116		out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
117		for _, topic := range topics {
118			out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
119		}
120		return out, noFileCompletion
121	}
122	
123	func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
124		names := ignore.BundledNames()
125		out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
126		for _, name := range names {
127			out = addCompletion(out, name, "bundled template", toComplete)
128		}
129		return out, noFileCompletion
130	}
131	
132	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
133		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
134			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
135			for _, value := range values {
136				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
137			}
138			return out, noFileCompletion
139		}
140	}
141	
142	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
143		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
144			panic(err)
145		}
146	}
147	
148	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
149		description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
150		needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
151		if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
152			return out
153		}
154		if description != "" {
155			value += "\t" + description
156		}
157		return append(out, value)
158	}

 // Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
 // flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
 // config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
 package cli
 
 import (
 	"context"
 	"fmt"
 	"io"
 	"os"
 
 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
 )
 
 // App is the state shared by every command.
 type App struct {
 	Cfg   config.Config
 	Tasks *task.Store
 
 	Out io.Writer
 	Err io.Writer
 
 	// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
 	configPath string
 	// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
 	runtimeOverride string
 	// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
 	noRuntime bool
+
+	// Completion requests parse the target command's persistent flags after the
+	// root pre-run hook. These fields let completion callbacks load once, at the
+	// correct time, while treating an invalid config as no dynamic candidates.
+	completionLoadAttempted bool
+	completionLoadErr       error
 }
 
 // Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
 func (a *App) Load() error {
 	cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
 	if err != nil {
 		return err
 	}
 	a.Cfg = cfg
 	a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
 	if a.Out == nil {
 		a.Out = os.Stdout
 	}
 	if a.Err == nil {
 		a.Err = os.Stderr
 	}
 	return nil
 }
 
 // Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
 // --runtime and --no-runtime.
 func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
 	if a.noRuntime {
 		return runtime.None{}
 	}
 	backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
 	if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
 		backend = a.runtimeOverride
 	}
 	rt := runtime.Select(backend)

1	package cli

15	var noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
16	
17	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
18	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
19	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
20	// persistent flags (notably --config).
21	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
22		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
23			return true
24		}
25		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
26			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
27				return true
28			}
29		}
30		return false
31	}
32	
33	// loadCompletion prepares local completion providers after Cobra has parsed the
34	// command line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break
35	// command and flag completion entirely.
36	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
37		if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
38			a.completionLoadAttempted = true
39			a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
40		}
41		return a.completionLoadErr == nil
42	}
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
46			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
47				return nil, noFileCompletion
48			}
49			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
54			for _, t := range tasks {
55				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
56				out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
57			}
58			return out, noFileCompletion
59		}
60	}
61	
62	func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
63		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
64			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
65				return nil, noFileCompletion
66			}
67			repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
68			if err != nil {
69				return nil, noFileCompletion
70			}
71			out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
72			for _, r := range repos {
73				out = addCompletion(out, r.Display(), config.Contract(r.Path), toComplete)
74			}
75			return out, noFileCompletion
76		}
77	}
78	
79	func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
80		return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
81			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
82				return nil, noFileCompletion
83			}
84			repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
85			repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
86			if err != nil {
87				return nil, noFileCompletion
88			}
89			worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
90			if err != nil {
91				return nil, noFileCompletion
92			}
93			out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
94			for _, wt := range worktrees {
95				if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
96					continue
97				}
98				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
99				if wt.Main {
100					description += " (main checkout)"
101				}
102				out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
103			}
104			return out, noFileCompletion
105		}
106	}
107	
108	func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
109		if len(args) > 0 {
110			return nil, noFileCompletion
111		}
112		topics, err := help.List()
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, noFileCompletion
115		}
116		out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
117		for _, topic := range topics {
118			out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
119		}
120		return out, noFileCompletion
121	}
122	
123	func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
124		names := ignore.BundledNames()
125		out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
126		for _, name := range names {
127			out = addCompletion(out, name, "bundled template", toComplete)
128		}
129		return out, noFileCompletion
130	}
131	
132	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
133		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
134			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
135			for _, value := range values {
136				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
137			}
138			return out, noFileCompletion
139		}
140	}
141	
142	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
143		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
144			panic(err)
145		}
146	}
147	
148	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
149		description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
150		needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
151		if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
152			return out
153		}
154		if description != "" {
155			value += "\t" + description
156		}
157		return append(out, value)
158	}

@@ -12,82 +12,113 @@ dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
 ```
 
 Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
 only what git cannot answer — a task's **state**, **owner** and **next
 action** — as one TOML file per task.
 
 ## The problem
 
 When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
 working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
 So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
 defeats the point of having one.
 
 The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
 the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
 
 Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
 the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
 expected.
 
 ```
 $ dev ls
    TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
 🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
 🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
 ❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
 ```
 
 ## Install
 
+### Homebrew (macOS)
+
 ```bash
-make install     # builds, installs to ~/.local/bin, installs the agent skill
+brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli
 dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
 ```
 
-Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
+The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
+does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.
+
+### Go or source
+
+```bash
+go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@v0.1.0
+# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
+```
+
+For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
+them:
 
 ```bash
-eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
+mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
+dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
+dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
+dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
+```
+
+Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
+worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
+a forge or the network.
+
+Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
+
+```bash
+eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
+eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
 dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
 ```
 
-The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
-working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
-directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
+A child process cannot change its parent's working directory, so the wrapper
+passes directory changes back through a private file while leaving normal
+stdout/stderr connected to the terminal. That preserves the interactive TUI and
+normal pipe behavior.
+
+The agent skill is an explicit, optional post-install step:
 
 ```bash
+dev skill install
 dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
 ```
 
-Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
-degrade cleanly when absent.
+Only **git** is required at runtime. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each
+enable more and degrade cleanly when absent.
 
 ## The lifecycle
 
 | State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
 | 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
 | ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
 | ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
 
 ```bash
 dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
 dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
 dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
 dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
 dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
 dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
 ```
 
 ### A task does not have to mean a worktree
 
 Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
 
 ```bash
 # No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
 dev repo open api
 
 # Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
 dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct

 // fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
 // forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
 //
 // merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
 // branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
 // a merge commit the user did not ask for.
 func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
 	fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
 	if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
 		return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
 			"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
 			err, config.Contract(checkout))

 	// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
 	fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)

 		return err

 // pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
 func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
 	if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
 		return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
 	}
 	fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
 	return nil
 }
 
 // resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
 // directory when no argument is given.
 func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
 	if len(args) == 1 {
 		return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
 	}
 	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
 	if err != nil {
 		return nil, err
 	}
 	t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
 	if err != nil {
 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
 			config.Contract(cwd))
 	}
 	return t, nil
 }

34		// correct time, while treating an invalid config as no dynamic candidates.
35		completionLoadAttempted bool
36		completionLoadErr       error

39	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
40	func (a *App) Load() error {
41		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
42		if err != nil {
43			return err
44		}
45		a.Cfg = cfg
46		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
47		if a.Out == nil {
48			a.Out = os.Stdout
49		}
50		if a.Err == nil {
51			a.Err = os.Stderr
52		}
53		return nil
54	}
55	
56	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
57	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
58	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
59		if a.noRuntime {
60			return runtime.None{}
61		}
62		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
63		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
64			backend = a.runtimeOverride
65		}
66		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
67		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
68			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
69		}
70		return rt
71	}

10	// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
11	// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
14	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
15	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  case "${1:-}" in
19	    __complete|__completeNoDesc)
20	      command %[1]s "$@"
21	      return $?
22	      ;;
23	  esac
24	
25	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
26	  __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX")" || return 1
27	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE="$__dev_cd_file" command %[1]s "$@"
28	  __dev_status=$?
29	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
30	    IFS= read -r __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
31	    if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
32	      builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
33	      __dev_status=$?
34	    fi
35	  fi
36	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
37	  return $__dev_status
38	}
39	`
40	
41	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
42	#   dev shell-init fish | source
43	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
44	function dev
45	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0; and contains -- $argv[1] __complete __completeNoDesc
46	        command %[1]s $argv
47	        return $status
48	    end
49	
50	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
51	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
52	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX")
53	    or return 1
54	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE $__dev_cd_file
55	    command %[1]s $argv
56	    set -l __dev_status $status
57	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
58	        read -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
59	        if test -n "$__dev_dir"
60	            builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
61	            set __dev_status $status
62	        end
63	    end
64	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
65	    return $__dev_status
66	end
67	`

75	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the

77	directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's

253			Short:   "Remove a worktree checkout (never the branch)",
254			Long: `Remove a worktree's checkout.
255	
256	The branch is never deleted: removing a checkout and abandoning a change
257	stream are different decisions, and conflating them is how work gets lost.
258	A checkout with uncommitted changes needs an explicit --force.`,
259			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
260			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
261				ctx := ctxOf()
262				repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
263				if err != nil {
264					return err
265				}
266				w, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, repoPath, args[0])
267				if err != nil {
268					return err
269				}
270				if !ok {
271					return fmt.Errorf("no worktree for branch %q", args[0])
272				}
273				if w.Main {
274					return fmt.Errorf("%s is the main checkout, not a linked worktree", config.Contract(w.Path))
275				}
276				if dirty, st, err := wt.DirtyCheck(ctx, w.Path); err == nil && dirty && !force {
277					return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes (%s).\n"+
278						"Commit them, or re-run with --force to discard them",
279						config.Contract(w.Path), st.Summary())
280				}
281	
282				// Close a runtime session pointing at the checkout first, so the
283				// multiplexer is not left on a deleted directory.
284				rt := app.Runtime()
285				var handle string
286				if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
287					for _, s := range sessions {
288						for _, d := range s.Dirs {
289							if d == w.Path {
290								handle = s.Handle
291							}
292						}
293					}
294				}
295				m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
296				if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
297					RepoPath: repoPath, Path: w.Path, Force: force, RuntimeHandle: handle,
298				}); err != nil {
299					return err
300				}
301				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "removed %s (branch %s kept)\n", config.Contract(w.Path), w.Branch)
302	
303				// Keep the registry honest about what is now gone.
304				if t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(w.Path); err == nil {
305					t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = "", ""
306					if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err == nil {
307						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "task %s updated — the branch still has the work\n", t.ID)
308					}
309				}
310				return nil
311			},
312		}

315		f.BoolVarP(&force, "force", "f", false, "remove even with uncommitted changes")
316		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "repo", completeRepos(app))
317		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeWorktrees(app, false)

387	func newWtPlanCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
388		var (
389			repoRef string
390			write   bool
391		)
392		cmd := &cobra.Command{
393			Use:   "plan",
394			Short: "Show what a new worktree of this repo would be provisioned with",
395			Long: `Report the project types detected in this repository and exactly what
396	provisioning a new worktree would do — which gitignored files get copied,
397	which dependency directories are copied or shared, and which install commands
398	run.
399	
400	A worktree that comes up broken is the commonest reason people abandon
401	worktrees, and the config alone cannot answer "what will this actually do":
402	that depends on which lockfiles exist, which tools are installed here, and
403	which files are genuinely gitignored. This computes all of it and changes
404	nothing.
405	
406	With --write, seed a .dev.toml from what was detected, so the repository can
407	commit its own setup and every machine gets the same one.`,
408			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
409			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
410				ctx := ctxOf()
411				repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
412				if err != nil {
413					return err
414				}
415				set := wt.SettingsFor(app.Cfg, repoPath)
416				plan := wt.BuildPlan(ctx, set, repoPath)
417	
418				if write {
419					return writeRepoTemplate(app, repoPath, plan, set)
420				}
421				renderPlan(app, plan, repoPath)
422				return nil
423			},
424		}
425		f := cmd.Flags()
426		f.StringVarP(&repoRef, "repo", "r", "", "repository (default: the current one)")
427		f.BoolVar(&write, "write", false, "seed a .dev.toml in the repository from what was detected")
428		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "repo", completeRepos(app))
429		return cmd
430	}
431	
432	// renderPlan prints a provisioning plan as a table plus its warnings.
433	func renderPlan(app *App, plan wt.Plan, repoPath string) {
434		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n\n", config.Contract(repoPath))
435	
436		if len(plan.Ecosystems) == 0 {
437			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No project type detected — only gitignored files will be carried over.")
438		} else {
439			t := NewTable("PROJECT", "MANAGER", "FROM", "DEPENDENCIES", "TOOL")
440			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
441				deps := "—"
442				if len(e.DepDirs) > 0 {
443					deps = strings.Join(e.DepDirs, ", ")
444				} else {
445					deps = "global cache"
446				}
447				tool := "installed"
448				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
449					tool = "MISSING: " + e.Tool
450				}
451				t.Add(e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, deps, tool)
452			}
453			t.Render(app.Out)
454		}
455	
456		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
457		if len(plan.Steps) == 0 {
458			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to provision.")
459		} else {
460			st := NewTable("", "ACTION", "WHAT", "WHY")
461			for _, s := range plan.Steps {
462				mark := "✓"
463				if s.Skipped {
464					mark = "·"
465				}
466				st.Add(mark, string(s.Kind), truncate(s.What, 34), s.Why)
467			}
468			st.Render(app.Out)
469		}
470	
471		for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
472			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\nwarning: %s\n", w)
473		}
474		if plan.Empty() {
475			fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "\nNothing would run. If a new worktree comes up broken, add what it needs to "+
476				"worktree.post_create, or commit a .dev.toml with `dev wt plan --write`.")
477		}
478	}
479	
480	// writeRepoTemplate seeds a .dev.toml from the detected plan.
481	//
482	// Committing it is what makes a project's worktree setup reproducible: the
483	// next machine, and the next person, get the same one without having to
484	// rediscover it.
485	func writeRepoTemplate(app *App, repoPath string, plan wt.Plan, set wt.Settings) error {
486		path := filepath.Join(repoPath, wt.OverrideFilename)
487		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
488			return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists — edit it directly", config.Contract(path))
489		}
490	
491		var b strings.Builder
492		b.WriteString("# dev worktree setup for this repository.\n")
493		b.WriteString("#\n")
494		b.WriteString("# Committed on purpose: a worktree is a clean checkout, so without this a\n")
495		b.WriteString("# new one comes up with no dependencies and none of the gitignored files the\n")
496		b.WriteString("# project needs. Seeded by `dev wt plan --write`; edit freely.\n\n")
497		b.WriteString("[worktree]\n")
498	
499		b.WriteString("# Gitignored files to carry into a new worktree. Only files that are BOTH\n")
500		b.WriteString("# listed here AND gitignored are copied — a tracked file is already in the\n")
501		b.WriteString("# checkout on the correct branch.\n")
502		b.WriteString("include = [")
503		for i, inc := range set.Include {
504			if i > 0 {
505				b.WriteString(", ")
506			}
507			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%q", inc)
508		}
509		b.WriteString("]\n\n")
510	
511		if len(plan.Ecosystems) > 0 {
512			b.WriteString("# Detected in this repository:\n")
513			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
514				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "#   %-8s %-8s (%s) → %s\n", e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, e.Install)
515			}
516			b.WriteString("#\n")
517			b.WriteString("# \"auto\" runs those install commands. Replace with an explicit list if this\n")
518			b.WriteString("# project needs something else:  post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
519			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n\n")
520	
521			b.WriteString("# How each project type gets its dependencies:\n")
522			b.WriteString("#   reinstall  run the install command (correct, the default)\n")
523			b.WriteString("#   copy       duplicate the directory from the source checkout (fast)\n")
524			b.WriteString("#   link       share one directory between checkouts (fastest, risky)\n")
525			b.WriteString("#   skip       leave the worktree without dependencies\n")
526			b.WriteString("[worktree.strategies]\n")
527			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
528				switch {
529				case len(e.DepDirs) == 0:
530					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# %-8s = \"reinstall\"  # %s uses a global cache; nothing to copy\n",
531						e.Name, e.Manager)
532				case e.CopySafe:
533					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # \"copy\" is sound here and much faster\n", e.Name)
534				default:
535					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # copy/link unsupported: %s\n", e.Name, e.Hazard)
536				}
537			}
538		} else {
539			b.WriteString("# No project type detected. Add the commands a fresh checkout needs:\n")
540			b.WriteString("# post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
541			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n")
542		}
543	
544		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
545			return err
546		}
547		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "wrote %s\n", config.Contract(path))
548		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Commit it so every machine provisions worktrees the same way.")
549		return nil
550	}
551

268	func newRepoSyncCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
269		var all bool
270		cmd := &cobra.Command{
271			Use:   "sync [repo]",
272			Short: "Fetch and prune, reporting what moved",
273			Long: `Fetch from origin and prune deleted remote-tracking refs.
274	
275	Deliberately not a pull: dev reports how each branch stands and leaves the
276	decision to you, because a pull that quietly merges or rebases is how a
277	history gets a shape nobody intended.`,
278			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
279			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
280				ctx := ctxOf()
281				var targets []repo.Repo
282				switch {
283				case all:
284					var err error
285					targets, err = repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
286					if err != nil {
287						return err
288					}
289				case len(args) == 1:
290					r, _, err := resolveRepoRef(app, args[0])
291					if err != nil {
292						return err
293					}
294					targets = []repo.Repo{r}
295				default:
296					path, name, err := repoContext(app, "")
297					if err != nil {
298						return err
299					}
300					targets = []repo.Repo{{Name: name, Path: path}}
301				}
302	
303				t := NewTable("REPO", "BRANCH", "GIT", "NOTE")
304				for _, r := range targets {
305					if r.Bare {
306						continue
307					}
308					note := ""
309					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, r.Path, "fetch", "--prune", "--quiet", "origin"); err != nil {
310						note = "fetch failed (no remote?)"
311					}
312					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
313					if err != nil {
314						continue
315					}
316					if note == "" {
317						switch {
318						case st.Behind > 0 && st.Ahead > 0:
319							note = "diverged — rebase or merge explicitly"
320						case st.Behind > 0 && !st.Dirty():
321							note = "behind — git pull --ff-only"
322						case st.Behind > 0:
323							note = "behind, and dirty — commit first"
324						case st.Ahead > 0:
325							note = "unpushed commits"
326						}
327					}
328					t.Add(truncate(r.Name, 28), truncate(st.Branch, 24), st.Summary(), note)
329				}
330				t.Render(app.Out)
331				return nil
332			},
333		}
334		cmd.Flags().BoolVarP(&all, "all", "a", false, "every repository under the scan roots")
335		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeRepos(app)
336		return cmd
337	}

339	// repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.
340	func repoNameFromRef(ref string) string {
341		ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")
342		if i := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:"); i >= 0 {
343			return ref[i+1:]
344		}
345		return ref
346	}
347	
348	func contractAll(paths []string) []string {
349		out := make([]string, len(paths))
350		for i, p := range paths {
351			out[i] = config.Contract(p)
352		}
353		return out
354	}

356	func newRepoRemoteCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
357		var (
358			jsonOut    bool
359			cachedOnly bool
360			limit      int
361		)
362		cmd := &cobra.Command{
363			Use:     "remote [query]",
364			Aliases: []string{"search"},
365			Short:   "List and search repositories visible through gh and glab",
366			Long: `Combine the repositories visible to the authenticated gh and glab CLIs, and
367	mark those already cloned under paths.scan_roots.
368	
369	The TUI exposes the same data in its REMOTE tab and filters it live with /.
370	This command is the non-interactive form for scripts, pipes and terminals where
371	a full-screen UI is not wanted. Use --cached for an instant, offline result;
372	the cache is private and expires according to forge.cache_ttl.`,
373			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
374			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
375				var (
376					rows []tui.RemoteRow
377					err  error
378				)
379				if cachedOnly {
380					var ok bool
381					rows, ok = cachedRemotes(ctxOf(), app)
382					if !ok {
383						return fmt.Errorf("no fresh remote cache; run `dev repo remote` once online")
384					}
385				} else {
386					rows, err = collectRemotes(ctxOf(), app, limit)
387				}
388				// Partial results are useful when one forge is authenticated and
389				// the other is not. Render them, then report the partial failure.
390				if len(rows) == 0 && err != nil {
391					return err
392				}
393				query := ""
394				if len(args) == 1 {
395					query = strings.ToLower(args[0])
396				}
397				var filtered []tui.RemoteRow
398				for _, r := range rows {
399					hay := strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
400						string(r.Repo.Forge), r.Repo.FullName, r.Repo.Description,
401						r.Repo.Visibility, r.LocalName,
402					}, " "))
403					matched := true
404					for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
405						if !strings.Contains(hay, term) {
406							matched = false
407							break
408						}
409					}
410					if matched {
411						filtered = append(filtered, r)
412					}
413				}
414	
415				if jsonOut {
416					enc := json.NewEncoder(app.Out)
417					enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
418					if encodeErr := enc.Encode(filtered); encodeErr != nil {
419						return encodeErr
420					}
421				} else {
422					t := NewTable("FORGE", "REPOSITORY", "VIS", "LOCAL", "UPDATED", "DESCRIPTION")
423					for _, r := range filtered {
424						local := "—"
425						if r.LocalPath != "" {
426							local = config.Contract(r.LocalPath)
427						}
428						updated := "—"
429						if !r.Repo.UpdatedAt.IsZero() {
430							updated = r.Repo.UpdatedAt.Format("2006-01-02")
431						}
432						t.Add(string(r.Repo.Forge), truncate(r.Repo.FullName, 36),
433							strings.ToLower(r.Repo.Visibility), truncate(local, 30), updated,
434							truncate(r.Repo.Description, 50))
435					}
436					if t.Len() == 0 {
437						fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No remote repositories match that query.")
438					} else {
439						t.Render(app.Out)
440					}
441				}
442				if err != nil {
443					app.warnf("partial remote results: %v", err)
444				}
445				return nil
446			},
447		}
448		f := cmd.Flags()
449		f.BoolVar(&jsonOut, "json", false, "emit JSON")
450		f.BoolVar(&cachedOnly, "cached", false, "use the fresh XDG cache without querying either forge")
451		f.IntVar(&limit, "limit", 0, "maximum repositories requested from each forge (default: config forge.remote_limit)")
452		return cmd
453	}

246					return err
247				}
248				store, err := stats.Open(stats.Path(app.Cfg.StateDir()))
249				if err != nil {
250					return err
251				}
252				defer store.Close()
253	
254				until := time.Now()
255				start, err := parseSince(since, until)
256				if err != nil {
257					return err
258				}
259				w := &stats.WakaTime{APIKey: key}
260				n, err := w.Import(ctx, store, start, until)
261				if err != nil {
262					return err
263				}
264				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "imported %d project-days from WakaTime\n", n)
265				return nil
266			},
267		}
268		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&since, "since", "6mo", "how far back to import")
269		return cmd
270	}
271	
272	// parseSince accepts a relative window ("30d", "6mo", "1y") or an absolute
273	// date. Relative is what people actually type; absolute is what scripts want.
274	func parseSince(s string, now time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
275		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
276		if s == "" {
277			return now.AddDate(-1, 0, 0), nil
278		}
279		if d, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", s, time.Local); err == nil {
280			return d, nil
281		}
282		var n int
283		var unit string
284		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(s, "%d%s", &n, &unit); err != nil || n <= 0 {
285			return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot parse --since %q: want 30d, 6mo, 1y or YYYY-MM-DD", s)
286		}
287		switch strings.ToLower(unit) {
288		case "d", "day", "days":
289			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n), nil
290		case "w", "week", "weeks":
291			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n*7), nil
292		case "mo", "month", "months":
293			return now.AddDate(0, -n, 0), nil
294		case "y", "yr", "year", "years":
295			return now.AddDate(-n, 0, 0), nil
296		}
297		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown unit %q in --since: want d, w, mo or y", unit)
298	}
299

12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.

16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1

19	    __complete|__completeNoDesc)

21	      return $?
22	      ;;
23	  esac
24	
25	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
26	  __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX")" || return 1
27	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE="$__dev_cd_file" command %[1]s "$@"
28	  __dev_status=$?
29	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
30	    IFS= read -r __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
31	    if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
32	      builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
33	      __dev_status=$?
34	    fi
35	  fi
36	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
37	  return $__dev_status
38	}
39	`

41	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
42	#   dev shell-init fish | source
43	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
44	function dev
45	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0; and contains -- $argv[1] __complete __completeNoDesc
46	        command %[1]s $argv
47	        return $status
48	    end
49	
50	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
51	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
52	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX")
53	    or return 1
54	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE $__dev_cd_file
55	    command %[1]s $argv
56	    set -l __dev_status $status
57	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
58	        read -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
59	        if test -n "$__dev_dir"
60	            builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
61	            set __dev_status $status
62	        end
63	    end
64	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
65	    return $__dev_status
66	end
67	`
68	
69	func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
70		cmd := &cobra.Command{
71			Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
72			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
73			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
74	
75	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
76	"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
77	directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
78	working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.
79	
80	Add to your shell rc file:
81	
82	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
83	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
84			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
85			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
86			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
87				self, err := os.Executable()
88				if err != nil || self == "" {
89					self = "dev"
90				}
91				switch args[0] {
92				case "bash", "zsh":
93					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
94				case "fish":
95					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
96				default:
97					return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
98				}
99				return nil
100			},
101		}
102		return cmd
103	}

14	// Version is set at build time via -ldflags. VersionFromBuild also recovers a
15	// module version for `go install ...@version` builds.
16	var Version = "dev"
17	
18	func versionFromBuild() string {
19		if Version != "dev" {
20			return Version
21		}
22		if info, ok := debug.ReadBuildInfo(); ok && info.Main.Version != "" && info.Main.Version != "(devel)" {
23			return info.Main.Version
24		}
25		return Version
26	}

28	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
29	
30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
31	
32	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
33	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
34	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
35	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
36	
37	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
38	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
39	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`
40	
41	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
42	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
43		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
44	}
45	
46	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
47	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
48	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
49	// descriptors.
50	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
51		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
52	
53		root := &cobra.Command{
54			Use:           "dev",
55			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
56			Long:          rootLong,
57			Version:       versionFromBuild(),
58			SilenceUsage:  true,
59			SilenceErrors: true,
60			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
61			// exists to answer.
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
64					out, err := skill.Render()
65					if err != nil {
66						return err
67					}
68					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
69					return nil
70				}
71				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
72				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
73				if interactive() {
74					return runTUI(app)
75				}
76				return runList(app, listOptions{})
77			},
78			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
79				if completionInvocation(cmd) {
80					return nil
81				}
82				return app.Load()
83			},
84		}
85	
86		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
87		pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
88		pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux or none")
89		pf.BoolVar(&app.noRuntime, "no-runtime", false, "do not touch any terminal multiplexer")
90		registerFlagCompletion(root, "runtime", fixedCompletions("herdr", "tmux", "none"))
91	
92		// Mirrors `herdr --skill`: the binary is the authority for its own agent
93		// skill, so a dotfiles installer can sync it without vendoring a copy.
94		root.Flags().Bool("skill", false, "print the bundled agent skill and exit")
95	
96		root.AddCommand(
97			newListCmd(app),
98			newTUICmd(app),
99			newStatusCmd(app),
100			newStartCmd(app),
101			newParkCmd(app),
102			newResumeCmd(app),
103			newDoneCmd(app),
104			newSweepCmd(app),
105			newAdoptCmd(app),
106			newBootstrapCmd(app),
107			newWorktreeCmd(app),
108			newRepoCmd(app),
109			newGitignoreCmd(app),
110			newTryCmd(app),
111			newGraduateCmd(app),
112			newStatsCmd(app),
113			newHelpTopicCmd(app),
114			newSkillCmd(app),
115			newDoctorCmd(app),
116			newShellInitCmd(app),
117			newConfigCmd(app),
118			newCacheCmd(app),
119			newEditCmd(app),
120		)
121		root.SetHelpCommand(&cobra.Command{Hidden: true, Use: "no-help"})
122		root.SetOut(out)
123		root.SetErr(errOut)
124		return root
125	}
126	
127	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
128	func Execute() int {
129		root := NewRootCommand()
130		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
131			msg := err.Error()
132			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
133			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
134				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
135			}
136			return 1
137		}
138		return 0
139	}

```text
1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	
32		// Completion requests parse the target command's persistent flags after the
33		// root pre-run hook. These fields let completion callbacks load once, at the
34		// correct time, while treating an invalid config as no dynamic candidates.
35		completionLoadAttempted bool
36		completionLoadErr       error
37	}
38	
39	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
40	func (a *App) Load() error {
41		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
42		if err != nil {
43			return err
44		}
45		a.Cfg = cfg
46		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
47		if a.Out == nil {
48			a.Out = os.Stdout
49		}
50		if a.Err == nil {
51			a.Err = os.Stderr
52		}
53		return nil
54	}
55	
56	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
57	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
58	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
59		if a.noRuntime {
60			return runtime.None{}
61		}
62		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
63		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
64			backend = a.runtimeOverride
65		}
66		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
67		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
68			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
69		}
70		return rt
71	}
72	
73	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
74	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
76	}
77	
78	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
79	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
80		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
81	}
82	
83	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
84	// gives dev a private file so normal command output can keep flowing directly
85	// to the terminal; without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by
86	// scripts and older integrations.
87	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
88		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
89			if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(dir), 0o600); err != nil {
90				a.warnf("could not write shell directory directive: %v", err)
91			}
92			return
93		}
94		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
95	}
96	
97	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
98	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
99

123		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
124		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
125			t.Fatalf("run wrapper: %v\nstdout:\n%s\nstderr:\n%s", err, stdout.String(), stderr.String())
126		}
127		for _, want := range []string{
128			"streamed stdout\n", "stream_status=0\n", "fail_status=7\n",
129			"cd_status=0\n", "pwd=" + target + "\n", "completion-direct\n", "leaked=no\n",
130		} {
131			if !strings.Contains(stdout.String(), want) {
132				t.Errorf("stdout missing %q:\n%s", want, stdout.String())
133			}
134		}
135		if !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "streamed stderr\n") {
136			t.Errorf("stderr was not passed through:\n%s", stderr.String())
137		}
138	}
139	
140	func writeFakeDev(t *testing.T) (path, tmp, target string) {
141		t.Helper()
142		root := t.TempDir()
143		tmp = filepath.Join(root, "tmp")
144		target = filepath.Join(root, "target with spaces")
145		if err := os.MkdirAll(tmp, 0o755); err != nil {
146			t.Fatal(err)
147		}
148		if err := os.MkdirAll(target, 0o755); err != nil {
149			t.Fatal(err)
150		}
151		path = filepath.Join(root, "fake dev")
152		body := `#!/bin/sh
153	case "${1:-}" in
154	  stream)
155	    printf 'streamed stdout\n'
156	    printf 'streamed stderr\n' >&2
157	    ;;
158	  fail)
159	    exit 7
160	    ;;
161	  cd)
162	    printf '%s' "$2" > "$DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"
163	    ;;
164	  __complete|__completeNoDesc)
165	    if [ -n "${DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE:-}" ]; then
166	      printf 'completion-wrapped\n'
167	    else
168	      printf 'completion-direct\n'
169	    fi
170	    ;;
171	esac
172	`
173		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o755); err != nil {
174			t.Fatal(err)
175		}
176		return path, tmp, target
177	}

2469	 func renderPlan(app *App, plan wt.Plan, repoPath string) {
2470	 	fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n\n", config.Contract(repoPath))
2471	 
2472	 	if len(plan.Ecosystems) == 0 {
2473	 		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No project type detected — only gitignored files will be carried over.")
2474	 	} else {
2475	 		t := NewTable("PROJECT", "MANAGER", "FROM", "DEPENDENCIES", "TOOL")
2476	 		for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
2477	 			deps := "—"
2478	 			if len(e.DepDirs) > 0 {
2479	 				deps = strings.Join(e.DepDirs, ", ")
2480	 			} else {
2481	 				deps = "global cache"
2482	 			}
2483	 			tool := "installed"
2484	 			if !e.ToolInstalled() {
2485	 				tool = "MISSING: " + e.Tool
2486	 			}
2487	 			t.Add(e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, deps, tool)
2488	 		}
2489	 		t.Render(app.Out)
2490	 	}
2491	 
2492	 	fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
2493	 	if len(plan.Steps) == 0 {
2494	 		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to provision.")
2495	 	} else {
2496	 		st := NewTable("", "ACTION", "WHAT", "WHY")
2497	 		for _, s := range plan.Steps {
2498	 			mark := "✓"
2499	 			if s.Skipped {
2500	 				mark = "·"
2501	 			}
2502	 			st.Add(mark, string(s.Kind), truncate(s.What, 34), s.Why)
2503	 		}
2504	 		st.Render(app.Out)
2505	 	}
2506	 
2507	 	for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
2508	 		fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\nwarning: %s\n", w)
2509	 	}

2511	 		fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "\nNothing would run. If a new worktree comes up broken, add what it needs to "+
2512	 			"worktree.post_create, or commit a .dev.toml with `dev wt plan --write`.")
2513	 	}

2516	 // writeRepoTemplate seeds a .dev.toml from the detected plan.
2517	 //
2518	 // Committing it is what makes a project's worktree setup reproducible: the
2519	 // next machine, and the next person, get the same one without having to
2520	 // rediscover it.
2521	 func writeRepoTemplate(app *App, repoPath string, plan wt.Plan, set wt.Settings) error {
2522	 	path := filepath.Join(repoPath, wt.OverrideFilename)
2523	 	if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
2524	 		return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists — edit it directly", config.Contract(path))
2525	 	}
2526	 
2527	 	var b strings.Builder
2528	 	b.WriteString("# dev worktree setup for this repository.\n")
2529	 	b.WriteString("#\n")
2530	 	b.WriteString("# Committed on purpose: a worktree is a clean checkout, so without this a\n")
2531	 	b.WriteString("# new one comes up with no dependencies and none of the gitignored files the\n")
2532	 	b.WriteString("# project needs. Seeded by `dev wt plan --write`; edit freely.\n\n")
2533	 	b.WriteString("[worktree]\n")
2534	 
2535	 	b.WriteString("# Gitignored files to carry into a new worktree. Only files that are BOTH\n")
2536	 	b.WriteString("# listed here AND gitignored are copied — a tracked file is already in the\n")
2537	 	b.WriteString("# checkout on the correct branch.\n")
2538	 	b.WriteString("include = [")
2539	 	for i, inc := range set.Include {
2540	 		if i > 0 {
2541	 			b.WriteString(", ")
2542	 		}
2543	 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%q", inc)
2544	 	}

 // Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
 // flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
 // config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
 package cli
 
 import (
 	"context"
 	"fmt"
 	"io"
 	"os"
 
 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
 )
 
 // App is the state shared by every command.
 type App struct {
 	Cfg   config.Config
 	Tasks *task.Store
 
 	Out io.Writer
 	Err io.Writer
 
 	// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
 	configPath string
 	// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
 	runtimeOverride string
 	// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
 	noRuntime bool
+
+	// Completion requests parse the target command's persistent flags after the
+	// root pre-run hook. These fields let completion callbacks load once, at the
+	// correct time, while treating an invalid config as no dynamic candidates.
+	completionLoadAttempted bool
+	completionLoadErr       error
 }
 
 // Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
 func (a *App) Load() error {
 	cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
 	if err != nil {
 		return err
 	}
 	a.Cfg = cfg
 	a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
 	if a.Out == nil {
 		a.Out = os.Stdout
 	}
 	if a.Err == nil {
 		a.Err = os.Stderr
 	}
 	return nil
 }
 
 // Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
 // --runtime and --no-runtime.
 func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
 	if a.noRuntime {
 		return runtime.None{}
 	}
 	backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
 	if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
 		backend = a.runtimeOverride
 	}
 	rt := runtime.Select(backend)
 	if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
 		return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
 	}
 	return rt
 }
 
 // printf writes to the command's stdout.
 func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
 	fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
 }
 
 // warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
 func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
 	fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
 }
 
-// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
-// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
-// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
-// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
+// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
+// gives dev a private file so normal command output can keep flowing directly
+// to the terminal; without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by
+// scripts and older integrations.
 func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
+	if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
+		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(dir), 0o600); err != nil {
+			a.warnf("could not write shell directory directive: %v", err)
+		}
+		return
+	}
 	fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
 }
 
 // ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
 func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }

 	Err io.Writer

 // Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
 func (a *App) Load() error {
 	cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
 	if err != nil {
 		return err
 	}
 	a.Cfg = cfg
 	a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
 	if a.Out == nil {
 		a.Out = os.Stdout
 	}
 	if a.Err == nil {
 		a.Err = os.Stderr
 	}
 	return nil
 }
 
 // Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
 // --runtime and --no-runtime.
 func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
 	if a.noRuntime {
 		return runtime.None{}
 	}
 	backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
 	if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
 		backend = a.runtimeOverride
 	}
 	rt := runtime.Select(backend)

 		return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)

 }

 ```
 
 Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
 only what git cannot answer — a task's **state**, **owner** and **next
 action** — as one TOML file per task.
 
 ## The problem
 
 When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
 working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
 So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
 defeats the point of having one.
 
 The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
 the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
 
 Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
 the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
 expected.
 
 ```
 $ dev ls
    TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
 🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
 🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
 ❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
 ```
 
 ## Install
 
+### Homebrew (macOS)
+
 ```bash
-make install     # builds, installs to ~/.local/bin, installs the agent skill
+brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli
 dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
 ```
 
-Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
+The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
+does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.
+
+### Go or source
+
+```bash
+go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@v0.1.0
+# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
+```
+
+For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
+them:
 
 ```bash
-eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
+mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
+dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
+dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
+dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
+```
+
+Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
+worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
+a forge or the network.
+
+Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
+
+```bash
+eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
+eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
 dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
 ```
 
-The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
-working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
-directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
+A child process cannot change its parent's working directory, so the wrapper
+passes directory changes back through a private file while leaving normal
+stdout/stderr connected to the terminal. That preserves the interactive TUI and
+normal pipe behavior.
+
+The agent skill is an explicit, optional post-install step:
 
 ```bash
+dev skill install
 dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
 ```
 
-Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
-degrade cleanly when absent.
+Only **git** is required at runtime. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each
+enable more and degrade cleanly when absent.
 
 ## The lifecycle
 
 | State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
 | 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
 | ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
 | ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
 
 ```bash
 dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
 dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
 dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
 dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
 dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
 dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
 ```
 
 ### A task does not have to mean a worktree
 
 Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
 
 ```bash
 # No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
 dev repo open api
 
 # Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
 dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct
 
diff --git a/scripts/e2e.sh b/scripts/e2e.sh
index 8b4b451..928ede7 100755
--- a/scripts/e2e.sh
+++ b/scripts/e2e.sh
@@ -186,35 +186,36 @@ git -C "$REPO" commit --quiet -m "feat: unmerged work"
 git -C "$REPO" switch --quiet main
 
 dev adopt | grep -q adopt-me || fail "adopt did not find the unmerged branch"
 if dev ls | grep -q adopt-me; then
   fail "adopt without --apply must create nothing"
 fi
 dev adopt --apply --yes >/dev/null
 dev ls | grep -q adopt-me || fail "adopt --apply did not record the task"
 # Adopting twice must not duplicate.
 if dev adopt | grep -q adopt-me; then
   fail "an already-tracked branch should not be offered again"
 fi
 ok "adopt reported, applied once, and stayed idempotent"
 
 step "config init detects the sandbox layout"
 dev config init --stdout | grep -q '\[paths\]' || fail "generated config looks wrong"
 ok "config generated"
 
 step "bootstrap a non-destructive repo index"
 INDEX="$HOME/repo-index"
 INDEX_CONFIG="$HOME/indexed.toml"
 dev bootstrap "$HOME/Program" --index "$INDEX" --apply \
   --config-out "$INDEX_CONFIG" >/dev/null
 [[ -L "$INDEX/demo" ]] || fail "bootstrap did not create the repo symlink"
 [[ -d "$REPO" ]]       || fail "bootstrap index moved the physical repo"
 # The generated config puts the index first but keeps new repos on the
 # physical project root.

   || fail "generated config would create physical repos inside the index"

+grep -q '~/repo-index/demo' <<<"$INDEXED_REPOS" \
