1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	
32		// Completion requests parse the target command's persistent flags after the
33		// root pre-run hook. These fields let completion callbacks load once, at the
34		// correct time, while treating an invalid config as no dynamic candidates.
35		completionLoadAttempted bool
36		completionLoadErr       error
37	}
38	
39	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
40	func (a *App) Load() error {
41		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
42		if err != nil {
43			return err
44		}
45		a.Cfg = cfg
46		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
47		if a.Out == nil {
48			a.Out = os.Stdout
49		}
50		if a.Err == nil {
51			a.Err = os.Stderr
52		}
53		return nil
54	}
55	
56	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
57	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
58	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
59		if a.noRuntime {
60			return runtime.None{}
61		}
62		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
63		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
64			backend = a.runtimeOverride
65		}
66		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
67		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
68			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
69		}
70		return rt
71	}
72	
73	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
74	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
76	}
77	
78	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
79	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
80		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
81	}
82	
83	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
84	// gives dev a private file so normal command output can keep flowing directly
85	// to the terminal; without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by
86	// scripts and older integrations.
87	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
88		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
89			if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(dir), 0o600); err != nil {
90				a.warnf("could not write shell directory directive: %v", err)
91			}
92			return
93		}
94		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
95	}
96	
97	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
98	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
99

23			return info.Main.Version

28	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
29	
30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
31	
32	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
33	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
34	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
35	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
36	
37	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
38	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
39	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`
40	
41	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
42	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
43		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
44	}
45	
46	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
47	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
48	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
49	// descriptors.
50	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
51		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}

53		root := &cobra.Command{
54			Use:           "dev",

56			Long:          rootLong,

58			SilenceUsage:  true,
59			SilenceErrors: true,
60			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
61			// exists to answer.
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
64					out, err := skill.Render()
65					if err != nil {
66						return err
67					}
68					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
69					return nil
70				}
71				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
72				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
73				if interactive() {
74					return runTUI(app)
75				}
76				return runList(app, listOptions{})
77			},
78			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
79				if completionInvocation(cmd) {

81				}

127	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
128	func Execute() int {
129		root := NewRootCommand()
130		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
131			msg := err.Error()
132			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
133			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
134				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
135			}
136			return 1
137		}
138		return 0
139	}

15	var noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
16	
17	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
18	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
19	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
20	// persistent flags (notably --config).
21	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
22		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
23			return true
24		}
25		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
26			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
27				return true
28			}
29		}
30		return false
31	}
32	
33	// loadCompletion prepares local completion providers after Cobra has parsed the
34	// command line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break
35	// command and flag completion entirely.
36	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
37		if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
38			a.completionLoadAttempted = true
39			a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
40		}
41		return a.completionLoadErr == nil
42	}
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
46			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
47				return nil, noFileCompletion
48			}
49			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
54			for _, t := range tasks {
55				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
56				out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
57			}
58			return out, noFileCompletion
59		}
60	}
61	
62	func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
63		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
64			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
65				return nil, noFileCompletion
66			}
67			repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
68			if err != nil {
69				return nil, noFileCompletion
70			}
71			out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
72			for _, r := range repos {
73				out = addCompletion(out, r.Display(), config.Contract(r.Path), toComplete)
74			}
75			return out, noFileCompletion
76		}
77	}
78	
79	func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
80		return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
81			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
82				return nil, noFileCompletion
83			}
84			repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
85			repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
86			if err != nil {
87				return nil, noFileCompletion
88			}
89			worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
90			if err != nil {
91				return nil, noFileCompletion
92			}
93			out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
94			for _, wt := range worktrees {
95				if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
96					continue
97				}
98				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
99				if wt.Main {
100					description += " (main checkout)"
101				}
102				out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
103			}
104			return out, noFileCompletion
105		}
106	}
107	
108	func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
109		if len(args) > 0 {
110			return nil, noFileCompletion
111		}
112		topics, err := help.List()
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, noFileCompletion
115		}
116		out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
117		for _, topic := range topics {
118			out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
119		}
120		return out, noFileCompletion
121	}
122	
123	func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
124		names := ignore.BundledNames()
125		out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
126		for _, name := range names {
127			out = addCompletion(out, name, "bundled template", toComplete)
128		}
129		return out, noFileCompletion
130	}
131	
132	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
133		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
134			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
135			for _, value := range values {
136				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
137			}
138			return out, noFileCompletion
139		}
140	}
141	
142	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
143		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
144			panic(err)
145		}
146	}
147	
148	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
149		description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
150		needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
151		if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
152			return out
153		}
154		if description != "" {
155			value += "\t" + description
156		}
157		return append(out, value)
158	}

 // repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.
 func repoNameFromRef(ref string) string {
 	ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")
 	if i := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:"); i >= 0 {
 		return ref[i+1:]
 	}
 	return ref
 }

 const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
 
 It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
 
   git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
   git worktree    a disposable local checkout
   herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
   dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
 
 Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
 what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
 closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`

 // pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
 func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
 	if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
 		return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
 	}
 	fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
 	return nil
 }

 So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which

 The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
 the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
 
 Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
 the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
 expected.
 
 ```
 $ dev ls
    TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
 🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
 🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
 ❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
 ```
 
 ## Install
 
+### Homebrew (macOS)
+
 ```bash
-make install     # builds, installs to ~/.local/bin, installs the agent skill
+brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli
 dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
 ```
 
-Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
+The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
+does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.
+
+### Go or source
+
+```bash
+go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@v0.1.0
+# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
+```
+
+For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
+them:
 
 ```bash
-eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
+mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
+dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
+dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
+dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
+```
+
+Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
+worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
+a forge or the network.
+
+Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
+
+```bash
+eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
+eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
 dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
 ```
 
-The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
-working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
-directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
+A child process cannot change its parent's working directory, so the wrapper
+passes directory changes back through a private file while leaving normal
+stdout/stderr connected to the terminal. That preserves the interactive TUI and
+normal pipe behavior.
+
+The agent skill is an explicit, optional post-install step:
 
 ```bash
+dev skill install
 dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
 ```
 
-Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
-degrade cleanly when absent.
+Only **git** is required at runtime. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each
+enable more and degrade cleanly when absent.
 
 ## The lifecycle
 
 | State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
 | 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
 | ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
 | ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
 
 ```bash
 dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
 dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
 dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
 dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
 dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
 dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
 ```
 
 ### A task does not have to mean a worktree

17	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
18	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
19	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
20	// persistent flags (notably --config).
21	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
22		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
23			return true
24		}
25		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
26			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
27				return true
28			}
29		}
30		return false
31	}
32	
33	// loadCompletion prepares local completion providers after Cobra has parsed the
34	// command line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break
35	// command and flag completion entirely.
36	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
37		if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
38			a.completionLoadAttempted = true
39			a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
40		}
41		return a.completionLoadErr == nil
42	}
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
46			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
47				return nil, noFileCompletion
48			}
49			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
54			for _, t := range tasks {
55				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
56				out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
57			}
58			return out, noFileCompletion
59		}
60	}
61	
62	func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
63		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
64			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
65				return nil, noFileCompletion
66			}
67			repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
68			if err != nil {
69				return nil, noFileCompletion
70			}
71			out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
72			for _, r := range repos {
73				out = addCompletion(out, r.Display(), config.Contract(r.Path), toComplete)
74			}
75			return out, noFileCompletion
76		}
77	}

79	func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
80		return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
81			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
82				return nil, noFileCompletion
83			}
84			repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
85			repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
86			if err != nil {
87				return nil, noFileCompletion
88			}
89			worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
90			if err != nil {
91				return nil, noFileCompletion
92			}
93			out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
94			for _, wt := range worktrees {
95				if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
96					continue
97				}
98				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
99				if wt.Main {
100					description += " (main checkout)"
101				}
102				out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
103			}
104			return out, noFileCompletion
105		}
106	}

124		names := ignore.BundledNames()

132	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
133		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
134			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
135			for _, value := range values {
136				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
137			}
138			return out, noFileCompletion
139		}

141	
142	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
143		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
144			panic(err)
145		}
146	}
147	
148	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
149		description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
150		needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
151		if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
152			return out
153		}
154		if description != "" {
155			value += "\t" + description
156		}
157		return append(out, value)
158	}

96	func TestFishShellWrapperPreservesStreamsStatusAndCD(t *testing.T) {
97		fish, err := exec.LookPath("fish")
98		if err != nil {

100		}
101		fake, tmp, target := writeFakeDev(t)
102		wrapper := fmt.Sprintf(fishInit, shellQuote(fake))
103		script := wrapper + `
104	dev stream
105	set stream_status $status
106	dev fail
107	set fail_status $status
108	dev cd "$DEV_TEST_TARGET"
109	set cd_status $status
110	printf 'stream_status=%s\nfail_status=%s\ncd_status=%s\npwd=%s\n' \
111	  $stream_status $fail_status $cd_status $PWD
112	dev __complete
113	if test -n (find "$TMPDIR" -name 'dev-cd.*' -print -quit)
114	    printf 'leaked=yes\n'
115	else
116	    printf 'leaked=no\n'
117	end
118	`

123		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr

136			t.Errorf("stderr was not passed through:\n%s", stderr.String())
137		}
138	}
139	
140	func writeFakeDev(t *testing.T) (path, tmp, target string) {
141		t.Helper()
142		root := t.TempDir()
143		tmp = filepath.Join(root, "tmp")
144		target = filepath.Join(root, "target with spaces")
145		if err := os.MkdirAll(tmp, 0o755); err != nil {
146			t.Fatal(err)
147		}
148		if err := os.MkdirAll(target, 0o755); err != nil {
149			t.Fatal(err)
150		}
151		path = filepath.Join(root, "fake dev")
152		body := `#!/bin/sh
153	case "${1:-}" in
154	  stream)
155	    printf 'streamed stdout\n'
156	    printf 'streamed stderr\n' >&2
157	    ;;
158	  fail)
159	    exit 7
160	    ;;
161	  cd)
162	    printf '%s' "$2" > "$DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"
163	    ;;
164	  __complete|__completeNoDesc)
165	    if [ -n "${DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE:-}" ]; then
166	      printf 'completion-wrapped\n'
167	    else
168	      printf 'completion-direct\n'
169	    fi
170	    ;;
171	esac
172	`
173		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o755); err != nil {
174			t.Fatal(err)
175		}
176		return path, tmp, target
177	}

14	// Version is set at build time via -ldflags. VersionFromBuild also recovers a
15	// module version for `go install ...@version` builds.
16	var Version = "dev"
17	
18	func versionFromBuild() string {
19		if Version != "dev" {
20			return Version
21		}
22		if info, ok := debug.ReadBuildInfo(); ok && info.Main.Version != "" && info.Main.Version != "(devel)" {
23			return info.Main.Version
24		}
25		return Version
26	}

28	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
29	
30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
31	
32	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
33	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
34	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
35	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
36	
37	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
38	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
39	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`
40	
41	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
42	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
43		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
44	}
45	
46	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
47	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
48	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
49	// descriptors.
50	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
51		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
52	
53		root := &cobra.Command{
54			Use:           "dev",
55			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
56			Long:          rootLong,
57			Version:       versionFromBuild(),
58			SilenceUsage:  true,
59			SilenceErrors: true,
60			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
61			// exists to answer.
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
64					out, err := skill.Render()
65					if err != nil {
66						return err
67					}
68					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
69					return nil
70				}
71				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
72				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
73				if interactive() {
74					return runTUI(app)
75				}
76				return runList(app, listOptions{})
77			},
78			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
79				if completionInvocation(cmd) {
80					return nil
81				}
82				return app.Load()
83			},
84		}
85	
86		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
87		pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
88		pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux or none")
89		pf.BoolVar(&app.noRuntime, "no-runtime", false, "do not touch any terminal multiplexer")
90		registerFlagCompletion(root, "runtime", fixedCompletions("herdr", "tmux", "none"))
91	
92		// Mirrors `herdr --skill`: the binary is the authority for its own agent
93		// skill, so a dotfiles installer can sync it without vendoring a copy.
94		root.Flags().Bool("skill", false, "print the bundled agent skill and exit")
95	
96		root.AddCommand(
97			newListCmd(app),
98			newTUICmd(app),
99			newStatusCmd(app),
100			newStartCmd(app),
101			newParkCmd(app),
102			newResumeCmd(app),
103			newDoneCmd(app),
104			newSweepCmd(app),
105			newAdoptCmd(app),
106			newBootstrapCmd(app),
107			newWorktreeCmd(app),
108			newRepoCmd(app),
109			newGitignoreCmd(app),
110			newTryCmd(app),
111			newGraduateCmd(app),
112			newStatsCmd(app),
113			newHelpTopicCmd(app),
114			newSkillCmd(app),
115			newDoctorCmd(app),
116			newShellInitCmd(app),
117			newConfigCmd(app),
118			newCacheCmd(app),
119			newEditCmd(app),
120		)
121		root.SetHelpCommand(&cobra.Command{Hidden: true, Use: "no-help"})
122		root.SetOut(out)
123		root.SetErr(errOut)
124		return root
125	}
126	
127	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
128	func Execute() int {
129		root := NewRootCommand()
130		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
131			msg := err.Error()
132			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
133			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
134				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
135			}
136			return 1
137		}
138		return 0
139	}

```text
1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	
32		// Completion requests parse the target command's persistent flags after the
33		// root pre-run hook. These fields let completion callbacks load once, at the
34		// correct time, while treating an invalid config as no dynamic candidates.
35		completionLoadAttempted bool
36		completionLoadErr       error
37	}
38	
39	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
40	func (a *App) Load() error {
41		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
42		if err != nil {
43			return err
44		}
45		a.Cfg = cfg
46		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
47		if a.Out == nil {
48			a.Out = os.Stdout
49		}
50		if a.Err == nil {
51			a.Err = os.Stderr
52		}
53		return nil
54	}
55	
56	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
57	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
58	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
59		if a.noRuntime {
60			return runtime.None{}
61		}
62		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
63		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
64			backend = a.runtimeOverride
65		}
66		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
67		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
68			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
69		}
70		return rt
71	}
72	
73	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
74	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
76	}
77	
78	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
79	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
80		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
81	}
82	
83	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
84	// gives dev a private file so normal command output can keep flowing directly
85	// to the terminal; without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by
86	// scripts and older integrations.
87	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
88		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
89			if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(dir), 0o600); err != nil {
90				a.warnf("could not write shell directory directive: %v", err)
91			}
92			return
93		}
94		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
95	}
96	
97	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
98	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
99

128	func Execute() int {
129		root := NewRootCommand()
130		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
131			msg := err.Error()
132			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.

134				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
135			}

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}

268	func newRepoSyncCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
269		var all bool
270		cmd := &cobra.Command{
271			Use:   "sync [repo]",
272			Short: "Fetch and prune, reporting what moved",
273			Long: `Fetch from origin and prune deleted remote-tracking refs.
274	
275	Deliberately not a pull: dev reports how each branch stands and leaves the
276	decision to you, because a pull that quietly merges or rebases is how a
277	history gets a shape nobody intended.`,
278			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
279			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
280				ctx := ctxOf()

282				switch {
283				case all:
284					var err error
285					targets, err = repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
286					if err != nil {
287						return err
288					}
289				case len(args) == 1:

291					if err != nil {
292						return err
293					}

295				default:

297					if err != nil {

301				}

303				t := NewTable("REPO", "BRANCH", "GIT", "NOTE")
304				for _, r := range targets {
305					if r.Bare {
306						continue
307					}
308					note := ""
309					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, r.Path, "fetch", "--prune", "--quiet", "origin"); err != nil {
310						note = "fetch failed (no remote?)"
311					}
312					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
313					if err != nil {
314						continue
315					}
316					if note == "" {
317						switch {
318						case st.Behind > 0 && st.Ahead > 0:
319							note = "diverged — rebase or merge explicitly"
320						case st.Behind > 0 && !st.Dirty():
321							note = "behind — git pull --ff-only"
322						case st.Behind > 0:
323							note = "behind, and dirty — commit first"
324						case st.Ahead > 0:
325							note = "unpushed commits"
326						}
327					}
328					t.Add(truncate(r.Name, 28), truncate(st.Branch, 24), st.Summary(), note)
329				}

332			},

335		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeRepos(app)

339	// repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.
340	func repoNameFromRef(ref string) string {
341		ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")
342		if i := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:"); i >= 0 {
343			return ref[i+1:]
344		}
345		return ref
346	}

348	func contractAll(paths []string) []string {
349		out := make([]string, len(paths))
350		for i, p := range paths {
351			out[i] = config.Contract(p)
352		}
353		return out
354	}

373			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),

211	// checkoutOf is where a task's code lives right now.
212	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
213		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
214			return t.WorktreePath
215		}
216		return t.RepoPath
217	}
218	
219	// annotate pushes the task's state and next action into the runtime as
220	// display-only metadata, so a sidebar can show why a session is open without
221	// anyone having to ask dev.
222	//
223	// For herdr this lands as workspace metadata tokens. A token only renders if
224	// the sidebar row layout in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g.
225	//
226	//	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
227	//	rows = [["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"], ["branch", "git_status"], ["$next"]]
228	//
229	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds and shows nothing,
230	// which is why dev never treats a failure here as an error.
231	func annotate(app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, t *task.Task) {
232		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
233			return
234		}
235		kv := map[string]string{
236			"stage": t.State.Label(),
237			"next":  t.Next,
238		}
239		if err := rt.Annotate(ctxOf(), t.RuntimeHandle, kv); err != nil {
240			app.warnf("could not annotate the runtime session: %v", err)
241		}
242	}

244	func reportProvision(app *App, res *wt.CreateResult) {
245		p := res.Provision
246		if n := len(p.Copied); n > 0 {
247			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   copied    %d gitignored file(s): %s\n", n, strings.Join(p.Copied, ", "))
248		}
249		if n := len(p.Linked); n > 0 {
250			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   linked    %s\n", strings.Join(p.Linked, ", "))
251		}
252		for _, e := range p.Failures {
253			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   warning   %v\n", e)
254		}
255	}

diff --git a/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/internal/cli/completion.go b/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/internal/cli/completion.go

--- /dev/null
+++ b/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/internal/cli/completion.go
@@ -0,0 +1,158 @@
+package cli
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/help"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/ignore"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/repo"
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+var noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
+
+// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
+// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
+// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
+// persistent flags (notably --config).
+func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
+	if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
+		return true
+	}
+	for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
+		if cur.Name() == "completion" {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// loadCompletion prepares local completion providers after Cobra has parsed the
+// command line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break
+// command and flag completion entirely.
+func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
+	if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
+		a.completionLoadAttempted = true
+		a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
+	}
+	return a.completionLoadErr == nil
+}
+
+func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
+		for _, t := range tasks {
+			description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
+			out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
+		for _, r := range repos {
+			out = addCompletion(out, r.Display(), config.Contract(r.Path), toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
+		repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
+		for _, wt := range worktrees {
+			if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
+				continue
+			}
+			description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
+			if wt.Main {
+				description += " (main checkout)"
+			}
+			out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+	if len(args) > 0 {
+		return nil, noFileCompletion
+	}
+	topics, err := help.List()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, noFileCompletion
+	}
+	out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
+	for _, topic := range topics {
+		out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
+	}
+	return out, noFileCompletion
+}
+
+func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+	names := ignore.BundledNames()
+	out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
+	for _, name := range names {
+		out = addCompletion(out, name, "bundled template", toComplete)
+	}
+	return out, noFileCompletion
+}
+
+func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
+		for _, value := range values {
+			out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
+	if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
+		panic(err)
+	}
+}
+
+func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
+	description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
+	needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
+	if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
+		return out
+	}
+	if description != "" {
+		value += "\t" + description
+	}
+	return append(out, value)
+}

```text
package cli

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

// zshInit and friends define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to leave
// the user *inside* the checkout.
//
// A process can never change its parent's working directory, so dev prints a
// `cd <path>` directive on stdout and the wrapper evaluates it. This is the
// same mechanism try-cli uses, and it is why `dev` is a shell function rather
// than only a binary.
const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
dev() {
  local __dev_out __dev_status
  __dev_out="$(command %[1]s "$@")"
  __dev_status=$?
  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ "${__dev_out#cd }" != "$__dev_out" ]; then
    eval "$__dev_out"
  elif [ -n "$__dev_out" ]; then
    printf '%%s\n' "$__dev_out"
  fi
  return $__dev_status
}
`

const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
#   dev shell-init fish | source
set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
function dev
    set -l __dev_out (command %[1]s $argv)
    set -l __dev_status $status
    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and string match -q 'cd *' -- "$__dev_out"
        eval $__dev_out
    else if test -n "$__dev_out"
        printf '%%s\n' $__dev_out
    end
    return $__dev_status
end
`

func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
		Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
		Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.

dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.

Add to your shell rc file:

    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
		Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
		ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			self, err := os.Executable()
			if err != nil || self == "" {
				self = "dev"
			}
			switch args[0] {
			case "bash", "zsh":
				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
			case "fish":
				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
			default:
				return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
			}
			return nil
		},
	}
	// Completion is a sibling concern but belongs to the same "wire dev into
	// my shell" moment, so it hangs off this command.
	cmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
		Use:       "completion <bash|zsh|fish>",
		Short:     "Print shell completions",
		Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
		ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			root := cmd.Root()
			switch args[0] {
			case "bash":
				return root.GenBashCompletionV2(app.Out, true)
			case "zsh":
				return root.GenZshCompletion(app.Out)
			case "fish":
				return root.GenFishCompletion(app.Out, true)
			}
			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q", args[0])
		},
	})
	return cmd
}

Base directory for this skill: /Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/.claude/skills/agent-history-hygiene

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `probe-specstory-redaction.py`   | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?"   |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

## Core invariants

1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
   history back.

## When to use this skill

Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:

- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
  chat history".
- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.

## When NOT to use

- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
  skip this skill entirely.
- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).

## Integration with existing infrastructure

This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
already has. It does not duplicate:

- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
  config the wrapper expects to find.
- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a
  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo
  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via
  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details
  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).

What this skill **adds**:

- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
  current transcript among many" problem.
- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
  committing.

## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene

Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
chat/plan artifacts.

```bash
# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh

# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
git add path/to/feature/file.ts
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.

# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
  exit 1
}

# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
git commit -m "feat: ..."
```

## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project

For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
installed. Runs once per repo.

```bash
cd /path/to/new/project
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit

# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
pre-commit run --all-files
```

What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:

1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`
   keeps it current everywhere.
2. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
3. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
4. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
   one-line patch if missing.
5. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.

Migrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed
`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):

```bash
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
```

removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
(idempotent; safe to re-run).

## Workflow C: post-leak remediation

When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
committed / pushed a secret":

1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
   become worth discussing.
4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.

## Gotchas

- **SpecStory >= 2.4.0 already redacts on write — plan around it, not
  against it.** Since
  [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) shipped in
  v2.4.0 (2026-07-20), the CLI redacts secrets via the
  [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset **by
  default**, covering both local markdown and cloud sync, writing
  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`. Measured coverage is 36 of 54 class/context pairs;
  15 are ours alone (every webhook rule, plus every custom key in prose
  context — betterleaks catches many classes only in `KEY=value` form via its
  entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule). So: **keep this layer, but never
  rewrite what SpecStory already cleaned.** `redact_secrets.py` writes the
  same `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` sentinel and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so
  a cleaned transcript is left untouched and pre-commit stops demanding a
  re-`git add`. Full matrix + knobs in
  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md).
  Only `[redaction] enabled` is configurable upstream — the PR's
  `extra_patterns` did not survive the Betterleaks rewrite, so repo-specific
  rules stay our job. For SpecStory older than 2.4.0 (or with redaction
  disabled), run `redact_secrets.py --fix --legacy`.
- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
  syntax everywhere.
- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
  `find-session.sh`.
- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
  agent artifacts, not after.
- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
  empty fields signal absence).

- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.

- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.

- **`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`**
  Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers, by
  synthesizing a Claude Code session and rendering it twice (with and without
  `--no-redact-secrets`). Prints a coverage matrix and the residual set our
  layer must still handle. Exit 30 when specstory isn't installed.

- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--migrate] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the current
  repo, wire the hook to the installed skill's redactor, then run
  `pre-commit install`. Audits
  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
  (warns, never silently edits).

## Bundled assets

- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
  regex.
- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
  standard hygiene hooks.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
  agent artifact dirs.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — the redactor, published to consuming repos
  as the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook (root
  `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`). Writes `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`, the sentinel
  SpecStory also writes natively; `--legacy` writes the pre-2.4.0
  placeholders instead. Release procedure in
  `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.

## Reference files

- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.
  Read when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.
- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),
  allowlist design, sync procedure for the bundled redactor. Read
  when tuning rules or debugging unexpected pre-commit failures.
- [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md)
  — what SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts on its own, measured per secret class and
  per context, plus the upstream PRs, config knobs, and why our layer is still
  load-bearing. Read before changing anything about redaction placeholders.
- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) —
  rotate-first runbook for "I committed / pushed a secret". Read
  **before** any `git filter-repo` / `git push --force` action.

## Tests

The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:

```bash
make test-skill
```

- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.
- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git
  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are
  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.
- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).
- `test_specstory_coverage.py` — locks in that SpecStory still redacts by
  default and still writes `[REDACTED:<label>]`; skips without the CLI.

The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each
regression the suite locks in.

## Related skills

- [`project-knowledge-harness`](../project-knowledge-harness/SKILL.md)
  — complementary memory harness (TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/) that
  references `.claude/plans/` as "ephemeral agent scratchpads". This
  skill fills the gap: those scratchpads belong in git, not ignored.

10	// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
11	// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
14	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
15	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  case "${1:-}" in
19	    __complete|__completeNoDesc)
20	      command %[1]s "$@"
21	      return $?
22	      ;;
23	  esac
24	
25	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
26	  __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX")" || return 1
27	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE="$__dev_cd_file" command %[1]s "$@"
28	  __dev_status=$?
29	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
30	    IFS= read -r __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
31	    if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
32	      builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
33	      __dev_status=$?
34	    fi
35	  fi
36	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
37	  return $__dev_status
38	}
39	`
40	
41	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
42	#   dev shell-init fish | source
43	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
44	function dev
45	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0; and contains -- $argv[1] __complete __completeNoDesc
46	        command %[1]s $argv
47	        return $status
48	    end
49	
50	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
51	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
52	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX")
53	    or return 1
54	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE $__dev_cd_file
55	    command %[1]s $argv
56	    set -l __dev_status $status
57	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
58	        read -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
59	        if test -n "$__dev_dir"
60	            builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
61	            set __dev_status $status
62	        end
63	    end
64	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
65	    return $__dev_status
66	end
67	`
68	
69	func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
70		cmd := &cobra.Command{
71			Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
72			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
73			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
74	
75	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
76	"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
77	directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
78	working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.
79	
80	Add to your shell rc file:
81	
82	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
83	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
84			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
85			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
86			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
87				self, err := os.Executable()
88				if err != nil || self == "" {
89					self = "dev"
90				}
91				switch args[0] {
92				case "bash", "zsh":
93					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
94				case "fish":
95					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
96				default:
97					return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
98				}
99				return nil
100			},
101		}
102		return cmd
103	}

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	
32		// Completion requests parse the target command's persistent flags after the
33		// root pre-run hook. These fields let completion callbacks load once, at the
34		// correct time, while treating an invalid config as no dynamic candidates.
35		completionLoadAttempted bool
36		completionLoadErr       error
37	}
38	
39	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
40	func (a *App) Load() error {
41		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
42		if err != nil {
43			return err
44		}
45		a.Cfg = cfg
46		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
47		if a.Out == nil {
48			a.Out = os.Stdout
49		}
50		if a.Err == nil {
51			a.Err = os.Stderr
52		}
53		return nil
54	}
55	
56	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
57	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
58	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
59		if a.noRuntime {
60			return runtime.None{}
61		}
62		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
63		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
64			backend = a.runtimeOverride
65		}
66		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
67		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
68			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
69		}
70		return rt
71	}
72	
73	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
74	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
76	}
77	
78	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
79	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
80		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
81	}
82	
83	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
84	// gives dev a private file so normal command output can keep flowing directly
85	// to the terminal; without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by
86	// scripts and older integrations.
87	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
88		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
89			if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(dir), 0o600); err != nil {
90				a.warnf("could not write shell directory directive: %v", err)
91			}
92			return
93		}
94		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
95	}
96	
97	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
98	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
99

14	// Version is set at build time via -ldflags. VersionFromBuild also recovers a
15	// module version for `go install ...@version` builds.
16	var Version = "dev"
17	
18	func versionFromBuild() string {
19		if Version != "dev" {
20			return Version
21		}
22		if info, ok := debug.ReadBuildInfo(); ok && info.Main.Version != "" && info.Main.Version != "(devel)" {
23			return info.Main.Version
24		}
25		return Version
26	}
