28	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
29	
30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
31	
32	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
33	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
34	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
35	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
36	
37	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
38	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
39	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`
40	
41	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
42	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
43		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
44	}
45	
46	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
47	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
48	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
49	// descriptors.
50	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
51		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
52	
53		root := &cobra.Command{
54			Use:           "dev",
55			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
56			Long:          rootLong,
57			Version:       versionFromBuild(),
58			SilenceUsage:  true,
59			SilenceErrors: true,
60			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
61			// exists to answer.
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
64					out, err := skill.Render()
65					if err != nil {
66						return err
67					}
68					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
69					return nil
70				}
71				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
72				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
73				if interactive() {
74					return runTUI(app)
75				}
76				return runList(app, listOptions{})
77			},
78			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
79				if completionInvocation(cmd) {
80					return nil
81				}
82				return app.Load()
83			},
84		}
85	
86		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
87		pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
88		pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux or none")
89		pf.BoolVar(&app.noRuntime, "no-runtime", false, "do not touch any terminal multiplexer")
90		registerFlagCompletion(root, "runtime", fixedCompletions("herdr", "tmux", "none"))
91	
92		// Mirrors `herdr --skill`: the binary is the authority for its own agent
93		// skill, so a dotfiles installer can sync it without vendoring a copy.
94		root.Flags().Bool("skill", false, "print the bundled agent skill and exit")
95	
96		root.AddCommand(
97			newListCmd(app),
98			newTUICmd(app),
99			newStatusCmd(app),
100			newStartCmd(app),
101			newParkCmd(app),
102			newResumeCmd(app),
103			newDoneCmd(app),
104			newSweepCmd(app),
105			newAdoptCmd(app),
106			newBootstrapCmd(app),
107			newWorktreeCmd(app),
108			newRepoCmd(app),
109			newGitignoreCmd(app),
110			newTryCmd(app),
111			newGraduateCmd(app),
112			newStatsCmd(app),
113			newHelpTopicCmd(app),
114			newSkillCmd(app),
115			newDoctorCmd(app),
116			newShellInitCmd(app),
117			newConfigCmd(app),
118			newCacheCmd(app),
119			newEditCmd(app),
120		)
121		root.SetHelpCommand(&cobra.Command{Hidden: true, Use: "no-help"})
122		root.SetOut(out)
123		root.SetErr(errOut)
124		return root
125	}
126	
127	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
128	func Execute() int {
129		root := NewRootCommand()
130		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
131			msg := err.Error()
132			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
133			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
134				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
135			}
136			return 1
137		}
138		return 0
139	}

{"parentUuid":"9c450cc9-0fa1-4224-8dde-31819ea8e153","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"dd939105-e022-4fe1-bab3-3f764b2285be","agentId":"aecbeeb4d1223c1af","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/.claude/skills/agent-history-hygiene\n\n# agent-history-hygiene\n\nKeep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the\ncode they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the\n`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.\n\nThree surfaces, separated by purpose:\n\n| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |\n|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `find-session.sh`                | \"Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?\"      |\n| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | \"Which agent files belong in the next commit?\"               |\n| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | \"How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?\" |\n| `scan-staged.sh`                 | \"Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?\"      |\n| `probe-specstory-redaction.py`   | \"What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?\"   |\n| `references/remediation.md`      | \"I already pushed a secret — now what?\"                      |\n\n## Core invariants\n\n1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff\n   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that\n   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.\n2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act\n   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting\n   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.\n3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a\n   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and\n   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old\n   history back.\n\n## When to use this skill\n\nUse it when the user (or you) surface any of:\n\n- \"Commit my chat\" / \"save the specstory session\" / \"include the plan\n  file in this commit\" / \"把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去\".\n- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,\n  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during\n  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.\n- \"Scrub this transcript\" / \"redact my key\" / \"gitleaks flagged my\n  chat history\".\n- \"Set up pre-commit for this repo\" / \"I'm starting a new project — how\n  do I get the hook stack?\" / \"bootstrap secret scanning here\".\n- \"I pushed a `.env`\" / \"a secret went to main\" / \"do I need to force\n  push?\" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and\n  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.\n\n## When NOT to use\n\n- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the\n  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and\n  skip this skill entirely.\n- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**\n  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.\n- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no\n  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.\n- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any\n  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).\n\n## Integration with existing infrastructure\n\nThis skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user\nalready has. It does not duplicate:\n\n- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)\n  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then\n  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level\n  config the wrapper expects to find.\n- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries\n  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,\n  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /\n  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the\n  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.\n- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a\n  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo\n  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via\n  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details\n  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).\n\nWhat this skill **adds**:\n\n- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).\n- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos\n  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.\n- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the \"find my\n  current transcript among many\" problem.\n- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before\n  committing.\n\n## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene\n\nDefault flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus\nchat/plan artifacts.\n\n```bash\n# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is \"ours\" — mostly\n#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.\nbash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh\n\n# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.\ngit add path/to/feature/file.ts\nbash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh\n# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;\n# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.\n\n# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.\nbash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {\n  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.\n  echo \"Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing.\" >&2\n  exit 1\n}\n\n# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets\n#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.\ngit commit -m \"feat: ...\"\n```\n\n## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project\n\nFor repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`\ninstalled. Runs once per repo.\n\n```bash\ncd /path/to/new/project\nbash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \\\n  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit\n\n# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.\npre-commit run --all-files\n```\n\nWhat `bootstrap-project.sh` does:\n\n1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo\n   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned\n   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a\n   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`\n   keeps it current everywhere.\n2. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if\n   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).\n3. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would\n   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.\n4. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the\n   one-line patch if missing.\n5. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls\n   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every\n   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.\n\nMigrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed\n`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):\n\n```bash\nbash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate\n```\n\nremoves the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned\nremote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched\n(idempotent; safe to re-run).\n\n## Workflow C: post-leak remediation\n\nWhen `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says \"I\ncommitted / pushed a secret\":\n\n1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.\n2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.\n3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast\n   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history\n   become worth discussing.\n4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.\n\n## Gotchas\n\n- **SpecStory >= 2.4.0 already redacts on write — plan around it, not\n  against it.** Since\n  [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) shipped in\n  v2.4.0 (2026-07-20), the CLI redacts secrets via the\n  [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset **by\n  default**, covering both local markdown and cloud sync, writing\n  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`. Measured coverage is 36 of 54 class/context pairs;\n  15 are ours alone (every webhook rule, plus every custom key in prose\n  context — betterleaks catches many classes only in `KEY=value` form via its\n  entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule). So: **keep this layer, but never\n  rewrite what SpecStory already cleaned.** `redact_secrets.py` writes the\n  same `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` sentinel and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so\n  a cleaned transcript is left untouched and pre-commit stops demanding a\n  re-`git add`. Full matrix + knobs in\n  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md).\n  Only `[redaction] enabled` is configurable upstream — the PR's\n  `extra_patterns` did not survive the Betterleaks rewrite, so repo-specific\n  rules stay our job. For SpecStory older than 2.4.0 (or with redaction\n  disabled), run `redact_secrets.py --fix --legacy`.\n- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code\n  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)\n  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some\n  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed\n  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`\n  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with\n  `\"plansDirectory\": \"./.claude/plans\"`) is the recommended default.\n- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use\n  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and\n  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still\n  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern\n  syntax everywhere.\n- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run\n  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot\n  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.\n- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed\n  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`\n  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.\n  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`\n  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.\n- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code\n  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`\n  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per\n  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts\n  for what feels like \"one session\" — mtime-newest wins in\n  `find-session.sh`.\n- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The\n  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it\n  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no\n  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with\n  agent artifacts, not after.\n- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard\n  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`\n  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's\n  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,\n  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an\n  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own\n  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n\n  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory\n  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle\n  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says \"Successfully redacted N\n  file(s)\" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,\n  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c\n  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit\n  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic\n  `python3 -c \"<in-place re.sub>\" && git add <file> && git commit -m\n  \"...\"` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write\n  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the\n  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with\n  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See\n  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in\n  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.\n  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the\n  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that\n  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about\n  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.\n  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the\n  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and\n  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still\n  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps\n  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)\n  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false\n  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit\n  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).\n\n## Available scripts\n\n- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**\n  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,\n  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,\n  empty fields signal absence).\n\n- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**\n  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.\n  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;\n  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.\n  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents \"commit just\n  transcript\"); override with `--allow-empty`.\n\n- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**\n  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes\n  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines\n  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.\n\n- **`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`**\n  Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers, by\n  synthesizing a Claude Code session and rendering it twice (with and without\n  `--no-redact-secrets`). Prints a coverage matrix and the residual set our\n  layer must still handle. Exit 30 when specstory isn't installed.\n\n- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--migrate] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**\n  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the current\n  repo, wire the hook to the installed skill's redactor, then run\n  `pre-commit install`. Audits\n  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations\n  (warns, never silently edits).\n\n## Bundled assets\n\n- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact\n  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode\n  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and\n  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`\n  regex.\n- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal\n  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +\n  standard hygiene hooks.\n- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi\n  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for\n  agent artifact dirs.\n- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — the redactor, published to consuming repos\n  as the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook (root\n  `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`). Writes `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`, the sentinel\n  SpecStory also writes natively; `--legacy` writes the pre-2.4.0\n  placeholders instead. Release procedure in\n  `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.\n\n## Reference files\n\n- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)\n  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.\n  Read when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.\n- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)\n  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),\n  allowlist design, sync procedure for the bundled redactor. Read\n  when tuning rules or debugging unexpected pre-commit failures.\n- [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md)\n  — what SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts on its own, measured per secret class and\n  per context, plus the upstream PRs, config knobs, and why our layer is still\n  load-bearing. Read before changing anything about redaction placeholders.\n- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) —\n  rotate-first runbook for \"I committed / pushed a secret\". Read\n  **before** any `git filter-repo` / `git push --force` action.\n\n## Tests\n\nThe skill ships with a three-level test suite under\n[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:\n\n```bash\nmake test-skill\n```\n\n- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.\n- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git\n  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are\n  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.\n- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for\n  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).\n- `test_specstory_coverage.py` — locks in that SpecStory still redacts by\n  default and still writes `[REDACTED:<label>]`; skips without the CLI.\n\nThe corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on\n`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each\nregression the suite locks in.\n\n## Related skills\n\n- [`project-knowledge-harness`](../project-knowledge-harness/SKILL.md)\n  — complementary memory harness (TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/) that\n  references `.claude/plans/` as \"ephemeral agent scratchpads\". 1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}

15	// RepoRow is one repository as the dashboard shows it: what it is, plus how
16	// much of it is currently in flight.
17	//
18	// The repository view exists because the task list alone answers only half the
19	// question. On a machine with forty repositories and no tasks recorded yet,
20	// a task-only dashboard is empty — and the honest answer to "what do I have
21	// here?" has to come before "what am I working on?"
22	type RepoRow struct {
23		Repo   repo.Repo
24		Status gitx.Status
25		// LastActivity is the newest commit time in this checkout. It is a durable,
26		// cheap approximation of "when was this repo last touched" and is sortable.
27		LastActivity time.Time
28		// Worktrees is the number of linked worktrees, excluding the main checkout.
29		Worktrees int
30		// Tasks are the recorded tasks belonging to this repository.
31		Tasks []*task.Task

33		Live          bool
34		Runtime       string

38		// this local checkout without rescanning every repo when a cache opens.

42	
43	// HotTasks counts the repository's tasks that are currently hot.
44	func (r RepoRow) HotTasks() int {
45		n := 0
46		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
47			if t.State == task.Hot {
48				n++
49			}
50		}
51		return n
52	}
53	
54	// StateSummary renders the repository's tasks as a compact per-state tally,
55	// which is what makes the list scannable at forty repositories.
56	func (r RepoRow) StateSummary() string {
57		if len(r.Tasks) == 0 {
58			return ""
59		}
60		counts := map[task.State]int{}
61		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
62			counts[t.State]++
63		}
64		var parts []string
65		for _, s := range task.States {
66			if counts[s] > 0 {
67				parts = append(parts, s.Icon()+strconv.Itoa(counts[s]))
68			}
69		}
70		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
71	}
72	
73	// searchText is what a filter query matches against.
74	func (r RepoRow) searchText() string {
75		var b strings.Builder
76		b.WriteString(r.Repo.Display())
77		b.WriteString(" ")
78		b.WriteString(r.Status.Branch)
79		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
80			b.WriteString(" ")
81			b.WriteString(t.Title())
82			b.WriteString(" ")

96	// matches reports whether every whitespace-separated term of the query appears
97	// in the haystack.
98	//
99	// Term-wise rather than substring so "auth api" finds a task named "api token
100	// auth" — the order words come to mind in is rarely the order they appear in.
101	func matches(haystack, query string) bool {
102		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
103		if query == "" {
104			return true
105		}
106		for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
107			if !strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
108				return false
109			}
110		}
111		return true
112	}

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"io"
6		"strings"
7		"time"
8		"unicode/utf8"
9	)
10	
11	// Table renders aligned columns. It measures width in runes rather than bytes
12	// so the CJK repo and branch names in a real inventory line up.
13	type Table struct {
14		head []string
15		rows [][]string
16	}
17	
18	// NewTable starts a table with the given header.
19	func NewTable(header ...string) *Table { return &Table{head: header} }
20	
21	// Add appends a row. Short rows are padded, long ones are truncated to the
22	// header width so a stray field can never shift the whole table.
23	func (t *Table) Add(cells ...string) {
24		row := make([]string, len(t.head))
25		copy(row, cells)
26		t.rows = append(t.rows, row)
27	}
28	
29	// Len reports the number of data rows.
30	func (t *Table) Len() int { return len(t.rows) }
31	
32	// Render writes the table, sizing every column to its widest cell.
33	func (t *Table) Render(w io.Writer) {
34		if len(t.rows) == 0 {
35			return
36		}
37		widths := make([]int, len(t.head))
38		for i, h := range t.head {
39			widths[i] = width(h)
40		}
41		for _, r := range t.rows {
42			for i, c := range r {
43				if n := width(c); n > widths[i] {
44					widths[i] = n
45				}
46			}
47		}
48		writeRow(w, t.head, widths)
49		for _, r := range t.rows {
50			writeRow(w, r, widths)
51		}
52	}
53	
54	func writeRow(w io.Writer, cells []string, widths []int) {
55		var b strings.Builder
56		for i, c := range cells {
57			if i == len(cells)-1 {
58				b.WriteString(c) // never pad the last column
59				break
60			}
61			b.WriteString(c)
62			b.WriteString(strings.Repeat(" ", widths[i]-width(c)+2))
63		}
64		fmt.Fprintln(w, strings.TrimRight(b.String(), " "))
65	}
66	
67	// width counts display columns, treating wide CJK runes as two.
68	func width(s string) int {
69		n := 0
70		for _, r := range s {
71			if isWide(r) {
72				n += 2
73			} else {
74				n++
75			}
76		}
77		return n
78	}
79	
80	func isWide(r rune) bool {
81		switch {
82		case r >= 0x1100 && r <= 0x115F, // Hangul Jamo
83			r >= 0x2E80 && r <= 0xA4CF, // CJK radicals through Yi
84			r >= 0xAC00 && r <= 0xD7A3, // Hangul syllables
85			r >= 0xF900 && r <= 0xFAFF, // CJK compatibility ideographs
86			r >= 0xFE30 && r <= 0xFE6F, // CJK compatibility forms
87			r >= 0xFF00 && r <= 0xFF60, // fullwidth forms
88			r >= 0xFFE0 && r <= 0xFFE6,
89			r >= 0x20000 && r <= 0x3FFFD: // CJK extension planes
90			return true
91		}
92		return false
93	}
94	
95	// truncate shortens s to at most n display columns, marking the cut with "…".
96	func truncate(s string, n int) string {
97		if n <= 0 || width(s) <= n {
98			return s
99		}
100		var b strings.Builder
101		used := 0
102		for _, r := range s {
103			rw := 1
104			if isWide(r) {
105				rw = 2
106			}
107			if used+rw > n-1 {
108				break
109			}
110			b.WriteRune(r)
111			used += rw
112		}
113		return b.String() + "…"
114	}
115	
116	// dash renders an empty value as a visible placeholder, so a blank column is
117	// never mistaken for a rendering bug.
118	func dash(s string) string {
119		if strings.TrimSpace(s) == "" {
120			return "—"
121		}
122		return s
123	}
124	
125	// humanAge renders a duration the way a changelog would: "3d", "2w", "5mo".
126	func humanAge(d time.Duration) string {
127		switch {
128		case d <= 0:
129			return "—"
130		case d < time.Hour:
131			return fmt.Sprintf("%dm", int(d.Minutes()))
132		case d < 24*time.Hour:
133			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
134		case d < 14*24*time.Hour:
135			return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", int(d.Hours()/24))
136		case d < 60*24*time.Hour:
137			return fmt.Sprintf("%dw", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
138		default:
139			return fmt.Sprintf("%dmo", int(d.Hours()/24/30))
140		}
141	}
142	
143	// shellQuote makes a path safe to paste into a POSIX shell command.
144	func shellQuote(s string) string {
145		if s == "" {
146			return "''"
147		}
148		safe := true
149		for _, r := range s {
150			if !(r == '/' || r == '.' || r == '-' || r == '_' || r == '~' ||
151				(r >= 'a' && r <= 'z') || (r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z') || (r >= '0' && r <= '9')) {
152				safe = false
153				break
154			}
155		}
156		if safe && utf8.ValidString(s) {
157			return s
158		}
159		return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) + "'"
160	}

8	import (
9		"embed"
10		"fmt"
11		"io/fs"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	)
15	
16	//go:embed all:topics
17	var topics embed.FS
18	
19	// Topic is one reference page.
20	type Topic struct {
21		Name    string
22		Title   string
23		Summary string
24		Body    string
25	}
26	
27	// List returns every topic, sorted by name.
28	func List() ([]Topic, error) {
29		entries, err := fs.ReadDir(topics, "topics")
30		if err != nil {
31			return nil, err
32		}
33		var out []Topic
34		for _, e := range entries {
35			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".md") {
36				continue
37			}
38			t, err := load(strings.TrimSuffix(e.Name(), ".md"))
39			if err != nil {
40				continue
41			}
42			out = append(out, t)
43		}
44		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name < out[j].Name })
45		return out, nil
46	}
47	
48	// Get returns one topic by exact name, or by unique prefix.
49	func Get(name string) (Topic, error) {
50		if t, err := load(name); err == nil {
51			return t, nil
52		}
53		all, err := List()
54		if err != nil {
55			return Topic{}, err
56		}
57		var hits []Topic
58		for _, t := range all {
59			if strings.HasPrefix(t.Name, name) || strings.Contains(t.Name, name) {
60				hits = append(hits, t)
61			}
62		}
63		switch len(hits) {
64		case 1:
65			return hits[0], nil
66		case 0:
67			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("no help topic %q; run `dev help` to list them", name)
68		default:
69			names := make([]string, len(hits))
70			for i, t := range hits {
71				names[i] = t.Name
72			}
73			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("%q matches several topics: %s", name, strings.Join(names, ", "))
74		}
75	}
76	
77	func load(name string) (Topic, error) {
78		b, err := topics.ReadFile("topics/" + name + ".md")
79		if err != nil {
80			return Topic{}, err
81		}
82		body := string(b)
83		t := Topic{Name: name, Body: body}
84		// The first heading is the title; the first paragraph after it is the
85		// summary shown in the index.
86		for _, line := range strings.Split(body, "\n") {
87			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
88			switch {
89			case t.Title == "" && strings.HasPrefix(line, "# "):
90				t.Title = strings.TrimPrefix(line, "# ")
91			case t.Title != "" && t.Summary == "" && line != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(line, "#"):
92				// A page may open with a blockquote or a list; the marker is
93				// formatting, not part of the one-line summary.
94				t.Summary = strings.TrimLeft(line, ">-* ")
95				return t, nil
96			}
97		}
98		return t, nil
99	}
100

1	// Package ignore assembles .gitignore files from GitHub's published templates
2	// plus the entries that every repository on a given machine wants but no
3	// language template includes.
4	//
5	// The split matters: a Python template says nothing about .DS_Store, and
6	// nothing at all about the worktree directories an agent harness creates —
7	// which, left untracked, show up as noise in every status.
8	package ignore
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"embed"
13		"fmt"
14		"io"
15		"net/http"
16		"os"
17		"path/filepath"
18		"sort"
19		"strings"
20		"time"
21	)
22	
23	//go:embed all:templates
24	var bundled embed.FS
25	
26	// TemplateAPI is GitHub's public gitignore endpoint. It needs no
27	// authentication, which is what lets this work before `gh auth login`.
28	const TemplateAPI = "https://api.github.com/gitignore/templates"
29	
30	// Source records where a section's content came from, so the generated file
31	// can say so honestly.
32	type Source string
33	
34	const (
35		// SourceRemote is GitHub's template API.
36		SourceRemote Source = "github"
37		// SourceCache is a previously fetched template on disk.
38		SourceCache Source = "cache"
39		// SourceBundled is a template compiled into the binary.
40		SourceBundled Source = "bundled"
41	)
42	
43	// Section is one named block of the generated file.
44	type Section struct {
45		Name   string
46		Body   string
47		Source Source
48	}
49	
50	// Fetcher resolves template names to content, preferring the network and
51	// falling back through the cache to the bundled copies.
52	type Fetcher struct {
53		CacheDir string
54		Client   *http.Client
55		// Offline skips the network entirely.
56		Offline bool
57		// BaseURL overrides the template endpoint; empty means TemplateAPI.
58		BaseURL string
59	}
60	
61	// NewFetcher returns a fetcher caching under dir.
62	func NewFetcher(cacheDir string) *Fetcher {
63		return &Fetcher{
64			CacheDir: cacheDir,
65			Client:   &http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second},
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// Get resolves one template by name, case-insensitively ("python", "Python",
70	// "PYTHON" all work, because nobody remembers GitHub's capitalisation).
71	func (f *Fetcher) Get(ctx context.Context, name string) (Section, error) {
72		canonical := Canonical(name)
73	
74		if !f.Offline {
75			body, err := f.fetch(ctx, canonical)
76			if err == nil {
77				f.writeCache(canonical, body)
78				return Section{Name: canonical, Body: body, Source: SourceRemote}, nil
79			}
80		}
81		if body, ok := f.readCache(canonical); ok {
82			return Section{Name: canonical, Body: body, Source: SourceCache}, nil
83		}
84		if body, ok := bundledTemplate(canonical); ok {
85			return Section{Name: canonical, Body: body, Source: SourceBundled}, nil
86		}
87		return Section{}, fmt.Errorf("no gitignore template for %q (offline, and no cached or bundled copy);"+
88			" available offline: %s", name, strings.Join(BundledNames(), ", "))
89	}
90	
91	// Canonical normalises a template name to GitHub's own capitalisation where
92	// it is known, and otherwise title-cases the input.
93	func Canonical(name string) string {
94		lower := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(name))
95		if c, ok := knownNames[lower]; ok {
96			return c
97		}
98		if lower == "" {
99			return ""
100		}
101		return strings.ToUpper(lower[:1]) + lower[1:]
102	}
103	
104	// knownNames maps the spellings people type to GitHub's file names. Only the
105	// cases where they differ need an entry.
106	var knownNames = map[string]string{
107		"python": "Python", "node": "Node", "nodejs": "Node", "js": "Node",
108		"javascript": "Node", "typescript": "Node", "ts": "Node",
109		"go": "Go", "golang": "Go", "rust": "Rust", "java": "Java",
110		"ruby": "Ruby", "elixir": "Elixir", "c": "C", "c++": "C++", "cpp": "C++",
111		"swift": "Swift", "kotlin": "Kotlin", "scala": "Scala", "haskell": "Haskell",
112		"r": "R", "julia": "Julia", "dart": "Dart", "flutter": "Dart",
113		"terraform": "Terraform", "unity": "Unity", "godot": "Godot",
114		"tex": "TeX", "latex": "TeX", "zig": "Zig", "lua": "Lua", "perl": "Perl",
115		"php": "Composer", "laravel": "Laravel", "rails": "Rails",
116		"android": "Android", "objective-c": "Objective-C", "objc": "Objective-C",
117		"csharp": "VisualStudio", "c#": "VisualStudio", "dotnet": "VisualStudio",
118	}
119	
120	func (f *Fetcher) fetch(ctx context.Context, name string) (string, error) {
121		base := f.BaseURL
122		if base == "" {
123			base = TemplateAPI
124		}
125		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, base+"/"+name, nil)
126		if err != nil {
127			return "", err
128		}
129		req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/vnd.github.raw")
130		client := f.Client
131		if client == nil {
132			client = http.DefaultClient
133		}
134		resp, err := client.Do(req)
135		if err != nil {
136			return "", err
137		}
138		defer resp.Body.Close()
139		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
140			return "", fmt.Errorf("github returned %s for %s", resp.Status, name)
141		}
142		body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20))
143		if err != nil {
144			return "", err
145		}
146		// The raw media type returns the file itself; if a proxy ignored the
147		// Accept header we would get JSON, which is not a usable gitignore.
148		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(string(body)), "{") {
149			return "", fmt.Errorf("unexpected JSON response for %s", name)
150		}
151		return strings.TrimRight(string(body), "\n"), nil
152	}
153	
154	func (f *Fetcher) cachePath(name string) string {
155		if f.CacheDir == "" {
156			return ""
157		}
158		return filepath.Join(f.CacheDir, name+".gitignore")
159	}
160	
161	func (f *Fetcher) readCache(name string) (string, bool) {
162		p := f.cachePath(name)
163		if p == "" {
164			return "", false
165		}
166		b, err := os.ReadFile(p)
167		if err != nil {
168			return "", false
169		}
170		return strings.TrimRight(string(b), "\n"), true
171	}
172	
173	func (f *Fetcher) writeCache(name, body string) {
174		p := f.cachePath(name)
175		if p == "" {
176			return
177		}
178		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p), 0o755); err != nil {
179			return // caching is an optimisation; failing to cache is not an error
180		}
181		_ = os.WriteFile(p, []byte(body+"\n"), 0o644)
182	}
183	
184	func bundledTemplate(name string) (string, bool) {
185		b, err := bundled.ReadFile("templates/" + name + ".gitignore")
186		if err != nil {
187			return "", false
188		}
189		return strings.TrimRight(string(b), "\n"), true
190	}
191	
192	// BundledNames lists the templates available with no network at all.
193	func BundledNames() []string {
194		entries, err := bundled.ReadDir("templates")
195		if err != nil {
196			return nil
197		}
198		var out []string
199		for _, e := range entries {
200			out = append(out, strings.TrimSuffix(e.Name(), ".gitignore"))
201		}
202		sort.Strings(out)
203		return out
204	}

```text
BINARY  := dev
PREFIX  ?= $(HOME)/.local
VERSION := $(shell git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
LDFLAGS := -s -w -X github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/cli.Version=$(VERSION)

.PHONY: build install test lint fmt vet skill-sync skill-check e2e clean all

all: fmt vet test build

build:
	go build -ldflags '$(LDFLAGS)' -o $(BINARY) ./cmd/dev

# Install the binary and its agent skill together, so the documentation an
# agent reads always matches the binary that is on PATH.
install: build
	install -d $(PREFIX)/bin
	install -m 0755 $(BINARY) $(PREFIX)/bin/$(BINARY)
	$(PREFIX)/bin/$(BINARY) skill install
	@echo
	@echo 'Add to your shell rc:  eval "$$($(PREFIX)/bin/$(BINARY) shell-init zsh)"'

test:
	go test ./...

vet:
	go vet ./...

fmt:
	gofmt -w .

# Regenerate the skill's command reference from the live command tree.
skill-sync: build
	./$(BINARY) skill sync
	$(MAKE) build

# Fail if the checked-in command reference has drifted from the command tree.
# Wire this into CI and a pre-push hook.
skill-check: build
	./$(BINARY) skill sync --check

e2e: build
	./scripts/e2e.sh

clean:
	rm -f $(BINARY)
	go clean -testcache
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: stable
          cache: true

      # gitx and wt shell out to git, and the test repos need an identity.
      - name: Configure git
        run: |
          git config --global user.email "ci@example.test"
          git config --global user.name "ci"
          git config --global init.defaultBranch main

      - run: gofmt -l . | tee /dev/stderr | (! read)
      - run: go vet ./...
      - run: go test -race ./...
      - run: go build ./cmd/dev

      # The skill documents the CLI; drift between them is a bug.
      - run: go run ./cmd/dev skill sync --check

      - run: ./scripts/e2e.sh
```

    10	// zshInit and friends define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to leave
    11	// the user *inside* the checkout.
    12	//
    13	// A process can never change its parent's working directory, so dev prints a
    14	// `cd <path>` directive on stdout and the wrapper evaluates it. This is the
    15	// same mechanism try-cli uses, and it is why `dev` is a shell function rather
    16	// than only a binary.
    17	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
    18	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
    19	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
    20	dev() {
    21	  local __dev_out __dev_status
    22	  __dev_out="$(command %[1]s "$@")"
    23	  __dev_status=$?
    24	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ "${__dev_out#cd }" != "$__dev_out" ]; then
    25	    eval "$__dev_out"
    26	  elif [ -n "$__dev_out" ]; then
    27	    printf '%%s\n' "$__dev_out"
    28	  fi
    29	  return $__dev_status
    30	}
    31	`
    32	
    33	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
    34	#   dev shell-init fish | source
    35	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
    36	function dev
    37	    set -l __dev_out (command %[1]s $argv)
    38	    set -l __dev_status $status
    39	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and string match -q 'cd *' -- "$__dev_out"
    40	        eval $__dev_out
    41	    else if test -n "$__dev_out"
    42	        printf '%%s\n' $__dev_out
    43	    end
    44	    return $__dev_status
    45	end
    46	`
    47	
    48	func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
    49		cmd := &cobra.Command{
    50			Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
    51			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
    52			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
    53	
    54	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
    55	"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
    56	directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
    57	working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.
    58	
    59	Add to your shell rc file:

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}

1	package task
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"io/fs"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"regexp"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	
14		"github.com/BurntSushi/toml"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}

1	package gitx
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"strings"
6	)
7	
8	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
9	type Worktree struct {
10		Path string
11		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
12		Head string
13		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
14		Branch   string
15		Detached bool
16		Bare     bool
17		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
18		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
19		Locked         bool
20		LockedReason   string
21		Prunable       bool
22		PrunableReason string
23		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
24		Main bool
25	}
26	
27	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
28	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
29	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
30		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
31		if err != nil {
32			return nil, err
33		}
34		var (
35			list []Worktree
36			cur  *Worktree
37		)
38		flush := func() {
39			if cur != nil {
40				list = append(list, *cur)
41				cur = nil
42			}
43		}
44		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
45			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
46				flush()
47				continue
48			}
49			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
50			switch key {
51			case "worktree":
52				flush()
53				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
54			case "HEAD":
55				if cur != nil {
56					cur.Head = val
57				}
58			case "branch":
59				if cur != nil {
60					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
61				}
62			case "detached":
63				if cur != nil {
64					cur.Detached = true
65				}
66			case "bare":
67				if cur != nil {
68					cur.Bare = true
69				}
70			case "locked":
71				if cur != nil {
72					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
73				}
74			case "prunable":
75				if cur != nil {
76					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
77				}
78			}
79		}
80		flush()
81		return list, nil
82	}
83	
84	// WorktreeFor finds the worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git refuses to
85	// check the same branch out twice, so at most one can match.
86	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
87		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
88		if err != nil {
89			return Worktree{}, false, err
90		}
91		for _, w := range list {
92			if w.Branch == branch {
93				return w, true, nil
94			}
95		}
96		return Worktree{}, false, nil
97	}
98	
99	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
100	//
101	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
102	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
103	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
104	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
105	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
106		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
107		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
108		if exists {
109			args = append(args, path, branch)
110		} else {
111			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
112			if base != "" {
113				args = append(args, base)
114			}
115		}
116		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
117		return err
118	}
119	
120	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
121	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
122	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
123		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
124		if force {
125			args = append(args, "--force")
126		}
127		args = append(args, path)
128		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
129		return err
130	}
131	
132	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
133	// were deleted behind git's back.
134	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
135		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
136		return err
137	}
138	
139	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
140	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
141		if branch == "" {
142			return false
143		}
144		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
145		return err == nil
146	}
147	
148	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
149	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
150		if ref == "" {
151			return false
152		}
153		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
154		return err == nil
155	}
156

173	func directPushHint(push bool) string {

175			return " --push"

180	// fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
181	// forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
182	//
183	// merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
184	// branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
185	// a merge commit the user did not ask for.
186	func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
187		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
188		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
189			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
190				"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
191				err, config.Contract(checkout))
192		}
193		// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
194		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
195		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
196			return err
197		}
198		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
199			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
200				"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
201		}
202		return nil
203	}
204	
205	// deleteMergedBranch removes a branch only when git agrees its commits are already
206	// contained in the base — the check that makes cleanup safe.
207	func deleteMergedBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, repoPath, branch, base string) error {
208		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", branch, base); err != nil {
209			return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)
210		}

38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
41			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
42			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
43				ctx := ctxOf()
44				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
45				if err != nil {
46					return err
47				}
48	
49				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
50				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
51					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
52						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
53				}
54				target := task.Warm
55				if cold {
56					target = task.Cold
57				}
58				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
59	
60				if next != "" {
61					t.Next = next
62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69	
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97	
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114	
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}

125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes
133					// the task reconstructible rather than lost.
134					t.WorktreePath = ""
135				}

138					// local + remote and resume switches back to it.
139					base := t.Base
140					if base == "" {
