```text
142					}
143					if base == "" {
144						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but its base branch is unknown")
145					}
146					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
147						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
148							base, err)
149					}
150				}
151	
152				t.State = target
153				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
154				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
155					return err
156				}
157				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
158				if t.Next != "" {
159					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
160				}
161				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
162				return nil
163			},
164		}
165		f := cmd.Flags()
166		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
167		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
168		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
169		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
170		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
171		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
172		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app)
173		return cmd
174	}
175	
176	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
177	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
178		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
179			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
180		}
181		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
182		return nil
183	}
184	
185	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
186	// directory when no argument is given.
187	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
188		if len(args) == 1 {
189			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
190		}
191		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
196		if err != nil {
197			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
198				config.Contract(cwd))
199		}
200		return t, nil
201	}
```

```text
25	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
26	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
27	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
28	identity.
29	
30	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,

38					return err
39				}
40	
41				host := config.Hostname()

44						"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
45						t.ID, t.Owner)
46				}
47	
48				if fetch {

62					if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
```

```text
320						case st.Behind > 0 && !st.Dirty():

322						case st.Behind > 0:
323							note = "behind, and dirty — commit first"
324						case st.Ahead > 0:
325							note = "unpushed commits"
326						}
327					}
328					t.Add(truncate(r.Name, 28), truncate(st.Branch, 24), st.Summary(), note)
329				}

339	// repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.
340	func repoNameFromRef(ref string) string {
341		ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")
342		if i := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:"); i >= 0 {
343			return ref[i+1:]
344		}
345		return ref
346	}
347	
348	func contractAll(paths []string) []string {
349		out := make([]string, len(paths))
350		for i, p := range paths {
351			out[i] = config.Contract(p)
352		}
353		return out
354	}
```

```text
432	// renderPlan prints a provisioning plan as a table plus its warnings.
433	func renderPlan(app *App, plan wt.Plan, repoPath string) {

444				} else {
445					deps = "global cache"
446				}

450				}
451				t.Add(e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, deps, tool)
452			}
453			t.Render(app.Out)
454		}
455	
456		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
457		if len(plan.Steps) == 0 {
458			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to provision.")
459		} else {
460			st := NewTable("", "ACTION", "WHAT", "WHY")
461			for _, s := range plan.Steps {

465				}
466				st.Add(mark, string(s.Kind), truncate(s.What, 34), s.Why)
467			}
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}
```

```text
33	func newHarness(t *testing.T) *harness {
34		t.Helper()
35		home := t.TempDir()
36		scanRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Program")
37		wtRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Worktrees")
38		if err := os.MkdirAll(scanRoot, 0o755); err != nil {
39			t.Fatal(err)
40		}
41	
42		// A repo inside the scan root, so `dev` discovers it the way it would in
43		// real use rather than via an absolute path.
44		r := gittest.New(t)
45		dest := filepath.Join(scanRoot, "demo")
46		if err := os.Rename(r.Root, dest); err != nil {
47			t.Fatal(err)
48		}
49		r.Root = dest
50	
51		// Isolate every path dev touches from the developer's real machine.
52		t.Setenv("HOME", home)
53		t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".local", "share"))
54		t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".config"))
55		t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".cache"))
56	
57		configPath := filepath.Join(home, "config.toml")
58		cfg := "" +
59			"[paths]\n" +
60			"scan_roots = [\"" + scanRoot + "\"]\n" +
61			"project_root = \"" + scanRoot + "\"\n" +
62			"tries_root = \"" + filepath.Join(home, "tries") + "\"\n" +
63			"worktree_root = \"" + wtRoot + "\"\n" +
64			"state_dir = \"" + filepath.Join(home, "state") + "\"\n" +
65			"\n[runtime]\nbackend = \"none\"\n" +
66			"\n[worktree]\ninclude = [\".env\"]\npost_create = []\n"
67		if err := os.WriteFile(configPath, []byte(cfg), 0o644); err != nil {
68			t.Fatal(err)
69		}
70		return &harness{t: t, home: home, configPath: configPath, scanRoot: scanRoot, wtRoot: wtRoot, repo: r}
71	}
72	
73	// run executes one dev invocation, capturing its output. Commands write
74	// through App, so the writers passed to NewRootCommandWithIO are all that is
75	// needed — no file-descriptor juggling.
76	func (h *harness) run(args ...string) (string, string, error) {
77		h.t.Helper()
78		var out, errBuf bytes.Buffer
79		root := cli.NewRootCommandWithIO(&out, &errBuf)
80		root.SetArgs(append([]string{"--config", h.configPath}, args...))
81		err := root.Execute()
82		return out.String(), errBuf.String(), err
83	}
84	
85	func (h *harness) mustRun(args ...string) string {
86		h.t.Helper()
87		out, errOut, err := h.run(args...)
88		if err != nil {
89			h.t.Fatalf("dev %s: %v\nstderr: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), err, errOut)
90		}
91		return out
92	}
```

```text
1	package gitx

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"os"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
11	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
12	type Repo struct {
13		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
14		Root string
15		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
16		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
17		GitCommonDir string
18		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
19		Name string
20		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
21		// the main checkout.
22		IsLinkedWorktree bool
23		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
24		MainRoot string
25		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
26		Bare bool
27	}
28	
29	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
30	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
31	
32	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
33	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
34		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
35		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
36		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
37			"rev-parse",
38			"--path-format=absolute",
39			"--show-toplevel",
40			"--git-common-dir",
41			"--is-bare-repository",
42		)
43		if err != nil {
44			return Repo{}, err
45		}
46		f := lines(out)
47		r := Repo{}
48		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
49		switch len(f) {
50		case 3:
51			r.Root = f[0]
52			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
53			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
54		case 2:
55			r.GitCommonDir = f[0]
56			r.Bare = f[1] == "true"
57		default:
58			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
59		}
60	
61		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
62		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
63		if r.Bare {
64			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
65		} else {
66			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
67		}
68		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.Root != r.MainRoot
69		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
70		if r.Bare {
71			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
72			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
73			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
74				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
75			}
76		}
77		return r, nil
78	}
79	
80	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
81	// a full Discover.
82	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
83		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
84		return err == nil
85	}
86	
87	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
88	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
89	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
90	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
91	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
92		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
93			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
94				return b
95			}
96		}
97		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
98			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
99				return cand
100			}
101		}
102		return ""
103	}
104	
105	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
106	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
107		if name == "" {
108			name = "origin"
109		}
110		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
111		if err != nil {
112			return ""
113		}
114		return out
115	}
116	
117	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
118	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
119	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
120	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
121	// semantics should use Remote instead.
122	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
123		if commonDir == "" {
124			return ""
125		}
126		if name == "" {
127			name = "origin"
128		}
129		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
130		if err != nil {
131			return ""
132		}
133		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
134		section := ""
135		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
136			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
137			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
138				continue
139			}
140			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
141				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
142				continue
143			}
144			if section != want {
145				continue
146			}
147			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
148			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
149				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
150			}
151		}
152		return ""
153	}
154
```

```text
 546 							if strings.HasPrefix(argAlias, toComplete) {
 547 								completions = append(completions, argAlias)

 549 						}

 551 				}

 554 				// Only one of ValidArgs or ValidArgsFunction can be used for a single command.
 555 				return finalCmd, completions, directive, nil

 559 			// even if we already found sub-commands.

 572 	}
 573 	if completionFn != nil {
 574 		// Go custom completion defined for this flag or command.
 575 		// Call the registered completion function to get the completions.
 576 		var comps []Completion
 577 		comps, directive = completionFn(finalCmd, finalArgs, toComplete)
 578 		completions = append(completions, comps...)
 579 	}
 580 
 581 	return finalCmd, completions, directive, nil
 582 }
```

```text
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }

28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.

31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)

33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}

54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now

69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.

85		}

100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
```

```text
1	// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
18	type Session struct {
19		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
20		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
21		Handle string
22		Label  string
23		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
24		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
25		// value.
26		Dirs []string
27		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
28		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
29		AgentStatus string
30		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
31		AgentSessions []string
32		Focused       bool
33	}
34	
35	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
36	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
37		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
38			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
39			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
40			// $HOME active.
41			if d == dir || strings.HasPrefix(d, dir+"/") {
42				return true
43			}
44		}
45		return false
46	}
47	
48	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
49	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
50	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
51	type Runtime interface {
52		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
53		Name() string
54		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
55		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
56		Available() bool
57		// Open makes dir live and returns a handle. Opening something already open
58		// focuses it rather than duplicating it.
59		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error)
60		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
61		// task entry.
62		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
63		// List enumerates live sessions.
64		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
65		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
66		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
67		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
68	}
69	
70	// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
71	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
72	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
73	type WorktreeOpener interface {
74		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error)
75	}
76	
77	// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
78	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
79	
80	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
81		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
82	}
83	
84	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
85	//
86	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
87	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then None.
88	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
89	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
90		herdr, tmux, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}
91		switch backend {
92		case "herdr":
93			return herdr
94		case "tmux":
95			return tmux
96		case "none":
97			return none
98		case "", "auto":
99			if herdr.Available() {
100				return herdr
101			}
102			if tmux.Available() {
103				return tmux
104			}
105			return none
106		}
107		return none
108	}
109	
110	// All returns every backend, for `dev doctor` to report on.
111	func All() []Runtime { return []Runtime{NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}} }
112
```

```text
 // repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.
 func repoNameFromRef(ref string) string {
 	ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")
 	if i := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:"); i >= 0 {
 		return ref[i+1:]
 	}
 	return ref
 }
 
 func contractAll(paths []string) []string {
 	out := make([]string, len(paths))
 	for i, p := range paths {
 		out[i] = config.Contract(p)
 	}
 	return out
 }
```

```text
21		Name string

33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.

38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.

44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.

73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,

79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth

88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users

130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
```

```text
21	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
22		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
23			return true
24		}
25		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {

36	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
37		if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
38			a.completionLoadAttempted = true
39			a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
40		}
41		return a.completionLoadErr == nil
42	}

44	func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
46			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
47				return nil, noFileCompletion
48			}
49			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()

51				return nil, noFileCompletion

53			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
54			for _, t := range tasks {
55				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
56				out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
57			}
58			return out, noFileCompletion
59		}
60	}

148	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
149		description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
```

```text
21	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
```

```text
9	
10	// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
11	// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
14	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
15	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  case "${1:-}" in
19	    __complete|__completeNoDesc)
20	      command %[1]s "$@"
21	      return $?
22	      ;;
23	  esac
24	
25	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
26	  __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX")" || return 1
27	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE="$__dev_cd_file" command %[1]s "$@"
28	  __dev_status=$?
29	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
30	    IFS= read -r __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
31	    if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
32	      builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
33	      __dev_status=$?
34	    fi
35	  fi
36	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
37	  return $__dev_status
38	}
39	`
40	
41	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
42	#   dev shell-init fish | source
43	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
44	function dev
45	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0; and contains -- $argv[1] __complete __completeNoDesc
46	        command %[1]s $argv
47	        return $status
48	    end
49	
50	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
51	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
52	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX")
53	    or return 1
54	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE $__dev_cd_file
55	    command %[1]s $argv
56	    set -l __dev_status $status
57	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
58	        read -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
59	        if test -n "$__dev_dir"
60	            builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
61	            set __dev_status $status
62	        end
63	    end
64	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
65	    return $__dev_status
66	end
67	`
68	
69	func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
70		cmd := &cobra.Command{
71			Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
72			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
73			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
74	
75	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
76	"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
77	directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
78	working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.
79	
80	Add to your shell rc file:
81	
82	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
83	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
84			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
85			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
86			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
87				self, err := os.Executable()
88				if err != nil || self == "" {
89					self = "dev"
90				}
91				switch args[0] {
92				case "bash", "zsh":
93					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
94				case "fish":
95					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
96				default:
97					return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
98				}
99				return nil
100			},
101		}
102		return cmd
103	}
```

```text
    feat: dev CLI for managing work in progress across repos
    
    dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
    It keeps four things separate that otherwise collapse into one: the remote
    (durable code state), worktrees (disposable checkouts), herdr/tmux (per-host
    runtime) and dev itself (human intent).
    
    Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live; dev persists
    only what git cannot answer — a task's state, owner and next action — as one
    TOML file per task, so a state directory can be a git repo and merge cleanly
    across machines.
    
    The problem it solves: when a multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of
    what you are working on, nothing can be closed without losing the thread,
    so it grows until it stops being scannable.
    
    - HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE task lifecycle with start/park/resume/done/sweep. Going
      cold is safe because the branch is the identity and the directory a cache.
    - One worktree ownership rule: dev owns anything a human may return to,
      Claude Code keeps .claude/worktrees for turn-scoped isolation. dev creates
      checkouts with git and asks herdr only to open them, so the configurable
      path policy holds on machines without herdr.
    - Worktree provisioning: gitignored-file copying, opt-in symlinks and
      lockfile-detected setup commands, overridable per repo via .dev.toml.
    - Pluggable runtime adapters (herdr, tmux, none) sharing one contract suite.
    - Repo discovery and gh/glab-backed clone, create, sync — both CLIs optional.
    - Dated experiments via try, promoted into real projects via graduate.
    - Activity heatmap from a session sampler, git backfill and WakaTime import.
    - Bundled agent skill embedded in the binary, with a command reference
      generated from the live command tree so the two cannot drift.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KfgWSELDAofucwXjMMxBao

@@ -0,0 +1,102 @@
+package cli
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+// zshInit and friends define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to leave
+// the user *inside* the checkout.
+//
+// A process can never change its parent's working directory, so dev prints a
+// `cd <path>` directive on stdout and the wrapper evaluates it. This is the
+// same mechanism try-cli uses, and it is why `dev` is a shell function rather
+// than only a binary.
+const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
+#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
+export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
+dev() {
+  local __dev_out __dev_status
+  __dev_out="$(command %[1]s "$@")"
+  __dev_status=$?
+  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ "${__dev_out#cd }" != "$__dev_out" ]; then
+    eval "$__dev_out"
+  elif [ -n "$__dev_out" ]; then
+    printf '%%s\n' "$__dev_out"
+  fi
+  return $__dev_status
+}
+`
+
+const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
+#   dev shell-init fish | source
+set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
+function dev
+    set -l __dev_out (command %[1]s $argv)
+    set -l __dev_status $status
+    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and string match -q 'cd *' -- "$__dev_out"
+        eval $__dev_out
+    else if test -n "$__dev_out"
+        printf '%%s\n' $__dev_out
+    end
+    return $__dev_status
+end
+`
+
+func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
+	cmd := &cobra.Command{
+		Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
+		Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
+		Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
+
+dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
+"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
+directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
+working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.
+
+Add to your shell rc file:
+
+    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
+    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
+		Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
+		ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
+		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
+			self, err := os.Executable()
+			if err != nil || self == "" {
+				self = "dev"
+			}
+			switch args[0] {
+			case "bash", "zsh":
+				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
+			case "fish":
+				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
+			default:
+				return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
+			}
+			return nil
+		},
+	}
+	// Completion is a sibling concern but belongs to the same "wire dev into
+	// my shell" moment, so it hangs off this command.
+	cmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
+		Use:       "completion <bash|zsh|fish>",
+		Short:     "Print shell completions",
+		Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
+		ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
+		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
+			root := cmd.Root()
+			switch args[0] {
+			case "bash":
+				return root.GenBashCompletionV2(app.Out, true)
+			case "zsh":
+				return root.GenZshCompletion(app.Out)
+			case "fish":
+				return root.GenFishCompletion(app.Out, true)
+			}
+			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q", args[0])
+		},
+	})
+	return cmd
+}
```

```text
40	func (a *App) Load() error {
41		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
42		if err != nil {
43			return err
44		}
45		a.Cfg = cfg
46		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())

59		if a.noRuntime {
```

```text
17	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
18	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
19	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
20	// persistent flags (notably --config).
21	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
22		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
23			return true
24		}
25		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
26			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
27				return true
28			}
29		}
30		return false
31	}
32	
33	// loadCompletion prepares local completion providers after Cobra has parsed the
34	// command line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break
35	// command and flag completion entirely.
36	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
37		if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
38			a.completionLoadAttempted = true
39			a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
40		}
41		return a.completionLoadErr == nil
42	}
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
46			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
47				return nil, noFileCompletion
48			}
49			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
54			for _, t := range tasks {
55				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
56				out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
57			}
58			return out, noFileCompletion
59		}
60	}

63		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
64			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
65				return nil, noFileCompletion
66			}
67			repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
68			if err != nil {

92			}

94			for _, wt := range worktrees {
95				if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
96					continue
97				}
98				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
99				if wt.Main {
100					description += " (main checkout)"
101				}
102				out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
103			}

105		}

108	func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
109		if len(args) > 0 {
110			return nil, noFileCompletion
111		}
112		topics, err := help.List()
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, noFileCompletion
115		}
116		out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
117		for _, topic := range topics {
118			out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
119		}
120		return out, noFileCompletion
121	}
122	
123	func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
124		names := ignore.BundledNames()
125		out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
126		for _, name := range names {
127			out = addCompletion(out, name, "bundled template", toComplete)
128		}
129		return out, noFileCompletion
130	}
131	
132	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
133		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
134			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
135			for _, value := range values {
136				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
137			}
138			return out, noFileCompletion
139		}
140	}
141	
142	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
143		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
144			panic(err)
145		}
146	}
147	
148	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
149		description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
150		needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
151		if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
152			return out
153		}
154		if description != "" {
155			value += "\t" + description
156		}
157		return append(out, value)
158	}
```

```text
1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	
32		// Completion requests parse the target command's persistent flags after the
33		// root pre-run hook. These fields let completion callbacks load once, at the
34		// correct time, while treating an invalid config as no dynamic candidates.
35		completionLoadAttempted bool
36		completionLoadErr       error
37	}
38	
39	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
40	func (a *App) Load() error {
41		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
42		if err != nil {
43			return err
44		}
45		a.Cfg = cfg
46		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
47		if a.Out == nil {
48			a.Out = os.Stdout
49		}
50		if a.Err == nil {
51			a.Err = os.Stderr
52		}
53		return nil
54	}
55	
56	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
57	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
58	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
59		if a.noRuntime {
60			return runtime.None{}
61		}
62		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
63		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
64			backend = a.runtimeOverride
65		}
66		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
67		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
68			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
69		}
70		return rt
71	}
72	
73	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
74	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
76	}
77	
78	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
79	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
80		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
81	}
82	
83	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
84	// gives dev a private file so normal command output can keep flowing directly
85	// to the terminal; without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by
86	// scripts and older integrations.
87	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
88		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
89			if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(dir), 0o600); err != nil {
90				a.warnf("could not write shell directory directive: %v", err)
91			}
92			return
93		}
94		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
95	}
96	
97	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
98	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
99
```

```text
1	package cli

3	import (
4		"fmt"

8	)
9	
10	// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
11	// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
14	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
15	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  case "${1:-}" in
19	    __complete|__completeNoDesc)
20	      command %[1]s "$@"
21	      return $?
22	      ;;
23	  esac
24	
25	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
26	  __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX")" || return 1
27	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE="$__dev_cd_file" command %[1]s "$@"
28	  __dev_status=$?
29	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
30	    IFS= read -r __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
31	    if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
32	      builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
33	      __dev_status=$?
34	    fi
35	  fi
36	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
37	  return $__dev_status
38	}
39	`
40	
41	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
42	#   dev shell-init fish | source
43	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
44	function dev
45	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0; and contains -- $argv[1] __complete __completeNoDesc
46	        command %[1]s $argv
47	        return $status
48	    end
49	
50	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
51	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
52	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX")
53	    or return 1
54	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE $__dev_cd_file
55	    command %[1]s $argv
56	    set -l __dev_status $status
57	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
58	        read -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
59	        if test -n "$__dev_dir"
60	            builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
61	            set __dev_status $status
62	        end
63	    end
64	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
65	    return $__dev_status
66	end
67	`
68	
69	func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
70		cmd := &cobra.Command{
71			Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
72			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
73			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
74	
75	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
76	"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
77	directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
78	working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.
79	
80	Add to your shell rc file:
81	
82	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
83	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
84			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
85			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
86			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
87				self, err := os.Executable()
88				if err != nil || self == "" {
89					self = "dev"
90				}
91				switch args[0] {
92				case "bash", "zsh":
93					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
94				case "fish":
95					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
96				default:
97					return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
98				}
99				return nil
100			},
101		}
102		return cmd
103	}
104
```

```text
83				repoTotals, err := store.RepoTotals(q)
84				if err != nil {
85					return err
86				}
87				if len(repoTotals) == 0 {
88					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nNothing recorded in that window.")
89					return nil
90				}
91				max := repoTotals[0].Seconds
92				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
93				t := NewTable("REPO", "TIME", "DAYS", "LAST", "")
94				for i, r := range repoTotals {
95					if limit > 0 && i >= limit {
96						break
97					}
98					t.Add(truncate(r.Repo, 30), stats.HumanDuration(r.Seconds),
99						fmt.Sprintf("%d", r.Days), r.Last, stats.Sparkline(r.Seconds, max, 24))
100				}
101				t.Render(app.Out)
102				return nil
103			},
104		}
105		f := cmd.Flags()
106		f.BoolVar(&heatmap, "heatmap", false, "show the day grid (shown by default unless --by-repo)")
107		f.StringVar(&since, "since", "12mo", "window: 30d, 6mo, 1y, or a YYYY-MM-DD date")

110		f.BoolVar(&byRepo, "by-repo", false, "show only the per-repo breakdown")
111		f.IntVar(&limit, "limit", 20, "maximum repositories in the breakdown (0 for all)")
112		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "repo", completeRepos(app))
113		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "source", fixedCompletions("session", "git", "wakatime"))
114	
115		cmd.AddCommand(
116			newStatsSampleCmd(app), newStatsBackfillCmd(app), newStatsImportCmd(app),
117			newStatsPathCmd(app), newStatsClearCmd(app),
118		)

214				n, err := stats.BackfillGit(ctx, store, reposToScan, start, author)
215				if err != nil {

217				}

220			},

230	func newStatsImportCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
231		var since string

233			Use:   "import-wakatime",
234			Short: "Import per-project daily totals from WakaTime",
235			Long: `Pull daily per-project totals from the WakaTime API.
236	
237	The API key is read from wakatime_config (~/.wakatime.cfg by default) — the
238	same file the editor plugins already use, so there is nothing new to configure.
239	Imported time is stored under its own source, because it overlaps with what
240	dev's sampler sees rather than replacing it.`,
241			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
242			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
243				ctx := ctxOf()
244				key, err := stats.APIKeyFromConfig(config.Expand(app.Cfg.Stats.WakaTimeConfig))
245				if err != nil {
246					return err
247				}
248				store, err := stats.Open(stats.Path(app.Cfg.StateDir()))
249				if err != nil {
250					return err
251				}
252				defer store.Close()
253	
254				until := time.Now()
255				start, err := parseSince(since, until)
256				if err != nil {
257					return err
258				}
259				w := &stats.WakaTime{APIKey: key}
260				n, err := w.Import(ctx, store, start, until)
261				if err != nil {
262					return err
263				}
264				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "imported %d project-days from WakaTime\n", n)
265				return nil
266			},
267		}
268		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&since, "since", "6mo", "how far back to import")
269		return cmd
270	}
271	
272	// parseSince accepts a relative window ("30d", "6mo", "1y") or an absolute
273	// date. Relative is what people actually type; absolute is what scripts want.
274	func parseSince(s string, now time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
275		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
276		if s == "" {
277			return now.AddDate(-1, 0, 0), nil
278		}
279		if d, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", s, time.Local); err == nil {
280			return d, nil
281		}
282		var n int
283		var unit string
284		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(s, "%d%s", &n, &unit); err != nil || n <= 0 {
285			return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot parse --since %q: want 30d, 6mo, 1y or YYYY-MM-DD", s)
286		}
287		switch strings.ToLower(unit) {
288		case "d", "day", "days":
289			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n), nil
290		case "w", "week", "weeks":
291			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n*7), nil
292		case "mo", "month", "months":
293			return now.AddDate(0, -n, 0), nil
294		case "y", "yr", "year", "years":
295			return now.AddDate(-n, 0, 0), nil
296		}
297		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown unit %q in --since: want d, w, mo or y", unit)
298	}

312	func newStatsClearCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
313		var (
314			all     bool
315			repo    string
316			sources []string
317			yes     bool
318		)
319		cmd := &cobra.Command{
320			Use:   "clear",
321			Short: "Delete selected activity data (this is durable data, not cache)",
322			Long: `Delete activity rows from $XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db.
323	
324	Stats are durable observations, not disposable cache: they include session
325	samples and WakaTime imports that cannot necessarily be reconstructed from Git.
326	Therefore a scope is required and the operation confirms unless --yes is
327	explicit.
328	
329	    dev stats clear --repo api
330	    dev stats clear --source git
331	    dev stats clear --repo api --source git
332	    dev stats clear --all
333	
334	Use "dev cache clear" for regenerable forge/gitignore caches instead.`,
335			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
336			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
337				if all && (repo != "" || len(sources) > 0) {
338					return fmt.Errorf("--all cannot be combined with --repo or --source")
339				}
340				if !all && repo == "" && len(sources) == 0 {
341					return fmt.Errorf("choose --repo, --source, or --all; stats data is not treated as disposable cache")
342				}
343				var parsed []stats.Source
344				for _, source := range sources {
345					s := stats.Source(strings.ToLower(source))
346					switch s {
347					case stats.SourceSession, stats.SourceGit, stats.SourceWakaTime:
348						parsed = append(parsed, s)
349					default:
350						return fmt.Errorf("unknown source %q: want session, git or wakatime", source)
351					}
352				}
353				description := "all activity data"
354				if !all {
355					var parts []string
356					if repo != "" {
357						parts = append(parts, "repo="+repo)
358					}
359					if len(parsed) > 0 {
360						parts = append(parts, "source="+strings.Join(sources, ","))
361					}
362					description = strings.Join(parts, " ")
363				}
364				if !yes {
365					in := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
366					if !confirm(app, in, "delete "+description+" from stats.db") {
367						fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "not changed")
368						return nil
369					}
370				}
371				store, err := stats.Open(stats.Path(app.Cfg.StateDir()))
372				if err != nil {
373					return err
374				}
375				defer store.Close()
376				q := stats.ClearQuery{}
377				if !all {
378					q.Repo, q.Sources = repo, parsed
379				}
380				n, err := store.Clear(q)
381				if err != nil {
382					return err
383				}
384				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "deleted %d activity row(s) from %s\n", n,
385					config.Contract(stats.Path(app.Cfg.StateDir())))
386				return nil
387			},
388		}
389		f := cmd.Flags()
390		f.BoolVar(&all, "all", false, "delete all activity and collector checkpoints")
391		f.StringVarP(&repo, "repo", "r", "", "delete this exact repository name")
392		f.StringSliceVar(&sources, "source", nil, "delete these sources: session, git, wakatime")
393		f.BoolVarP(&yes, "yes", "y", false, "do not prompt")
394		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "repo", completeRepos(app))
395		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "source", fixedCompletions("session", "git", "wakatime"))
396		return cmd
397	}
```

```text
21	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
22		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
23			return true
24		}

26			if cur.Name() == "completion" {

37		if !a.completionLoadAttempted {

39			a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
40		}

42	}

148	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {

150		needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
151		if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
152			return out
153		}
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}
```
