256	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
257	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
258	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
259	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
260		cfg := Default()
261		if path == "" {
262			path = ConfigFile()
263		}
264		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
265		switch {
266		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
267			return cfg, nil
268		case err != nil:
269			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
270		}
271		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
272			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
273			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
274			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
275		}
276		cfg.Source = path
277		return cfg, cfg.Validate()
278	}
279	
280	// Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a
281	// worktree create, when a directory has already been made.
282	func (c Config) Validate() error {
283		switch c.Runtime.Backend {
284		case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "none":
285		default:
286			return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
287		}
288		if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
289			return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
290		}
291		if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
292			return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
293		}
294		switch c.Bootstrap.Layout {
295		case "", "flat", "preserve":
296		default:
297			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.layout %q: want flat or preserve", c.Bootstrap.Layout)
298		}
299		if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
300			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
301		}
302		if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
303			return fmt.Errorf("forge.remote_limit must be zero (use default) or positive")
304		}
305		validStrategy := func(v string) bool {
306			switch v {
307			case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
308				return true
309			}
310			return false
311		}
312		if !validStrategy(c.Worktree.Strategy) {
313			return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategy %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip", c.Worktree.Strategy)
314		}
315		for ecosystem, strategy := range c.Worktree.Strategies {
316			if !validStrategy(strategy) {
317				return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategies.%s %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip",
318					ecosystem, strategy)
319			}
320		}
321		validColumns := map[string]bool{
322			"repo": true, "branch": true, "git": true, "live": true,
323			"latest": true, "worktrees": true, "tasks": true,
324			"category": true, "path": true,
325		}
326		for i, column := range c.TUI.Repos.Columns {
327			if !validColumns[column] {
328				return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.columns[%d] %q: unknown column", i, column)
329			}
330		}
331		switch c.EffectiveRepoSort() {
332		case "activity", "latest", "name", "git", "tasks":
333		default:
334			return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.sort %q: want activity, latest, name, git or tasks", c.TUI.Repos.Sort)
335		}
336		seen := map[string]string{}
337		for i, t := range c.TUI.Tools {
338			switch {
339			case t.Key == "":
340				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key is required", i)
341			case t.Run == "":
342				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d] (%s): run is required", i, t.Key)
343			}
344			if binding, ok := ReservedKey(t.Key); ok {
345				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is the dashboard's %q binding; pick another",
346					i, t.Key, binding)
347			}
348			if prev, ok := seen[t.Key]; ok {
349				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is already bound to %q", i, t.Key, prev)
350			}
351			seen[t.Key] = t.Name
352		}
353		return nil
354	}

	Out io.Writer
	Err io.Writer

	// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
	configPath string
	// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
	runtimeOverride string
	// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
	noRuntime bool
}

// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
func (a *App) Load() error {
	cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	a.Cfg = cfg
	a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
	if a.Out == nil {
		a.Out = os.Stdout
	}
	if a.Err == nil {
		a.Err = os.Stderr
	}
	return nil
}

// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
// --runtime and --no-runtime.
func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
	if a.noRuntime {
		return runtime.None{}
	}
	backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
	if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
		backend = a.runtimeOverride
	}
	rt := runtime.Select(backend)
	if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
		return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
	}
	return rt
}

// printf writes to the command's stdout.
func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
	fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
}

// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
	fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
}

// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
	fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
}

// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
package cli

import (
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"strings"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/skill"
	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

// Version is set at build time via -ldflags.
var Version = "dev"

const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.

It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:

  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next

Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`

// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
	return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
}

// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
// descriptors.
func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
	app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}

	root := &cobra.Command{
		Use:           "dev",
		Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
		Long:          rootLong,
		Version:       Version,
		SilenceUsage:  true,
		SilenceErrors: true,
		// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
		// exists to answer.
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
				out, err := skill.Render()
				if err != nil {
					return err
				}
				fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
				return nil
			}
			// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
			// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
			if interactive() {
				return runTUI(app)
			}
			return runList(app, listOptions{})
		},
		PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			return app.Load()
		},
	}

	pf := root.PersistentFlags()
	pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
	pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux or none")
	pf.BoolVar(&app.noRuntime, "no-runtime", false, "do not touch any terminal multiplexer")

	// Mirrors `herdr --skill`: the binary is the authority for its own agent
	// skill, so a dotfiles installer can sync it without vendoring a copy.
	root.Flags().Bool("skill", false, "print the bundled agent skill and exit")

	root.AddCommand(
		newListCmd(app),
		newTUICmd(app),
		newStatusCmd(app),
		newStartCmd(app),
		newParkCmd(app),
		newResumeCmd(app),
		newDoneCmd(app),
		newSweepCmd(app),
		newAdoptCmd(app),
		newBootstrapCmd(app),
		newWorktreeCmd(app),
		newRepoCmd(app),
		newGitignoreCmd(app),
		newTryCmd(app),
		newGraduateCmd(app),
		newStatsCmd(app),
		newHelpTopicCmd(app),
		newSkillCmd(app),
		newDoctorCmd(app),
		newShellInitCmd(app),
		newConfigCmd(app),
		newCacheCmd(app),
		newEditCmd(app),
	)
	root.SetHelpCommand(&cobra.Command{Hidden: true, Use: "no-help"})
	root.SetOut(out)
	root.SetErr(errOut)
	return root
}

// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
func Execute() int {
	root := NewRootCommand()
	if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
		msg := err.Error()
		// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
		if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
		}
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

10	// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
11	// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
14	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
15	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  case "${1:-}" in
19	    __complete|__completeNoDesc)
20	      command %[1]s "$@"
21	      return $?
22	      ;;
23	  esac
24	
25	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
26	  __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX")" || return 1
27	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE="$__dev_cd_file" command %[1]s "$@"
28	  __dev_status=$?
29	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
30	    IFS= read -r __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
31	    if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
32	      builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
33	      __dev_status=$?
34	    fi
35	  fi
36	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
37	  return $__dev_status
38	}
39	`
40	
41	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
42	#   dev shell-init fish | source
43	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
44	function dev
45	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0; and contains -- $argv[1] __complete __completeNoDesc
46	        command %[1]s $argv
47	        return $status
48	    end
49	
50	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
51	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
52	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX")
53	    or return 1
54	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE $__dev_cd_file
55	    command %[1]s $argv
56	    set -l __dev_status $status
57	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
58	        read -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
59	        if test -n "$__dev_dir"
60	            builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
61	            set __dev_status $status
62	        end
63	    end
64	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
65	    return $__dev_status
66	end
67	`

74	
75	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
76	"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
77	directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's

13	func TestCDDirectiveUsesPrivateFile(t *testing.T) {
14		path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "directive")
15		if err := os.WriteFile(path, nil, 0o600); err != nil {
16			t.Fatal(err)
17		}
18		t.Setenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE", path)
19	
20		var out, errOut bytes.Buffer
21		app := &App{Out: &out, Err: &errOut}
22		dir := "/tmp/a directory"
23		app.cdDirective(dir)
24	
25		body, err := os.ReadFile(path)
26		if err != nil {
27			t.Fatal(err)
28		}
29		if string(body) != dir {
30			t.Errorf("directive file = %q, want raw path %q", body, dir)
31		}
32		if out.Len() != 0 || errOut.Len() != 0 {
33			t.Errorf("file transport should not write streams: stdout=%q stderr=%q", out.String(), errOut.String())
34		}
35	}

37	func TestCDDirectiveFallsBackToPrintableCommand(t *testing.T) {

39		var out bytes.Buffer

41		app.cdDirective("/tmp/a directory")
42		if out.String() != "cd '/tmp/a directory'\n" {
43			t.Errorf("fallback directive = %q", out.String())
44		}
45	}

47	func TestPosixShellWrapperPreservesStreamsStatusAndCD(t *testing.T) {
48		fake, tmp, target := writeFakeDev(t)
49		for _, shell := range []string{"bash", "zsh"} {
50			path, err := exec.LookPath(shell)
51			if err != nil {
52				t.Logf("%s not installed; skipping", shell)
53				continue
54			}
55			t.Run(shell, func(t *testing.T) {
56				wrapper := fmt.Sprintf(posixInit, shellQuote(fake), shell)
57				script := wrapper + `
58	dev stream
59	stream_status=$?
60	dev fail
61	fail_status=$?
62	dev cd "$DEV_TEST_TARGET"
63	cd_status=$?
64	printf 'stream_status=%s\nfail_status=%s\ncd_status=%s\npwd=%s\n' \
65	  "$stream_status" "$fail_status" "$cd_status" "$PWD"
66	dev __complete
67	if [ -n "$(find "$TMPDIR" -name 'dev-cd.*' -print -quit)" ]; then
68	  printf 'leaked=yes\n'
69	else
70	  printf 'leaked=no\n'
71	fi
72	`
73				cmd := exec.Command(path)
74				cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(script)
75				cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "TMPDIR="+tmp, "DEV_TEST_TARGET="+target)
76				var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
77				cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
78				if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
79					t.Fatalf("run wrapper: %v\nstdout:\n%s\nstderr:\n%s", err, stdout.String(), stderr.String())
80				}
81				for _, want := range []string{
82					"streamed stdout\n", "stream_status=0\n", "fail_status=7\n",
83					"cd_status=0\n", "pwd=" + target + "\n", "completion-direct\n", "leaked=no\n",
84				} {
85					if !strings.Contains(stdout.String(), want) {
86						t.Errorf("stdout missing %q:\n%s", want, stdout.String())
87					}
88				}
89				if !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "streamed stderr\n") {
90					t.Errorf("stderr was not passed through:\n%s", stderr.String())
91				}
92			})
93		}
94	}

140	func writeFakeDev(t *testing.T) (path, tmp, target string) {
141		t.Helper()
142		root := t.TempDir()
143		tmp = filepath.Join(root, "tmp")
144		target = filepath.Join(root, "target with spaces")
145		if err := os.MkdirAll(tmp, 0o755); err != nil {
146			t.Fatal(err)
147		}
148		if err := os.MkdirAll(target, 0o755); err != nil {
149			t.Fatal(err)
150		}
151		path = filepath.Join(root, "fake dev")
152		body := `#!/bin/sh
153	case "${1:-}" in
154	  stream)
155	    printf 'streamed stdout\n'
156	    printf 'streamed stderr\n' >&2
157	    ;;
158	  fail)
159	    exit 7
160	    ;;
161	  cd)
162	    printf '%s' "$2" > "$DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"
163	    ;;
164	  __complete|__completeNoDesc)
165	    if [ -n "${DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE:-}" ]; then
166	      printf 'completion-wrapped\n'
167	    else
168	      printf 'completion-direct\n'
169	    fi
170	    ;;
171	esac
172	`
173		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o755); err != nil {
174			t.Fatal(err)
175		}
176		return path, tmp, target
177	}

30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:

60			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
61			// exists to answer.
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
64					out, err := skill.Render()
65					if err != nil {
66						return err
67					}

69					return nil
70				}

73				if interactive() {
74					return runTUI(app)
75				}
76				return runList(app, listOptions{})
77			},
78			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
79				if completionInvocation(cmd) {
80					return nil
81				}
82				return app.Load()
83			},
84		}

127	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
128	func Execute() int {
129		root := NewRootCommand()
130		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
131			msg := err.Error()
132			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
133			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
134				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
135			}
136			return 1
137		}

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}
283
```

253			Short:   "Remove a worktree checkout (never the branch)",
254			Long: `Remove a worktree's checkout.
255	
256	The branch is never deleted: removing a checkout and abandoning a change
257	stream are different decisions, and conflating them is how work gets lost.
258	A checkout with uncommitted changes needs an explicit --force.`,
259			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),

262				repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
263				if err != nil {
264					return err
265				}
266				w, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, repoPath, args[0])
267				if err != nil {
268					return err
269				}
270				if !ok {
271					return fmt.Errorf("no worktree for branch %q", args[0])
272				}
273				if w.Main {
274					return fmt.Errorf("%s is the main checkout, not a linked worktree", config.Contract(w.Path))
275				}
276				if dirty, st, err := wt.DirtyCheck(ctx, w.Path); err == nil && dirty && !force {
277					return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes (%s).\n"+
278						"Commit them, or re-run with --force to discard them",
279						config.Contract(w.Path), st.Summary())
280				}
281	
282				// Close a runtime session pointing at the checkout first, so the
283				// multiplexer is not left on a deleted directory.
284				rt := app.Runtime()
285				var handle string
286				if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
287					for _, s := range sessions {
288						for _, d := range s.Dirs {
289							if d == w.Path {
290								handle = s.Handle
291							}
292						}
293					}
294				}
295				m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
296				if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
297					RepoPath: repoPath, Path: w.Path, Force: force, RuntimeHandle: handle,
298				}); err != nil {
299					return err
300				}
301				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "removed %s (branch %s kept)\n", config.Contract(w.Path), w.Branch)
302	
303				// Keep the registry honest about what is now gone.
304				if t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(w.Path); err == nil {
305					t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = "", ""
306					if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err == nil {
307						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "task %s updated — the branch still has the work\n", t.ID)
308					}
309				}

311			},
312		}

393			Use:   "plan",

395			Long: `Report the project types detected in this repository and exactly what
396	provisioning a new worktree would do — which gitignored files get copied,
397	which dependency directories are copied or shared, and which install commands
398	run.
399	
400	A worktree that comes up broken is the commonest reason people abandon
401	worktrees, and the config alone cannot answer "what will this actually do":
402	that depends on which lockfiles exist, which tools are installed here, and

418				if write {
419					return writeRepoTemplate(app, repoPath, plan, set)
420				}
421				renderPlan(app, plan, repoPath)
422				return nil
423			},
424		}

432	// renderPlan prints a provisioning plan as a table plus its warnings.
433	func renderPlan(app *App, plan wt.Plan, repoPath string) {
434		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n\n", config.Contract(repoPath))
435	
436		if len(plan.Ecosystems) == 0 {
437			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No project type detected — only gitignored files will be carried over.")
438		} else {
439			t := NewTable("PROJECT", "MANAGER", "FROM", "DEPENDENCIES", "TOOL")
440			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
441				deps := "—"
442				if len(e.DepDirs) > 0 {
443					deps = strings.Join(e.DepDirs, ", ")
444				} else {
445					deps = "global cache"
446				}
447				tool := "installed"
448				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
449					tool = "MISSING: " + e.Tool
450				}
451				t.Add(e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, deps, tool)
452			}
453			t.Render(app.Out)
454		}
455	
456		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
457		if len(plan.Steps) == 0 {
458			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to provision.")
459		} else {
460			st := NewTable("", "ACTION", "WHAT", "WHY")
461			for _, s := range plan.Steps {
462				mark := "✓"
463				if s.Skipped {
464					mark = "·"
465				}
466				st.Add(mark, string(s.Kind), truncate(s.What, 34), s.Why)
467			}
468			st.Render(app.Out)
469		}
470	
471		for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
472			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\nwarning: %s\n", w)
473		}
474		if plan.Empty() {
475			fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "\nNothing would run. If a new worktree comes up broken, add what it needs to "+
476				"worktree.post_create, or commit a .dev.toml with `dev wt plan --write`.")
477		}
478	}
479	
480	// writeRepoTemplate seeds a .dev.toml from the detected plan.
481	//
482	// Committing it is what makes a project's worktree setup reproducible: the
483	// next machine, and the next person, get the same one without having to
484	// rediscover it.
485	func writeRepoTemplate(app *App, repoPath string, plan wt.Plan, set wt.Settings) error {
486		path := filepath.Join(repoPath, wt.OverrideFilename)
487		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
488			return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists — edit it directly", config.Contract(path))
489		}
490	
491		var b strings.Builder
492		b.WriteString("# dev worktree setup for this repository.\n")
493		b.WriteString("#\n")
494		b.WriteString("# Committed on purpose: a worktree is a clean checkout, so without this a\n")
495		b.WriteString("# new one comes up with no dependencies and none of the gitignored files the\n")
496		b.WriteString("# project needs. Seeded by `dev wt plan --write`; edit freely.\n\n")
497		b.WriteString("[worktree]\n")
498	
499		b.WriteString("# Gitignored files to carry into a new worktree. Only files that are BOTH\n")
500		b.WriteString("# listed here AND gitignored are copied — a tracked file is already in the\n")
501		b.WriteString("# checkout on the correct branch.\n")
502		b.WriteString("include = [")
503		for i, inc := range set.Include {
504			if i > 0 {
505				b.WriteString(", ")
506			}
507			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%q", inc)
508		}
509		b.WriteString("]\n\n")
510	
511		if len(plan.Ecosystems) > 0 {
512			b.WriteString("# Detected in this repository:\n")
513			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
514				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "#   %-8s %-8s (%s) → %s\n", e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, e.Install)
515			}
516			b.WriteString("#\n")
517			b.WriteString("# \"auto\" runs those install commands. Replace with an explicit list if this\n")
518			b.WriteString("# project needs something else:  post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
519			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n\n")
520	
521			b.WriteString("# How each project type gets its dependencies:\n")
522			b.WriteString("#   reinstall  run the install command (correct, the default)\n")
523			b.WriteString("#   copy       duplicate the directory from the source checkout (fast)\n")
524			b.WriteString("#   link       share one directory between checkouts (fastest, risky)\n")
525			b.WriteString("#   skip       leave the worktree without dependencies\n")
526			b.WriteString("[worktree.strategies]\n")
527			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
528				switch {
529				case len(e.DepDirs) == 0:
530					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# %-8s = \"reinstall\"  # %s uses a global cache; nothing to copy\n",
531						e.Name, e.Manager)
532				case e.CopySafe:
533					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # \"copy\" is sound here and much faster\n", e.Name)
534				default:
535					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # copy/link unsupported: %s\n", e.Name, e.Hazard)
536				}
537			}
538		} else {
539			b.WriteString("# No project type detected. Add the commands a fresh checkout needs:\n")
540			b.WriteString("# post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
541			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n")
542		}
543	
544		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
545			return err
546		}
547		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "wrote %s\n", config.Contract(path))
548		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Commit it so every machine provisions worktrees the same way.")
549		return nil
550	}
551

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5

7		"context"

14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	
32		// Completion requests parse the target command's persistent flags after the
33		// root pre-run hook. These fields let completion callbacks load once, at the
34		// correct time, while treating an invalid config as no dynamic candidates.
35		completionLoadAttempted bool
36		completionLoadErr       error
37	}

39	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
40	func (a *App) Load() error {
41		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
42		if err != nil {
43			return err
44		}
45		a.Cfg = cfg
46		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
47		if a.Out == nil {
48			a.Out = os.Stdout
49		}
50		if a.Err == nil {
51			a.Err = os.Stderr
52		}
53		return nil
54	}
55	
56	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
57	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
58	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
59		if a.noRuntime {
60			return runtime.None{}
61		}
62		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
63		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
64			backend = a.runtimeOverride
65		}
66		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
67		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
68			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
69		}
70		return rt
71	}
72	
73	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
74	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
76	}
77	
78	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
79	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
80		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
81	}
82	
83	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
84	// gives dev a private file so normal command output can keep flowing directly
85	// to the terminal; without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by
86	// scripts and older integrations.
87	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
88		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
89			if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(dir), 0o600); err != nil {
90				a.warnf("could not write shell directory directive: %v", err)
91			}
92			return
93		}
94		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
95	}

162	// findTry locates an existing try whose name contains the slug, preferring the
163	// most recent when several match.
164	func findTry(root, slug string) string {
165		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
166		if err != nil {
167			return ""
168		}
169		var best string
170		var bestTime time.Time
171		for _, e := range entries {
172			if !e.IsDir() || !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(e.Name()), strings.ToLower(slug)) {
173				continue
174			}
175			info, err := e.Info()
176			if err != nil {
177				continue
178			}
179			if info.ModTime().After(bestTime) {
180				best, bestTime = filepath.Join(root, e.Name()), info.ModTime()
181			}

package cli

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

// zshInit and friends define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to leave
// the user *inside* the checkout.
//
// A process can never change its parent's working directory, so dev prints a
// `cd <path>` directive on stdout and the wrapper evaluates it. This is the
// same mechanism try-cli uses, and it is why `dev` is a shell function rather
// than only a binary.
const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
dev() {
  local __dev_out __dev_status
  __dev_out="$(command %[1]s "$@")"
  __dev_status=$?
  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ "${__dev_out#cd }" != "$__dev_out" ]; then
    eval "$__dev_out"
  elif [ -n "$__dev_out" ]; then
    printf '%%s\n' "$__dev_out"
  fi
  return $__dev_status
}
`

const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
#   dev shell-init fish | source
set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
function dev
    set -l __dev_out (command %[1]s $argv)
    set -l __dev_status $status
    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and string match -q 'cd *' -- "$__dev_out"
        eval $__dev_out
    else if test -n "$__dev_out"
        printf '%%s\n' $__dev_out
    end
    return $__dev_status
end
`

func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
		Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
		Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.

dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
"none" runtime) print a "cd <path>" directive rather than trying to change
directory themselves, because a child process cannot change its parent's
working directory. The wrapper evaluates that directive.

Add to your shell rc file:

    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
		Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
		ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			self, err := os.Executable()
			if err != nil || self == "" {
				self = "dev"
			}
			switch args[0] {
			case "bash", "zsh":
				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
			case "fish":
				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
			default:
				return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
			}
			return nil
		},
	}
```

162	// findTry locates an existing try whose name contains the slug, preferring the
163	// most recent when several match.
164	func findTry(root, slug string) string {
165		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
166		if err != nil {
167			return ""
168		}
169		var best string
170		var bestTime time.Time
171		for _, e := range entries {
172			if !e.IsDir() || !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(e.Name()), strings.ToLower(slug)) {
173				continue
174			}
175			info, err := e.Info()
176			if err != nil {
177				continue
178			}
179			if info.ModTime().After(bestTime) {
180				best, bestTime = filepath.Join(root, e.Name()), info.ModTime()
181			}
182		}
183		return best
184	}
185	
186	func openOrCD(app *App, ctx context.Context, dir, label string) error {
187		rt := app.Runtime()
188		if rt.Name() == "none" {
189			app.cdDirective(dir)
190			return nil
191		}
192		if _, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, dir, label); err != nil {
193			app.warnf("could not open a session: %v", err)
194		}
195		return nil
196	}

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	
32		// Completion requests parse the target command's persistent flags after the
33		// root pre-run hook. These fields let completion callbacks load once, at the
34		// correct time, while treating an invalid config as no dynamic candidates.
35		completionLoadAttempted bool
36		completionLoadErr       error
37	}
38	
39	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
40	func (a *App) Load() error {
41		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
42		if err != nil {
43			return err
44		}
45		a.Cfg = cfg
46		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
47		if a.Out == nil {
48			a.Out = os.Stdout
49		}
50		if a.Err == nil {
51			a.Err = os.Stderr
52		}
53		return nil
54	}
55	
56	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
57	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
58	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
59		if a.noRuntime {
60			return runtime.None{}
61		}
62		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
63		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
64			backend = a.runtimeOverride
65		}
66		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
67		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
68			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
69		}
70		return rt
71	}
72	
73	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
74	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
76	}
77	
78	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
79	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
80		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
81	}
82	
83	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
84	// gives dev a private file so normal command output can keep flowing directly
85	// to the terminal; without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by
86	// scripts and older integrations.
87	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
88		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
89			if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(dir), 0o600); err != nil {
90				a.warnf("could not write shell directory directive: %v", err)
91			}
92			return
93		}
94		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
95	}
96	
97	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
98	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }

125	// humanAge renders a duration the way a changelog would: "3d", "2w", "5mo".
126	func humanAge(d time.Duration) string {
127		switch {
128		case d <= 0:
129			return "—"
130		case d < time.Hour:
131			return fmt.Sprintf("%dm", int(d.Minutes()))
132		case d < 24*time.Hour:
133			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
134		case d < 14*24*time.Hour:
135			return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", int(d.Hours()/24))
136		case d < 60*24*time.Hour:
137			return fmt.Sprintf("%dw", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
138		default:
139			return fmt.Sprintf("%dmo", int(d.Hours()/24/30))
140		}
141	}
142	
143	// shellQuote makes a path safe to paste into a POSIX shell command.
144	func shellQuote(s string) string {
145		if s == "" {
146			return "''"
147		}
148		safe := true
149		for _, r := range s {
150			if !(r == '/' || r == '.' || r == '-' || r == '_' || r == '~' ||
151				(r >= 'a' && r <= 'z') || (r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z') || (r >= '0' && r <= '9')) {
152				safe = false
153				break
154			}
155		}
156		if safe && utf8.ValidString(s) {
157			return s
158		}
159		return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) + "'"
160	}

15	const worktreeLong = `Manage the linked worktrees dev owns.
16	
17	Who owns which worktree — the rule dev encodes, so nobody has to improvise:
18	
19	  dev            anything you might come back to tomorrow: features, fixes,
20	                 experiments, cross-machine handoffs. Placed at
21	                 paths.worktree_path, outside the repo.
22	  Claude Code    turn-scoped subagent isolation that dies with the turn, in
23	                 .claude/worktrees/ (keep that gitignored).
24	  herdr          dev does not call "herdr worktree create". It creates the
25	                 worktree with git and asks herdr to open it, so the path
26	                 policy holds on machines without herdr too.
27	
28	A new worktree is a clean checkout: no node_modules, no .venv, none of the
29	gitignored env files the project needs. dev provisions it — see the config's
30	[worktree] section, or a repo's own .dev.toml.`

50	// repoContext resolves the repository to operate on: an explicit --repo, else
51	// the current directory.
52	func repoContext(app *App, ref string) (path, name string, err error) {
53		ctx := ctxOf()
54		if ref != "" {
55			r, _, err := resolveRepoRef(app, ref)
56			if err != nil {
57				return "", "", err
58			}
59			return r.Path, r.Name, nil
60		}
61		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
62		if err != nil {
63			return "", "", err
64		}
65		g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd)
66		if err != nil {
67			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("%s is not a git repository — pass --repo",
68				config.Contract(cwd))
69		}
70		return g.MainRoot, g.Name, nil
71	}

80				ctx := ctxOf()

85				list, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, repoPath)
86				if err != nil {

89				rt := app.Runtime()
90				sessions, _ := rt.List(ctx)
91	
92				t := NewTable("", "BRANCH", "PATH", "GIT", "SESSION")
93				for _, w := range list {
94					marker := "  "
95					if w.Main {
96						marker = "★ " // the canonical checkout
97					}
98					branch := w.Branch
99					if branch == "" {
100						branch = "(detached)"
101					}
102					gitCol := "—"
103					if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, w.Path); err == nil {
104						gitCol = st.Summary()
105					}
106					switch {
107					case w.Prunable:
108						gitCol = "prunable"
109					case w.Locked:
110						gitCol = "locked"
111					}
112					session := "—"
113					for _, s := range sessions {
114						for _, d := range s.Dirs {
115							if d == w.Path {
116								session = rt.Name() + " " + s.Handle
117							}
118						}
119					}
120					t.Add(marker, branch, config.Contract(w.Path), gitCol, session)
121				}
122				t.Render(app.Out)
123				return nil
124			},
125		}

245	func newWtRemoveCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
246		var (
247			repoRef string
248			force   bool
249		)
250		cmd := &cobra.Command{
251			Use:     "rm <branch>",
252			Aliases: []string{"remove"},
253			Short:   "Remove a worktree checkout (never the branch)",
254			Long: `Remove a worktree's checkout.
255	
256	The branch is never deleted: removing a checkout and abandoning a change
257	stream are different decisions, and conflating them is how work gets lost.
258	A checkout with uncommitted changes needs an explicit --force.`,
259			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
260			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
261				ctx := ctxOf()
262				repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
263				if err != nil {
264					return err
265				}
266				w, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, repoPath, args[0])
267				if err != nil {
268					return err
269				}
270				if !ok {
271					return fmt.Errorf("no worktree for branch %q", args[0])
272				}
273				if w.Main {
274					return fmt.Errorf("%s is the main checkout, not a linked worktree", config.Contract(w.Path))
275				}
276				if dirty, st, err := wt.DirtyCheck(ctx, w.Path); err == nil && dirty && !force {
277					return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes (%s).\n"+
278						"Commit them, or re-run with --force to discard them",
279						config.Contract(w.Path), st.Summary())
280				}
281	
282				// Close a runtime session pointing at the checkout first, so the
283				// multiplexer is not left on a deleted directory.
284				rt := app.Runtime()
285				var handle string
286				if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
287					for _, s := range sessions {
288						for _, d := range s.Dirs {
289							if d == w.Path {
290								handle = s.Handle
291							}
292						}
293					}
294				}
295				m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
296				if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
297					RepoPath: repoPath, Path: w.Path, Force: force, RuntimeHandle: handle,
298				}); err != nil {
299					return err
300				}
301				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "removed %s (branch %s kept)\n", config.Contract(w.Path), w.Branch)
302	
303				// Keep the registry honest about what is now gone.
304				if t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(w.Path); err == nil {
305					t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = "", ""
306					if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err == nil {
307						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "task %s updated — the branch still has the work\n", t.ID)
308					}
309				}
310				return nil
311			},
312		}
313		f := cmd.Flags()
314		f.StringVarP(&repoRef, "repo", "r", "", "repository (default: the current one)")
315		f.BoolVarP(&force, "force", "f", false, "remove even with uncommitted changes")
316		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "repo", completeRepos(app))
317		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeWorktrees(app, false)
318		return cmd
319	}

326			Long: `Bring an existing checkout up to a working state again.
327	
328	Copies the gitignored files, applies the dependency strategy and runs the
329	post-create commands — useful after adding a new .env, or when a worktree was

339				}

373				}
374				for _, s := range res.Skipped {

376				}
377				for _, e := range res.Failures {
378					app.warnf("%v", e)

387	func newWtPlanCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
388		var (
389			repoRef string
390			write   bool
391		)
392		cmd := &cobra.Command{
393			Use:   "plan",
394			Short: "Show what a new worktree of this repo would be provisioned with",
395			Long: `Report the project types detected in this repository and exactly what
396	provisioning a new worktree would do — which gitignored files get copied,
397	which dependency directories are copied or shared, and which install commands
398	run.
399	
400	A worktree that comes up broken is the commonest reason people abandon
401	worktrees, and the config alone cannot answer "what will this actually do":
402	that depends on which lockfiles exist, which tools are installed here, and
403	which files are genuinely gitignored. This computes all of it and changes
404	nothing.
405	
406	With --write, seed a .dev.toml from what was detected, so the repository can
407	commit its own setup and every machine gets the same one.`,
408			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
409			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
410				ctx := ctxOf()
411				repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
412				if err != nil {
413					return err
414				}
415				set := wt.SettingsFor(app.Cfg, repoPath)
416				plan := wt.BuildPlan(ctx, set, repoPath)
417	
418				if write {
419					return writeRepoTemplate(app, repoPath, plan, set)
420				}
421				renderPlan(app, plan, repoPath)
422				return nil
423			},
424		}
425		f := cmd.Flags()
426		f.StringVarP(&repoRef, "repo", "r", "", "repository (default: the current one)")
427		f.BoolVar(&write, "write", false, "seed a .dev.toml in the repository from what was detected")
428		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "repo", completeRepos(app))
429		return cmd
430	}
431	
432	// renderPlan prints a provisioning plan as a table plus its warnings.
433	func renderPlan(app *App, plan wt.Plan, repoPath string) {
434		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n\n", config.Contract(repoPath))
435	
436		if len(plan.Ecosystems) == 0 {
437			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No project type detected — only gitignored files will be carried over.")
438		} else {
439			t := NewTable("PROJECT", "MANAGER", "FROM", "DEPENDENCIES", "TOOL")
440			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
441				deps := "—"
442				if len(e.DepDirs) > 0 {
443					deps = strings.Join(e.DepDirs, ", ")
444				} else {
445					deps = "global cache"
446				}
447				tool := "installed"
448				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
449					tool = "MISSING: " + e.Tool
450				}
451				t.Add(e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, deps, tool)
452			}
453			t.Render(app.Out)
454		}
455	
456		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
457		if len(plan.Steps) == 0 {
458			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to provision.")
459		} else {
460			st := NewTable("", "ACTION", "WHAT", "WHY")
461			for _, s := range plan.Steps {
462				mark := "✓"
463				if s.Skipped {
464					mark = "·"
465				}
466				st.Add(mark, string(s.Kind), truncate(s.What, 34), s.Why)
467			}
468			st.Render(app.Out)
469		}
470	
471		for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
472			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\nwarning: %s\n", w)
473		}
474		if plan.Empty() {
475			fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "\nNothing would run. If a new worktree comes up broken, add what it needs to "+
476				"worktree.post_create, or commit a .dev.toml with `dev wt plan --write`.")
477		}
478	}
479	
480	// writeRepoTemplate seeds a .dev.toml from the detected plan.
481	//
482	// Committing it is what makes a project's worktree setup reproducible: the
483	// next machine, and the next person, get the same one without having to
484	// rediscover it.
485	func writeRepoTemplate(app *App, repoPath string, plan wt.Plan, set wt.Settings) error {
486		path := filepath.Join(repoPath, wt.OverrideFilename)
487		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
488			return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists — edit it directly", config.Contract(path))
489		}
490	
491		var b strings.Builder
492		b.WriteString("# dev worktree setup for this repository.\n")
493		b.WriteString("#\n")
494		b.WriteString("# Committed on purpose: a worktree is a clean checkout, so without this a\n")
495		b.WriteString("# new one comes up with no dependencies and none of the gitignored files the\n")
496		b.WriteString("# project needs. Seeded by `dev wt plan --write`; edit freely.\n\n")
497		b.WriteString("[worktree]\n")
498	
499		b.WriteString("# Gitignored files to carry into a new worktree. Only files that are BOTH\n")
500		b.WriteString("# listed here AND gitignored are copied — a tracked file is already in the\n")
501		b.WriteString("# checkout on the correct branch.\n")
502		b.WriteString("include = [")
503		for i, inc := range set.Include {
504			if i > 0 {
505				b.WriteString(", ")
506			}
507			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%q", inc)
508		}
509		b.WriteString("]\n\n")
510	
511		if len(plan.Ecosystems) > 0 {
512			b.WriteString("# Detected in this repository:\n")
513			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
514				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "#   %-8s %-8s (%s) → %s\n", e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, e.Install)
515			}
516			b.WriteString("#\n")
517			b.WriteString("# \"auto\" runs those install commands. Replace with an explicit list if this\n")
518			b.WriteString("# project needs something else:  post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
519			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n\n")
520	
521			b.WriteString("# How each project type gets its dependencies:\n")
522			b.WriteString("#   reinstall  run the install command (correct, the default)\n")
523			b.WriteString("#   copy       duplicate the directory from the source checkout (fast)\n")
524			b.WriteString("#   link       share one directory between checkouts (fastest, risky)\n")
525			b.WriteString("#   skip       leave the worktree without dependencies\n")
526			b.WriteString("[worktree.strategies]\n")
527			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
528				switch {
529				case len(e.DepDirs) == 0:
530					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# %-8s = \"reinstall\"  # %s uses a global cache; nothing to copy\n",
531						e.Name, e.Manager)
532				case e.CopySafe:
533					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # \"copy\" is sound here and much faster\n", e.Name)
534				default:
535					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # copy/link unsupported: %s\n", e.Name, e.Hazard)
536				}
537			}
538		} else {
539			b.WriteString("# No project type detected. Add the commands a fresh checkout needs:\n")
540			b.WriteString("# post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
541			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n")
542		}
543	
544		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
545			return err
546		}
547		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "wrote %s\n", config.Contract(path))
548		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Commit it so every machine provisions worktrees the same way.")
549		return nil
550	}

14	func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			noProvision bool
17			fetch       bool
18			force       bool
19		)
20		cmd := &cobra.Command{
21			Use:   "resume <task>",
22			Short: "Pick a task back up, rebuilding whatever is missing",
23			Long: `Make a parked task hot again.
24	
25	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
26	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
27	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
28	identity.
29	
30	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
33			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
34			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
35				ctx := ctxOf()
36				t, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
37				if err != nil {
38					return err
39				}
40	
41				host := config.Hostname()
42				if !t.OwnedBy(host) && !force {
43					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is owned by %s.\n"+
44						"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
45						t.ID, t.Owner)
46				}
47	
48				if fetch {
49					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "fetch", "--prune", "origin"); err != nil {
50						app.warnf("fetch failed: %v", err)
51					}
52				}
53	
54				rt := app.Runtime()
55				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
56				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
57	
58				switch mode {
59				case task.ModeWorktree:
60					_, statErr := os.Stat(checkout)
61					// Rebuild the worktree when it is gone — the cold-to-hot path.
62					if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
63						base := t.Base
64						// Prefer the published branch: a cold task's work lives on
65						// the remote, and a stale local ref could drop it.
66						if remote := "origin/" + t.Branch; gitx.RefExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, remote) {
67							base = remote
68						}
69						m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
70						res, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
71							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, RepoName: t.Repo, Branch: t.Branch,
72							Base: base, Label: t.Title(), NoProvision: noProvision,
73						})
74						if err != nil {
75							var exists *wt.ErrExists
76							if asError(err, &exists) {
77								t.WorktreePath = exists.Path
78							} else {
79								return err
80							}
81						} else {
82							t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = res.Path, res.RuntimeHandle
83							reportProvision(app, res)
84							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebuilt    %s\n", config.Contract(res.Path))
85						}
86						checkout = t.WorktreePath
87					}
88	
89				case task.ModeBranch:
90					checkout = t.RepoPath
91					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
92					if err != nil {
93						return err
94					}
95					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
96						if st.Dirty() {
97							return fmt.Errorf("cannot switch the canonical checkout from %s to %s: %s",
98								st.Branch, t.Branch, st.Breakdown())
99						}
100						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "switch", t.Branch); err != nil {
101							return err
102						}
103					}
104	
105				case task.ModeDirect:
106					checkout = t.RepoPath
107					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
108					if err != nil {
109						return err
110					}
111					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
112						return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s tracks %s, but the canonical checkout is on %s; "+
113							"switch back explicitly or start a worktree task", t.Title(), t.Branch, st.Branch)
114					}
115				}
116				if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
117					handle, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, checkout, t.Title())
118					if err != nil {
119						app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
120					}
121					if rt.Name() != "none" {
122						t.RuntimeHandle = handle
123					}
124				}
125	
126				t.State = task.Hot
127				t.Owner = host
128				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
129					return err
130				}
131				annotate(app, rt, t)
132	
133				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s  %s on %s (%s)\n",
134					task.Hot.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, mode)
135				if t.Next != "" {
136					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   next      %s\n", t.Next)
137				}
138				if t.AgentSession != "" {
139					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   agent     %s (resumable)\n", t.AgentSession)
140				}
141				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout); err == nil {
142					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   git       %s\n", st.Summary())
143					if st.Behind > 0 {
144						app.warnf("branch is %d behind upstream — `git pull --ff-only` before you start", st.Behind)
145					}
146				}
147				if rt.Name() == "none" {
148					app.cdDirective(checkout)
149				}
150				return nil
151			},
152		}
153		f := cmd.Flags()
154		f.BoolVar(&noProvision, "no-provision", false, "skip dependency install when rebuilding a worktree")
155		f.BoolVar(&fetch, "fetch", true, "fetch from origin first")
156		f.BoolVar(&force, "force", false, "take ownership of a task owned by another machine")
157		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app)
158		return cmd
159	}

339	// repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.

171		flag := c.Flag(flagName)

204		}
205		if d&ShellCompDirectiveNoSpace != 0 {

216		}

218			directives = append(directives, "ShellCompDirectiveKeepOrder")
219		}
220		if len(directives) == 0 {

222		}

224		if d >= shellCompDirectiveMaxValue {
225			return fmt.Sprintf("ERROR: unexpected ShellCompDirective value: %d", d)
226		}

+package cli
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/help"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/ignore"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/repo"
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+var noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
+
+// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
+// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
+// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
+// persistent flags (notably --config).
+func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
+	if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
+		return true
+	}
+	for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
+		if cur.Name() == "completion" {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// loadCompletion prepares local completion providers after Cobra has parsed the
+// command line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break
+// command and flag completion entirely.
+func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
+	if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
+		a.completionLoadAttempted = true
+		a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
+	}
+	return a.completionLoadErr == nil
+}
+
+func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
+		for _, t := range tasks {
+			description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
+			out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
+		for _, r := range repos {
+			out = addCompletion(out, r.Display(), config.Contract(r.Path), toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
+		repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
+		for _, wt := range worktrees {
+			if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
+				continue
+			}
+			description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
+			if wt.Main {
+				description += " (main checkout)"
+			}
+			out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+	if len(args) > 0 {
+		return nil, noFileCompletion
+	}
+	topics, err := help.List()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, noFileCompletion
+	}
+	out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
+	for _, topic := range topics {
+		out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
+	}
+	return out, noFileCompletion
+}
+
+func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+	names := ignore.BundledNames()
+	out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
+	for _, name := range names {
+		out = addCompletion(out, name, "bundled template", toComplete)
+	}
+	return out, noFileCompletion
+}
+
+func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
+		for _, value := range values {
+			out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
+	if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
+		panic(err)
+	}
+}
+
+func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
+	description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
+	needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
+	if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
+		return out
+	}
+	if description != "" {
+		value += "\t" + description
+	}
+	return append(out, value)
+}

+package cli_test

+func (h *harness) runRaw(args ...string) (string, string, error) {
+	h.t.Helper()
+	var out, errBuf bytes.Buffer
+	root := cli.NewRootCommandWithIO(&out, &errBuf)
+	root.SetArgs(args)
+	err := root.Execute()
+	return out.String(), errBuf.String(), err

92	func (s *Store) Add(entries ...Entry) error {
93		if len(entries) == 0 {

97		if err != nil {
98			return err
99		}

102		stmt, err := tx.Prepare(`
103	INSERT INTO activity (day, repo, branch, source, seconds) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
104	ON CONFLICT (day, repo, branch, source) DO UPDATE SET seconds = seconds + excluded.seconds`)
105		if err != nil {
106			return err
107		}
108		defer stmt.Close()
109	
110		for _, e := range entries {
111			if e.Seconds <= 0 || e.Repo == "" {
112				continue
113			}
114			if _, err := stmt.Exec(e.Day.Format(dayFormat), e.Repo, e.Branch, string(e.Source), e.Seconds); err != nil {
115				return err
116			}
117		}
118		return tx.Commit()

150	const dayFormat = "2006-01-02"

152	// Query narrows a report.
153	type Query struct {
154		Since time.Time
155		Until time.Time
156		Repo  string
157		// ExactRepo uses equality rather than the report-friendly substring match.
158		// Per-repo TUI panels set it so "api" does not include "my-api".
159		ExactRepo bool
160		// Sources limits which collectors count. Empty means all of them.

162	}

164	func (q Query) where() (string, []any) {
165		clause := "WHERE day >= ? AND day <= ?"
166		args := []any{q.Since.Format(dayFormat), q.Until.Format(dayFormat)}
167		if q.Repo != "" {
168			if q.ExactRepo {
169				clause += " AND repo = ?"
170				args = append(args, q.Repo)
171			} else {
172				clause += " AND repo LIKE ?"
173				args = append(args, "%"+q.Repo+"%")
174			}
175		}
176		if len(q.Sources) > 0 {
177			clause += " AND source IN (" + placeholders(len(q.Sources)) + ")"
178			for _, s := range q.Sources {
179				args = append(args, string(s))
180			}
181		}
182		return clause, args
183	}

185	func placeholders(n int) string {
186		if n == 0 {
187			return ""
188		}
189		out := make([]byte, 0, n*2-1)
190		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
191			if i > 0 {
192				out = append(out, ',')
193			}
194			out = append(out, '?')
195		}
196		return string(out)
197	}

201		clause, args := q.where()
202		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT day, SUM(seconds) FROM activity `+clause+` GROUP BY day`, args...)
203		if err != nil {
204			return nil, err
205		}
206		defer rows.Close()
207	
208		out := map[string]int{}
209		for rows.Next() {
210			var day string
211			var secs int
212			if err := rows.Scan(&day, &secs); err != nil {
213				return nil, err
214			}
215			out[day] = secs
216		}
217		return out, rows.Err()
218	}

299		clause := ""

303			args = append(args, q.Repo)
304		}

312			for _, source := range q.Sources {

317		if err != nil {

13	
14	// SampleInterval is how much time one sampler run attributes to each active
15	// session. It must match how often the sampler actually runs, so the caller
16	// passes it explicitly rather than relying on a default that silently drifts.
17	const SampleInterval = 5 * time.Minute
18	
19	// Sample attributes one interval of time to every live session whose working
20	// directory sits inside a known repository.
21	//
22	// Only sessions with a *working* agent, or any session when includeIdle is
23	// set, are counted. A workspace left open for three weeks is not three weeks
24	// of work, and counting it that way would make the whole chart meaningless.
25	func Sample(ctx context.Context, s *Store, rt runtime.Runtime, repos []repo.Repo, interval time.Duration, includeIdle bool) (int, error) {
26		sessions, err := rt.List(ctx)
27		if err != nil {
28			return 0, err
29		}
30		now := time.Now()
31		seen := map[string]bool{}
32		var entries []Entry
33	
34		for _, sess := range sessions {
35			if !includeIdle && !isActive(sess.AgentStatus) {
36				continue
37			}
38			for _, dir := range sess.Dirs {
39				r, ok := repoContaining(repos, dir)
40				if !ok {
41					continue
42				}
43				// One session covering several panes in the same repo is still one
44				// person working, so credit it once.
45				key := sess.Handle + "\x00" + r.Name
46				if seen[key] {
47					continue
48				}
49				seen[key] = true
50				branch := ""
51				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, dir); err == nil {
52					branch = st.Branch
53				}
54				entries = append(entries, Entry{
55					Day: now, Repo: r.Name, Branch: branch,
56					Source: SourceSession, Seconds: int(interval.Seconds()),
57				})
58			}
59		}
60		if err := s.Add(entries...); err != nil {
61			return 0, err
62		}
63		return len(entries), s.MarkCollected("session", now)
64	}
65	
66	// isActive reports a session doing something worth counting. Backends that
67	// report no status at all are counted, since the alternative is recording
68	// nothing on tmux.
69	func isActive(status string) bool {
70		switch strings.ToLower(status) {
71		case "working", "running", "busy", "":
72			return true
73		}
74		return false
75	}
76	
77	func repoContaining(repos []repo.Repo, dir string) (repo.Repo, bool) {
78		var best repo.Repo
79		bestLen := 0
80		for _, r := range repos {
81			if dir == r.Path || strings.HasPrefix(dir, r.Path+"/") {
82				if len(r.Path) > bestLen {
83					best, bestLen = r, len(r.Path)
84				}
85			}
86		}
87		return best, bestLen > 0
88	}
89	
90	// CommitWeight is the time credited to one commit when backfilling from git
91	// history. Commits are evidence that work happened on a day, not a measure of
92	// how long it took, so this is a coarse stand-in — enough to shade a heatmap
93	// cell, not to bill against.
94	const CommitWeight = 20 * time.Minute
95	
96	// BackfillGit reads commit history and records one CommitWeight per commit,
97	// per day, per repo.
98	//
99	// This is what makes a heatmap useful on the day dev is installed rather than
100	// three months later, and what lets the chart survive losing stats.db.
101	func BackfillGit(ctx context.Context, s *Store, repos []repo.Repo, since time.Time, author string) (int, error) {
102		var entries []Entry
103		for _, r := range repos {
104			if r.Bare {
105				continue
106			}
107			args := []string{"log", "--all", "--no-merges",
108				"--since=" + since.Format("2006-01-02"), "--format=%at%x09%aE"}
109			out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, r.Path, args...)
110			if err != nil || out == "" {
111				continue
112			}
113			// Commits land in buckets by day; several commits on one day add up.
114			perDay := map[string]int{}
115			for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
116				ts, email, _ := strings.Cut(line, "\t")
117				if author != "" && !strings.EqualFold(email, author) {
118					continue
119				}
120				unix, err := strconv.ParseInt(strings.TrimSpace(ts), 10, 64)
121				if err != nil {
122					continue
123				}
124				perDay[time.Unix(unix, 0).Format(dayFormat)]++
125			}
126			for day, count := range perDay {
127				d, err := time.ParseInLocation(dayFormat, day, time.Local)
128				if err != nil {
129					continue
130				}
131				entries = append(entries, Entry{
132					Day: d, Repo: r.Name, Source: SourceGit,
133					Seconds: count * int(CommitWeight.Seconds()),
134				})
135			}
136		}
137		// Set, not Add: re-running a backfill over the same window must not double
138		// the numbers.
139		if err := s.Set(entries...); err != nil {
140			return 0, err
141		}
142		return len(entries), s.MarkCollected("git", time.Now())
143	}

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-27 16:53:05Z)**_

Public reachability is straightforward: root dispatch inherits the process environment unchanged, and `--no-runtime` forces `runtime.None`, causing successful `repo open`, `wt open/create`, `resume`, `start`, and related flows to call the sink. The generated wrappers normally provide a fresh `mktemp` path, but that convention is neither authenticated nor required by direct CLI execution.

79	// Create adds a linked worktree, provisions it and surfaces it in the runtime.
80	func (m *Manager) Create(ctx context.Context, req CreateRequest) (*CreateResult, error) {
81		if req.Branch == "" {
82			return nil, errors.New("branch is required")
83		}
84		repo, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, req.RepoPath)
85		if err != nil {
86			return nil, err
87		}
88		// Always operate from the main checkout: creating a worktree from inside
89		// another worktree works, but the relative paths and the base ref get
90		// confusing fast.
91		repoPath := repo.MainRoot
92		if req.RepoName == "" {
93			req.RepoName = repo.Name
94		}
95	
96		// Git refuses to check one branch out twice, so an existing worktree for
97		// this branch is a reuse, not an error the user needs to resolve.
98		if existing, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch); err == nil && ok {
99			return nil, &ErrExists{Branch: req.Branch, Path: existing.Path}
100		}
101	
102		path := req.Path
103		if path == "" {
104			path, err = m.Cfg.WorktreePathFor(req.RepoName, repoPath, req.Branch, req.Category)
105			if err != nil {
106				return nil, err
107			}
108		} else {
109			path = config.Expand(path)
110		}
111		if err := m.checkTarget(path, repoPath); err != nil {
112			return nil, err
113		}
114	
115		base := req.Base
116		branchExisted := gitx.BranchExists(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch)
117		if !branchExisted {

119				base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
120			}
121			if base != "" && !gitx.RefExists(ctx, repoPath, base) {
122				return nil, fmt.Errorf("base ref %q does not exist in %s", base, repoPath)
123			}
124		}
125	
126		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
127			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create worktree parent: %w", err)
128		}
129		if err := gitx.AddWorktree(ctx, repoPath, path, req.Branch, base); err != nil {
130			return nil, err
131		}
132		m.logf("worktree %s -> %s", req.Branch, config.Contract(path))
133	
134		res := &CreateResult{Path: path, Branch: req.Branch, BranchCreated: !branchExisted}
135	
136		if !req.NoProvision {

138			// its setup where a teammate on another machine picks it up too.
139			p := &Provisioner{

141				Timeout:  m.Cfg.Worktree.ProvisionTimeout.Duration,
142				Log:      m.Log,
143			}
144			pr, err := p.Provision(ctx, repoPath, path)
145			if err != nil {
146				// The checkout exists and is usable; provisioning is best-effort.
147				m.logf("warning: provisioning: %v", err)
148			}
149			res.Provision = pr
150		}

152		if !req.NoRuntime && m.Runtime != nil {
153			label := req.Label
154			if label == "" {
155				label = req.RepoName + "/" + req.Branch
156			}
157			handle, err := m.surface(ctx, path, label)
158			if err != nil {

160			} else if m.Runtime.Name() != "none" {
161				res.RuntimeHandle, res.RuntimeName = handle, m.Runtime.Name()
162			}
163		}
164		return res, nil
165	}
