167	// surface registers the checkout with the runtime. When the backend
168	// understands git worktrees it is asked to open it as one, which is what makes
169	// the checkout appear grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and
170	// ahead/behind row rather than as an unrelated directory.
171	func (m *Manager) surface(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error) {
172		if wo, ok := m.Runtime.(runtime.WorktreeOpener); ok {
173			return wo.OpenWorktree(ctx, path, label)
174		}
175		return m.Runtime.Open(ctx, path, label)
176	}
177	
178	// checkTarget refuses locations that would cause trouble later.
179	func (m *Manager) checkTarget(path, repoPath string) error {
180		if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
181			if !info.IsDir() {
182				return fmt.Errorf("%s exists and is not a directory", path)
183			}
184			entries, err := os.ReadDir(path)
185			if err != nil {
186				return err
187			}
188			if len(entries) > 0 {
189				return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists and is not empty", config.Contract(path))
190			}
191		}
192		// A worktree nested inside another checkout means every indexer, file
193		// watcher and ripgrep run in the outer repo sees a second copy of the
194		// tree. dev keeps checkouts as siblings under the worktree root instead.
195		if path == repoPath || strings.HasPrefix(path, repoPath+string(filepath.Separator)) {
196			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to create a worktree inside the repository (%s); "+
197				"set paths.worktree_path to a location outside %s",
198				config.Contract(path), config.Contract(repoPath))
199		}
200		return nil
201	}
202	
203	// RemoveRequest describes a worktree removal.
204	type RemoveRequest struct {
205		RepoPath string
206		Path     string
207		// Force allows removing a checkout with uncommitted changes. dev never
208		// sets this on its own: losing uncommitted work is exactly the outcome the
209		// tool exists to prevent.
210		Force bool
211		// RuntimeHandle is closed before the checkout is removed, so the
212		// multiplexer is not left pointing at a deleted directory.
213		RuntimeHandle string
214	}
215	
216	// Remove deletes a worktree checkout. It never deletes the branch — that stays
217	// a separate, explicit decision, matching git's own separation.
218	func (m *Manager) Remove(ctx context.Context, req RemoveRequest) error {
219		if req.RuntimeHandle != "" && m.Runtime != nil {
220			if err := m.Runtime.Close(ctx, req.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
221				m.logf("warning: could not close runtime session %s: %v", req.RuntimeHandle, err)
222			}
223		}
224		if _, err := os.Stat(req.Path); errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
225			// The directory is already gone; clear git's administrative entry.
226			return gitx.PruneWorktrees(ctx, req.RepoPath)
227		}
228		if err := gitx.RemoveWorktree(ctx, req.RepoPath, req.Path, req.Force); err != nil {
229			return err
230		}
231		m.logf("removed worktree %s", config.Contract(req.Path))
232		return nil
233	}
234	
235	// DirtyCheck reports whether a checkout has uncommitted work, so callers can
236	// refuse to remove it without an explicit --force.
237	func DirtyCheck(ctx context.Context, path string) (bool, gitx.Status, error) {
238		st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, path)
239		if err != nil {
240			return false, st, err
241		}
242		return st.Dirty(), st, nil
243	}

1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"regexp"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// Path templates are deliberately *not* text/template: the syntax users write
10	// in config.toml ("{{worktree_root}}/{{repo}}/{{branch|slug}}") needs to stay
11	// readable and to fail loudly on an unknown variable rather than silently
12	// rendering "<no value>".
13	
14	var tmplVar = regexp.MustCompile(`\{\{\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*(?:\|\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*)?\}\}`)
15	
16	// Vars is the substitution environment for a path template.
17	type Vars map[string]string
18	
19	// Render substitutes every {{var}} / {{var|filter}} occurrence in tmpl.
20	// An unknown variable or filter is an error — a typo in worktree_path should
21	// surface at create time, not as a directory literally named "{{rep}}".
22	func Render(tmpl string, vars Vars) (string, error) {
23		var firstErr error
24		out := tmplVar.ReplaceAllStringFunc(tmpl, func(m string) string {
25			g := tmplVar.FindStringSubmatch(m)
26			name, filter := g[1], g[2]
27			val, ok := vars[name]
28			if !ok {
29				if firstErr == nil {
30					firstErr = fmt.Errorf("unknown template variable %q in %q (known: %s)", name, tmpl, strings.Join(sortedKeys(vars), ", "))
31				}
32				return m
33			}
34			switch filter {
35			case "":
36				return val
37			case "slug":
38				return Slug(val)
39			case "lower":
40				return strings.ToLower(val)
41			case "base":
42				if i := strings.LastIndexByte(val, '/'); i >= 0 {
43					return val[i+1:]
44				}
45				return val
46			default:
47				if firstErr == nil {
48					firstErr = fmt.Errorf("unknown template filter %q in %q (known: slug, lower, base)", filter, tmpl)
49				}
50				return m
51			}
52		})
53		if firstErr != nil {
54			return "", firstErr
55		}
56		return out, nil
57	}
58	
59	var slugStrip = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
60	
61	// Slug makes a branch name safe to use as a single filesystem component:
62	// "feat/auth/oauth-refresh" becomes "feat-auth-oauth-refresh". Leading dots
63	// and dashes are trimmed so the result can never be a hidden directory or be
64	// mistaken for a flag.
65	func Slug(s string) string {
66		s = slugStrip.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
67		for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
68			s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
69		}
70		s = strings.Trim(s, "-._")
71		if s == "" {
72			return "unnamed"
73		}
74		return s
75	}
76	
77	func sortedKeys(v Vars) []string {
78		out := make([]string, 0, len(v))
79		for k := range v {
80			out = append(out, k)
81		}
82		// small map; insertion sort keeps this dependency-free
83		for i := 1; i < len(out); i++ {
84			for j := i; j > 0 && out[j] < out[j-1]; j-- {
85				out[j], out[j-1] = out[j-1], out[j]
86			}
87		}
88		return out
89	}

1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"os"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// XDG base directories, resolved the way the spec prescribes: honor the
10	// environment variable when it holds an absolute path, otherwise fall back to
11	// the documented default under $HOME.
12	
13	func xdgDir(envVar, fallback string) string {
14		if v := os.Getenv(envVar); filepath.IsAbs(v) {
15			return v
16		}
17		return filepath.Join(home(), fallback)
18	}
19	
20	func home() string {
21		if h, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil && h != "" {
22			return h
23		}
24		return os.Getenv("HOME")
25	}
26	
27	// ConfigHome is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (default ~/.config).
28	func ConfigHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", ".config") }
29	
30	// DataHome is $XDG_DATA_HOME (default ~/.local/share).
31	func DataHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_DATA_HOME", ".local/share") }
32	
33	// CacheHome is $XDG_CACHE_HOME (default ~/.cache).
34	func CacheHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CACHE_HOME", ".cache") }
35	
36	// ConfigFile is the path dev loads its TOML configuration from.
37	func ConfigFile() string { return filepath.Join(ConfigHome(), "dev", "config.toml") }
38	
39	// Expand resolves a leading ~ and any environment variables in p, then makes
40	// the result absolute. Paths in config.toml are written by humans, so both
41	// "~/Worktrees" and "$WORK/trees" have to work.
42	func Expand(p string) string {
43		if p == "" {
44			return ""
45		}
46		p = os.ExpandEnv(p)
47		switch {
48		case p == "~":
49			p = home()
50		case strings.HasPrefix(p, "~/"):
51			p = filepath.Join(home(), p[2:])
52		}
53		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(p); err == nil {
54			return abs

1	package gitx

8	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
9	type Worktree struct {
10		Path string
11		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
12		Head string
13		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
14		Branch   string
15		Detached bool
16		Bare     bool
17		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
18		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
19		Locked         bool
20		LockedReason   string
21		Prunable       bool
22		PrunableReason string
23		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
24		Main bool
25	}
26	
27	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
28	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
29	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
30		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
31		if err != nil {
32			return nil, err
33		}
34		var (
35			list []Worktree
36			cur  *Worktree
37		)
38		flush := func() {
39			if cur != nil {
40				list = append(list, *cur)
41				cur = nil
42			}
43		}
44		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
45			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
46				flush()
47				continue
48			}
49			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
50			switch key {
51			case "worktree":
52				flush()
53				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
54			case "HEAD":
55				if cur != nil {
56					cur.Head = val
57				}
58			case "branch":
59				if cur != nil {
60					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
61				}
62			case "detached":
63				if cur != nil {
64					cur.Detached = true
65				}
66			case "bare":
67				if cur != nil {
68					cur.Bare = true
69				}
70			case "locked":
71				if cur != nil {
72					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
73				}
74			case "prunable":
75				if cur != nil {
76					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
77				}
78			}
79		}
80		flush()
81		return list, nil
82	}
83	
84	// WorktreeFor finds the worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git refuses to
85	// check the same branch out twice, so at most one can match.
86	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
87		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
88		if err != nil {
89			return Worktree{}, false, err
90		}
91		for _, w := range list {
92			if w.Branch == branch {
93				return w, true, nil
94			}
95		}
96		return Worktree{}, false, nil
97	}
98	
99	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
100	//
101	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
102	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
103	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
104	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
105	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
106		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
107		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
108		if exists {
109			args = append(args, path, branch)
110		} else {
111			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
112			if base != "" {
113				args = append(args, base)
114			}
115		}
116		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
117		return err
118	}
119	
120	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
121	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
122	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
123		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
124		if force {
125			args = append(args, "--force")
126		}
127		args = append(args, path)
128		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
129		return err
130	}
131	
132	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
133	// were deleted behind git's back.
134	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
135		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
136		return err
137	}
138	
139	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
140	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
141		if branch == "" {
142			return false
143		}
144		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
145		return err == nil
146	}
147	
148	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
149	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
150		if ref == "" {
151			return false
152		}
153		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
154		return err == nil
155	}

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}

25	func newAdoptCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
26		var (
27			apply       bool
28			yes         bool
29			noWorktrees bool
30			noSessions  bool
31			noBranches  bool
32			state       string
33		)
34		cmd := &cobra.Command{
35			Use:   "adopt",
36			Short: "Import existing worktrees, sessions and branches as tasks",
37			Long: `Bring what is already on this machine under dev's inventory.
38	
39	There is nothing to migrate to start using dev — repositories are discovered
40	wherever your scan roots point, and no directory is moved or renamed. What is
41	worth importing is the work already in flight: linked worktrees created by
42	hand or by another tool, runtime sessions sitting in a repo, and local
43	branches that are ahead of their base.
44	
45	Reports by default. Nothing is created without --apply, and nothing on disk is
46	ever moved, renamed or deleted by this command.`,
47			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
48			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
49				ctx := ctxOf()
50	
51				target, err := task.ParseState(state)
52				if err != nil {
53					return err
54				}
55	
56				repos, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
57				if err != nil {
58					return err
59				}
60				existing, err := app.Tasks.List()
61				if err != nil {
62					return err
63				}
64				known := map[string]bool{}
65				for _, t := range existing {
66					known[t.ID] = true
67				}
68	
69				rt := app.Runtime()
70				var sessions []runtime.Session
71				if !noSessions {
72					sessions, _ = rt.List(ctx)
73				}
74	
75				var found []candidate
76				for _, r := range repos {
77					if r.Bare {
78						continue
79					}
80					found = append(found, scanRepo(ctx, app, r, sessions, known, target,
81						!noWorktrees, !noSessions, !noBranches)...)
82				}
83	
84				if len(found) == 0 {
85					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to adopt — everything in flight is already tracked.")

87				}
88	
89				sort.Slice(found, func(i, j int) bool {
90					if found[i].Task.Repo != found[j].Task.Repo {
91						return found[i].Task.Repo < found[j].Task.Repo
92					}
93					return found[i].Task.Branch < found[j].Task.Branch
94				})
95	
96				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%d candidate(s):\n\n", len(found))

139	// scanRepo collects everything in one repository that looks like work in
140	// flight but is not yet recorded.
141	func scanRepo(ctx context.Context, app *App, r repo.Repo, sessions []runtime.Session,
142		known map[string]bool, target task.State, doWorktrees, doSessions, doBranches bool) []candidate {
143	
144		var out []candidate
145		seen := map[string]bool{}
146	
147		add := func(branch, worktree, reason string, state task.State) {
148			if branch == "" || seen[branch] {
149				return
150			}
151			id := task.MakeID(r.Name, branch)
152			if known[id] {
153				return
154			}
155			seen[branch] = true
156			out = append(out, candidate{
157				Reason: reason,
158				Task: &task.Task{
159					ID:           id,
160					Name:         branch,
161					Repo:         r.Name,
162					RepoPath:     r.Path,
163					Branch:       branch,
164					Base:         gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, r.Path),
165					WorktreePath: worktree,
166					State:        state,
167					Owner:        config.Hostname(),
168				},
169			})
170		}
171	
172		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path)
173		if err != nil {
174			return nil
175		}
176	
177		if doWorktrees {
178			for _, w := range worktrees {
179				if w.Main || w.Branch == "" || w.Prunable {
180					continue
181				}
182				// A harness's turn-scoped worktree is not a change stream a human
183				// tracks; adopting those would fill the inventory with noise that
184				// the harness will delete on its own.
185				if isEphemeralWorktree(w.Path, w.Branch) {
186					continue
187				}
188				state := target
189				reason := "existing worktree"
190				if sessionAt(sessions, w.Path) != nil {
191					state, reason = task.Hot, "worktree with a live session"
192				}
193				add(w.Branch, w.Path, reason, state)
194			}
195		}
196	
197		if doSessions {
198			for i := range sessions {
199				for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
200					if d != r.Path {
201						continue
202					}
203					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
204					if err != nil || st.Branch == "" {
205						continue
206					}
207					add(st.Branch, "", "live session in the main checkout", task.Hot)
208				}
209			}
210		}

1	// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
18	type Session struct {
19		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
20		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
21		Handle string
22		Label  string
23		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
24		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
25		// value.
26		Dirs []string
27		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
28		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
29		AgentStatus string
30		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
31		AgentSessions []string
32		Focused       bool
33	}
34	
35	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
36	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
37		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
38			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
39			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
40			// $HOME active.
41			if d == dir || strings.HasPrefix(d, dir+"/") {
42				return true
43			}
44		}
45		return false
46	}
47	
48	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
49	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
50	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
51	type Runtime interface {
52		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
53		Name() string
54		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
55		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
56		Available() bool
57		// Open makes dir live and returns a handle. Opening something already open
58		// focuses it rather than duplicating it.
59		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error)
60		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
61		// task entry.
62		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
63		// List enumerates live sessions.
64		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
65		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
66		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
67		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
68	}
69

71	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
72	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
73	type WorktreeOpener interface {
74		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error)
75	}

78	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
79	
80	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
81		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
82	}
83	
84	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
85	//
86	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
87	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then None.
88	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
89	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
90		herdr, tmux, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}
91		switch backend {
92		case "herdr":
93			return herdr
94		case "tmux":
95			return tmux
96		case "none":
97			return none
98		case "", "auto":
99			if herdr.Available() {
100				return herdr
101			}
102			if tmux.Available() {
103				return tmux
104			}
105			return none
106		}
107		return none
108	}

231	            __%[1]s_reprint_commandLine

+	root.SetArgs(args)
+	err := root.Execute()
+	return out.String(), errBuf.String(), err

2	// shells out to git rather than linking a Go implementation: git is already a

4	// keeps dev's behaviour identical to what the user sees when they run the same

7	
8	import (
9		"bytes"
10		"context"
11		"errors"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"

16	
17	// ErrNotARepo is returned when a directory is not inside a git working tree.
18	var ErrNotARepo = errors.New("not a git repository")
19	
20	// Error carries the failing command and git's own stderr, which is almost
21	// always more useful than the exit status alone.
22	type Error struct {
23		Args   []string
24		Dir    string
25		Stderr string
26		Err    error
27	}
28	
29	func (e *Error) Error() string {
30		msg := strings.TrimSpace(e.Stderr)
31		if msg == "" {
32			msg = e.Err.Error()
33		}
34		return fmt.Sprintf("git %s: %s", strings.Join(e.Args, " "), msg)
35	}
36	
37	func (e *Error) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
38	
39	// run executes git in dir and returns trimmed stdout.
40	func run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
41		// -c core.quotepath=false keeps non-ASCII paths readable rather than
42		// octal-escaped, which matters for the Chinese-named files in these repos.
43		full := append([]string{"-c", "core.quotepath=false"}, args...)
44		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", full...)
45		cmd.Dir = dir
46		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
47		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
48		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
49		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
50			gerr := &Error{Args: args, Dir: dir, Stderr: stderr.String(), Err: err}
51			if strings.Contains(gerr.Stderr, "not a git repository") {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", dir, ErrNotARepo)
53			}
54			return "", gerr
55		}
56		return strings.TrimRight(stdout.String(), "\n"), nil
57	}
58	
59	// Run executes an arbitrary git command in dir. Exported for the few callers
60	// (park's wip commit, done's merge) that need a one-off command.
61	func Run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
62		return run(ctx, dir, args...)
63	}

67		if s == "" {
68			return nil
69		}
70		out := strings.Split(s, "\n")
71		filtered := out[:0]
72		for _, l := range out {
73			if l != "" {
74				filtered = append(filtered, l)
75			}
76		}
77		return filtered
78	}

    if [ "$mode" = noninteractive ]; then opts=-c; else opts=-ic; fi
    output=$(TARGET="$tmp" TMPDIR="$run_tmp" "$shell" "$opts" ". '$wrapper'; set -e; dev cd; printf 'after pwd=%s\\n' \"\$PWD\"; exit" </dev/null 2>&1)

21	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
22		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
23			return true
24		}
25		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
26			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
27				return true
28			}
29		}
30		return false
31	}
32	
33	// loadCompletion prepares local completion providers after Cobra has parsed the
34	// command line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break
35	// command and flag completion entirely.
36	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
37		if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
38			a.completionLoadAttempted = true
39			a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
40		}
41		return a.completionLoadErr == nil
42	}
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
46			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
47				return nil, noFileCompletion
48			}
49			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
54			for _, t := range tasks {
55				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
56				out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
57			}
58			return out, noFileCompletion
59		}
60	}
61	
62	func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
63		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
64			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
65				return nil, noFileCompletion
66			}
67			repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
68			if err != nil {
69				return nil, noFileCompletion
70			}
71			out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
72			for _, r := range repos {
73				out = addCompletion(out, r.Display(), config.Contract(r.Path), toComplete)
74			}
75			return out, noFileCompletion
76		}
77	}
78	
79	func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
80		return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
81			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
82				return nil, noFileCompletion
83			}
84			repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
85			repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
86			if err != nil {
87				return nil, noFileCompletion
88			}
89			worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
90			if err != nil {
91				return nil, noFileCompletion
92			}
93			out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
94			for _, wt := range worktrees {
95				if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
96					continue
97				}
98				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
99				if wt.Main {
100					description += " (main checkout)"
101				}
102				out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
103			}
104			return out, noFileCompletion
105		}
106	}
107	
108	func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
109		if len(args) > 0 {
110			return nil, noFileCompletion
111		}
112		topics, err := help.List()
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, noFileCompletion
115		}
116		out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
117		for _, topic := range topics {
118			out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
119		}
120		return out, noFileCompletion
121	}
122	
123	func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
124		names := ignore.BundledNames()
125		out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
126		for _, name := range names {
127			out = addCompletion(out, name, "bundled template", toComplete)
128		}
129		return out, noFileCompletion
130	}
131	
132	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
133		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
134			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
135			for _, value := range values {
136				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
137			}
138			return out, noFileCompletion
139		}
140	}
141	
142	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
143		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
144			panic(err)
145		}
146	}
147	
148	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
149		description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
150		needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
151		if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
152			return out
153		}
154		if description != "" {
155			value += "\t" + description
156		}
157		return append(out, value)
158	}
159

40	## Install
41	
42	### Homebrew (macOS)
43	
44	```bash
45	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli
46	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
47	```
48	
49	The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
50	does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.
51	
52	### Go or source
53	
54	```bash
55	go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@v0.1.0
56	# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
57	```
58	
59	For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
60	them:
61	
62	```bash
63	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
64	dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
65	dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
66	dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
67	```
68	
69	Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
70	worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
71	a forge or the network.
72	
73	Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
74	
75	```bash
76	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
77	eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
78	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
79	```
```

30	    IFS= read -r __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
31	    if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then

33	      __dev_status=$?
34	    fi

36	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"

38	}

Base directory for this skill: /Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/.claude/skills/agent-history-hygiene

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `probe-specstory-redaction.py`   | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?"   |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

## Core invariants

1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
   history back.

## When to use this skill

Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:

- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
  chat history".
- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.

## When NOT to use

- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
  skip this skill entirely.
- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).

## Integration with existing infrastructure

This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
already has. It does not duplicate:

- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
  config the wrapper expects to find.
- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a
  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo
  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via
  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details
  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).

What this skill **adds**:

- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
  current transcript among many" problem.
- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
  committing.

## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene

Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
chat/plan artifacts.

```bash
# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh

# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
git add path/to/feature/file.ts
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.

# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
  exit 1
}

# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
git commit -m "feat: ..."
```

## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project

For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
installed. Runs once per repo.

```bash
cd /path/to/new/project
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit

# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
pre-commit run --all-files
```

What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:

1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`
   keeps it current everywhere.
2. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
3. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
4. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
   one-line patch if missing.
5. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.

Migrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed
`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):

```bash
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
```

removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
(idempotent; safe to re-run).

## Workflow C: post-leak remediation

When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
committed / pushed a secret":

1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
   become worth discussing.
4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.

## Gotchas

- **SpecStory >= 2.4.0 already redacts on write — plan around it, not
  against it.** Since
  [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) shipped in
  v2.4.0 (2026-07-20), the CLI redacts secrets via the
  [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset **by
  default**, covering both local markdown and cloud sync, writing
  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`. Measured coverage is 36 of 54 class/context pairs;
  15 are ours alone (every webhook rule, plus every custom key in prose
  context — betterleaks catches many classes only in `KEY=value` form via its
  entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule). So: **keep this layer, but never
  rewrite what SpecStory already cleaned.** `redact_secrets.py` writes the
  same `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` sentinel and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so
  a cleaned transcript is left untouched and pre-commit stops demanding a
  re-`git add`. Full matrix + knobs in
  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md).
  Only `[redaction] enabled` is configurable upstream — the PR's
  `extra_patterns` did not survive the Betterleaks rewrite, so repo-specific
  rules stay our job. For SpecStory older than 2.4.0 (or with redaction
  disabled), run `redact_secrets.py --fix --legacy`.
- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
  syntax everywhere.
- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
  `find-session.sh`.
- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
  agent artifacts, not after.
- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
  empty fields signal absence).

- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.

- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.

- **`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`**
  Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers, by
  synthesizing a Claude Code session and rendering it twice (with and without
  `--no-redact-secrets`). Prints a coverage matrix and the residual set our
  layer must still handle. Exit 30 when specstory isn't installed.

- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--migrate] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the current
  repo, wire the hook to the installed skill's redactor, then run
  `pre-commit install`. Audits
  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
  (warns, never silently edits).

## Bundled assets

- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
  regex.
- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
  standard hygiene hooks.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
  agent artifact dirs.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — the redactor, published to consuming repos
  as the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook (root
  `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`). Writes `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`, the sentinel
  SpecStory also writes natively; `--legacy` writes the pre-2.4.0
  placeholders instead. Release procedure in
  `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.

## Reference files

- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.
  Read when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.
- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),
  allowlist design, sync procedure for the bundled redactor. Read
  when tuning rules or debugging unexpected pre-commit failures.
- [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md)
  — what SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts on its own, measured per secret class and
  per context, plus the upstream PRs, config knobs, and why our layer is still
  load-bearing. Read before changing anything about redaction placeholders.
- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) —
  rotate-first runbook for "I committed / pushed a secret". Read
  **before** any `git filter-repo` / `git push --force` action.

## Tests

The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:

```bash
make test-skill
```

- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.
- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git
  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are
  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.
- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).
- `test_specstory_coverage.py` — locks in that SpecStory still redacts by
  default and still writes `[REDACTED:<label>]`; skips without the CLI.

The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each
regression the suite locks in.

## Related skills

- [`project-knowledge-harness`](../project-knowledge-harness/SKILL.md)
  — complementary memory harness (TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/) that
  references `.claude/plans/` as "ephemeral agent scratchpads". This
  skill fills the gap: those scratchpads belong in git, not ignored.

17	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
18	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
19	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
20	// persistent flags (notably --config).
21	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
22		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd {
23			return true
24		}
25		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
26			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
27				return true
28			}
29		}
30		return false
31	}
32	
33	// loadCompletion prepares local completion providers after Cobra has parsed the
34	// command line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break
35	// command and flag completion entirely.
36	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool {
37		if !a.completionLoadAttempted {
38			a.completionLoadAttempted = true
39			a.completionLoadErr = a.Load()
40		}
41		return a.completionLoadErr == nil
42	}
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
46			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
47				return nil, noFileCompletion
48			}
49			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
54			for _, t := range tasks {
55				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
56				out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
57			}
58			return out, noFileCompletion
59		}
60	}

63		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
64			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
65				return nil, noFileCompletion
66			}
67			repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
68			if err != nil {
69				return nil, noFileCompletion
70			}

72			for _, r := range repos {

74			}
75			return out, noFileCompletion

97				}
98				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)

124		names := ignore.BundledNames()

127			out = addCompletion(out, name, "bundled template", toComplete)

132	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
133		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
134			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
135			for _, value := range values {
136				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
137			}
138			return out, noFileCompletion
139		}

142	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
143		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
144			panic(err)
145		}
146	}
147	
148	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
149		description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
150		needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
151		if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
152			return out
153		}
154		if description != "" {
155			value += "\t" + description
156		}
157		return append(out, value)
158	}

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11		"strconv"
12	
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16	)
17	
18	// App is the state shared by every command.
19	type App struct {
20		Cfg   config.Config
21		Tasks *task.Store
22	
23		Out io.Writer
24		Err io.Writer
25	
26		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
27		configPath string
28		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
29		runtimeOverride string
30		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
31		noRuntime bool
32	
33	}
34	
35	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
36	func (a *App) Load() error {
37		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
38		if err != nil {
39			return err
40		}
41		a.Cfg = cfg
42		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
43		if a.Out == nil {
44			a.Out = os.Stdout
45		}
46		if a.Err == nil {
47			a.Err = os.Stderr
48		}
49		return nil
50	}
51	
52	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
53	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
54	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
55		if a.noRuntime {
56			return runtime.None{}
57		}
58		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
59		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
60			backend = a.runtimeOverride
61		}
62		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
63		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
64			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
65		}
66		return rt
67	}
68	
69	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
70	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
71		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
72	}
73	
74	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
75	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
76		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
77	}
78	
79	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
80	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
81	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
82	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
83	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
84	// integrations.
85	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
86		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
87			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
88			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
89				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
90			}
91			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
92			if file == nil {
93				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
94			}
95			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
96				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
97			}
98			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
99				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
100			}
101			return nil
102		}
103		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
104		return err
105	}
106	
107	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
108	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
109

1	package cli

6		"os"
7	
8		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"

10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"

12		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
13	)
14	
15	func newParkCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
16		var (
17			next   string
18			note   string
19			wip    bool
20			push   bool
21			cold   bool
22			keepRT bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "park [task]",
26			Short: "Stop working on a task without losing the thread",
27			Long: `Park the current task (or the one named) so its runtime session can close.
28	
29	Parking is the missing move that makes a crowded sidebar shrink. It records
30	what to do next, optionally checkpoints uncommitted work, and closes the
31	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
32	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.
33	
34	  warm (default)  worktree and branch stay; session closes. Back within days.
35	  cold (--cold)   work is committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstruct
36	                  it anywhere later with dev resume.
37	
38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
41			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
42			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
43				ctx := ctxOf()
44				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
45				if err != nil {
46					return err
47				}
48	
49				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
50				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
51					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
52						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
53				}
54				target := task.Warm
55				if cold {
56					target = task.Cold
57				}
58				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
59	
60				if next != "" {
61					t.Next = next
62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69	
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97	
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114	
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}
124	
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes
133					// the task reconstructible rather than lost.
134					t.WorktreePath = ""
135				}
136				if cold && mode == task.ModeBranch {
137					// Free the canonical checkout for other work. The branch remains
138					// local + remote and resume switches back to it.
139					base := t.Base
140					if base == "" {
141						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
142					}
143					if base == "" {
144						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but its base branch is unknown")
145					}
146					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
147						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
148							base, err)
149					}
150				}
151	
152				t.State = target
153				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
154				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
155					return err
156				}
157				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
158				if t.Next != "" {
159					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
160				}
161				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
162				return nil
163			},
164		}
165		f := cmd.Flags()
166		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
167		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
168		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
169		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
170		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
171		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
172		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app)
173		return cmd
174	}
175	
176	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
177	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
178		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
179			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
180		}
181		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
182		return nil
183	}
184	
185	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
186	// directory when no argument is given.
187	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
188		if len(args) == 1 {
189			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
190		}
191		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
196		if err != nil {
197			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
198				config.Contract(cwd))
199		}
200		return t, nil
201	}

16	func newDoneCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

18			ff           bool

20			deleteBranch bool
21			keepWorktree bool

23		)

28	
29	Two integration modes, matching the two shapes a branch's history takes:
30	
31	  --ff    rebase onto the base and fast-forward it. Use when the branch's
32	          commits are worth keeping in the base's history.
33	  --pr    push and open a pull/merge request with gh or glab, leaving the
34	          merge to review and CI. Use when someone (or something) should look
35	          at it first.
36	
37	With neither, dev only reports what it would do.
38	
39	Cleanup is deliberately conservative: the worktree is removed, the task entry
40	is marked done, and the branch is deleted only with --delete-branch. A merged
41	branch that still has unpushed commits is never deleted.`,
42			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),

48				}
49				checkout := checkoutOf(t)

52				}
53	
54				st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
55				if err != nil {
56					return err
57				}
58				if st.Dirty() {
59					return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes: %s.\n"+
60						"Commit them, or park the task with --wip, before finishing it",
61						config.Contract(checkout), st.Breakdown())
62				}
63

68							"Run `dev done` without --ff/--pr/--delete-branch/--keep-worktree", t.Title(), t.Branch)
69					}
70					if push {
71						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
72							return err
73						}
74					}
75					rt := app.Runtime()
76					if t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
77						if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {

85					}

97				}
98

173	func directPushHint(push bool) string {
174		if push {
175			return " --push"
176		}
177		return ""
178	}
179	
180	// fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
181	// forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
182	//
183	// merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
184	// branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
185	// a merge commit the user did not ask for.
186	func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
187		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
188		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
189			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
190				"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
191				err, config.Contract(checkout))
192		}
193		// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
194		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
195		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
196			return err
197		}
198		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
199			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
200				"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
201		}
202		return nil
203	}
204	
205	// deleteMergedBranch removes a branch only when git agrees its commits are already
206	// contained in the base — the check that makes cleanup safe.
207	func deleteMergedBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, repoPath, branch, base string) error {
208		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", branch, base); err != nil {
209			return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)
210		}
211		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "branch", "-d", branch); err != nil {
212			return fmt.Errorf("could not delete %s: %w", branch, err)
213		}
214		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   deleted    branch %s\n", branch)
215		return nil
216	}
217	
218	// openPR pushes the branch and asks the forge CLI to open a pull/merge
219	// request. When no forge CLI is available dev prints the push result and the
220	// URL to open by hand, rather than failing: the branch being published is the
221	// part that actually matters.
222	func openPR(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
223		if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
224			return err
225		}
226		kind := forge.Detect(ctx, t.RepoPath)
227		f, err := forge.For(kind)
228		if err != nil || !f.Available() {
229			app.warnf("no forge CLI for this remote — the branch is pushed; open the request in your browser")
230			return nil
231		}
232		url, err := f.CreatePR(ctx, checkout, forge.PRRequest{
233			Base: base, Head: t.Branch, Fill: true,
234		})
235		if err != nil {
236			return err
237		}
238		if url != "" {
239			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   opened     %s\n", url)
240		}
241		return nil
242	}
