```text
1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123	
124		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
125		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
126	}
127	
128	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}
141	
142	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),

2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.

9

11		"context"
12		"fmt"

19		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
20		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
21		Handle string
22		Label  string
23		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
24		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
25		// value.
26		Dirs []string
27		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
28		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.

31		AgentSessions []string

33	}

35	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
36	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
37		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
38			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
39			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
40			// $HOME active.
41			if d == dir || strings.HasPrefix(d, dir+"/") {
42				return true
43			}
44		}
45		return false
46	}
47	
48	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
49	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
50	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
51	type Runtime interface {
52		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
53		Name() string
54		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
55		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
56		Available() bool
57		// Open makes dir live and returns a handle. Opening something already open
58		// focuses it rather than duplicating it.
59		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error)
60		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
61		// task entry.
62		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
63		// List enumerates live sessions.
64		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
65		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
66		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
67		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error

87	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then None.
88	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
89	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
90		herdr, tmux, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}
91		switch backend {

96		case "none":

98		case "", "auto":

2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in

18	// App is the state shared by every command.
19	type App struct {
20		Cfg   config.Config
21		Tasks *task.Store
22	
23		Out io.Writer
24		Err io.Writer
25	
26		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
27		configPath string
28		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.

30		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.

33	}

35	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
36	func (a *App) Load() error {
37		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
38		if err != nil {
39			return err
40		}
41		a.Cfg = cfg
42		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
43		if a.Out == nil {
44			a.Out = os.Stdout
45		}
46		if a.Err == nil {
47			a.Err = os.Stderr
48		}
49		return nil
50	}
51	
52	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
53	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
54	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
55		if a.noRuntime {
56			return runtime.None{}
57		}
58		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
59		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
60			backend = a.runtimeOverride
61		}
62		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
63		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
64			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
65		}
66		return rt
67	}
68

71		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
72	}

79	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
80	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
81	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
82	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
83	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
84	// integrations.
85	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
86		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
87			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
88			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
89				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
90			}
91			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
92			if file == nil {
93				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
94			}
95			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
96				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
97			}
98			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
99				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
100			}
101			return nil
102		}
103		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
104		return err

79	func TestBackendContract(t *testing.T) {

+normal pipe behavior.

1	package ignore
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"os"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"runtime"
8		"sort"
9		"strings"
10	)
11	
12	// Extras are the blocks no language template provides but almost every
13	// repository wants. They are kept separate from the language sections so a
14	// later regeneration can replace a language block without losing them.
15	type Extras struct {
16		// OS adds the platform's junk files (.DS_Store, Thumbs.db).
17		OS bool
18		// Editors adds editor and IDE local state.
19		Editors bool
20		// Agents adds the directories coding-agent harnesses create.
21		Agents bool
22		// Env adds the usual local secret files.
23		Env bool
24	}
25	
26	// DefaultExtras is what `dev gitignore` adds unless told otherwise.
27	func DefaultExtras() Extras { return Extras{OS: true, Editors: true, Agents: true, Env: true} }
28	
29	const (
30		// Markers delimit the region dev manages, so re-running it updates that
31		// region and leaves anything the user added by hand untouched.
32		blockBegin = "# >>> dev gitignore >>>"
33		blockEnd   = "# <<< dev gitignore <<<"
34	)
35	
36	// osSection returns the junk files the host platform scatters through a repo.
37	func osSection() string {
38		switch runtime.GOOS {
39		case "darwin":
40			return `# macOS
41	.DS_Store
42	.AppleDouble
43	.LSOverride
44	._*
45	.Spotlight-V100
46	.Trashes`
47		case "windows":
48			return `# Windows
49	Thumbs.db
50	Thumbs.db:encryptable
51	ehthumbs.db
52	Desktop.ini
53	$RECYCLE.BIN/`
54		default:
55			return `# Linux
56	*~
57	.fuse_hidden*
58	.directory
59	.Trash-*
60	.nfs*`
61		}
62	}
63	
64	const editorsSection = `# Editors and IDEs
65	.idea/
66	*.iml
67	.vscode/*
68	!.vscode/settings.json
69	!.vscode/extensions.json
70	!.vscode/launch.json
71	*.swp
72	*.swo
73	.nvimlog
74	.null-ls_*`
75	
76	// agentsSection covers the directories coding-agent harnesses create inside a
77	// repository. The worktree entries matter most: an agent's linked checkout
78	// left untracked makes every `git status` in the main checkout unreadable.
79	const agentsSection = `# Coding agent harnesses
80	.claude/worktrees/
81	.claude/settings.local.json
82	.aider*
83	.cursor/rules/_generated/
84	.specstory/history/`
85	
86	const envSection = `# Local environment and secrets — never commit real values
87	.env
88	.env.*
89	!.env.example
90	!.env.template
91	*.local
92	.direnv/`
93	
94	// Compose renders the managed block from the given sections and extras.
95	func Compose(sections []Section, extras Extras) string {
96		var b strings.Builder
97		b.WriteString(blockBegin + "\n")
98		b.WriteString("# Generated by `dev gitignore`. Edit outside this block, or re-run to update.\n")
99	
100		for _, s := range sections {
101			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n# --- %s (%s) ---\n%s\n", s.Name, s.Source, s.Body)
102		}
103	
104		var tail []string
105		if extras.OS {
106			tail = append(tail, osSection())
107		}
108		if extras.Editors {
109			tail = append(tail, editorsSection)
110		}
111		if extras.Agents {
112			tail = append(tail, agentsSection)
113		}
114		if extras.Env {
115			tail = append(tail, envSection)
116		}
117		for _, t := range tail {
118			b.WriteString("\n" + t + "\n")
119		}
120	
121		b.WriteString(blockEnd + "\n")
122		return b.String()
123	}
124	
125	// Merge splices a generated block into an existing .gitignore.
126	//
127	// Replacing only the delimited region is what makes this safe to re-run: a
128	// project accumulates hand-written rules over time, and regenerating must
129	// never be the thing that loses them.
130	func Merge(existing, block string) string {
131		start := strings.Index(existing, blockBegin)
132		end := strings.Index(existing, blockEnd)
133		if start >= 0 && end > start {
134			tailStart := end + len(blockEnd)
135			if tailStart < len(existing) && existing[tailStart] == '\n' {
136				tailStart++
137			}
138			return existing[:start] + block + existing[tailStart:]
139		}
140		if strings.TrimSpace(existing) == "" {
141			return block
142		}
143		if !strings.HasSuffix(existing, "\n") {
144			existing += "\n"
145		}
146		return existing + "\n" + block
147	}
148	
149	// HasManagedBlock reports whether a file already carries dev's markers.
150	func HasManagedBlock(content string) bool {
151		return strings.Contains(content, blockBegin) && strings.Contains(content, blockEnd)
152	}
153	
154	// Detect infers which language templates a repository needs from the files it
155	// contains, so `dev gitignore` can be run with no arguments.
156	func Detect(dir string) []string {
157		markers := map[string][]string{
158			"Python":       {"pyproject.toml", "requirements.txt", "setup.py", "uv.lock", "Pipfile"},
159			"Node":         {"package.json", "pnpm-lock.yaml", "yarn.lock", "bun.lockb"},
160			"Go":           {"go.mod"},
161			"Rust":         {"Cargo.toml"},
162			"Ruby":         {"Gemfile"},
163			"Java":         {"pom.xml"},
164			"Gradle":       {"build.gradle", "build.gradle.kts"},
165			"Elixir":       {"mix.exs"},
166			"Terraform":    {"main.tf", ".terraform.lock.hcl"},
167			"Dart":         {"pubspec.yaml"},
168			"Swift":        {"Package.swift"},
169			"Composer":     {"composer.json"},
170			"TeX":          {"main.tex"},
171			"VisualStudio": {"*.sln"},
172		}
173		var found []string
174		for name, files := range markers {
175			for _, f := range files {
176				if strings.ContainsRune(f, '*') {
177					if matches, _ := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(dir, f)); len(matches) > 0 {
178						found = append(found, name)
179						break
180					}
181					continue
182				}
183				if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, f)); err == nil {
184					found = append(found, name)
185					break
186				}
187			}
188		}
189		sort.Strings(found)
190		return found
191	}
192

13	// Herdr drives the herdr terminal workspace manager over its CLI, which emits

15	//
16	// Division of responsibility, deliberately: dev creates worktrees with plain
17	// `git worktree add` at its own configured path and then asks herdr to *open*
18	// that path. `herdr worktree create` is not used, because it would put the
19	// path policy in a second place — and that policy has to hold on machines
20	// where herdr is not installed at all.
21	type Herdr struct {
22		bin string
23		// metadataSource namespaces the workspace metadata tokens dev reports.
24		metadataSource string
25	}

30	// WithMetadataSource sets the --source id used for workspace metadata tokens.
31	func (h *Herdr) WithMetadataSource(src string) *Herdr {
32		if src != "" {
33			h.metadataSource = src
34		}
35		return h
36	}
37	
38	// Name implements Runtime.
39	func (h *Herdr) Name() string { return "herdr" }
40	
41	// Available reports whether the binary exists *and* a server is reachable.
42	// The binary alone is not enough: every dev call goes through the socket API,
43	// so a stopped server must degrade to the next backend rather than making
44	// every command fail.
45	func (h *Herdr) Available() bool {

12	// Tmux is the fallback backend for machines without herdr. It models a task as
13	// a named tmux session rooted at the checkout.
14	type Tmux struct{ bin string }
15	
16	// NewTmux returns the tmux adapter.
17	func NewTmux() *Tmux { return &Tmux{bin: "tmux"} }
18	
19	// Name implements Runtime.
20	func (t *Tmux) Name() string { return "tmux" }
21	
22	// Available reports whether tmux is installed. Unlike herdr, tmux needs no
23	// running server for `new-session -d` to work, so presence is enough.
24	func (t *Tmux) Available() bool { return haveBinary(t.bin) }
25	
26	func (t *Tmux) run(ctx context.Context, args ...string) (string, error) {
27		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, t.bin, args...)
28		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
29		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
30		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
31			msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
32			if msg == "" {
33				msg = err.Error()
34			}
35			return "", fmt.Errorf("tmux %s: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), msg)

The replacement is correct under `set -euo pipefail`: non-quiet `grep` reads to EOF, so a successful producer is not turned into SIGPIPE, while `pipefail` still catches a genuine `repo list` failure and grep still returns 1 on no match. The gain is limited to eliminating Bash’s output buffer/copy and here-string; `repo list` itself already collects all repository rows and renders a table, and this sandbox has only one deduplicated repo row, so the concrete memory saving here is small.

+// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
+// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
+// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
+// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
+// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
+// integrations.
+func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
+	if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
+		fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
+		if err != nil || fd < 3 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
+		}
+		file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
+		if file == nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
+		}
+		if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
+	return err
 }

-Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
+The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
+does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.
+
+### Go or source
+
+```bash
+go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@v0.1.0
+# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
+```
+
+For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
+them:
 
 ```bash
-eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
+mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
+dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
+dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
+dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
+```
+
+Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
+worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
+a forge or the network.
+
+Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
+
+```bash
+eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
+eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
 dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
 ```
 
-The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
-working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
-directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
+A child process cannot change its parent's working directory, so the wrapper
+passes directory changes back through a private file while leaving normal
+stdout/stderr connected to the terminal. That preserves the interactive TUI and
+normal pipe behavior.
+
+The agent skill is an explicit, optional post-install step:

+dev skill install

142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}

181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}

213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}

```text
1	# Parking and resuming
2	
3	How to stop working on something without losing the thread.
4	
5	## Why this exists
6	
7	When the terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
8	working on, nothing can ever be closed — closing it loses the thread. So the
9	sidebar grows until it is no longer scannable, which defeats its purpose.
10	
11	`dev` gives that record a home outside the runtime. Then closing a session is
12	just closing a session.
13	
14	## Pick a checkout mode first
15	
16	A task is intent, not necessarily a worktree:
17	
18	```bash
19	dev repo open api                         # ad hoc; no task at all
20	dev start api --task "typo" --direct      # current branch, usually main
21	dev start api --task "small" --branch-only --base main
22	dev start api --task "parallel" --base main  # default worktree
23	```
24	
25	Direct tasks can go HOT ↔ WARM and finish directly; they cannot go COLD because
26	the canonical checkout cannot be removed. A branch-only task can go cold by
27	pushing and switching the canonical checkout back to its base. A worktree task
28	uses the full lifecycle below.
29	
30	## The states
31	
32	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
33	|---|---|---|---|
34	| 🔥 hot | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
35	| 🌤 warm | worktree + branch kept | session closed | back within days |
36	| ❄️ cold | committed and pushed, worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible |
37	| ✅ done | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
38	
39	Aim for **three to seven hot tasks per machine**. That is a cognitive limit,
40	not a technical one.
41	
42	## Parking
43	
44	```bash
45	dev park --next "reproduce the token refresh race, then add a regression test"
46	dev park --wip                  # checkpoint uncommitted work first
47	dev park --cold --push          # push, then remove the worktree
48	```
49	
50	`--next` is the part that matters. Without it, resuming means re-deriving where
51	you were from a diff — which is most of the cost of a context switch.
52	
53	## Resuming
54	
55	```bash
56	dev resume "token refresh"
57	```
58	
59	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a session. Cold
60	tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from `origin/<branch>`.
61	
62	That is why going cold is safe. **The branch is the identity; the directory is
63	a cache.** Once that is true, the local filesystem stops being a graveyard of
64	half-finished checkouts.
65	
66	## Moving between machines
67	
68	The remote is the handoff boundary. Do not sync worktrees or runtime state —
69	sync branches.
70	
71	```bash
72	# on the machine holding the work
73	dev park --cold --push
74	
75	# on the machine picking it up
76	dev resume <task> --fetch
77	```
78	
79	**One writer per branch at a time.** `dev` records an owner host and refuses to
80	resume someone else's task without `--force`. Two machines committing to one
81	branch is the reliable way to produce a conflict here; the ownership check
82	prevents it.
83	
84	If two machines genuinely need the same feature at once, split the branch —
85	`feat/auth-ui`, `feat/auth-api` — and integrate afterwards. Parallel writers
86	get parallel branches.
87	
88	## Sweeping
89	
90	```bash
91	dev sweep            # report only
92	dev sweep --apply    # act, confirming each change
93	```
94	
95	Reports drift (hot with no session, a worktree git no longer knows about),
96	staleness (warm and untouched, clean and pushed → could go cold), and live
97	sessions no task claims.
98	
99	It never deletes uncommitted work and never acts without `--apply`. Cleanup
100	usually fails not from unwillingness but from the absence of a trustworthy
101	guarantee that the work is recoverable. Reporting first is that guarantee.
102
```

```text
1	# Task lifecycle
2	
3	Read this when work needs to be paused, picked up on another machine, or when
4	a machine has accumulated more open sessions than anyone can hold in mind.
5	
6	## The problem
7	
8	A terminal multiplexer's sidebar is a *runtime* view: it shows what is running
9	now. When it is also the only record of what you are working on, nothing can be
10	closed, because closing it loses the thread. The sidebar grows until it stops
11	being scannable, which defeats its purpose.
12	
13	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home that is
14	not the runtime.
15	
16	## Pick a checkout mode before a lifecycle
17	
18	A task records human intent; it does not imply a worktree:
19	
20	| Command | Checkout boundary | Use when |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| `dev repo open api` | none; no task | browsing or truly ad-hoc work |
23	| `dev start api -t typo --direct` | current branch, usually main | one short tracked change |
24	| `dev start api -t small --branch-only` | branch in canonical checkout | lightweight isolation, no concurrency |
25	| `dev start api -t auth --base main` | branch + linked worktree | interruption, experiment, parallel writer |
26	
27	Direct tasks go HOT ↔ WARM and finish with plain `dev done`; they cannot go
28	COLD because the canonical checkout cannot be removed. Branch-only tasks can go
29	cold after push by switching the canonical checkout back to base. The full
30	state machine below describes the default worktree mode.
31	
32	Do not create isolation before it has a job. Equally, a new parallel worktree
33	starts from committed HEAD — it does not carry dirty main changes — so
34	checkpoint first when the new task depends on them.
35	
36	## The four states
37	
38	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
39	|---|---|---|---|
40	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
41	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
42	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
43	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
44	
45	Only the transitions between them cost anything:
46	
47	```
48	        dev start
49	            │
50	            ▼
51	         🔥 hot ──── dev done ────► ✅ done
52	          │  ▲
53	   dev park│  │dev resume
54	          ▼  │
55	        🌤 warm
56	          │  ▲
57	dev park  │  │dev resume
58	  --cold  ▼  │  (rebuilds the worktree)
59	        ❄️ cold
60	```
61	
62	**A machine should hold roughly three to seven hot tasks.** That is a
63	cognitive limit, not a technical one. Everything else belongs in `dev ls`.
64	
65	## Parking
66	
67	```bash
68	dev park --next "reproduce the token refresh race, then add a regression test"
69	```
70	
71	This is the move the whole design exists to make safe. It records what to do
72	next, closes the runtime session, and leaves the checkout boundary exactly
73	where it is. In direct mode that is the current branch; in worktree mode it is
74	the branch and linked checkout.
75	
76	`--next` is the important part. Without it, resuming means re-deriving where
77	you were from a diff, which is most of the cost of a context switch. Always
78	supply one.
79	
80	Useful variations:
81	
82	```bash
83	dev park --wip                    # checkpoint uncommitted work first
84	dev park --cold --push            # push, remove the worktree, keep the branch
85	dev park --keep-session           # record the state, leave the session open
86	```
87	
88	## Checkpoint commits, not stashes
89	
90	`--wip` makes a `wip: checkpoint — <next>` commit rather than a `git stash`.
91	
92	A stash is invisible in the log, easy to forget, and **cannot be pushed** — so
93	it can never reach another machine. That last point is decisive: the whole
94	value of parking is that the work is recoverable from anywhere.
95	
96	Messy WIP commits on a feature branch are fine. Branch history is *construction
97	history*; the base branch's history is *product history*. They do not have to
98	match — clean the branch up at the integration boundary with an interactive
99	rebase, or squash it, and decide then.
100	
101	## Cold, and why it is safe
102	
103	Going cold removes the checkout. That feels lossy, and is not, because:
104	
105	- the branch still holds every commit;
106	- `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, so the remote holds
107	  them too;
108	- `dev resume` rebuilds the worktree from `origin/<branch>`.
109	
110	The directory is a cache. The branch is the identity. Once that is true, a
111	local filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished checkouts.
112	
113	## Moving work between machines
114	
115	The remote is the handoff boundary. Do not sync worktrees, runtime state, or
116	the multiplexer's database between machines — sync branches.
117	
118	On the machine holding the work:
119	
120	```bash
121	dev park --cold --push
122	```
123	
124	On the machine picking it up:
125	
126	```bash
127	dev resume <task> --fetch
128	```
129	
130	**One writer per branch at a time.** `dev` records an `owner` host and refuses
131	to resume a task owned by another machine without `--force`. Two machines
132	committing to one branch is the only reliable way to make this workflow produce
133	a conflict; the ownership check is what prevents it.
134	
135	If two machines genuinely need to work the same feature at once, split the
136	branch — `feat/auth-ui` and `feat/auth-api` — and integrate afterwards. That is
137	the same rule as for parallel agents: parallel writers get parallel branches.
138	
139	The task registry itself (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`) is one small TOML file
140	per task, specifically so it can live in a private git repo and merge cleanly
141	across machines. Point `paths.state_dir` at one if you want a shared view.
142	
143	## Sweeping
144	
145	```bash
146	dev sweep            # report only
147	dev sweep --apply    # act, confirming each change
148	```
149	
150	`sweep` reports two kinds of problem:
151	
152	- **Drift** — a task marked hot with no live session, a warm task with one, a
153	  recorded worktree git no longer knows about.
154	- **Staleness** — a warm task nobody has touched in two weeks, clean and
155	  pushed, that could go cold.
156	
157	It also lists **live sessions no task claims** — the other half of a crowded
158	sidebar, and usually the larger half.
159	
160	`sweep` never deletes uncommitted work, and never acts without `--apply`. The
161	reason cleanup usually does not happen is not unwillingness; it is the absence
162	of a trustworthy guarantee that the work is recoverable. Reporting first, and
163	requiring confirmation, is that guarantee.
164	
165	## Integration
166	
167	```bash
168	dev done --ff     # rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it
169	dev done --pr     # push and open a pull/merge request via gh or glab
170	```
171	
172	Which one depends on a single question: **are this branch's commits worth
173	keeping in the base's history?**
174	
175	- Yes → `--ff`. Linear history, no merge commit, `git bisect` and `git blame`
176	  stay legible.
177	- No, it is WIP noise → squash at the integration point.
178	- Someone (or CI) should look first → `--pr`.
179	
180	`dev done` refuses on a dirty tree, and `--delete-branch` only removes a branch
181	git agrees is fully contained in the base. "Merged" is not always "finished" —
182	work often continues on a branch after its first integration, which is why the
183	branch survives by default.
184
```

python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import json,re
root=Path('/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-completion-and-brew/.specstory')
data=json.loads((root/'statistics.json').read_text())['sessions']
files={}
for p in sorted((root/'history').glob('*.md')):
    prefix=p.read_bytes()[:4096].decode(errors='replace')
    m=re.search(r'<!-- (?:Claude Code|Codex CLI) Session ([0-9a-f-]+)',prefix)
    if m: files[m.group(1)]=p
for sid,e in data.items():
    p=files.get(sid)
    print(json.dumps({'session_id':sid,'mapped_file':p.name if p else None,'metadata_bytes':e['markdown_size_bytes'],'current_file_bytes':p.stat().st_size if p else None,'delta':p.stat().st_size-e['markdown_size_bytes'] if p else None,'provider':e['provider'],'last_updated':e['last_updated']},separators=(',',':')))
for sid,p in files.items():
    if sid not in data:
        print(json.dumps({'session_id':sid,'mapped_file':p.name,'metadata_entry':None,'current_file_bytes':p.stat().st_size},separators=(',',':')))
PY
```

package cli

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/help"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/ignore"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/repo"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/stats"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

const noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp

var completionDescriptionSanitizer = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ")

// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
// persistent flags (notably --config).
func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
	if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd || cmd.CalledAs() == cobra.ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd {
		return true
	}
	for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
		if cur.Name() == "completion" {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// loadCompletion prepares local providers after Cobra has parsed the command
// line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break command and
// flag completion entirely. Cobra invokes one custom provider per request, so
// loading here avoids state leaking when a command tree is reused.
func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool { return a.Load() == nil }

func completeTasks(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
	return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
		for _, t := range tasks {
			description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
			out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
		}
		return out, noFileCompletion
	}
}

// completeRepos supplies positional repository references. Commands resolve a
// unique display name, while duplicate displays use their absolute path so the
// selected token still identifies exactly one checkout.
func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
	return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
		if len(args) > 0 {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, false)
	}
}

// completeRepoFlag is the same domain without a positional-argument guard: a
// flag may legally appear after another argument, e.g. wt open branch --repo.
func completeRepoFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
	return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
		return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, false)
	}
}

// completeRepoNameFlag returns the name stored in tasks and stats, not the
// Category/Name display reference used by repository commands.
func completeRepoNameFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
	return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
		return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, true)
	}
}

func repositoryCompletions(app *App, toComplete string, namesOnly bool) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
	if !app.loadCompletion() {
		return nil, noFileCompletion
	}
	repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
	if err != nil {
		return nil, noFileCompletion
	}
	displayCount := make(map[string]int, len(repos))
	for _, r := range repos {
		displayCount[r.Display()]++
	}
	seen := make(map[string]bool, len(repos))
	out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
	for _, r := range repos {
		value := r.Display()
		description := config.Contract(r.Path)
		switch {
		case namesOnly:
			value = r.Name
			description = r.Display() + " · " + description
		case displayCount[value] > 1:
			value = r.Path
			description = r.Display() + " · " + description
		}
		if seen[value] {
			continue
		}
		seen[value] = true
		out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
	}
	return out, noFileCompletion
}

func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
	return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
		repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, noFileCompletion
		}
		out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
		for _, wt := range worktrees {
			if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
				continue
			}
			description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
			if wt.Main {
				description += " (main checkout)"
			}
			out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
		}
		return out, noFileCompletion
	}
}

func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
	if len(args) > 0 {
		return nil, noFileCompletion
	}
	topics, err := help.List()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, noFileCompletion
	}
	out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
	for _, topic := range topics {
		out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
	}
	return out, noFileCompletion
}

func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
	used := make(map[string]bool, len(args))
	for _, name := range args {
		used[strings.ToLower(name)] = true
	}
	names := ignore.BundledNames()
	out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
	for _, name := range names {
		value := strings.ToLower(name)
		if !used[value] {
			out = addCompletion(out, value, name+" bundled template", toComplete)
		}
	}
	return out, noFileCompletion
}

func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
	return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
		out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
		for _, value := range values {
			out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
		}
		return out, noFileCompletion
	}
}

func runtimeCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
	backends := runtime.All()
	values := make([]string, len(backends))
	for i, backend := range backends {
		values[i] = backend.Name()
	}
	return fixedCompletions(values...)
}

func taskStateCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
	values := make([]string, len(task.States))
	for i, state := range task.States {
		values[i] = string(state)
	}
	return fixedCompletions(values...)
}

func statsSourceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
	return fixedCompletions(
		string(stats.SourceSession), string(stats.SourceGit), string(stats.SourceWakaTime),
	)
}

func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
	if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}

func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
	if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
		return out
	}
	if description != "" {
		description = completionDescriptionSanitizer.Replace(description)
		value = cobra.CompletionWithDesc(value, description)
	}
	return append(out, value)
}

1-v2.10.0	2026-08-17T22:14:25Z	\n### 📢 Announcements\n\n- The SpecStory CLI now supports [Muse Code](https://developer.meta.com/ai/products/muse-code/) for agent sessions created from Muse Code `0.1.0-R708.1` or higher. Sessions from earlier versions may work, but are not officially supported. This provides the same support for saving to local markdown files and to the SpecStory Cloud as for [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/docs/api/claude-code), [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/docs/cli), [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/), Factory's [Droid CLI](https://factory.ai/product/cli), [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/product), [Visual Studio Code Copilot](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/copilot), Google's [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/) and [DeepSeek TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI).\n- You can use `specstory resume` to resume Muse Code sessions in other coding agents, and to resume any agent's session into Muse Code.\n\n### 🐛 Bug Fixes\n\n- `output_dir` in `config.toml` is now honored by `specstory watch` and `specstory resume`, not just by `run` and `sync`. Previously only the `--output-dir` flag reached `watch`, so with the setting in your config file the startup save went to your configured directory while everything written during the watch went to `./.specstory/history` — leaving markdown in two places, with the configured copy going stale. Thanks to [petercurcio](https://github.com/petercurcio) for the detailed report in [issue 273](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/issues/273). If you hit this, the copies under `./.specstory/history` are the newer ones; move or delete them once, and everything lands in your configured directory from now on.\n- Codex CLI sessions started in Codex `0.147.0`+ are saved again. Codex changed how its Codex CLI TUI records a conversation in that release, and SpecStory read only the older form, so those sessions produced a markdown file containing just a header, with every prompt and reply missing. Both forms are now read. This affects only sessions **started** in `0.147.0`+. Sessions from earlier versions, and older sessions you resume under `0.147` were never affected, and their markdown is unchanged. Re-run `specstory sync` to fill in any sessions that were saved empty.\n- `specstory watch` and `specstory run` now behave the same way at startup whichever agent you are watching: they save new activity from that point on, and leave sessions that already exist alone. Previously Codex CLI, Droid CLI, DeepSeek TUI and Antigravity CLI re-saved and re-synced their existing sessions on every start, while Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Gemini CLI and Muse Code did not. Run `specstory sync` when you want existing sessions written or refreshed.\n- The first update to a session that already had a markdown file is no longer missing from `specstory watch` output. The line was sometimes being swallowed as if it were startup noise, so for some agents, some of the time your first prompt after starting `watch` appeared to do nothing; only the second one showed up.\n- `specstory run` and `specstory watch` no longer reprocess your entire Codex CLI history every time they start. Codex stores sessions by date, and while SpecStory only ever watched the last few days for live changes, it was scanning and re-saving every day directory going back to your first ever session — rewriting all that markdown and re-syncing it to the SpecStory Cloud on each launch. Startup now covers the same trailing window that live watching does, plus the day of a session you are resuming, however old it is. If you have a long Codex history, expect `run` and `watch` to start noticeably faster and stop touching old markdown files; a full `specstory sync` still processes everything as before.
2:v2.9.0	2026-08-12T21:20:48Z	\n### 📢 Announcements\n\n- The SpecStory CLI now supports native Windows and the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL). Install on Windows by downloading `SpecStoryCLI_Windows_x86_64.zip` (or `_arm64`) from the [GitHub release](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/releases) and putting `specstory.exe` on your PATH. Signing the binary, and a package manager install (e.g. winget) is planned. Since the binaries are not yet code-signed, Windows SmartScreen may show an "unrecognized app" warning on first run. WSL users should just keep using the standard Linux install, which now reads Windows-side IDE data automatically.\n\n### 🔧 CLI Configuration & Commands\n\n- New `--user-data-dir` flag on `sync`, `check`, `list` and `watch` points an IDE provider at a non-default install location, for portable installs and for reading a Windows-side install from WSL. It takes a `provider_id:path` pair and is repeatable, e.g. `--user-data-dir cursoride:D:\\apps\\cursor\\current\\data\\user-data --user-data-dir copilotide:/opt/vscode/data`. The path is the user-data-dir itself (the parent of the `User` directory), the same value the IDE's own `--user-data-dir` argument takes. Supported provider IDs are `cursoride`, `copilotide`, `copilotide-insiders`, `copilotide-vscodium` and `copilotide-vscodium-insiders`. If the override path doesn't exist, SpecStory warns and falls back to the standard location for your OS rather than leaving the provider idle.\n- New `--config-dir` flag on `run`, `sync` and `watch` relocates the project-level config directory — both where the default `config.toml` is created and where it is read from — for cases where the project directory itself shouldn't be written to, e.g. `specstory sync --config-dir ~/specstory-configs/myproject`. Without the flag the project-level config stays at `./.specstory/cli/config.toml`.\n- New `--no-stats` flag on `run`, `sync`, `watch`, `resume` and `search` skips session statistics entirely, so `./.specstory/statistics.json` is neither read nor written. Statistics stay on by default; `--no-stats` cannot be combined with `--only-stats`.\n\n### ⚙️ Improvements\n\n- Cursor IDE and VS Code Copilot conversations from WSL and SSH remote workspaces are now discovered and saved. The IDE records the same project differently depending on how it was opened (local path, WSL distro, or SSH remote); SpecStory now matches all of these forms and aggregates the sessions from every matching workspace entry, so conversations are found no matter which environment they were created in. Running from inside WSL also works: SpecStory detects WSL and reads the IDE's data from the Windows side via `/mnt/c/`.\n- When `--output-dir` is set, the project identity file `.project.json` now lives in that directory alongside the markdown, statistics and debug output, instead of staying at `./.specstory/.project.json` — so you still capture every SpecStory output file under one directory, and SpecStory Cloud sync reads the identity from there too. If you already use `--output-dir` with SpecStory Cloud, copy your existing `./.specstory/.project.json` into the output directory once to keep the same project identity.\n- Session statistics (`./.specstory/statistics.json`) now stay current during `run`, `watch`, `resume` and `sync -s` as each session saves, instead of updating only during a full `sync`. Use the new `--no-stats` flag if you don't want this.
3-v2.8.0	2026-08-10T13:08:00Z	\n### 🐛 Bug Fixes\n\n- Fenced code blocks in the rendered markdown (those triple backticks) are now sized correctly across all providers. When a session included tool output that itself contained embedded code fences — a cat of a README, a diff of a markdown file — the resulting markdown could become unbalanced and wreck how rendering engines display everything after it. Fences are now sized past any backtick runs in the content, and the old backslash-escape workaround (which left visible \\ artifacts) is gone. Thanks to [huangruizhe](https://github.com/huangruizhe) for diagnosing the problem and proposing the fix in [PR 241](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/241), which was the inspiration for this change. Note: your existing markdown files may update once on your next sync as fences are resized and escape artifacts removed.\n- Consecutive user messages (e.g. from a turn the agent never answered) are now separated by a --- divider in the generated markdown for all providers. This may also cause small one-time markdown updates on your next sync.\n- `specstory watch` no longer silently disables an IDE provider when the watch starts before the project has ever been opened in that IDE. Previously, running `specstory watch` in a fresh directory and then opening it in Cursor or VS Code meant nothing was ever saved; the watcher now waits for the IDE to create the workspace and picks up the first session automatically.\n- The Cursor IDE provider now prefers the workspace entry whose path exactly matches the on-disk spelling of the project directory. On macOS's case-insensitive filesystem, opening the same folder as ~/source/... and ~/Source/... creates two separate workspace entries, splitting sessions between them; SpecStory now reads and writes the entry the IDE itself will use, and launches the IDE with the canonical path so it stops creating case-duplicate entries.\n- `specstory run` for an IDE provider no longer hangs before watching starts when a custom launcher command includes `--wait`.\n\n### ⚙️ Improvements\n\n- `specstory run` with an IDE provider (Cursor IDE, VS Code Copilot) now shows progress in the terminal: a note while waiting for the IDE to open the project, confirmation when it connects, and a line for each session save, instead of sitting silent while you work in the IDE.

```text
package session

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"time"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

// SessionStatistics contains computed statistics for a single session
type SessionStatistics struct {
	UserMessageCount  int    `json:"user_message_count"`
	AgentMessageCount int    `json:"agent_message_count"`
	StartTimestamp    string `json:"start_timestamp"`
	EndTimestamp      string `json:"end_timestamp"`
	MarkdownSizeBytes int    `json:"markdown_size_bytes"`
	Provider          string `json:"provider"`
	LastUpdated       string `json:"last_updated"`
}

// StatisticsFile is the root structure for the statistics.json file
type StatisticsFile struct {
	Sessions map[string]SessionStatistics `json:"sessions"`
}

// StatisticsCollector handles thread-safe statistics collection and persistence.
// Stats are accumulated in memory via AddSessionStats and written to disk in a
// single read-modify-write cycle when Flush is called.
type StatisticsCollector struct {
	statsPath string
	mu        sync.Mutex
	pending   map[string]SessionStatistics // in-memory buffer of stats awaiting flush
}

// NewStatisticsCollector creates a new statistics collector that writes to the given path
func NewStatisticsCollector(statsPath string) *StatisticsCollector {
	return &StatisticsCollector{
		statsPath: statsPath,
		pending:   make(map[string]SessionStatistics),
	}
}

// sharedCollectors hands out one collector per statistics file so every writer
// in the process serializes on the same mutex. The collector's locking only
// protects its own instance: separate instances racing through Flush's
// read-modify-write would silently drop sessions when concurrent watch-mode
// callbacks save at the same time. Serialization across processes (a running
// `watch` plus a manual `sync`) is handled separately, by the file lock Flush
// takes around the read-merge-write cycle.
var (
	sharedCollectorsMu sync.Mutex
	sharedCollectors   = map[string]*StatisticsCollector{}

	// lockTokenCounter makes lock-file owner tokens unique within the process
	// even when minted in the same clock tick (see acquireFileLock).
	lockTokenCounter atomic.Uint64
)

// SharedStatisticsCollector returns the process-wide collector for statsPath,
// creating it on first use. All statistics writers — bulk sync batching,
// per-session saves from run/watch callbacks, `sync -s` — should go through
// this rather than NewStatisticsCollector so their writes serialize.
func SharedStatisticsCollector(statsPath string) *StatisticsCollector {
	sharedCollectorsMu.Lock()
	defer sharedCollectorsMu.Unlock()

	collector, ok := sharedCollectors[statsPath]
	if !ok {
		collector = NewStatisticsCollector(statsPath)
		sharedCollectors[statsPath] = collector
	}
	return collector
}

// ComputeSessionStatistics extracts statistics from SessionData and markdown content.
// providerID is the registry/CLI provider id (e.g. "claude"), deliberately NOT
// sessionData.Provider.ID (e.g. "claude-code") — statistics.json has stored
// registry ids since the feature shipped, and external consumers group by them,
// so switching id spaces would silently rewrite documented output.
func ComputeSessionStatistics(sessionData *schema.SessionData, markdownContent string, providerID string) SessionStatistics {
	stats := SessionStatistics{
		Provider:          providerID,
		MarkdownSizeBytes: len(markdownContent),
		LastUpdated:       time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
	}

	// Count user and agent messages by iterating through exchanges
	userMsgCount := 0
	agentMsgCount := 0
	for _, exchange := range sessionData.Exchanges {
		for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
			if msg.Role == schema.RoleUser {
				userMsgCount++
			} else {
				agentMsgCount++
			}
		}
	}
	stats.UserMessageCount = userMsgCount
	stats.AgentMessageCount = agentMsgCount

	// Extract start timestamp - use first exchange start time if available, else session CreatedAt
	if len(sessionData.Exchanges) > 0 && sessionData.Exchanges[0].StartTime != "" {
		stats.StartTimestamp = sessionData.Exchanges[0].StartTime
	} else {
		stats.StartTimestamp = sessionData.CreatedAt
	}

	// Extract end timestamp - use last exchange end time if available, else session UpdatedAt, else CreatedAt
	if len(sessionData.Exchanges) > 0 {
		lastExchange := sessionData.Exchanges[len(sessionData.Exchanges)-1]
		if lastExchange.EndTime != "" {
			stats.EndTimestamp = lastExchange.EndTime
		} else if sessionData.UpdatedAt != "" {
			stats.EndTimestamp = sessionData.UpdatedAt
		} else {
			stats.EndTimestamp = sessionData.CreatedAt
		}
	} else if sessionData.UpdatedAt != "" {
		stats.EndTimestamp = sessionData.UpdatedAt
	} else {
		stats.EndTimestamp = sessionData.CreatedAt
	}

	return stats
}

// AddSessionStats accumulates session statistics in memory. Call Flush to
// persist all pending stats to disk in a single I/O operation.
func (c *StatisticsCollector) AddSessionStats(sessionID string, stats SessionStatistics) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()

	c.pending[sessionID] = stats
	slog.Debug("Buffered session statistics", "sessionId", sessionID)
}

// acquireFileLock takes a cross-process lock by creating lockPath with O_EXCL,
// which is atomic on every platform (no syscall flock needed, so no platform
// build tags and no new dependency). The in-process mutex alone cannot stop two
// processes — a long-running `watch` and a manual `sync` — from interleaving
// Flush's read-merge-write and silently dropping the loser's sessions.
//
// Polls briefly while the lock is held: flushes are millisecond-scale, so a
// two-second budget is generous. A lock file older than staleLockAge is
// presumed abandoned by a crashed process and stolen; the steal itself has a
// benign race (two stealers, one wins O_EXCL, the other retries).
//
// The lock file carries an owner token, and release deletes the file only when
// the token is still ours. Without that, a steal cascades: if a live-but-slow
// owner is stolen from, its unconditional release would delete the NEW owner's
// lock and let a third writer into the critical section. With the token, the
// stale original's release becomes a no-op. A small read-then-remove window
// remains (this is a lock file, not an OS lock); the residual worst case is the
// pre-lock behavior — one lost merge — not corruption.
// Returns the release func on success.
func acquireFileLock(lockPath string) (func(), error) {
	const (
		retryDelay   = 10 * time.Millisecond
		retryBudget  = 2 * time.Second
		staleLockAge = 30 * time.Second
	)

	// The counter disambiguates tokens minted within one clock tick: Windows'
	// timer granularity is coarse enough that two acquisitions in the same
	// process can observe the same UnixNano, and identical tokens would let a
	// stolen-from owner's release delete the new owner's lock after all.
	token := fmt.Sprintf("%d-%d-%d", os.Getpid(), lockTokenCounter.Add(1), time.Now().UnixNano())
	deadline := time.Now().Add(retryBudget)
	for {
		f, err := os.OpenFile(lockPath, os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL|os.O_WRONLY, 0644)
		if err == nil {
			_, _ = f.WriteString(token)
			_ = f.Close()
			return func() {
				if data, readErr := os.ReadFile(lockPath); readErr == nil && string(data) == token {
					_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
				}
			}, nil
		}
		if !os.IsExist(err) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create lock file: %w", err)
		}
		// Held by another process — steal it if it looks abandoned. Fast-retry
		// only when the removal actually succeeded: a failing removal (directory
		// permissions, antivirus briefly holding the file on Windows) must fall
		// through to the deadline and sleep below, or this loop would spin
		// forever without ever honoring the retry budget.
		if info, statErr := os.Stat(lockPath); statErr == nil && time.Since(info.ModTime()) > staleLockAge {
			if removeErr := os.Remove(lockPath); removeErr == nil {
				continue
			}
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("statistics lock still held after %s: %s", retryBudget, lockPath)
		}
		time.Sleep(retryDelay)
	}
}

// Flush writes all pending session statistics to the statistics.json file in a
// single read-modify-write cycle, then clears the pending buffer. A file lock
// spans the whole cycle so concurrent processes can't lose each other's merges.
func (c *StatisticsCollector) Flush() error {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()

	// Nothing to flush
	if len(c.pending) == 0 {
		return nil
	}

	unlock, err := acquireFileLock(c.statsPath + ".lock")
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to lock statistics file: %w", err)
	}
	defer unlock()

	statsPath := c.statsPath

	// Read existing statistics file
	statsFile := StatisticsFile{
		Sessions: make(map[string]SessionStatistics),
	}

	data, err := os.ReadFile(statsPath)
	if err == nil {
		// File exists, try to parse it
		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &statsFile); err != nil {
			// Corrupt JSON - log warning and start fresh
			slog.Warn("Failed to parse existing statistics.json, starting fresh", "error", err)
			statsFile.Sessions = make(map[string]SessionStatistics)
		}
	} else if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		// Error other than "file doesn't exist"
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to read statistics file: %w", err)
	}

	// Merge all pending stats into the file
	for sessionID, stats := range c.pending {
		statsFile.Sessions[sessionID] = stats
	}

	// Marshal to JSON with indentation for readability
	jsonData, err := json.MarshalIndent(statsFile, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal statistics: %w", err)
	}
	jsonData = append(jsonData, '\n')

	// Write atomically using temp file + rename
	tempPath := statsPath + ".tmp"
	if err := os.WriteFile(tempPath, jsonData, 0644); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write temp statistics file: %w", err)
	}

	if err := os.Rename(tempPath, statsPath); err != nil {
		// Clean up temp file on failure
		_ = os.Remove(tempPath)
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename temp statistics file: %w", err)
	}

	slog.Debug("Flushed session statistics", "count", len(c.pending), "path", statsPath)

	// Clear pending buffer
	c.pending = make(map[string]SessionStatistics)
	return nil
}

// TestCollectSessionStatistics_ConcurrentSaves guards the shared-collector design:
// concurrent CollectSessionStatistics calls (as watch-mode callbacks produce) must
// all land in statistics.json. Per-call collector instances would race in Flush's
// read-modify-write cycle and silently drop sessions.
func TestCollectSessionStatistics_ConcurrentSaves(t *testing.T) {
	config := &utils.OutputPathConfig{BaseDir: t.TempDir()}

	const sessionCount = 25
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for i := 0; i < sessionCount; i++ {
		wg.Go(func() {
			sess := &spi.AgentChatSession{
				SessionID: fmt.Sprintf("session-%02d", i),
				SessionData: &schema.SessionData{
					Provider:  schema.ProviderInfo{ID: "claude", Name: "Claude"},
					CreatedAt: "2026-02-09T10:00:00Z",
				},
			}
			if err := CollectSessionStatistics("claude", sess, "# markdown", config); err != nil {
				t.Errorf("CollectSessionStatistics(%s): %v", sess.SessionID, err)
			}
		})
	}
	wg.Wait()

	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(config.GetSpecstoryDir(), utils.STATISTICS_FILE))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Failed to read statistics.json: %v", err)
	}
	var statsFile StatisticsFile
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &statsFile); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Failed to parse statistics.json: %v", err)
	}
	if len(statsFile.Sessions) != sessionCount {
		t.Errorf("statistics.json has %d sessions, want %d — concurrent saves dropped sessions",
			len(statsFile.Sessions), sessionCount)
	}

// testStatsPath returns the full statistics.json path for a temp directory.
func testStatsPath(dir string) string {
	return filepath.Join(dir, "statistics.json")
}

// readStatisticsFile is a test helper that reads and parses the statistics.json file.
func readStatisticsFile(t *testing.T, dir string) StatisticsFile {
	t.Helper()
	data, err := os.ReadFile(testStatsPath(dir))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Failed to read statistics.json: %v", err)
	}
	var sf StatisticsFile
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &sf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Failed to parse statistics.json: %v", err)
	}
	return sf
}

func TestStatisticsCollector_CreateNewFile(t *testing.T) {
	tempDir := t.TempDir()
	collector := NewStatisticsCollector(testStatsPath(tempDir))

	stats := SessionStatistics{
		UserMessageCount:  5,
		AgentMessageCount: 8,
		StartTimestamp:    "2026-02-09T10:00:00Z",
		EndTimestamp:      "2026-02-09T10:15:00Z",
		MarkdownSizeBytes: 1234,
		Provider:          "claude",
		LastUpdated:       "2026-02-09T10:20:00Z",
	}

	collector.AddSessionStats("session-1", stats)

	if err := collector.Flush(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Flush failed: %v", err)
	}

	sf := readStatisticsFile(t, tempDir)
	if len(sf.Sessions) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("Expected 1 session, got %d", len(sf.Sessions))
	}
	retrieved := sf.Sessions["session-1"]
	if retrieved.UserMessageCount != 5 {
		t.Errorf("UserMessageCount = %d, want 5", retrieved.UserMessageCount)
	}
	if retrieved.Provider != "claude" {
		t.Errorf("Provider = %s, want claude", retrieved.Provider)
	}
}

// TestAcquireFileLock exercises the cross-process lock primitive that Flush
// wraps around its read-merge-write cycle: a held lock blocks acquisition until
// released, and a lock left behind by a crashed process (detected by age) is
// stolen rather than deadlocking every future flush.
func TestAcquireFileLock(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("held lock blocks until released, then acquires", func(t *testing.T) {
		lockPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "statistics.json.lock")

		unlock, err := acquireFileLock(lockPath)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("first acquire failed: %v", err)
		}

		// A second acquirer must wait; release shortly after it starts polling.
		go func() {
			time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
			unlock()
		}()

		start := time.Now()
		unlock2, err := acquireFileLock(lockPath)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("second acquire failed after release: %v", err)
		}
		defer unlock2()
		if time.Since(start) < 40*time.Millisecond {
			t.Error("second acquire returned before the first lock was released")
		}
	})

	t.Run("stale lock from a crashed process is stolen", func(t *testing.T) {
		lockPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "statistics.json.lock")
		if err := os.WriteFile(lockPath, nil, 0644); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("failed to plant stale lock: %v", err)
		}
		// Backdate past the stale threshold to simulate a crashed owner.
		old := time.Now().Add(-time.Minute)
		if err := os.Chtimes(lockPath, old, old); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("failed to backdate lock: %v", err)
		}

		unlock, err := acquireFileLock(lockPath)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("acquire should have stolen the stale lock: %v", err)
		}
		unlock()
	})

	t.Run("unremovable stale lock times out instead of spinning forever", func(t *testing.T) {
		// Unix mode bits can't make a directory read-only on Windows, so the
		// removal failure can't be provoked there.
		if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
			t.Skip("directory write permissions cannot be revoked via mode bits on Windows")
		}
		dir := t.TempDir()
		lockPath := filepath.Join(dir, "statistics.json.lock")
		if err := os.WriteFile(lockPath, nil, 0644); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("failed to plant stale lock: %v", err)
		}
		old := time.Now().Add(-time.Minute)
		if err := os.Chtimes(lockPath, old, old); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("failed to backdate lock: %v", err)
		}
		// Read-only dir: the steal's os.Remove fails on every iteration.
		if err := os.Chmod(dir, 0555); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("failed to chmod dir: %v", err)
		}
		t.Cleanup(func() { _ = os.Chmod(dir, 0755) })

		start := time.Now()
		_, err := acquireFileLock(lockPath)
		elapsed := time.Since(start)
		if err == nil {
			t.Fatal("acquire should fail when the stale lock cannot be removed")
		}
		// The retry budget is 2s; anything wildly beyond it means the loop spun
		// past the deadline check. Generous bound for slow CI.
		if elapsed > 10*time.Second {
			t.Fatalf("acquire took %s — the removal-failure path is bypassing the deadline", elapsed)
		}
	})

	t.Run("stolen-from owner's release cannot delete the new owner's lock", func(t *testing.T) {
		lockPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "statistics.json.lock")

		releaseOld, err := acquireFileLock(lockPath)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("first acquire failed: %v", err)
		}
		// Backdate so the next acquirer treats the (still-live) owner as crashed
		// and steals — the slow-writer scenario.
		old := time.Now().Add(-time.Minute)
		if err := os.Chtimes(lockPath, old, old); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("failed to backdate lock: %v", err)
		}
		releaseNew, err := acquireFileLock(lockPath)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("steal acquire failed: %v", err)
		}

		// The stale original releases; the new owner's lock must survive, or a
		// third writer could enter the critical section.
		releaseOld()
		if _, err := os.Stat(lockPath); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("previous owner's release deleted the new owner's lock: %v", err)
		}

		releaseNew()
		if _, err := os.Stat(lockPath); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
			t.Errorf("new owner's release should remove the lock, stat err = %v", err)
		}
	})
}
