14	// Version is set at build time via -ldflags. VersionFromBuild also recovers a
15	// module version for `go install ...@version` builds.
16	var Version = "dev"
17	
18	func versionFromBuild() string {
19		if Version != "dev" {
20			return Version
21		}
22		if info, ok := debug.ReadBuildInfo(); ok && info.Main.Version != "" && info.Main.Version != "(devel)" {
23			return info.Main.Version
24		}
25		return Version
26	}
27	
28	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
29	
30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
31	
32	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
33	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
34	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
35	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
36	
37	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
38	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
39	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`
40	
41	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
42	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
43		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
44	}
45	
46	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
47	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
48	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
49	// descriptors.
50	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
51		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
52	
53		root := &cobra.Command{
54			Use:           "dev",
55			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
56			Long:          rootLong,
57			Version:       versionFromBuild(),
58			SilenceUsage:  true,
59			SilenceErrors: true,
60			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
61			// exists to answer.
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
64					out, err := skill.Render()
65					if err != nil {
66						return err
67					}
68					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
69					return nil
70				}
71				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
72				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
73				if interactive() {
74					return runTUI(app)
75				}
76				return runList(app, listOptions{})
77			},
78			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
79				if completionInvocation(cmd) {
80					return nil
81				}
82				return app.Load()
83			},
84		}
85	
86		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
87		pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
88		pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux or none")
89		pf.BoolVar(&app.noRuntime, "no-runtime", false, "do not touch any terminal multiplexer")
90		registerFlagCompletion(root, "runtime", runtimeCompletions())
91	
92		// Mirrors `herdr --skill`: the binary is the authority for its own agent
93		// skill, so a dotfiles installer can sync it without vendoring a copy.
94		root.Flags().Bool("skill", false, "print the bundled agent skill and exit")
95	
96		root.AddCommand(
97			newListCmd(app),
98			newTUICmd(app),
99			newStatusCmd(app),
100			newStartCmd(app),
101			newParkCmd(app),
102			newResumeCmd(app),
103			newDoneCmd(app),
104			newSweepCmd(app),
105			newAdoptCmd(app),
106			newBootstrapCmd(app),
107			newWorktreeCmd(app),
108			newRepoCmd(app),
109			newGitignoreCmd(app),
110			newTryCmd(app),
111			newGraduateCmd(app),
112			newStatsCmd(app),
113			newHelpTopicCmd(app),
114			newSkillCmd(app),
115			newDoctorCmd(app),
116			newShellInitCmd(app),
117			newConfigCmd(app),
118			newCacheCmd(app),
119			newEditCmd(app),
120		)
121		root.SetHelpCommand(&cobra.Command{Hidden: true, Use: "no-help"})
122		root.SetOut(out)
123		root.SetErr(errOut)
124		return root
125	}
126	
127	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
128	func Execute() int {
129		root := NewRootCommand()
130		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
131			msg := err.Error()
132			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
133			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
134				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
135			}
136			return 1
137		}
138		return 0
139	}

1	// Package gitx wraps the git porcelain commands dev depends on. Every helper
2	// shells out to git rather than linking a Go implementation: git is already a
3	// hard dependency, its porcelain formats are stable and documented, and this
4	// keeps dev's behaviour identical to what the user sees when they run the same
5	// command by hand.
6	package gitx
7	
8	import (
9		"bytes"
10		"context"
11		"errors"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotARepo is returned when a directory is not inside a git working tree.
18	var ErrNotARepo = errors.New("not a git repository")
19	
20	// Error carries the failing command and git's own stderr, which is almost
21	// always more useful than the exit status alone.
22	type Error struct {
23		Args   []string
24		Dir    string
25		Stderr string
26		Err    error
27	}
28	
29	func (e *Error) Error() string {
30		msg := strings.TrimSpace(e.Stderr)
31		if msg == "" {
32			msg = e.Err.Error()
33		}
34		return fmt.Sprintf("git %s: %s", strings.Join(e.Args, " "), msg)
35	}
36	
37	func (e *Error) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
38	
39	// run executes git in dir and returns trimmed stdout.
40	func run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
41		// -c core.quotepath=false keeps non-ASCII paths readable rather than
42		// octal-escaped, which matters for the Chinese-named files in these repos.
43		full := append([]string{"-c", "core.quotepath=false"}, args...)
44		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", full...)
45		cmd.Dir = dir
46		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
47		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
48		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
49		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
50			gerr := &Error{Args: args, Dir: dir, Stderr: stderr.String(), Err: err}
51			if strings.Contains(gerr.Stderr, "not a git repository") {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", dir, ErrNotARepo)
53			}
54			return "", gerr
55		}
56		return strings.TrimRight(stdout.String(), "\n"), nil
57	}
58	
59	// Run executes an arbitrary git command in dir. Exported for the few callers
60	// (park's wip commit, done's merge) that need a one-off command.
61	func Run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
62		return run(ctx, dir, args...)
63	}
64	
65	// lines splits git output into non-empty lines.
66	func lines(s string) []string {
67		if s == "" {
68			return nil
69		}
70		out := strings.Split(s, "\n")
71		filtered := out[:0]
72		for _, l := range out {
73			if l != "" {
74				filtered = append(filtered, l)
75			}
76		}
77		return filtered
78	}
79	
80	// nulLines splits NUL-delimited git output (-z forms).
81	func nulLines(s string) []string {
82		s = strings.TrimRight(s, "\x00")
83		if s == "" {
84			return nil
85		}
86		return strings.Split(s, "\x00")
87	}

40	## Install
41	
42	### Homebrew (macOS)
43	
44	```bash
45	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli
46	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
47	```
48	
49	The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
50	does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.
51	
52	### Go or source
53	
54	```bash
55	go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@v0.1.0
56	# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
57	```
58	
59	For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
60	them:
61	
62	```bash
63	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
64	dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
65	dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
66	dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
67	```
68	
69	Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
70	worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
71	a forge or the network.
72	
73	Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
74	
75	```bash
76	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
77	eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
```
</details></tool-use>

460	actual file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` with either form:
461	
462	```bash
463	dev edit
464	dev config edit
465	DEV_EDITOR=unused dev edit --editor "code --wait"   # explicit override
466	```
467	
468	If the file does not exist, `edit` generates the machine-detected starter first
469	rather than opening an empty file. Resolution is `--editor` → `$VISUAL` →
470	`$EDITOR` → `nvim` → `vim` → `vi`.
471	
472	Every path is configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine —
473	a faster volume, a different naming convention:
474	
475	```toml
476	[paths]
477	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries"]
478	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
479	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
480	state_dir     = "~/.local/share/dev"        # point at a git repo to sync it
481	```
482	
483	Template variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`,
484	`host`, `date`. Filters: `|slug` (`feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`), `|lower`,
485	`|base`. A typo in a variable name fails at load, not as a directory literally
486	named `{{rep}}`.
487	
488	A flat project layout is already first-class — it needs no migration and no
489	special mode:
490	
491	```toml
492	[paths]
493	scan_roots   = ["~/code"]
494	project_root = "~/code"       # repo new/clone/graduate land at ~/code/<repo>
495	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/wt"
496	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}--{{branch|slug}}"
497	```
498	
499	Omit `--category` and canonical repos stay flat. Categories are metadata the
500	user may choose, never a directory structure dev imposes.
501	
502	## Multiple machines
503	
504	Do not sync worktrees or runtime state. Sync branches, and let the remote be
505	the handoff boundary:
506	
507	```bash
508	dev park --cold --push      # on the machine holding the work
509	dev resume <task> --fetch   # on the machine picking it up
510	```

130	**One writer per branch at a time.** `dev` records an `owner` host and refuses
131	to resume a task owned by another machine without `--force`. Two machines
132	committing to one branch is the only reliable way to make this workflow produce
133	a conflict; the ownership check is what prevents it.
134	
135	If two machines genuinely need to work the same feature at once, split the
136	branch — `feat/auth-ui` and `feat/auth-api` — and integrate afterwards. That is
137	the same rule as for parallel agents: parallel writers get parallel branches.
138	
139	The task registry itself (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`) is one small TOML file
140	per task, specifically so it can live in a private git repo and merge cleanly
141	across machines. Point `paths.state_dir` at one if you want a shared view.
142	
143	## Sweeping
144	
145	```bash
146	dev sweep            # report only
147	dev sweep --apply    # act, confirming each change

5		"os"

9	
10	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
11	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
12	type Repo struct {
13		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
14		Root string
15		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
16		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
17		GitCommonDir string
18		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
19		Name string
20		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
21		// the main checkout.
22		IsLinkedWorktree bool
23		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
24		MainRoot string
25		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
26		Bare bool
27	}
28	
29	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
30	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
31	
32	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
33	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
34		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
35		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
36		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
37			"rev-parse",
38			"--path-format=absolute",
39			"--show-toplevel",
40			"--git-common-dir",
41			"--is-bare-repository",
42		)
43		if err != nil {
44			return Repo{}, err
45		}
46		f := lines(out)
47		r := Repo{}
48		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
49		switch len(f) {
50		case 3:
51			r.Root = f[0]
52			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
53			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
54		case 2:
55			r.GitCommonDir = f[0]
56			r.Bare = f[1] == "true"
57		default:
58			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
59		}
60	
61		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
62		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
63		if r.Bare {
64			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
65		} else {
66			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
67		}
68		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.Root != r.MainRoot
69		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
70		if r.Bare {
71			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
72			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
73			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
74				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
75			}
76		}
77		return r, nil
78	}
79	
80	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
81	// a full Discover.
82	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
83		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
84		return err == nil
85	}
86	
87	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
88	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
89	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
90	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
91	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
92		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
93			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
94				return b
95			}
96		}
97		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
98			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
99				return cand
100			}
101		}
102		return ""
103	}
104	
105	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
106	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
107		if name == "" {
108			name = "origin"
109		}
110		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
111		if err != nil {
112			return ""
113		}
114		return out
115	}
116	
117	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
118	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
119	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
120	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
121	// semantics should use Remote instead.
122	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
123		if commonDir == "" {
124			return ""
125		}
126		if name == "" {
127			name = "origin"
128		}
129		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
130		if err != nil {
131			return ""
132		}
133		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
134		section := ""
135		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
136			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
137			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
138				continue
139			}
140			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
141				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
142				continue
143			}
144			if section != want {
145				continue
146			}
147			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
148			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
149				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
150			}
151		}
152		return ""
153	}

1	// Package gitx wraps the git porcelain commands dev depends on. Every helper
2	// shells out to git rather than linking a Go implementation: git is already a
3	// hard dependency, its porcelain formats are stable and documented, and this
4	// keeps dev's behaviour identical to what the user sees when they run the same
5	// command by hand.
6	package gitx
7	
8	import (
9		"bytes"
10		"context"
11		"errors"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotARepo is returned when a directory is not inside a git working tree.
18	var ErrNotARepo = errors.New("not a git repository")
19	
20	// Error carries the failing command and git's own stderr, which is almost
21	// always more useful than the exit status alone.
22	type Error struct {
23		Args   []string
24		Dir    string
25		Stderr string
26		Err    error
27	}
28	
29	func (e *Error) Error() string {
30		msg := strings.TrimSpace(e.Stderr)
31		if msg == "" {
32			msg = e.Err.Error()
33		}
34		return fmt.Sprintf("git %s: %s", strings.Join(e.Args, " "), msg)
35	}
36	
37	func (e *Error) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
38	
39	// run executes git in dir and returns trimmed stdout.
40	func run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
41		// -c core.quotepath=false keeps non-ASCII paths readable rather than
42		// octal-escaped, which matters for the Chinese-named files in these repos.
43		full := append([]string{"-c", "core.quotepath=false"}, args...)
44		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", full...)
45		cmd.Dir = dir
46		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
47		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
48		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
49		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
50			gerr := &Error{Args: args, Dir: dir, Stderr: stderr.String(), Err: err}
51			if strings.Contains(gerr.Stderr, "not a git repository") {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", dir, ErrNotARepo)
53			}
54			return "", gerr
55		}
56		return strings.TrimRight(stdout.String(), "\n"), nil
57	}
58	
59	// Run executes an arbitrary git command in dir. Exported for the few callers
60	// (park's wip commit, done's merge) that need a one-off command.
61	func Run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
62		return run(ctx, dir, args...)
63	}
64	
65	// lines splits git output into non-empty lines.
66	func lines(s string) []string {
67		if s == "" {
68			return nil
69		}
70		out := strings.Split(s, "\n")
71		filtered := out[:0]
72		for _, l := range out {
73			if l != "" {
74				filtered = append(filtered, l)
75			}
76		}
77		return filtered
78	}
79	
80	// nulLines splits NUL-delimited git output (-z forms).
81	func nulLines(s string) []string {
82		s = strings.TrimRight(s, "\x00")
83		if s == "" {
84			return nil
85		}
86		return strings.Split(s, "\x00")
87	}

228				aliases := "—"
229				if len(r.Aliases) > 0 {
230					aliases = fmt.Sprintf("%d", len(r.Aliases))
231				}
232				path := config.Contract(r.Path)
233				if r.Symlink {
234					path += " → " + config.Contract(r.RealPath)
235				}
236				t.Add(string(r.Kind), r.Name, dash(r.Branch), git, aliases, path)
237			}
238			t.Render(app.Out)
239		}
240	
241		counts := map[bootstrap.Kind]int{}
242		aliases := 0
243		clones := map[string]bool{}
244		for _, r := range repos {
245			counts[r.Kind]++
246			aliases += len(r.Aliases)
247			clones[r.CloneKey()] = true
248		}
249		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d clone(s): %d canonical, %d worktree, %d bare, %d symlink alias(es)\n",
250			len(clones), counts[bootstrap.Canonical], counts[bootstrap.Worktree], counts[bootstrap.Bare], aliases)
251		for _, w := range warnings {
252			app.warnf("scan: %v", w)
253		}
254	}
255	
256	func renderOrganizePlan(app *App, p bootstrap.OrganizePlan) {
257		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%s plan — %s layout at %s\n\n",
258			strings.ToUpper(p.Mode), p.Layout, config.Contract(p.Root))
259		if len(p.Actions) == 0 {
260			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No canonical repositories to organise.")
261			return
262		}
263		t := NewTable("STATE", "REPO", "SOURCE", "TARGET / REASON")
264		for _, a := range p.Actions {
265			last := config.Contract(a.Target)
266			if a.Reason != "" {
267				last += " — " + a.Reason
268			}
269			t.Add(string(a.State), a.Repo.Name, config.Contract(a.Source), last)
270		}
271		t.Render(app.Out)
272		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d ready, %d blocked, %d already current\n",
273			len(p.Ready()), len(p.Blocked()), countActionState(p.Actions, bootstrap.Current))
274	}
275	
276	func countActionState(actions []bootstrap.Action, state bootstrap.ActionState) int {
277		n := 0
278		for _, a := range actions {
279			if a.State == state {

281			}
282		}
283		return n
284	}

286	// blockLiveMoves adds runtime and cwd safety checks to the filesystem plan.
287	func blockLiveMoves(app *App, p *bootstrap.OrganizePlan) {
288		ctx := ctxOf()
289		sessions, _ := app.Runtime().List(ctx)
290		cwd, _ := os.Getwd()
291		for i := range p.Actions {
292			a := &p.Actions[i]
293			if a.State != bootstrap.Ready {
294				continue
295			}
296			if cwd == a.Source || strings.HasPrefix(cwd, a.Source+string(filepath.Separator)) {
297				a.State, a.Reason = bootstrap.Blocked, "the current shell is inside this repository"
298				continue
299			}
300			for _, s := range sessions {
301				for _, dir := range s.Dirs {
302					if dir == a.Source || strings.HasPrefix(dir, a.Source+string(filepath.Separator)) {
303						a.State, a.Reason = bootstrap.Blocked,
304							fmt.Sprintf("live %s session %s is inside the repository", app.Runtime().Name(), s.Handle)
305						break
306					}
307				}
308			}
309		}
310	}

312	func applyMovePlan(app *App, plan bootstrap.OrganizePlan, yes bool) error {
313		in := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
314		moved := 0
315		for _, a := range plan.Actions {
316			if a.State != bootstrap.Ready {
317				continue
318			}
319			if !yes && !confirm(app, in, fmt.Sprintf("move %s to %s", a.Repo.Name, config.Contract(a.Target))) {
320				continue
321			}
322			one := bootstrap.OrganizePlan{Mode: "move", Root: plan.Root, Layout: plan.Layout,
323				Actions: []bootstrap.Action{a}}
324			n, err := bootstrap.ApplyMoves(one)
325			if err != nil {
326				return fmt.Errorf("%d repository(s) moved before failure: %w", moved, err)
327			}
328			moved += n
329			if err := rewriteTaskRepoPaths(app, a.Source, a.Target); err != nil {
330				app.warnf("repository moved, but task paths could not be updated: %v", err)
331			}
332		}
333		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\nmoved %d repository(s) atomically\n", moved)
334		if moved > 0 {
335			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Update paths.scan_roots if the destination is not already covered, or use --config-out next time.")
336		}
337		return nil
338	}
339	
340	// rewriteTaskRepoPaths keeps task entries usable after an explicit move.
341	func rewriteTaskRepoPaths(app *App, from, to string) error {
342		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
343		if err != nil {
344			return err
345		}
346		for _, t := range tasks {
347			if t.RepoPath != from {
348				continue
349			}
350			t.RepoPath = to
351			// MovePlan refuses linked worktrees, so a task cannot have a valid
352			// worktree path under the moved clone. Clear a stale one defensively.
353			if t.WorktreePath != "" && strings.HasPrefix(t.WorktreePath, from+string(filepath.Separator)) {
354				t.WorktreePath = strings.Replace(t.WorktreePath, from, to, 1)
355			}
356			if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
357				return err
358			}
359		}
360		return nil
361	}
362	
363	func writeBootstrapConfig(app *App, path string, roots []string, projectRoot string, force bool) error {
364		path = config.Expand(path)
365		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil && !force {
366			return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists; use --force-config to overwrite", config.Contract(path))
367		}
368		contracted := contractAll(roots)
369		layout := config.Layout{
370			ScanRoots: contracted, ProjectRoot: config.Contract(projectRoot),
371			TriesRoot: app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot, WorktreeRoot: app.Cfg.Paths.WorktreeRoot,
372		}
373		body := renderStarterConfig(layout.Fallbacks())
374		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
375			return err
376		}
377		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil {
378			return err
379		}
380		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\nwrote %s with scan_roots = %v\n", config.Contract(path), contracted)
381		return nil
382	}
383	
384	type bootstrapJSON struct {
385		Roots        []string               `json:"roots"`
386		Repositories []bootstrap.Repository `json:"repositories"`
387		Warnings     []string               `json:"warnings,omitempty"`
388	}
389	
390	func renderBootstrapJSON(app *App, roots []string, repos []bootstrap.Repository, warnings []error) error {
391		out := bootstrapJSON{Roots: roots, Repositories: repos}
392		for _, w := range warnings {
393			out.Warnings = append(out.Warnings, w.Error())
394		}
395		enc := json.NewEncoder(app.Out)
396		enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
397		return enc.Encode(out)
398	}

88	// IndexPlan proposes a non-destructive symlink catalog of canonical checkouts.
89	// Linked worktrees are execution state, not projects, and are deliberately not
90	// indexed alongside repositories.
91	func IndexPlan(repos []Repository, root string, layout Layout, relative bool) OrganizePlan {
92		p := OrganizePlan{Mode: "index", Root: root, Layout: layout}
93		nameTargets := map[string][]int{}
94	
95		for _, r := range repos {
96			if r.Kind != Canonical {
97				continue
98			}
99			target := targetFor(root, layout, r)
100			a := Action{Repo: r, Source: r.RealPath, Target: target, State: Ready}
101			if relative {
102				rel, err := filepath.Rel(filepath.Dir(target), r.RealPath)
103				if err == nil {
104					a.RelativeTarget = rel
105				}
106			}
107			classifyIndexTarget(&a)
108			nameTargets[target] = append(nameTargets[target], len(p.Actions))
109			p.Actions = append(p.Actions, a)
110		}
111	
112		// A flat index cannot represent duplicate repo names. Block every claimant
113		// rather than picking one or inventing a suffix the user did not ask for.
114		for target, indices := range nameTargets {
115			if len(indices) < 2 {
116				continue
117			}
118			var sources []string
119			for _, i := range indices {
120				sources = append(sources, p.Actions[i].Source)
121			}
122			reason := "duplicate target " + target + " from: " + strings.Join(sources, ", ")
123			for _, i := range indices {
124				p.Actions[i].State, p.Actions[i].Reason = Blocked, reason
125			}
126		}
127		sortActions(p.Actions)
128		return p
129	}

131	func classifyIndexTarget(a *Action) {
132		info, err := os.Lstat(a.Target)
133		switch {
134		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist):
135			return
136		case err != nil:
137			a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, err.Error()
138			return
139		case info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0:
140			dest, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(a.Target)
141			if err != nil {
142				a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "existing broken symlink"
143				return
144			}
145			dest, _ = filepath.Abs(dest)
146			source, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(a.Source)
147			if dest == source {
148				a.State, a.Reason = Current, "already points at this repository"
149				return
150			}
151			a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "existing symlink points at "+dest
152		default:
153			a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "target already exists and is not a symlink"
154		}
155	}

157	// ApplyIndex creates the ready symlinks. It never replaces anything.
158	func ApplyIndex(plan OrganizePlan) (int, error) {
159		if plan.Mode != "index" {
160			return 0, fmt.Errorf("cannot apply %q as an index plan", plan.Mode)
161		}
162		created := 0
163		for _, a := range plan.Actions {
164			if a.State != Ready {
165				continue
166			}
167			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(a.Target), 0o755); err != nil {
168				return created, err
169			}
170			payload := a.Source
171			if a.RelativeTarget != "" {
172				payload = a.RelativeTarget
173			}
174			// os.Symlink refuses an occupied target: this is the final race-safe
175			// guard after the plan classified it.
176			if err := os.Symlink(payload, a.Target); err != nil {
177				return created, fmt.Errorf("link %s -> %s: %w", a.Target, payload, err)
178			}
179			created++
180		}
181		return created, nil
182	}
183	
184	// MovePlan proposes atomic moves of canonical checkouts into root.
185	//
186	// Moving is intentionally much stricter than indexing. It is blocked when a
187	// repo is dirty, has linked worktrees, has symlink aliases, crosses a
188	// filesystem, or would hit an occupied target. Those are exactly the states
189	// where a simple os.Rename could lose access or leave Git metadata pointing at
190	// an old path.
191	func MovePlan(ctx context.Context, repos []Repository, root string, layout Layout) OrganizePlan {
192		p := OrganizePlan{Mode: "move", Root: root, Layout: layout}
193		nameTargets := map[string][]int{}
194	
195		for _, r := range repos {
196			if r.Kind != Canonical {
197				continue
198			}
199			target := targetFor(root, layout, r)
200			a := Action{Repo: r, Source: r.Path, Target: target, State: Ready}
201	
202			switch {
203			case r.Dirty():
204				a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "repository has uncommitted changes"
205			case len(r.Aliases) > 0:
206				a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "repository has symlink aliases that would become broken"
207			case samePath(r.Path, target):
208				a.State, a.Reason = Current, "already at the target"
209			default:
210				if list, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path); err != nil {
211					a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "cannot inspect worktrees: "+err.Error()
212				} else if len(list) > 1 {
213					a.State, a.Reason = Blocked,
214						fmt.Sprintf("repository has %d linked worktree(s); remove or move those first", len(list)-1)
215				} else if info, err := os.Lstat(target); err == nil {
216					_ = info
217					a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "target already exists"
218				} else if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
219					a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, err.Error()
220				} else if !sameFilesystem(r.Path, nearestExisting(filepath.Dir(target))) {
221					a.State, a.Reason = Blocked,
222						"source and target are on different filesystems; atomic rename is impossible"
223				}
224			}
225			nameTargets[target] = append(nameTargets[target], len(p.Actions))
226			p.Actions = append(p.Actions, a)
227		}
228	
229		for target, indices := range nameTargets {
230			if len(indices) < 2 {
231				continue
232			}
233			reason := "duplicate target " + target + "; use preserve layout or separate roots"
234			for _, i := range indices {
235				p.Actions[i].State, p.Actions[i].Reason = Blocked, reason
236			}
237		}
238		sortActions(p.Actions)
239		return p
240	}
241	
242	// ApplyMoves atomically renames every ready repository. It stops on the first
243	// failure and returns how many completed — there is no rollback because a
244	// rollback can fail too, and every completed rename is itself a valid repo.
245	func ApplyMoves(plan OrganizePlan) (int, error) {
246		if plan.Mode != "move" {
247			return 0, fmt.Errorf("cannot apply %q as a move plan", plan.Mode)
248		}
249		moved := 0
250		for _, a := range plan.Actions {
251			if a.State != Ready {
252				continue
253			}
254			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(a.Target), 0o755); err != nil {
255				return moved, err
256			}
257			if err := os.Rename(a.Source, a.Target); err != nil {
258				return moved, fmt.Errorf("move %s -> %s: %w", a.Source, a.Target, err)
259			}
260			moved++
261		}
262		return moved, nil
263	}

265	func targetFor(root string, layout Layout, r Repository) string {
266		if layout == Preserve {
267			return filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(r.Relative))
268		}
269		return filepath.Join(root, r.Name)
270	}
271	
272	func samePath(a, b string) bool {
273		aAbs, _ := filepath.Abs(a)
274		bAbs, _ := filepath.Abs(b)
275		return filepath.Clean(aAbs) == filepath.Clean(bAbs)
276	}
277	
278	func nearestExisting(path string) string {
279		for {
280			if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
281				return path
282			}
283			parent := filepath.Dir(path)
284			if parent == path {
285				return path
286			}
287			path = parent
288		}
289	}
290	
291	func sortActions(actions []Action) {
292		sort.Slice(actions, func(i, j int) bool {
293			if actions[i].State != actions[j].State {
294				return actionRank(actions[i].State) < actionRank(actions[j].State)
295			}
296			return actions[i].Target < actions[j].Target
297		})
298	}
299	
300	func actionRank(s ActionState) int {
301		switch s {
302		case Ready:
303			return 0
304		case Blocked:
305			return 1
306		case Current:
307			return 2
308		}
309		return 3
310	}

1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`

126	}
127	
128	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}
141	
142	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}
174

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-27 17:04:37Z)**_

The Git inspection is exactly one synchronous `git -c core.quotepath=false rev-parse --path-format=absolute --show-toplevel --git-common-dir --is-bare-repository` process for every non-bare repository root found (bare repositories avoid it). Before that, each visited directory incurs `.git` `Lstat` and, when absent, up to three bare-marker `Stat` calls; symlinks add target `Stat`/`EvalSymlinks`, so even pre-Git discovery is proportional to the scanned tree.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/cli/completion.go
@@ -0,0 +1,239 @@
+package cli
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/help"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/ignore"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/repo"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/stats"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+const noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
+
+var completionDescriptionSanitizer = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ")
+
+// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
+// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
+// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
+// persistent flags (notably --config).
+func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
+	if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd || cmd.CalledAs() == cobra.ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd {
+		return true
+	}
+	for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
+		if cur.Name() == "completion" {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// loadCompletion prepares local providers after Cobra has parsed the command
+// line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break command and
+// flag completion entirely. Cobra invokes one custom provider per request, so
+// loading here avoids state leaking when a command tree is reused.
+func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool { return a.Load() == nil }
+
+func completeTasks(app *App, states ...task.State) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	allowed := make(map[task.State]bool, len(states))
+	for _, state := range states {
+		allowed[state] = true
+	}
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
+		for _, t := range tasks {
+			if !allowed[t.State] {
+				continue
+			}
+			description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
+			out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+// completeRepos supplies positional repository references. Commands resolve a
+// unique display name, while duplicate displays use their absolute path so the
+// selected token still identifies exactly one checkout.
+func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		if len(args) > 0 {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, false)
+	}
+}
+
+// completeRepoFlag is the same domain without a positional-argument guard: a
+// flag may legally appear after another argument, e.g. wt open branch --repo.
+func completeRepoFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, false)
+	}
+}
+
+// completeRepoNameFlag returns the name stored in tasks and stats, not the
+// Category/Name display reference used by repository commands.
+func completeRepoNameFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, true)
+	}
+}
+
+func repositoryCompletions(app *App, toComplete string, namesOnly bool) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+	if !app.loadCompletion() {
+		return nil, noFileCompletion
+	}
+	repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, noFileCompletion
+	}
+	displayCount := make(map[string]int, len(repos))
+	for _, r := range repos {
+		displayCount[r.Display()]++
+	}
+	seen := make(map[string]bool, len(repos))
+	out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
+	for _, r := range repos {
+		value := r.Display()
+		description := config.Contract(r.Path)
+		switch {
+		case namesOnly:
+			value = r.Name
+			description = r.Display() + " · " + description
+		case displayCount[value] > 1:
+			value = r.Path
+			description = r.Display() + " · " + description
+		}
+		if seen[value] {
+			continue
+		}
+		seen[value] = true
+		out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
+	}
+	return out, noFileCompletion
+}
+
+func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
+		repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
+		for _, wt := range worktrees {
+			if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
+				continue
+			}
+			description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
+			if wt.Main {
+				description += " (main checkout)"
+			}
+			out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+	if len(args) > 0 {
+		return nil, noFileCompletion
+	}
+	topics, err := help.List()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, noFileCompletion
+	}
+	out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
+	for _, topic := range topics {
+		out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
+	}
+	return out, noFileCompletion
+}
+
+func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+	used := make(map[string]bool, len(args))
+	for _, name := range args {
+		used[strings.ToLower(name)] = true
+	}
+	names := ignore.BundledNames()
+	out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
+	for _, name := range names {
+		value := strings.ToLower(name)
+		if !used[value] {
+			out = addCompletion(out, value, name+" bundled template", toComplete)
+		}
+	}
+	return out, noFileCompletion
+}
+
+func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
+		for _, value := range values {
+			out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+func runtimeCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	backends := runtime.All()
+	values := make([]string, len(backends))
+	for i, backend := range backends {
+		values[i] = backend.Name()
+	}
+	return fixedCompletions(values...)
+}
+
+func taskStateCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	values := make([]string, len(task.States))
+	for i, state := range task.States {
+		values[i] = string(state)
+	}
+	return fixedCompletions(values...)
+}
+
+func statsSourceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return fixedCompletions(
+		string(stats.SourceSession), string(stats.SourceGit), string(stats.SourceWakaTime),
+	)
+}
+
+func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
+	if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
+		panic(err)
+	}
+}
+
+func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
+	if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
+		return out
+	}
+	if description != "" {
+		description = completionDescriptionSanitizer.Replace(description)
+		value = cobra.CompletionWithDesc(value, description)
+	}
+	return append(out, value)
+}
```

3	import (

8	
9	// XDG base directories, resolved the way the spec prescribes: honor the
10	// environment variable when it holds an absolute path, otherwise fall back to
11	// the documented default under $HOME.
12	
13	func xdgDir(envVar, fallback string) string {
14		if v := os.Getenv(envVar); filepath.IsAbs(v) {
15			return v
16		}
17		return filepath.Join(home(), fallback)
18	}
19	
20	func home() string {
21		if h, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil && h != "" {
22			return h
23		}
24		return os.Getenv("HOME")
25	}
26	
27	// ConfigHome is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (default ~/.config).
28	func ConfigHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", ".config") }
29	
30	// DataHome is $XDG_DATA_HOME (default ~/.local/share).
31	func DataHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_DATA_HOME", ".local/share") }
32	
33	// CacheHome is $XDG_CACHE_HOME (default ~/.cache).
34	func CacheHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CACHE_HOME", ".cache") }
35	
36	// ConfigFile is the path dev loads its TOML configuration from.
37	func ConfigFile() string { return filepath.Join(ConfigHome(), "dev", "config.toml") }
38	
39	// Expand resolves a leading ~ and any environment variables in p, then makes
40	// the result absolute. Paths in config.toml are written by humans, so both
41	// "~/Worktrees" and "$WORK/trees" have to work.
42	func Expand(p string) string {
43		if p == "" {
44			return ""
45		}
46		p = os.ExpandEnv(p)
47		switch {
48		case p == "~":
49			p = home()
50		case strings.HasPrefix(p, "~/"):
51			p = filepath.Join(home(), p[2:])
52		}
53		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(p); err == nil {
54			return abs
55		}
56		return filepath.Clean(p)
57	}
58	
59	// Contract renders p with $HOME collapsed back to ~, for display only.
60	func Contract(p string) string {
61		h := home()
62		if h != "" && p == h {
63			return "~"
64		}
65		if h != "" && strings.HasPrefix(p, h+string(filepath.Separator)) {
66			return "~" + p[len(h):]
67		}
68		return p
69	}

+// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
+// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
+// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
+// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
+// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
+// integrations.
+func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
+	if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
+		fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
+		if err != nil || fd < 3 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
+		}
+		file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
+		if file == nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
+		}
+		if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
+	return err
 }

12	// Replacer replaces a list of strings with replacements.
13	// It is safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines.
14	type Replacer struct {
15		once   sync.Once // guards buildOnce method
16		r      replacer
17		oldnew []string
18	}
19	
20	// replacer is the interface that a replacement algorithm needs to implement.
21	type replacer interface {
22		Replace(s string) string
23		WriteString(w io.Writer, s string) (n int, err error)
24	}
25	
26	// NewReplacer returns a new [Replacer] from a list of old, new string
27	// pairs. Replacements are performed in the order they appear in the
28	// target string, without overlapping matches. The old string
29	// comparisons are done in argument order.
30	//
31	// NewReplacer panics if given an odd number of arguments.
32	func NewReplacer(oldnew ...string) *Replacer {
33		if len(oldnew)%2 == 1 {
34			panic("strings.NewReplacer: odd argument count")
35		}
36		return &Replacer{oldnew: append([]string(nil), oldnew...)}
37	}
38	
39	func (r *Replacer) buildOnce() {
40		r.r = r.build()
41		r.oldnew = nil
42	}
43	
44	func (b *Replacer) build() replacer {
45		oldnew := b.oldnew
46		if len(oldnew) == 2 && len(oldnew[0]) > 1 {
47			return makeSingleStringReplacer(oldnew[0], oldnew[1])
48		}
49	
50		allNewBytes := true
51		for i := 0; i < len(oldnew); i += 2 {
52			if len(oldnew[i]) != 1 {
53				return makeGenericReplacer(oldnew)
54			}
55			if len(oldnew[i+1]) != 1 {
56				allNewBytes = false
57			}
58		}
59	
60		if allNewBytes {
61			r := byteReplacer{}
62			for i := range r {
63				r[i] = byte(i)
64			}
65			// The first occurrence of old->new map takes precedence
66			// over the others with the same old string.
67			for i := len(oldnew) - 2; i >= 0; i -= 2 {
68				o := oldnew[i][0]
69				n := oldnew[i+1][0]
70				r[o] = n
71			}
72			return &r
73		}
74	
75		r := byteStringReplacer{toReplace: make([]string, 0, len(oldnew)/2)}
76		// The first occurrence of old->new map takes precedence
77		// over the others with the same old string.
78		for i := len(oldnew) - 2; i >= 0; i -= 2 {
79			o := oldnew[i][0]
80			n := oldnew[i+1]
81			// To avoid counting repetitions multiple times.
82			if r.replacements[o] == nil {
83				// We need to use string([]byte{o}) instead of string(o),
84				// to avoid utf8 encoding of o.
85				// E. g. byte(150) produces string of length 2.
86				r.toReplace = append(r.toReplace, string([]byte{o}))
87			}
88			r.replacements[o] = []byte(n)
89	
90		}
91		return &r
92	}
93	
94	// Replace returns a copy of s with all replacements performed.
95	func (r *Replacer) Replace(s string) string {
96		r.once.Do(r.buildOnce)
97		return r.r.Replace(s)
98	}
99	
100	// WriteString writes s to w with all replacements performed.
101	func (r *Replacer) WriteString(w io.Writer, s string) (n int, err error) {
102		r.once.Do(r.buildOnce)
103		return r.r.WriteString(w, s)
104	}

16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}

79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,

        run: |

```go
package completionbench

import (
    "strings"
    "testing"
)

var sanitizer = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ")
var sink []string

func oldFilter(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
    description = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(description)
    needle := strings.ToLower(toComplete)
    if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value+" "+description), needle) {
        return out
    }
    if description != "" {
        value += "\t" + description
    }
    return append(out, value)
}

func newFilter(out []string, value, description, needle string) []string {
    description = sanitizer.Replace(description)
    if needle != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value), needle) && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(description), needle) {
        return out
    }
    if description != "" {
        value += "\t" + description
    }
    return append(out, value)
}

func BenchmarkOld100(b *testing.B) {
    for b.Loop() {
        out := make([]string, 0, 100)
        for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
            out = oldFilter(out, "demo__feat-auth", "hot · Auth task · demo · feat/auth", "AUTH")
        }
        sink = out
    }
}

func BenchmarkNew100(b *testing.B) {
    for b.Loop() {
        out := make([]string, 0, 100)
        needle := strings.ToLower("AUTH")
        for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
            out = newFilter(out, "demo__feat-auth", "hot · Auth task · demo · feat/auth", needle)
        }
        sink = out
    }
}

```

137		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer

10	// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
11	// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
14	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
15	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  # Commands outside the navigation surface need no side channel. Besides
19	  # avoiding two subprocesses, this keeps them working when TMPDIR is stale.
20	  case "${1:-}" in
21	    __complete|__completeNoDesc|--help|-h|--version|--skill|completion|config|doctor|done|edit|gitignore|ignore|help|list|ls|park|skill|stats|status|sweep|adopt|bootstrap)
22	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
23	      return 0
24	      ;;
25	  esac
26	
27	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
28	  if ! __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"; then
29	    __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || {
30	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
31	      return 0
32	    }
33	  fi
34	
35	  __dev_status=0
36	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FD=3 command %[1]s "$@" 3>"$__dev_cd_file" || __dev_status=$?
37	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
38	    if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"; then
39	      if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
40	        builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir" || __dev_status=$?
41	      fi
42	    else
43	      __dev_status=1
44	    fi
45	  fi
46	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" || :
47	  return $__dev_status
48	}
49	`
50	
51	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
52	#   dev shell-init fish | source
53	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
54	function dev
55	    set -l __dev_command
56	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0
57	        set __dev_command $argv[1]
58	    end
59	    if contains -- $__dev_command __complete __completeNoDesc --help -h --version --skill completion config doctor done edit gitignore ignore help list ls park skill stats status sweep adopt bootstrap
60	        command %[1]s $argv
61	        return $status
62	    end
63	
64	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
65	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
66	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
67	    if test $status -ne 0
68	        set __dev_cd_file (mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
69	    end
70	    if test -z "$__dev_cd_file"
71	        command %[1]s $argv
72	        return $status
73	    end
74	
75	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FD 3
76	    command %[1]s $argv 3>"$__dev_cd_file"
77	    set -l __dev_status $status
78	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
79	        if read -z -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
80	            if test -n "$__dev_dir"

84	        else

86	        end
87	    end
88	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"

90	end

93	func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

95			Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
96			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
97			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
98	
99	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
100	"none" runtime) pass the destination through a child-only file descriptor,
101	because a child process cannot change its parent's working directory. The
102	wrapper reads that path and changes directory without evaluating shell code.

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11		"strconv"
12	
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16	)
17	
18	// App is the state shared by every command.
19	type App struct {
20		Cfg   config.Config
21		Tasks *task.Store
22	
23		Out io.Writer
24		Err io.Writer
25	
26		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
27		configPath string
28		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
29		runtimeOverride string
30		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
31		noRuntime bool
32	
33	}
34	
35	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
36	func (a *App) Load() error {
37		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
38		if err != nil {
39			return err
40		}
41		a.Cfg = cfg
42		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
43		if a.Out == nil {
44			a.Out = os.Stdout
45		}
46		if a.Err == nil {
47			a.Err = os.Stderr
48		}
49		return nil
50	}
51	
52	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
53	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
54	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
55		if a.noRuntime {
56			return runtime.None{}
57		}
58		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
59		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
60			backend = a.runtimeOverride
61		}
62		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
63		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
64			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
65		}
66		return rt
67	}
68	
69	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
70	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
71		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
72	}
73	
74	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
75	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
76		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
77	}
78	
79	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
80	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
81	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
82	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
83	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
84	// integrations.
85	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
86		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
87			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
88			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
89				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
90			}
91			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
92			if file == nil {
93				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
94			}
95			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
96				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
97			}
98			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
99				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
100			}
101			return nil
102		}
103		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
104		return err
105	}
106	
107	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
108	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }

110	
111	func TestFishShellWrapperPreservesStreamsStatusAndCD(t *testing.T) {
112		fish, err := exec.LookPath("fish")
113		if err != nil {
114			t.Skip("fish not installed")
115		}
116		fake, tmp, target := writeFakeDev(t)
117		wrapper := fmt.Sprintf(fishInit, shellQuote(fake))
118		script := wrapper + `
119	dev stream
120	set stream_status $status
121	dev fail
122	set fail_status $status
123	dev cd "$DEV_TEST_TARGET"
124	set cd_status $status
125	printf 'stream_status=%s\nfail_status=%s\ncd_status=%s\npwd=%s\n' \
126	  $stream_status $fail_status $cd_status $PWD
127	dev __complete
128	if test -n (find "$TMPDIR" -name 'dev-cd.*' -print -quit)
129	    printf 'leaked=yes\n'
130	else
131	    printf 'leaked=no\n'
132	end
133	`
134		cmd := exec.Command(fish)
135		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(script)
136		cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "TMPDIR="+tmp, "DEV_TEST_TARGET="+target)
137		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
138		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
139		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
140			t.Fatalf("run wrapper: %v\nstdout:\n%s\nstderr:\n%s", err, stdout.String(), stderr.String())
141		}
142		for _, want := range []string{
143			"streamed stdout\n", "stream_status=0\n", "fail_status=7\n",
144			"cd_status=0\n", "pwd=" + target + "\n", "completion-direct\n", "leaked=no\n",
145		} {
146			if !strings.Contains(stdout.String(), want) {
147				t.Errorf("stdout missing %q:\n%s", want, stdout.String())
148			}
149		}
150		if !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "streamed stderr\n") {
151			t.Errorf("stderr was not passed through:\n%s", stderr.String())
152		}
153	}
154	
155	func writeFakeDev(t *testing.T) (path, tmp, target string) {
156		t.Helper()
157		root := t.TempDir()
158		tmp = filepath.Join(root, "tmp")
159		target = filepath.Join(root, "target with spaces\nand a newline")
160		if err := os.MkdirAll(tmp, 0o755); err != nil {
161			t.Fatal(err)
162		}
163		if err := os.MkdirAll(target, 0o755); err != nil {
164			t.Fatal(err)
165		}
166		path = filepath.Join(root, "fake dev")
167		body := `#!/bin/sh
168	case "${1:-}" in
169	  stream)
170	    printf 'streamed stdout\n'
171	    printf 'streamed stderr\n' >&2
172	    ;;
173	  fail)
174	    exit 7
175	    ;;
176	  cd)
177	    printf '%s\0' "$2" >&3
178	    ;;
179	  __complete|__completeNoDesc)
180	    if [ -n "${DEV_SHELL_CD_FD:-}" ]; then
181	      printf 'completion-wrapped\n'
182	    else
183	      printf 'completion-direct\n'
184	    fi
185	    ;;
186	esac
187	`
188		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o755); err != nil {
189			t.Fatal(err)
190		}
191		return path, tmp, target
192	}
193

+name: Release
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags: ["v*"]
+
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+
+jobs:

+    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

+  release:
+    needs: validate
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

+    steps:

+      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
+        with:

+
+      - name: Build tagged version
+        run: |
+          make build
+          test "$(./dev --version)" = "dev version $VERSION"
+
+      - name: Create GitHub release
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+        run: |
+          if ! gh release view "$VERSION" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+            gh release create "$VERSION" --verify-tag --generate-notes --title "$VERSION"
+          fi
