1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11		"strconv"
12	
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16	)
17	
18	// App is the state shared by every command.
19	type App struct {
20		Cfg   config.Config
21		Tasks *task.Store
22	
23		Out io.Writer
24		Err io.Writer
25	
26		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
27		configPath string
28		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
29		runtimeOverride string
30		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
31		noRuntime bool
32	}
33	
34	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
35	func (a *App) Load() error {
36		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
37		if err != nil {
38			return err
39		}
40		a.Cfg = cfg
41		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
42		if a.Out == nil {
43			a.Out = os.Stdout
44		}
45		if a.Err == nil {
46			a.Err = os.Stderr
47		}
48		return nil
49	}
50	
51	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
52	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
53	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
54		if a.noRuntime {
55			return runtime.None{}
56		}
57		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
58		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
59			backend = a.runtimeOverride
60		}
61		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
62		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
63			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
64		}
65		return rt
66	}
67	
68	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
69	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
70		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
71	}
72	
73	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
74	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
76	}
77	
78	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
79	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
80	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
81	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
82	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
83	// integrations.
84	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
85		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
86			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
87			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
88				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
89			}
90			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
91			if file == nil {
92				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
93			}
94			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
95				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
96			}
97			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
98				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
99			}
100			return nil
101		}
102		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
103		return err
104	}
105	
106	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
107	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }

28	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
29	
30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
31	
32	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
33	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
34	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
35	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
36	
37	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
38	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
39	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`

10	// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
11	// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
14	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
15	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  # Commands outside the navigation surface need no side channel. Besides
19	  # avoiding two subprocesses, this keeps them working when TMPDIR is stale.
20	  case "${1:-}" in
21	    __complete|__completeNoDesc|--help|-h|--version|--skill|completion|config|doctor|done|edit|gitignore|ignore|help|list|ls|park|skill|stats|status|sweep|adopt|bootstrap)
22	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
23	      return 0
24	      ;;
25	  esac
26	
27	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
28	  if ! __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"; then
29	    __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || {
30	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
31	      return 0
32	    }
33	  fi
34	
35	  __dev_status=0
36	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FD=3 command %[1]s "$@" 3>"$__dev_cd_file" || __dev_status=$?
37	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
38	    if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"; then
39	      if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
40	        builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir" || __dev_status=$?
41	      fi
42	    else
43	      __dev_status=1
44	    fi
45	  fi
46	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" || :
47	  return $__dev_status
48	}
49	`
50	
51	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
52	#   dev shell-init fish | source
53	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
54	function dev
55	    set -l __dev_command ""
56	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0
57	        set __dev_command $argv[1]
58	    end
59	    if contains -- $__dev_command __complete __completeNoDesc --help -h --version --skill completion config doctor done edit gitignore ignore help list ls park skill stats status sweep adopt bootstrap
60	        command %[1]s $argv
61	        return $status
62	    end
63	
64	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
65	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
66	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
67	    if test $status -ne 0
68	        set __dev_cd_file (mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
69	    end
70	    if test -z "$__dev_cd_file"
71	        command %[1]s $argv
72	        return $status
73	    end
74	
75	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FD 3
76	    command %[1]s $argv 3>"$__dev_cd_file"
77	    set -l __dev_status $status
78	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
79	        if read -z -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
80	            if test -n "$__dev_dir"
81	                builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
82	                set __dev_status $status
83	            end
84	        else
85	            set __dev_status 1
86	        end
87	    end
88	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
89	    return $__dev_status
90	end
91	`

96			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
97			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
98	
99	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
100	"none" runtime) pass the destination through a child-only file descriptor,
101	because a child process cannot change its parent's working directory. The
102	wrapper reads that path and changes directory without evaluating shell code.
103	
104	Add to your shell rc file:
105	
106	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
107	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
108			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
109			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
110			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
111				self, err := os.Executable()
112				if err != nil || self == "" {
113					self = "dev"
114				}
115				switch args[0] {
116				case "bash", "zsh":
117					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
118				case "fish":
119					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
120				default:
121					return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
122				}
123				return nil
124			},
125		}
126		return cmd
127	}

 ## Install
 
+### Homebrew (macOS)
+
 ```bash
-make install     # builds, installs to ~/.local/bin, installs the agent skill
+brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli
 dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
 ```
 
-Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
+The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
+does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.
+
+### Go or source
+
+```bash
+go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@latest
+# Pin @v0.1.0 instead when you need a reproducible install.
+# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
+```
+
+For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
+them:
 
 ```bash
-eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
+mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
+dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
+dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
+dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
+```
+
+Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
+worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
+a forge or the network.
+
+Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
+
+```bash
+eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
+eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
 dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
 ```
 
-The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
-working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
-directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
+A child process cannot change its parent's working directory, so the wrapper
+passes directory changes back through a private, child-only file descriptor
+while leaving normal stdout/stderr connected to the terminal. That preserves
+the interactive TUI and normal pipe behavior.
+
+The agent skill is an explicit, optional post-install step:
 
 ```bash
+dev skill install
 dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
 ```
 
-Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
-degrade cleanly when absent.

@@ -0,0 +1,239 @@
+package cli
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/help"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/ignore"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/repo"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/stats"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+const noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
+
+var completionDescriptionSanitizer = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ")
+
+// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
+// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
+// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
+// persistent flags (notably --config).
+func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
+	if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd || cmd.CalledAs() == cobra.ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd {
+		return true
+	}
+	for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
+		if cur.Name() == "completion" {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// loadCompletion prepares local providers after Cobra has parsed the command
+// line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break command and
+// flag completion entirely. Cobra invokes one custom provider per request, so
+// loading here avoids state leaking when a command tree is reused.
+func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool { return a.Load() == nil }
+
+func completeTasks(app *App, states ...task.State) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	allowed := make(map[task.State]bool, len(states))
+	for _, state := range states {
+		allowed[state] = true
+	}
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
+		for _, t := range tasks {
+			if !allowed[t.State] {
+				continue
+			}
+			description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
+			out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+// completeRepos supplies positional repository references. Commands resolve a
+// unique display name, while duplicate displays use their absolute path so the
+// selected token still identifies exactly one checkout.
+func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		if len(args) > 0 {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, false)
+	}
+}
+
+// completeRepoFlag is the same domain without a positional-argument guard: a
+// flag may legally appear after another argument, e.g. wt open branch --repo.
+func completeRepoFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, false)
+	}
+}
+
+// completeRepoNameFlag returns the name stored in tasks and stats, not the
+// Category/Name display reference used by repository commands.
+func completeRepoNameFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, true)
+	}
+}
+
+func repositoryCompletions(app *App, toComplete string, namesOnly bool) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+	if !app.loadCompletion() {
+		return nil, noFileCompletion
+	}
+	repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, noFileCompletion
+	}
+	displayCount := make(map[string]int, len(repos))
+	for _, r := range repos {
+		displayCount[r.Display()]++
+	}
+	seen := make(map[string]bool, len(repos))
+	out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
+	for _, r := range repos {
+		value := r.Display()
+		description := config.Contract(r.Path)
+		switch {
+		case namesOnly:
+			value = r.Name
+			description = r.Display() + " · " + description
+		case displayCount[value] > 1:
+			value = r.Path
+			description = r.Display() + " · " + description
+		}
+		if seen[value] {
+			continue
+		}
+		seen[value] = true
+		out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
+	}
+	return out, noFileCompletion
+}
+
+func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
+		repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, noFileCompletion
+		}
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
+		for _, wt := range worktrees {
+			if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
+				continue
+			}
+			description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
+			if wt.Main {
+				description += " (main checkout)"
+			}
+			out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+	if len(args) > 0 {
+		return nil, noFileCompletion
+	}
+	topics, err := help.List()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, noFileCompletion
+	}
+	out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
+	for _, topic := range topics {
+		out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
+	}
+	return out, noFileCompletion
+}
+
+func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+	used := make(map[string]bool, len(args))
+	for _, name := range args {
+		used[strings.ToLower(name)] = true
+	}
+	names := ignore.BundledNames()
+	out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
+	for _, name := range names {
+		value := strings.ToLower(name)
+		if !used[value] {
+			out = addCompletion(out, value, name+" bundled template", toComplete)
+		}
+	}
+	return out, noFileCompletion
+}
+
+func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
+		for _, value := range values {
+			out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
+		}
+		return out, noFileCompletion
+	}
+}
+
+func runtimeCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	backends := runtime.All()
+	values := make([]string, len(backends))
+	for i, backend := range backends {
+		values[i] = backend.Name()
+	}
+	return fixedCompletions(values...)
+}
+
+func taskStateCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	values := make([]string, len(task.States))
+	for i, state := range task.States {
+		values[i] = string(state)
+	}
+	return fixedCompletions(values...)
+}
+
+func statsSourceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
+	return fixedCompletions(
+		string(stats.SourceSession), string(stats.SourceGit), string(stats.SourceWakaTime),
+	)
+}
+
+func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
+	if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
+		panic(err)
+	}
+}
+
+func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
+	if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
+		return out
+	}
+	if description != "" {
+		description = completionDescriptionSanitizer.Replace(description)
+		value = cobra.CompletionWithDesc(value, description)
+	}
+	return append(out, value)
+}
```

38			return err
39		}

85		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {

28	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
29	
30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
31	
32	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
33	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
34	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
35	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
36	
37	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
38	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
39	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`

41	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
42	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
43		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
44	}
45	
46	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
47	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
48	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
49	// descriptors.
50	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
51		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
52	
53		root := &cobra.Command{
54			Use:           "dev",
55			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
56			Long:          rootLong,
57			Version:       versionFromBuild(),
58			SilenceUsage:  true,
59			SilenceErrors: true,
60			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
61			// exists to answer.
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
64					out, err := skill.Render()
65					if err != nil {
66						return err
67					}
68					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
69					return nil
70				}
71				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
72				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
73				if interactive() {
74					return runTUI(app)
75				}
76				return runList(app, listOptions{})
77			},
78			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
79				if completionInvocation(cmd) {
80					return nil
81				}
82				return app.Load()
83			},
84		}
85	
86		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
87		pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
88		pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux or none")
89		pf.BoolVar(&app.noRuntime, "no-runtime", false, "do not touch any terminal multiplexer")
90		registerFlagCompletion(root, "runtime", runtimeCompletions())
91	
92		// Mirrors `herdr --skill`: the binary is the authority for its own agent
93		// skill, so a dotfiles installer can sync it without vendoring a copy.
94		root.Flags().Bool("skill", false, "print the bundled agent skill and exit")

96		root.AddCommand(

98			newTUICmd(app),
99			newStatusCmd(app),
100			newStartCmd(app),

113			newHelpTopicCmd(app),
114			newSkillCmd(app),
115			newDoctorCmd(app),

117			newConfigCmd(app),
118			newCacheCmd(app),
119			newEditCmd(app),
120		)
121		root.SetHelpCommand(&cobra.Command{Hidden: true, Use: "no-help"})
122		root.SetOut(out)
123		root.SetErr(errOut)
124		return root
125	}
126	
127	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
128	func Execute() int {
129		root := NewRootCommand()
130		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
131			msg := err.Error()
132			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
133			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
134				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
135			}
136			return 1
137		}
138		return 0
139	}

10	// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
11	// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
14	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
15	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  # Commands outside the navigation surface need no side channel. Besides
19	  # avoiding two subprocesses, this keeps them working when TMPDIR is stale.
20	  case "${1:-}" in
21	    __complete|__completeNoDesc|--help|-h|--version|--skill|completion|config|doctor|done|edit|gitignore|ignore|help|list|ls|park|skill|stats|status|sweep|adopt|bootstrap)
22	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
23	      return 0
24	      ;;
25	  esac
26	
27	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
28	  if ! __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"; then
29	    __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || {
30	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
31	      return 0
32	    }
33	  fi
34	
35	  __dev_status=0
36	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FD=3 command %[1]s "$@" 3>"$__dev_cd_file" || __dev_status=$?
37	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
38	    if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"; then
39	      if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
40	        builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir" || __dev_status=$?
41	      fi
42	    else
43	      __dev_status=1
44	    fi
45	  fi
46	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" || :
47	  return $__dev_status
48	}
49	`
50	
51	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
52	#   dev shell-init fish | source
53	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
54	function dev
55	    set -l __dev_command ""
56	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0
57	        set __dev_command $argv[1]
58	    end
59	    if contains -- $__dev_command __complete __completeNoDesc --help -h --version --skill completion config doctor done edit gitignore ignore help list ls park skill stats status sweep adopt bootstrap
60	        command %[1]s $argv
61	        return $status
62	    end
63	
64	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
65	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
66	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
67	    if test $status -ne 0
68	        set __dev_cd_file (mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
69	    end
70	    if test -z "$__dev_cd_file"
71	        command %[1]s $argv
72	        return $status
73	    end
74	
75	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FD 3
76	    command %[1]s $argv 3>"$__dev_cd_file"
77	    set -l __dev_status $status
78	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
79	        if read -z -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
80	            if test -n "$__dev_dir"
81	                builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
82	                set __dev_status $status
83	            end
84	        else
85	            set __dev_status 1
86	        end
87	    end
88	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
89	    return $__dev_status
90	end
91	`
92	
93	func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
94		cmd := &cobra.Command{
95			Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
96			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
97			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
98	
99	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
100	"none" runtime) pass the destination through a child-only file descriptor,
101	because a child process cannot change its parent's working directory. The
102	wrapper reads that path and changes directory without evaluating shell code.
103	
104	Add to your shell rc file:
105	
106	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
107	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
108			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
109			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
110			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
111				self, err := os.Executable()
112				if err != nil || self == "" {
113					self = "dev"
114				}
115				switch args[0] {
116				case "bash", "zsh":
117					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
118				case "fish":
119					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
120				default:
121					return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
122				}
123				return nil
124			},
125		}
126		return cmd
127	}

317						switch {
318						case st.Behind > 0 && st.Ahead > 0:
319							note = "diverged — rebase or merge explicitly"
320						case st.Behind > 0 && !st.Dirty():
321							note = "behind — git pull --ff-only"
322						case st.Behind > 0:
323							note = "behind, and dirty — commit first"
324						case st.Ahead > 0:
325							note = "unpushed commits"
326						}
327					}
328					t.Add(truncate(r.Name, 28), truncate(st.Branch, 24), st.Summary(), note)
329				}
330				t.Render(app.Out)
331				return nil
332			},
333		}
334		cmd.Flags().BoolVarP(&all, "all", "a", false, "every repository under the scan roots")
335		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeRepos(app)
336		return cmd
337	}

339	// repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.
340	func repoNameFromRef(ref string) string {
341		ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")
342		if i := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:"); i >= 0 {
343			return ref[i+1:]
344		}
345		return ref
346	}

348	func contractAll(paths []string) []string {
349		out := make([]string, len(paths))
350		for i, p := range paths {
351			out[i] = config.Contract(p)
352		}
353		return out
354	}

356	func newRepoRemoteCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
357		var (
358			jsonOut    bool
359			cachedOnly bool
360			limit      int
361		)
362		cmd := &cobra.Command{
363			Use:     "remote [query]",
364			Aliases: []string{"search"},
365			Short:   "List and search repositories visible through gh and glab",
366			Long: `Combine the repositories visible to the authenticated gh and glab CLIs, and
367	mark those already cloned under paths.scan_roots.
368	
369	The TUI exposes the same data in its REMOTE tab and filters it live with /.
370	This command is the non-interactive form for scripts, pipes and terminals where
371	a full-screen UI is not wanted. Use --cached for an instant, offline result;
372	the cache is private and expires according to forge.cache_ttl.`,
373			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
374			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
375				var (
376					rows []tui.RemoteRow
377					err  error
378				)
379				if cachedOnly {
380					var ok bool
381					rows, ok = cachedRemotes(ctxOf(), app)
382					if !ok {
383						return fmt.Errorf("no fresh remote cache; run `dev repo remote` once online")
384					}
385				} else {
386					rows, err = collectRemotes(ctxOf(), app, limit)
387				}
388				// Partial results are useful when one forge is authenticated and
389				// the other is not. Render them, then report the partial failure.
390				if len(rows) == 0 && err != nil {
391					return err
392				}
393				query := ""
394				if len(args) == 1 {
395					query = strings.ToLower(args[0])
396				}
397				var filtered []tui.RemoteRow
398				for _, r := range rows {
399					hay := strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
400						string(r.Repo.Forge), r.Repo.FullName, r.Repo.Description,
401						r.Repo.Visibility, r.LocalName,
402					}, " "))
403					matched := true
404					for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
405						if !strings.Contains(hay, term) {
406							matched = false
407							break
408						}
409					}
410					if matched {
411						filtered = append(filtered, r)
412					}
413				}
414	
415				if jsonOut {
416					enc := json.NewEncoder(app.Out)
417					enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
418					if encodeErr := enc.Encode(filtered); encodeErr != nil {
419						return encodeErr
420					}
421				} else {
422					t := NewTable("FORGE", "REPOSITORY", "VIS", "LOCAL", "UPDATED", "DESCRIPTION")
423					for _, r := range filtered {
424						local := "—"
425						if r.LocalPath != "" {
426							local = config.Contract(r.LocalPath)
427						}
428						updated := "—"
429						if !r.Repo.UpdatedAt.IsZero() {
430							updated = r.Repo.UpdatedAt.Format("2006-01-02")
431						}
432						t.Add(string(r.Repo.Forge), truncate(r.Repo.FullName, 36),
433							strings.ToLower(r.Repo.Visibility), truncate(local, 30), updated,
434							truncate(r.Repo.Description, 50))
435					}
436					if t.Len() == 0 {
437						fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No remote repositories match that query.")
438					} else {
439						t.Render(app.Out)
440					}
441				}
442				if err != nil {
443					app.warnf("partial remote results: %v", err)
444				}
445				return nil
446			},
447		}
448		f := cmd.Flags()
449		f.BoolVar(&jsonOut, "json", false, "emit JSON")
450		f.BoolVar(&cachedOnly, "cached", false, "use the fresh XDG cache without querying either forge")
451		f.IntVar(&limit, "limit", 0, "maximum repositories requested from each forge (default: config forge.remote_limit)")
452		return cmd
453	}

432	// renderPlan prints a provisioning plan as a table plus its warnings.
433	func renderPlan(app *App, plan wt.Plan, repoPath string) {
434		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n\n", config.Contract(repoPath))
435	
436		if len(plan.Ecosystems) == 0 {
437			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No project type detected — only gitignored files will be carried over.")
438		} else {
439			t := NewTable("PROJECT", "MANAGER", "FROM", "DEPENDENCIES", "TOOL")
440			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
441				deps := "—"
442				if len(e.DepDirs) > 0 {
443					deps = strings.Join(e.DepDirs, ", ")
444				} else {
445					deps = "global cache"
446				}
447				tool := "installed"
448				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
449					tool = "MISSING: " + e.Tool
450				}
451				t.Add(e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, deps, tool)
452			}
453			t.Render(app.Out)
454		}
455	
456		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
457		if len(plan.Steps) == 0 {
458			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to provision.")
459		} else {
460			st := NewTable("", "ACTION", "WHAT", "WHY")
461			for _, s := range plan.Steps {
462				mark := "✓"
463				if s.Skipped {
464					mark = "·"
465				}
466				st.Add(mark, string(s.Kind), truncate(s.What, 34), s.Why)
467			}
468			st.Render(app.Out)
469		}
470	
471		for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
472			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\nwarning: %s\n", w)
473		}
474		if plan.Empty() {
475			fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "\nNothing would run. If a new worktree comes up broken, add what it needs to "+
476				"worktree.post_create, or commit a .dev.toml with `dev wt plan --write`.")
477		}
478	}
479	
480	// writeRepoTemplate seeds a .dev.toml from the detected plan.
481	//
482	// Committing it is what makes a project's worktree setup reproducible: the
483	// next machine, and the next person, get the same one without having to
484	// rediscover it.
485	func writeRepoTemplate(app *App, repoPath string, plan wt.Plan, set wt.Settings) error {
486		path := filepath.Join(repoPath, wt.OverrideFilename)
487		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
488			return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists — edit it directly", config.Contract(path))
489		}
490	
491		var b strings.Builder
492		b.WriteString("# dev worktree setup for this repository.\n")
493		b.WriteString("#\n")
494		b.WriteString("# Committed on purpose: a worktree is a clean checkout, so without this a\n")
495		b.WriteString("# new one comes up with no dependencies and none of the gitignored files the\n")
496		b.WriteString("# project needs. Seeded by `dev wt plan --write`; edit freely.\n\n")
497		b.WriteString("[worktree]\n")
498	
499		b.WriteString("# Gitignored files to carry into a new worktree. Only files that are BOTH\n")
500		b.WriteString("# listed here AND gitignored are copied — a tracked file is already in the\n")
501		b.WriteString("# checkout on the correct branch.\n")
502		b.WriteString("include = [")
503		for i, inc := range set.Include {
504			if i > 0 {
505				b.WriteString(", ")
506			}
507			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%q", inc)
508		}
509		b.WriteString("]\n\n")
510	
511		if len(plan.Ecosystems) > 0 {
512			b.WriteString("# Detected in this repository:\n")
513			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
514				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "#   %-8s %-8s (%s) → %s\n", e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, e.Install)
515			}
516			b.WriteString("#\n")
517			b.WriteString("# \"auto\" runs those install commands. Replace with an explicit list if this\n")
518			b.WriteString("# project needs something else:  post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
519			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n\n")
520	
521			b.WriteString("# How each project type gets its dependencies:\n")
522			b.WriteString("#   reinstall  run the install command (correct, the default)\n")
523			b.WriteString("#   copy       duplicate the directory from the source checkout (fast)\n")
524			b.WriteString("#   link       share one directory between checkouts (fastest, risky)\n")
525			b.WriteString("#   skip       leave the worktree without dependencies\n")
526			b.WriteString("[worktree.strategies]\n")
527			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
528				switch {
529				case len(e.DepDirs) == 0:
530					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# %-8s = \"reinstall\"  # %s uses a global cache; nothing to copy\n",
531						e.Name, e.Manager)
532				case e.CopySafe:
533					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # \"copy\" is sound here and much faster\n", e.Name)
534				default:
535					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # copy/link unsupported: %s\n", e.Name, e.Hazard)
536				}
537			}
538		} else {
539			b.WriteString("# No project type detected. Add the commands a fresh checkout needs:\n")
540			b.WriteString("# post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
541			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n")
542		}
543	
544		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
545			return err
546		}
547		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "wrote %s\n", config.Contract(path))
548		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Commit it so every machine provisions worktrees the same way.")
549		return nil
550	}

272	// parseSince accepts a relative window ("30d", "6mo", "1y") or an absolute
273	// date. Relative is what people actually type; absolute is what scripts want.
274	func parseSince(s string, now time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
275		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
276		if s == "" {
277			return now.AddDate(-1, 0, 0), nil
278		}
279		if d, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", s, time.Local); err == nil {
280			return d, nil
281		}
282		var n int
283		var unit string
284		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(s, "%d%s", &n, &unit); err != nil || n <= 0 {
285			return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot parse --since %q: want 30d, 6mo, 1y or YYYY-MM-DD", s)
286		}
287		switch strings.ToLower(unit) {
288		case "d", "day", "days":
289			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n), nil
290		case "w", "week", "weeks":
291			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n*7), nil
292		case "mo", "month", "months":
293			return now.AddDate(0, -n, 0), nil
294		case "y", "yr", "year", "years":
295			return now.AddDate(-n, 0, 0), nil
296		}
297		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown unit %q in --since: want d, w, mo or y", unit)
298	}

3	`dev-cli` 目前只能從 source 以 `make install` 安裝；沒有公開 GitHub repo/tag、Homebrew formula、release 流程或已部署的 completion。CLI 實際是 Go/Cobra（不是 Tyro），而 Cobra 已自動提供 `dev completion <shell>`，但專案又另有未文件化的 `dev shell-init completion ...`，且兩者都沒有被 package manager 安裝或測試。現有 shell wrapper 以 command substitution 捕捉整段 stdout，會讓裸跑 `dev` 看不到 stdout TTY、從 TUI 退化成 plain list。
4	
5	目標是把 `dev-cli` 以 public MIT 專案從 `v0.1.0` 開始發布；macOS 可用 `brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli` 安裝 executable `dev` 並立即取得 bash/zsh/fish completion，Linux 則沿用 dotfiles 的版本鎖定 `go_tools`。同時把 `dev` 納入 dotfiles 的預設開發工具、completion cache、shell directory-change integration 與工具文件，而且不讓 Formula 在安裝期寫入使用者的 agent skill 目錄。
6	
7	# Implementation plan
8	
9	## 1. 先在 `dev-cli` 收斂 shell integration 與 completion
10	
11	- 在 `internal/cli/shell.go` 與 `internal/cli/app.go` 改寫 bash/zsh/fish wrapper：
12	  - 每次呼叫建立權限受限的暫存檔，透過 `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` 傳給真正的 `dev` process；binary 的 stdout/stderr 直接連到原 terminal，不再包在 `$()` 內。
13	  - `App.cdDirective` 在該環境變數存在時只把「原始目錄路徑」寫入檔案；wrapper 成功執行後讀取路徑並以 `cd -- "$path"` 切換，不 `eval` 檔案內容；未載入 wrapper 時保留目前輸出 shell-quoted `cd ...` 的行為。
14	  - 保留 `DEV_SHELL_INIT=1`、child exit status、即時 stdout/stderr、pipe 行為與可靠 cleanup；確認裸 `dev`/`dev tui` 仍看到真實 TTY。
15	- 移除 `newShellInitCmd` 下重複且未文件化的 `shell-init completion` 子命令；唯一公開介面採 Cobra 慣例：`dev completion bash|zsh|fish`（Cobra 現有 PowerShell 可保留，但本次安裝範圍為三種 shell）。
16	- 新增 `internal/cli/completion.go`，以可重用的 `ValidArgsFunction` / `RegisterFlagCompletionFunc` 接到既有 command constructors：
17	  - task：`park`、`resume`、`done`，重用 `internal/task.Store.List`，以穩定 task ID 為值並提供 title/state/repo/branch 描述；
18	  - repo：`start`、`repo open/sync` 與適用的 `--repo`，重用 `internal/repo.Discover`、`Repo.Display`、`resolveRepoRef`；
19	  - worktree：`wt open/rm`，重用 `repoContext`、`internal/gitx.Worktrees`，排除 detached，且 `rm` 排除 main checkout；
20	  - embedded/enum：`help` 重用 `internal/help.List`、`gitignore` 重用 `internal/ignore.BundledNames`，以及 `--runtime`、stats `--source` 等有限值；domain 值回傳 `ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp`，真正的 path arguments 維持 filesystem completion。
21	  - completion 只讀本機 config/task/repo/worktree/embedded data；不在每次 Tab 查 forge/network、collect runtime/status 或寫入 cache。
22	- 修正 `internal/cli/root.go` 的 completion 載入時機：hidden `cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd` 進入 root `PersistentPreRunE` 時，目標 command 的 persistent flags（尤其 `--config`）尚未由 `getCompletions` parse，因此先略過一般 `App.Load`，由 dynamic callback 在 flags parse 後 lazy-load。載入/探索失敗時靜默回傳無 dynamic candidates，仍保留 Cobra 的 command/flag 靜態 completion；執行 `dev completion <shell>` 產生腳本時也不依賴使用者 config。

+// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to

+func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
+	if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {

+		if err != nil || fd < 3 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)

 // repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.
 func repoNameFromRef(ref string) string {
 	ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")
 	if i := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:"); i >= 0 {
 		return ref[i+1:]
 	}
 	return ref
 }

 func pathIn(path string, roots []string) bool {
 	path = filepath.Clean(path)
 	for _, r := range roots {
 		r = filepath.Clean(r)
 		if path == r || strings.HasPrefix(path, r+string(filepath.Separator)) {
 			return true
 		}
 	}
 	return false

-Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
+The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
+does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.

+### Go or source
+
+```bash

+# Pin @v0.1.0 instead when you need a reproducible install.
+# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill

+
+For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
+them:
 
 ```bash
-eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
+mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
+dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
+dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
+dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
+```
+
+Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
+worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
+a forge or the network.
+
+Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
+
+```bash
+eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
+eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash

-The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
-working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`

+A child process cannot change its parent's working directory, so the wrapper
+passes directory changes back through a private, child-only file descriptor
+while leaving normal stdout/stderr connected to the terminal. That preserves
+the interactive TUI and normal pipe behavior.
+
+The agent skill is an explicit, optional post-install step:

+dev skill install

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  validate:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

  release:
    needs: validate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: true

      - name: Validate release tag
        shell: bash
        run: |
          [[ "$VERSION" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([.-][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]

      - name: Build tagged version
        run: |
          make build
          test "$(./dev --version)" = "dev version $VERSION"

      - name: Create GitHub release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if ! gh release view "$VERSION" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release create "$VERSION" --verify-tag --generate-notes --title "$VERSION"
          fi

26	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {

97	func repositoryCompletions(app *App, toComplete string, namesOnly bool) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
98		if !app.loadCompletion() {
99			return nil, noFileCompletion
100		}
101		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
102		if err != nil {
103			return nil, noFileCompletion
104		}
105		displayCount := make(map[string]int, len(repos))
106		for _, r := range repos {
107			displayCount[r.Display()]++
108		}
109		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(repos))
110		out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
111		for _, r := range repos {
112			value := r.Display()
113			description := config.Contract(r.Path)
114			switch {
115			case namesOnly:
116				value = r.Name
117				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
118			case displayCount[value] > 1:
119				value = r.Path
120				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
121			}
122			if seen[value] {
123				continue
124			}
125			seen[value] = true
126			out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
127		}
128		return out, noFileCompletion
129	}
130	
131	func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
132		return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
133			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
134				return nil, noFileCompletion
135			}
136			repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
137			repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
138			if err != nil {
139				return nil, noFileCompletion
140			}
141			worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
142			if err != nil {
143				return nil, noFileCompletion
144			}
145			out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
146			for _, wt := range worktrees {
147				if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
148					continue
149				}
150				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
151				if wt.Main {
152					description += " (main checkout)"
153				}
154				out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
155			}
156			return out, noFileCompletion
157		}
158	}
159	
160	func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
161		if len(args) > 0 {
162			return nil, noFileCompletion
163		}
164		topics, err := help.List()
165		if err != nil {
166			return nil, noFileCompletion
167		}
168		out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
169		for _, topic := range topics {
170			out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
171		}
172		return out, noFileCompletion
173	}
174	
175	func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
176		used := make(map[string]bool, len(args))
177		for _, name := range args {
178			used[strings.ToLower(name)] = true
179		}
180		names := ignore.BundledNames()
181		out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
182		for _, name := range names {
183			value := strings.ToLower(name)
184			if !used[value] {
185				out = addCompletion(out, value, name+" bundled template", toComplete)
186			}
187		}
188		return out, noFileCompletion
189	}
190	
191	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
192		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
193			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
194			for _, value := range values {
195				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
196			}
197			return out, noFileCompletion
198		}
199	}
200	
201	func runtimeCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
202		backends := runtime.All()
203		values := make([]string, len(backends))
204		for i, backend := range backends {
205			values[i] = backend.Name()
206		}
207		return fixedCompletions(values...)
208	}
209	
210	func taskStateCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
211		values := make([]string, len(task.States))
212		for i, state := range task.States {
213			values[i] = string(state)
214		}
215		return fixedCompletions(values...)
216	}
217	
218	func statsSourceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
219		return fixedCompletions(
220			string(stats.SourceSession), string(stats.SourceGit), string(stats.SourceWakaTime),
221		)
222	}
223	
224	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
225		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
226			panic(err)
227		}
228	}
229	
230	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
231		if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
232			return out
233		}
234		if description != "" {
235			description = completionDescriptionSanitizer.Replace(description)
236			value = cobra.CompletionWithDesc(value, description)
237		}
238		return append(out, value)
239	}

150		fake, tmp, target := writeFakeDev(t)
151		wrapper := fmt.Sprintf(fishInit, shellQuote(fake))
152		script := wrapper + `
153	dev stream
154	set stream_status $status
155	dev fail
156	set fail_status $status
157	dev cd "$DEV_TEST_TARGET"
158	set cd_status $status
159	printf 'stream_status=%s\nfail_status=%s\ncd_status=%s\npwd=%s\n' \
160	  $stream_status $fail_status $cd_status $PWD
161	dev __complete
162	if test -n (find "$TMPDIR" -name 'dev-cd.*' -print -quit)
163	    printf 'leaked=yes\n'
164	else
165	    printf 'leaked=no\n'
166	end
167	`
168		cmd := exec.Command(fish)
169		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(script)
170		cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "TMPDIR="+tmp, "DEV_TEST_TARGET="+target)
171		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
172		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
173		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
174			t.Fatalf("run wrapper: %v\nstdout:\n%s\nstderr:\n%s", err, stdout.String(), stderr.String())
175		}
176		for _, want := range []string{
177			"streamed stdout\n", "stream_status=0\n", "fail_status=7\n",
178			"cd_status=0\n", "pwd=" + target + "\n", "completion-direct\n", "leaked=no\n",
179		} {
180			if !strings.Contains(stdout.String(), want) {
181				t.Errorf("stdout missing %q:\n%s", want, stdout.String())
182			}
183		}
184		if !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "streamed stderr\n") {
185			t.Errorf("stderr was not passed through:\n%s", stderr.String())
186		}
187	}
188	
189	func writeFakeDev(t *testing.T) (path, tmp, target string) {
190		t.Helper()
191		root := t.TempDir()
192		tmp = filepath.Join(root, "tmp")
193		target = filepath.Join(root, "target with spaces\nand a newline")
194		if err := os.MkdirAll(tmp, 0o755); err != nil {
195			t.Fatal(err)
196		}
197		if err := os.MkdirAll(target, 0o755); err != nil {
198			t.Fatal(err)
199		}
200		path = filepath.Join(root, "fake dev")
201		body := `#!/bin/sh
202	case "${1:-}" in
203	  stream)
204	    printf 'streamed stdout\n'
205	    printf 'streamed stderr\n' >&2
206	    ;;
207	  fail)
208	    exit 7
209	    ;;
210	  status)
211	    printf 'status-direct\n'
212	    ;;
213	  cd)
214	    printf '%s\0' "$2" >&3
215	    ;;
216	  __complete|__completeNoDesc)
217	    if [ -n "${DEV_SHELL_CD_FD:-}" ]; then
218	      printf 'completion-wrapped\n'
219	    else
220	      printf 'completion-direct\n'
221	    fi
222	    ;;
223	esac
224	`
225		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o755); err != nil {
226			t.Fatal(err)
227		}
228		return path, tmp, target
229	}

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11		"strconv"
12	
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16	)
17	
18	// App is the state shared by every command.
19	type App struct {
20		Cfg   config.Config
21		Tasks *task.Store
22	
23		Out io.Writer
24		Err io.Writer
25	
26		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
27		configPath string
28		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
29		runtimeOverride string
30		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
31		noRuntime bool
32	}
33	
34	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
35	func (a *App) Load() error {
36		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
37		if err != nil {
38			return err
39		}
40		a.Cfg = cfg
41		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
42		if a.Out == nil {
43			a.Out = os.Stdout
44		}
45		if a.Err == nil {
46			a.Err = os.Stderr
47		}
48		return nil
49	}
50	
51	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
52	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
53	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
54		if a.noRuntime {
55			return runtime.None{}
56		}
57		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
58		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
59			backend = a.runtimeOverride
60		}
61		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
62		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
63			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
64		}
65		return rt
66	}
67	
68	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
69	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
70		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
71	}
72	
73	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
74	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
76	}
77	
78	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
79	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
80	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
81	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
82	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
83	// integrations.
84	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
85		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
86			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
87			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
88				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
89			}
90			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
91			if file == nil {
92				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
93			}
94			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
95				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
96			}
97			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
98				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
99			}
100			return nil
101		}
102		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
103		return err
104	}
105	
106	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
107	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
108

29	
30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
31	
32	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
33	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
34	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
35	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
36	
37	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
38	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
39	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`

61			// exists to answer.
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
64					out, err := skill.Render()
65					if err != nil {
66						return err
67					}
68					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
69					return nil
70				}

72				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
73				if interactive() {
74					return runTUI(app)
75				}
76				return runList(app, listOptions{})

78			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
79				if completionInvocation(cmd) {

10	// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
11	// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
14	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
15	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  # Commands outside the navigation surface need no side channel. Besides
19	  # avoiding two subprocesses, this keeps them working when TMPDIR is stale.
20	  case "${1:-}" in
21	    __complete|__completeNoDesc|--help|-h|--version|--skill|completion|config|doctor|done|edit|gitignore|ignore|help|list|ls|park|skill|stats|status|sweep|adopt|bootstrap)
22	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
23	      return 0
24	      ;;
25	  esac
26	
27	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
28	  if ! __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"; then
29	    __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || {
30	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
31	      return 0
32	    }
33	  fi
34	
35	  __dev_status=0
36	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FD=3 command %[1]s "$@" 3>"$__dev_cd_file" || __dev_status=$?
37	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
38	    if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"; then
39	      if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
40	        builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir" || __dev_status=$?
41	      fi
42	    else
43	      __dev_status=1
44	    fi
45	  fi
46	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" || :
47	  return $__dev_status
48	}
49	`
50	
51	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
52	#   dev shell-init fish | source
53	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
54	function dev
55	    set -l __dev_command ""
56	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0
57	        set __dev_command $argv[1]
58	    end
59	    if contains -- $__dev_command __complete __completeNoDesc --help -h --version --skill completion config doctor done edit gitignore ignore help list ls park skill stats status sweep adopt bootstrap
60	        command %[1]s $argv
61	        return $status
62	    end
63	
64	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
65	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
66	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
67	    if test $status -ne 0
68	        set __dev_cd_file (mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
69	    end
70	    if test -z "$__dev_cd_file"
71	        command %[1]s $argv
72	        return $status
73	    end
74	
75	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FD 3
76	    command %[1]s $argv 3>"$__dev_cd_file"
77	    set -l __dev_status $status
78	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
79	        if read -z -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
80	            if test -n "$__dev_dir"
81	                builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
82	                set __dev_status $status
83	            end
84	        else
85	            set __dev_status 1
86	        end
87	    end
88	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
89	    return $__dev_status
90	end
91	`

98	
99	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
100	"none" runtime) pass the destination through a child-only file descriptor,
101	because a child process cannot change its parent's working directory. The
102	wrapper reads that path and changes directory without evaluating shell code.
103	
104	Add to your shell rc file:
105

108			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),

114				}

118				case "fish":

81	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
82	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
83	// integrations.
84	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
85		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
86			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
87			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
88				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
89			}
90			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
91			if file == nil {
92				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
93			}
94			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
95				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
96			}
97			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
98				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
99			}
100			return nil
101		}
102		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
103		return err
104	}

107	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }

10	// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
11	// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
14	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
15	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  # Commands outside the navigation surface need no side channel. Besides
19	  # avoiding two subprocesses, this keeps them working when TMPDIR is stale.
20	  case "${1:-}" in
21	    __complete|__completeNoDesc|--help|-h|--version|--skill|completion|config|doctor|done|edit|gitignore|ignore|help|list|ls|park|skill|stats|status|sweep|adopt|bootstrap)
22	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
23	      return 0
24	      ;;
25	  esac
26	
27	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
28	  if ! __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"; then
29	    __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || {
30	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
31	      return 0
32	    }
33	  fi
34	
35	  __dev_status=0
36	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FD=3 command %[1]s "$@" 3>"$__dev_cd_file" || __dev_status=$?
37	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
38	    if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"; then
39	      if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
40	        builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir" || __dev_status=$?
41	      fi
42	    else
43	      __dev_status=1
44	    fi
45	  fi
46	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" || :
47	  return $__dev_status
48	}
49	`
50	
51	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
52	#   dev shell-init fish | source
53	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
54	function dev
55	    set -l __dev_command ""
56	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0
57	        set __dev_command $argv[1]
58	    end
59	    if contains -- $__dev_command __complete __completeNoDesc --help -h --version --skill completion config doctor done edit gitignore ignore help list ls park skill stats status sweep adopt bootstrap
60	        command %[1]s $argv
61	        return $status
62	    end
63	
64	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
65	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
66	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
67	    if test $status -ne 0
68	        set __dev_cd_file (mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
69	    end
70	    if test -z "$__dev_cd_file"
71	        command %[1]s $argv
72	        return $status
73	    end
74	
75	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FD 3
76	    command %[1]s $argv 3>"$__dev_cd_file"
77	    set -l __dev_status $status
78	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
79	        if read -z -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
80	            if test -n "$__dev_dir"
81	                builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
82	                set __dev_status $status
83	            end
84	        else
85	            set __dev_status 1
86	        end
87	    end
88	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
89	    return $__dev_status
90	end
91	`

98	
99	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
100	"none" runtime) pass the destination through a child-only file descriptor,
101	because a child process cannot change its parent's working directory. The
102	wrapper reads that path and changes directory without evaluating shell code.
103	
104	Add to your shell rc file:
105

107	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
108			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
109			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
110			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {

122				}
123				return nil

 }

 	a.Cfg = cfg

 // Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
 // --runtime and --no-runtime.
 func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
 	if a.noRuntime {
 		return runtime.None{}
 	}
 	backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
 	if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
 		backend = a.runtimeOverride
 	}
 	rt := runtime.Select(backend)
 	if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
 		return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
 	}
 	return rt
 }

 }

-// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
-// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
-// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the

+// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
+// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
+// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
+// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
+// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
+// integrations.
+func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
+	if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
+		fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
+		if err != nil || fd < 3 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
+		}
+		file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
+		if file == nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
+		}
+		if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
+	return err
 }
 
 // ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
 func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11		"strconv"
12	
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16	)
17	
18	// App is the state shared by every command.
19	type App struct {
20		Cfg   config.Config
21		Tasks *task.Store
22	
23		Out io.Writer
24		Err io.Writer
25	
26		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
27		configPath string
28		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
29		runtimeOverride string
30		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
31		noRuntime bool
32	}
33	
34	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
35	func (a *App) Load() error {
36		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
37		if err != nil {
38			return err
39		}
40		a.Cfg = cfg
41		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
42		if a.Out == nil {
43			a.Out = os.Stdout
44		}
45		if a.Err == nil {
46			a.Err = os.Stderr
47		}
48		return nil
49	}
50	
51	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
52	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
53	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
54		if a.noRuntime {
55			return runtime.None{}
56		}
57		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
58		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
59			backend = a.runtimeOverride
60		}
61		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
62		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
63			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
64		}
65		return rt
66	}
67	
68	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
69	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
70		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
71	}
72	
73	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
74	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
76	}
77	
78	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
79	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
80	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
81	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
82	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
83	// integrations.
84	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
85		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
86			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
87			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
88				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
89			}
90			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
91			if file == nil {
92				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
93			}
94			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
95				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
96			}
97			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
98				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
99			}
100			return nil
101		}
102		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
103		return err
104	}
105	
106	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
107	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
108

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}
