15	const worktreeLong = `Manage the linked worktrees dev owns.
16	
17	Who owns which worktree — the rule dev encodes, so nobody has to improvise:
18	
19	  dev            anything you might come back to tomorrow: features, fixes,
20	                 experiments, cross-machine handoffs. Placed at
21	                 paths.worktree_path, outside the repo.
22	  Claude Code    turn-scoped subagent isolation that dies with the turn, in
23	                 .claude/worktrees/ (keep that gitignored).
24	  herdr          dev does not call "herdr worktree create". It creates the
25	                 worktree with git and asks herdr to open it, so the path
26	                 policy holds on machines without herdr too.
27	
28	A new worktree is a clean checkout: no node_modules, no .venv, none of the
29	gitignored env files the project needs. dev provisions it — see the config's
30	[worktree] section, or a repo's own .dev.toml.`
31	
32	func newWorktreeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
33		cmd := &cobra.Command{
34			Use:     "wt",
35			Aliases: []string{"worktree"},
36			Short:   "Create, list, open and remove worktrees",
37			Long:    worktreeLong,
38		}
39		cmd.AddCommand(
40			newWtListCmd(app),
41			newWtCreateCmd(app),
42			newWtOpenCmd(app),
43			newWtRemoveCmd(app),
44			newWtPlanCmd(app),
45			newWtProvisionCmd(app),
46		)
47		return cmd
48	}
49	
50	// repoContext resolves the repository to operate on: an explicit --repo, else
51	// the current directory.
52	func repoContext(app *App, ref string) (path, name string, err error) {
53		ctx := ctxOf()
54		if ref != "" {
55			r, _, err := resolveRepoRef(app, ref)
56			if err != nil {
57				return "", "", err
58			}
59			return r.Path, r.Name, nil
60		}
61		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
62		if err != nil {
63			return "", "", err
64		}
65		g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd)
66		if err != nil {
67			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("%s is not a git repository — pass --repo",
68				config.Contract(cwd))
69		}
70		return g.MainRoot, g.Name, nil
71	}
72	
73	func newWtListCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
74		var repoRef string
75		cmd := &cobra.Command{
76			Use:   "list",
77			Short: "List the worktrees of a repository",
78			Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
79			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
80				ctx := ctxOf()
81				repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
82				if err != nil {
83					return err
84				}
85				list, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, repoPath)
86				if err != nil {
87					return err
88				}
89				rt := app.Runtime()
90				sessions, _ := rt.List(ctx)
91	
92				t := NewTable("", "BRANCH", "PATH", "GIT", "SESSION")
93				for _, w := range list {
94					marker := "  "
95					if w.Main {
96						marker = "★ " // the canonical checkout
97					}
98					branch := w.Branch
99					if branch == "" {
100						branch = "(detached)"
101					}
102					gitCol := "—"
103					if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, w.Path); err == nil {
104						gitCol = st.Summary()
105					}
106					switch {
107					case w.Prunable:
108						gitCol = "prunable"
109					case w.Locked:
110						gitCol = "locked"
111					}
112					session := "—"
113					for _, s := range sessions {
114						for _, d := range s.Dirs {
115							if d == w.Path {
116								session = rt.Name() + " " + s.Handle
117							}
118						}
119					}
120					t.Add(marker, branch, config.Contract(w.Path), gitCol, session)
121				}
122				t.Render(app.Out)
123				return nil
124			},
125		}
126		cmd.Flags().StringVarP(&repoRef, "repo", "r", "", "repository (default: the current one)")
127		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "repo", completeRepoFlag(app))

3	import (
4		"context"

8	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
9	type Worktree struct {
10		Path string
11		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
12		Head string
13		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
14		Branch   string
15		Detached bool
16		Bare     bool
17		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
18		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
19		Locked         bool
20		LockedReason   string
21		Prunable       bool
22		PrunableReason string
23		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
24		Main bool
25	}
26	
27	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
28	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
29	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
30		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
31		if err != nil {
32			return nil, err
33		}
34		var (
35			list []Worktree
36			cur  *Worktree
37		)
38		flush := func() {
39			if cur != nil {
40				list = append(list, *cur)
41				cur = nil
42			}
43		}
44		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
45			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
46				flush()
47				continue
48			}
49			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
50			switch key {
51			case "worktree":
52				flush()
53				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
54			case "HEAD":
55				if cur != nil {
56					cur.Head = val
57				}
58			case "branch":
59				if cur != nil {
60					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
61				}
62			case "detached":
63				if cur != nil {
64					cur.Detached = true
65				}
66			case "bare":
67				if cur != nil {
68					cur.Bare = true
69				}
70			case "locked":
71				if cur != nil {
72					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
73				}
74			case "prunable":
75				if cur != nil {
76					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
77				}
78			}
79		}
80		flush()
81		return list, nil
82	}
83	
84	// WorktreeFor finds the worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git refuses to
85	// check the same branch out twice, so at most one can match.
86	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
87		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
88		if err != nil {
89			return Worktree{}, false, err
90		}
91		for _, w := range list {
92			if w.Branch == branch {
93				return w, true, nil
94			}
95		}
96		return Worktree{}, false, nil
97	}
98	
99	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
100	//
101	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
102	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
103	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
104	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
105	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
106		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
107		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
108		if exists {
109			args = append(args, path, branch)
110		} else {
111			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
112			if base != "" {
113				args = append(args, base)
114			}
115		}
116		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
117		return err
118	}
119	
120	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
121	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
122	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
123		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
124		if force {
125			args = append(args, "--force")
126		}
127		args = append(args, path)
128		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
129		return err
130	}
131	
132	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
133	// were deleted behind git's back.
134	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
135		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
136		return err
137	}
138	
139	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
140	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
141		if branch == "" {
142			return false
143		}
144		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
145		return err == nil
146	}
147	
148	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
149	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
150		if ref == "" {
151			return false
152		}
153		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
154		return err == nil
155	}

16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}

84	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.

88	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.

31			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
32				return true
33			}
34		}
35		return false
36	}
37	
38	// loadCompletion prepares local providers after Cobra has parsed the command
39	// line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break command and
40	// flag completion entirely. Cobra invokes one custom provider per request, so
41	// loading here avoids state leaking when a command tree is reused.
42	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool { return a.Load() == nil }
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App, states ...task.State) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		allowed := make(map[task.State]bool, len(states))
46		for _, state := range states {
47			allowed[state] = true
48		}
49		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
50			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
54			if err != nil {
55				return nil, noFileCompletion
56			}
57			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
58			for _, t := range tasks {
59				if !allowed[t.State] {
60					continue
61				}
62				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch)
63				out = addCompletion(out, t.ID, description, toComplete)
64			}
65			return out, noFileCompletion
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// completeRepos supplies positional repository references. Commands resolve a
70	// unique display name, while duplicate displays use their absolute path so the
71	// selected token still identifies exactly one checkout.
72	func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
73		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
74			if len(args) > 0 {
75				return nil, noFileCompletion
76			}
77			return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, false)
78		}
79	}
80	
81	// completeRepoFlag is the same domain without a positional-argument guard: a
82	// flag may legally appear after another argument, e.g. wt open branch --repo.
83	func completeRepoFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
84		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
85			return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, false)
86		}
87	}
88	
89	// completeRepoNameFlag returns the name stored in tasks and stats, not the
90	// Category/Name display reference used by repository commands.
91	func completeRepoNameFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
92		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
93			return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, true)
94		}
95	}
96	
97	func repositoryCompletions(app *App, toComplete string, namesOnly bool) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
98		if !app.loadCompletion() {
99			return nil, noFileCompletion
100		}
101		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
102		if err != nil {
103			return nil, noFileCompletion
104		}
105		displayCount := make(map[string]int, len(repos))
106		for _, r := range repos {
107			displayCount[r.Display()]++
108		}
109		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(repos))
110		out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
111		for _, r := range repos {
112			value := r.Display()
113			description := config.Contract(r.Path)
114			switch {
115			case namesOnly:
116				value = r.Name
117				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
118			case displayCount[value] > 1:
119				value = r.Path
120				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
121			}
122			if seen[value] {
123				continue
124			}
125			seen[value] = true
126			out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
127		}
128		return out, noFileCompletion
129	}
130	
131	func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
132		return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
133			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
134				return nil, noFileCompletion
135			}
136			repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
137			repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
138			if err != nil {
139				return nil, noFileCompletion
140			}
141			worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
142			if err != nil {
143				return nil, noFileCompletion
144			}
145			out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
146			for _, wt := range worktrees {
147				if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
148					continue
149				}
150				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
151				if wt.Main {
152					description += " (main checkout)"
153				}
154				out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
155			}
156			return out, noFileCompletion
157		}
158	}
159	
160	func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
161		if len(args) > 0 {
162			return nil, noFileCompletion
163		}
164		topics, err := help.List()
165		if err != nil {
166			return nil, noFileCompletion
167		}
168		out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
169		for _, topic := range topics {
170			out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
171		}
172		return out, noFileCompletion
173	}
174	
175	func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
176		used := make(map[string]bool, len(args))
177		for _, name := range args {
178			used[strings.ToLower(name)] = true
179		}
180		names := ignore.BundledNames()
181		out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
182		for _, name := range names {
183			value := strings.ToLower(name)
184			if !used[value] {
185				out = addCompletion(out, value, name+" bundled template", toComplete)
186			}
187		}
188		return out, noFileCompletion
189	}
190	
191	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
192		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
193			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
194			for _, value := range values {
195				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
196			}
197			return out, noFileCompletion
198		}
199	}
200	
201	func runtimeCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
202		backends := runtime.All()
203		values := make([]string, len(backends))
204		for i, backend := range backends {
205			values[i] = backend.Name()
206		}
207		return fixedCompletions(values...)
208	}
209	
210	func taskStateCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
211		values := make([]string, len(task.States))
212		for i, state := range task.States {
213			values[i] = string(state)
214		}
215		return fixedCompletions(values...)
216	}
217	
218	func statsSourceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
219		return fixedCompletions(
220			string(stats.SourceSession), string(stats.SourceGit), string(stats.SourceWakaTime),
221		)
222	}
223	
224	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
225		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
226			panic(err)
227		}
228	}
229	
230	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
231		if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
232			return out
233		}
234		if description != "" {
235			description = completionDescriptionSanitizer.Replace(description)
236			value = cobra.CompletionWithDesc(value, description)
237		}
238		return append(out, value)
239	}

95				}
96				for _, want := range []string{
97					"streamed stdout\n", "stream_status=0\n", "fail_status=7\n",
98					"cd_status=0\n", "pwd=" + target + "\n", "completion-direct\n", "leaked=no\n",
99				} {

102					}
103				}

189	func writeFakeDev(t *testing.T) (path, tmp, target string) {
190		t.Helper()
191		root := t.TempDir()
192		tmp = filepath.Join(root, "tmp")
193		target = filepath.Join(root, "target with spaces\nand a newline")
194		if err := os.MkdirAll(tmp, 0o755); err != nil {
195			t.Fatal(err)
196		}
197		if err := os.MkdirAll(target, 0o755); err != nil {
198			t.Fatal(err)
199		}
200		path = filepath.Join(root, "fake dev")
201		body := `#!/bin/sh
202	case "${1:-}" in
203	  stream)
204	    printf 'streamed stdout\n'
205	    printf 'streamed stderr\n' >&2
206	    ;;
207	  fail)
208	    exit 7
209	    ;;
210	  status)
211	    printf 'status-direct\n'
212	    ;;
213	  cd)
214	    printf '%s\0' "$2" >&3
215	    ;;
216	  __complete|__completeNoDesc)
217	    if [ -n "${DEV_SHELL_CD_FD:-}" ]; then
218	      printf 'completion-wrapped\n'
219	    else
220	      printf 'completion-direct\n'
221	    fi
222	    ;;
223	esac
224	`
225		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o755); err != nil {
226			t.Fatal(err)
227		}
228		return path, tmp, target
229	}

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11		"strconv"
12	
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16	)
17	
18	// App is the state shared by every command.
19	type App struct {
20		Cfg   config.Config
21		Tasks *task.Store
22	
23		Out io.Writer
24		Err io.Writer
25	
26		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
27		configPath string
28		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
29		runtimeOverride string
30		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
31		noRuntime bool
32	}
33	
34	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
35	func (a *App) Load() error {
36		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
37		if err != nil {
38			return err
39		}
40		a.Cfg = cfg
41		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
42		if a.Out == nil {
43			a.Out = os.Stdout
44		}
45		if a.Err == nil {
46			a.Err = os.Stderr
47		}
48		return nil
49	}
50	
51	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
52	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
53	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
54		if a.noRuntime {
55			return runtime.None{}
56		}
57		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
58		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
59			backend = a.runtimeOverride
60		}
61		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
62		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
63			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
64		}
65		return rt
66	}
67	
68	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
69	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
70		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
71	}
72	
73	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
74	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
76	}
77	
78	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
79	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
80	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
81	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
82	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
83	// integrations.
84	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
85		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
86			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
87			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
88				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
89			}
90			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
91			if file == nil {
92				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
93			}
94			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
95				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
96			}
97			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
98				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
99			}
100			return nil
101		}
102		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
103		return err
104	}
105	
106	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
107	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
108

318						case st.Behind > 0 && st.Ahead > 0:
319							note = "diverged — rebase or merge explicitly"
320						case st.Behind > 0 && !st.Dirty():
321							note = "behind — git pull --ff-only"
322						case st.Behind > 0:
323							note = "behind, and dirty — commit first"
324						case st.Ahead > 0:
325							note = "unpushed commits"
326						}
327					}
328					t.Add(truncate(r.Name, 28), truncate(st.Branch, 24), st.Summary(), note)
329				}

339	// repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.
340	func repoNameFromRef(ref string) string {
341		ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")
342		if i := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:"); i >= 0 {
343			return ref[i+1:]
344		}
345		return ref
346	}
347	
348	func contractAll(paths []string) []string {
349		out := make([]string, len(paths))
350		for i, p := range paths {
351			out[i] = config.Contract(p)
352		}
353		return out
354	}

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}
283

1	// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
18	type Session struct {
19		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
20		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
21		Handle string
22		Label  string
23		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
24		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
25		// value.
26		Dirs []string
27		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
28		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
29		AgentStatus string
30		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
31		AgentSessions []string
32		Focused       bool
33	}
34	
35	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
36	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
37		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
38			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
39			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
40			// $HOME active.
41			if d == dir || strings.HasPrefix(d, dir+"/") {
42				return true
43			}
44		}
45		return false
46	}
47	
48	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
49	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
50	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
51	type Runtime interface {
52		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
53		Name() string
54		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
55		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
56		Available() bool
57		// Open makes dir live and returns a handle. Opening something already open
58		// focuses it rather than duplicating it.
59		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error)
60		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
61		// task entry.
62		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
63		// List enumerates live sessions.
64		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
65		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
66		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
67		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
68	}
69	
70	// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
71	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
72	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
73	type WorktreeOpener interface {
74		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error)
75	}
76	
77	// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
78	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
79	
80	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
81		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
82	}
83	
84	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
85	//
86	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
87	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then None.
88	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
89	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
90		herdr, tmux, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}
91		switch backend {
92		case "herdr":
93			return herdr
94		case "tmux":
95			return tmux
96		case "none":
97			return none
98		case "", "auto":
99			if herdr.Available() {
100				return herdr
101			}
102			if tmux.Available() {
103				return tmux
104			}
105			return none
106		}
107		return none
108	}
109	
110	// All returns every backend, for `dev doctor` to report on.
111	func All() []Runtime { return []Runtime{NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}} }
112	
113	// haveBinary reports whether name is on PATH.
114	func haveBinary(name string) bool {
115		_, err := exec.LookPath(name)
116		return err == nil
117	}
118

1	// Package stats records where development time actually goes, and renders it
2	// as a contribution-style heatmap.
3	//
4	// Two sources, because neither alone is honest. A sampler watches live agent
5	// and terminal sessions, which is the only way to count the hours spent
6	// reading and debugging rather than committing. Git history backfills the days
7	// before dev was installed and survives a lost database. WakaTime, when
8	// enabled, adds editor time dev cannot observe from the terminal.
9	package stats
10	
11	import (
12		"database/sql"
13		"os"
14		"path/filepath"
15		"time"
16	
17		_ "modernc.org/sqlite"
18	)
19	
20	// Source labels where a measurement came from, so double counting is visible
21	// rather than silent: the same hour can legitimately appear from the sampler
22	// and from WakaTime, and a query decides which to trust.
23	type Source string
24	
25	const (
26		// SourceSession is dev's own sampler watching live runtime sessions.
27		SourceSession Source = "session"
28		// SourceGit is derived from commit timestamps.
29		SourceGit Source = "git"
30		// SourceWakaTime is imported from the WakaTime API.
31		SourceWakaTime Source = "wakatime"
32	)
33	
34	// Store is the activity database.
35	type Store struct{ db *sql.DB }
36	
37	// Open creates or opens the database at path.
38	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
39		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
40			return nil, err
41		}
42		// A short busy timeout matters: the sampler may run from cron while an
43		// interactive `dev stats` is reading.
44		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", path+"?_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)")
45		if err != nil {
46			return nil, err
47		}
48		s := &Store{db: db}
49		if err := s.migrate(); err != nil {
50			db.Close()
51			return nil, err
52		}
53		return s, nil
54	}
55	
56	// Close releases the database.
57	func (s *Store) Close() error { return s.db.Close() }
58	
59	func (s *Store) migrate() error {
60		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
61	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS activity (
62	  day     TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- local date, YYYY-MM-DD
63	  repo    TEXT    NOT NULL,
64	  branch  TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
65	  source  TEXT    NOT NULL,
66	  seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
67	  PRIMARY KEY (day, repo, branch, source)
68	);
69	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS activity_day  ON activity(day);
70	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS activity_repo ON activity(repo);
71	
72	-- Records the last successful run of each collector, so a backfill can pick up
73	-- where it left off instead of rescanning every repo's whole history.
74	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS collector (
75	  name    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
76	  last_at INTEGER NOT NULL
77	);
78	`)
79		return err
80	}
81	
82	// Entry is one measurement.
83	type Entry struct {
84		Day     time.Time
85		Repo    string
86		Branch  string
87		Source  Source
88		Seconds int
89	}
90	
91	// Add accumulates seconds onto a (day, repo, branch, source) bucket.
92	func (s *Store) Add(entries ...Entry) error {
93		if len(entries) == 0 {
94			return nil
95		}
96		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
97		if err != nil {
98			return err
99		}
100		defer tx.Rollback()
101	
102		stmt, err := tx.Prepare(`
103	INSERT INTO activity (day, repo, branch, source, seconds) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
104	ON CONFLICT (day, repo, branch, source) DO UPDATE SET seconds = seconds + excluded.seconds`)
105		if err != nil {
106			return err
107		}
108		defer stmt.Close()
109	
110		for _, e := range entries {
111			if e.Seconds <= 0 || e.Repo == "" {
112				continue
113			}
114			if _, err := stmt.Exec(e.Day.Format(dayFormat), e.Repo, e.Branch, string(e.Source), e.Seconds); err != nil {
115				return err
116			}
117		}
118		return tx.Commit()
119	}
120	
121	// Set replaces a bucket rather than accumulating. Used by importers that are
122	// re-runnable: WakaTime reports the same day's total again on every import, so
123	// adding would inflate it.
124	func (s *Store) Set(entries ...Entry) error {
125		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
126		if err != nil {
127			return err
128		}
129		defer tx.Rollback()
130	
131		stmt, err := tx.Prepare(`
132	INSERT INTO activity (day, repo, branch, source, seconds) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
133	ON CONFLICT (day, repo, branch, source) DO UPDATE SET seconds = excluded.seconds`)
134		if err != nil {
135			return err
136		}
137		defer stmt.Close()
138	
139		for _, e := range entries {
140			if e.Repo == "" {
141				continue
142			}
143			if _, err := stmt.Exec(e.Day.Format(dayFormat), e.Repo, e.Branch, string(e.Source), e.Seconds); err != nil {
144				return err
145			}
146		}
147		return tx.Commit()
148	}
149	
150	const dayFormat = "2006-01-02"
151	
152	// Query narrows a report.
153	type Query struct {
154		Since time.Time
155		Until time.Time
156		Repo  string
157		// ExactRepo uses equality rather than the report-friendly substring match.
158		// Per-repo TUI panels set it so "api" does not include "my-api".
159		ExactRepo bool
160		// Sources limits which collectors count. Empty means all of them.
161		Sources []Source
162	}
163	
164	func (q Query) where() (string, []any) {
165		clause := "WHERE day >= ? AND day <= ?"
166		args := []any{q.Since.Format(dayFormat), q.Until.Format(dayFormat)}
167		if q.Repo != "" {
168			if q.ExactRepo {
169				clause += " AND repo = ?"
170				args = append(args, q.Repo)
171			} else {
172				clause += " AND repo LIKE ?"
173				args = append(args, "%"+q.Repo+"%")
174			}
175		}
176		if len(q.Sources) > 0 {
177			clause += " AND source IN (" + placeholders(len(q.Sources)) + ")"
178			for _, s := range q.Sources {
179				args = append(args, string(s))
180			}
181		}
182		return clause, args
183	}
184	
185	func placeholders(n int) string {
186		if n == 0 {
187			return ""
188		}
189		out := make([]byte, 0, n*2-1)
190		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
191			if i > 0 {
192				out = append(out, ',')
193			}
194			out = append(out, '?')
195		}
196		return string(out)
197	}
198	
199	// DayTotals returns seconds per calendar day.
200	func (s *Store) DayTotals(q Query) (map[string]int, error) {
201		clause, args := q.where()
202		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT day, SUM(seconds) FROM activity `+clause+` GROUP BY day`, args...)
203		if err != nil {
204			return nil, err
205		}
206		defer rows.Close()
207	
208		out := map[string]int{}
209		for rows.Next() {
210			var day string
211			var secs int
212			if err := rows.Scan(&day, &secs); err != nil {
213				return nil, err
214			}
215			out[day] = secs
216		}
217		return out, rows.Err()
218	}
219	
220	// RepoTotal is one row of the per-repo breakdown.
221	type RepoTotal struct {
222		Repo    string
223		Seconds int
224		Days    int
225		Last    string
226	}
227	
228	// RepoTotals returns seconds per repository, busiest first.
229	func (s *Store) RepoTotals(q Query) ([]RepoTotal, error) {
230		clause, args := q.where()
231		rows, err := s.db.Query(`
232	SELECT repo, SUM(seconds) AS secs, COUNT(DISTINCT day) AS days, MAX(day)
233	FROM activity `+clause+`
234	GROUP BY repo ORDER BY secs DESC`, args...)
235		if err != nil {
236			return nil, err
237		}
238		defer rows.Close()
239	
240		var out []RepoTotal
241		for rows.Next() {
242			var r RepoTotal
243			if err := rows.Scan(&r.Repo, &r.Seconds, &r.Days, &r.Last); err != nil {
244				return nil, err
245			}
246			out = append(out, r)
247		}
248		return out, rows.Err()
249	}
250	
251	// RepoDayTotals returns per-day seconds for one repository, for a per-repo
252	// heatmap.
253	func (s *Store) RepoDayTotals(repo string, q Query) (map[string]int, error) {
254		q.Repo = repo
255		return s.DayTotals(q)
256	}
257	
258	// MarkCollected records that a collector ran, so incremental runs know their
259	// starting point.
260	func (s *Store) MarkCollected(name string, at time.Time) error {
261		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
262	INSERT INTO collector (name, last_at) VALUES (?, ?)
263	ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET last_at = excluded.last_at`, name, at.Unix())
264		return err
265	}
266	
267	// LastCollected reports when a collector last ran, zero when never.
268	func (s *Store) LastCollected(name string) time.Time {
269		var unix int64
270		if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT last_at FROM collector WHERE name = ?`, name).Scan(&unix); err != nil {
271			return time.Time{}
272		}
273		return time.Unix(unix, 0)
274	}
275	
276	// Empty reports whether anything has been recorded yet, so the CLI can explain
277	// how to start collecting instead of printing a blank chart.
278	func (s *Store) Empty() bool {
279		var n int
280		if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activity`).Scan(&n); err != nil {
281			return true
282		}
283		return n == 0
284	}
285	
286	// Path is where the database lives inside a state directory.
287	func Path(stateDir string) string { return filepath.Join(stateDir, "stats.db") }
288	
289	// ClearQuery selects durable activity rows to delete. Repo is an exact name —
290	// deletion must not use the fuzzy LIKE semantics a report does.
291	type ClearQuery struct {
292		Repo    string
293		Sources []Source
294	}
295	
296	// Clear deletes matching activity and returns the number of rows removed.
297	// With an empty query it clears all activity and collector checkpoints.
298	func (s *Store) Clear(q ClearQuery) (int64, error) {
299		clause := ""
300		var args []any
301		if q.Repo != "" {
302			clause = " WHERE repo = ?"
303			args = append(args, q.Repo)
304		}
305		if len(q.Sources) > 0 {
306			if clause == "" {
307				clause = " WHERE "
308			} else {
309				clause += " AND "
310			}
311			clause += "source IN (" + placeholders(len(q.Sources)) + ")"
312			for _, source := range q.Sources {
313				args = append(args, string(source))
314			}
315		}
316		result, err := s.db.Exec("DELETE FROM activity"+clause, args...)
317		if err != nil {
318			return 0, err
319		}
320		if q.Repo == "" && len(q.Sources) == 0 {
321			if _, err := s.db.Exec("DELETE FROM collector"); err != nil {
322				return 0, err
323			}
324		}
325		return result.RowsAffected()
326	}

```text
1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123	
124		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
125		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
126	}
127	
128	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}
141	
142	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}

50	// repoContext resolves the repository to operate on: an explicit --repo, else
51	// the current directory.
52	func repoContext(app *App, ref string) (path, name string, err error) {
53		ctx := ctxOf()
54		if ref != "" {
55			r, _, err := resolveRepoRef(app, ref)
56			if err != nil {
57				return "", "", err
58			}
59			return r.Path, r.Name, nil
60		}
61		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
62		if err != nil {
63			return "", "", err
64		}
65		g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd)
66		if err != nil {
67			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("%s is not a git repository — pass --repo",
68				config.Contract(cwd))
69		}
70		return g.MainRoot, g.Name, nil
71	}

245	func newWtRemoveCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
246		var (
247			repoRef string
248			force   bool
249		)
250		cmd := &cobra.Command{
251			Use:     "rm <branch>",
252			Aliases: []string{"remove"},
253			Short:   "Remove a worktree checkout (never the branch)",
254			Long: `Remove a worktree's checkout.
255	
256	The branch is never deleted: removing a checkout and abandoning a change
257	stream are different decisions, and conflating them is how work gets lost.
258	A checkout with uncommitted changes needs an explicit --force.`,
259			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
260			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
261				ctx := ctxOf()
262				repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
263				if err != nil {
264					return err
265				}
266				w, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, repoPath, args[0])
267				if err != nil {
268					return err
269				}
270				if !ok {
271					return fmt.Errorf("no worktree for branch %q", args[0])
272				}
273				if w.Main {
274					return fmt.Errorf("%s is the main checkout, not a linked worktree", config.Contract(w.Path))
275				}
276				if dirty, st, err := wt.DirtyCheck(ctx, w.Path); err == nil && dirty && !force {
277					return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes (%s).\n"+
278						"Commit them, or re-run with --force to discard them",
279						config.Contract(w.Path), st.Summary())
280				}
281	
282				// Close a runtime session pointing at the checkout first, so the
283				// multiplexer is not left on a deleted directory.
284				rt := app.Runtime()
285				var handle string
286				if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
287					for _, s := range sessions {
288						for _, d := range s.Dirs {
289							if d == w.Path {
290								handle = s.Handle
291							}
292						}
293					}
294				}
295				m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
296				if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
297					RepoPath: repoPath, Path: w.Path, Force: force, RuntimeHandle: handle,
298				}); err != nil {
299					return err
300				}
301				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "removed %s (branch %s kept)\n", config.Contract(w.Path), w.Branch)
302	
303				// Keep the registry honest about what is now gone.
304				if t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(w.Path); err == nil {
305					t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = "", ""
306					if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err == nil {
307						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "task %s updated — the branch still has the work\n", t.ID)
308					}
309				}
310				return nil
311			},
312		}
313		f := cmd.Flags()
314		f.StringVarP(&repoRef, "repo", "r", "", "repository (default: the current one)")
315		f.BoolVarP(&force, "force", "f", false, "remove even with uncommitted changes")
316		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "repo", completeRepoFlag(app))
317		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeWorktrees(app, false)
318		return cmd
319	}

328	Copies the gitignored files, applies the dependency strategy and runs the

333			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
334			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {

337				if err != nil {
338					return err
339				}
340				if len(args) == 1 {
341					target = config.Expand(args[0])
342				}
343				g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, target)
344				if err != nil {
345					return err
346				}
347	
348				set := wt.SettingsFor(app.Cfg, g.MainRoot)
349				plan := wt.BuildPlan(ctx, set, g.MainRoot)
350				if dryRun {
351					renderPlan(app, plan, g.MainRoot)
352					return nil
353				}
354	
355				p := &wt.Provisioner{
356					Settings: set,
357					Timeout:  app.Cfg.Worktree.ProvisionTimeout.Duration,
358					Log:      app.Err,
359				}
360				res, err := p.Apply(ctx, plan, g.MainRoot, g.Root)
361				if err != nil {
362					return err
363				}
364				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "provisioned %s\n", config.Contract(g.Root))
365				if len(res.Copied) > 0 {
366					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  copied   %s\n", strings.Join(res.Copied, ", "))
367				}
368				if len(res.Linked) > 0 {
369					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  linked   %s\n", strings.Join(res.Linked, ", "))
370				}
371				if len(res.Ran) > 0 {
372					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  ran      %s\n", strings.Join(res.Ran, ", "))
373				}
374				for _, s := range res.Skipped {
375					fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "  skipped  %s\n", s)
376				}
377				for _, e := range res.Failures {
378					app.warnf("%v", e)
379				}
380				return nil
381			},
382		}
383		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&dryRun, "dry-run", false, "show the plan instead of applying it")
384		return cmd

432	// renderPlan prints a provisioning plan as a table plus its warnings.
433	func renderPlan(app *App, plan wt.Plan, repoPath string) {
434		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n\n", config.Contract(repoPath))
435	
436		if len(plan.Ecosystems) == 0 {
437			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No project type detected — only gitignored files will be carried over.")
438		} else {
439			t := NewTable("PROJECT", "MANAGER", "FROM", "DEPENDENCIES", "TOOL")
440			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
441				deps := "—"
442				if len(e.DepDirs) > 0 {
443					deps = strings.Join(e.DepDirs, ", ")
444				} else {
445					deps = "global cache"
446				}
447				tool := "installed"
448				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
449					tool = "MISSING: " + e.Tool
450				}
451				t.Add(e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, deps, tool)
452			}
453			t.Render(app.Out)
454		}
455	
456		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
457		if len(plan.Steps) == 0 {
458			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to provision.")
459		} else {
460			st := NewTable("", "ACTION", "WHAT", "WHY")

211	// checkoutOf is where a task's code lives right now.
212	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
213		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
214			return t.WorktreePath
215		}
216		return t.RepoPath
217	}
218	
219	// annotate pushes the task's state and next action into the runtime as
220	// display-only metadata, so a sidebar can show why a session is open without
221	// anyone having to ask dev.
222	//
223	// For herdr this lands as workspace metadata tokens. A token only renders if
224	// the sidebar row layout in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g.
225	//
226	//	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
227	//	rows = [["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"], ["branch", "git_status"], ["$next"]]
228	//
229	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds and shows nothing,
230	// which is why dev never treats a failure here as an error.
231	func annotate(app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, t *task.Task) {
232		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
233			return
234		}
235		kv := map[string]string{
236			"stage": t.State.Label(),
237			"next":  t.Next,
238		}
239		if err := rt.Annotate(ctxOf(), t.RuntimeHandle, kv); err != nil {
240			app.warnf("could not annotate the runtime session: %v", err)
```

14	func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			noProvision bool
17			fetch       bool
18			force       bool
19		)
20		cmd := &cobra.Command{
21			Use:   "resume <task>",
22			Short: "Pick a task back up, rebuilding whatever is missing",
23			Long: `Make a parked task hot again.
24	
25	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
26	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
27	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
28	identity.
29	
30	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
33			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
34			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
35				ctx := ctxOf()
36				t, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
37				if err != nil {
38					return err
39				}
40	
41				host := config.Hostname()
42				if !t.OwnedBy(host) && !force {
43					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is owned by %s.\n"+
44						"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
45						t.ID, t.Owner)
46				}
47	
48				if fetch {
49					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "fetch", "--prune", "origin"); err != nil {
50						app.warnf("fetch failed: %v", err)
51					}
52				}
53	
54				rt := app.Runtime()
55				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
56				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
57	
58				switch mode {
59				case task.ModeWorktree:
60					_, statErr := os.Stat(checkout)
61					// Rebuild the worktree when it is gone — the cold-to-hot path.
62					if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
63						base := t.Base
64						// Prefer the published branch: a cold task's work lives on
65						// the remote, and a stale local ref could drop it.
66						if remote := "origin/" + t.Branch; gitx.RefExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, remote) {
67							base = remote
68						}
69						m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
70						res, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
71							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, RepoName: t.Repo, Branch: t.Branch,
72							Base: base, Label: t.Title(), NoProvision: noProvision,
73						})
74						if err != nil {
75							var exists *wt.ErrExists
76							if asError(err, &exists) {
77								t.WorktreePath = exists.Path
78							} else {
79								return err
80							}
81						} else {
82							t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = res.Path, res.RuntimeHandle
83							reportProvision(app, res)
84							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebuilt    %s\n", config.Contract(res.Path))
85						}
86						checkout = t.WorktreePath
87					}
88	
89				case task.ModeBranch:
90					checkout = t.RepoPath
91					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
92					if err != nil {
93						return err
94					}
95					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
96						if st.Dirty() {
97							return fmt.Errorf("cannot switch the canonical checkout from %s to %s: %s",
98								st.Branch, t.Branch, st.Breakdown())
99						}
100						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "switch", t.Branch); err != nil {
101							return err
102						}
103					}
104	
105				case task.ModeDirect:
106					checkout = t.RepoPath
107					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
108					if err != nil {
109						return err
110					}
111					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
112						return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s tracks %s, but the canonical checkout is on %s; "+
113							"switch back explicitly or start a worktree task", t.Title(), t.Branch, st.Branch)
114					}
115				}
116				if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
117					handle, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, checkout, t.Title())
118					if err != nil {
119						app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
120					}
121					if rt.Name() != "none" {
122						t.RuntimeHandle = handle
123					}
124				}
125	
126				t.State = task.Hot
127				t.Owner = host
128				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
129					return err
130				}
131				annotate(app, rt, t)
132	
133				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s  %s on %s (%s)\n",
134					task.Hot.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, mode)
135				if t.Next != "" {
136					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   next      %s\n", t.Next)
137				}
138				if t.AgentSession != "" {
139					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   agent     %s (resumable)\n", t.AgentSession)
140				}
141				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout); err == nil {
142					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   git       %s\n", st.Summary())
143					if st.Behind > 0 {
144						app.warnf("branch is %d behind upstream — `git pull --ff-only` before you start", st.Behind)
145					}
146				}
147				if rt.Name() == "none" {
148					return app.cdDirective(checkout)
149				}
150				return nil
151			},
152		}

155		f.BoolVar(&fetch, "fetch", true, "fetch from origin first")
156		f.BoolVar(&force, "force", false, "take ownership of a task owned by another machine")
157		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app, task.Warm, task.Cold)
158		return cmd
159	}

432	// renderPlan prints a provisioning plan as a table plus its warnings.
433	func renderPlan(app *App, plan wt.Plan, repoPath string) {
434		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n\n", config.Contract(repoPath))
435	
436		if len(plan.Ecosystems) == 0 {
437			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No project type detected — only gitignored files will be carried over.")
438		} else {
439			t := NewTable("PROJECT", "MANAGER", "FROM", "DEPENDENCIES", "TOOL")
440			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
441				deps := "—"
442				if len(e.DepDirs) > 0 {
443					deps = strings.Join(e.DepDirs, ", ")
444				} else {
445					deps = "global cache"
446				}
447				tool := "installed"
448				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
449					tool = "MISSING: " + e.Tool
450				}
451				t.Add(e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, deps, tool)
452			}
453			t.Render(app.Out)
454		}
455	
456		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
457		if len(plan.Steps) == 0 {
458			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to provision.")
459		} else {
460			st := NewTable("", "ACTION", "WHAT", "WHY")
461			for _, s := range plan.Steps {
462				mark := "✓"
463				if s.Skipped {
464					mark = "·"
465				}
466				st.Add(mark, string(s.Kind), truncate(s.What, 34), s.Why)
467			}
468			st.Render(app.Out)
469		}
470	
471		for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
472			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\nwarning: %s\n", w)
473		}
474		if plan.Empty() {
475			fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "\nNothing would run. If a new worktree comes up broken, add what it needs to "+
476				"worktree.post_create, or commit a .dev.toml with `dev wt plan --write`.")
477		}
478	}
479	
480	// writeRepoTemplate seeds a .dev.toml from the detected plan.
481	//
482	// Committing it is what makes a project's worktree setup reproducible: the
483	// next machine, and the next person, get the same one without having to
484	// rediscover it.
485	func writeRepoTemplate(app *App, repoPath string, plan wt.Plan, set wt.Settings) error {
486		path := filepath.Join(repoPath, wt.OverrideFilename)
487		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
488			return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists — edit it directly", config.Contract(path))
489		}
490	
491		var b strings.Builder
492		b.WriteString("# dev worktree setup for this repository.\n")
493		b.WriteString("#\n")
494		b.WriteString("# Committed on purpose: a worktree is a clean checkout, so without this a\n")
495		b.WriteString("# new one comes up with no dependencies and none of the gitignored files the\n")
496		b.WriteString("# project needs. Seeded by `dev wt plan --write`; edit freely.\n\n")
497		b.WriteString("[worktree]\n")
498	
499		b.WriteString("# Gitignored files to carry into a new worktree. Only files that are BOTH\n")
500		b.WriteString("# listed here AND gitignored are copied — a tracked file is already in the\n")
501		b.WriteString("# checkout on the correct branch.\n")
502		b.WriteString("include = [")
503		for i, inc := range set.Include {
504			if i > 0 {
505				b.WriteString(", ")
506			}
507			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%q", inc)
508		}
509		b.WriteString("]\n\n")
510	
511		if len(plan.Ecosystems) > 0 {
512			b.WriteString("# Detected in this repository:\n")
513			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
514				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "#   %-8s %-8s (%s) → %s\n", e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, e.Install)
515			}
516			b.WriteString("#\n")
517			b.WriteString("# \"auto\" runs those install commands. Replace with an explicit list if this\n")
518			b.WriteString("# project needs something else:  post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
519			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n\n")
520	
521			b.WriteString("# How each project type gets its dependencies:\n")
522			b.WriteString("#   reinstall  run the install command (correct, the default)\n")
523			b.WriteString("#   copy       duplicate the directory from the source checkout (fast)\n")
524			b.WriteString("#   link       share one directory between checkouts (fastest, risky)\n")
525			b.WriteString("#   skip       leave the worktree without dependencies\n")
526			b.WriteString("[worktree.strategies]\n")
527			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
528				switch {
529				case len(e.DepDirs) == 0:
530					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# %-8s = \"reinstall\"  # %s uses a global cache; nothing to copy\n",
531						e.Name, e.Manager)
532				case e.CopySafe:
533					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # \"copy\" is sound here and much faster\n", e.Name)
534				default:
535					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # copy/link unsupported: %s\n", e.Name, e.Hazard)
536				}
537			}
538		} else {
539			b.WriteString("# No project type detected. Add the commands a fresh checkout needs:\n")
540			b.WriteString("# post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
541			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n")
542		}
543	
544		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
545			return err
546		}
547		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "wrote %s\n", config.Contract(path))
548		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Commit it so every machine provisions worktrees the same way.")
549		return nil
550	}

339	// repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.
