```text
18	func newTryCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
19		var (
20			list  bool
21			clone string
22			noGit bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "try [name]",
26			Short: "Make a dated scratch directory for an experiment",
27			Long: `Create (or jump to) a dated experiment directory under paths.tries_root.
28	
29	Experiments need a home that is neither /tmp (where they vanish) nor your
30	projects directory (where they accumulate as clutter you are afraid to delete).
31	A try is date-prefixed, disposable by default, and promotable with
32	"dev graduate" when it turns out to be real.
33	
34	  dev try                    list what is there
35	  dev try redis-streams      jump to a matching try, or create 2026-08-27-redis-streams
36	  dev try --clone <url>      clone a repo into a dated try directory`,
37			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
38			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
39				ctx := ctxOf()
40				root := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot)
41				if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o755); err != nil {
42					return err
43				}
44	
45				if list || (len(args) == 0 && clone == "") {
46					return listTries(app, root)
47				}
48	
49				name := ""
50				if len(args) == 1 {
51					name = args[0]
52				}
53				if clone != "" && name == "" {
54					name = repoNameFromRef(clone)
55				}
56				slug := config.Slug(strings.ReplaceAll(name, " ", "-"))
57	
58				// An existing try wins over creating a near-duplicate: the whole
59				// point is to stop accumulating test/test2/test-actually.
60				if match := findTry(root, slug); match != "" && clone == "" {
61					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(match))
62					return openOrCD(app, ctx, match, filepath.Base(match))
63				}
64	
65				dir := filepath.Join(root, time.Now().Format("2006-01-02")+"-"+slug)
66				if _, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil {
67					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(dir))
68					return openOrCD(app, ctx, dir, filepath.Base(dir))
69				}
70	
71				if clone != "" {
72					url := clone
73					if k := forge.FromURL(clone); k != forge.Unknown {
74						if f, err := forge.For(k); err == nil {
75							url = f.CloneURL(clone)
76						}
77					}
78					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, root, "clone", url, dir); err != nil {
79						return err
80					}
81				} else {
82					if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
83						return err
84					}
85					if !noGit {
86						// A try with git history can be graduated without losing
87						// the path that got there, which is most of its value.
88						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "init", "-b", "main"); err != nil {
89							app.warnf("could not git init: %v", err)
90						}
91					}
92				}
93				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(dir))
94				return openOrCD(app, ctx, dir, filepath.Base(dir))
95			},
96		}
97		f := cmd.Flags()
98		f.BoolVarP(&list, "list", "l", false, "list existing tries")
99		f.StringVar(&clone, "clone", "", "clone a repository into the new try")
100		f.BoolVar(&noGit, "no-git", false, "do not git init the new directory")
101		return cmd
102	}
103	
104	// tryEntry is one scratch directory with the facts needed to rank it.
105	type tryEntry struct {
106		name     string
107		path     string
108		modified time.Time
109		isRepo   bool
110		dirty    bool
111	}
112	
113	func listTries(app *App, root string) error {
114		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
115		if err != nil {
116			return err
117		}
118		var tries []tryEntry
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			if !e.IsDir() || strings.HasPrefix(e.Name(), ".") {
121				continue
122			}
123			info, err := e.Info()
124			if err != nil {
125				continue
126			}
127			path := filepath.Join(root, e.Name())
128			t := tryEntry{name: e.Name(), path: path, modified: info.ModTime()}
129			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
130				t.isRepo = true
131				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctxOf(), path); err == nil {
132					t.dirty = st.Dirty()
133				}
134			}
135			tries = append(tries, t)
136		}
137		if len(tries) == 0 {
138			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "No tries yet under %s\n", config.Contract(root))
139			return nil
140		}
141		// Most recently touched first: "what was I doing yesterday?" is the
142		// question a list of experiments actually gets asked.
143		sort.Slice(tries, func(i, j int) bool { return tries[i].modified.After(tries[j].modified) })
144	
145		tbl := NewTable("TRY", "AGE", "GIT")
146		for _, t := range tries {
147			gitCol := "—"
148			switch {
149			case t.isRepo && t.dirty:
150				gitCol = "repo ●"
151			case t.isRepo:
152				gitCol = "repo"
153			}
154			tbl.Add(truncate(t.name, 44), humanAge(time.Since(t.modified)), gitCol)
155		}
156		tbl.Render(app.Out)
157		fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\n%d tries under %s — promote one with `dev graduate <try>`\n",
158			len(tries), config.Contract(root))
159		return nil
160	}
161	
162	// findTry locates an existing try whose name contains the slug, preferring the
163	// most recent when several match.
164	func findTry(root, slug string) string {
165		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
166		if err != nil {
167			return ""
168		}
169		var best string
170		var bestTime time.Time
171		for _, e := range entries {
172			if !e.IsDir() || !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(e.Name()), strings.ToLower(slug)) {
173				continue
174			}
175			info, err := e.Info()
176			if err != nil {
177				continue
178			}
179			if info.ModTime().After(bestTime) {
180				best, bestTime = filepath.Join(root, e.Name()), info.ModTime()
181			}
182		}
183		return best
184	}
185	
186	func openOrCD(app *App, ctx context.Context, dir, label string) error {
187		rt := app.Runtime()
188		if rt.Name() == "none" {
189			return app.cdDirective(dir)
190		}
191		if _, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, dir, label); err != nil {
192			app.warnf("could not open a session: %v", err)
193		}
194		return nil
195	}
```

```text
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"os"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
11	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
12	type Repo struct {
13		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
14		Root string
15		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
16		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
17		GitCommonDir string
18		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
19		Name string
20		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
21		// the main checkout.
22		IsLinkedWorktree bool
23		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
24		MainRoot string
25		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
26		Bare bool
27	}
28	
29	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
30	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
31	
32	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
33	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
34		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
35		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
36		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
37			"rev-parse",
38			"--path-format=absolute",
39			"--show-toplevel",
40			"--git-common-dir",
41			"--is-bare-repository",
42		)
43		if err != nil {
44			return Repo{}, err
45		}
46		f := lines(out)
47		r := Repo{}
48		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
49		switch len(f) {
50		case 3:
51			r.Root = f[0]
52			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
53			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
54		case 2:
55			r.GitCommonDir = f[0]
56			r.Bare = f[1] == "true"
57		default:
58			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
59		}
60	
61		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
62		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
63		if r.Bare {
64			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
65		} else {
66			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
67		}
68		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.Root != r.MainRoot
69		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
70		if r.Bare {
71			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
72			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
73			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
74				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
75			}
76		}
77		return r, nil
78	}
79	
80	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
81	// a full Discover.
82	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
83		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
84		return err == nil
85	}
86	
87	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
88	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
89	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
90	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
91	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
92		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
93			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
94				return b
95			}
96		}
97		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
98			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
99				return cand
100			}
101		}
102		return ""
103	}
104	
105	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
106	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
107		if name == "" {
108			name = "origin"
109		}
110		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
111		if err != nil {
112			return ""
113		}
114		return out
115	}
116	
117	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
118	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
119	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
120	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
121	// semantics should use Remote instead.
122	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
123		if commonDir == "" {
124			return ""
125		}
126		if name == "" {
127			name = "origin"
128		}
129		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
130		if err != nil {
131			return ""
132		}
133		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
134		section := ""
135		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
136			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
137			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
138				continue
139			}
140			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
141				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
142				continue
143			}
144			if section != want {
145				continue
146			}
147			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
148			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
149				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
150			}
151		}
152		return ""
153	}
```

```text
62				}

64				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "graduate  %s\n", config.Contract(src))
65				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "       →  %s\n", config.Contract(dest))
66				if dryRun {
67					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\n(dry run — nothing moved)")
68					return nil
69				}
70	
71				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dest), 0o755); err != nil {
72					return err
73				}
74				// Rename first: it is atomic within a filesystem and leaves
75				// nothing half-copied if it fails.
76				if err := os.Rename(src, dest); err != nil {
77					return fmt.Errorf("move %s: %w\n"+
78						"If the projects root is on another filesystem, copy it by hand and remove the try",
79						config.Contract(src), err)
80				}
81	
82				if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dest, ".git")); err != nil {
83					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dest, "init", "-b", "main"); err != nil {
84						return err
85					}
86					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   git init")
87				}
88				// An experiment usually has files but no commit. A project needs
89				// one: without a HEAD there is no default branch, so `dev start`
90				// would have nothing to base a worktree on.
91				if made, err := ensureInitialCommit(ctx, dest, name); err != nil {
92					app.warnf("could not make an initial commit: %v", err)
93				} else if made {
94					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   committed the existing work")
95				}
96	
97				if remote {
98					f, err := forge.Preferred()
99					if err != nil {
100						app.warnf("%v — the project is in place; add a remote by hand", err)
101					} else {
102						url, err := f.CreateRepo(ctx, dest, forge.RepoRequest{
103							Name: name, Private: private, Push: push,
104						})
105						if err != nil {
106							app.warnf("could not create the remote: %v", err)
107						} else {
108							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   remote    %s\n", url)
109						}
110					}
111				}
112	
113				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%s is now a project. Start work on it with:\n  dev start %s --task <name>\n",
114					name, name)
115				return openOrCD(app, ctx, dest, name)
116			},
117		}
118		f := cmd.Flags()
119		f.StringVarP(&category, "category", "c", "", "category subdirectory under project_root")
120		f.StringVar(&name, "name", "", "project name (default: the try name without its date prefix)")
121		f.BoolVar(&private, "private", true, "create the remote as private")
122		f.BoolVar(&remote, "remote", false, "create a remote repository with gh or glab")
123		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", true, "push after creating the remote")
124		f.BoolVar(&dryRun, "dry-run", false, "show what would happen without moving anything")
125		return cmd
126	}
127	
128	// resolveTry finds the try directory to graduate: an explicit reference, or
129	// the try containing the current directory.
130	func resolveTry(app *App, triesRoot string, args []string) (string, error) {
131		if len(args) == 1 {
132			ref := args[0]
133			if abs := config.Expand(ref); isDir(abs) {
134				return abs, nil
135			}
136			direct := filepath.Join(triesRoot, ref)
137			if isDir(direct) {
138				return direct, nil
139			}
140			if match := findTry(triesRoot, ref); match != "" {
141				return match, nil
142			}
143			return "", fmt.Errorf("no try matching %q under %s", ref, config.Contract(triesRoot))
144		}
145	
146		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
147		if err != nil {
148			return "", err
149		}
150		if !strings.HasPrefix(cwd, triesRoot+string(filepath.Separator)) {
151			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s is not inside %s — name the try to graduate",
152				config.Contract(cwd), config.Contract(triesRoot))
153		}
154		// Walk up to the try's own top-level directory, so running this from a
155		// subdirectory still graduates the whole experiment.
156		rel, _ := filepath.Rel(triesRoot, cwd)
157		first := strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator))[0]
158		return filepath.Join(triesRoot, first), nil
159	}
160	
161	func isDir(p string) bool {
162		info, err := os.Stat(p)
163		return err == nil && info.IsDir()
164	}
165	
166	// ensureInitialCommit gives a repository a first commit if it has none,
167	// seeding a README when the tree is otherwise empty. Reports whether it made
168	// one.
169	func ensureInitialCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) (bool, error) {
170		if _, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, dir); err == nil {
171			return false, nil // already has history
172		}
173		if empty, err := isEmptyTree(dir); err != nil {
174			return false, err
175		} else if empty {
176			readme := filepath.Join(dir, "README.md")
177			if err := os.WriteFile(readme, []byte("# "+name+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
178				return false, err
179			}
180		}
181		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
182			return false, err
183		}
184		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "commit", "-m", "chore: graduate experiment into a project"); err != nil {
185			return false, err
186		}
187		return true, nil
188	}
189	
190	// isEmptyTree reports a directory with nothing in it but git's own metadata.
191	func isEmptyTree(dir string) (bool, error) {
192		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
193		if err != nil {
194			return false, err
195		}
196		for _, e := range entries {
197			if e.Name() != ".git" {
198				return false, nil
199			}
200		}
201		return true, nil
202	}
203
```

```text
33	func newHarness(t *testing.T) *harness {
34		t.Helper()
35		home := t.TempDir()
36		scanRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Program")
37		wtRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Worktrees")
38		if err := os.MkdirAll(scanRoot, 0o755); err != nil {
39			t.Fatal(err)
40		}
41	
42		// A repo inside the scan root, so `dev` discovers it the way it would in
43		// real use rather than via an absolute path.
44		r := gittest.New(t)
45		dest := filepath.Join(scanRoot, "demo")
46		if err := os.Rename(r.Root, dest); err != nil {
47			t.Fatal(err)
48		}
49		r.Root = dest
50	
51		// Isolate every path dev touches from the developer's real machine.
52		t.Setenv("HOME", home)
53		t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".local", "share"))
54		t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".config"))
55		t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".cache"))
56	
57		configPath := filepath.Join(home, "config.toml")
58		cfg := "" +
59			"[paths]\n" +
60			"scan_roots = [\"" + scanRoot + "\"]\n" +
61			"project_root = \"" + scanRoot + "\"\n" +
62			"tries_root = \"" + filepath.Join(home, "tries") + "\"\n" +
63			"worktree_root = \"" + wtRoot + "\"\n" +
64			"state_dir = \"" + filepath.Join(home, "state") + "\"\n" +
65			"\n[runtime]\nbackend = \"none\"\n" +
66			"\n[worktree]\ninclude = [\".env\"]\npost_create = []\n"
67		if err := os.WriteFile(configPath, []byte(cfg), 0o644); err != nil {
68			t.Fatal(err)

73	// run executes one dev invocation, capturing its output. Commands write
74	// through App, so the writers passed to NewRootCommandWithIO are all that is
75	// needed — no file-descriptor juggling.
76	func (h *harness) run(args ...string) (string, string, error) {
77		h.t.Helper()
78		var out, errBuf bytes.Buffer
79		root := cli.NewRootCommandWithIO(&out, &errBuf)

83	}

90		}
91		return out
92	}

97		// An empty inventory should tell the user how to start, not print nothing.

103		// start: branch + worktree + task entry.

105		if !strings.Contains(out, "feat/auth") {

107		}

111		}
112	
113		// The task appears in the inventory as hot.
114		out = h.mustRun("ls")
115		if !strings.Contains(out, "auth") || !strings.Contains(out, "HOT") {
116			t.Errorf("ls after start: %q", out)

118	
119		// JSON is a stable contract for other tools.
120		out = h.mustRun("ls", "--json")
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a

4	// package task.
5	package repo

11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"

15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"

18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}
```

```text
26	func (t *Tmux) run(ctx context.Context, args ...string) (string, error) {
27		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, t.bin, args...)
28		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer

30		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {

34			}
35			return "", fmt.Errorf("tmux %s: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), msg)
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
```

```text
1	// Package stats records where development time actually goes, and renders it
2	// as a contribution-style heatmap.
3	//
4	// Two sources, because neither alone is honest. A sampler watches live agent
5	// and terminal sessions, which is the only way to count the hours spent
6	// reading and debugging rather than committing. Git history backfills the days
7	// before dev was installed and survives a lost database. WakaTime, when
8	// enabled, adds editor time dev cannot observe from the terminal.
9	package stats
10	
11	import (
12		"database/sql"
13		"os"
14		"path/filepath"
15		"time"
16	
17		_ "modernc.org/sqlite"
18	)
19	
20	// Source labels where a measurement came from, so double counting is visible
21	// rather than silent: the same hour can legitimately appear from the sampler
22	// and from WakaTime, and a query decides which to trust.
23	type Source string
24	
25	const (
26		// SourceSession is dev's own sampler watching live runtime sessions.
27		SourceSession Source = "session"
28		// SourceGit is derived from commit timestamps.
29		SourceGit Source = "git"
30		// SourceWakaTime is imported from the WakaTime API.
31		SourceWakaTime Source = "wakatime"
32	)
33	
34	// Store is the activity database.
35	type Store struct{ db *sql.DB }
36	
37	// Open creates or opens the database at path.
38	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
39		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
40			return nil, err
41		}
42		// A short busy timeout matters: the sampler may run from cron while an
43		// interactive `dev stats` is reading.
44		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", path+"?_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)")
45		if err != nil {
46			return nil, err
47		}
48		s := &Store{db: db}
49		if err := s.migrate(); err != nil {
50			db.Close()
51			return nil, err
52		}
53		return s, nil
54	}
55	
56	// Close releases the database.
57	func (s *Store) Close() error { return s.db.Close() }
58	
59	func (s *Store) migrate() error {
60		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
61	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS activity (
62	  day     TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- local date, YYYY-MM-DD
63	  repo    TEXT    NOT NULL,
64	  branch  TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
65	  source  TEXT    NOT NULL,
66	  seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
67	  PRIMARY KEY (day, repo, branch, source)
68	);
69	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS activity_day  ON activity(day);
70	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS activity_repo ON activity(repo);
71	
72	-- Records the last successful run of each collector, so a backfill can pick up
73	-- where it left off instead of rescanning every repo's whole history.
74	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS collector (
75	  name    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
76	  last_at INTEGER NOT NULL
77	);
78	`)
79		return err
80	}
```

```text
1	// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
18	type Session struct {
19		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
20		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
21		Handle string
22		Label  string
23		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
24		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
25		// value.
26		Dirs []string
27		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
28		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
29		AgentStatus string
30		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
31		AgentSessions []string
32		Focused       bool
33	}
34	
35	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
36	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
37		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
38			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
39			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
40			// $HOME active.
41			if d == dir || strings.HasPrefix(d, dir+"/") {
42				return true
43			}
44		}
45		return false
46	}
47	
48	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
49	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
50	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
51	type Runtime interface {
52		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
53		Name() string
54		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
55		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
56		Available() bool
57		// Open makes dir live and returns a handle. Opening something already open
58		// focuses it rather than duplicating it.
59		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error)
60		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
61		// task entry.
62		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
63		// List enumerates live sessions.
64		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
65		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
66		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
67		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
68	}
69	
70	// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
71	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
72	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
73	type WorktreeOpener interface {
74		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error)
75	}
76	
77	// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
78	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
79	
80	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
81		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
82	}
83	
84	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
85	//
86	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
87	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then None.
88	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
89	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
90		herdr, tmux, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}
91		switch backend {
92		case "herdr":
93			return herdr
94		case "tmux":
95			return tmux
96		case "none":
97			return none
98		case "", "auto":
99			if herdr.Available() {
100				return herdr
101			}
102			if tmux.Available() {
103				return tmux
104			}
105			return none
106		}
107		return none
108	}
109	
110	// All returns every backend, for `dev doctor` to report on.
111	func All() []Runtime { return []Runtime{NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}} }
112	
113	// haveBinary reports whether name is on PATH.
114	func haveBinary(name string) bool {
115		_, err := exec.LookPath(name)
116		return err == nil
117	}
118
```

```text
1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70
```

```text
56	func runList(app *App, o listOptions) error {
57		ctx := ctxOf()
58		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
59		if err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62	
63		filter := inventory.Filter{Repo: o.repo, LiveOnly: o.live, DirtyOnly: o.dirty}
64		for _, s := range o.states {
65			st, err := task.ParseState(s)
66			if err != nil {
67				return err
68			}
69			filter.States = append(filter.States, st)
70		}
71		if len(filter.States) == 0 && !o.showAll {
72			filter.States = []task.State{task.Hot, task.Warm, task.Cold}
73		}
74	
75		rt := app.Runtime()
76		rows := inventory.Collect(ctx, tasks, rt, inventory.Options{SkipRuntime: o.noRuntime})
77		rows = filter.Apply(rows)
78	
79		if o.jsonOut {
80			return emitJSON(app, rows)
81		}
82	
83		if len(rows) == 0 {
84			if len(tasks) == 0 {
85				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No tasks yet. Start one with:  dev start <repo> --task <name>")
86			} else {
87				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No tasks match that filter. Try `dev ls --all`.")
88			}
89			return nil
90		}
91	
92		t := NewTable("", "TASK", "STATE", "REPO", "BRANCH", "GIT", "AGE", "SESSION", "NEXT")
93		for _, r := range rows {
94			session := "—"
95			if r.Live() {
96				session = rt.Name()
97				if r.Session.AgentStatus != "" {
98					session += ":" + r.Session.AgentStatus
99				}
100			}
101			gitCol := r.Status.Summary()
102			switch {
103			case r.StatusErr != nil:
104				gitCol = "?"
105			case !r.CheckoutExists:
106				gitCol = "no checkout"
107			}
108			t.Add(
109				r.Task.State.Icon(),
110				truncate(r.Task.Title(), 28),
111				r.Task.State.Label(),
112				truncate(r.Task.Repo, 20),
113				truncate(r.Task.Branch, 28),
114				gitCol,
115				humanAge(r.Age()),
116				session,
117				truncate(dash(r.Task.Next), 40),
118			)
119		}
120		t.Render(app.Out)
121	
122		// Surface drift as a hint rather than rewriting state behind the user's
123		// back: dev reports, the user decides.
124		var drifted int
125		for _, r := range rows {
126			if r.StateDrift() != "" {
127				drifted++
128			}
129		}
130		if drifted > 0 {
131			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\n%d task(s) drifted from their recorded state — run `dev sweep` to review.\n", drifted)
132		}
133		return nil
134	}
```

```text
272	// parseSince accepts a relative window ("30d", "6mo", "1y") or an absolute
273	// date. Relative is what people actually type; absolute is what scripts want.
274	func parseSince(s string, now time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
275		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
276		if s == "" {
277			return now.AddDate(-1, 0, 0), nil
278		}
279		if d, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", s, time.Local); err == nil {
280			return d, nil
281		}
282		var n int
283		var unit string
284		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(s, "%d%s", &n, &unit); err != nil || n <= 0 {
285			return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot parse --since %q: want 30d, 6mo, 1y or YYYY-MM-DD", s)
286		}
287		switch strings.ToLower(unit) {
288		case "d", "day", "days":
289			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n), nil
290		case "w", "week", "weeks":
291			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n*7), nil
292		case "mo", "month", "months":
293			return now.AddDate(0, -n, 0), nil
294		case "y", "yr", "year", "years":
295			return now.AddDate(-n, 0, 0), nil
296		}
297		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown unit %q in --since: want d, w, mo or y", unit)
298	}
```

```text
17	// datePrefix matches the "2026-08-27-" a try directory carries.

20	func newGraduateCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
21		var (
22			category string
23			name     string
24			private  bool

30			Use:   "graduate [try]",
31			Short: "Promote an experiment into a real project",
32			Long: `Move a try out of the scratch directory and into your projects tree.
33	
34	An experiment that turns out to matter should stop being an experiment, and
35	that transition is where things usually get lost — the directory keeps its date
36	prefix forever, or it gets copied by hand and the history is left behind.
37	
38	graduate moves the directory to <project_root>/<category>/<name>, drops the
39	date prefix, makes sure it has a git repo and a first commit, and optionally
40	creates the remote with gh or glab.
41	
42	With no argument, the try containing the current directory is used.`,
43			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
44			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
45				ctx := ctxOf()
46				triesRoot := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot)
47	
48				src, err := resolveTry(app, triesRoot, args)
49				if err != nil {
50					return err
51				}
52				if name == "" {
53					name = datePrefix.ReplaceAllString(filepath.Base(src), "")
54				}
55				if name == "" {
56					return fmt.Errorf("could not derive a project name from %s — pass --name", src)
57				}
58	
59				dest := filepath.Join(config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot), category, name)
60				if _, err := os.Stat(dest); err == nil {
61					return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists", config.Contract(dest))
62				}
63	
64				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "graduate  %s\n", config.Contract(src))
65				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "       →  %s\n", config.Contract(dest))

70	
71				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dest), 0o755); err != nil {
72					return err
73				}
74				// Rename first: it is atomic within a filesystem and leaves
75				// nothing half-copied if it fails.
76				if err := os.Rename(src, dest); err != nil {
77					return fmt.Errorf("move %s: %w\n"+

128	// resolveTry finds the try directory to graduate: an explicit reference, or
129	// the try containing the current directory.
130	func resolveTry(app *App, triesRoot string, args []string) (string, error) {
131		if len(args) == 1 {
132			ref := args[0]
133			if abs := config.Expand(ref); isDir(abs) {
134				return abs, nil
135			}
136			direct := filepath.Join(triesRoot, ref)
137			if isDir(direct) {
138				return direct, nil
139			}
140			if match := findTry(triesRoot, ref); match != "" {
141				return match, nil
142			}
143			return "", fmt.Errorf("no try matching %q under %s", ref, config.Contract(triesRoot))
144		}
145	
146		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
147		if err != nil {
148			return "", err
149		}
150		if !strings.HasPrefix(cwd, triesRoot+string(filepath.Separator)) {
151			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s is not inside %s — name the try to graduate",
152				config.Contract(cwd), config.Contract(triesRoot))
153		}
154		// Walk up to the try's own top-level directory, so running this from a
155		// subdirectory still graduates the whole experiment.
156		rel, _ := filepath.Rel(triesRoot, cwd)
157		first := strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator))[0]
158		return filepath.Join(triesRoot, first), nil
159	}
160	
161	func isDir(p string) bool {
162		info, err := os.Stat(p)
163		return err == nil && info.IsDir()
164	}
165	
166	// ensureInitialCommit gives a repository a first commit if it has none,
167	// seeding a README when the tree is otherwise empty. Reports whether it made
168	// one.
169	func ensureInitialCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) (bool, error) {
170		if _, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, dir); err == nil {
171			return false, nil // already has history
172		}
173		if empty, err := isEmptyTree(dir); err != nil {
174			return false, err
175		} else if empty {
176			readme := filepath.Join(dir, "README.md")
177			if err := os.WriteFile(readme, []byte("# "+name+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
178				return false, err
179			}
180		}
181		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
182			return false, err
183		}
184		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "commit", "-m", "chore: graduate experiment into a project"); err != nil {
185			return false, err
186		}
187		return true, nil
188	}
189	
190	// isEmptyTree reports a directory with nothing in it but git's own metadata.
191	func isEmptyTree(dir string) (bool, error) {
192		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
193		if err != nil {
194			return false, err
195		}
196		for _, e := range entries {
197			if e.Name() != ".git" {
198				return false, nil
199			}
200		}
201		return true, nil
202	}
```

```text
14	func newCacheCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

18			Long: `Manage files under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev.
19	
20	These are disposable accelerators: the remote forge inventory and fetched
21	GitHub gitignore templates. Activity statistics are deliberately not here —
22	$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db contains observations that may not be
23	reconstructible; use "dev stats path/clear" for it.`,
24		}
25		cmd.AddCommand(newCacheListCmd(app), newCachePathCmd(app), newCacheClearCmd(app))

29	func cacheRoot() string { return filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev") }
30	
31	func newCachePathCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
32		return &cobra.Command{
33			Use:   "path",
34			Short: "Print dev's XDG cache directory",
35			Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
36			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
37				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, cacheRoot())
38				return nil
39			},
40		}
41	}
42	
43	func newCacheListCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
44		return &cobra.Command{
45			Use:   "list",
46			Short: "List cache paths, sizes, and ages",
47			Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
48			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
49				t := NewTable("CACHE", "SIZE", "AGE", "PATH")
50				for _, item := range cacheItems() {
51					size, modified, exists := cacheInfo(item.path)
52					if !exists {
53						t.Add(item.name, "—", "—", config.Contract(item.path)+" (absent)")
54						continue
55					}
56					t.Add(item.name, humanBytes(size), humanAge(time.Since(modified)), config.Contract(item.path))
57				}
58				t.Render(app.Out)
59				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\nStats data: %s (not cache; use `dev stats clear`)\n",
60					config.Contract(filepath.Join(app.Cfg.StateDir(), "stats.db")))
61				return nil
62			},
63		}
64	}
65	
66	type cacheItem struct{ name, path string }
67	
68	func cacheItems() []cacheItem {
69		return []cacheItem{
70			{"remote", filepath.Join(cacheRoot(), "remotes.json")},
71			{"gitignore", filepath.Join(cacheRoot(), "gitignore")},
72		}
73	}
74	
75	func newCacheClearCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
76		return &cobra.Command{
77			Use:       "clear <remote|gitignore|all>",
78			Short:     "Remove a regenerable cache",
79			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
80			ValidArgs: []string{"remote", "gitignore", "all"},
81			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
82				var targets []cacheItem
83				switch args[0] {
84				case "remote", "remotes":
85					targets = cacheItems()[:1]
86				case "gitignore":
87					targets = cacheItems()[1:]
88				case "all":
89					targets = cacheItems()
90				default:
91					return fmt.Errorf("unknown cache %q: want remote, gitignore or all", args[0])
92				}
93				removed := 0
94				for _, item := range targets {
95					if _, err := os.Lstat(item.path); os.IsNotExist(err) {
96						continue
97					}
98					if err := os.RemoveAll(item.path); err != nil {
99						return fmt.Errorf("clear %s: %w", item.name, err)
100					}
101					removed++
102				}
103				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "cleared %d cache(s) under %s\n", removed, config.Contract(cacheRoot()))
104				return nil
105			},
106		}
107	}
108	
109	func cacheInfo(path string) (size int64, modified time.Time, exists bool) {
110		info, err := os.Stat(path)
111		if err != nil {
112			return 0, time.Time{}, false
113		}
114		exists, modified = true, info.ModTime()
115		if !info.IsDir() {
116			return info.Size(), modified, true
117		}
118		_ = filepath.WalkDir(path, func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
119			if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
120				return nil
121			}
122			if i, err := d.Info(); err == nil {
123				size += i.Size()
124				if i.ModTime().After(modified) {
125					modified = i.ModTime()
126				}
127			}
128			return nil
129		})
130		return size, modified, true
131	}
132	
133	func humanBytes(n int64) string {
134		const unit = 1024
135		switch {
136		case n < unit:
137			return fmt.Sprintf("%dB", n)
138		case n < unit*unit:
139			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fK", float64(n)/unit)
140		case n < unit*unit*unit:
141			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fM", float64(n)/(unit*unit))
142		default:
143			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fG", float64(n)/(unit*unit*unit))
144		}
145	}
```

```text
56			Use:   "init",
57			Short: "Write a starter config.toml, detecting this machine's layout",
58			Long: `Generate a commented config.toml describing the paths that actually exist on
59	this machine.
60	
61	Where repositories live differs from person to person — ~/Documents/Program,
62	~/src, ~/code, a ghq root — so the generated file is built from what is found
63	rather than from a fixed set of defaults. A config pointing at directories that
64	do not exist is worse than none: dev would discover nothing and give no clue

66	
67	Every value it writes is still a default you can change; nothing is inferred

82				}

86				}

89				}

105	// reportDetection explains what was found, so the user can see whether the
106	// generated config actually matches how they work.
107	func reportDetection(app *App, l config.Layout) {
108		if len(l.Found) == 0 {
109			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No repository directories were recognised, so the defaults were used.")
110			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Edit paths.scan_roots to point at where you keep projects.")
111			return
112		}
113		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Detected:")
114		t := NewTable("ROOT", "REPOS", "ROLE")
115		for _, r := range l.ScanRoots {
116			role := "scan root"
117			switch r {
118			case l.ProjectRoot:
119				role = "scan root, new projects land here"
120			case l.TriesRoot:
121				role = "scan root, experiments"
122			}
123			t.Add(r, fmt.Sprintf("%d", l.Found[r]), role)
124		}
125		t.Render(app.Out)
126		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\nWorktrees will go to %s — change paths.worktree_root if that volume is wrong.\n",
127			l.WorktreeRoot)
128	}
129	
130	// renderStarterConfig fills the annotated template with detected paths.
131	func renderStarterConfig(l config.Layout) string {
132		roots := make([]string, len(l.ScanRoots))
133		for i, r := range l.ScanRoots {
134			roots[i] = strconv.Quote(r)
135		}
136		r := strings.NewReplacer(
137			"@@SCAN_ROOTS@@", strings.Join(roots, ", "),
138			"@@TRIES_ROOT@@", l.TriesRoot,
139			"@@PROJECT_ROOT@@", l.ProjectRoot,
140			"@@WORKTREE_ROOT@@", l.WorktreeRoot,
141		)
142		return r.Replace(starterConfig)
143	}
144	
145	const starterConfig = `# dev configuration.
146	#
147	# The paths below were detected on this machine by "dev config init"; everything
148	# else is dev's built-in default. Delete anything you do not want to override.
149	
150	[paths]

190	# matched here AND gitignored are copied: a tracked file is already in the new
191	# checkout on the correct branch, so listing it would overwrite it.
192	include = [".env", ".env.local"]

194	# Directories to symlink instead of copying. Opt-in and empty by default:
195	# sharing node_modules across checkouts breaks native builds often enough that
196	# it must never happen by accident.

199	# "auto" detects from lockfiles (uv.lock -> uv sync, package-lock.json ->

204	# How a new worktree gets its installed dependencies:
205	#   reinstall  run the install command (always correct, can be slow)
206	#   copy       duplicate the directory from the source checkout (fast)
207	#   link       share one directory between checkouts (fastest, and risky)
```

```text
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}
```

```text
8	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
9	type Worktree struct {
10		Path string
11		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
12		Head string
13		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
14		Branch   string
15		Detached bool
16		Bare     bool
17		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
18		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
19		Locked         bool
20		LockedReason   string
21		Prunable       bool
22		PrunableReason string
23		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
24		Main bool
25	}
26	
27	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
28	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
29	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
30		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
31		if err != nil {
32			return nil, err
33		}
34		var (
35			list []Worktree
36			cur  *Worktree
37		)
38		flush := func() {
39			if cur != nil {
40				list = append(list, *cur)
41				cur = nil
42			}
43		}
44		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
45			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
46				flush()
47				continue
48			}
49			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
50			switch key {
51			case "worktree":
52				flush()
53				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
54			case "HEAD":
55				if cur != nil {
56					cur.Head = val
57				}
58			case "branch":
59				if cur != nil {
60					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
61				}
62			case "detached":
63				if cur != nil {
64					cur.Detached = true
65				}
66			case "bare":
67				if cur != nil {
68					cur.Bare = true
69				}
70			case "locked":
71				if cur != nil {
72					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
73				}
74			case "prunable":
75				if cur != nil {
76					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
77				}
78			}
79		}
80		flush()
81		return list, nil
82	}
83	
84	// WorktreeFor finds the worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git refuses to
85	// check the same branch out twice, so at most one can match.
86	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
87		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
88		if err != nil {
89			return Worktree{}, false, err
90		}
91		for _, w := range list {
92			if w.Branch == branch {
93				return w, true, nil
94			}
95		}
96		return Worktree{}, false, nil
97	}
98	
99	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
100	//
101	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
102	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
103	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
104	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
105	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
106		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
107		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
108		if exists {
109			args = append(args, path, branch)
110		} else {
111			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
112			if base != "" {
113				args = append(args, base)
114			}
115		}
116		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
117		return err
118	}
119	
120	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
121	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
122	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
123		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
124		if force {
125			args = append(args, "--force")
126		}
127		args = append(args, path)
128		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
129		return err
130	}
131	
132	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
133	// were deleted behind git's back.
134	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
135		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
136		return err
137	}
138	
139	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
140	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
141		if branch == "" {
142			return false
143		}
144		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
145		return err == nil
146	}
147	
148	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
149	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
150		if ref == "" {
151			return false
152		}
153		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
154		return err == nil
155	}
```

 `./.claude/plans/dot-config-homebrew-brewfile-tmpl-14-ta-flickering-tarjan.md`

```text
1	# Context
2	
3	`dev-cli` 目前只能從 source 以 `make install` 安裝；沒有公開 GitHub repo/tag、Homebrew formula、release 流程或已部署的 completion。CLI 實際是 Go/Cobra（不是 Tyro），而 Cobra 已自動提供 `dev completion <shell>`，但專案又另有未文件化的 `dev shell-init completion ...`，且兩者都沒有被 package manager 安裝或測試。現有 shell wrapper 以 command substitution 捕捉整段 stdout，會讓裸跑 `dev` 看不到 stdout TTY、從 TUI 退化成 plain list。
4	
5	目標是把 `dev-cli` 以 public MIT 專案從 `v0.1.0` 開始發布；macOS 可用 `brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli` 安裝 executable `dev` 並立即取得 bash/zsh/fish completion，Linux 則沿用 dotfiles 的版本鎖定 `go_tools`。同時把 `dev` 納入 dotfiles 的預設開發工具、completion cache、shell directory-change integration 與工具文件，而且不讓 Formula 在安裝期寫入使用者的 agent skill 目錄。
6	
7	# Implementation plan
8	
9	## 1. 先在 `dev-cli` 收斂 shell integration 與 completion
10	
11	- 在 `internal/cli/shell.go` 與 `internal/cli/app.go` 改寫 bash/zsh/fish wrapper：
12	  - 每次呼叫建立權限受限的暫存檔，透過 `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` 傳給真正的 `dev` process；binary 的 stdout/stderr 直接連到原 terminal，不再包在 `$()` 內。
13	  - `App.cdDirective` 在該環境變數存在時只把「原始目錄路徑」寫入檔案；wrapper 成功執行後讀取路徑並以 `cd -- "$path"` 切換，不 `eval` 檔案內容；未載入 wrapper 時保留目前輸出 shell-quoted `cd ...` 的行為。
14	  - 保留 `DEV_SHELL_INIT=1`、child exit status、即時 stdout/stderr、pipe 行為與可靠 cleanup；確認裸 `dev`/`dev tui` 仍看到真實 TTY。
15	- 移除 `newShellInitCmd` 下重複且未文件化的 `shell-init completion` 子命令；唯一公開介面採 Cobra 慣例：`dev completion bash|zsh|fish`（Cobra 現有 PowerShell 可保留，但本次安裝範圍為三種 shell）。
16	- 新增 `internal/cli/completion.go`，以可重用的 `ValidArgsFunction` / `RegisterFlagCompletionFunc` 接到既有 command constructors：
17	  - task：`park`、`resume`、`done`，重用 `internal/task.Store.List`，以穩定 task ID 為值並提供 title/state/repo/branch 描述；
18	  - repo：`start`、`repo open/sync` 與適用的 `--repo`，重用 `internal/repo.Discover`、`Repo.Display`、`resolveRepoRef`；
19	  - worktree：`wt open/rm`，重用 `repoContext`、`internal/gitx.Worktrees`，排除 detached，且 `rm` 排除 main checkout；
20	  - embedded/enum：`help` 重用 `internal/help.List`、`gitignore` 重用 `internal/ignore.BundledNames`，以及 `--runtime`、stats `--source` 等有限值；domain 值回傳 `ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp`，真正的 path arguments 維持 filesystem completion。
21	  - completion 只讀本機 config/task/repo/worktree/embedded data；不在每次 Tab 查 forge/network、collect runtime/status 或寫入 cache。
22	- 修正 `internal/cli/root.go` 的 completion 載入時機：hidden `cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd` 進入 root `PersistentPreRunE` 時，目標 command 的 persistent flags（尤其 `--config`）尚未由 `getCompletions` parse，因此先略過一般 `App.Load`，由 dynamic callback 在 flags parse 後 lazy-load。載入/探索失敗時靜默回傳無 dynamic candidates，仍保留 Cobra 的 command/flag 靜態 completion；執行 `dev completion <shell>` 產生腳本時也不依賴使用者 config。
23	- 在 `internal/cli/cli_test.go`（必要時拆出 focused test file）使用既有 `NewRootCommandWithIO` harness 測試：三種 script generation、移除 duplicate path、直接呼叫 `__complete` 的 task/repo/worktree/help/gitignore/enum candidates、`--config` 生效、壞 config 仍能補 command/flag、NoFileComp directive；另以 subprocess shell tests 驗證 wrapper 的 stdout/stderr、exit status、directory change、cleanup 與 TTY-preserving 行為。
24	- 跑 `make skill-sync` 更新 `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`，再以 `make skill-check` 防止 command tree drift。
25	
26	## 2. 準備 public `v0.1.0` source release
27	
28	- 新增專案層 MIT `LICENSE`。
29	- 更新 `README.md`：Homebrew 與版本化 `go install` 安裝、`dev completion bash|zsh|fish` 手動產生方式、shell-init、以及明確 opt-in 的 `dev skill install`；說明 Formula 不會修改 `~/.agents/skills`。
30	- 將 `Makefile` 的 `VERSION` 改為可由 `VERSION=v0.1.0 make build` 覆寫，並測試 injected `internal/cli.Version` 會由 `dev --version` 顯示；Homebrew source archive 沒有 `.git`，不能依賴 `git describe`。
31	- 新增最小 `.github/workflows/release.yml`：只在 `v*` tag 觸發，執行 format/vet/test/skill-check/E2E、以 tag 注入版本並 assert `dev --version`，成功後用 GitHub CLI 建立 generated-notes Release；不加入 GoReleaser、binary matrix 或跨 repo PAT automation，Formula 仍沿用 `translate` 的 source-build 慣例。
32	- 本地全部驗證通過後，另行確認再建立 public `github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli`、設定 `origin`、推 branch/PR。合併後再次確認，才在 exact merged commit 建立並 push immutable `v0.1.0` tag；若有錯誤發布新版本，不移動既有 tag。下載公開 archive 並計算 SHA-256，供 formula 使用。
33	
34	## 3. 在既有 `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap` 加 Formula
35	
36	- 先在 `/usr/local/Homebrew/Library/Taps/daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap` 建 feature branch，再新增 `Formula/dev-cli.rb`，沿用 `Formula/translate.rb`：
37	  - class `DevCli`、public homepage/tag archive URL、實測 SHA-256、MIT、`head` main、`depends_on "go" => :build`；
38	  - 直接 `go build` `./cmd/dev` 到 `bin/"dev"`，以 `-X github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/cli.Version=v#{version}` 注入版本；絕不呼叫會執行 `dev skill install` 的 `make install`；
39	  - 使用 Homebrew 官方 Cobra 形式 `generate_completions_from_executable(bin/"dev", shell_parameter_format: :cobra)`，自動安裝 bash/zsh/fish completion；
40	  - test block 驗證 `--version`、`--help` 與 completion script 可生成。
41	- 更新 tap `README.md` 的安裝與人工升版順序（publish immutable tag → checksum → bump URL/SHA → lint/install/test → publish tap），保持與 `translate` 一樣不需要 cross-repo secret。
42	- formula 本地 build-from-source、audit、test 與 completion keg 檢查通過後，另行確認才 push/merge tap；再從 published tap 做 fresh install 驗證。
43	
44	## 4. Formula 公開可用後再接入 chezmoi dotfiles
45	
46	- `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl`：保留既有單一 `tap "daviddwlee84/tap"`，在 `translate` 旁新增 Darwin 的 `brew "daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli"`；沿用現有 `trust_bundle_taps`，不新增 trust task，也不改 brew-bundle 的 profile/global skip semantics。
```

```text
1	// Package help serves the git-workflow quick-reference pages dev bundles.
2	//
3	// These exist because the hard part of this workflow is not running the
4	// commands, it is remembering which one applies. A page you can reach in one
5	// keystroke from the terminal you are already in beats a bookmark.
6	package help
7	
8	import (
9		"embed"
10		"fmt"
11		"io/fs"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	)
15	
16	//go:embed all:topics
17	var topics embed.FS
18	
19	// Topic is one reference page.
20	type Topic struct {
21		Name    string
22		Title   string
23		Summary string
24		Body    string
25	}
26	
27	// List returns every topic, sorted by name.
28	func List() ([]Topic, error) {
29		entries, err := fs.ReadDir(topics, "topics")
30		if err != nil {
31			return nil, err
32		}
33		var out []Topic
34		for _, e := range entries {
35			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".md") {
36				continue
37			}
38			t, err := load(strings.TrimSuffix(e.Name(), ".md"))
39			if err != nil {
40				continue
41			}
42			out = append(out, t)
43		}
44		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name < out[j].Name })
45		return out, nil
46	}
47	
48	// Get returns one topic by exact name, or by unique prefix.
49	func Get(name string) (Topic, error) {
50		if t, err := load(name); err == nil {
51			return t, nil
52		}
53		all, err := List()
54		if err != nil {
55			return Topic{}, err
56		}
57		var hits []Topic
58		for _, t := range all {
59			if strings.HasPrefix(t.Name, name) || strings.Contains(t.Name, name) {
60				hits = append(hits, t)
61			}
62		}
63		switch len(hits) {
64		case 1:
65			return hits[0], nil
66		case 0:
67			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("no help topic %q; run `dev help` to list them", name)
68		default:
69			names := make([]string, len(hits))
70			for i, t := range hits {
71				names[i] = t.Name
72			}
73			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("%q matches several topics: %s", name, strings.Join(names, ", "))
74		}
75	}
76	
77	func load(name string) (Topic, error) {
78		b, err := topics.ReadFile("topics/" + name + ".md")
79		if err != nil {
80			return Topic{}, err
81		}
82		body := string(b)
83		t := Topic{Name: name, Body: body}
84		// The first heading is the title; the first paragraph after it is the
85		// summary shown in the index.
86		for _, line := range strings.Split(body, "\n") {
87			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
88			switch {
89			case t.Title == "" && strings.HasPrefix(line, "# "):
90				t.Title = strings.TrimPrefix(line, "# ")
91			case t.Title != "" && t.Summary == "" && line != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(line, "#"):
92				// A page may open with a blockquote or a list; the marker is
93				// formatting, not part of the one-line summary.
94				t.Summary = strings.TrimLeft(line, ">-* ")
95				return t, nil
96			}
97		}
98		return t, nil
99	}
```

```text
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}
```

```text
256	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
257	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
258	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
259	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
260		cfg := Default()
261		if path == "" {
262			path = ConfigFile()
263		}
264		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
265		switch {
266		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
267			return cfg, nil
268		case err != nil:
269			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
270		}
271		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
272			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
273			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
274			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
275		}
276		cfg.Source = path
277		return cfg, cfg.Validate()
278	}
```
