15	func newParkCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
16		var (
17			next   string
18			note   string
19			wip    bool
20			push   bool
21			cold   bool
22			keepRT bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "park [task]",
26			Short: "Stop working on a task without losing the thread",
27			Long: `Park the current task (or the one named) so its runtime session can close.
28	
29	Parking is the missing move that makes a crowded sidebar shrink. It records
30	what to do next, optionally checkpoints uncommitted work, and closes the
31	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
32	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.
33	
34	  warm (default)  worktree and branch stay; session closes. Back within days.
35	  cold (--cold)   work is committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstruct
36	                  it anywhere later with dev resume.
37	
38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
41			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
42			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
43				ctx := ctxOf()
44				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
45				if err != nil {
46					return err
47				}
48	
49				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
50				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
51					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
52						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
53				}
54				target := task.Warm
55				if cold {
56					target = task.Cold
57				}
58				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
59	
60				if next != "" {
61					t.Next = next
62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69	
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97	
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114	
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}
124	
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes
133					// the task reconstructible rather than lost.
134					t.WorktreePath = ""
135				}
136				if cold && mode == task.ModeBranch {
137					// Free the canonical checkout for other work. The branch remains
138					// local + remote and resume switches back to it.
139					base := t.Base
140					if base == "" {
141						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
142					}
143					if base == "" {
144						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but its base branch is unknown")
145					}
146					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
147						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
148							base, err)
149					}
150				}
151	
152				t.State = target
153				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
154				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
155					return err
156				}
157				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
158				if t.Next != "" {
159					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
160				}
161				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
162				return nil
163			},
164		}
165		f := cmd.Flags()
166		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
167		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
168		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
169		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
170		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
171		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
172		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app, task.Hot, task.Warm)
173		return cmd
174	}
175	
176	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
177	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
178		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
179			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
180		}
181		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
182		return nil
183	}
184	
185	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
186	// directory when no argument is given.
187	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
188		if len(args) == 1 {
189			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
190		}
191		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
196		if err != nil {
197			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
198				config.Contract(cwd))
199		}
200		return t, nil
201	}

3	import (
4		"fmt"

11		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
12	)
13	
14	func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			noProvision bool
17			fetch       bool
18			force       bool
19		)
20		cmd := &cobra.Command{
21			Use:   "resume <task>",
22			Short: "Pick a task back up, rebuilding whatever is missing",
23			Long: `Make a parked task hot again.
24	
25	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
26	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
27	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
28	identity.
29	
30	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
33			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
34			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
35				ctx := ctxOf()
36				t, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
37				if err != nil {
38					return err
39				}
40	
41				host := config.Hostname()
42				if !t.OwnedBy(host) && !force {
43					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is owned by %s.\n"+
44						"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
45						t.ID, t.Owner)
46				}
47	
48				if fetch {
49					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "fetch", "--prune", "origin"); err != nil {
50						app.warnf("fetch failed: %v", err)
51					}
52				}
53	
54				rt := app.Runtime()
55				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
56				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
57	
58				switch mode {
59				case task.ModeWorktree:
60					_, statErr := os.Stat(checkout)
61					// Rebuild the worktree when it is gone — the cold-to-hot path.
62					if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
63						base := t.Base
64						// Prefer the published branch: a cold task's work lives on
65						// the remote, and a stale local ref could drop it.
66						if remote := "origin/" + t.Branch; gitx.RefExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, remote) {
67							base = remote
68						}
69						m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
70						res, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
71							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, RepoName: t.Repo, Branch: t.Branch,
72							Base: base, Label: t.Title(), NoProvision: noProvision,
73						})
74						if err != nil {
75							var exists *wt.ErrExists
76							if asError(err, &exists) {
77								t.WorktreePath = exists.Path
78							} else {
79								return err
80							}
81						} else {
82							t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = res.Path, res.RuntimeHandle
83							reportProvision(app, res)
84							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebuilt    %s\n", config.Contract(res.Path))
85						}
86						checkout = t.WorktreePath
87					}
88	
89				case task.ModeBranch:
90					checkout = t.RepoPath
91					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
92					if err != nil {
93						return err
94					}
95					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
96						if st.Dirty() {
97							return fmt.Errorf("cannot switch the canonical checkout from %s to %s: %s",
98								st.Branch, t.Branch, st.Breakdown())
99						}
100						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "switch", t.Branch); err != nil {
101							return err
102						}
103					}
104	
105				case task.ModeDirect:
106					checkout = t.RepoPath
107					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
108					if err != nil {
109						return err
110					}
111					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
112						return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s tracks %s, but the canonical checkout is on %s; "+
113							"switch back explicitly or start a worktree task", t.Title(), t.Branch, st.Branch)
114					}
115				}
116				if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
117					handle, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, checkout, t.Title())
118					if err != nil {
119						app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
120					}
121					if rt.Name() != "none" {
122						t.RuntimeHandle = handle
123					}
124				}
125	
126				t.State = task.Hot
127				t.Owner = host
128				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
129					return err
130				}
131				annotate(app, rt, t)
132	
133				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s  %s on %s (%s)\n",
134					task.Hot.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, mode)
135				if t.Next != "" {
136					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   next      %s\n", t.Next)
137				}
138				if t.AgentSession != "" {
139					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   agent     %s (resumable)\n", t.AgentSession)
140				}
141				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout); err == nil {
142					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   git       %s\n", st.Summary())
143					if st.Behind > 0 {
144						app.warnf("branch is %d behind upstream — `git pull --ff-only` before you start", st.Behind)
145					}
146				}
147				if rt.Name() == "none" {
148					return app.cdDirective(checkout)
149				}
150				return nil
151			},
152		}
153		f := cmd.Flags()
154		f.BoolVar(&noProvision, "no-provision", false, "skip dependency install when rebuilding a worktree")
155		f.BoolVar(&fetch, "fetch", true, "fetch from origin first")
156		f.BoolVar(&force, "force", false, "take ownership of a task owned by another machine")
157		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app, task.Warm, task.Cold)
158		return cmd
159	}

16	func newDoneCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
17		var (
18			ff           bool
19			pr           bool
20			deleteBranch bool
21			keepWorktree bool
22			push         bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "done [task]",
26			Short: "Integrate a finished change stream and clean up",
27			Long: `Finish a task: integrate the branch, then remove what it leaves behind.
28	
29	Two integration modes, matching the two shapes a branch's history takes:
30	
31	  --ff    rebase onto the base and fast-forward it. Use when the branch's
32	          commits are worth keeping in the base's history.
33	  --pr    push and open a pull/merge request with gh or glab, leaving the
34	          merge to review and CI. Use when someone (or something) should look
35	          at it first.
36	
37	With neither, dev only reports what it would do.
38	
39	Cleanup is deliberately conservative: the worktree is removed, the task entry
40	is marked done, and the branch is deleted only with --delete-branch. A merged

69					}

73						}

78							app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
79						}
80						t.RuntimeHandle = ""
81					}
82					t.State = task.Done
83					if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
84						return err
85					}
86					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s completed directly on %s\n", task.Done.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Branch)
87					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   no branch or worktree was created or removed")
88					return nil
89				}
90	
91				base := t.Base
92				if base == "" {
93					base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
94				}
95				if base == "" {
96					return fmt.Errorf("cannot determine the base branch for %s — pass --base when starting a task", t.Repo)
97				}

125					} else {

127					}

130				rt := app.Runtime()

132					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {

134					}
135					t.RuntimeHandle = ""

256	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
257	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
258	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
259	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
260		cfg := Default()
261		if path == "" {
262			path = ConfigFile()
263		}
264		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
265		switch {
266		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
267			return cfg, nil
268		case err != nil:
269			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
270		}
271		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
272			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
273			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
274			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
275		}
276		cfg.Source = path
277		return cfg, cfg.Validate()
278	}
279	
280	// Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a
281	// worktree create, when a directory has already been made.
282	func (c Config) Validate() error {
283		switch c.Runtime.Backend {
284		case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "none":
285		default:
286			return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
287		}
288		if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
289			return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
290		}
291		if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
292			return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
293		}
294		switch c.Bootstrap.Layout {
295		case "", "flat", "preserve":
296		default:
297			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.layout %q: want flat or preserve", c.Bootstrap.Layout)
298		}
299		if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
300			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
301		}
302		if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
303			return fmt.Errorf("forge.remote_limit must be zero (use default) or positive")
304		}

306			switch v {
307			case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
308				return true
309			}

17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil

2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"

15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}

199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}

17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.

20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}

142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}

181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}

213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}
283

1	package stats
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"strconv"
6		"strings"
7		"time"
8	
9		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/repo"
11		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
12	)
13	
14	// SampleInterval is how much time one sampler run attributes to each active
15	// session. It must match how often the sampler actually runs, so the caller
16	// passes it explicitly rather than relying on a default that silently drifts.
17	const SampleInterval = 5 * time.Minute
18	
19	// Sample attributes one interval of time to every live session whose working
20	// directory sits inside a known repository.
21	//
22	// Only sessions with a *working* agent, or any session when includeIdle is
23	// set, are counted. A workspace left open for three weeks is not three weeks
24	// of work, and counting it that way would make the whole chart meaningless.
25	func Sample(ctx context.Context, s *Store, rt runtime.Runtime, repos []repo.Repo, interval time.Duration, includeIdle bool) (int, error) {
26		sessions, err := rt.List(ctx)
27		if err != nil {
28			return 0, err
29		}
30		now := time.Now()
31		seen := map[string]bool{}
32		var entries []Entry
33	
34		for _, sess := range sessions {
35			if !includeIdle && !isActive(sess.AgentStatus) {
36				continue
37			}
38			for _, dir := range sess.Dirs {
39				r, ok := repoContaining(repos, dir)
40				if !ok {
41					continue
42				}
43				// One session covering several panes in the same repo is still one
44				// person working, so credit it once.
45				key := sess.Handle + "\x00" + r.Name
46				if seen[key] {
47					continue
48				}
49				seen[key] = true
50				branch := ""
51				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, dir); err == nil {
52					branch = st.Branch
53				}
54				entries = append(entries, Entry{
55					Day: now, Repo: r.Name, Branch: branch,
56					Source: SourceSession, Seconds: int(interval.Seconds()),
57				})
58			}
59		}
60		if err := s.Add(entries...); err != nil {
61			return 0, err
62		}
63		return len(entries), s.MarkCollected("session", now)
64	}
65	
66	// isActive reports a session doing something worth counting. Backends that
67	// report no status at all are counted, since the alternative is recording
68	// nothing on tmux.
69	func isActive(status string) bool {
70		switch strings.ToLower(status) {
71		case "working", "running", "busy", "":
72			return true
73		}
74		return false
75	}
76	
77	func repoContaining(repos []repo.Repo, dir string) (repo.Repo, bool) {
78		var best repo.Repo
79		bestLen := 0
80		for _, r := range repos {
81			if dir == r.Path || strings.HasPrefix(dir, r.Path+"/") {
82				if len(r.Path) > bestLen {
83					best, bestLen = r, len(r.Path)
84				}
85			}
86		}
87		return best, bestLen > 0
88	}
89	
90	// CommitWeight is the time credited to one commit when backfilling from git
91	// history. Commits are evidence that work happened on a day, not a measure of
92	// how long it took, so this is a coarse stand-in — enough to shade a heatmap
93	// cell, not to bill against.
94	const CommitWeight = 20 * time.Minute
95	
96	// BackfillGit reads commit history and records one CommitWeight per commit,
97	// per day, per repo.
98	//
99	// This is what makes a heatmap useful on the day dev is installed rather than
100	// three months later, and what lets the chart survive losing stats.db.
101	func BackfillGit(ctx context.Context, s *Store, repos []repo.Repo, since time.Time, author string) (int, error) {
102		var entries []Entry
103		for _, r := range repos {
104			if r.Bare {
105				continue
106			}
107			args := []string{"log", "--all", "--no-merges",
108				"--since=" + since.Format("2006-01-02"), "--format=%at%x09%aE"}
109			out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, r.Path, args...)
110			if err != nil || out == "" {
111				continue
112			}
113			// Commits land in buckets by day; several commits on one day add up.
114			perDay := map[string]int{}
115			for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
116				ts, email, _ := strings.Cut(line, "\t")
117				if author != "" && !strings.EqualFold(email, author) {
118					continue
119				}
120				unix, err := strconv.ParseInt(strings.TrimSpace(ts), 10, 64)
121				if err != nil {
122					continue
123				}
124				perDay[time.Unix(unix, 0).Format(dayFormat)]++
125			}
126			for day, count := range perDay {
127				d, err := time.ParseInLocation(dayFormat, day, time.Local)
128				if err != nil {
129					continue
130				}
131				entries = append(entries, Entry{
132					Day: d, Repo: r.Name, Source: SourceGit,
133					Seconds: count * int(CommitWeight.Seconds()),
134				})
135			}
136		}
137		// Set, not Add: re-running a backfill over the same window must not double
138		// the numbers.
139		if err := s.Set(entries...); err != nil {
140			return 0, err
141		}
142		return len(entries), s.MarkCollected("git", time.Now())
143	}
144

1	// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
18	type Session struct {
19		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
20		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
21		Handle string
22		Label  string
23		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
24		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
25		// value.
26		Dirs []string
27		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
28		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
29		AgentStatus string
30		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
31		AgentSessions []string
32		Focused       bool
33	}
34	
35	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
36	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
37		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
38			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
39			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
40			// $HOME active.
41			if d == dir || strings.HasPrefix(d, dir+"/") {
42				return true
43			}
44		}
45		return false
46	}
47	
48	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
49	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
50	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
51	type Runtime interface {
52		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
53		Name() string
54		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
55		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
56		Available() bool
57		// Open makes dir live and returns a handle. Opening something already open
58		// focuses it rather than duplicating it.
59		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error)
60		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
61		// task entry.
62		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
63		// List enumerates live sessions.
64		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
65		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
66		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
67		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
68	}
69	
70	// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
71	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
72	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
73	type WorktreeOpener interface {
74		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error)
75	}
76	
77	// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
78	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
79	
80	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
81		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
82	}
83	
84	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
85	//
86	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
87	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then None.
88	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
89	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
90		herdr, tmux, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}
91		switch backend {
92		case "herdr":
93			return herdr
94		case "tmux":
95			return tmux
96		case "none":
97			return none
98		case "", "auto":
99			if herdr.Available() {
100				return herdr
101			}
102			if tmux.Available() {
103				return tmux
104			}
105			return none
106		}
107		return none
108	}
109	
110	// All returns every backend, for `dev doctor` to report on.
111	func All() []Runtime { return []Runtime{NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}} }
112	
113	// haveBinary reports whether name is on PATH.
114	func haveBinary(name string) bool {
115		_, err := exec.LookPath(name)
116		return err == nil
117	}
118

173	func directPushHint(push bool) string {
174		if push {
175			return " --push"
176		}
177		return ""
178	}
179	
180	// fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
181	// forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
182	//
183	// merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
184	// branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
185	// a merge commit the user did not ask for.
186	func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
187		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
188		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
189			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
190				"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
191				err, config.Contract(checkout))
192		}
193		// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
194		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
195		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
196			return err
197		}
198		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
199			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
200				"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
201		}
202		return nil
203	}
204	
205	// deleteMergedBranch removes a branch only when git agrees its commits are already
206	// contained in the base — the check that makes cleanup safe.
207	func deleteMergedBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, repoPath, branch, base string) error {
208		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", branch, base); err != nil {
209			return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)
210		}
211		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "branch", "-d", branch); err != nil {
212			return fmt.Errorf("could not delete %s: %w", branch, err)
213		}
214		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   deleted    branch %s\n", branch)
215		return nil
216	}
217	
218	// openPR pushes the branch and asks the forge CLI to open a pull/merge
219	// request. When no forge CLI is available dev prints the push result and the
220	// URL to open by hand, rather than failing: the branch being published is the
221	// part that actually matters.
222	func openPR(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
223		if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
224			return err
225		}
226		kind := forge.Detect(ctx, t.RepoPath)
227		f, err := forge.For(kind)
228		if err != nil || !f.Available() {
229			app.warnf("no forge CLI for this remote — the branch is pushed; open the request in your browser")
230			return nil
231		}
232		url, err := f.CreatePR(ctx, checkout, forge.PRRequest{
233			Base: base, Head: t.Branch, Fill: true,
234		})
235		if err != nil {
236			return err
237		}
238		if url != "" {
239			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   opened     %s\n", url)
240		}
241		return nil
242	}

15	func newParkCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
16		var (
17			next   string
18			note   string
19			wip    bool
20			push   bool
21			cold   bool
22			keepRT bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "park [task]",
26			Short: "Stop working on a task without losing the thread",
27			Long: `Park the current task (or the one named) so its runtime session can close.
28	
29	Parking is the missing move that makes a crowded sidebar shrink. It records
30	what to do next, optionally checkpoints uncommitted work, and closes the
31	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
32	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.
33	
34	  warm (default)  worktree and branch stay; session closes. Back within days.
35	  cold (--cold)   work is committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstruct
36	                  it anywhere later with dev resume.
37	
38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
41			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
42			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
43				ctx := ctxOf()
44				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
45				if err != nil {
46					return err
47				}
48	
49				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
50				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
51					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
52						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
53				}
54				target := task.Warm
55				if cold {
56					target = task.Cold
57				}
58				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
59	
60				if next != "" {
61					t.Next = next
62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69	
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97	
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114	
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}
124	
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes
133					// the task reconstructible rather than lost.
134					t.WorktreePath = ""
135				}
136				if cold && mode == task.ModeBranch {
137					// Free the canonical checkout for other work. The branch remains
138					// local + remote and resume switches back to it.
139					base := t.Base
140					if base == "" {
141						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
142					}
143					if base == "" {
144						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but its base branch is unknown")
145					}
146					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
147						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
148							base, err)
149					}
150				}
151	
152				t.State = target
153				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
154				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
155					return err
156				}
157				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
158				if t.Next != "" {
159					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
160				}
161				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
162				return nil
163			},
164		}
165		f := cmd.Flags()
166		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
167		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
168		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
169		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
170		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
171		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
172		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app, task.Hot, task.Warm)
173		return cmd
174	}
175	
176	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
177	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
178		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
179			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
180		}
181		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
182		return nil
183	}
184	
185	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
186	// directory when no argument is given.
187	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
188		if len(args) == 1 {
189			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
190		}
191		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
196		if err != nil {
197			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
198				config.Contract(cwd))
199		}
200		return t, nil
201	}

218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}

147	// not trigger file completions.

149	// This method satisfies [CompletionFunc].

151	func NoFileCompletions(cmd *Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]Completion, ShellCompDirective) {
152		return nil, ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp

156	// returns the same results.

159	// It can be used with [Command.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc] and for [Command.ValidArgsFunction].
160	func FixedCompletions(choices []Completion, directive ShellCompDirective) CompletionFunc {
161		return func(cmd *Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]Completion, ShellCompDirective) {
162			return choices, directive
163		}
164	}

166	// RegisterFlagCompletionFunc should be called to register a function to provide completion for a flag.
167	//
168	// You can use pre-defined completion functions such as [FixedCompletions] or [NoFileCompletions],
169	// or you can define your own.
170	func (c *Command) RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(flagName string, f CompletionFunc) error {
171		flag := c.Flag(flagName)
172		if flag == nil {
173			return fmt.Errorf("RegisterFlagCompletionFunc: flag '%s' does not exist", flagName)
174		}
175		flagCompletionMutex.Lock()
176		defer flagCompletionMutex.Unlock()
177	
178		if _, exists := flagCompletionFunctions[flag]; exists {
179			return fmt.Errorf("RegisterFlagCompletionFunc: flag '%s' already registered", flagName)
180		}
181		flagCompletionFunctions[flag] = f
182		return nil
183	}

The completion layer exposes a deeper identity split: most repository arguments insert `Category/Name` or a path, while stats/list completion has a separate “basename only” mode because those stores persist `Repo.Name`. With two projects sharing a basename, completion can display both contexts but can only insert the same token, so filtering/clearing cannot target one project; I’m tracing each `--repo` consumer to distinguish this domain flaw from harmless presentation differences.

1	// Package inventory joins the three sources that describe work in progress:
2	// the task registry (human intent), git (durable code state) and the runtime
3	// (what is live right now). It is the single code path behind `dev ls`,
4	// `dev status`, `dev sweep` and the TUI, so all four can never disagree.
5	package inventory
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"os"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"sync"
13		"time"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
18	)
19	
20	// Row is one task enriched with everything derived live.
21	type Row struct {
22		Task *task.Task
23	
24		// Checkout is where the task's code currently lives: its worktree if it
25		// has one, else the repo. Empty when nothing exists on disk.
26		Checkout string
27		// CheckoutExists reports whether that directory is actually present. A
28		// cold task, or one whose worktree was removed behind dev's back, is not.
29		CheckoutExists bool
30		// WorktreeMissing flags a task that records a worktree path which is no
31		// longer a registered git worktree — the drift `dev sweep` reports.
32		WorktreeMissing bool
33	
34		// Status is the live git status of Checkout. Zero when there is nothing
35		// on disk to inspect.
36		Status    gitx.Status
37		StatusErr error
38	
39		// LastCommit is the author time of HEAD, used to age a task.
40		LastCommit time.Time
41	
42		// Session is the live runtime session hosting this checkout, if any.
43		Session *runtime.Session
44		// sessionsTracked reports whether the runtime can observe sessions at all.
45		// With the "none" backend it cannot, so "hot but nothing live" is not
46		// drift — it is the only state that backend can ever produce.
47		sessionsTracked bool
48	}
49	
50	// Live reports whether a runtime session is currently hosting this task.
51	func (r Row) Live() bool { return r.Session != nil }
52	
53	// StateDrift reports a task whose recorded state disagrees with reality:
54	// hot with no live session, or warm/cold with one. It is what `dev sweep`
55	// turns into suggestions — dev reports drift and never silently rewrites it.
56	func (r Row) StateDrift() string {
57		if r.sessionsTracked {
58			switch r.Task.State {
59			case task.Hot:
60				if !r.Live() {
61					return "no live session"
62				}
63			case task.Warm, task.Cold:
64				if r.Live() {
65					return "session is live"
66				}
67			}
68		}
69		if r.Task.State == task.Cold && r.CheckoutExists && r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
70			return "worktree still on disk"
71		}
72		if r.WorktreeMissing {
73			return "worktree is gone"
74		}
75		return ""
76	}
77	
78	// Age is how long since the task's last commit, falling back to when the entry
79	// was last written for a task with no commits of its own.
80	func (r Row) Age() time.Duration {
81		ref := r.LastCommit
82		if ref.IsZero() || r.Task.Updated.After(ref) {
83			ref = r.Task.Updated
84		}
85		if ref.IsZero() {
86			return 0
87		}
88		return time.Since(ref)
89	}
90	
91	// Options tunes what a Collect call spends time on.
92	type Options struct {
93		// SkipRuntime avoids querying the multiplexer, for callers that only need
94		// git facts (and for tests).
95		SkipRuntime bool
96		// SkipGit avoids running git per task, for a fast listing.
97		SkipGit bool
98	}
99	
100	// Collect builds the enriched inventory. Git probes run concurrently: each is
101	// a handful of process spawns, and a machine with dozens of tasks would
102	// otherwise make `dev ls` feel slow.
103	func Collect(ctx context.Context, tasks []*task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opts Options) []Row {
104		rows := make([]Row, len(tasks))
105	
106		var sessions []runtime.Session
107		tracked := false
108		if !opts.SkipRuntime && rt != nil && rt.Name() != "none" {
109			if s, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
110				sessions, tracked = s, true
111			}
112		}
113	
114		var wg sync.WaitGroup
115		// Bound concurrency: git is process-heavy and an unbounded fan-out over a
116		// large inventory would thrash.
117		sem := make(chan struct{}, 8)
118	
119		for i, t := range tasks {
120			rows[i].Task = t
121			rows[i].Checkout = checkoutOf(t)
122	
123			if opts.SkipGit || rows[i].Checkout == "" {
124				continue
125			}
126			wg.Add(1)
127			go func(i int) {
128				defer wg.Done()
129				sem <- struct{}{}
130				defer func() { <-sem }()
131				enrich(ctx, &rows[i])
132			}(i)
133		}
134		wg.Wait()
135	
136		for i := range rows {
137			rows[i].Session = matchSession(sessions, rows[i])
138			rows[i].sessionsTracked = tracked
139		}
140		return rows
141	}
142	
143	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
144		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
145			return t.WorktreePath
146		}
147		return t.RepoPath
148	}
149	
150	func enrich(ctx context.Context, r *Row) {
151		info, err := os.Stat(r.Checkout)
152		r.CheckoutExists = err == nil && info.IsDir()
153		if !r.CheckoutExists {
154			if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
155				r.WorktreeMissing = true
156			}
157			return
158		}
159		if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Checkout); err != nil {
160			r.StatusErr = err
161		} else {
162			r.Status = st
163		}
164		if unix, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, r.Checkout); err == nil && unix > 0 {
165			r.LastCommit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
166		}
167		// A recorded worktree that git no longer knows about is drift worth
168		// surfacing: the directory may exist while the administrative entry is gone.
169		if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
170			if _, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, r.Task.RepoPath, r.Task.Branch); err == nil && !ok {
171				r.WorktreeMissing = true
172			}
173		}
174	}
175	
176	// matchSession picks the runtime session hosting a row's checkout. An exact
177	// directory match is preferred over a containing one, so a worktree's own
178	// session always wins over the parent repo's.
179	func matchSession(sessions []runtime.Session, r Row) *runtime.Session {
180		if r.Checkout == "" {
181			return nil
182		}
183		var contains *runtime.Session
184		for i := range sessions {
185			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
186				if d == r.Checkout {
187					return &sessions[i]
188				}
189				if strings.HasPrefix(d, r.Checkout+"/") && contains == nil {
190					contains = &sessions[i]
191				}
192			}
193		}
194		return contains
195	}
196	
197	// Filter narrows rows by state and repo. An empty filter matches everything.
198	type Filter struct {
199		States []task.State
200		Repo   string
201		// LiveOnly keeps only tasks with a runtime session.
202		LiveOnly bool
203		// DirtyOnly keeps only tasks with uncommitted work.
204		DirtyOnly bool
205	}
206	
207	// Apply returns the rows matching f.
208	func (f Filter) Apply(rows []Row) []Row {
209		out := rows[:0:0]
210		for _, r := range rows {
211			if len(f.States) > 0 && !containsState(f.States, r.Task.State) {
212				continue
213			}
214			if f.Repo != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Task.Repo), strings.ToLower(f.Repo)) {
215				continue
216			}
217			if f.LiveOnly && !r.Live() {
218				continue
219			}
220			if f.DirtyOnly && !r.Status.Dirty() {
221				continue
222			}
223			out = append(out, r)
224		}
225		return out
226	}
227	
228	func containsState(list []task.State, s task.State) bool {
229		for _, v := range list {
230			if v == s {
231				return true
232			}
233		}
234		return false
235	}
236	
237	// Orphans reports live runtime sessions that no task claims — the "I opened
238	// this and never wrote it down" case that makes a sidebar grow without bound.
239	func Orphans(sessions []runtime.Session, rows []Row) []runtime.Session {
240		claimed := map[string]bool{}
241		for _, r := range rows {
242			if r.Session != nil {
243				claimed[r.Session.Handle] = true
244			}
245		}
246		var out []runtime.Session
247		for _, s := range sessions {
248			if !claimed[s.Handle] {
249				out = append(out, s)
250			}
251		}
252		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Label < out[j].Label })
253		return out
254	}
