```text
1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123	
124		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
125		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`

127	
128	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}
141	
142	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}

20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}

52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}

106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {

110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err

114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {

117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue

120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")

124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}

133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}

142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}

181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}

213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}

```text
1	// Package stats records where development time actually goes, and renders it
2	// as a contribution-style heatmap.
3	//
4	// Two sources, because neither alone is honest. A sampler watches live agent
5	// and terminal sessions, which is the only way to count the hours spent
6	// reading and debugging rather than committing. Git history backfills the days
7	// before dev was installed and survives a lost database. WakaTime, when
8	// enabled, adds editor time dev cannot observe from the terminal.
9	package stats
10	
11	import (
12		"database/sql"
13		"os"
14		"path/filepath"
15		"time"
16	
17		_ "modernc.org/sqlite"
18	)
19	
20	// Source labels where a measurement came from, so double counting is visible
21	// rather than silent: the same hour can legitimately appear from the sampler
22	// and from WakaTime, and a query decides which to trust.
23	type Source string
24	
25	const (
26		// SourceSession is dev's own sampler watching live runtime sessions.
27		SourceSession Source = "session"
28		// SourceGit is derived from commit timestamps.
29		SourceGit Source = "git"
30		// SourceWakaTime is imported from the WakaTime API.
31		SourceWakaTime Source = "wakatime"
32	)
33	
34	// Store is the activity database.
35	type Store struct{ db *sql.DB }
36	
37	// Open creates or opens the database at path.
38	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
39		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
40			return nil, err
41		}
42		// A short busy timeout matters: the sampler may run from cron while an
43		// interactive `dev stats` is reading.
44		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", path+"?_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)")
45		if err != nil {
46			return nil, err
47		}
48		s := &Store{db: db}
49		if err := s.migrate(); err != nil {
50			db.Close()
51			return nil, err
52		}
53		return s, nil
54	}
55	
56	// Close releases the database.
57	func (s *Store) Close() error { return s.db.Close() }
58	
59	func (s *Store) migrate() error {
60		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
61	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS activity (
62	  day     TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- local date, YYYY-MM-DD
63	  repo    TEXT    NOT NULL,
64	  branch  TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
65	  source  TEXT    NOT NULL,
66	  seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
67	  PRIMARY KEY (day, repo, branch, source)
68	);
69	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS activity_day  ON activity(day);
70	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS activity_repo ON activity(repo);
71	
72	-- Records the last successful run of each collector, so a backfill can pick up
73	-- where it left off instead of rescanning every repo's whole history.
74	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS collector (
75	  name    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
76	  last_at INTEGER NOT NULL
77	);
78	`)
79		return err
80	}
81	
82	// Entry is one measurement.
83	type Entry struct {
84		Day     time.Time
85		Repo    string
86		Branch  string
87		Source  Source
88		Seconds int
89	}
90	
91	// Add accumulates seconds onto a (day, repo, branch, source) bucket.
92	func (s *Store) Add(entries ...Entry) error {
93		if len(entries) == 0 {
94			return nil
95		}
96		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
97		if err != nil {
98			return err
99		}
100		defer tx.Rollback()
101	
102		stmt, err := tx.Prepare(`
103	INSERT INTO activity (day, repo, branch, source, seconds) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
104	ON CONFLICT (day, repo, branch, source) DO UPDATE SET seconds = seconds + excluded.seconds`)
105		if err != nil {
106			return err
107		}
108		defer stmt.Close()
109	
110		for _, e := range entries {
111			if e.Seconds <= 0 || e.Repo == "" {
112				continue
113			}
114			if _, err := stmt.Exec(e.Day.Format(dayFormat), e.Repo, e.Branch, string(e.Source), e.Seconds); err != nil {
115				return err
116			}
117		}
118		return tx.Commit()
119	}
120	
121	// Set replaces a bucket rather than accumulating. Used by importers that are
122	// re-runnable: WakaTime reports the same day's total again on every import, so
123	// adding would inflate it.
124	func (s *Store) Set(entries ...Entry) error {
125		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
126		if err != nil {
127			return err
128		}
129		defer tx.Rollback()
130	
131		stmt, err := tx.Prepare(`
132	INSERT INTO activity (day, repo, branch, source, seconds) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
133	ON CONFLICT (day, repo, branch, source) DO UPDATE SET seconds = excluded.seconds`)
134		if err != nil {
135			return err
136		}
137		defer stmt.Close()
138	
139		for _, e := range entries {
140			if e.Repo == "" {
141				continue
142			}
143			if _, err := stmt.Exec(e.Day.Format(dayFormat), e.Repo, e.Branch, string(e.Source), e.Seconds); err != nil {
144				return err
145			}
146		}
147		return tx.Commit()
148	}
149	
150	const dayFormat = "2006-01-02"
151	
152	// Query narrows a report.
153	type Query struct {
154		Since time.Time
155		Until time.Time
156		Repo  string
157		// ExactRepo uses equality rather than the report-friendly substring match.
158		// Per-repo TUI panels set it so "api" does not include "my-api".
159		ExactRepo bool
160		// Sources limits which collectors count. Empty means all of them.
161		Sources []Source
162	}
163	
164	func (q Query) where() (string, []any) {
165		clause := "WHERE day >= ? AND day <= ?"
166		args := []any{q.Since.Format(dayFormat), q.Until.Format(dayFormat)}
167		if q.Repo != "" {
168			if q.ExactRepo {
169				clause += " AND repo = ?"
170				args = append(args, q.Repo)
171			} else {
172				clause += " AND repo LIKE ?"
173				args = append(args, "%"+q.Repo+"%")
174			}
175		}
176		if len(q.Sources) > 0 {
177			clause += " AND source IN (" + placeholders(len(q.Sources)) + ")"
178			for _, s := range q.Sources {
179				args = append(args, string(s))
180			}
181		}
182		return clause, args
183	}
184	
185	func placeholders(n int) string {
186		if n == 0 {
187			return ""
188		}
189		out := make([]byte, 0, n*2-1)
190		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
191			if i > 0 {
192				out = append(out, ',')
193			}
194			out = append(out, '?')
195		}
196		return string(out)
197	}
198	
199	// DayTotals returns seconds per calendar day.
200	func (s *Store) DayTotals(q Query) (map[string]int, error) {
201		clause, args := q.where()
202		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT day, SUM(seconds) FROM activity `+clause+` GROUP BY day`, args...)
203		if err != nil {
204			return nil, err
205		}
206		defer rows.Close()
207	
208		out := map[string]int{}
209		for rows.Next() {
210			var day string
211			var secs int
212			if err := rows.Scan(&day, &secs); err != nil {
213				return nil, err
214			}
215			out[day] = secs
216		}
217		return out, rows.Err()
218	}
219	
220	// RepoTotal is one row of the per-repo breakdown.
221	type RepoTotal struct {
222		Repo    string
223		Seconds int
224		Days    int
225		Last    string
226	}
227	
228	// RepoTotals returns seconds per repository, busiest first.
229	func (s *Store) RepoTotals(q Query) ([]RepoTotal, error) {
230		clause, args := q.where()
231		rows, err := s.db.Query(`
232	SELECT repo, SUM(seconds) AS secs, COUNT(DISTINCT day) AS days, MAX(day)
233	FROM activity `+clause+`
234	GROUP BY repo ORDER BY secs DESC`, args...)
235		if err != nil {
236			return nil, err
237		}
238		defer rows.Close()
239	
240		var out []RepoTotal
241		for rows.Next() {
242			var r RepoTotal
243			if err := rows.Scan(&r.Repo, &r.Seconds, &r.Days, &r.Last); err != nil {
244				return nil, err
245			}
246			out = append(out, r)
247		}
248		return out, rows.Err()
249	}
250	
251	// RepoDayTotals returns per-day seconds for one repository, for a per-repo
252	// heatmap.
253	func (s *Store) RepoDayTotals(repo string, q Query) (map[string]int, error) {
254		q.Repo = repo
255		return s.DayTotals(q)
256	}
257	
258	// MarkCollected records that a collector ran, so incremental runs know their
259	// starting point.
260	func (s *Store) MarkCollected(name string, at time.Time) error {
261		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
262	INSERT INTO collector (name, last_at) VALUES (?, ?)
263	ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET last_at = excluded.last_at`, name, at.Unix())
264		return err
265	}
266	
267	// LastCollected reports when a collector last ran, zero when never.
268	func (s *Store) LastCollected(name string) time.Time {
269		var unix int64
270		if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT last_at FROM collector WHERE name = ?`, name).Scan(&unix); err != nil {
271			return time.Time{}
272		}
273		return time.Unix(unix, 0)
274	}
275	
276	// Empty reports whether anything has been recorded yet, so the CLI can explain
277	// how to start collecting instead of printing a blank chart.
278	func (s *Store) Empty() bool {
279		var n int
280		if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activity`).Scan(&n); err != nil {
281			return true
282		}
283		return n == 0
284	}
285	
286	// Path is where the database lives inside a state directory.
287	func Path(stateDir string) string { return filepath.Join(stateDir, "stats.db") }
288	
289	// ClearQuery selects durable activity rows to delete. Repo is an exact name —
290	// deletion must not use the fuzzy LIKE semantics a report does.
291	type ClearQuery struct {
292		Repo    string
293		Sources []Source
294	}
295	
296	// Clear deletes matching activity and returns the number of rows removed.
297	// With an empty query it clears all activity and collector checkpoints.
298	func (s *Store) Clear(q ClearQuery) (int64, error) {
299		clause := ""
300		var args []any
301		if q.Repo != "" {
302			clause = " WHERE repo = ?"
303			args = append(args, q.Repo)
304		}
305		if len(q.Sources) > 0 {
306			if clause == "" {
307				clause = " WHERE "
308			} else {
309				clause += " AND "
310			}
311			clause += "source IN (" + placeholders(len(q.Sources)) + ")"
312			for _, source := range q.Sources {
313				args = append(args, string(source))
314			}
315		}
316		result, err := s.db.Exec("DELETE FROM activity"+clause, args...)
317		if err != nil {
318			return 0, err
319		}
320		if q.Repo == "" && len(q.Sources) == 0 {
321			if _, err := s.db.Exec("DELETE FROM collector"); err != nil {
322				return 0, err
323			}
324		}
325		return result.RowsAffected()
326	}

27	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
28	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
29	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
30		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
31		if err != nil {
32			return nil, err
33		}
34		var (
35			list []Worktree
36			cur  *Worktree
37		)
38		flush := func() {
39			if cur != nil {
40				list = append(list, *cur)
41				cur = nil
42			}
43		}
44		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
45			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
46				flush()
47				continue
48			}
49			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
50			switch key {
51			case "worktree":
52				flush()
53				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
54			case "HEAD":
55				if cur != nil {
56					cur.Head = val
57				}
58			case "branch":
59				if cur != nil {
60					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
61				}
62			case "detached":
63				if cur != nil {
64					cur.Detached = true
65				}
66			case "bare":
67				if cur != nil {
68					cur.Bare = true
69				}
70			case "locked":
71				if cur != nil {
72					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
73				}
74			case "prunable":
75				if cur != nil {
76					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
77				}
78			}
79		}
80		flush()
81		return list, nil
82	}

84	// WorktreeFor finds the worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git refuses to
85	// check the same branch out twice, so at most one can match.
86	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
87		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
88		if err != nil {
89			return Worktree{}, false, err
90		}
91		for _, w := range list {
92			if w.Branch == branch {
93				return w, true, nil
94			}
95		}
96		return Worktree{}, false, nil
97	}

99	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
100	//
101	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
102	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
103	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
104	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
105	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
106		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
107		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
108		if exists {
109			args = append(args, path, branch)
110		} else {
111			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
112			if base != "" {
113				args = append(args, base)
114			}
115		}
116		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
117		return err
118	}
119	
120	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
121	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
122	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
123		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
124		if force {
125			args = append(args, "--force")
126		}
127		args = append(args, path)
128		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
129		return err
130	}
131	
132	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
133	// were deleted behind git's back.
134	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
135		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
136		return err
137	}
138	
139	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
140	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
141		if branch == "" {
142			return false
143		}
144		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
145		return err == nil
146	}
147

149	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
150		if ref == "" {
151			return false
152		}
153		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
154		return err == nil
155	}

38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
41			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
42			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
43				ctx := ctxOf()
44				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
45				if err != nil {
46					return err
47				}
48	
49				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
50				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
51					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
52						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
53				}
54				target := task.Warm
55				if cold {
56					target = task.Cold
57				}
58				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
59	
60				if next != "" {
61					t.Next = next
62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69	
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97	
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114	
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}
124	
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes
133					// the task reconstructible rather than lost.
134					t.WorktreePath = ""
135				}
136				if cold && mode == task.ModeBranch {
137					// Free the canonical checkout for other work. The branch remains
138					// local + remote and resume switches back to it.
139					base := t.Base
140					if base == "" {
141						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
142					}
143					if base == "" {
144						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but its base branch is unknown")
145					}
146					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
147						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
148							base, err)
149					}
150				}
151	
152				t.State = target
153				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
154				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
155					return err
156				}
157				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
158				if t.Next != "" {
159					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
160				}
161				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
162				return nil
163			},
164		}
165		f := cmd.Flags()
166		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
167		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
168		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
169		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
170		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
171		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
172		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app, task.Hot, task.Warm)
173		return cmd
174	}
175	
176	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
177	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
178		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
179			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
180		}
181		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
182		return nil
183	}
184	
185	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
186	// directory when no argument is given.
187	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
188		if len(args) == 1 {
189			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
190		}

14	func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

24	
25	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
26	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
27	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
28	identity.
29	
30	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
33			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),

36				t, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
37				if err != nil {
38					return err
39				}
40	
41				host := config.Hostname()
42				if !t.OwnedBy(host) && !force {
43					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is owned by %s.\n"+
44						"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
45						t.ID, t.Owner)
46				}
47	
48				if fetch {

50						app.warnf("fetch failed: %v", err)
51					}
52				}
53	
54				rt := app.Runtime()
55				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
56				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
57	
58				switch mode {
59				case task.ModeWorktree:
60					_, statErr := os.Stat(checkout)
61					// Rebuild the worktree when it is gone — the cold-to-hot path.
62					if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
63						base := t.Base
64						// Prefer the published branch: a cold task's work lives on
65						// the remote, and a stale local ref could drop it.
66						if remote := "origin/" + t.Branch; gitx.RefExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, remote) {
67							base = remote
68						}
69						m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
70						res, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
71							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, RepoName: t.Repo, Branch: t.Branch,
72							Base: base, Label: t.Title(), NoProvision: noProvision,
73						})

79								return err
80							}
81						} else {
82							t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = res.Path, res.RuntimeHandle
83							reportProvision(app, res)
84							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebuilt    %s\n", config.Contract(res.Path))
85						}
86						checkout = t.WorktreePath
87					}
88	
89				case task.ModeBranch:
90					checkout = t.RepoPath
91					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
92					if err != nil {
93						return err
94					}
95					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
96						if st.Dirty() {

98								st.Branch, t.Branch, st.Breakdown())

113							"switch back explicitly or start a worktree task", t.Title(), t.Branch, st.Branch)

248					// 2- Even without completions, we need to print the directive

266						comp = strings.SplitN(comp, "\t", 2)[0]

270					// This is needed if a description contains a linebreak.
271					// Otherwise the shell scripts will interpret the other lines as new flags
272					// and could therefore provide a wrong completion.
273					comp = strings.SplitN(comp, "\n", 2)[0]

275					// Finally trim the completion.  This is especially important to get rid
276					// of a trailing tab when there are no description following it.
277					// For example, a sub-command without a description should not be completed

279					// although there is no description).

291				// Print some helpful info to stderr for the user to understand.
292				// Output from stderr must be ignored by the completion script.
293				fmt.Fprintf(finalCmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Completion ended with directive: %s\n", directive.string())

142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}

8	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
9	type Worktree struct {
10		Path string
11		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
12		Head string
13		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
14		Branch   string
15		Detached bool
16		Bare     bool
17		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
18		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
19		Locked         bool
20		LockedReason   string
21		Prunable       bool
22		PrunableReason string
23		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
24		Main bool
25	}
26	
27	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
28	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
29	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
30		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
31		if err != nil {
32			return nil, err
33		}
34		var (
35			list []Worktree
36			cur  *Worktree
37		)
38		flush := func() {
39			if cur != nil {
40				list = append(list, *cur)
41				cur = nil
42			}
43		}
44		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
45			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
46				flush()
47				continue
48			}
49			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
50			switch key {
51			case "worktree":
52				flush()
53				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
54			case "HEAD":
55				if cur != nil {
56					cur.Head = val
57				}
58			case "branch":
59				if cur != nil {
60					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
61				}
62			case "detached":
63				if cur != nil {
64					cur.Detached = true
65				}
66			case "bare":
67				if cur != nil {
68					cur.Bare = true
69				}
70			case "locked":
71				if cur != nil {
72					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
73				}
74			case "prunable":
75				if cur != nil {
76					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
77				}
78			}
79		}
80		flush()
81		return list, nil
82	}
83	
84	// WorktreeFor finds the worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git refuses to
85	// check the same branch out twice, so at most one can match.
86	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
87		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
88		if err != nil {
89			return Worktree{}, false, err
90		}
91		for _, w := range list {
92			if w.Branch == branch {
93				return w, true, nil
94			}
95		}
96		return Worktree{}, false, nil
97	}
98	
99	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
100	//
101	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
102	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
103	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
104	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
105	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
106		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
107		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
108		if exists {
109			args = append(args, path, branch)
110		} else {
111			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
112			if base != "" {
113				args = append(args, base)
114			}
115		}
116		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
117		return err
118	}
119	
120	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
121	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
122	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
123		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
124		if force {
125			args = append(args, "--force")
126		}
127		args = append(args, path)
128		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
129		return err
130	}
131	
132	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
133	// were deleted behind git's back.
134	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
135		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
136		return err
137	}
138	
139	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
140	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
141		if branch == "" {
142			return false
143		}
144		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)

40	creates the remote with gh or glab.
41	
42	With no argument, the try containing the current directory is used.`,
43			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
44			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
45				ctx := ctxOf()
46				triesRoot := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot)
47	
48				src, err := resolveTry(app, triesRoot, args)
49				if err != nil {
50					return err
51				}
52				if name == "" {
53					name = datePrefix.ReplaceAllString(filepath.Base(src), "")
54				}
55				if name == "" {
56					return fmt.Errorf("could not derive a project name from %s — pass --name", src)
57				}
58	
59				dest := filepath.Join(config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot), category, name)
60				if _, err := os.Stat(dest); err == nil {
61					return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists", config.Contract(dest))
62				}
63	
64				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "graduate  %s\n", config.Contract(src))
65				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "       →  %s\n", config.Contract(dest))
66				if dryRun {
67					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\n(dry run — nothing moved)")
68					return nil
69				}
70	
71				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dest), 0o755); err != nil {
72					return err
73				}
74				// Rename first: it is atomic within a filesystem and leaves
75				// nothing half-copied if it fails.
76				if err := os.Rename(src, dest); err != nil {
77					return fmt.Errorf("move %s: %w\n"+
78						"If the projects root is on another filesystem, copy it by hand and remove the try",
79						config.Contract(src), err)
80				}
81	
82				if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dest, ".git")); err != nil {
83					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dest, "init", "-b", "main"); err != nil {
84						return err
85					}
86					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   git init")
87				}
88				// An experiment usually has files but no commit. A project needs
89				// one: without a HEAD there is no default branch, so `dev start`
90				// would have nothing to base a worktree on.
91				if made, err := ensureInitialCommit(ctx, dest, name); err != nil {
92					app.warnf("could not make an initial commit: %v", err)
93				} else if made {
94					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   committed the existing work")
95				}
96	
97				if remote {
98					f, err := forge.Preferred()
99					if err != nil {
100						app.warnf("%v — the project is in place; add a remote by hand", err)
101					} else {
102						url, err := f.CreateRepo(ctx, dest, forge.RepoRequest{
103							Name: name, Private: private, Push: push,
104						})
105						if err != nil {
106							app.warnf("could not create the remote: %v", err)
107						} else {
108							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   remote    %s\n", url)
109						}
110					}
111				}
112	
113				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%s is now a project. Start work on it with:\n  dev start %s --task <name>\n",
114					name, name)
115				return openOrCD(app, ctx, dest, name)
116			},
117		}
118		f := cmd.Flags()
119		f.StringVarP(&category, "category", "c", "", "category subdirectory under project_root")
120		f.StringVar(&name, "name", "", "project name (default: the try name without its date prefix)")
121		f.BoolVar(&private, "private", true, "create the remote as private")
122		f.BoolVar(&remote, "remote", false, "create a remote repository with gh or glab")
123		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", true, "push after creating the remote")
124		f.BoolVar(&dryRun, "dry-run", false, "show what would happen without moving anything")
125		return cmd
126	}
127	
128	// resolveTry finds the try directory to graduate: an explicit reference, or
129	// the try containing the current directory.
130	func resolveTry(app *App, triesRoot string, args []string) (string, error) {
131		if len(args) == 1 {
132			ref := args[0]
133			if abs := config.Expand(ref); isDir(abs) {
134				return abs, nil
135			}
136			direct := filepath.Join(triesRoot, ref)
137			if isDir(direct) {
138				return direct, nil
139			}
140			if match := findTry(triesRoot, ref); match != "" {
141				return match, nil
142			}
143			return "", fmt.Errorf("no try matching %q under %s", ref, config.Contract(triesRoot))
144		}
145	
146		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
147		if err != nil {
148			return "", err
149		}
150		if !strings.HasPrefix(cwd, triesRoot+string(filepath.Separator)) {
151			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s is not inside %s — name the try to graduate",
152				config.Contract(cwd), config.Contract(triesRoot))
153		}
154		// Walk up to the try's own top-level directory, so running this from a
155		// subdirectory still graduates the whole experiment.
156		rel, _ := filepath.Rel(triesRoot, cwd)
157		first := strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator))[0]
158		return filepath.Join(triesRoot, first), nil
159	}
160	
161	func isDir(p string) bool {
162		info, err := os.Stat(p)
163		return err == nil && info.IsDir()
164	}
165	
166	// ensureInitialCommit gives a repository a first commit if it has none,
167	// seeding a README when the tree is otherwise empty. Reports whether it made
168	// one.
169	func ensureInitialCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) (bool, error) {
170		if _, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, dir); err == nil {
171			return false, nil // already has history
172		}
173		if empty, err := isEmptyTree(dir); err != nil {
174			return false, err
175		} else if empty {
176			readme := filepath.Join(dir, "README.md")
177			if err := os.WriteFile(readme, []byte("# "+name+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
178				return false, err
179			}
180		}
181		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
182			return false, err
183		}
184		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "commit", "-m", "chore: graduate experiment into a project"); err != nil {
185			return false, err
186		}
187		return true, nil
188	}
189	
190	// isEmptyTree reports a directory with nothing in it but git's own metadata.

50	}

54	type Worktree struct {
55		// Include lists .gitignore-syntax patterns; matching files are copied into
56		// a new worktree only when they are actually gitignored in the source
57		// checkout. Tracked files are already in the checkout.
58		Include []string `toml:"include"`
59		// Link names directories symlinked rather than copied (opt-in: sharing
60		// node_modules across checkouts breaks native builds often enough that it
61		// must never be a default).
62		Link []string `toml:"link"`
63		// PostCreate is either the string "auto" (detect from lockfiles) or an
64		// explicit list of shell commands run in the new worktree.
65		PostCreate PostCreate `toml:"post_create"`
66		// Strategy is how a new worktree gets its installed dependencies:
67		// "reinstall" (correct, the default), "copy", "link" or "skip". dev
68		// narrows an unsound choice back to reinstall and says why — copying a
69		// virtualenv, for instance, cannot work, because it bakes its own
70		// absolute path into pyvenv.cfg.
71		Strategy string `toml:"strategy"`
72		// Strategies overrides Strategy per ecosystem ("python", "node", "go",
73		// "rust", "ruby", "elixir").
74		Strategies map[string]string `toml:"strategies"`
75		// ProvisionTimeout caps a single post-create command.

92		// wandering through a mounted filesystem forever.

654	func checkIfFlagCompletion(finalCmd *Command, args []string, lastArg string) (*pflag.Flag, []string, string, error) {
655		if finalCmd.DisableFlagParsing {
656			// We only do flag completion if we are allowed to parse flags
657			// This is important for commands which have requested to do their own flag completion.
658			return nil, args, lastArg, nil
659		}
660	
661		var flagName string
662		trimmedArgs := args
663		flagWithEqual := false
664		orgLastArg := lastArg
665	
666		// When doing completion of a flag name, as soon as an argument starts with
667		// a '-' we know it is a flag.  We cannot use isFlagArg() here as that function
668		// requires the flag name to be complete
669		if len(lastArg) > 0 && lastArg[0] == '-' {
670			if index := strings.Index(lastArg, "="); index >= 0 {
671				// Flag with an =
672				if strings.HasPrefix(lastArg[:index], "--") {
673					// Flag has full name
674					flagName = lastArg[2:index]
675				} else {
676					// Flag is shorthand
677					// We have to get the last shorthand flag name
678					// e.g. `-asd` => d to provide the correct completion
679					// https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1257
680					flagName = lastArg[index-1 : index]
681				}
682				lastArg = lastArg[index+1:]
683				flagWithEqual = true
684			} else {
685				// Normal flag completion
686				return nil, args, lastArg, nil
687			}
688		}
689	
690		if len(flagName) == 0 {
691			if len(args) > 0 {
692				prevArg := args[len(args)-1]
693				if isFlagArg(prevArg) {
694					// Only consider the case where the flag does not contain an =.
695					// If the flag contains an = it means it has already been fully processed,
696					// so we don't need to deal with it here.
697					if index := strings.Index(prevArg, "="); index < 0 {
698						if strings.HasPrefix(prevArg, "--") {
699							// Flag has full name
700							flagName = prevArg[2:]
701						} else {
702							// Flag is shorthand
703							// We have to get the last shorthand flag name
704							// e.g. `-asd` => d to provide the correct completion
705							// https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1257
706							flagName = prevArg[len(prevArg)-1:]
707						}
708						// Remove the uncompleted flag or else there could be an error created
709						// for an invalid value for that flag
710						trimmedArgs = args[:len(args)-1]
711					}
712				}
713			}
714		}
715	
716		if len(flagName) == 0 {
717			// Not doing flag completion
718			return nil, trimmedArgs, lastArg, nil
719		}
720

722		if flag == nil {

724			return nil, args, orgLastArg, &flagCompError{subCommand: finalCmd.Name(), flagName: flagName}
725		}
726	
727		if !flagWithEqual {

730				// In that case, there is no value following it, so we are not really doing flag completion.
731				// Reset everything to do noun completion.
732				trimmedArgs = args

734			}
735		}
736	
737		return flag, trimmedArgs, lastArg, nil
738	}

A nested `dev` launched by a post-create hook can write the first NUL record into the outer invocation’s file, causing the wrapper to change to the nested command’s directory; I’m confirming the exec environment path and then ranking this against the lifecycle/identity findings.

1	// Package wt creates, provisions and removes the linked worktrees dev owns.
2	//
3	// Ownership, stated once so agents and humans stop improvising: dev owns every

7	// that dies with the turn. dev never calls `herdr worktree create`, because
8	// the path policy has to hold on machines without herdr; it creates the

10	package wt

12	import (

24	// Provisioner brings a fresh checkout up to a working state.
25	//
26	// A worktree is a clean checkout: no node_modules, no .venv, and none of the
27	// gitignored env files the project needs. Without this step every new worktree
28	// starts broken, which is the commonest reason people give up on worktrees.
29	type Provisioner struct {
30		Settings Settings
31		Timeout  time.Duration
32		// Log receives progress lines; nil discards them.
33		Log io.Writer
34	}
35	
36	// Result records what provisioning did, so callers can report it honestly.
37	type Result struct {
38		Copied  []string
39		Linked  []string
40		Ran     []string
41		Skipped []string
42		// Failures are non-fatal: a failed `npm ci` leaves a usable checkout the
43		// user can fix by hand, so it is reported rather than rolled back.
44		Failures []error
45	}
46	
47	func (p *Provisioner) logf(format string, args ...any) {
48		if p.Log != nil {
49			fmt.Fprintf(p.Log, format+"\n", args...)
50		}
51	}
52	
53	// Provision brings dst up to a working state, using src as the source of
54	// gitignored files and any copied dependency trees.
55	func (p *Provisioner) Provision(ctx context.Context, src, dst string) (Result, error) {
56		plan := BuildPlan(ctx, p.Settings, src)
57		return p.Apply(ctx, plan, src, dst)
58	}
59	
60	// Apply executes a plan. Splitting this from BuildPlan is what lets
61	// `dev wt plan` show exactly what would happen without doing any of it.
62	func (p *Provisioner) Apply(ctx context.Context, plan Plan, src, dst string) (Result, error) {
63		var res Result
64		for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
65			p.logf("warning: %s", w)
66		}
67	
68		for _, step := range plan.Steps {
69			if step.Skipped {
70				res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, step.What+" ("+step.Why+")")
71				continue
72			}
73			switch step.Kind {
74			case StepCopyFile:
75				if err := p.copyFileStep(src, dst, step.What); err != nil {
76					res.Failures = append(res.Failures, err)
77					continue
78				}
79				res.Copied = append(res.Copied, step.What)
80				p.logf("copied %s", step.What)
81	
82			case StepCopyDir:
83				from, to := filepath.Join(src, step.What), filepath.Join(dst, step.What)
84				if _, err := os.Lstat(to); err == nil {
85					res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, step.What+" (already present)")
86					continue
87				}
88				p.logf("copying %s …", step.What)
89				if err := copyTree(from, to); err != nil {
90					res.Failures = append(res.Failures, fmt.Errorf("copy %s: %w", step.What, err))
91					continue
92				}
93				res.Copied = append(res.Copied, step.What+"/")
94				p.logf("copied %s", step.What)
95	
96			case StepLinkDir:
97				if err := p.linkStep(src, dst, step.What); err != nil {
98					if errors.Is(err, errAlreadyPresent) {
99						res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, step.What+" (already present)")
100						continue
101					}
102					res.Failures = append(res.Failures, err)
103					continue
104				}
105				res.Linked = append(res.Linked, step.What)
106				p.logf("linked %s", step.What)
107	
108			case StepRun:
109				p.logf("running: %s", step.What)
110				if err := p.runShell(ctx, dst, step.What); err != nil {
111					res.Failures = append(res.Failures, err)
112					continue
113				}
114				res.Ran = append(res.Ran, step.What)
115			}
116		}
117		return res, nil
118	}
119	
120	var errAlreadyPresent = errors.New("already present")
121	
122	func (p *Provisioner) copyFileStep(src, dst, rel string) error {
123		from, to := filepath.Join(src, rel), filepath.Join(dst, rel)
124		info, err := os.Lstat(from)
125		if err != nil {
126			return nil // vanished between planning and applying; nothing to do
127		}
128		if _, err := os.Stat(to); err == nil {
129			return nil // never clobber what the checkout already has
130		}
131		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(to), 0o755); err != nil {
132			return err
133		}
134		if err := copyFile(from, to, info.Mode()); err != nil {
135			return fmt.Errorf("copy %s: %w", rel, err)
136		}
137		return nil
138	}
139	
140	func (p *Provisioner) linkStep(src, dst, rel string) error {
141		target, link := filepath.Join(src, rel), filepath.Join(dst, rel)
142		if _, err := os.Stat(target); err != nil {
143			return fmt.Errorf("link %s: not present in the source checkout", rel)
144		}
145		if _, err := os.Lstat(link); err == nil {
146			return errAlreadyPresent
147		}
148		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(link), 0o755); err != nil {
149			return err
150		}
151		if err := os.Symlink(target, link); err != nil {
152			return fmt.Errorf("link %s: %w", rel, err)
153		}
154		return nil
155	}
156	
157	func (p *Provisioner) runShell(ctx context.Context, dir, command string) error {
158		timeout := p.Timeout
159		if timeout <= 0 {
160			timeout = 10 * time.Minute
161		}
162		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
163		defer cancel()
164	
165		shell := os.Getenv("SHELL")
166		if shell == "" {
167			shell = "/bin/sh"
168		}
169		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, shell, "-c", command)
170		cmd.Dir = dir

176			return fmt.Errorf("post_create %q: %w", command, err)

181	func copyFile(from, to string, mode os.FileMode) error {
182		in, err := os.Open(from)
183		if err != nil {
184			return err
185		}
186		defer in.Close()
187		out, err := os.OpenFile(to, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL, mode.Perm())
188		if err != nil {
189			return err
190		}
191		defer out.Close()
192		w := bufio.NewWriter(out)
193		if _, err := io.Copy(w, in); err != nil {
194			return err
195		}
196		return w.Flush()
197	}
198	
199	// copyTree duplicates a directory.
200	//
201	// Symlinks are recreated rather than followed: a pnpm node_modules is a farm
202	// of links into a global store, and dereferencing them would turn a 200MB
203	// copy into several gigabytes of duplicated packages.
204	func copyTree(from, to string) error {
205		return filepath.Walk(from, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, err error) error {
206			if err != nil {
207				return err
208			}
209			rel, err := filepath.Rel(from, path)
210			if err != nil {
211				return err
212			}
213			target := filepath.Join(to, rel)
214	
215			switch {
216			case info.IsDir():
217				return os.MkdirAll(target, info.Mode().Perm())
218			case info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0:
219				dest, err := os.Readlink(path)
220				if err != nil {
221					return err
222				}
223				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(target), 0o755); err != nil {
224					return err
225				}
226				os.Remove(target)
227				return os.Symlink(dest, target)
228			case info.Mode().IsRegular():
229				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(target), 0o755); err != nil {
230					return err
231				}
232				return copyFile(path, target, info.Mode())
233			}
234			return nil // sockets, devices and the like have no place in a checkout
235		})
236	}

1	// Package gitx wraps the git porcelain commands dev depends on. Every helper
2	// shells out to git rather than linking a Go implementation: git is already a
3	// hard dependency, its porcelain formats are stable and documented, and this
4	// keeps dev's behaviour identical to what the user sees when they run the same
5	// command by hand.
6	package gitx
7	
8	import (
9		"bytes"
10		"context"
11		"errors"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotARepo is returned when a directory is not inside a git working tree.
18	var ErrNotARepo = errors.New("not a git repository")
19	
20	// Error carries the failing command and git's own stderr, which is almost
21	// always more useful than the exit status alone.
22	type Error struct {
23		Args   []string
24		Dir    string
25		Stderr string
26		Err    error
27	}
28	
29	func (e *Error) Error() string {
30		msg := strings.TrimSpace(e.Stderr)
31		if msg == "" {
32			msg = e.Err.Error()
33		}
34		return fmt.Sprintf("git %s: %s", strings.Join(e.Args, " "), msg)
35	}
36	
37	func (e *Error) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
38	
39	// run executes git in dir and returns trimmed stdout.
40	func run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
41		// -c core.quotepath=false keeps non-ASCII paths readable rather than
42		// octal-escaped, which matters for the Chinese-named files in these repos.
43		full := append([]string{"-c", "core.quotepath=false"}, args...)
44		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", full...)
45		cmd.Dir = dir
46		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
47		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
48		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
49		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
50			gerr := &Error{Args: args, Dir: dir, Stderr: stderr.String(), Err: err}
51			if strings.Contains(gerr.Stderr, "not a git repository") {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", dir, ErrNotARepo)
53			}
54			return "", gerr
55		}
56		return strings.TrimRight(stdout.String(), "\n"), nil
57	}
58	
59	// Run executes an arbitrary git command in dir. Exported for the few callers
60	// (park's wip commit, done's merge) that need a one-off command.
61	func Run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
62		return run(ctx, dir, args...)
63	}
64	
65	// lines splits git output into non-empty lines.
66	func lines(s string) []string {
67		if s == "" {
68			return nil
69		}
70		out := strings.Split(s, "\n")
71		filtered := out[:0]
72		for _, l := range out {
73			if l != "" {
74				filtered = append(filtered, l)
75			}
76		}
77		return filtered
78	}
79	
80	// nulLines splits NUL-delimited git output (-z forms).
81	func nulLines(s string) []string {
82		s = strings.TrimRight(s, "\x00")
83		if s == "" {
84			return nil
85		}
86		return strings.Split(s, "\x00")
87	}

31	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
32	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.

36	                  it anywhere later with dev resume.

38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,

62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69	
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97	
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114	
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}
124	
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes
133					// the task reconstructible rather than lost.
134					t.WorktreePath = ""
135				}
136				if cold && mode == task.ModeBranch {
137					// Free the canonical checkout for other work. The branch remains
138					// local + remote and resume switches back to it.
139					base := t.Base
140					if base == "" {
141						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
142					}
143					if base == "" {
144						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but its base branch is unknown")
145					}
146					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
147						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
148							base, err)
149					}
150				}
151	
152				t.State = target
153				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
154				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
155					return err
156				}
157				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
158				if t.Next != "" {
159					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
160				}
161				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
162				return nil
163			},
164		}
165		f := cmd.Flags()
166		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
167		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
168		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
169		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
170		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
171		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
172		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app, task.Hot, task.Warm)
173		return cmd
174	}
175	
176	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
177	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
178		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
179			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
180		}
181		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
182		return nil
183	}
184	
185	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
186	// directory when no argument is given.
187	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
188		if len(args) == 1 {
189			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
190		}
191		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
196		if err != nil {
197			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
198				config.Contract(cwd))
199		}
200		return t, nil
201	}

31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,

1	package task
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"io/fs"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"regexp"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	
14		"github.com/BurntSushi/toml"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}

170	In some cases it is not possible to provide a list of completions in advance.  Instead, the list of completions must be determined at execution-time. In a similar fashion as for static completions, you can use the `ValidArgsFunction` field to provide a Go function that Cobra will execute when it needs the list of completion choices for the nouns of a command.  Note that either `ValidArgs` or `ValidArgsFunction` can be used for a single cobra command, but not both.
171	Simplified code from `helm status` looks like:
172	
173	```go
174	cmd := &cobra.Command{
175		Use:   "status RELEASE_NAME",
176		Short: "Display the status of the named release",
177		Long:  status_long,

182			if len(args) != 0 {

184			}
185			return getReleasesFromCluster(toComplete), cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
186		},
187	}

194	harbor notary rook thanos

272	// parseSince accepts a relative window ("30d", "6mo", "1y") or an absolute
273	// date. Relative is what people actually type; absolute is what scripts want.
274	func parseSince(s string, now time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
275		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
276		if s == "" {
277			return now.AddDate(-1, 0, 0), nil
278		}
279		if d, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", s, time.Local); err == nil {
280			return d, nil
281		}
282		var n int
283		var unit string
284		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(s, "%d%s", &n, &unit); err != nil || n <= 0 {
285			return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot parse --since %q: want 30d, 6mo, 1y or YYYY-MM-DD", s)
286		}
287		switch strings.ToLower(unit) {
288		case "d", "day", "days":
289			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n), nil
290		case "w", "week", "weeks":
291			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n*7), nil
292		case "mo", "month", "months":
293			return now.AddDate(0, -n, 0), nil
294		case "y", "yr", "year", "years":
295			return now.AddDate(-n, 0, 0), nil
296		}
297		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown unit %q in --since: want d, w, mo or y", unit)
298	}

5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
18	type Session struct {
19		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
20		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
21		Handle string
22		Label  string
23		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
24		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
25		// value.
26		Dirs []string
27		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
28		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
29		AgentStatus string
30		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
31		AgentSessions []string
32		Focused       bool
33	}
34	
35	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
36	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
37		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
38			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
39			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
40			// $HOME active.
41			if d == dir || strings.HasPrefix(d, dir+"/") {
42				return true
43			}
44		}
45		return false
46	}
47	
48	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
49	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
50	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
51	type Runtime interface {
52		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
53		Name() string
54		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
55		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
56		Available() bool
57		// Open makes dir live and returns a handle. Opening something already open
58		// focuses it rather than duplicating it.
59		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error)
60		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
61		// task entry.
62		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
63		// List enumerates live sessions.
64		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
65		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
66		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
67		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
68	}
69	
70	// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
71	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
72	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
73	type WorktreeOpener interface {
74		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error)
75	}
76	
77	// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
78	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
79	
80	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
81		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
82	}
83	
84	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
85	//
86	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
87	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then None.
88	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
89	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
90		herdr, tmux, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}
91		switch backend {
92		case "herdr":
93			return herdr
94		case "tmux":
95			return tmux
96		case "none":
97			return none
98		case "", "auto":
99			if herdr.Available() {
100				return herdr
101			}
102			if tmux.Available() {
103				return tmux
104			}
105			return none
106		}
107		return none
108	}
109	
110	// All returns every backend, for `dev doctor` to report on.
111	func All() []Runtime { return []Runtime{NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}} }
112	
113	// haveBinary reports whether name is on PATH.
114	func haveBinary(name string) bool {
115		_, err := exec.LookPath(name)
116		return err == nil
117	}
118
