```text
commit 90276d54911b136ca9228d13fd149da6d260f150
Author: Da-Wei Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Aug 27 17:32:28 2026 +0800

    feat: add direct tasks and richer repository state
    
    Expose Starship-style Git state throughout the CLI and TUI, including ahead,
    behind, divergence, conflict, staged, unstaged, and untracked counts. Preserve
    a unique changed-path total and classify added, modified, deleted, and renamed
    paths in status details and JSON.
    
    Make task checkout boundaries explicit. Ad-hoc repo open creates no task;
    --direct tracks the current branch without creating a branch or worktree;
    --branch-only switches a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout; and the
    default remains an isolated, provisioned worktree. Update park, resume, and
    done semantics for each mode.
    
    Make live Herdr/tmux workspace state explicit in the REPOS view, add an H
    selected-repo heatmap overlay, and add e config editing plus r live reload of
    config, inventory, remote data, and tool bindings. Fix broad-cwd runtime
    matching so a workspace at $HOME no longer marks every descendant repo active.
    
    Add dev edit/config edit with machine-detected config creation and explicit
    VISUAL/EDITOR fallback order, plus docs and lifecycle coverage.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KfgWSELDAofucwXjMMxBao

diff --git a/internal/cli/cli_test.go b/internal/cli/cli_test.go
index 4dcd93e..6252b09 100644
--- a/internal/cli/cli_test.go
+++ b/internal/cli/cli_test.go
@@ -763,3 +763,117 @@ func TestEditEditorFlagOverridesEnvironment(t *testing.T) {
 		t.Errorf("--editor should win, got %q", got)
 	}
 }
+
+func TestStartDirectTracksCurrentBranchWithoutCreatingAnything(t *testing.T) {
+	h := newHarness(t)
+	out := h.mustRun("start", "demo", "--task", "quick fix", "--direct")
+	if !strings.Contains(out, "main (direct)") {
+		t.Errorf("start output should make the mode explicit: %q", out)
+	}
+	if branches := h.repo.Git("branch", "--format=%(refname:short)"); branches != "main" {
+		t.Errorf("direct mode should create no branch, got %q", branches)
+	}
+	if worktrees := h.repo.Git("worktree", "list", "--porcelain"); strings.Count(worktrees, "worktree ") != 1 {
+		t.Errorf("direct mode should create no worktree:\n%s", worktrees)
+	}
+	ls := h.mustRun("ls", "--json")
+	if !strings.Contains(ls, `"mode": "direct"`) || !strings.Contains(ls, `"branch": "main"`) {
+		t.Errorf("task should explicitly record direct/main:\n%s", ls)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestDirectTaskWarmResumeAndDone(t *testing.T) {
+	h := newHarness(t)
+	h.mustRun("start", "demo", "--task", "quick fix", "--direct")
+	os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(h.repo.Root, "quick.txt"), []byte("done\n"), 0o644)
+	h.repo.Git("add", "quick.txt")
+	h.repo.Git("commit", "-m", "fix: quick change")
+
+	h.mustRun("park", "quick fix", "--next", "check the result")
+	out := h.mustRun("resume", "quick fix")
+	if !strings.Contains(out, "(direct)") {
+		t.Errorf("resume should preserve direct mode: %q", out)
+	}
+	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(h.wtRoot, "demo")); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
+		t.Error("resuming a direct task must not invent a worktree")
+	}
+
+	out = h.mustRun("done", "quick fix")
+	if !strings.Contains(out, "completed directly on main") {
+		t.Errorf("direct done should need no integration mode: %q", out)
+	}
+	// A done direct task used repo__main as its identity. The next quick task
+	// on main must be able to replace it without a manual sweep first.
+	out = h.mustRun("start", "demo", "--task", "another quick fix", "--direct")
+	if !strings.Contains(out, "another quick fix") {
+		t.Errorf("done direct task should not block reuse of main: %q", out)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestDirectTaskCannotGoCold(t *testing.T) {
+	h := newHarness(t)
+	h.mustRun("start", "demo", "--task", "quick fix", "--direct")
+	_, _, err := h.run("park", "quick fix", "--cold")
+	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "cannot go cold") {
+		t.Errorf("direct task cannot remove the canonical checkout, got %v", err)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestStartBranchOnlyActuallySwitchesBranch(t *testing.T) {
+	h := newHarness(t)
+	out := h.mustRun("start", "demo", "--task", "local feature",
+		"--branch", "feat/local", "--base", "main", "--branch-only")
+	if !strings.Contains(out, "(branch)") {
+		t.Errorf("mode should be explicit: %q", out)
+	}
+	if branch := h.repo.Git("branch", "--show-current"); branch != "feat/local" {
+		t.Errorf("branch-only must switch the canonical checkout, got %q", branch)
+	}
+	if worktrees := h.repo.Git("worktree", "list", "--porcelain"); strings.Count(worktrees, "worktree ") != 1 {
+		t.Errorf("branch-only should create no linked worktree:\n%s", worktrees)

+	}

+func TestStatusAndJSONExposeRichChangeCounts(t *testing.T) {
+	h := newHarness(t)
+	h.mustRun("start", "demo", "--task", "inspect changes", "--direct")
+	// One path staged and then modified again, plus one untracked path: two
+	// unique paths, but staged=1, unstaged=1, untracked=1.
+	h.repo.Write("both.txt", "staged\n")
+	h.repo.Git("add", "both.txt")
+	h.repo.Write("both.txt", "modified after stage\n")
+	h.repo.Write("untracked.txt", "new\n")
+
+	cwd, _ := os.Getwd()
+	os.Chdir(h.repo.Root)
+	defer os.Chdir(cwd)
+	out := h.mustRun("status")
+	if !strings.Contains(out, "branch     main  +1 !1 ?1") ||
+		!strings.Contains(out, "2 changed paths (+1 staged, !1 unstaged, ?1 untracked)") {
+		t.Errorf("status should show rich counts:\n%s", out)
+	}
+
+	out = h.mustRun("ls", "--json")
+	var rows []map[string]any
+	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(out), &rows); err != nil || len(rows) != 1 {
+		t.Fatalf("json: %v %s", err, out)
+	}
+	for key, want := range map[string]float64{
+		"changed": 2, "staged": 1, "unstaged": 1, "untracked": 1,
+	} {
+		if got := rows[0][key]; got != want {
+			t.Errorf("%s = %v, want %v", key, got, want)
+		}
+	}
```

The app contract confirms the concern: with no descriptor, `cdDirective` writes `cd <quoted path>` to normal stdout and returns nil. Because `start`, `resume`, `try`, `wt create`, and `wt open` call it only after their operational work, the wrapper’s no-side-channel fallback cannot distinguish successful mutation from successful navigation.

```text
211	// checkoutOf is where a task's code lives right now.
212	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
213		if t.WorktreePath != "" {

216		return t.RepoPath

221	// anyone having to ask dev.
222	//

224	// the sidebar row layout in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g.
225	//
226	//	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
227	//	rows = [["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"], ["branch", "git_status"], ["$next"]]
228	//
229	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds and shows nothing,
230	// which is why dev never treats a failure here as an error.
231	func annotate(app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, t *task.Task) {
232		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
233			return
234		}
235		kv := map[string]string{
236			"stage": t.State.Label(),
237			"next":  t.Next,
238		}
239		if err := rt.Annotate(ctxOf(), t.RuntimeHandle, kv); err != nil {
240			app.warnf("could not annotate the runtime session: %v", err)
241		}
242	}

248		}
249		if n := len(p.Linked); n > 0 {
250			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   linked    %s\n", strings.Join(p.Linked, ", "))
251		}
252		for _, e := range p.Failures {
253			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   warning   %v\n", e)
254		}
255	}
```

```text
28	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
29	
30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
31	
32	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
33	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
34	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
35	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
36	
37	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
38	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
39	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`

41	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
42	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
43		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
44	}
45	
46	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
47	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
48	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
49	// descriptors.
50	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
51		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
52	
53		root := &cobra.Command{
54			Use:           "dev",
55			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
56			Long:          rootLong,

58			SilenceUsage:  true,
59			SilenceErrors: true,
60			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
61			// exists to answer.
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
64					out, err := skill.Render()
65					if err != nil {
66						return err
67					}
68					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
69					return nil
70				}
71				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
72				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
73				if interactive() {
74					return runTUI(app)
75				}
76				return runList(app, listOptions{})
77			},
78			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
79				if completionInvocation(cmd) {
80					return nil
81				}
82				return app.Load()
83			},
84		}

86		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
```

```text
1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"os"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// XDG base directories, resolved the way the spec prescribes: honor the
10	// environment variable when it holds an absolute path, otherwise fall back to
11	// the documented default under $HOME.
12	
13	func xdgDir(envVar, fallback string) string {
14		if v := os.Getenv(envVar); filepath.IsAbs(v) {
15			return v
16		}
17		return filepath.Join(home(), fallback)
18	}
19	
20	func home() string {
21		if h, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil && h != "" {
22			return h
23		}
24		return os.Getenv("HOME")
25	}
26	
27	// ConfigHome is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (default ~/.config).
28	func ConfigHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", ".config") }
29	
30	// DataHome is $XDG_DATA_HOME (default ~/.local/share).
31	func DataHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_DATA_HOME", ".local/share") }
32	
33	// CacheHome is $XDG_CACHE_HOME (default ~/.cache).
34	func CacheHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CACHE_HOME", ".cache") }
35	
36	// ConfigFile is the path dev loads its TOML configuration from.
37	func ConfigFile() string { return filepath.Join(ConfigHome(), "dev", "config.toml") }
38	
39	// Expand resolves a leading ~ and any environment variables in p, then makes
40	// the result absolute. Paths in config.toml are written by humans, so both
41	// "~/Worktrees" and "$WORK/trees" have to work.
42	func Expand(p string) string {
43		if p == "" {
44			return ""
45		}
46		p = os.ExpandEnv(p)
47		switch {
48		case p == "~":
49			p = home()
50		case strings.HasPrefix(p, "~/"):
51			p = filepath.Join(home(), p[2:])
52		}
53		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(p); err == nil {
54			return abs
55		}
56		return filepath.Clean(p)
57	}
58	
59	// Contract renders p with $HOME collapsed back to ~, for display only.
60	func Contract(p string) string {
61		h := home()
62		if h != "" && p == h {
63			return "~"
64		}
65		if h != "" && strings.HasPrefix(p, h+string(filepath.Separator)) {
66			return "~" + p[len(h):]
67		}
68		return p
69	}
```

```text
2	# End-to-end smoke test: drives the real binary through a full task lifecycle
3	# in a throwaway HOME, with the runtime backend pinned to "none" so no
4	# multiplexer is touched.
5	set -euo pipefail
6	
7	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
8	BIN="${BIN:-$ROOT/dev}"
9	
10	# Always rebuild. The Go build cache makes this nearly free, and testing a
11	# stale binary against fresh assertions is worse than not testing at all.
12	echo "building $BIN"
13	(cd "$ROOT" && go build -o "$BIN" ./cmd/dev)
14	
15	SANDBOX="$(mktemp -d)"
16	trap 'rm -rf "$SANDBOX"' EXIT
17	
18	export HOME="$SANDBOX/home"
19	export XDG_DATA_HOME="$HOME/.local/share"
20	export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"
21	mkdir -p "$HOME/Program"
22	
23	# A local "remote" so the push and cold-park paths are exercised for real.
24	git init --bare --quiet --initial-branch=main "$SANDBOX/origin.git"
25	
26	cat > "$SANDBOX/config.toml" <<CONFIG
27	[paths]
28	scan_roots    = ["$HOME/Program"]
29	project_root  = "$HOME/Program"
30	tries_root    = "$HOME/tries"
31	worktree_root = "$HOME/Worktrees"
32	state_dir     = "$HOME/state"
33	
34	[runtime]
35	backend = "none"
36	
37	[worktree]
38	include     = [".env"]
39	post_create = []

44	step() { printf '\n\033[1m▸ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
45	fail() { printf '\033[31m✗ %s\033[0m\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
46	ok()   { printf '  \033[32m✓\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
```

```text
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}

127			out = append(out, t)

129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
```

```text
1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`

115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a

118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`

129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}

146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}
```

```text
50	// Live reports whether a runtime session is currently hosting this task.
51	func (r Row) Live() bool { return r.Session != nil }

53	// StateDrift reports a task whose recorded state disagrees with reality:
54	// hot with no live session, or warm/cold with one. It is what `dev sweep`
55	// turns into suggestions — dev reports drift and never silently rewrites it.
56	func (r Row) StateDrift() string {
57		if r.sessionsTracked {
58			switch r.Task.State {
59			case task.Hot:
60				if !r.Live() {
61					return "no live session"
62				}
63			case task.Warm, task.Cold:
64				if r.Live() {
65					return "session is live"
66				}
67			}
68		}
69		if r.Task.State == task.Cold && r.CheckoutExists && r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
70			return "worktree still on disk"
71		}
72		if r.WorktreeMissing {
73			return "worktree is gone"
74		}
75		return ""
76	}

78	// Age is how long since the task's last commit, falling back to when the entry
79	// was last written for a task with no commits of its own.
80	func (r Row) Age() time.Duration {
81		ref := r.LastCommit
82		if ref.IsZero() || r.Task.Updated.After(ref) {
83			ref = r.Task.Updated

94		// git facts (and for tests).
95		SkipRuntime bool
96		// SkipGit avoids running git per task, for a fast listing.

98	}
99	
100	// Collect builds the enriched inventory. Git probes run concurrently: each is
101	// a handful of process spawns, and a machine with dozens of tasks would
102	// otherwise make `dev ls` feel slow.
103	func Collect(ctx context.Context, tasks []*task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opts Options) []Row {
104		rows := make([]Row, len(tasks))
105	
106		var sessions []runtime.Session
107		tracked := false
108		if !opts.SkipRuntime && rt != nil && rt.Name() != "none" {
109			if s, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
110				sessions, tracked = s, true
111			}
112		}
113	
114		var wg sync.WaitGroup
115		// Bound concurrency: git is process-heavy and an unbounded fan-out over a
116		// large inventory would thrash.
117		sem := make(chan struct{}, 8)
118	
119		for i, t := range tasks {
120			rows[i].Task = t
121			rows[i].Checkout = checkoutOf(t)
122	
123			if opts.SkipGit || rows[i].Checkout == "" {
124				continue
125			}
126			wg.Add(1)
127			go func(i int) {
128				defer wg.Done()
129				sem <- struct{}{}
130				defer func() { <-sem }()
131				enrich(ctx, &rows[i])
132			}(i)
133		}
134		wg.Wait()
135	
136		for i := range rows {
137			rows[i].Session = matchSession(sessions, rows[i])
138			rows[i].sessionsTracked = tracked
139		}
140		return rows
141	}

150	func enrich(ctx context.Context, r *Row) {
151		info, err := os.Stat(r.Checkout)
152		r.CheckoutExists = err == nil && info.IsDir()
153		if !r.CheckoutExists {
154			if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
155				r.WorktreeMissing = true
156			}
157			return
158		}
159		if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Checkout); err != nil {
160			r.StatusErr = err
161		} else {
162			r.Status = st
163		}
164		if unix, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, r.Checkout); err == nil && unix > 0 {
165			r.LastCommit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
166		}
167		// A recorded worktree that git no longer knows about is drift worth
168		// surfacing: the directory may exist while the administrative entry is gone.
169		if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
170			if _, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, r.Task.RepoPath, r.Task.Branch); err == nil && !ok {
171				r.WorktreeMissing = true

176	// matchSession picks the runtime session hosting a row's checkout. An exact

179	func matchSession(sessions []runtime.Session, r Row) *runtime.Session {
180		if r.Checkout == "" {

182		}

184		for i := range sessions {

190					contains = &sessions[i]

193		}

212				continue
213			}

232			}
233		}
234		return false
235	}

237	// Orphans reports live runtime sessions that no task claims — the "I opened
238	// this and never wrote it down" case that makes a sidebar grow without bound.
239	func Orphans(sessions []runtime.Session, rows []Row) []runtime.Session {
240		claimed := map[string]bool{}

244			}

249				out = append(out, s)
250			}
251		}
252		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Label < out[j].Label })
```

```text
175		}
176		if len(q.Sources) > 0 {
177			clause += " AND source IN (" + placeholders(len(q.Sources)) + ")"
178			for _, s := range q.Sources {
179				args = append(args, string(s))
180			}
181		}

185	func placeholders(n int) string {

188		}
189		out := make([]byte, 0, n*2-1)

194			out = append(out, '?')

199	// DayTotals returns seconds per calendar day.
200	func (s *Store) DayTotals(q Query) (map[string]int, error) {
201		clause, args := q.where()
202		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT day, SUM(seconds) FROM activity `+clause+` GROUP BY day`, args...)
203		if err != nil {
204			return nil, err
205		}
206		defer rows.Close()
207	
208		out := map[string]int{}
209		for rows.Next() {
210			var day string
211			var secs int
212			if err := rows.Scan(&day, &secs); err != nil {
213				return nil, err
214			}
215			out[day] = secs
216		}
217		return out, rows.Err()
218	}

220	// RepoTotal is one row of the per-repo breakdown.

222		Repo    string
223		Seconds int
224		Days    int
225		Last    string
226	}

228	// RepoTotals returns seconds per repository, busiest first.
229	func (s *Store) RepoTotals(q Query) ([]RepoTotal, error) {
230		clause, args := q.where()
231		rows, err := s.db.Query(`
232	SELECT repo, SUM(seconds) AS secs, COUNT(DISTINCT day) AS days, MAX(day)
233	FROM activity `+clause+`
234	GROUP BY repo ORDER BY secs DESC`, args...)
235		if err != nil {
236			return nil, err
237		}
238		defer rows.Close()
239	
240		var out []RepoTotal
241		for rows.Next() {
242			var r RepoTotal
243			if err := rows.Scan(&r.Repo, &r.Seconds, &r.Days, &r.Last); err != nil {
244				return nil, err
245			}
246			out = append(out, r)
247		}
248		return out, rows.Err()
249	}

254		q.Repo = repo
255		return s.DayTotals(q)

258	// MarkCollected records that a collector ran, so incremental runs know their
259	// starting point.
260	func (s *Store) MarkCollected(name string, at time.Time) error {
261		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
262	INSERT INTO collector (name, last_at) VALUES (?, ?)
263	ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET last_at = excluded.last_at`, name, at.Unix())
264		return err
265	}
266	
267	// LastCollected reports when a collector last ran, zero when never.
268	func (s *Store) LastCollected(name string) time.Time {
269		var unix int64
270		if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT last_at FROM collector WHERE name = ?`, name).Scan(&unix); err != nil {
271			return time.Time{}
272		}
273		return time.Unix(unix, 0)
274	}

276	// Empty reports whether anything has been recorded yet, so the CLI can explain
277	// how to start collecting instead of printing a blank chart.
278	func (s *Store) Empty() bool {
279		var n int
280		if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activity`).Scan(&n); err != nil {
281			return true
282		}
283		return n == 0
284	}

286	// Path is where the database lives inside a state directory.

289	// ClearQuery selects durable activity rows to delete. Repo is an exact name —
290	// deletion must not use the fuzzy LIKE semantics a report does.
291	type ClearQuery struct {

293		Sources []Source
294	}
295	
296	// Clear deletes matching activity and returns the number of rows removed.
297	// With an empty query it clears all activity and collector checkpoints.
298	func (s *Store) Clear(q ClearQuery) (int64, error) {
299		clause := ""
300		var args []any
301		if q.Repo != "" {
302			clause = " WHERE repo = ?"
303			args = append(args, q.Repo)
304		}
305		if len(q.Sources) > 0 {
306			if clause == "" {
307				clause = " WHERE "
308			} else {
309				clause += " AND "
310			}
311			clause += "source IN (" + placeholders(len(q.Sources)) + ")"
312			for _, source := range q.Sources {
313				args = append(args, string(source))
314			}
315		}
316		result, err := s.db.Exec("DELETE FROM activity"+clause, args...)
317		if err != nil {
318			return 0, err
319		}
320		if q.Repo == "" && len(q.Sources) == 0 {
321			if _, err := s.db.Exec("DELETE FROM collector"); err != nil {
322				return 0, err
323			}
324		}
325		return result.RowsAffected()
326	}
```

```text
71	// Import fetches per-project daily totals for a date range and stores them.
72	//
73	// WakaTime's summaries endpoint caps a single request at roughly a year, and
74	// re-importing a day returns the same total, so entries are written with Set
75	// rather than accumulated.
76	func (w *WakaTime) Import(ctx context.Context, s *Store, since, until time.Time) (int, error) {
77		if w.APIKey == "" {
78			return 0, fmt.Errorf("no WakaTime API key")
79		}
80		base := w.BaseURL
81		if base == "" {
82			base = DefaultWakaTimeURL
83		}
84		client := w.Client
85		if client == nil {
86			client = &http.Client{Timeout: 30 * time.Second}
87		}
88	
89		url := fmt.Sprintf("%s/users/current/summaries?start=%s&end=%s",
90			base, since.Format(dayFormat), until.Format(dayFormat))
91		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil)
92		if err != nil {
93			return 0, err
94		}
95		// WakaTime authenticates with the base64 of the key as a Basic credential.
96		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Basic "+base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(w.APIKey)))
97	
98		resp, err := client.Do(req)
99		if err != nil {
100			return 0, fmt.Errorf("wakatime request: %w", err)
101		}
102		defer resp.Body.Close()
103		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
104			return 0, fmt.Errorf("wakatime returned %s", resp.Status)
105		}
106	
107		var body summariesResponse
108		if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&body); err != nil {
109			return 0, fmt.Errorf("decode wakatime response: %w", err)
110		}
111	
112		var entries []Entry
113		for _, day := range body.Data {
114			d, err := time.ParseInLocation(dayFormat, day.Range.Date, time.Local)
115			if err != nil {
116				continue
117			}
118			for _, p := range day.Projects {
119				if p.TotalSeconds <= 0 {
120					continue
121				}
122				entries = append(entries, Entry{
123					Day: d, Repo: p.Name, Source: SourceWakaTime,
124					Seconds: int(p.TotalSeconds),
125				})
126			}
127		}
128		if err := s.Set(entries...); err != nil {
129			return 0, err
130		}
131		return len(entries), s.MarkCollected("wakatime", time.Now())
132	}
```

```text
86	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
87	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
88	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
89	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
90		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
91			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
92		}
93		seen := map[string]bool{}
94		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
95		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
96		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
97		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
98		identities := map[string]bool{}
99		var out []Repo
100	
101		for _, root := range roots {
102			info, err := os.Stat(root)
103			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
104				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
105			}
106			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
107	
108			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
109				if err != nil {
110					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
111				}
112				if ctx.Err() != nil {
113					return ctx.Err()
114				}
115				if path == rootClean {
116					return nil
117				}
118				name := d.Name()
119				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
120				isDir := d.IsDir()
121				if isLink {
122					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
123					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
124					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
125					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
126						isDir = info.IsDir()
127					}
128				}
129				if !isDir {
130					return nil
131				}
132				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
133					return filepath.SkipDir
134				}
135	
136				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
137				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
138	
139				if isRepoDir(path) {
140					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
141					if real == "" {
142						real = path
143					}
144					bare := isBareDir(path)
145					identity, commonDir := real, real
146					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
147						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
148						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
149						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
150						return filepath.SkipDir
151					}
152					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
153						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {

155							// project in the repo inventory.
156							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {

158							}
159							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir

180					return filepath.SkipDir

184				}
185				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
186					if !seen[path] {
```

The provider does not call `Resolve`; it lists allowed-state tasks and passes only `t.ID` to `addCompletion`, whose guard is a case-sensitive `strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete)`. In contrast, `Resolve("auth")` lowercases and searches ID, title, branch, and repo, so the demo’s unique `demo__feat-auth` is executable via `resume auth` but is eliminated before any shell sees it; the current completion test uses the prefix `demo`, which masks this mismatch.

```text
9	
10	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
11	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
12	type Repo struct {
13		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
14		Root string
15		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
16		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
17		GitCommonDir string
18		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
19		Name string
20		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
21		// the main checkout.
22		IsLinkedWorktree bool
23		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
24		MainRoot string
25		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
26		Bare bool
27	}
28	
29	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
30	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
31	
32	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
33	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
34		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
35		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
36		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
37			"rev-parse",
38			"--path-format=absolute",
39			"--show-toplevel",
40			"--git-common-dir",
41			"--is-bare-repository",
42		)
43		if err != nil {
44			return Repo{}, err
45		}
46		f := lines(out)
47		r := Repo{}
48		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
49		switch len(f) {
50		case 3:
51			r.Root = f[0]
52			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
53			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
54		case 2:
55			r.GitCommonDir = f[0]
56			r.Bare = f[1] == "true"
57		default:
58			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
59		}
60	
61		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
62		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
63		if r.Bare {
64			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
65		} else {
66			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
67		}
68		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.Root != r.MainRoot
69		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
70		if r.Bare {
71			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
72			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
73			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
74				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
75			}
76		}
77		return r, nil
78	}
79	
80	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
81	// a full Discover.
82	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
83		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
84		return err == nil
85	}
86	
87	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
88	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
89	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
90	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
91	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
92		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
93			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
94				return b
95			}
96		}
97		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
98			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
99				return cand
100			}
101		}
102		return ""
103	}
104	
105	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
106	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
107		if name == "" {
108			name = "origin"
109		}
110		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
111		if err != nil {
112			return ""
113		}
114		return out
115	}
116	
117	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
118	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
119	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
120	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
121	// semantics should use Remote instead.
122	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
123		if commonDir == "" {
124			return ""
125		}
126		if name == "" {
127			name = "origin"
128		}
129		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
130		if err != nil {
131			return ""
132		}
133		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
134		section := ""
135		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
136			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
137			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
138				continue
139			}
140			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
141				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
142				continue
143			}
144			if section != want {
145				continue
146			}
147			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
148			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
149				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
150			}
151		}
152		return ""
153	}
```

```text
80	
81	// completeRepoFlag is the same domain without a positional-argument guard: a
82	// flag may legally appear after another argument, e.g. wt open branch --repo.
83	func completeRepoFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
84		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
85			return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, false)
86		}
87	}
88	
89	// completeRepoNameFlag returns the name stored in tasks and stats, not the
90	// Category/Name display reference used by repository commands.
91	func completeRepoNameFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
92		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
93			return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, true)
94		}
95	}
96	
97	func repositoryCompletions(app *App, toComplete string, namesOnly bool) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
98		if !app.loadCompletion() {
99			return nil, noFileCompletion
100		}
101		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.CompletionOptions())
102		if err != nil {
103			return nil, noFileCompletion
104		}
105		displayCount := make(map[string]int, len(repos))
106		for _, r := range repos {
107			displayCount[r.Display()]++
108		}
109		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(repos))
110		out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
111		for _, r := range repos {
112			value := r.Display()
113			description := config.Contract(r.Path)
114			switch {
115			case namesOnly:
116				value = r.Name
117				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
118			case displayCount[value] > 1:
119				value = r.Path
120				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
121			}
122			if seen[value] {
123				continue
124			}
125			seen[value] = true
126			out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
127		}
128		return out, noFileCompletion
129	}
130	
131	func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
132		return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
133			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
134				return nil, noFileCompletion
135			}
136			repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
137			var repoPath string
138			if repoRef == "" {
139				var err error
140				repoPath, _, err = repoContext(app, "")
141				if err != nil {
142					return nil, noFileCompletion
143				}
144			} else {
145				r, _, err := repo.ResolveCompletion(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repoRef)
146				if err != nil {
147					return nil, noFileCompletion
148				}
149				repoPath = r.Path
150			}
151			worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
152			if err != nil {
153				return nil, noFileCompletion
154			}
155			out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
156			for _, wt := range worktrees {
157				if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
158					continue
159				}
160				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
161				if wt.Main {
162					description += " (main checkout)"
163				}
164				out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
165			}
166			return out, noFileCompletion
167		}
168	}
```

```text
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.

16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  # Commands outside the navigation surface need no side channel. Besides

20	  case "${1:-}" in
21	    __complete|__completeNoDesc|--help|-h|--version|--skill|completion|config|doctor|done|edit|gitignore|ignore|help|list|ls|park|skill|stats|status|sweep|adopt|bootstrap)
22	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
23	      return 0
24	      ;;
25	  esac
26	
27	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
28	  if ! __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"; then
29	    __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || {
30	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
31	      return 0
32	    }
33	  fi
34	
35	  __dev_status=0
36	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FD=3 command %[1]s "$@" 3>"$__dev_cd_file" || __dev_status=$?
37	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
38	    if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"; then
39	      if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
40	        builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir" || __dev_status=$?
41	      fi
42	    else
43	      __dev_status=1
44	    fi
45	  fi
46	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" || :
47	  return $__dev_status
48	}
49	`

52	#   dev shell-init fish | source

56	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0
57	        set __dev_command $argv[1]
58	    end
59	    if contains -- "$__dev_command" __complete __completeNoDesc --help -h --version --skill completion config doctor done edit gitignore ignore help list ls park skill stats status sweep adopt bootstrap
60	        command %[1]s $argv
61	        return $status
62	    end
63	
64	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
65	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
66	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
67	    if test $status -ne 0
68	        set __dev_cd_file (mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
69	    end
70	    if test -z "$__dev_cd_file"
71	        command %[1]s $argv
72	        return $status
73	    end
74	
75	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FD 3
76	    command %[1]s $argv 3>"$__dev_cd_file"
77	    set -l __dev_status $status
78	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
79	        if read -z -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
80	            if test -n "$__dev_dir"

82	                set __dev_status $status
83	            end
84	        else
85	            set __dev_status 1
86	        end
87	    end
88	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
89	    return $__dev_status
90	end

97			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
98	
99	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
100	"none" runtime) pass the destination through a child-only file descriptor,
101	because a child process cannot change its parent's working directory. The
102	wrapper reads that path and changes directory without evaluating shell code.
103	
104	Add to your shell rc file:
105	
106	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
107	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
108			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
109			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
110			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {

114				}
115				switch args[0] {
116				case "bash", "zsh":

123				return nil
124			},
```

```text
1	package runtime
2	
3	import "context"
4	
5	// None is the no-multiplexer backend. It is always available, which is what
6	// guarantees dev's core inventory and worktree commands work on a bare machine
7	// with nothing but git installed.
8	//
9	// Open returns the directory itself as the handle: the shell wrapper installed
10	// by `dev shell-init` turns that into a cd in the calling shell, since a child
11	// process can never change its parent's working directory.
12	type None struct{}
13	
14	// Name implements Runtime.
15	func (None) Name() string { return "none" }
16	
17	// Available implements Runtime; the null backend always is.
18	func (None) Available() bool { return true }
19	
20	// Open implements Runtime by reporting the directory to change into.
21	func (None) Open(_ context.Context, dir, _ string) (string, error) { return dir, nil }
22	
23	// Close implements Runtime as a no-op: there is no session to end.
24	func (None) Close(context.Context, string) error { return nil }
25	
26	// List implements Runtime; without a multiplexer nothing is tracked as live.
27	func (None) List(context.Context) ([]Session, error) { return nil, nil }
28	
29	// Annotate implements Runtime as a no-op.
30	func (None) Annotate(context.Context, string, map[string]string) error { return nil }
```

```text
68	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
69	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
70		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
71	}
72	
73	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
74	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
76	}
77	
78	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
79	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
80	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
81	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
82	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
83	// integrations.
84	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
85		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
86			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
87			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
88				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
89			}
90			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
91			if file == nil {
92				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
93			}
94			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
95				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
96			}
97			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
98				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
99			}
100			return nil
101		}
102		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
103		return err
104	}
105	
106	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
107	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
```

```text
8	//
9	// Open returns the directory itself as the handle: the shell wrapper installed
10	// by `dev shell-init` turns that into a cd in the calling shell, since a child
11	// process can never change its parent's working directory.
12	type None struct{}
13	
14	// Name implements Runtime.
15	func (None) Name() string { return "none" }
16	
17	// Available implements Runtime; the null backend always is.
18	func (None) Available() bool { return true }
19	
20	// Open implements Runtime by reporting the directory to change into.
21	func (None) Open(_ context.Context, dir, _ string) (string, error) { return dir, nil }
22	
23	// Close implements Runtime as a no-op: there is no session to end.
24	func (None) Close(context.Context, string) error { return nil }
25	
26	// List implements Runtime; without a multiplexer nothing is tracked as live.
27	func (None) List(context.Context) ([]Session, error) { return nil, nil }
28	
29	// Annotate implements Runtime as a no-op.
30	func (None) Annotate(context.Context, string, map[string]string) error { return nil }
31
```

```bash
      rc=$?
      after=$PWD
      tracked=no
      $DEV_BIN --config "$DEV_CONFIG" ls --json | grep -q "verify-'"$name"'" && tracked=yes
      legacy=no
      grep -q "^cd .*Program/demo" "$OUTSIDE/output" && legacy=yes
      printf "shell=%s rc=%s tracked=%s legacy_cd=%s cwd_unchanged=%s before=%s after=%s\n" \
        '"$name"' "$rc" "$tracked" "$legacy" "$([ "$before" = "$after" ] && printf yes || printf no)" "$before" "$after"
    '
done
```

40	## Install
41	
42	### Homebrew (macOS)
43	
44	```bash
45	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli
46	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
47	```
48	
49	The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
50	does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.
51	
52	### Go or source
53	
54	```bash
55	go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@latest
56	# Pin @v0.1.0 instead when you need a reproducible install.
57	# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
58	```
59	
60	For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
61	them:
62	
63	```bash
64	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
65	dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
66	dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
67	dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
68	```
69	
70	Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
71	worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
72	a forge or the network.
73	
74	Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
75	
76	```bash
77	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
78	eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
79	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-27 17:50:29Z)**_

The Go child only validates and writes descriptor 3; it has neither the temporary pathname nor unlink capability. The shell’s `command … || status=$?` guard does ensure ordinary failures and a child killed by a signal still flow to the trailing `rm`, but it cannot execute that tail after the wrapper shell itself exits.

```text
5	目標是把 `dev-cli` 以 public MIT 專案從 `v0.1.0` 開始發布；macOS 可用 `brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli` 安裝 executable `dev` 並立即取得 bash/zsh/fish completion，Linux 則沿用 dotfiles 的版本鎖定 `go_tools`。同時把 `dev` 納入 dotfiles 的預設開發工具、completion cache、shell directory-change integration 與工具文件，而且不讓 Formula 在安裝期寫入使用者的 agent skill 目錄。

14	  - 保留 `DEV_SHELL_INIT=1`、child exit status、即時 stdout/stderr、pipe 行為與可靠 cleanup；確認裸 `dev`/`dev tui` 仍看到真實 TTY。
15	- 移除 `newShellInitCmd` 下重複且未文件化的 `shell-init completion` 子命令；唯一公開介面採 Cobra 慣例：`dev completion bash|zsh|fish`（Cobra 現有 PowerShell 可保留，但本次安裝範圍為三種 shell）。
```

```text
If a matching git tag does not yet exist, one will automatically get created
from the latest state of the default branch.
Use `--target` to point to a different branch or commit for the automatic tag creation.
Use `--verify-tag` to abort the release if the tag doesn't already exist.
To fetch the new tag locally after the release, do `git fetch --tags origin`.

To create a release from an annotated git tag, first create one locally with
git, push the tag to GitHub, then run this command.
Use `--notes-from-tag` to get the release notes from the annotated git tag.
If the tag is not annotated, the commit message will be used instead.

Use `--generate-notes` to automatically generate notes using GitHub Release Notes API.
When using automatically generated release notes, a release title will also be automatically
generated unless a title was explicitly passed. Additional release notes can be prepended to
automatically generated notes by using the `--notes` flag.

By default, the release is created even if there are no new commits since the last release.
This may result in the same or duplicate release which may not be desirable in some cases.
Use `--fail-on-no-commits` to fail if no new commits are available. This flag has no
effect if there are no existing releases or this is the very first release.

## Immutable Releases

When release immutability is enabled for a repository, the following protections are enforced:
- Git tags associated with a release cannot be modified or deleted.
- Release assets cannot be modified or deleted.

Immutability is enforced only after a release is published. Draft releases can be modified
or deleted, and the associated git tags can be modified or deleted as well.

When using the `create` command to attach assets to a release, separate API calls
are made to create the release as a draft, upload the assets, and then publish the release.
Immutability protections will be enforced ONLY after the release is published.


USAGE
  gh release create [<tag>] [<filename>... | <pattern>...]

ALIASES
  gh release new

FLAGS
      --discussion-category string   Start a discussion in the specified category
  -d, --draft                        Save the release as a draft instead of publishing it
      --fail-on-no-commits           Fail if there are no commits since the last release (no impact on the first release)
      --generate-notes               Automatically generate title and notes for the release via GitHub Release Notes API
      --latest                       Mark this release as "Latest" (default [automatic based on date and version]). --latest=false to explicitly NOT set as latest
  -n, --notes string                 Release notes
  -F, --notes-file file              Read release notes from file (use "-" to read from standard input)
      --notes-from-tag               Fetch notes from the tag annotation or message of commit associated with tag
      --notes-start-tag string       Tag to use as the starting point for generating release notes
  -p, --prerelease                   Mark the release as a prerelease
      --target branch                Target branch or full commit SHA (default [main branch])
  -t, --title string                 Release title
      --verify-tag                   Abort in case the git tag doesn't already exist in the remote repository

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

EXAMPLES
  # Interactively create a release
  $ gh release create
  
  # Interactively create a release from specific tag
  $ gh release create v1.2.3
  
  # Non-interactively create a release
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 --notes "bugfix release"
  
  # Use automatically generated via GitHub Release Notes API release notes
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 --generate-notes
  
  # Use release notes from a file
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 -F release-notes.md
  
  # Use tag annotation or associated commit message as notes
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 --notes-from-tag
  
  # Don't mark the release as latest
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 --latest=false
  
  # Upload all tarballs in a directory as release assets
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 ./dist/*.tgz
  
  # Upload a release asset with a display label
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 '/path/to/asset.zip#My display label'
  
  # Create a release and start a discussion
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 --discussion-category "General"
  
  # Create a release only if there are new commits available since the last release
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 --fail-on-no-commits

LEARN MORE
  Use `gh <command> <subcommand> --help` for more information about a command.
  Read the manual at https://cli.github.com/manual
  Learn about exit codes using `gh help exit-codes`
  Learn about accessibility experiences using `gh help accessibility`
```

```bash
import os, pathlib, signal, subprocess, tempfile, time, json

    fake.chmod(0o755)
    for shell in ('/usr/local/bin/bash','/usr/local/bin/zsh'):
      for signame in ('SIGHUP','SIGTERM','SIGINT'):
        tmp=root/(pathlib.Path(shell).name+'-'+signame)
        tmp.mkdir()
        script=f'''dev() {{
  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
  __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${{TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/dev-cd.XXXXXX")" || return
  __dev_status=0
  DEV_SHELL_CD_FD=3 command {fake} "$@" 3>"$__dev_cd_file" || __dev_status=$?
  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
    IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file" || __dev_status=1
  fi
  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" || :
  return $__dev_status
}}
dev hold
'''
        p=subprocess.Popen([shell], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                           text=True, env={**os.environ,'TMPDIR':str(tmp)}, start_new_session=True)
        p.stdin.write(script); p.stdin.close()
        files=[]
        deadline=time.time()+3
        while time.time()<deadline:
          files=list(tmp.glob('dev-cd.*'))
          if files and files[0].stat().st_size:
            break
          time.sleep(.01)
        active=(p.poll() is None)
        data=files[0].read_bytes() if files else b''
        os.killpg(p.pid, getattr(signal,signame))
        try: rc=p.wait(timeout=2)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
          os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL); rc=p.wait()
        leaked=list(tmp.glob('dev-cd.*'))
        results.append({'shell':pathlib.Path(shell).name,'signal':signame,'active_at_signal':active,
                        'pre_signal_hex':data.hex(),'exit':rc,'leaked':bool(leaked),
                        'leaked_hex':leaked[0].read_bytes().hex() if leaked else ''})
print(json.dumps(results,separators=(',',':')))
PY
```

```text
9	
10	// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to
11	// leave the user *inside* the checkout. The binary keeps its real stdout so a
12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
14	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
15	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  # Commands outside the navigation surface need no side channel. Besides
19	  # avoiding two subprocesses, this keeps them working when TMPDIR is stale.
20	  case "${1:-}" in
21	    __complete|__completeNoDesc|--help|-h|--version|--skill|completion|config|doctor|done|edit|gitignore|ignore|help|list|ls|park|skill|stats|status|sweep|adopt|bootstrap)
22	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
23	      return 0
24	      ;;
25	  esac
26	
27	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
28	  if ! __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"; then
29	    __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || {
30	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
31	      return 0
32	    }
33	  fi
34	
35	  __dev_status=0
36	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FD=3 command %[1]s "$@" 3>"$__dev_cd_file" || __dev_status=$?
37	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
38	    if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"; then
39	      if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
40	        builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir" || __dev_status=$?
41	      fi
42	    else
43	      __dev_status=1
44	    fi
45	  fi
46	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" || :
47	  return $__dev_status
48	}
49	`
50	
51	const fishInit = `# dev shell integration — add to config.fish:
52	#   dev shell-init fish | source
53	set -gx DEV_SHELL_INIT 1
54	function dev
55	    set -l __dev_command ""
56	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0
57	        set __dev_command $argv[1]
58	    end
59	    if contains -- "$__dev_command" __complete __completeNoDesc --help -h --version --skill completion config doctor done edit gitignore ignore help list ls park skill stats status sweep adopt bootstrap
60	        command %[1]s $argv
61	        return $status
62	    end
63	
64	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
65	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
66	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
67	    if test $status -ne 0
68	        set __dev_cd_file (mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
69	    end
70	    if test -z "$__dev_cd_file"
71	        command %[1]s $argv
72	        return $status
73	    end
74	
75	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FD 3
76	    command %[1]s $argv 3>"$__dev_cd_file"
77	    set -l __dev_status $status
78	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"
79	        if read -z -l __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
80	            if test -n "$__dev_dir"
81	                builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir"
82	                set __dev_status $status
83	            end
84	        else
85	            set __dev_status 1
86	        end
87	    end
88	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"
89	    return $__dev_status
90	end
91	`

93	func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
94		cmd := &cobra.Command{
95			Use:   "shell-init <bash|zsh|fish>",
96			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
97			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
98	
99	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
100	"none" runtime) pass the destination through a child-only file descriptor,
101	because a child process cannot change its parent's working directory. The
102	wrapper reads that path and changes directory without evaluating shell code.
103	
104	Add to your shell rc file:
105	
106	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
107	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
108			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
109			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
110			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
111				self, err := os.Executable()
112				if err != nil || self == "" {
113					self = "dev"
114				}
115				switch args[0] {
116				case "bash", "zsh":
117					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
118				case "fish":

120				default:
121					return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
122				}
123				return nil
124			},
```

```text
-// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
-// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
-// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
-// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
-func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
-	fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
+// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
+// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
+// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
+// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
+// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
+// integrations.
+func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
+	if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
+		fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
+		if err != nil || fd < 3 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
+		}
+		file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
+		if file == nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
+		}
+		if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
+	return err
 }
 
 // ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
```

```text
10	// posixInit and fishInit define the wrapper that makes `dev resume` able to

12	// terminal still opens the TUI and a pipe still receives plain output; a
13	// private file carries only the requested parent-directory change.
14	const posixInit = `# dev shell integration — add to your rc file:
15	#   eval "$(dev shell-init %[2]s)"
16	export DEV_SHELL_INIT=1
17	dev() {
18	  # Commands outside the navigation surface need no side channel. Besides
19	  # avoiding two subprocesses, this keeps them working when TMPDIR is stale.
20	  case "${1:-}" in
21	    __complete|__completeNoDesc|--help|-h|--version|--skill|completion|config|doctor|done|edit|gitignore|ignore|help|list|ls|park|skill|stats|status|sweep|adopt|bootstrap)
22	      command %[1]s "$@" || return $?
23	      return 0
24	      ;;
25	  esac
26	
27	  local __dev_cd_file __dev_dir __dev_status
28	  if ! __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"; then
29	    __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || {
30	      printf 'dev: cannot create the shell directory side channel\n' >&2
31	      return 1
32	    }
33	  fi
34	
35	  __dev_status=0
36	  DEV_SHELL_CD_FD=3 command %[1]s "$@" 3>"$__dev_cd_file" || __dev_status=$?
37	  if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]; then
38	    if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"; then
39	      if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]; then
40	        builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir" || __dev_status=$?
41	      fi
42	    else
43	      __dev_status=1
44	    fi
45	  fi
46	  rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" || :
47	  return $__dev_status
48	}
49	`

56	    if test (count $argv) -gt 0
57	        set __dev_command $argv[1]
58	    end
59	    if contains -- "$__dev_command" __complete __completeNoDesc --help -h --version --skill completion config doctor done edit gitignore ignore help list ls park skill stats status sweep adopt bootstrap
60	        command %[1]s $argv
61	        return $status
62	    end
63	
64	    set -l __dev_tmpdir /tmp
65	    set -q TMPDIR; and set __dev_tmpdir $TMPDIR
66	    set -l __dev_cd_file (mktemp "$__dev_tmpdir/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)
67	    if test $status -ne 0

69	    end
70	    if test -z "$__dev_cd_file"
71	        printf 'dev: cannot create the shell directory side channel\n' >&2

73	    end
74	
75	    set -lx DEV_SHELL_CD_FD 3
76	    command %[1]s $argv 3>"$__dev_cd_file"

78	    if test $__dev_status -eq 0; and test -s "$__dev_cd_file"

87	    end
88	    rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file"

90	end
91	`

93	func newShellInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

96			Short: "Print the shell wrapper that lets dev change your directory",
97			Long: `Print a shell function that wraps the dev binary.
98	
99	dev commands that move you into a checkout (resume, try, wt open with the
100	"none" runtime) pass the destination through a child-only file descriptor,
101	because a child process cannot change its parent's working directory. The
102	wrapper reads that path and changes directory without evaluating shell code.
103	
104	Add to your shell rc file:
105	
106	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"          # bash and zsh
107	    dev shell-init fish | source          # fish`,
108			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
109			ValidArgs: []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"},
110			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
111				self, err := os.Executable()
112				if err != nil || self == "" {
113					self = "dev"
114				}
115				switch args[0] {
116				case "bash", "zsh":
117					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, posixInit, shellQuote(self), args[0])
118				case "fish":
119					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, fishInit, shellQuote(self))
120				default:
121					return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell %q: want bash, zsh or fish", args[0])
122				}
123				return nil
124			},
125		}
126		return cmd
127	}
```

```text
14	// Version is set at build time via -ldflags. VersionFromBuild also recovers a
15	// module version for `go install ...@version` builds.
16	var Version = "dev"
17	
18	func versionFromBuild() string {
19		if Version != "dev" {
20			return Version
21		}
22		if info, ok := debug.ReadBuildInfo(); ok && info.Main.Version != "" && info.Main.Version != "(devel)" {
23			return info.Main.Version
24		}
25		return Version
26	}

28	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
29	
30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
31	
32	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
33	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
34	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
35	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
36	
37	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
38	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
39	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`
40	
41	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
42	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
43		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
44	}
45	
46	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
47	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
48	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
49	// descriptors.
50	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
51		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
52	
53		root := &cobra.Command{
54			Use:           "dev",
55			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
56			Long:          rootLong,
57			Version:       versionFromBuild(),
58			SilenceUsage:  true,
59			SilenceErrors: true,
60			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
61			// exists to answer.
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
64					out, err := skill.Render()
65					if err != nil {
66						return err
67					}
68					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
69					return nil
70				}
71				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
72				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
73				if interactive() {
74					return runTUI(app)
75				}
76				return runList(app, listOptions{})
77			},
78			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
79				if completionInvocation(cmd) {
80					return nil
81				}
82				return app.Load()
83			},
84		}
85	
86		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
87		pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
88		pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux or none")
89		pf.BoolVar(&app.noRuntime, "no-runtime", false, "do not touch any terminal multiplexer")
90		registerFlagCompletion(root, "runtime", runtimeCompletions())
91	
92		// Mirrors `herdr --skill`: the binary is the authority for its own agent
93		// skill, so a dotfiles installer can sync it without vendoring a copy.
94		root.Flags().Bool("skill", false, "print the bundled agent skill and exit")
95	
96		root.AddCommand(

98			newTUICmd(app),

122		root.SetOut(out)
123		root.SetErr(errOut)
```

```text
1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11		"strconv"
12	
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16	)
17	
18	// App is the state shared by every command.
19	type App struct {
20		Cfg   config.Config
21		Tasks *task.Store
22	
23		Out io.Writer
24		Err io.Writer
25	
26		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
27		configPath string
28		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
29		runtimeOverride string
30		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
31		noRuntime bool
32	}
33	
34	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
35	func (a *App) Load() error {
36		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
37		if err != nil {
38			return err
39		}
40		a.Cfg = cfg
41		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
42		if a.Out == nil {
43			a.Out = os.Stdout
44		}
45		if a.Err == nil {
46			a.Err = os.Stderr
47		}
48		return nil
49	}
50	
51	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
52	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
53	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
54		if a.noRuntime {
55			return runtime.None{}
56		}
57		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
58		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
59			backend = a.runtimeOverride
60		}
61		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
62		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
63			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
64		}
65		return rt
66	}
67	
68	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
69	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
70		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
71	}
72	
73	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
74	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
76	}
77	
78	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
79	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
80	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
81	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
82	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
83	// integrations.
84	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
85		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
86			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
87			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
88				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
89			}
90			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
91			if file == nil {
92				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
93			}
94			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
95				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
96			}
97			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
98				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
99			}
100			return nil
101		}
102		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
103		return err
104	}
105	
106	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
107	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
108
```
