If a matching git tag does not yet exist, one will automatically get created
from the latest state of the default branch.
Use `--target` to point to a different branch or commit for the automatic tag creation.
Use `--verify-tag` to abort the release if the tag doesn't already exist.
To fetch the new tag locally after the release, do `git fetch --tags origin`.

To create a release from an annotated git tag, first create one locally with
git, push the tag to GitHub, then run this command.
Use `--notes-from-tag` to get the release notes from the annotated git tag.
If the tag is not annotated, the commit message will be used instead.

Use `--generate-notes` to automatically generate notes using GitHub Release Notes API.
When using automatically generated release notes, a release title will also be automatically
generated unless a title was explicitly passed. Additional release notes can be prepended to
automatically generated notes by using the `--notes` flag.

By default, the release is created even if there are no new commits since the last release.
This may result in the same or duplicate release which may not be desirable in some cases.
Use `--fail-on-no-commits` to fail if no new commits are available. This flag has no
effect if there are no existing releases or this is the very first release.

## Immutable Releases

When release immutability is enabled for a repository, the following protections are enforced:
- Git tags associated with a release cannot be modified or deleted.
- Release assets cannot be modified or deleted.

Immutability is enforced only after a release is published. Draft releases can be modified
or deleted, and the associated git tags can be modified or deleted as well.

When using the `create` command to attach assets to a release, separate API calls
are made to create the release as a draft, upload the assets, and then publish the release.
Immutability protections will be enforced ONLY after the release is published.


USAGE
  gh release create [<tag>] [<filename>... | <pattern>...]

ALIASES
  gh release new

FLAGS
      --discussion-category string   Start a discussion in the specified category
  -d, --draft                        Save the release as a draft instead of publishing it
      --fail-on-no-commits           Fail if there are no commits since the last release (no impact on the first release)
      --generate-notes               Automatically generate title and notes for the release via GitHub Release Notes API
      --latest                       Mark this release as "Latest" (default [automatic based on date and version]). --latest=false to explicitly NOT set as latest
  -n, --notes string                 Release notes
  -F, --notes-file file              Read release notes from file (use "-" to read from standard input)
      --notes-from-tag               Fetch notes from the tag annotation or message of commit associated with tag
      --notes-start-tag string       Tag to use as the starting point for generating release notes
  -p, --prerelease                   Mark the release as a prerelease
      --target branch                Target branch or full commit SHA (default [main branch])
  -t, --title string                 Release title
      --verify-tag                   Abort in case the git tag doesn't already exist in the remote repository

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

EXAMPLES
  # Interactively create a release
  $ gh release create
  
  # Interactively create a release from specific tag
  $ gh release create v1.2.3
  
  # Non-interactively create a release
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 --notes "bugfix release"
  
  # Use automatically generated via GitHub Release Notes API release notes
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 --generate-notes
  
  # Use release notes from a file
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 -F release-notes.md
  
  # Use tag annotation or associated commit message as notes
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 --notes-from-tag
  
  # Don't mark the release as latest
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 --latest=false
  
  # Upload all tarballs in a directory as release assets
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 ./dist/*.tgz
  
  # Upload a release asset with a display label
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 '/path/to/asset.zip#My display label'
  
  # Create a release and start a discussion
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 --discussion-category "General"
  
  # Create a release only if there are new commits available since the last release
  $ gh release create v1.2.3 --fail-on-no-commits

LEARN MORE
  Use `gh <command> <subcommand> --help` for more information about a command.
  Read the manual at https://cli.github.com/manual
  Learn about exit codes using `gh help exit-codes`
  Learn about accessibility experiences using `gh help accessibility`

86		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
87		pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
88		pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux or none")
89		pf.BoolVar(&app.noRuntime, "no-runtime", false, "do not touch any terminal multiplexer")
90		registerFlagCompletion(root, "runtime", runtimeCompletions())
91	
92		// Mirrors `herdr --skill`: the binary is the authority for its own agent
93		// skill, so a dotfiles installer can sync it without vendoring a copy.
94		root.Flags().Bool("skill", false, "print the bundled agent skill and exit")
95	
96		root.AddCommand(
97			newListCmd(app),
98			newTUICmd(app),
99			newStatusCmd(app),
100			newStartCmd(app),
101			newParkCmd(app),
102			newResumeCmd(app),
103			newDoneCmd(app),
104			newSweepCmd(app),
105			newAdoptCmd(app),
106			newBootstrapCmd(app),
107			newWorktreeCmd(app),
108			newRepoCmd(app),
109			newGitignoreCmd(app),
110			newTryCmd(app),
111			newGraduateCmd(app),
112			newStatsCmd(app),
113			newHelpTopicCmd(app),
114			newSkillCmd(app),
115			newDoctorCmd(app),
116			newShellInitCmd(app),
117			newConfigCmd(app),
118			newCacheCmd(app),
119			newEditCmd(app),
120		)
121		root.SetHelpCommand(&cobra.Command{Hidden: true, Use: "no-help"})
122		root.SetOut(out)
123		root.SetErr(errOut)
124		return root
125	}
126	
127	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
128	func Execute() int {
129		root := NewRootCommand()
130		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
131			msg := err.Error()
132			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
133			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
134				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
135			}
136			return 1
137		}
138		return 0
139	}

22	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
23	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
24	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
25	// persistent flags (notably --config).
26	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
27		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd || cmd.CalledAs() == cobra.ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd {
28			return true
29		}
30		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
31			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
32				return true
33			}
34		}
35		return false
36	}

38	// loadCompletion prepares local providers after Cobra has parsed the command
39	// line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break command and
40	// flag completion entirely. Cobra invokes one custom provider per request, so
41	// loading here avoids state leaking when a command tree is reused.
42	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool { return a.Load() == nil }

44	func completeTasks(app *App, states ...task.State) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		allowed := make(map[task.State]bool, len(states))
46		for _, state := range states {
47			allowed[state] = true
48		}
49		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
50			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
54			if err != nil {
55				return nil, noFileCompletion
56			}
57			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
58			for _, t := range tasks {
59				if !allowed[t.State] {
60					continue
61				}
62				value := t.ID
63				if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
64					for _, ref := range []string{t.Title(), t.Branch} {
65						if candidate, ok := taskCompletionRef(tasks, t, ref, toComplete); ok {
66							value = candidate
67							break
68						}
69					}
70				}
71				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.ID)
72				out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
73			}
74			return out, noFileCompletion
75		}
76	}
77	
78	func taskCompletionRef(all []*task.Task, target *task.Task, ref, typed string) (string, bool) {
79		if len(typed) > len(ref) || !strings.EqualFold(ref[:len(typed)], typed) {
80			return "", false
81		}
82		candidate := typed + ref[len(typed):]
83		var exact []*task.Task
84		for _, t := range all {
85			if t.ID == candidate || t.Branch == candidate {
86				exact = append(exact, t)
87			}
88		}
89		if len(exact) > 0 {
90			return candidate, len(exact) == 1 && exact[0].ID == target.ID
91		}
92		needle := strings.ToLower(candidate)
93		var match *task.Task
94		for _, t := range all {
95			haystack := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
96			if !strings.Contains(haystack, needle) {
97				continue
98			}
99			if match != nil {
100				return "", false
101			}
102			match = t
103		}
104		return candidate, match != nil && match.ID == target.ID
105	}

156	func repositoryCompletions(app *App, toComplete string, namesOnly bool) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
157		if !app.loadCompletion() {
158			return nil, noFileCompletion
159		}
160		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.CompletionOptions())
161		if err != nil {
162			return nil, noFileCompletion
163		}
164		displayCount := make(map[string]int, len(repos))
165		for _, r := range repos {
166			displayCount[r.Display()]++
167		}
168		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(repos))
169		out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
170		for _, r := range repos {
171			value := r.Display()
172			description := config.Contract(r.Path)
173			switch {
174			case namesOnly:
175				value = r.Name
176				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
177			case displayCount[value] > 1:
178				value = r.Path
179				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
180			}
181			if seen[value] {
182				continue
183			}
184			seen[value] = true
185			out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
186		}
187		return out, noFileCompletion
188	}

```text
1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11		"strconv"
12	
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16	)
17	
18	// App is the state shared by every command.
19	type App struct {
20		Cfg   config.Config
21		Tasks *task.Store
22	
23		Out io.Writer
24		Err io.Writer
25	
26		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
27		configPath string
28		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
29		runtimeOverride string
30		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
31		noRuntime bool
32	}
33	
34	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
35	func (a *App) Load() error {
36		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
37		if err != nil {
38			return err
39		}
40		a.Cfg = cfg
41		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
42		if a.Out == nil {
43			a.Out = os.Stdout
44		}
45		if a.Err == nil {
46			a.Err = os.Stderr
47		}
48		return nil
49	}
50	
51	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
52	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
53	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
54		if a.noRuntime {
55			return runtime.None{}
56		}
57		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
58		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
59			backend = a.runtimeOverride
60		}
61		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
62		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
63			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
64		}
65		return rt
66	}
67	
68	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
69	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
70		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
71	}
72	
73	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
74	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
76	}
77	
78	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
79	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
80	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
81	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
82	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
83	// integrations.
84	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
85		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
86			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
87			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
88				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
89			}
90			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
91			if file == nil {
92				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
93			}
94			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
95				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
96			}
97			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
98				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
99			}
100			return nil
101		}
102		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
103		return err
104	}
105	
106	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
107	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
108

18	const noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp

20	var completionDescriptionSanitizer = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ")

22	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
23	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
24	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
25	// persistent flags (notably --config).
26	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
27		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd || cmd.CalledAs() == cobra.ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd {
28			return true
29		}
30		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
31			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
32				return true
33			}
34		}
35		return false
36	}
37	
38	// loadCompletion prepares local providers after Cobra has parsed the command
39	// line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break command and
40	// flag completion entirely. Cobra invokes one custom provider per request, so
41	// loading here avoids state leaking when a command tree is reused.
42	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool { return a.Load() == nil }
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App, states ...task.State) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		allowed := make(map[task.State]bool, len(states))
46		for _, state := range states {
47			allowed[state] = true
48		}
49		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
50			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
54			if err != nil {
55				return nil, noFileCompletion
56			}
57			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
58			for _, t := range tasks {
59				if !allowed[t.State] {
60					continue
61				}
62				value := t.ID
63				if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
64					for _, ref := range []string{t.Title(), t.Branch} {
65						if candidate, ok := taskCompletionRef(tasks, t, ref, toComplete); ok {
66							value = candidate
67							break
68						}
69					}
70				}
71				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.ID)
72				out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
73			}
74			return out, noFileCompletion
75		}
76	}
77	
78	func taskCompletionRef(all []*task.Task, target *task.Task, ref, typed string) (string, bool) {
79		if len(typed) > len(ref) || !strings.EqualFold(ref[:len(typed)], typed) {
80			return "", false
81		}
82		candidate := typed + ref[len(typed):]
83		var exact []*task.Task
84		for _, t := range all {
85			if t.ID == candidate || t.Branch == candidate {
86				exact = append(exact, t)
87			}
88		}
89		if len(exact) > 0 {
90			return candidate, len(exact) == 1 && exact[0].ID == target.ID
91		}
92		needle := strings.ToLower(candidate)
93		var match *task.Task
94		for _, t := range all {
95			haystack := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
96			if !strings.Contains(haystack, needle) {
97				continue
98			}
99			if match != nil {
100				return "", false
101			}
102			match = t
103		}
104		return candidate, match != nil && match.ID == target.ID
105	}

156	func repositoryCompletions(app *App, toComplete string, namesOnly bool) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
157		if !app.loadCompletion() {
158			return nil, noFileCompletion
159		}
160		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.CompletionOptions())
161		if err != nil {
162			return nil, noFileCompletion
163		}
164		displayCount := make(map[string]int, len(repos))
165		for _, r := range repos {
166			displayCount[r.Display()]++
167		}
168		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(repos))
169		out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
170		for _, r := range repos {
171			value := r.Display()
172			description := config.Contract(r.Path)
173			switch {
174			case namesOnly:
175				value = r.Name
176				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
177			case displayCount[value] > 1:
178				value = r.Path
179				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
180			}
181			if seen[value] {
182				continue
183			}
184			seen[value] = true
185			out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
186		}
187		return out, noFileCompletion
188	}

17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}

105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65		// Fast avoids per-repository git subprocesses. It is intended for shell
66		// completion: direct .git-file checkouts are skipped as linked worktrees and
67		// symlink aliases are deduplicated by their physical path.
68		Fast bool
69	}
70	
71	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
72	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
73	
74	// CompletionOptions trades full Git metadata for interactive latency.
75	func CompletionOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3, Fast: true} }
76	
77	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
78	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
79	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
80		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
81		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
82		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
83		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
84	}
85	
86	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
87	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
88	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
89	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
90		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
91			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
92		}
93		seen := map[string]bool{}
94		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
95		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
96		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
97		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
98		identities := map[string]bool{}
99		var out []Repo
100	
101		for _, root := range roots {
102			info, err := os.Stat(root)
103			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
104				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
105			}
106			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
107	
108			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
109				if err != nil {
110					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
111				}
112				if ctx.Err() != nil {
113					return ctx.Err()
114				}
115				if path == rootClean {
116					return nil
117				}
118				name := d.Name()
119				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
120				isDir := d.IsDir()
121				if isLink {
122					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
123					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
124					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
125					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
126						isDir = info.IsDir()
127					}
128				}
129				if !isDir {
130					return nil
131				}
132				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
133					return filepath.SkipDir
134				}
135	
136				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
137				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
138	
139				if isRepoDir(path) {
140					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
141					if real == "" {
142						real = path
143					}
144					bare := isBareDir(path)
145					identity, commonDir := real, real
146					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
147						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
148						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
149						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
150						return filepath.SkipDir
151					}
152					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
153						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
154							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
155							// project in the repo inventory.
156							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
157								return filepath.SkipDir
158							}
159							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
160							real = g.MainRoot
161						}
162					}
163					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
164						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
165						out = append(out, Repo{
166							Name:      name,
167							Path:      path,
168							RealPath:  real,
169							Symlink:   isLink,
170							Root:      rootClean,
171							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
172							CommonDir: commonDir,
173							Bare:      bare,
174							HasGit:    true,
175						})
176					}
177					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
178					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
179					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
180					return filepath.SkipDir
181				}
182				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
183					return filepath.SkipDir
184				}
185				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
186					if !seen[path] {
187						seen[path] = true
188						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
189					}
190				}
191				return nil
192			})
193			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
194				return out, ctx.Err()
195			}
196		}
197	
198		for i := range out {
199			if out[i].Category == "." {
200				out[i].Category = ""
201			}
202		}
203		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
204			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
205				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
206			}
207			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
208		})
209		return out, nil
210	}
211	
212	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
213	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
214	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
215		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
216			return true
217		}
218		return isBareDir(path)
219	}
220	
221	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
222		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
223		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
224	}
225	
226	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
227	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
228		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
229			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
230				return false
231			}
232		}
233		return true
234	}
235	
236	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
237	//
238	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
239	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
240	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
241	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
242		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
243	}
244	
245	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
246	// process per repository in the scan roots.
247	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
248		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
249	}
250	
251	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
252		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
253		if err != nil {
254			return Repo{}, nil, err
255		}
256		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
257			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
258				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
259				if real == "" {
260					real = g.MainRoot
261				}
262				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
263				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
264				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
265				return Repo{
266					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
267					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
268				}, nil, nil
269			}
270		}
271		for _, r := range all {
272			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
273				return r, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
277		var hits []Repo
278		for _, r := range all {
279			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
280				hits = append(hits, r)
281			}
282		}
283		switch len(hits) {
284		case 1:
285			return hits[0], nil, nil
286		case 0:
287			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
288		default:
289			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
290		}
291	}
292	
293	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
294	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
295	
296	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
297	
298	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
299	type AmbiguousError struct {
300		Ref        string
301		Candidates []Repo
302	}
303	
304	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
305		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
306		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
307			names[i] = c.Display()
308		}
309		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
310	}

22	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
23	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
24	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
25	// persistent flags (notably --config).
26	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
27		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd || cmd.CalledAs() == cobra.ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd {
28			return true
29		}
30		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
31			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
32				return true
33			}
34		}
35		return false
36	}
37	
38	// loadCompletion prepares local providers after Cobra has parsed the command
39	// line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break command and
40	// flag completion entirely. Cobra invokes one custom provider per request, so
41	// loading here avoids state leaking when a command tree is reused.
42	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool { return a.Load() == nil }
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App, states ...task.State) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		allowed := make(map[task.State]bool, len(states))
46		for _, state := range states {
47			allowed[state] = true
48		}
49		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
50			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
54			if err != nil {
55				return nil, noFileCompletion
56			}
57			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
58			for _, t := range tasks {
59				if !allowed[t.State] {
60					continue
61				}
62				value := t.ID
63				if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
64					for _, ref := range []string{t.Title(), t.Branch} {
65						if candidate, ok := taskCompletionRef(tasks, t, ref, toComplete); ok {
66							value = candidate
67							break
68						}
69					}
70				}
71				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.ID)
72				out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
73			}
74			return out, noFileCompletion
75		}
76	}

78	func taskCompletionRef(all []*task.Task, target *task.Task, ref, typed string) (string, bool) {
79		if len(typed) > len(ref) || !strings.EqualFold(ref[:len(typed)], typed) {
80			return "", false
81		}
82		candidate := typed + ref[len(typed):]
83		var exact []*task.Task
84		for _, t := range all {
85			if t.ID == candidate || t.Branch == candidate {
86				exact = append(exact, t)
87			}
88		}
89		if len(exact) > 0 {
90			return candidate, len(exact) == 1 && exact[0].ID == target.ID
91		}
92		needle := strings.ToLower(candidate)
93		var match *task.Task
94		for _, t := range all {
95			haystack := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
96			if !strings.Contains(haystack, needle) {
97				continue
98			}
99			if match != nil {
100				return "", false
101			}
102			match = t
103		}
104		return candidate, match != nil && match.ID == target.ID
105	}

13	// tree builds a directory layout: keys are relative paths, a value of "git"
14	// makes the directory a repo root.
15	func tree(t *testing.T, layout map[string]string) string {
16		t.Helper()
17		root := t.TempDir()
18		for rel, kind := range layout {
19			dir := filepath.Join(root, rel)
20			if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
21				t.Fatal(err)
22			}
23			if kind == "git" {
24				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(dir, ".git"), 0o755); err != nil {
25					t.Fatal(err)
26				}
27			}
28		}
29		return root
30	}
31	
32	func names(rs []repo.Repo) []string {
33		out := make([]string, len(rs))
34		for i, r := range rs {
35			out[i] = r.Display()
36		}
37		return out
38	}

40	func TestDiscoverFindsCategorisedAndFlatRepos(t *testing.T) {
41		root := tree(t, map[string]string{
42			"Quant/backtest-engine": "git",
43			"Quant/orderbook":       "git",
44			"Web/music-notes":       "git",
45			"flat-repo":             "git",
46			"Quant/not-a-repo":      "",
47			"empty-dir":             "",
48		})
49	
50		got, err := repo.Discover(context.Background(), []string{root}, repo.DefaultOptions())
51		if err != nil {
52			t.Fatal(err)
53		}
54		want := []string{"Quant/backtest-engine", "flat-repo", "Web/music-notes", "Quant/orderbook"}
55		if len(got) != len(want) {
56			t.Fatalf("found %v, want %d repos", names(got), len(want))
57		}
58		byName := map[string]repo.Repo{}
59		for _, r := range got {
60			byName[r.Name] = r
61		}
62		if byName["backtest-engine"].Category != "Quant" {
63			t.Errorf("category = %q, want Quant", byName["backtest-engine"].Category)
64		}
65		if byName["flat-repo"].Category != "" {
66			t.Errorf("a repo directly in the root should have no category, got %q", byName["flat-repo"].Category)

-// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's

-func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {

+// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
+// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
+// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
+// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
+// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
+// integrations.
+func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
+	if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
+		fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
+		if err != nil || fd < 3 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
+		}
+		file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
+		if file == nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
+		}
+		if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
+	return err
 }

1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123	
124		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
125		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
126	}
127	
128	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}
141	
142	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}

1	// Package stats records where development time actually goes, and renders it
2	// as a contribution-style heatmap.
3	//
4	// Two sources, because neither alone is honest. A sampler watches live agent
5	// and terminal sessions, which is the only way to count the hours spent
6	// reading and debugging rather than committing. Git history backfills the days
7	// before dev was installed and survives a lost database. WakaTime, when
8	// enabled, adds editor time dev cannot observe from the terminal.
9	package stats
10	
11	import (
12		"database/sql"
13		"os"
14		"path/filepath"
15		"time"
16	
17		_ "modernc.org/sqlite"
18	)
19	
20	// Source labels where a measurement came from, so double counting is visible
21	// rather than silent: the same hour can legitimately appear from the sampler
22	// and from WakaTime, and a query decides which to trust.
23	type Source string
24	
25	const (
26		// SourceSession is dev's own sampler watching live runtime sessions.
27		SourceSession Source = "session"
28		// SourceGit is derived from commit timestamps.
29		SourceGit Source = "git"
30		// SourceWakaTime is imported from the WakaTime API.
31		SourceWakaTime Source = "wakatime"
32	)
33	
34	// Store is the activity database.
35	type Store struct{ db *sql.DB }
36	
37	// Open creates or opens the database at path.
38	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
39		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
40			return nil, err
41		}
42		// A short busy timeout matters: the sampler may run from cron while an
43		// interactive `dev stats` is reading.
44		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", path+"?_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)")
45		if err != nil {
46			return nil, err
47		}
48		s := &Store{db: db}
49		if err := s.migrate(); err != nil {
50			db.Close()
51			return nil, err
52		}
53		return s, nil
54	}
55	
56	// Close releases the database.
57	func (s *Store) Close() error { return s.db.Close() }
58	
59	func (s *Store) migrate() error {
60		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
61	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS activity (
62	  day     TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- local date, YYYY-MM-DD
63	  repo    TEXT    NOT NULL,
64	  branch  TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
65	  source  TEXT    NOT NULL,
66	  seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
67	  PRIMARY KEY (day, repo, branch, source)
68	);
69	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS activity_day  ON activity(day);
70	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS activity_repo ON activity(repo);
71	
72	-- Records the last successful run of each collector, so a backfill can pick up
73	-- where it left off instead of rescanning every repo's whole history.
74	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS collector (
75	  name    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
76	  last_at INTEGER NOT NULL
77	);
78	`)
79		return err
80	}
81	
82	// Entry is one measurement.
83	type Entry struct {
84		Day     time.Time
85		Repo    string
86		Branch  string
87		Source  Source
88		Seconds int
89	}
90	
91	// Add accumulates seconds onto a (day, repo, branch, source) bucket.
92	func (s *Store) Add(entries ...Entry) error {
93		if len(entries) == 0 {
94			return nil
95		}
96		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
97		if err != nil {
98			return err
99		}
100		defer tx.Rollback()
101	
102		stmt, err := tx.Prepare(`
103	INSERT INTO activity (day, repo, branch, source, seconds) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
104	ON CONFLICT (day, repo, branch, source) DO UPDATE SET seconds = seconds + excluded.seconds`)
105		if err != nil {
106			return err
107		}
108		defer stmt.Close()
109	
110		for _, e := range entries {
111			if e.Seconds <= 0 || e.Repo == "" {
112				continue
113			}
114			if _, err := stmt.Exec(e.Day.Format(dayFormat), e.Repo, e.Branch, string(e.Source), e.Seconds); err != nil {
115				return err
116			}
117		}
118		return tx.Commit()
119	}
120	
121	// Set replaces a bucket rather than accumulating. Used by importers that are
122	// re-runnable: WakaTime reports the same day's total again on every import, so
123	// adding would inflate it.
124	func (s *Store) Set(entries ...Entry) error {
125		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
126		if err != nil {
127			return err
128		}
129		defer tx.Rollback()
130	
131		stmt, err := tx.Prepare(`
132	INSERT INTO activity (day, repo, branch, source, seconds) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
133	ON CONFLICT (day, repo, branch, source) DO UPDATE SET seconds = excluded.seconds`)
134		if err != nil {
135			return err
136		}
137		defer stmt.Close()
138	
139		for _, e := range entries {
140			if e.Repo == "" {
141				continue
142			}
143			if _, err := stmt.Exec(e.Day.Format(dayFormat), e.Repo, e.Branch, string(e.Source), e.Seconds); err != nil {
144				return err
145			}
146		}
147		return tx.Commit()
148	}
149	
150	const dayFormat = "2006-01-02"
151	
152	// Query narrows a report.
153	type Query struct {
154		Since time.Time
155		Until time.Time
156		Repo  string
157		// ExactRepo uses equality rather than the report-friendly substring match.
158		// Per-repo TUI panels set it so "api" does not include "my-api".
159		ExactRepo bool
160		// Sources limits which collectors count. Empty means all of them.
161		Sources []Source
162	}
163	
164	func (q Query) where() (string, []any) {
165		clause := "WHERE day >= ? AND day <= ?"
166		args := []any{q.Since.Format(dayFormat), q.Until.Format(dayFormat)}
167		if q.Repo != "" {
168			if q.ExactRepo {
169				clause += " AND repo = ?"
170				args = append(args, q.Repo)
171			} else {
172				clause += " AND repo LIKE ?"
173				args = append(args, "%"+q.Repo+"%")
174			}
175		}
176		if len(q.Sources) > 0 {
177			clause += " AND source IN (" + placeholders(len(q.Sources)) + ")"
178			for _, s := range q.Sources {
179				args = append(args, string(s))
180			}
181		}
182		return clause, args
183	}
184	
185	func placeholders(n int) string {
186		if n == 0 {
187			return ""
188		}
189		out := make([]byte, 0, n*2-1)
190		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
191			if i > 0 {
192				out = append(out, ',')
193			}
194			out = append(out, '?')
195		}
196		return string(out)
197	}
198	
199	// DayTotals returns seconds per calendar day.
200	func (s *Store) DayTotals(q Query) (map[string]int, error) {
201		clause, args := q.where()
202		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT day, SUM(seconds) FROM activity `+clause+` GROUP BY day`, args...)
203		if err != nil {
204			return nil, err
205		}
206		defer rows.Close()
207	
208		out := map[string]int{}
209		for rows.Next() {
210			var day string
211			var secs int
212			if err := rows.Scan(&day, &secs); err != nil {
213				return nil, err
214			}
215			out[day] = secs
216		}
217		return out, rows.Err()
218	}
219	
220	// RepoTotal is one row of the per-repo breakdown.
221	type RepoTotal struct {
222		Repo    string
223		Seconds int
224		Days    int
225		Last    string
226	}
227	
228	// RepoTotals returns seconds per repository, busiest first.
229	func (s *Store) RepoTotals(q Query) ([]RepoTotal, error) {
230		clause, args := q.where()
231		rows, err := s.db.Query(`
232	SELECT repo, SUM(seconds) AS secs, COUNT(DISTINCT day) AS days, MAX(day)
233	FROM activity `+clause+`
234	GROUP BY repo ORDER BY secs DESC`, args...)
235		if err != nil {
236			return nil, err
237		}
238		defer rows.Close()
239	
240		var out []RepoTotal
241		for rows.Next() {
242			var r RepoTotal
243			if err := rows.Scan(&r.Repo, &r.Seconds, &r.Days, &r.Last); err != nil {
244				return nil, err
245			}
246			out = append(out, r)
247		}
248		return out, rows.Err()
249	}
250	
251	// RepoDayTotals returns per-day seconds for one repository, for a per-repo
252	// heatmap.
253	func (s *Store) RepoDayTotals(repo string, q Query) (map[string]int, error) {
254		q.Repo = repo
255		return s.DayTotals(q)
256	}
257	
258	// MarkCollected records that a collector ran, so incremental runs know their
259	// starting point.
260	func (s *Store) MarkCollected(name string, at time.Time) error {
261		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
262	INSERT INTO collector (name, last_at) VALUES (?, ?)
263	ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET last_at = excluded.last_at`, name, at.Unix())
264		return err
265	}
266	
267	// LastCollected reports when a collector last ran, zero when never.
268	func (s *Store) LastCollected(name string) time.Time {
269		var unix int64
270		if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT last_at FROM collector WHERE name = ?`, name).Scan(&unix); err != nil {
271			return time.Time{}
272		}
273		return time.Unix(unix, 0)
274	}
275	
276	// Empty reports whether anything has been recorded yet, so the CLI can explain
277	// how to start collecting instead of printing a blank chart.
278	func (s *Store) Empty() bool {
279		var n int
280		if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activity`).Scan(&n); err != nil {
281			return true
282		}
283		return n == 0
284	}
285	
286	// Path is where the database lives inside a state directory.
287	func Path(stateDir string) string { return filepath.Join(stateDir, "stats.db") }
288	
289	// ClearQuery selects durable activity rows to delete. Repo is an exact name —
290	// deletion must not use the fuzzy LIKE semantics a report does.
291	type ClearQuery struct {
292		Repo    string
293		Sources []Source
294	}
295	
296	// Clear deletes matching activity and returns the number of rows removed.
297	// With an empty query it clears all activity and collector checkpoints.
298	func (s *Store) Clear(q ClearQuery) (int64, error) {
299		clause := ""
300		var args []any
301		if q.Repo != "" {
302			clause = " WHERE repo = ?"
303			args = append(args, q.Repo)
304		}
305		if len(q.Sources) > 0 {
306			if clause == "" {
307				clause = " WHERE "
308			} else {
309				clause += " AND "
310			}
311			clause += "source IN (" + placeholders(len(q.Sources)) + ")"
312			for _, source := range q.Sources {
313				args = append(args, string(source))
314			}
315		}
316		result, err := s.db.Exec("DELETE FROM activity"+clause, args...)
317		if err != nil {
318			return 0, err
319		}
320		if q.Repo == "" && len(q.Sources) == 0 {
321			if _, err := s.db.Exec("DELETE FROM collector"); err != nil {
322				return 0, err
323			}
324		}
325		return result.RowsAffected()
326	}

```text
1	package stats
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"strconv"
6		"strings"
7		"time"
8	
9		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/repo"
11		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
12	)
13	
14	// SampleInterval is how much time one sampler run attributes to each active
15	// session. It must match how often the sampler actually runs, so the caller
16	// passes it explicitly rather than relying on a default that silently drifts.
17	const SampleInterval = 5 * time.Minute
18	
19	// Sample attributes one interval of time to every live session whose working
20	// directory sits inside a known repository.
21	//
22	// Only sessions with a *working* agent, or any session when includeIdle is
23	// set, are counted. A workspace left open for three weeks is not three weeks
24	// of work, and counting it that way would make the whole chart meaningless.
25	func Sample(ctx context.Context, s *Store, rt runtime.Runtime, repos []repo.Repo, interval time.Duration, includeIdle bool) (int, error) {
26		sessions, err := rt.List(ctx)
27		if err != nil {
28			return 0, err
29		}
30		now := time.Now()
31		seen := map[string]bool{}
32		var entries []Entry
33	
34		for _, sess := range sessions {
35			if !includeIdle && !isActive(sess.AgentStatus) {
36				continue
37			}
38			for _, dir := range sess.Dirs {
39				r, ok := repoContaining(repos, dir)
40				if !ok {
41					continue
42				}
43				// One session covering several panes in the same repo is still one
44				// person working, so credit it once.
45				key := sess.Handle + "\x00" + r.Name
46				if seen[key] {
47					continue
48				}
49				seen[key] = true
50				branch := ""
51				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, dir); err == nil {
52					branch = st.Branch
53				}
54				entries = append(entries, Entry{
55					Day: now, Repo: r.Name, Branch: branch,
56					Source: SourceSession, Seconds: int(interval.Seconds()),
57				})
58			}
59		}
60		if err := s.Add(entries...); err != nil {
61			return 0, err
62		}
63		return len(entries), s.MarkCollected("session", now)
64	}
65	
66	// isActive reports a session doing something worth counting. Backends that
67	// report no status at all are counted, since the alternative is recording
68	// nothing on tmux.
69	func isActive(status string) bool {
70		switch strings.ToLower(status) {
71		case "working", "running", "busy", "":
72			return true
73		}
74		return false
75	}
76	
77	func repoContaining(repos []repo.Repo, dir string) (repo.Repo, bool) {
78		var best repo.Repo
79		bestLen := 0
80		for _, r := range repos {
81			if dir == r.Path || strings.HasPrefix(dir, r.Path+"/") {
82				if len(r.Path) > bestLen {
83					best, bestLen = r, len(r.Path)
84				}
85			}
86		}
87		return best, bestLen > 0
88	}
89	
90	// CommitWeight is the time credited to one commit when backfilling from git
91	// history. Commits are evidence that work happened on a day, not a measure of
92	// how long it took, so this is a coarse stand-in — enough to shade a heatmap
93	// cell, not to bill against.
94	const CommitWeight = 20 * time.Minute
95	
96	// BackfillGit reads commit history and records one CommitWeight per commit,
97	// per day, per repo.
98	//
99	// This is what makes a heatmap useful on the day dev is installed rather than
100	// three months later, and what lets the chart survive losing stats.db.
101	func BackfillGit(ctx context.Context, s *Store, repos []repo.Repo, since time.Time, author string) (int, error) {
102		var entries []Entry
103		for _, r := range repos {
104			if r.Bare {
105				continue
106			}
107			args := []string{"log", "--all", "--no-merges",
108				"--since=" + since.Format("2006-01-02"), "--format=%at%x09%aE"}
109			out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, r.Path, args...)
110			if err != nil || out == "" {
111				continue
112			}
113			// Commits land in buckets by day; several commits on one day add up.
114			perDay := map[string]int{}
115			for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
116				ts, email, _ := strings.Cut(line, "\t")
117				if author != "" && !strings.EqualFold(email, author) {
118					continue
119				}
120				unix, err := strconv.ParseInt(strings.TrimSpace(ts), 10, 64)
121				if err != nil {
122					continue
123				}
124				perDay[time.Unix(unix, 0).Format(dayFormat)]++
125			}
126			for day, count := range perDay {
127				d, err := time.ParseInLocation(dayFormat, day, time.Local)
128				if err != nil {
129					continue
130				}
131				entries = append(entries, Entry{
132					Day: d, Repo: r.Name, Source: SourceGit,
133					Seconds: count * int(CommitWeight.Seconds()),
134				})
135			}
136		}
137		// Set, not Add: re-running a backfill over the same window must not double
138		// the numbers.
139		if err := s.Set(entries...); err != nil {
140			return 0, err
141		}
142		return len(entries), s.MarkCollected("git", time.Now())
143	}
144

53		}

86	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
87	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
88	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
89	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
90		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
91			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
92		}

95		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
96		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
97		// simply by ordering scan_roots.

100	
101		for _, root := range roots {

105			}
106			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)

108			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {

128				}
129				if !isDir {
130					return nil
131				}
132				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
133					return filepath.SkipDir
134				}
135

137				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))

139				if isRepoDir(path) {

141					if real == "" {

143					}

149						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
150						return filepath.SkipDir

152					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
153						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
154							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
155							// project in the repo inventory.
156							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
157								return filepath.SkipDir
158							}
159							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir

161						}
162					}
163					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
164						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
165						out = append(out, Repo{
166							Name:      name,
167							Path:      path,
168							RealPath:  real,
169							Symlink:   isLink,
170							Root:      rootClean,
171							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
172							CommonDir: commonDir,
173							Bare:      bare,
174							HasGit:    true,
175						})
176					}
177					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
178					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
179					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
180					return filepath.SkipDir
181				}
182				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
183					return filepath.SkipDir
184				}
185				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
186					if !seen[path] {
187						seen[path] = true
188						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
189					}

192			})
193			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
194				return out, ctx.Err()
195			}
196		}

202		}

204			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
205				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
206			}
207			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path

210	}

212	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
213	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
214	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {

216			return true
217		}
218		return isBareDir(path)
219	}

222		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
223		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
224	}

227	func isBareDir(path string) bool {

230				return false

236	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
237	//
238	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
239	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
240	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
241	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
242		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
243	}
244	
245	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
246	// process per repository in the scan roots.
247	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
248		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
249	}
250	
251	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
252		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
253		if err != nil {
254			return Repo{}, nil, err
255		}
256		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
257			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
258				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
259				if real == "" {
260					real = g.MainRoot
261				}
262				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
263				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
264				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
265				return Repo{
266					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
267					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
268				}, nil, nil
269			}
270		}
271		for _, r := range all {
272			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
273				return r, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
277		var hits []Repo
278		for _, r := range all {
279			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
280				hits = append(hits, r)
281			}
282		}
283		switch len(hits) {
284		case 1:
285			return hits[0], nil, nil
286		case 0:
287			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
288		default:
289			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
290		}
291	}

293	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
294	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
295	
296	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
297	
298	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
299	type AmbiguousError struct {
300		Ref        string
301		Candidates []Repo
302	}
303	
304	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
305		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
306		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
307			names[i] = c.Display()
308		}
309		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
310	}

10	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
11	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
12	type Repo struct {
13		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
14		Root string
15		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
16		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
17		GitCommonDir string
18		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
19		Name string
20		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
21		// the main checkout.
22		IsLinkedWorktree bool
23		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
24		MainRoot string
25		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
26		Bare bool
27	}
28	
29	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
30	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
31	
32	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
33	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
34		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
35		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
36		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
37			"rev-parse",
38			"--path-format=absolute",
39			"--show-toplevel",
40			"--git-common-dir",
41			"--is-bare-repository",
42		)
43		if err != nil {
44			return Repo{}, err
45		}
46		f := lines(out)
47		r := Repo{}
48		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
49		switch len(f) {
50		case 3:
51			r.Root = f[0]
52			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
53			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
54		case 2:
55			r.GitCommonDir = f[0]
56			r.Bare = f[1] == "true"
57		default:
58			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
59		}
60	
61		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
62		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
63		if r.Bare {
64			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
65		} else {
66			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
67		}
68		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.Root != r.MainRoot
69		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
70		if r.Bare {
71			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
72			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
73			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
74				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
75			}
76		}
77		return r, nil
78	}

80	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
81	// a full Discover.
82	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
83		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
84		return err == nil
85	}

87	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
88	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
89	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
90	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
91	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
92		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
93			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
94				return b
95			}
96		}
97		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
98			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
99				return cand
100			}
101		}
102		return ""
103	}

106	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
107		if name == "" {
108			name = "origin"
109		}
110		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
111		if err != nil {
112			return ""
113		}
114		return out
115	}

117	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
118	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
119	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
120	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
121	// semantics should use Remote instead.
122	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
123		if commonDir == "" {
124			return ""
125		}
126		if name == "" {
127			name = "origin"
128		}
129		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
130		if err != nil {
131			return ""
132		}
133		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
134		section := ""
135		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
136			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
137			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
138				continue
139			}
140			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
141				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
142				continue
143			}
144			if section != want {
145				continue
146			}
147			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
148			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
149				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
150			}
151		}
152		return ""
153	}

8	// PostCreate accepts either of two TOML shapes, because both read naturally:
9	//
10	//	post_create = "auto"
11	//	post_create = ["uv sync", "npm ci"]
12	type PostCreate struct {
13		Auto     bool
14		Commands []string
15	}
16	
17	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
18	func (p *PostCreate) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
19		switch t := v.(type) {
20		case string:
21			if t != "auto" {
22				return fmt.Errorf("post_create: %q is not a valid string form (use \"auto\" or a list of commands)", t)
23			}
24			*p = PostCreate{Auto: true}
25			return nil
26		case []any:
27			cmds := make([]string, 0, len(t))
28			for i, e := range t {
29				s, ok := e.(string)
30				if !ok {
31					return fmt.Errorf("post_create[%d]: want a command string, got %T", i, e)
32				}
33				cmds = append(cmds, s)
34			}
35			*p = PostCreate{Commands: cmds}
36			return nil
37		default:
38			return fmt.Errorf("post_create: want \"auto\" or a list of command strings, got %T", v)
39		}
40	}
41	
42	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler so a config round-trips.
43	func (p PostCreate) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
44		if p.Auto {
45			return []byte(`"auto"`), nil
46		}
47		out := []byte("[")
48		for i, c := range p.Commands {
49			if i > 0 {
50				out = append(out, ", "...)
51			}
52			out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%q", c)...)
53		}
54		return append(out, ']'), nil
55	}
56	
57	// Duration is a time.Duration written in TOML as a Go duration string
58	// ("10m", "90s"), which is friendlier than a bare number of seconds.
59	type Duration struct{ time.Duration }
60	
61	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
62	func (d *Duration) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
63		switch t := v.(type) {
64		case string:
65			parsed, err := time.ParseDuration(t)
66			if err != nil {
67				return fmt.Errorf("duration %q: %w", t, err)
68			}
69			d.Duration = parsed
70			return nil
71		case int64:
72			d.Duration = time.Duration(t) * time.Second
73			return nil
74		default:
75			return fmt.Errorf("duration: want a string like \"10m\", got %T", v)
76		}
77	}
78	
79	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler.
80	func (d Duration) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
81		return []byte(fmt.Sprintf("%q", d.Duration.String())), nil
82	}

229	func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
230		if len(args) > 0 {
231			return nil, noFileCompletion
232		}
233		topics, err := help.List()
234		if err != nil {
235			return nil, noFileCompletion
236		}
237		out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
238		for _, topic := range topics {
239			out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
240		}
241		return out, noFileCompletion
242	}
243	
244	func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
245		used := make(map[string]bool, len(args))
246		for _, name := range args {
247			used[strings.ToLower(name)] = true
248		}
249		names := ignore.BundledNames()
250		out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
251		for _, name := range names {
252			value := strings.ToLower(name)
253			if !used[value] {
254				out = addCompletion(out, value, name+" bundled template", toComplete)
255			}
256		}
257		return out, noFileCompletion
258	}
259	
260	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
261		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
262			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
263			for _, value := range values {
264				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
265			}
266			return out, noFileCompletion
267		}
268	}
269	
270	func runtimeCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
271		backends := runtime.All()
272		values := make([]string, 1, len(backends)+1)
273		values[0] = "auto"
274		for _, backend := range backends {
275			values = append(values, backend.Name())
276		}
277		return fixedCompletions(values...)
278	}

281		values := make([]string, len(task.States))

300	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
301		if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
302			return out
303		}
304		if description != "" {
305			description = completionDescriptionSanitizer.Replace(description)
306			value = cobra.CompletionWithDesc(value, description)
307		}
308		return append(out, value)

22	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
23	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
24	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
25	// persistent flags (notably --config).
26	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
27		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd || cmd.CalledAs() == cobra.ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd {
28			return true
29		}
30		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
31			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
32				return true
33			}
34		}
35		return false
36	}

39	// line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break command and
40	// flag completion entirely. Cobra invokes one custom provider per request, so
41	// loading here avoids state leaking when a command tree is reused.
42	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool { return a.Load() == nil }
