44	func completeTasks(app *App, states ...task.State) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		allowed := make(map[task.State]bool, len(states))
46		for _, state := range states {
47			allowed[state] = true
48		}
49		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
50			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
54			if err != nil {
55				return nil, noFileCompletion
56			}
57			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
58			for _, t := range tasks {
59				if !allowed[t.State] {
60					continue
61				}
62				value := t.ID
63				if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
64					for _, ref := range []string{t.Title(), t.Branch} {
65						if candidate, ok := taskCompletionRef(tasks, t, ref, toComplete); ok {
66							value = candidate
67							break
68						}
69					}
70				}
71				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.ID)
72				out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
73			}
74			return out, noFileCompletion
75		}
76	}

78	func taskCompletionRef(all []*task.Task, target *task.Task, ref, typed string) (string, bool) {
79		if len(typed) > len(ref) || !strings.EqualFold(ref[:len(typed)], typed) {
80			return "", false
81		}
82		candidate := typed + ref[len(typed):]
83		var exact []*task.Task
84		for _, t := range all {
85			if t.ID == candidate || t.Branch == candidate {
86				exact = append(exact, t)
87			}
88		}
89		if len(exact) > 0 {
90			return candidate, len(exact) == 1 && exact[0].ID == target.ID
91		}
92		needle := strings.ToLower(candidate)
93		var match *task.Task
94		for _, t := range all {
95			haystack := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
96			if !strings.Contains(haystack, needle) {
97				continue
98			}
99			if match != nil {
100				return "", false
101			}
102			match = t
103		}
104		return candidate, match != nil && match.ID == target.ID
105	}

156	func repositoryCompletions(app *App, toComplete string, namesOnly bool) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
157		if !app.loadCompletion() {

167		}
168		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(repos))
169		out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
170		for _, r := range repos {
171			value := r.Display()
172			description := config.Contract(r.Path)
173			switch {
174			case namesOnly:
175				value = r.Name
176				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
177			case displayCount[value] > 1:
178				value = r.Path
179				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
180			}
181			if seen[value] {
182				continue
183			}
184			seen[value] = true
185			out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
186		}
187		return out, noFileCompletion

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"os"
6	
7		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
8		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
9		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/wt"
11		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
12	)
13	
14	func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			noProvision bool
17			fetch       bool
18			force       bool
19		)
20		cmd := &cobra.Command{
21			Use:   "resume <task>",
22			Short: "Pick a task back up, rebuilding whatever is missing",
23			Long: `Make a parked task hot again.
24	
25	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
26	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
27	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
28	identity.
29	
30	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
33			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
34			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
35				ctx := ctxOf()
36				t, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
37				if err != nil {
38					return err
39				}
40	
41				host := config.Hostname()
42				if !t.OwnedBy(host) && !force {
43					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is owned by %s.\n"+
44						"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
45						t.ID, t.Owner)
46				}
47	
48				if fetch {
49					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "fetch", "--prune", "origin"); err != nil {
50						app.warnf("fetch failed: %v", err)
51					}
52				}
53	
54				rt := app.Runtime()
55				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
56				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
57	
58				switch mode {
59				case task.ModeWorktree:
60					_, statErr := os.Stat(checkout)
61					// Rebuild the worktree when it is gone — the cold-to-hot path.
62					if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
63						base := t.Base
64						// Prefer the published branch: a cold task's work lives on
65						// the remote, and a stale local ref could drop it.
66						if remote := "origin/" + t.Branch; gitx.RefExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, remote) {
67							base = remote
68						}
69						m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
70						res, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
71							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, RepoName: t.Repo, Branch: t.Branch,
72							Base: base, Label: t.Title(), NoProvision: noProvision,
73						})
74						if err != nil {
75							var exists *wt.ErrExists
76							if asError(err, &exists) {
77								t.WorktreePath = exists.Path
78							} else {
79								return err
80							}
81						} else {
82							t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = res.Path, res.RuntimeHandle
83							reportProvision(app, res)
84							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebuilt    %s\n", config.Contract(res.Path))
85						}
86						checkout = t.WorktreePath
87					}
88	
89				case task.ModeBranch:
90					checkout = t.RepoPath
91					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
92					if err != nil {
93						return err
94					}
95					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
96						if st.Dirty() {
97							return fmt.Errorf("cannot switch the canonical checkout from %s to %s: %s",
98								st.Branch, t.Branch, st.Breakdown())
99						}
100						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "switch", t.Branch); err != nil {
101							return err
102						}
103					}
104	
105				case task.ModeDirect:

15	func newParkCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

20			push   bool
21			cold   bool
22			keepRT bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "park [task]",
26			Short: "Stop working on a task without losing the thread",
27			Long: `Park the current task (or the one named) so its runtime session can close.
28	
29	Parking is the missing move that makes a crowded sidebar shrink. It records
30	what to do next, optionally checkpoints uncommitted work, and closes the
31	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
32	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.
33	
34	  warm (default)  worktree and branch stay; session closes. Back within days.
35	  cold (--cold)   work is committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstruct
36	                  it anywhere later with dev resume.
37	
38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
41			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
42			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
43				ctx := ctxOf()

45				if err != nil {
46					return err
47				}
48	
49				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
50				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
51					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
52						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
53				}
54				target := task.Warm
55				if cold {
56					target = task.Cold
57				}
58				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
59	
60				if next != "" {
61					t.Next = next
62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69	
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97	
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {

105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {

110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114	
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)

124	
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{

145					}
146					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
147						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
148							base, err)
149					}
150				}
151	
152				t.State = target
153				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
154				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
155					return err
156				}
157				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
158				if t.Next != "" {
159					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
160				}
161				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
162				return nil
163			},
164		}
165		f := cmd.Flags()
166		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
167		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
168		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
169		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
170		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
171		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")

173		return cmd

176	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
177	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
178		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
179			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
180		}
181		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
182		return nil
183	}
184	
185	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
186	// directory when no argument is given.
187	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
188		if len(args) == 1 {
189			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
190		}
191		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
196		if err != nil {
197			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
198				config.Contract(cwd))
199		}
200		return t, nil
201	}

29	Two integration modes, matching the two shapes a branch's history takes:
30	
31	  --ff    rebase onto the base and fast-forward it. Use when the branch's
32	          commits are worth keeping in the base's history.

69					}

73						}

173	func directPushHint(push bool) string {
174		if push {
175			return " --push"
176		}
177		return ""
178	}
179	
180	// fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
181	// forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
182	//
183	// merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
184	// branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
185	// a merge commit the user did not ask for.
186	func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
187		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
188		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
189			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
190				"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
191				err, config.Contract(checkout))
192		}
193		// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
194		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
195		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
196			return err
197		}
198		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
199			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
200				"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
201		}
202		return nil
203	}
204	
205	// deleteMergedBranch removes a branch only when git agrees its commits are already
206	// contained in the base — the check that makes cleanup safe.
207	func deleteMergedBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, repoPath, branch, base string) error {
208		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", branch, base); err != nil {
209			return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)
210		}
211		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "branch", "-d", branch); err != nil {
212			return fmt.Errorf("could not delete %s: %w", branch, err)
213		}
214		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   deleted    branch %s\n", branch)
215		return nil
216	}
217	
218	// openPR pushes the branch and asks the forge CLI to open a pull/merge
219	// request. When no forge CLI is available dev prints the push result and the
220	// URL to open by hand, rather than failing: the branch being published is the
221	// part that actually matters.
222	func openPR(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
223		if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
224			return err
225		}
226		kind := forge.Detect(ctx, t.RepoPath)
227		f, err := forge.For(kind)
228		if err != nil || !f.Available() {
229			app.warnf("no forge CLI for this remote — the branch is pushed; open the request in your browser")
230			return nil
231		}
232		url, err := f.CreatePR(ctx, checkout, forge.PRRequest{
233			Base: base, Head: t.Branch, Fill: true,
234		})
235		if err != nil {
236			return err
237		}
238		if url != "" {
239			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   opened     %s\n", url)
240		}
241		return nil
242	}

```text
1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123	
124		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
125		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
126	}
127	
128	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}
141	
142	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}

1	package task
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"io/fs"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"regexp"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	
14		"github.com/BurntSushi/toml"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}

90	dev skill install

92	```
93	
94	Only **git** is required at runtime. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each
95	enable more and degrade cleanly when absent.
96	
97	## The lifecycle
98	
99	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
100	|---|---|---|---|
101	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
102	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
103	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
104	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
105	
106	```bash
107	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
108	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
109	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
110	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
111	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
112	dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
113	```
114	
115	### A task does not have to mean a worktree
116	
117	Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
118	
119	```bash
120	# No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
121	dev repo open api
122	
123	# Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
124	dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct
125	
126	# Use a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout, but no linked worktree.
127	dev start api --task "small feature" --branch-only --base main
128	
129	# Default: independent branch + worktree, provisioned and runtime-opened.
130	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
131	```
132	
133	Direct work can be parked WARM and resumed, but cannot go COLD because the
134	canonical checkout cannot be removed. `dev done` on a clean direct task needs
135	no `--ff` or `--pr`: the work is already on its destination branch.
136	
137	Start direct for one change stream, then create a normal worktree task later
138	when real parallelism appears. A new worktree starts from committed HEAD; dirty
139	main changes are deliberately not smuggled into it, so checkpoint first when
140	the parallel task depends on them.
141	
142	### The dashboard
143	
144	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens three lists, switched with `tab`:
145	
146	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
147	- **REPOS** — every repository under the scan roots, with its branch, dirty
148	  state, worktree count and per-state task tally, sorted so anything in flight
149	  is at the top. What do I have here.
150	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through the authenticated `gh` and `glab`
151	  CLIs, marked when a local clone exists. What can I open or clone.
152	
153	TASKS and REPOS come from the same code paths as `dev ls` and `dev repo list`,
154	so they cannot disagree. The repo list matters on day one: with forty repositories and
155	no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just be empty.
156	
157	Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
158	
159	```
160	j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
161	g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
162	/          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
163	```
164
```

+name: Release
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags: ["v*"]
+
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+
+jobs:
+  validate:
+    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml
+
+  release:
+    needs: validate
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    env:
+      VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
+        with:
+          go-version-file: go.mod
+          cache: true
+
+      - name: Validate release tag
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          [[ "$VERSION" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([.-][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]
+
+      - name: Build tagged version
+        run: |
+          make build
+          test "$(./dev --version)" = "dev version $VERSION"
+
+      - name: Create GitHub release
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+        run: |
+          if ! gh release view "$VERSION" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+            gh release create "$VERSION" --verify-tag --generate-notes --title "$VERSION"
+          fi

1	# Context
2	
3	`dev-cli` 目前只能從 source 以 `make install` 安裝；沒有公開 GitHub repo/tag、Homebrew formula、release 流程或已部署的 completion。CLI 實際是 Go/Cobra（不是 Tyro），而 Cobra 已自動提供 `dev completion <shell>`，但專案又另有未文件化的 `dev shell-init completion ...`，且兩者都沒有被 package manager 安裝或測試。現有 shell wrapper 以 command substitution 捕捉整段 stdout，會讓裸跑 `dev` 看不到 stdout TTY、從 TUI 退化成 plain list。
4	
5	目標是把 `dev-cli` 以 public MIT 專案從 `v0.1.0` 開始發布；macOS 可用 `brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli` 安裝 executable `dev` 並立即取得 bash/zsh/fish completion，Linux 則沿用 dotfiles 的版本鎖定 `go_tools`。同時把 `dev` 納入 dotfiles 的預設開發工具、completion cache、shell directory-change integration 與工具文件，而且不讓 Formula 在安裝期寫入使用者的 agent skill 目錄。
6	
7	# Implementation plan
8	
9	## 1. 先在 `dev-cli` 收斂 shell integration 與 completion
10	
11	- 在 `internal/cli/shell.go` 與 `internal/cli/app.go` 改寫 bash/zsh/fish wrapper：
12	  - 每次呼叫建立權限受限的暫存檔，透過 `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` 傳給真正的 `dev` process；binary 的 stdout/stderr 直接連到原 terminal，不再包在 `$()` 內。
13	  - `App.cdDirective` 在該環境變數存在時只把「原始目錄路徑」寫入檔案；wrapper 成功執行後讀取路徑並以 `cd -- "$path"` 切換，不 `eval` 檔案內容；未載入 wrapper 時保留目前輸出 shell-quoted `cd ...` 的行為。
14	  - 保留 `DEV_SHELL_INIT=1`、child exit status、即時 stdout/stderr、pipe 行為與可靠 cleanup；確認裸 `dev`/`dev tui` 仍看到真實 TTY。
15	- 移除 `newShellInitCmd` 下重複且未文件化的 `shell-init completion` 子命令；唯一公開介面採 Cobra 慣例：`dev completion bash|zsh|fish`（Cobra 現有 PowerShell 可保留，但本次安裝範圍為三種 shell）。
16	- 新增 `internal/cli/completion.go`，以可重用的 `ValidArgsFunction` / `RegisterFlagCompletionFunc` 接到既有 command constructors：
17	  - task：`park`、`resume`、`done`，重用 `internal/task.Store.List`，以穩定 task ID 為值並提供 title/state/repo/branch 描述；
18	  - repo：`start`、`repo open/sync` 與適用的 `--repo`，重用 `internal/repo.Discover`、`Repo.Display`、`resolveRepoRef`；
19	  - worktree：`wt open/rm`，重用 `repoContext`、`internal/gitx.Worktrees`，排除 detached，且 `rm` 排除 main checkout；
20	  - embedded/enum：`help` 重用 `internal/help.List`、`gitignore` 重用 `internal/ignore.BundledNames`，以及 `--runtime`、stats `--source` 等有限值；domain 值回傳 `ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp`，真正的 path arguments 維持 filesystem completion。
21	  - completion 只讀本機 config/task/repo/worktree/embedded data；不在每次 Tab 查 forge/network、collect runtime/status 或寫入 cache。
22	- 修正 `internal/cli/root.go` 的 completion 載入時機：hidden `cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd` 進入 root `PersistentPreRunE` 時，目標 command 的 persistent flags（尤其 `--config`）尚未由 `getCompletions` parse，因此先略過一般 `App.Load`，由 dynamic callback 在 flags parse 後 lazy-load。載入/探索失敗時靜默回傳無 dynamic candidates，仍保留 Cobra 的 command/flag 靜態 completion；執行 `dev completion <shell>` 產生腳本時也不依賴使用者 config。
23	- 在 `internal/cli/cli_test.go`（必要時拆出 focused test file）使用既有 `NewRootCommandWithIO` harness 測試：三種 script generation、移除 duplicate path、直接呼叫 `__complete` 的 task/repo/worktree/help/gitignore/enum candidates、`--config` 生效、壞 config 仍能補 command/flag、NoFileComp directive；另以 subprocess shell tests 驗證 wrapper 的 stdout/stderr、exit status、directory change、cleanup 與 TTY-preserving 行為。
24	- 跑 `make skill-sync` 更新 `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`，再以 `make skill-check` 防止 command tree drift。

30	- 將 `Makefile` 的 `VERSION` 改為可由 `VERSION=v0.1.0 make build` 覆寫，並測試 injected `internal/cli.Version` 會由 `dev --version` 顯示；Homebrew source archive 沒有 `.git`，不能依賴 `git describe`。

46	- `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl`：保留既有單一 `tap "daviddwlee84/tap"`，在 `translate` 旁新增 Darwin 的 `brew "daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli"`；沿用現有 `trust_bundle_taps`，不新增 trust task，也不改 brew-bundle 的 profile/global skip semantics。

19	
20	These are disposable accelerators: the remote forge inventory and fetched
21	GitHub gitignore templates. Activity statistics are deliberately not here —
22	$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db contains observations that may not be
23	reconstructible; use "dev stats path/clear" for it.`,
24		}

39			},

43	func newCacheListCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
44		return &cobra.Command{
45			Use:   "list",
46			Short: "List cache paths, sizes, and ages",
47			Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
48			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
49				t := NewTable("CACHE", "SIZE", "AGE", "PATH")
50				for _, item := range cacheItems() {
51					size, modified, exists := cacheInfo(item.path)
52					if !exists {
53						t.Add(item.name, "—", "—", config.Contract(item.path)+" (absent)")
54						continue
55					}
56					t.Add(item.name, humanBytes(size), humanAge(time.Since(modified)), config.Contract(item.path))
57				}
58				t.Render(app.Out)
59				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\nStats data: %s (not cache; use `dev stats clear`)\n",
60					config.Contract(filepath.Join(app.Cfg.StateDir(), "stats.db")))
61				return nil
62			},
63		}
64	}

66	type cacheItem struct{ name, path string }

68	func cacheItems() []cacheItem {
69		return []cacheItem{
70			{"remote", filepath.Join(cacheRoot(), "remotes.json")},
71			{"gitignore", filepath.Join(cacheRoot(), "gitignore")},
72		}

75	func newCacheClearCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
76		return &cobra.Command{
77			Use:       "clear <remote|gitignore|all>",
78			Short:     "Remove a regenerable cache",
79			Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
80			ValidArgs: []string{"remote", "gitignore", "all"},
81			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
82				var targets []cacheItem
83				switch args[0] {
84				case "remote", "remotes":
85					targets = cacheItems()[:1]
86				case "gitignore":
87					targets = cacheItems()[1:]
88				case "all":
89					targets = cacheItems()
90				default:
91					return fmt.Errorf("unknown cache %q: want remote, gitignore or all", args[0])
92				}
93				removed := 0
94				for _, item := range targets {
95					if _, err := os.Lstat(item.path); os.IsNotExist(err) {
96						continue
97					}
98					if err := os.RemoveAll(item.path); err != nil {
99						return fmt.Errorf("clear %s: %w", item.name, err)
100					}
101					removed++
102				}
103				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "cleared %d cache(s) under %s\n", removed, config.Contract(cacheRoot()))
104				return nil
105			},
106		}
107	}
108	
109	func cacheInfo(path string) (size int64, modified time.Time, exists bool) {
110		info, err := os.Stat(path)
111		if err != nil {
112			return 0, time.Time{}, false
113		}
114		exists, modified = true, info.ModTime()
115		if !info.IsDir() {
116			return info.Size(), modified, true
117		}
118		_ = filepath.WalkDir(path, func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
119			if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
120				return nil
121			}
122			if i, err := d.Info(); err == nil {
123				size += i.Size()
124				if i.ModTime().After(modified) {
125					modified = i.ModTime()
126				}
127			}
128			return nil
129		})
130		return size, modified, true
131	}
132	
133	func humanBytes(n int64) string {
134		const unit = 1024
135		switch {
136		case n < unit:
137			return fmt.Sprintf("%dB", n)
138		case n < unit*unit:
139			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fK", float64(n)/unit)
140		case n < unit*unit*unit:
141			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fM", float64(n)/(unit*unit))
142		default:
143			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fG", float64(n)/(unit*unit*unit))
144		}
145	}

18	const noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
19	
20	var completionDescriptionSanitizer = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ")
21	
22	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
23	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
24	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
25	// persistent flags (notably --config).
26	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
27		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd || cmd.CalledAs() == cobra.ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd {
28			return true
29		}
30		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
31			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
32				return true
33			}
34		}
35		return false
36	}
37	
38	// loadCompletion prepares local providers after Cobra has parsed the command
39	// line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break command and
40	// flag completion entirely. Cobra invokes one custom provider per request, so
41	// loading here avoids state leaking when a command tree is reused.
42	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool { return a.Load() == nil }
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App, states ...task.State) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		allowed := make(map[task.State]bool, len(states))
46		for _, state := range states {
47			allowed[state] = true
48		}
49		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
50			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
54			if err != nil {
55				return nil, noFileCompletion
56			}
57			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
58			for _, t := range tasks {
59				if !allowed[t.State] {
60					continue
61				}
62				value := t.ID
63				if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
64					for _, ref := range []string{t.Title(), t.Branch} {
65						if candidate, ok := taskCompletionRef(tasks, t, ref, toComplete); ok {
66							value = candidate
67							break
68						}
69					}
70				}
71				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.ID)
72				out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
73			}
74			return out, noFileCompletion
75		}
76	}
77	
78	func taskCompletionRef(all []*task.Task, target *task.Task, ref, typed string) (string, bool) {
79		if len(typed) > len(ref) || !strings.EqualFold(ref[:len(typed)], typed) {
80			return "", false
81		}
82		candidate := typed + ref[len(typed):]
83		var exact []*task.Task
84		for _, t := range all {
85			if t.ID == candidate || t.Branch == candidate {
86				exact = append(exact, t)
87			}
88		}
89		if len(exact) > 0 {
90			return candidate, len(exact) == 1 && exact[0].ID == target.ID
91		}
92		needle := strings.ToLower(candidate)
93		var match *task.Task
94		for _, t := range all {
95			haystack := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
96			if !strings.Contains(haystack, needle) {
97				continue
98			}
99			if match != nil {
100				return "", false
101			}
102			match = t
103		}
104		return candidate, match != nil && match.ID == target.ID
105	}

111		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {

156	func repositoryCompletions(app *App, toComplete string, namesOnly bool) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
157		if !app.loadCompletion() {

161		if err != nil {
162			return nil, noFileCompletion
163		}
164		displayCount := make(map[string]int, len(repos))
165		for _, r := range repos {

167		}
168		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(repos))
169		out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
170		for _, r := range repos {
171			value := r.Display()
172			description := config.Contract(r.Path)
173			switch {
174			case namesOnly:
175				value = r.Name
176				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
177			case displayCount[value] > 1:
178				value = r.Path
179				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
180			}
181			if seen[value] {
182				continue
183			}
184			seen[value] = true
185			out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
186		}
187		return out, noFileCompletion
188	}

30	Two sources feed this, because neither alone is honest:

32	  session   dev's sampler, watching live agent and terminal sessions. The only

122	func newStatsSampleCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
123		var (
124			interval    time.Duration
125			includeIdle bool
126		)
127		cmd := &cobra.Command{
128			Use:   "sample",
129			Short: "Record one interval of live session activity",
130			Long: `Attribute one interval of time to every live session working in a known repo.
131	
132	Run this periodically — the interval you pass must match how often it runs, or
133	the totals will be wrong. With cron, every five minutes:
134	
135	    */5 * * * * /usr/local/bin/dev stats sample --interval 5m
136	
137	Idle sessions are skipped by default: a workspace left open for three weeks is
138	not three weeks of work, and counting it that way makes the chart meaningless.`,
139			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
140			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
141				if !app.Cfg.Stats.Sampler {
142					return fmt.Errorf("sampling is disabled (set stats.sampler = true in %s)",
143						config.Contract(config.ConfigFile()))
144				}
145				ctx := ctxOf()
146				store, err := stats.Open(stats.Path(app.Cfg.StateDir()))
147				if err != nil {
148					return err
149				}
150				defer store.Close()
151	
152				repos, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
153				if err != nil {
154					return err
155				}
156				n, err := stats.Sample(ctx, store, app.Runtime(), repos, interval, includeIdle)
157				if err != nil {
158					return err
159				}
160				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "recorded %s across %d active session(s)\n", interval, n)
161				return nil
162			},
163		}
164		f := cmd.Flags()
165		f.DurationVar(&interval, "interval", stats.SampleInterval, "time to attribute, matching how often this runs")
166		f.BoolVar(&includeIdle, "include-idle", false, "also count sessions whose agent is idle")
167		return cmd
168	}

226		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "repo", completeRepoFlag(app))

272	// parseSince accepts a relative window ("30d", "6mo", "1y") or an absolute
273	// date. Relative is what people actually type; absolute is what scripts want.
274	func parseSince(s string, now time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
275		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
276		if s == "" {
277			return now.AddDate(-1, 0, 0), nil
278		}
279		if d, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", s, time.Local); err == nil {
280			return d, nil
281		}
282		var n int
283		var unit string
284		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(s, "%d%s", &n, &unit); err != nil || n <= 0 {
285			return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot parse --since %q: want 30d, 6mo, 1y or YYYY-MM-DD", s)
286		}
287		switch strings.ToLower(unit) {
288		case "d", "day", "days":
289			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n), nil
290		case "w", "week", "weeks":
291			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n*7), nil
292		case "mo", "month", "months":
293			return now.AddDate(0, -n, 0), nil
294		case "y", "yr", "year", "years":
295			return now.AddDate(-n, 0, 0), nil
296		}
297		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown unit %q in --since: want d, w, mo or y", unit)
298	}

211	// checkoutOf is where a task's code lives right now.
212	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
213		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
214			return t.WorktreePath
215		}
216		return t.RepoPath
217	}
218	
219	// annotate pushes the task's state and next action into the runtime as
220	// display-only metadata, so a sidebar can show why a session is open without
221	// anyone having to ask dev.
222	//
223	// For herdr this lands as workspace metadata tokens. A token only renders if
224	// the sidebar row layout in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g.
225	//
226	//	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
227	//	rows = [["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"], ["branch", "git_status"], ["$next"]]
228	//
229	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds and shows nothing,
230	// which is why dev never treats a failure here as an error.
231	func annotate(app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, t *task.Task) {
232		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
233			return
234		}
235		kv := map[string]string{
236			"stage": t.State.Label(),
237			"next":  t.Next,
238		}
239		if err := rt.Annotate(ctxOf(), t.RuntimeHandle, kv); err != nil {
240			app.warnf("could not annotate the runtime session: %v", err)
241		}
242	}
243	
244	func reportProvision(app *App, res *wt.CreateResult) {
245		p := res.Provision
246		if n := len(p.Copied); n > 0 {
247			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   copied    %d gitignored file(s): %s\n", n, strings.Join(p.Copied, ", "))
248		}
249		if n := len(p.Linked); n > 0 {
250			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   linked    %s\n", strings.Join(p.Linked, ", "))
251		}
252		for _, e := range p.Failures {
253			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   warning   %v\n", e)
254		}
255	}

18	
19	// candidate is something already on the machine that could become a task.
20	type candidate struct {
21		Task   *task.Task
22		Reason string
23	}
24	
25	func newAdoptCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
26		var (
27			apply       bool
28			yes         bool
29			noWorktrees bool
30			noSessions  bool
31			noBranches  bool
32			state       string
33		)
34		cmd := &cobra.Command{
35			Use:   "adopt",
36			Short: "Import existing worktrees, sessions and branches as tasks",
37			Long: `Bring what is already on this machine under dev's inventory.
38	
39	There is nothing to migrate to start using dev — repositories are discovered
40	wherever your scan roots point, and no directory is moved or renamed. What is
41	worth importing is the work already in flight: linked worktrees created by
42	hand or by another tool, runtime sessions sitting in a repo, and local
43	branches that are ahead of their base.
44	
45	Reports by default. Nothing is created without --apply, and nothing on disk is
46	ever moved, renamed or deleted by this command.`,
47			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
48			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
49				ctx := ctxOf()
50	
51				target, err := task.ParseState(state)
52				if err != nil {
53					return err
54				}
55	
56				repos, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
57				if err != nil {
58					return err
59				}
60				existing, err := app.Tasks.List()
61				if err != nil {
62					return err
63				}
64				known := map[string]bool{}
65				for _, t := range existing {
66					known[t.ID] = true
67				}
68	
69				rt := app.Runtime()
70				var sessions []runtime.Session
71				if !noSessions {
72					sessions, _ = rt.List(ctx)
73				}
74	
75				var found []candidate
76				for _, r := range repos {
77					if r.Bare {
78						continue
79					}
80					found = append(found, scanRepo(ctx, app, r, sessions, known, target,
81						!noWorktrees, !noSessions, !noBranches)...)
82				}
83	
84				if len(found) == 0 {
85					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to adopt — everything in flight is already tracked.")
86					return nil
87				}
88	
89				sort.Slice(found, func(i, j int) bool {
90					if found[i].Task.Repo != found[j].Task.Repo {
91						return found[i].Task.Repo < found[j].Task.Repo
92					}
93					return found[i].Task.Branch < found[j].Task.Branch
94				})
95	
96				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%d candidate(s):\n\n", len(found))
97				t := NewTable("REPO", "BRANCH", "STATE", "WHY", "CHECKOUT")
98				for _, c := range found {

100						c.Task.State.Label(), c.Reason, config.Contract(checkoutOf(c.Task)))
101				}

103

108				}

114						continue
115					}
116					if err := app.Tasks.Save(c.Task); err != nil {
117						app.warnf("%s: %v", c.Task.Branch, err)
118						continue
119					}
120					adopted++
121				}
122				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\nadopted %d task(s) — see them with `dev ls`\n", adopted)
123				if adopted > 0 {
124					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Give each one a next action so parking it stays cheap: dev park <task> --next \"…\"")

132		f.BoolVar(&noWorktrees, "no-worktrees", false, "skip existing linked worktrees")

134		f.BoolVar(&noBranches, "no-branches", false, "skip local branches ahead of their base")
135		f.StringVar(&state, "state", string(task.Warm), "state to record adopted tasks in ("+task.JoinStates(", ")+")")
136		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "state", taskStateCompletions())
137		return cmd
138	}
139	
140	// scanRepo collects everything in one repository that looks like work in
141	// flight but is not yet recorded.
142	func scanRepo(ctx context.Context, app *App, r repo.Repo, sessions []runtime.Session,
143		known map[string]bool, target task.State, doWorktrees, doSessions, doBranches bool) []candidate {
144	
145		var out []candidate
146		seen := map[string]bool{}
147	
148		add := func(branch, worktree, reason string, state task.State) {
149			if branch == "" || seen[branch] {
150				return
151			}
152			id := task.MakeID(r.Name, branch)
153			if known[id] {
154				return
155			}
156			seen[branch] = true
157			out = append(out, candidate{
158				Reason: reason,
159				Task: &task.Task{
160					ID:           id,
161					Name:         branch,
162					Repo:         r.Name,
163					RepoPath:     r.Path,
164					Branch:       branch,
165					Base:         gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, r.Path),
166					WorktreePath: worktree,
167					State:        state,
168					Owner:        config.Hostname(),
169				},
170			})
171		}
172	
173		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path)
174		if err != nil {
175			return nil
176		}
177	
178		if doWorktrees {
179			for _, w := range worktrees {
180				if w.Main || w.Branch == "" || w.Prunable {
181					continue
182				}
183				// A harness's turn-scoped worktree is not a change stream a human
184				// tracks; adopting those would fill the inventory with noise that
185				// the harness will delete on its own.
186				if isEphemeralWorktree(w.Path, w.Branch) {
187					continue
188				}
189				state := target
190				reason := "existing worktree"
191				if sessionAt(sessions, w.Path) != nil {
192					state, reason = task.Hot, "worktree with a live session"
193				}
194				add(w.Branch, w.Path, reason, state)
195			}
196		}
197	
198		if doSessions {
199			for i := range sessions {
200				for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
201					if d != r.Path {
202						continue
203					}
204					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
205					if err != nil || st.Branch == "" {
206						continue
207					}
208					add(st.Branch, "", "live session in the main checkout", task.Hot)
209				}
210			}
211		}
212	
213		if doBranches {
214			for _, branch := range unmergedBranches(ctx, r.Path) {
215				add(branch, worktreePathFor(worktrees, branch), "branch ahead of the base", target)
216			}
217		}
218		return out
219	}
220	
221	// isEphemeralWorktree recognises the checkouts an agent harness creates and
222	// cleans up itself.
223	func isEphemeralWorktree(path, branch string) bool {
224		return strings.Contains(path, "/.claude/worktrees/") ||
225			strings.HasPrefix(branch, "worktree-")
226	}
227	
228	func sessionAt(sessions []runtime.Session, dir string) *runtime.Session {
229		for i := range sessions {
230			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
231				if d == dir {
232					return &sessions[i]
233				}
234			}
235		}
236		return nil
237	}
238	
239	func worktreePathFor(worktrees []gitx.Worktree, branch string) string {
240		for _, w := range worktrees {
241			if w.Branch == branch && !w.Main {
242				return w.Path
243			}
244		}
245		return ""
246	}
247	
248	// unmergedBranches lists local branches carrying commits the default branch
249	// does not — unfinished work that would otherwise be invisible to dev.
250	func unmergedBranches(ctx context.Context, repoPath string) []string {
251		base := gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
252		if base == "" {
253			return nil
254		}
255		out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname:short)", "refs/heads/")
256		if err != nil {
257			return nil
258		}
259		var branches []string
260		for _, b := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
261			b = strings.TrimSpace(b)
262			if b == "" || b == base || isEphemeralWorktree("", b) {
263				continue
264			}
265			// Contained in the base means the work has already landed.
266			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", b, base); err == nil {
267				continue
268			}
269			branches = append(branches, b)
270		}
271		return branches
272	}
273

1	package stats
2	
3	import (
4		"bufio"
5		"context"
6		"encoding/base64"
7		"encoding/json"
8		"fmt"
9		"net/http"
10		"os"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	)
14	
15	// WakaTime imports durations from the WakaTime API.
16	//
17	// It covers the time dev's own sampler cannot see: hours spent in an editor
18	// rather than a terminal session. The two are stored under separate sources so
19	// a report can choose either, or both, knowing they overlap.
20	type WakaTime struct {
21		APIKey  string
22		BaseURL string
23		Client  *http.Client
24	}
25	
26	// DefaultWakaTimeURL is the public API root.
27	const DefaultWakaTimeURL = "https://wakatime.com/api/v1"
28	
29	// APIKeyFromConfig reads api_key out of a ~/.wakatime.cfg ini file, which is
30	// where the editor plugins already put it — asking the user to configure the
31	// key a second time would be the wrong kind of setup.
32	func APIKeyFromConfig(path string) (string, error) {
33		f, err := os.Open(path)
34		if err != nil {
35			return "", fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
36		}
37		defer f.Close()
38	
39		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(f)
40		for scanner.Scan() {
41			line := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())
42			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
43				continue
44			}
45			key, val, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
46			if !ok {
47				continue
48			}
49			if strings.TrimSpace(key) == "api_key" {
50				return strings.TrimSpace(val), nil
51			}
52		}
53		if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
54			return "", err
55		}
56		return "", fmt.Errorf("no api_key in %s", path)
57	}
58	
59	type summariesResponse struct {
60		Data []struct {
61			Range struct {
62				Date string `json:"date"`
63			} `json:"range"`
64			Projects []struct {
65				Name         string  `json:"name"`
66				TotalSeconds float64 `json:"total_seconds"`
67			} `json:"projects"`
68		} `json:"data"`
69	}
70	
71	// Import fetches per-project daily totals for a date range and stores them.
72	//
73	// WakaTime's summaries endpoint caps a single request at roughly a year, and
74	// re-importing a day returns the same total, so entries are written with Set
75	// rather than accumulated.
76	func (w *WakaTime) Import(ctx context.Context, s *Store, since, until time.Time) (int, error) {
77		if w.APIKey == "" {
78			return 0, fmt.Errorf("no WakaTime API key")
79		}
80		base := w.BaseURL
81		if base == "" {
82			base = DefaultWakaTimeURL
83		}
84		client := w.Client
85		if client == nil {
86			client = &http.Client{Timeout: 30 * time.Second}
87		}
88	
89		url := fmt.Sprintf("%s/users/current/summaries?start=%s&end=%s",
90			base, since.Format(dayFormat), until.Format(dayFormat))
91		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil)
92		if err != nil {
93			return 0, err
94		}
95		// WakaTime authenticates with the base64 of the key as a Basic credential.
96		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Basic "+base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(w.APIKey)))
97	
98		resp, err := client.Do(req)
99		if err != nil {
100			return 0, fmt.Errorf("wakatime request: %w", err)
101		}
102		defer resp.Body.Close()
103		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
104			return 0, fmt.Errorf("wakatime returned %s", resp.Status)
105		}
106	
107		var body summariesResponse
108		if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&body); err != nil {
109			return 0, fmt.Errorf("decode wakatime response: %w", err)
110		}
111	
112		var entries []Entry
113		for _, day := range body.Data {
114			d, err := time.ParseInLocation(dayFormat, day.Range.Date, time.Local)
115			if err != nil {
116				continue
117			}
118			for _, p := range day.Projects {
119				if p.TotalSeconds <= 0 {
120					continue
121				}
122				entries = append(entries, Entry{
123					Day: d, Repo: p.Name, Source: SourceWakaTime,
124					Seconds: int(p.TotalSeconds),
125				})
126			}
127		}
128		if err := s.Set(entries...); err != nil {
129			return 0, err
130		}
131		return len(entries), s.MarkCollected("wakatime", time.Now())
132	}
133

13	// tree builds a directory layout: keys are relative paths, a value of "git"
14	// makes the directory a repo root.
15	func tree(t *testing.T, layout map[string]string) string {
16		t.Helper()
17		root := t.TempDir()
18		for rel, kind := range layout {
19			dir := filepath.Join(root, rel)
20			if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
21				t.Fatal(err)
22			}
23			if kind == "git" {
24				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(dir, ".git"), 0o755); err != nil {
25					t.Fatal(err)
26				}
27			}
28		}
29		return root
30	}

22	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
23	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
24	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
25	// persistent flags (notably --config).
26	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
27		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd || cmd.CalledAs() == cobra.ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd {
28			return true
29		}
30		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
31			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
32				return true
33			}
34		}
35		return false
36	}

38	// loadCompletion prepares local providers after Cobra has parsed the command
39	// line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break command and
40	// flag completion entirely. Cobra invokes one custom provider per request, so
41	// loading here avoids state leaking when a command tree is reused.
42	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool { return a.Load() == nil }

44	func completeTasks(app *App, states ...task.State) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		allowed := make(map[task.State]bool, len(states))
46		for _, state := range states {
47			allowed[state] = true
48		}
49		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
50			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
54			if err != nil {
55				return nil, noFileCompletion
56			}
57			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
58			for _, t := range tasks {
59				if !allowed[t.State] {
60					continue
61				}
62				value := t.ID
63				if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
64					for _, ref := range []string{t.Title(), t.Branch} {
65						if candidate, ok := taskCompletionRef(tasks, t, ref, toComplete); ok {
66							value = candidate
67							break
68						}
69					}
70				}
71				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.ID)
72				out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
73			}
74			return out, noFileCompletion
75		}
76	}
77	
78	func taskCompletionRef(all []*task.Task, target *task.Task, ref, typed string) (string, bool) {
79		if len(typed) > len(ref) || !strings.EqualFold(ref[:len(typed)], typed) {
80			return "", false
81		}
82		candidate := typed + ref[len(typed):]
83		var exact []*task.Task
84		for _, t := range all {
85			if t.ID == candidate || t.Branch == candidate {
86				exact = append(exact, t)
87			}
88		}
89		if len(exact) > 0 {
90			return candidate, len(exact) == 1 && exact[0].ID == target.ID
91		}
92		needle := strings.ToLower(candidate)
93		var match *task.Task
94		for _, t := range all {
95			haystack := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
96			if !strings.Contains(haystack, needle) {
97				continue
98			}
99			if match != nil {
100				return "", false
101			}
102			match = t
103		}
104		return candidate, match != nil && match.ID == target.ID
105	}

156	func repositoryCompletions(app *App, toComplete string, namesOnly bool) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
157		if !app.loadCompletion() {
158			return nil, noFileCompletion
159		}
160		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.CompletionOptions())
161		if err != nil {
162			return nil, noFileCompletion
163		}
164		displayCount := make(map[string]int, len(repos))
165		for _, r := range repos {
166			displayCount[r.Display()]++
167		}
168		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(repos))
169		out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
170		for _, r := range repos {
171			value := r.Display()
172			description := config.Contract(r.Path)
173			switch {
174			case namesOnly:
175				value = r.Name
176				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
177			case displayCount[value] > 1:
178				value = r.Path
179				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
180			}
181			if seen[value] {
182				continue
183			}
184			seen[value] = true
185			out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
186		}
187		return out, noFileCompletion
188	}

25	                 worktree with git and asks herdr to open it, so the path
26	                 policy holds on machines without herdr too.

28	A new worktree is a clean checkout: no node_modules, no .venv, none of the
29	gitignored env files the project needs. dev provisions it — see the config's
30	[worktree] section, or a repo's own .dev.toml.`
31	
32	func newWorktreeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

50	// repoContext resolves the repository to operate on: an explicit --repo, else
51	// the current directory.
52	func repoContext(app *App, ref string) (path, name string, err error) {
53		ctx := ctxOf()

68				config.Contract(cwd))

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65		// Fast avoids per-repository git subprocesses. It is intended for shell
66		// completion: direct .git-file checkouts are skipped as linked worktrees and
67		// symlink aliases are deduplicated by their physical path.
68		Fast bool
69	}
70	
71	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
72	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
73	
74	// CompletionOptions trades full Git metadata for interactive latency.
75	func CompletionOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3, Fast: true} }
76	
77	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
78	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
79	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
80		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
81		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
82		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
83		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
84	}
85	
86	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
87	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
88	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
89	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
90		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
91			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
92		}
93		seen := map[string]bool{}
94		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
95		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
96		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
97		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
98		identities := map[string]bool{}
99		var out []Repo
100	
101		for _, root := range roots {
102			info, err := os.Stat(root)
103			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
104				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
105			}
106			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
107	
108			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
109				if err != nil {
110					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
111				}
112				if ctx.Err() != nil {
113					return ctx.Err()
114				}
115				if path == rootClean {
116					return nil
117				}
118				name := d.Name()
119				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
120				isDir := d.IsDir()
121				if isLink {
122					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
123					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
124					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
125					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
126						isDir = info.IsDir()
127					}
128				}
129				if !isDir {
130					return nil
131				}
132				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
133					return filepath.SkipDir
134				}
135	
136				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
137				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
138	
139				if isRepoDir(path) {
140					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
141					if real == "" {
142						real = path
143					}
144					bare := isBareDir(path)
145					identity, commonDir := real, real
146					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
147						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
148						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
149						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
150						return filepath.SkipDir
151					}
152					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
153						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
154							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
155							// project in the repo inventory.
156							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
157								return filepath.SkipDir
158							}
159							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
160							real = g.MainRoot
161						}
162					}
163					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
164						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
165						out = append(out, Repo{
166							Name:      name,
167							Path:      path,
168							RealPath:  real,
169							Symlink:   isLink,
170							Root:      rootClean,
171							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
172							CommonDir: commonDir,
173							Bare:      bare,
174							HasGit:    true,
175						})
176					}
177					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
178					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
179					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
180					return filepath.SkipDir
181				}
182				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
183					return filepath.SkipDir
184				}
185				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
186					if !seen[path] {
187						seen[path] = true
188						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
189					}
190				}
191				return nil
192			})
193			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
194				return out, ctx.Err()
195			}
196		}
197	
198		for i := range out {
199			if out[i].Category == "." {
200				out[i].Category = ""
201			}
202		}
203		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
204			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
205				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
206			}
207			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
208		})
209		return out, nil
210	}
211	
212	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
213	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
214	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
215		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
216			return true
217		}
218		return isBareDir(path)
219	}
220	
221	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
222		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
223		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
224	}
225	
226	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
227	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
228		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
229			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
230				return false
231			}
232		}
233		return true
234	}
235	
236	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
237	//
238	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
239	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
240	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
241	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
242		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
243	}
244	
245	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
246	// process per repository in the scan roots.
247	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
248		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
249	}
250	
251	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
252		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
253		if err != nil {
254			return Repo{}, nil, err
255		}
256		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
257			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
258				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
259				if real == "" {
260					real = g.MainRoot
261				}
262				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
263				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
264				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
265				return Repo{
266					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
267					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
268				}, nil, nil
269			}
270		}
271		for _, r := range all {
272			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
273				return r, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
277		var hits []Repo
278		for _, r := range all {
279			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
280				hits = append(hits, r)
281			}
282		}
283		switch len(hits) {
284		case 1:
285			return hits[0], nil, nil
286		case 0:
287			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
288		default:
289			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
290		}
291	}
292	
293	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
294	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
295	
296	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
297	
298	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
299	type AmbiguousError struct {
300		Ref        string
301		Candidates []Repo
302	}
303	
304	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
305		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
306		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
307			names[i] = c.Display()
308		}
309		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
310	}

 const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
 
 It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
 
   git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
   git worktree    a disposable local checkout
   herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
   dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
 
 Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
 what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
 closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`
 
 // NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
 func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
 	return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)

 // NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
 // Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
 // tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
 // descriptors.
 func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
 	app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
 
 	root := &cobra.Command{
 		Use:           "dev",
 		Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
 		Long:          rootLong,

 				if err != nil {
 					return err

 				fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
 				return nil
 			}
 			// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
 			// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
 			if interactive() {
 				return runTUI(app)
 			}
 			return runList(app, listOptions{})
 		},
 		PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {

 	root.AddCommand(

 // Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
 func Execute() int {
 	root := NewRootCommand()
 	if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
 		msg := err.Error()
 		// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
 		if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
 			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
 		}
 		return 1
 	}
 	return 0
 }

The fast branch is decisive: repository candidate generation still scans configured roots, but it never enters the `gitx.Discover` block because that block is guarded by `!opts.Fast`. Normal clones are identified by `.git` filesystem metadata, linked worktrees by a `.git` regular-file check, and aliases by `EvalSymlinks`; I’m separating that remaining syscall cost from the distinct one-off Git calls in worktree completion.

10	// openCheckout makes a directory live, asking the backend to treat it as a git
11	// worktree when it knows how — that is what groups the checkout under its
12	// parent repo in a sidebar instead of listing it as an unrelated directory.
13	func openCheckout(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, dir, label string) (string, error) {
14		if wo, ok := rt.(runtime.WorktreeOpener); ok {
15			return wo.OpenWorktree(ctx, dir, label)
16		}
17		return rt.Open(ctx, dir, label)
18	}
19	
20	// asError is errors.As with a typed target, kept here so call sites read as
21	// one line.
22	func asError[T error](err error, target *T) bool { return errors.As(err, target) }
23

14	// newEditCmd is the top-level `dev edit` convenience command.
