```text
28	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
29	
30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
31	
32	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
33	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
34	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
35	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
36	
37	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
38	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
39	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`
40	
41	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
42	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
43		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
44	}
45	
46	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
47	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
48	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
49	// descriptors.
50	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
51		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
52	
53		root := &cobra.Command{
54			Use:           "dev",
55			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
56			Long:          rootLong,
57			Version:       versionFromBuild(),
58			SilenceUsage:  true,
59			SilenceErrors: true,
60			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
61			// exists to answer.
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
64					out, err := skill.Render()
65					if err != nil {
66						return err
67					}
68					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
69					return nil
70				}
71				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
72				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
73				if interactive() {
74					return runTUI(app)
75				}
76				return runList(app, listOptions{})
77			},
78			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
79				if completionInvocation(cmd) {
80					return nil
81				}
82				return app.Load()
83			},
84		}
85	
86		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
87		pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
88		pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux or none")
89		pf.BoolVar(&app.noRuntime, "no-runtime", false, "do not touch any terminal multiplexer")
90		registerFlagCompletion(root, "runtime", runtimeCompletions())
91	
92		// Mirrors `herdr --skill`: the binary is the authority for its own agent
93		// skill, so a dotfiles installer can sync it without vendoring a copy.
94		root.Flags().Bool("skill", false, "print the bundled agent skill and exit")
95	
96		root.AddCommand(
97			newListCmd(app),
98			newTUICmd(app),
99			newStatusCmd(app),
100			newStartCmd(app),
101			newParkCmd(app),
102			newResumeCmd(app),
103			newDoneCmd(app),
104			newSweepCmd(app),
105			newAdoptCmd(app),
106			newBootstrapCmd(app),
107			newWorktreeCmd(app),
108			newRepoCmd(app),
109			newGitignoreCmd(app),
110			newTryCmd(app),
111			newGraduateCmd(app),
112			newStatsCmd(app),
113			newHelpTopicCmd(app),
114			newSkillCmd(app),
115			newDoctorCmd(app),
116			newShellInitCmd(app),
117			newConfigCmd(app),
118			newCacheCmd(app),
119			newEditCmd(app),
120		)
121		root.SetHelpCommand(&cobra.Command{Hidden: true, Use: "no-help"})
122		root.SetOut(out)
123		root.SetErr(errOut)
124		return root
125	}
126	
127	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
128	func Execute() int {
129		root := NewRootCommand()
130		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
131			msg := err.Error()
132			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
133			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
134				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
135			}
136			return 1
137		}
138		return 0
139	}
```

```text
16	func newBootstrapCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
17		var (
18			maxDepth      int
19			followLinks   bool
20			includeWT     bool
21			jsonOut       bool
22			indexRoot     string
23			moveRoot      string
24			layoutName    string
25			relativeLinks bool
26			apply         bool
27			yes           bool
28			configOut     string
29			forceConfig   bool
30		)
31		cmd := &cobra.Command{
32			Use:   "bootstrap [path...]",
33			Short: "Discover and optionally organise an existing machine without breaking its layout",
34			Long: `Recursively find Git repositories under the paths you name (or paths.scan_roots
35	when none are given), deduplicate them by Git identity, and classify canonical
36	checkouts, linked worktrees, bare repositories and symlink aliases.
37	
38	The default is a report. It changes nothing.
39	
40	For a non-destructive navigation layer, make a symlink index:
41	
42	    dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work --index ~/Projects --layout flat
43	    dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work --index ~/Projects --apply
44	
45	The physical repositories stay where they are. Put the index first in
46	paths.scan_roots if you want its names to be the UI; direct symlinks to repos
47	are first-class discovery entries and physical + indexed paths are shown once.
48	
49	Physical moves are supported, but deliberately strict:
50	
51	    dev bootstrap ~/old --move ~/Projects --layout preserve
52	    dev bootstrap ~/old --move ~/Projects --apply
53	
54	Move refuses dirty repos, linked worktrees, live sessions, symlink aliases,
55	occupied destinations and cross-filesystem renames. It reports before acting,
56	and --apply still confirms each repository unless --yes is explicit.
57	
58	Layout is never imposed globally. flat means <target>/<repo>; preserve mirrors
59	the path relative to each scan root. Existing scan_roots, project_root and
60	worktree_path remain freely configurable for any structure.`,
61			Args: cobra.ArbitraryArgs,
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				ctx := ctxOf()
64				// Flags override policy; otherwise the generated config is the one
65				// place a machine says how deep to scan and how an index is laid out.
66				if !cmd.Flags().Changed("max-depth") {
67					maxDepth = app.Cfg.Bootstrap.MaxDepth
68				}
69				if !cmd.Flags().Changed("follow-symlinks") {
70					followLinks = app.Cfg.Bootstrap.FollowSymlinks
71				}
72				if !cmd.Flags().Changed("layout") && app.Cfg.Bootstrap.Layout != "" {
73					layoutName = app.Cfg.Bootstrap.Layout
74				}
75				if !cmd.Flags().Changed("relative-links") {
76					relativeLinks = app.Cfg.Bootstrap.RelativeLinks
77				}
78				if !cmd.Flags().Changed("index") && moveRoot == "" && app.Cfg.Bootstrap.IndexRoot != "" {
79					indexRoot = app.Cfg.Bootstrap.IndexRoot
80				}
81	
82				roots := expandRoots(args)
83				if len(roots) == 0 {
84					roots = app.Cfg.ScanRoots()
85					// An orphan checkout whose canonical repo is outside the scan
86					// roots cannot be found through git worktree list. Include dev's
87					// configured pool when it exists, without warning on a fresh
88					// machine where it has not been created yet.
89					wtRoot := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.WorktreeRoot)
90					if info, err := os.Stat(wtRoot); err == nil && info.IsDir() && !pathIn(wtRoot, roots) {
91						roots = append(roots, wtRoot)
92					}
93				}
94				if len(roots) == 0 {
95					return fmt.Errorf("no paths to scan — pass one, or configure paths.scan_roots")
96				}
97				if indexRoot != "" && moveRoot != "" {
98					return fmt.Errorf("--index and --move are different strategies; pick one")
99				}
100	
101				layout, err := bootstrap.ParseLayout(layoutName)
102				if err != nil {
103					return err
104				}
105				repos, warnings := bootstrap.Scan(ctx, roots, bootstrap.Options{
106					MaxDepth: maxDepth, FollowSymlinkDirs: followLinks, IncludeWorktrees: includeWT,
107				})
108				if moveRoot != "" {
109					// The explicit roots decide which repos are candidates, but the
110					// configured roots may hold a symlink index whose aliases would
111					// break. Fold those aliases into matching candidates without
112					// adding unrelated repos to the move plan.
113					known, moreWarnings := bootstrap.Scan(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), bootstrap.Options{
114						MaxDepth: maxDepth, FollowSymlinkDirs: followLinks, IncludeWorktrees: includeWT,
115					})
116					repos = bootstrap.EnrichAliases(repos, known)
117					warnings = append(warnings, moreWarnings...)
118				}
119	
120				if jsonOut {
121					return renderBootstrapJSON(app, roots, repos, warnings)
122				}
123				renderBootstrapScan(app, roots, repos, warnings)
124	
125				var plan bootstrap.OrganizePlan
126				switch {
127				case indexRoot != "":
128					indexRoot = config.Expand(indexRoot)
129					plan = bootstrap.IndexPlan(repos, indexRoot, layout, relativeLinks)
130					renderOrganizePlan(app, plan)
131					if apply {
132						n, err := bootstrap.ApplyIndex(plan)
133						if err != nil {
134							return err
135						}
136						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\ncreated %d symlink(s); no repository moved\n", n)
137					}
138	
139				case moveRoot != "":
140					moveRoot = config.Expand(moveRoot)
141					plan = bootstrap.MovePlan(ctx, repos, moveRoot, layout)
142					blockLiveMoves(app, &plan)
143					renderOrganizePlan(app, plan)
144					if apply {
145						if len(plan.Blocked()) > 0 {
146							return fmt.Errorf("move plan has %d blocked repository(s); resolve them before applying. "+
147								"No repository moved", len(plan.Blocked()))
148						}
149						if err := applyMovePlan(app, plan, yes); err != nil {
150							return err
151						}
152					}
153				}
154	
155				if configOut != "" {
156					configRoots := roots
157					projectRoot := roots[0]
158					if indexRoot != "" {
159						// The index is a navigation layer, not where physical new
160						// repos should be created. Put it first so its names are the
161						// UI, retain the physical roots as fallback, and keep the
162						// first physical root as project_root.
163						configRoots = append([]string{indexRoot}, roots...)
164						projectRoot = roots[0]
165					} else if moveRoot != "" {
166						configRoots, projectRoot = []string{moveRoot}, moveRoot
167					}
168					if err := writeBootstrapConfig(app, configOut, configRoots, projectRoot, forceConfig); err != nil {
169						return err
170					}
171				}
172	
173				if !apply && (indexRoot != "" || moveRoot != "") {
174					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nReport only. Re-run with --apply to act on ready rows.")
175				}
176				return nil
177			},
178		}
179		f := cmd.Flags()
180		f.IntVar(&maxDepth, "max-depth", 8, "recursive depth; 0 means unlimited")
181		f.BoolVar(&followLinks, "follow-symlinks", true, "follow symlinked container directories with cycle detection")
182		f.BoolVar(&includeWT, "worktrees", true, "include linked worktrees in the report")
183		f.BoolVar(&jsonOut, "json", false, "emit the scan as JSON")
184		f.StringVar(&indexRoot, "index", "", "plan a non-destructive symlink catalog at this path")
185		f.StringVar(&moveRoot, "move", "", "plan physical repository moves into this path")
186		f.StringVar(&layoutName, "layout", "flat", "target layout: flat or preserve")
187		f.BoolVar(&relativeLinks, "relative-links", false, "use relative symlink payloads in an index")
188		f.BoolVar(&apply, "apply", false, "apply the ready index or move actions")
189		f.BoolVar(&yes, "yes", false, "with --move --apply, do not confirm each repository")
190		f.StringVar(&configOut, "config-out", "", "write a new config.toml for the resulting roots")
191		f.BoolVar(&forceConfig, "force-config", false, "overwrite config-out if it exists")
192		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "layout", fixedCompletions(string(bootstrap.Flat), string(bootstrap.Preserve)))
193		return cmd

196	func pathIn(path string, roots []string) bool {
197		path = filepath.Clean(path)
198		for _, r := range roots {
199			r = filepath.Clean(r)
200			if path == r || strings.HasPrefix(path, r+string(filepath.Separator)) {
201				return true
202			}
203		}
204		return false
205	}
206	
207	func expandRoots(args []string) []string {
208		out := make([]string, 0, len(args))
209		for _, r := range args {
210			if expanded := config.Expand(r); expanded != "" {
211				out = append(out, expanded)
212			}
213		}
214		return out
215	}
216	
217	func renderBootstrapScan(app *App, roots []string, repos []bootstrap.Repository, warnings []error) {
218		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "Scanned %s\n\n", strings.Join(contractAll(roots), ", "))
219		if len(repos) == 0 {
220			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No repositories found.")
221		} else {
222			t := NewTable("KIND", "REPO", "BRANCH", "GIT", "ALIASES", "PATH")
223			for _, r := range repos {
224				git := "—"
225				if r.Kind != bootstrap.Bare {
226					git = r.Status.Summary()
227				}
228				aliases := "—"
229				if len(r.Aliases) > 0 {
230					aliases = fmt.Sprintf("%d", len(r.Aliases))
231				}
232				path := config.Contract(r.Path)
233				if r.Symlink {
234					path += " → " + config.Contract(r.RealPath)
235				}
236				t.Add(string(r.Kind), r.Name, dash(r.Branch), git, aliases, path)
237			}
238			t.Render(app.Out)
239		}
240	
241		counts := map[bootstrap.Kind]int{}
242		aliases := 0
243		clones := map[string]bool{}
244		for _, r := range repos {
245			counts[r.Kind]++
246			aliases += len(r.Aliases)
247			clones[r.CloneKey()] = true
248		}
249		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d clone(s): %d canonical, %d worktree, %d bare, %d symlink alias(es)\n",
250			len(clones), counts[bootstrap.Canonical], counts[bootstrap.Worktree], counts[bootstrap.Bare], aliases)
251		for _, w := range warnings {
252			app.warnf("scan: %v", w)
253		}
254	}
255	
256	func renderOrganizePlan(app *App, p bootstrap.OrganizePlan) {
257		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%s plan — %s layout at %s\n\n",
258			strings.ToUpper(p.Mode), p.Layout, config.Contract(p.Root))
259		if len(p.Actions) == 0 {
260			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No canonical repositories to organise.")
261			return
262		}
263		t := NewTable("STATE", "REPO", "SOURCE", "TARGET / REASON")
264		for _, a := range p.Actions {
265			last := config.Contract(a.Target)
266			if a.Reason != "" {
267				last += " — " + a.Reason
268			}
269			t.Add(string(a.State), a.Repo.Name, config.Contract(a.Source), last)
270		}
271		t.Render(app.Out)
272		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d ready, %d blocked, %d already current\n",
273			len(p.Ready()), len(p.Blocked()), countActionState(p.Actions, bootstrap.Current))
274	}
275	
276	func countActionState(actions []bootstrap.Action, state bootstrap.ActionState) int {
277		n := 0
278		for _, a := range actions {
279			if a.State == state {
280				n++
281			}
282		}
283		return n
284	}
285	
286	// blockLiveMoves adds runtime and cwd safety checks to the filesystem plan.
287	func blockLiveMoves(app *App, p *bootstrap.OrganizePlan) {
288		ctx := ctxOf()
289		sessions, _ := app.Runtime().List(ctx)
290		cwd, _ := os.Getwd()
291		for i := range p.Actions {
292			a := &p.Actions[i]
293			if a.State != bootstrap.Ready {
294				continue
295			}
296			if cwd == a.Source || strings.HasPrefix(cwd, a.Source+string(filepath.Separator)) {
297				a.State, a.Reason = bootstrap.Blocked, "the current shell is inside this repository"
298				continue
299			}
300			for _, s := range sessions {
301				for _, dir := range s.Dirs {
302					if dir == a.Source || strings.HasPrefix(dir, a.Source+string(filepath.Separator)) {
303						a.State, a.Reason = bootstrap.Blocked,
304							fmt.Sprintf("live %s session %s is inside the repository", app.Runtime().Name(), s.Handle)
305						break
306					}
307				}
308			}
309		}
310	}
311	
312	func applyMovePlan(app *App, plan bootstrap.OrganizePlan, yes bool) error {
313		in := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
314		moved := 0

316			if a.State != bootstrap.Ready {

318			}
319			if !yes && !confirm(app, in, fmt.Sprintf("move %s to %s", a.Repo.Name, config.Contract(a.Target))) {

327			}

336		}
337		return nil
338	}

340	// rewriteTaskRepoPaths keeps task entries usable after an explicit move.
341	func rewriteTaskRepoPaths(app *App, from, to string) error {
342		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
343		if err != nil {
344			return err
345		}
346		for _, t := range tasks {
347			if t.RepoPath != from {
348				continue
349			}
350			t.RepoPath = to
351			// MovePlan refuses linked worktrees, so a task cannot have a valid
352			// worktree path under the moved clone. Clear a stale one defensively.
353			if t.WorktreePath != "" && strings.HasPrefix(t.WorktreePath, from+string(filepath.Separator)) {
354				t.WorktreePath = strings.Replace(t.WorktreePath, from, to, 1)
355			}
356			if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
357				return err
358			}
359		}
360		return nil
361	}

363	func writeBootstrapConfig(app *App, path string, roots []string, projectRoot string, force bool) error {
364		path = config.Expand(path)
365		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil && !force {
366			return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists; use --force-config to overwrite", config.Contract(path))
367		}
368		contracted := contractAll(roots)
369		layout := config.Layout{
370			ScanRoots: contracted, ProjectRoot: config.Contract(projectRoot),
371			TriesRoot: app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot, WorktreeRoot: app.Cfg.Paths.WorktreeRoot,
372		}
373		body := renderStarterConfig(layout.Fallbacks())
374		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
375			return err
376		}
377		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil {
378			return err
379		}
380		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\nwrote %s with scan_roots = %v\n", config.Contract(path), contracted)
381		return nil
382	}

386		Repositories []bootstrap.Repository `json:"repositories"`
387		Warnings     []string               `json:"warnings,omitempty"`
388	}
389	
390	func renderBootstrapJSON(app *App, roots []string, repos []bootstrap.Repository, warnings []error) error {
391		out := bootstrapJSON{Roots: roots, Repositories: repos}
392		for _, w := range warnings {
393			out.Warnings = append(out.Warnings, w.Error())
394		}
395		enc := json.NewEncoder(app.Out)
396		enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
397		return enc.Encode(out)
398	}
```

```text
package os // import "os"

func NewFile(fd uintptr, name string) *File
    NewFile returns a new File with the given file descriptor and name.
    The returned value will be nil if fd is not a valid file descriptor.

    NewFile's behavior differs on some platforms:

      - On Unix, if fd is in non-blocking mode, NewFile will attempt to return a
        pollable file.
      - On Windows, if fd is opened for asynchronous I/O (that is,
        syscall.FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED has been specified in the
        syscall.CreateFile call), NewFile will attempt to return a pollable
        file by associating fd with the Go runtime I/O completion port. The I/O
        operations will be performed synchronously if the association fails.

    Only pollable files support File.SetDeadline, File.SetReadDeadline,
    and File.SetWriteDeadline.

    After passing it to NewFile, fd may become invalid under the same conditions
    described in the comments of File.Fd, and the same constraints apply.
```

```text
15	// Layout controls how an organisation target names repositories.
16	type Layout string
17	
18	const (

20		Flat Layout = "flat"
21		// Preserve mirrors the repository's relative path under its scan root.

24	
25	// ParseLayout validates a layout.
26	func ParseLayout(s string) (Layout, error) {
27		switch Layout(s) {
28		case Flat, Preserve:
29			return Layout(s), nil
30		default:
31			return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown layout %q: want flat or preserve", s)
32		}
33	}

35	// ActionState is whether an organisation action can run.
36	type ActionState string
37	
38	const (
39		// Ready means applying will create or move something.
40		Ready ActionState = "ready"
41		// Current means the target already has the desired state.
42		Current ActionState = "current"
43		// Blocked means applying would be unsafe or ambiguous.
44		Blocked ActionState = "blocked"
45	)
46	
47	// Action is one index-link creation or physical move.
48	type Action struct {
49		Repo   Repository
50		Source string
51		Target string
52		State  ActionState
53		Reason string
54		// RelativeTarget is the symlink payload when relative links are requested.
55		RelativeTarget string
56	}

58	// Plan holds a complete organisation proposal.

60		Mode    string // "index" or "move"
61		Root    string
62		Layout  Layout
63		Actions []Action
64	}
65	
66	// Ready returns actions that will change the filesystem.
67	func (p OrganizePlan) Ready() []Action {
68		var out []Action
69		for _, a := range p.Actions {
70			if a.State == Ready {
71				out = append(out, a)
72			}
73		}
74		return out
75	}
76	
77	// Blocked returns unsafe or ambiguous actions.
78	func (p OrganizePlan) Blocked() []Action {
79		var out []Action
80		for _, a := range p.Actions {
81			if a.State == Blocked {
82				out = append(out, a)
83			}
84		}
85		return out
86	}

88	// IndexPlan proposes a non-destructive symlink catalog of canonical checkouts.
89	// Linked worktrees are execution state, not projects, and are deliberately not
90	// indexed alongside repositories.
91	func IndexPlan(repos []Repository, root string, layout Layout, relative bool) OrganizePlan {
92		p := OrganizePlan{Mode: "index", Root: root, Layout: layout}
93		nameTargets := map[string][]int{}
94	
95		for _, r := range repos {
96			if r.Kind != Canonical {
97				continue
98			}
99			target := targetFor(root, layout, r)
100			a := Action{Repo: r, Source: r.RealPath, Target: target, State: Ready}
101			if relative {
102				rel, err := filepath.Rel(filepath.Dir(target), r.RealPath)
103				if err == nil {
104					a.RelativeTarget = rel
105				}
106			}
107			classifyIndexTarget(&a)
108			nameTargets[target] = append(nameTargets[target], len(p.Actions))
109			p.Actions = append(p.Actions, a)
110		}
111	
112		// A flat index cannot represent duplicate repo names. Block every claimant
113		// rather than picking one or inventing a suffix the user did not ask for.
114		for target, indices := range nameTargets {
115			if len(indices) < 2 {
116				continue
117			}
118			var sources []string
119			for _, i := range indices {
120				sources = append(sources, p.Actions[i].Source)
121			}
122			reason := "duplicate target " + target + " from: " + strings.Join(sources, ", ")
123			for _, i := range indices {
124				p.Actions[i].State, p.Actions[i].Reason = Blocked, reason
125			}
126		}
127		sortActions(p.Actions)
128		return p
129	}

131	func classifyIndexTarget(a *Action) {
132		info, err := os.Lstat(a.Target)
133		switch {
134		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist):
135			return
136		case err != nil:
137			a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, err.Error()
138			return
139		case info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0:
140			dest, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(a.Target)
141			if err != nil {
142				a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "existing broken symlink"
143				return
144			}
145			dest, _ = filepath.Abs(dest)
146			source, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(a.Source)
147			if dest == source {
148				a.State, a.Reason = Current, "already points at this repository"
149				return
150			}
151			a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "existing symlink points at "+dest
152		default:
153			a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "target already exists and is not a symlink"
154		}
155	}
156	
157	// ApplyIndex creates the ready symlinks. It never replaces anything.
158	func ApplyIndex(plan OrganizePlan) (int, error) {
159		if plan.Mode != "index" {
160			return 0, fmt.Errorf("cannot apply %q as an index plan", plan.Mode)
161		}
162		created := 0
163		for _, a := range plan.Actions {
164			if a.State != Ready {
165				continue
166			}
167			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(a.Target), 0o755); err != nil {
168				return created, err
169			}
170			payload := a.Source
171			if a.RelativeTarget != "" {
172				payload = a.RelativeTarget
173			}
174			// os.Symlink refuses an occupied target: this is the final race-safe
175			// guard after the plan classified it.
176			if err := os.Symlink(payload, a.Target); err != nil {
177				return created, fmt.Errorf("link %s -> %s: %w", a.Target, payload, err)
178			}
179			created++
180		}
181		return created, nil
182	}
183	
184	// MovePlan proposes atomic moves of canonical checkouts into root.
185	//
186	// Moving is intentionally much stricter than indexing. It is blocked when a
187	// repo is dirty, has linked worktrees, has symlink aliases, crosses a
188	// filesystem, or would hit an occupied target. Those are exactly the states
189	// where a simple os.Rename could lose access or leave Git metadata pointing at
190	// an old path.
191	func MovePlan(ctx context.Context, repos []Repository, root string, layout Layout) OrganizePlan {
192		p := OrganizePlan{Mode: "move", Root: root, Layout: layout}
193		nameTargets := map[string][]int{}
194	
195		for _, r := range repos {
196			if r.Kind != Canonical {
197				continue
198			}
199			target := targetFor(root, layout, r)
200			a := Action{Repo: r, Source: r.Path, Target: target, State: Ready}
201	
202			switch {
203			case r.Dirty():
204				a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "repository has uncommitted changes"
205			case len(r.Aliases) > 0:
206				a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "repository has symlink aliases that would become broken"
207			case samePath(r.Path, target):
208				a.State, a.Reason = Current, "already at the target"
209			default:
210				if list, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path); err != nil {
211					a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "cannot inspect worktrees: "+err.Error()
212				} else if len(list) > 1 {
213					a.State, a.Reason = Blocked,
214						fmt.Sprintf("repository has %d linked worktree(s); remove or move those first", len(list)-1)
215				} else if info, err := os.Lstat(target); err == nil {
216					_ = info
217					a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, "target already exists"
218				} else if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
219					a.State, a.Reason = Blocked, err.Error()
220				} else if !sameFilesystem(r.Path, nearestExisting(filepath.Dir(target))) {
221					a.State, a.Reason = Blocked,
222						"source and target are on different filesystems; atomic rename is impossible"
223				}
224			}
225			nameTargets[target] = append(nameTargets[target], len(p.Actions))
226			p.Actions = append(p.Actions, a)
227		}
228	
229		for target, indices := range nameTargets {
230			if len(indices) < 2 {
231				continue
232			}
233			reason := "duplicate target " + target + "; use preserve layout or separate roots"
234			for _, i := range indices {
235				p.Actions[i].State, p.Actions[i].Reason = Blocked, reason
236			}
237		}
238		sortActions(p.Actions)
239		return p
240	}
241	
242	// ApplyMoves atomically renames every ready repository. It stops on the first
243	// failure and returns how many completed — there is no rollback because a
244	// rollback can fail too, and every completed rename is itself a valid repo.
245	func ApplyMoves(plan OrganizePlan) (int, error) {
246		if plan.Mode != "move" {
247			return 0, fmt.Errorf("cannot apply %q as a move plan", plan.Mode)
248		}
249		moved := 0
250		for _, a := range plan.Actions {
251			if a.State != Ready {
252				continue
253			}
254			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(a.Target), 0o755); err != nil {
255				return moved, err
256			}
257			if err := os.Rename(a.Source, a.Target); err != nil {
258				return moved, fmt.Errorf("move %s -> %s: %w", a.Source, a.Target, err)
259			}
260			moved++
261		}
262		return moved, nil
263	}
264	
265	func targetFor(root string, layout Layout, r Repository) string {
266		if layout == Preserve {
267			return filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(r.Relative))
268		}
269		return filepath.Join(root, r.Name)
270	}
271	
272	func samePath(a, b string) bool {
273		aAbs, _ := filepath.Abs(a)
274		bAbs, _ := filepath.Abs(b)
275		return filepath.Clean(aAbs) == filepath.Clean(bAbs)
276	}
277	
278	func nearestExisting(path string) string {
279		for {
280			if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
281				return path
282			}
283			parent := filepath.Dir(path)
284			if parent == path {
285				return path
286			}
287			path = parent
288		}
289	}
290	
291	func sortActions(actions []Action) {
292		sort.Slice(actions, func(i, j int) bool {
293			if actions[i].State != actions[j].State {
294				return actionRank(actions[i].State) < actionRank(actions[j].State)
295			}
296			return actions[i].Target < actions[j].Target
297		})
298	}
299	
300	func actionRank(s ActionState) int {
301		switch s {
302		case Ready:
303			return 0
304		case Blocked:
305			return 1
306		case Current:
307			return 2
308		}
309		return 3
310	}
311
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65		// Fast avoids per-repository git subprocesses. It is intended for shell
66		// completion: direct .git-file checkouts are skipped as linked worktrees and
67		// symlink aliases are deduplicated by their physical path.
68		Fast bool
69	}
70	
71	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
72	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
73	
74	// CompletionOptions trades full Git metadata for interactive latency.
75	func CompletionOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3, Fast: true} }
76	
77	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
78	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
79	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
80		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
81		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
82		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
83		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
84	}
85	
86	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
87	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
88	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
89	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
90		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
91			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
92		}
93		seen := map[string]bool{}
94		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
95		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
96		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
97		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
98		identities := map[string]bool{}
99		var out []Repo
100	
101		for _, root := range roots {
102			info, err := os.Stat(root)
103			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
104				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
105			}
106			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
107	
108			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
109				if err != nil {
110					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
111				}
112				if ctx.Err() != nil {
113					return ctx.Err()
114				}
115				if path == rootClean {
116					return nil
117				}
118				name := d.Name()
119				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
120				isDir := d.IsDir()
121				if isLink {
122					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
123					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
124					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
125					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
126						isDir = info.IsDir()
127					}
128				}
129				if !isDir {
130					return nil
131				}
132				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
133					return filepath.SkipDir
134				}
135	
136				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
137				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
138	
139				if isRepoDir(path) {
140					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
141					if real == "" {
142						real = path
143					}
144					bare := isBareDir(path)
145					identity, commonDir := real, real
146					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
147						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
148						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
149						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
150						return filepath.SkipDir
151					}
152					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
153						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
154							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
155							// project in the repo inventory.
156							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
157								return filepath.SkipDir
158							}
159							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
160							real = g.MainRoot
161						}
162					}
163					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
164						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
165						out = append(out, Repo{
166							Name:      name,
167							Path:      path,
168							RealPath:  real,
169							Symlink:   isLink,
170							Root:      rootClean,
171							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
172							CommonDir: commonDir,
173							Bare:      bare,
174							HasGit:    true,
175						})
176					}
177					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
178					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
179					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
180					return filepath.SkipDir
181				}
182				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
183					return filepath.SkipDir
184				}
185				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
186					if !seen[path] {
187						seen[path] = true
188						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
189					}
190				}
191				return nil
192			})
193			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
194				return out, ctx.Err()
195			}
196		}
197	
198		for i := range out {
199			if out[i].Category == "." {
200				out[i].Category = ""
201			}
202		}
203		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
204			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
205				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
206			}
207			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
208		})
209		return out, nil
210	}
211	
212	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
213	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
214	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
215		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
216			return true
217		}
218		return isBareDir(path)
219	}
220	
221	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
222		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
223		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
224	}
225	
226	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
227	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
228		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
229			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
230				return false
231			}
232		}
233		return true
234	}
235	
236	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
237	//
238	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
239	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
240	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
241	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
242		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
243	}
244	
245	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
246	// process per repository in the scan roots.
247	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
248		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
249	}
250	
251	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
252		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
253		if err != nil {
254			return Repo{}, nil, err
255		}
256		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
257			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
258				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
259				if real == "" {
260					real = g.MainRoot
261				}
262				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
263				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
264				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
265				return Repo{
266					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
267					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
268				}, nil, nil
269			}
270		}
271		for _, r := range all {
272			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
273				return r, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
277		var hits []Repo
278		for _, r := range all {
279			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
280				hits = append(hits, r)
281			}
282		}
283		switch len(hits) {
284		case 1:
285			return hits[0], nil, nil
286		case 0:
287			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
288		default:
289			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
290		}
291	}
292	
293	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
294	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
295	
296	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
297	
298	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
299	type AmbiguousError struct {
300		Ref        string
301		Candidates []Repo
302	}
303	
304	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
305		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
306		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
307			names[i] = c.Display()
308		}
309		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
310	}
```

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-27 18:33:16Z)**_

The duplicate is real for ordinary and linked-worktree roots: `isRepoDir(path)` discards an `os.Lstat(path/.git)` result, and the Fast branch later calls `gitEntryIsFile(path)`, which performs the identical `os.Lstat` again. Bare repositories are an exception because `bare == true` short-circuits the second call, so I’m checking the actual Fast-mode callers and whether this is on a latency-sensitive path before assigning the verdict.

```text
+type ClearQuery struct {

+
+// Clear deletes matching activity and returns the number of rows removed.
+// With an empty query it clears all activity and collector checkpoints.
+func (s *Store) Clear(q ClearQuery) (int64, error) {
+	clause := ""
+	var args []any
+	if q.Repo != "" {
+		clause = " WHERE repo = ?"
+		args = append(args, q.Repo)
+	}
+	if len(q.Sources) > 0 {
+		if clause == "" {
+			clause = " WHERE "
+		} else {
+			clause += " AND "
+		}
+		clause += "source IN (" + placeholders(len(q.Sources)) + ")"

+		}
```

```text
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.

18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.

30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}

43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
```

```text
8	
9	// XDG base directories, resolved the way the spec prescribes: honor the
10	// environment variable when it holds an absolute path, otherwise fall back to
11	// the documented default under $HOME.
12	
13	func xdgDir(envVar, fallback string) string {
14		if v := os.Getenv(envVar); filepath.IsAbs(v) {
15			return v
16		}
17		return filepath.Join(home(), fallback)
18	}
19	
20	func home() string {
21		if h, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil && h != "" {
22			return h
23		}
24		return os.Getenv("HOME")
25	}
26	
27	// ConfigHome is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (default ~/.config).
28	func ConfigHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", ".config") }
29	
30	// DataHome is $XDG_DATA_HOME (default ~/.local/share).
31	func DataHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_DATA_HOME", ".local/share") }
32	
33	// CacheHome is $XDG_CACHE_HOME (default ~/.cache).
34	func CacheHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CACHE_HOME", ".cache") }
35	
36	// ConfigFile is the path dev loads its TOML configuration from.
37	func ConfigFile() string { return filepath.Join(ConfigHome(), "dev", "config.toml") }
38	
39	// Expand resolves a leading ~ and any environment variables in p, then makes
40	// the result absolute. Paths in config.toml are written by humans, so both
41	// "~/Worktrees" and "$WORK/trees" have to work.
42	func Expand(p string) string {
43		if p == "" {
44			return ""
45		}
46		p = os.ExpandEnv(p)
47		switch {
48		case p == "~":
49			p = home()
50		case strings.HasPrefix(p, "~/"):
51			p = filepath.Join(home(), p[2:])
52		}
53		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(p); err == nil {
54			return abs
55		}
56		return filepath.Clean(p)
57	}
58	
59	// Contract renders p with $HOME collapsed back to ~, for display only.
60	func Contract(p string) string {
61		h := home()
62		if h != "" && p == h {
63			return "~"
64		}
65		if h != "" && strings.HasPrefix(p, h+string(filepath.Separator)) {
66			return "~" + p[len(h):]
67		}
68		return p
69	}
```

```text
260	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
261		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
262			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
263			for _, value := range values {
264				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
265			}
266			return out, noFileCompletion
267		}
268	}
269	
270	func commaSeparatedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
271		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
272			prefix, current := "", toComplete
273			if i := strings.LastIndexByte(toComplete, ','); i >= 0 {
274				prefix, current = toComplete[:i+1], toComplete[i+1:]
275			}
276			used := make(map[string]bool)
277			for _, value := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(prefix, ","), ",") {
278				used[value] = value != ""
279			}
280			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
281			for _, value := range values {
282				candidate := prefix + value
283				if !used[value] && strings.HasPrefix(value, current) {
284					out = append(out, candidate)
285				}
286			}
287			return out, noFileCompletion
288		}
289	}
```

```go
package completionalloc

import (
	"slices"
	"testing"
)

type state string
type completion func(state) bool

const (
	hot state = "hot"
	warm state = "warm"
)

var callbackSink completion

func mapCompletion(states ...state) completion {
	allowed := make(map[state]bool, len(states))
	for _, s := range states {
		allowed[s] = true
	}
	return func(s state) bool { return allowed[s] }
}

func sliceCompletion(states ...state) completion {
	return func(s state) bool { return slices.Contains(states, s) }
}

func BenchmarkMapCompletionConstruction(b *testing.B) {
	for b.Loop() {
		callbackSink = mapCompletion(hot, warm)
	}
}

func BenchmarkSliceCompletionConstruction(b *testing.B) {
	for b.Loop() {
		callbackSink = sliceCompletion(hot, warm)
	}
}

```

```text
 	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
@@ -74,12 +75,32 @@ func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {

 }
 
-// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
-// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
-// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
-// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
-func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
-	fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
+// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
+// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
+// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
+// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
+// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
+// integrations.
+func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
+	if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
+		fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
+		if err != nil || fd < 3 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
+		}
+		file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
+		if file == nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
+		}
+		if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
+	return err
 }
 
 // ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
```

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-27 18:41:14Z)**_

The API documentation is broader than the implementation: it says `nil` for an invalid descriptor, but Go 1.26.4 does not probe whether a nonnegative Unix/Plan 9 descriptor is open, and Windows only recognizes the all-ones invalid-handle sentinel. That sentinel is impossible after `Atoi` accepts `fd >= 3`, since a positive `int` cannot occupy all `uintptr` bits; therefore the write is the realistic validation point on every implementation present in the pinned toolchain.

```text
44	func completeTasks(app *App, states ...task.State) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		allowed := make(map[task.State]bool, len(states))
46		for _, state := range states {
47			allowed[state] = true
48		}
49		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {

60					continue

78	func taskCompletionRef(all []*task.Task, target *task.Task, ref, typed string) (string, bool) {
79		if len(typed) > len(ref) || !strings.EqualFold(ref[:len(typed)], typed) {
80			return "", false
81		}
82		candidate := typed + ref[len(typed):]
83		var exact []*task.Task
84		for _, t := range all {
85			if t.ID == candidate || t.Branch == candidate {
86				exact = append(exact, t)
87			}
88		}
89		if len(exact) > 0 {
90			return candidate, len(exact) == 1 && exact[0].ID == target.ID
91		}
92		needle := strings.ToLower(candidate)
93		var match *task.Task
94		for _, t := range all {
95			haystack := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
96			if !strings.Contains(haystack, needle) {
97				continue
98			}
99			if match != nil {
100				return "", false
101			}
102			match = t
103		}
104		return candidate, match != nil && match.ID == target.ID
105	}

251		for _, name := range names {
252			value := strings.ToLower(name)
253			if !used[value] {
254				out = addCompletion(out, value, name+" bundled template", toComplete)
255			}
256		}
257		return out, noFileCompletion
258	}
259	
260	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
261		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
262			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
263			for _, value := range values {
264				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
265			}
266			return out, noFileCompletion
267		}
268	}
269	
270	func commaSeparatedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
271		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
272			prefix, current := "", toComplete
273			if i := strings.LastIndexByte(toComplete, ','); i >= 0 {
274				prefix, current = toComplete[:i+1], toComplete[i+1:]
275			}
276			used := make(map[string]bool)
277			for _, value := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(prefix, ","), ",") {
278				used[value] = value != ""
279			}
280			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
281			for _, value := range values {
282				candidate := prefix + value
283				if !used[value] && strings.HasPrefix(value, current) {
284					out = append(out, candidate)
285				}
286			}
287			return out, noFileCompletion
288		}
289	}
290	
291	func runtimeCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
292		backends := runtime.All()
293		values := make([]string, 1, len(backends)+1)
294		values[0] = "auto"
295		for _, backend := range backends {
296			values = append(values, backend.Name())
297		}
298		return fixedCompletions(values...)
299	}
300	
301	func taskStateNames() []string {
302		values := make([]string, len(task.States))
303		for i, state := range task.States {
304			values[i] = string(state)
305		}
306		return values
307	}
308	
309	func taskStateCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
310		return fixedCompletions(taskStateNames()...)
311	}
312	
313	func taskStateSliceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
314		return commaSeparatedCompletions(taskStateNames()...)
315	}
316	
317	func statsSourceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
318		return commaSeparatedCompletions(
319			string(stats.SourceSession), string(stats.SourceGit), string(stats.SourceWakaTime),
320		)
321	}
322	
323	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
324		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
325			panic(err)
326		}
327	}
328	
329	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
330		if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
331			return out
332		}
333		if description != "" {
334			description = completionDescriptionSanitizer.Replace(description)
335			value = cobra.CompletionWithDesc(value, description)
336		}
337		return append(out, value)
338	}
339
```

```text
263				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
264				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.

267					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
268				}, nil, nil
269			}
270		}
271		for _, r := range all {

273				return r, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
```

```text
79		if len(typed) > len(ref) || !strings.EqualFold(ref[:len(typed)], typed) {

91		}

190	func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
191		return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
192			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
193				return nil, noFileCompletion
194			}
195			repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
196			var repoPath string
197			if repoRef == "" {
198				var err error
199				repoPath, _, err = repoContext(app, "")
200				if err != nil {
201					return nil, noFileCompletion
202				}
203			} else {
204				r, _, err := repo.ResolveCompletion(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repoRef)
205				if err != nil {
206					return nil, noFileCompletion
207				}
208				repoPath = r.Path
209			}
210			worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
211			if err != nil {
212				return nil, noFileCompletion
213			}
214			out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
215			for _, wt := range worktrees {
216				if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
217					continue
218				}
219				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
220				if wt.Main {
221					description += " (main checkout)"
222				}
223				out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
224			}
225			return out, noFileCompletion
226		}
227	}
228	
229	func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
230		if len(args) > 0 {
231			return nil, noFileCompletion
232		}
233		topics, err := help.List()
234		if err != nil {
235			return nil, noFileCompletion
236		}
237		out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
238		for _, topic := range topics {
239			out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
240		}
241		return out, noFileCompletion
242	}
243	
244	func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
245		used := make(map[string]bool, len(args))
246		for _, name := range args {
247			used[strings.ToLower(name)] = true
248		}
249		names := ignore.BundledNames()
250		out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
251		for _, name := range names {
252			value := strings.ToLower(name)
253			if !used[value] {
254				out = addCompletion(out, value, name+" bundled template", toComplete)
255			}
256		}
257		return out, noFileCompletion
258	}
259	
260	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
261		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
262			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
263			for _, value := range values {
264				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
265			}
266			return out, noFileCompletion
267		}
268	}
269	
270	func commaSeparatedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
271		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
272			prefix, current := "", toComplete
273			if i := strings.LastIndexByte(toComplete, ','); i >= 0 {
274				prefix, current = toComplete[:i+1], toComplete[i+1:]
275			}
276			used := make(map[string]bool)
277			for _, value := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(prefix, ","), ",") {
278				used[value] = value != ""
279			}
280			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
281			for _, value := range values {
282				candidate := prefix + value
283				if !used[value] && strings.HasPrefix(value, current) {
284					out = append(out, candidate)
285				}
286			}
287			return out, noFileCompletion
288		}
289	}
290	
291	func runtimeCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
292		backends := runtime.All()
293		values := make([]string, 1, len(backends)+1)
294		values[0] = "auto"
295		for _, backend := range backends {
296			values = append(values, backend.Name())
297		}
298		return fixedCompletions(values...)
299	}
300	
301	func taskStateNames() []string {
302		values := make([]string, len(task.States))
303		for i, state := range task.States {
304			values[i] = string(state)
305		}
306		return values
307	}
308	
309	func taskStateCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
310		return fixedCompletions(taskStateNames()...)
311	}
312	
313	func taskStateSliceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
314		return commaSeparatedCompletions(taskStateNames()...)
315	}
316	
317	func statsSourceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
318		return commaSeparatedCompletions(
319			string(stats.SourceSession), string(stats.SourceGit), string(stats.SourceWakaTime),
320		)
321	}
322	
323	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
324		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
325			panic(err)
326		}
327	}
328	
329	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
330		if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
331			return out
332		}
333		if description != "" {
334			description = completionDescriptionSanitizer.Replace(description)
335			value = cobra.CompletionWithDesc(value, description)
336		}
337		return append(out, value)
338	}
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65		// Fast avoids per-repository git subprocesses. It is intended for shell
66		// completion: direct .git-file checkouts are skipped as linked worktrees and
67		// symlink aliases are deduplicated by their physical path.
68		Fast bool
69	}
70	
71	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
72	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
73	
74	// CompletionOptions trades full Git metadata for interactive latency.
75	func CompletionOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3, Fast: true} }
76	
77	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
78	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
79	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
80		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
81		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
82		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
83		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
84	}
85	
86	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
87	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
88	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
89	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
90		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
91			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
92		}
93		seen := map[string]bool{}
94		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
95		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
96		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
97		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
98		identities := map[string]bool{}
99		var out []Repo
100	
101		for _, root := range roots {
102			info, err := os.Stat(root)
103			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
104				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
105			}
106			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
107	
108			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
109				if err != nil {
110					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
111				}
112				if ctx.Err() != nil {
113					return ctx.Err()
114				}
115				if path == rootClean {
116					return nil
117				}
118				name := d.Name()
119				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
120				isDir := d.IsDir()
121				if isLink {
122					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
123					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
124					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
125					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
126						isDir = info.IsDir()
127					}
128				}
129				if !isDir {
130					return nil
131				}
132				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
133					return filepath.SkipDir
134				}
135	
136				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
137				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
138	
139				if isRepoDir(path) {
140					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
141					if real == "" {
142						real = path
143					}
144					bare := isBareDir(path)
145					identity, commonDir := real, real
146					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
147						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
148						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
149						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
150						return filepath.SkipDir
151					}
152					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
153						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
154							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
155							// project in the repo inventory.
156							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
157								return filepath.SkipDir
158							}
159							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
160							real = g.MainRoot
161						}
162					}
163					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
164						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
165						out = append(out, Repo{
166							Name:      name,
167							Path:      path,
168							RealPath:  real,
169							Symlink:   isLink,
170							Root:      rootClean,
171							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
172							CommonDir: commonDir,
173							Bare:      bare,
174							HasGit:    true,
175						})
176					}
177					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
178					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
179					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
180					return filepath.SkipDir
181				}
182				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
183					return filepath.SkipDir
184				}
185				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
186					if !seen[path] {
187						seen[path] = true
188						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
189					}
190				}
191				return nil
192			})
193			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
194				return out, ctx.Err()
195			}
196		}
197	
198		for i := range out {
199			if out[i].Category == "." {
200				out[i].Category = ""
201			}
202		}
203		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
204			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
205				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
206			}
207			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
208		})
209		return out, nil
210	}
211	
212	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
213	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
214	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
215		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
216			return true
217		}
218		return isBareDir(path)
219	}
220	
221	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
222		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
223		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
224	}
225	
226	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
227	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
228		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
229			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
230				return false
231			}
232		}
233		return true
234	}
235	
236	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
237	//
238	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
239	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
240	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
241	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
242		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
243	}
244	
245	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
246	// process per repository in the scan roots.
247	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
248		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
249	}
250	
251	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
252		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
253		if err != nil {
254			return Repo{}, nil, err
255		}
256		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
257			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
258				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
259				if real == "" {
260					real = g.MainRoot
261				}
262				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
263				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
264				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
265				return Repo{
266					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
267					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
268				}, nil, nil
269			}
270		}
271		for _, r := range all {
272			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
273				return r, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
277		var hits []Repo
278		for _, r := range all {
279			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
280				hits = append(hits, r)
281			}
282		}
283		switch len(hits) {
284		case 1:
285			return hits[0], nil, nil
286		case 0:
287			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
288		default:
289			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
290		}
291	}
292	
293	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
294	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
295	
296	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
297	
298	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
299	type AmbiguousError struct {
300		Ref        string
301		Candidates []Repo
302	}
303	
304	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
305		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
306		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
307			names[i] = c.Display()
308		}
309		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
310	}
```

-// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
-// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
-// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
-// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
-func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
-	fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
+// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
+// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
+// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
+// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
+// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
+// integrations.
+func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
+	if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
+		fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
+		if err != nil || fd < 3 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
+		}
+		file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
+		if file == nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
+		}
+		if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
+	return err
 }

```text
 func directPushHint(push bool) string {

 }
 
 // fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
 // forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
 //
 // merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
 // branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
 // a merge commit the user did not ask for.
 func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
 	fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
 	if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
 		return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
 			"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
 			err, config.Contract(checkout))
 	}
 	// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
 	fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
 	if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
 		return err
 	}
 	if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
 		return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
 			"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
 	}
 	return nil
 }

 		return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)

 		if usage := c.UseLine(); usage != "" {
 			fmt.Fprintf(b, "```\n%s\n```\n\n", usage)
 		}
 		if flags := renderFlags(c); flags != "" {
 			b.WriteString(flags)
 			b.WriteString("\n")
 		}

 func renderFlags(c *cobra.Command) string {
 	var b strings.Builder
 	c.LocalNonPersistentFlags().VisitAll(func(f *pflag.Flag) {
 		if f.Hidden {
 			return
 		}
 		name := "--" + f.Name
 		if f.Shorthand != "" {
 			name = "-" + f.Shorthand + ", " + name
 		}
 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` — %s\n", name, f.Usage)
 	})

 func firstLine(s string) string {

 // Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
 // display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan

 func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {

 // isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
 // (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
 func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
 	if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
 		return true
 	}
 	return isBareDir(path)
 }

 // isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
 func isBareDir(path string) bool {
 	for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
 		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
 			return false
 		}
 	}
 	return true
 }
 
 // Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
 //
 // Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
 // only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
 // is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
 func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
-	all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
+	return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
+}
+
+// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
+// process per repository in the scan roots.
+func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
+	return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
+}
+
+func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
+	all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
 	if err != nil {
 		return Repo{}, nil, err
 	}
 	if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
 		if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
 			real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
 			if real == "" {
 				real = g.MainRoot
 			}
 			// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
 			// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
 			// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
 			return Repo{
 				Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
 				Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
 			}, nil, nil
 		}
 	}
 	for _, r := range all {
 		if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
 			return r, nil, nil
 		}
 	}
 	needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
 	var hits []Repo
 	for _, r := range all {
 		if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
 			hits = append(hits, r)
 		}
 	}
 	switch len(hits) {
 	case 1:
 		return hits[0], nil, nil
 	case 0:
 		return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
 	default:
 		return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
 	}
 }
```

```text
78	func taskCompletionRef(all []*task.Task, target *task.Task, ref, typed string) (string, bool) {
79		if len(typed) > len(ref) || !strings.EqualFold(ref[:len(typed)], typed) {
80			return "", false
81		}
82		candidate := typed + ref[len(typed):]
83		var exact []*task.Task
84		for _, t := range all {
85			if t.ID == candidate || t.Branch == candidate {
86				exact = append(exact, t)
87			}
88		}
89		if len(exact) > 0 {
90			return candidate, len(exact) == 1 && exact[0].ID == target.ID
91		}
92		needle := strings.ToLower(candidate)
93		var match *task.Task
94		for _, t := range all {
95			haystack := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
96			if !strings.Contains(haystack, needle) {
97				continue
98			}
99			if match != nil {
100				return "", false
101			}
102			match = t
103		}
104		return candidate, match != nil && match.ID == target.ID
105	}

292		backends := runtime.All()
293		values := make([]string, 1, len(backends)+1)
294		values[0] = "auto"
295		for _, backend := range backends {
296			values = append(values, backend.Name())
297		}
298		return fixedCompletions(values...)
299	}

301	func taskStateNames() []string {
302		values := make([]string, len(task.States))
303		for i, state := range task.States {
304			values[i] = string(state)
305		}
306		return values
307	}
308	
309	func taskStateCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
310		return fixedCompletions(taskStateNames()...)
311	}
312	
313	func taskStateSliceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
314		return commaSeparatedCompletions(taskStateNames()...)
315	}
316	
317	func statsSourceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
318		return commaSeparatedCompletions(
319			string(stats.SourceSession), string(stats.SourceGit), string(stats.SourceWakaTime),
320		)
321	}
322	
323	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
324		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
325			panic(err)
326		}
327	}
328	
329	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
330		if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
331			return out
332		}
333		if description != "" {
334			description = completionDescriptionSanitizer.Replace(description)
335			value = cobra.CompletionWithDesc(value, description)
336		}
337		return append(out, value)
338	}
```
