```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65		// Fast avoids per-repository git subprocesses. It is intended for shell
66		// completion: direct .git-file checkouts are skipped as linked worktrees and
67		// symlink aliases are deduplicated by their physical path.
68		Fast bool
69	}
70	
71	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
72	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
73	
74	// CompletionOptions trades full Git metadata for interactive latency.
75	func CompletionOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3, Fast: true} }
76	
77	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
78	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
79	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
80		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
81		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
82		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
83		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
84	}
85	
86	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
87	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
88	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
89	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
90		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
91			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
92		}
93		seen := map[string]bool{}
94		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
95		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
96		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
97		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
98		identities := map[string]bool{}
99		var out []Repo
100	
101		for _, root := range roots {
102			info, err := os.Stat(root)
103			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
104				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
105			}
106			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
107	
108			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
109				if err != nil {
110					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
111				}
112				if ctx.Err() != nil {
113					return ctx.Err()
114				}
115				if path == rootClean {
116					return nil
117				}
118				name := d.Name()
119				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
120				isDir := d.IsDir()
121				if isLink {
122					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
123					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
124					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
125					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
126						isDir = info.IsDir()
127					}
128				}
129				if !isDir {
130					return nil
131				}
132				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
133					return filepath.SkipDir
134				}
135	
136				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
137				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
138	
139				if isRepoDir(path) {
140					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
141					if real == "" {
142						real = path
143					}
144					bare := isBareDir(path)
145					identity, commonDir := real, real
146					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
147						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
148						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
149						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
150						return filepath.SkipDir
151					}
152					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
153						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
154							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
155							// project in the repo inventory.
156							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
157								return filepath.SkipDir
158							}
159							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
160							real = g.MainRoot
161						}
162					}
163					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
164						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
165						out = append(out, Repo{
166							Name:      name,
167							Path:      path,
168							RealPath:  real,
169							Symlink:   isLink,
170							Root:      rootClean,
171							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
172							CommonDir: commonDir,
173							Bare:      bare,
174							HasGit:    true,
175						})
176					}
177					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
178					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
179					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
180					return filepath.SkipDir
181				}
182				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
183					return filepath.SkipDir
184				}
185				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
186					if !seen[path] {
187						seen[path] = true
188						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
189					}
190				}
191				return nil
192			})
193			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
194				return out, ctx.Err()
195			}
196		}
197	
198		for i := range out {
199			if out[i].Category == "." {
200				out[i].Category = ""
201			}
202		}
203		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
204			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
205				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
206			}
207			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
208		})
209		return out, nil
210	}
211	
212	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
213	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
214	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
215		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
216			return true
217		}
218		return isBareDir(path)
219	}
220	
221	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
222		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
223		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
224	}
225	
226	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
227	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
228		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
229			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
230				return false
231			}
232		}
233		return true
234	}
235	
236	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
237	//
238	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
239	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
240	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
241	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
242		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
243	}
244	
245	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
246	// process per repository in the scan roots.
247	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
248		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
249	}
250	
251	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
252		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
253		if err != nil {
254			return Repo{}, nil, err
255		}
256		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
257			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
258				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
259				if real == "" {
260					real = g.MainRoot
261				}
262				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
263				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
264				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
265				return Repo{
266					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
267					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
268				}, nil, nil
269			}
270		}
271		for _, r := range all {
272			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
273				return r, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
277		var hits []Repo
278		for _, r := range all {
279			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
280				hits = append(hits, r)
281			}
282		}
283		switch len(hits) {
284		case 1:
285			return hits[0], nil, nil
286		case 0:
287			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
288		default:
289			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
290		}
291	}
292	
293	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
294	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
295	
296	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
297	
298	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
299	type AmbiguousError struct {
300		Ref        string
301		Candidates []Repo
302	}
303	
304	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
305		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
306		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
307			names[i] = c.Display()
308		}
309		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
310	}
311
```

```text
1	// Package skill embeds and installs dev's agent skill.
2	//
3	// The binary is the authority for its own skill, the same way `herdr --skill`
4	// is: a skill vendored separately drifts from the tool it documents, and an
5	// agent reading a stale command list is worse than one reading none. Embedding
6	// means the skill shipped is always the skill this build implements.
7	package skill
8	
9	import (
10		"embed"
11		"fmt"
12		"io/fs"
13		"os"
14		"path/filepath"
15		"strings"
16	)
17	
18	//go:embed all:dev-cli
19	var files embed.FS
20	
21	// Name is the skill's directory and frontmatter name.
22	//
23	// Deliberately not "dev", matching the binary: a skill is selected by its name
24	// and description, and "dev" describes nothing. The binary is typed dozens of
25	// times a day and should stay short; the skill is read by an agent deciding
26	// whether it is relevant, and should say what it covers.
27	const Name = "dev-cli"
28	
29	// Render returns the SKILL.md body.
30	func Render() (string, error) {
31		b, err := files.ReadFile("dev-cli/SKILL.md")
32		if err != nil {
33			return "", fmt.Errorf("bundled skill is missing: %w", err)
34		}
35		return string(b), nil
36	}
37	
38	// Files walks the embedded skill tree, yielding relative paths and contents.
39	func Files() (map[string][]byte, error) {
40		out := map[string][]byte{}
41		err := fs.WalkDir(files, "dev-cli", func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
42			if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
43				return err
44			}
45			b, err := files.ReadFile(p)
46			if err != nil {
47				return err
48			}
49			out[strings.TrimPrefix(p, "dev-cli/")] = b
50			return nil
51		})
52		return out, err
53	}
54	
55	// InstallResult reports what an install changed.
56	type InstallResult struct {
57		Dir     string
58		Written []string
59		Skipped []string
60		Links   []string
61	}
62	
63	// DefaultDir is where the skill is installed: the shared agent skills
64	// directory, which Claude Code, Codex and others all read.
65	func DefaultDir() string {
66		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
67		return filepath.Join(home, ".agents", "skills", Name)
68	}
69	
70	// LinkDirs are the tool-specific directories that get a symlink back to the
71	// shared install, matching the layout these tools already use.
72	func LinkDirs() []string {
73		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
74		return []string{filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "skills")}
75	}
76	
77	// Install writes the embedded skill to dir and links it into the per-tool
78	// skill directories. Writes are content-compared first, so re-running is a
79	// no-op and does not churn mtimes that other tools watch.
80	func Install(dir string, link bool) (InstallResult, error) {
81		res := InstallResult{Dir: dir}
82		all, err := Files()
83		if err != nil {
84			return res, err
85		}
86		if len(all) == 0 {
87			return res, fmt.Errorf("no skill files are embedded in this build")
88		}
89	
90		for rel, content := range all {
91			dst := filepath.Join(dir, rel)
92			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o755); err != nil {
93				return res, err
94			}
95			if existing, err := os.ReadFile(dst); err == nil && string(existing) == string(content) {
96				res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, rel)
97				continue
98			}
99			if err := os.WriteFile(dst, content, 0o644); err != nil {
100				return res, fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", dst, err)
101			}
102			res.Written = append(res.Written, rel)
103		}
104	
105		if !link {
106			return res, nil
107		}
108		for _, base := range LinkDirs() {
109			if _, err := os.Stat(base); err != nil {
110				continue // that tool is not installed here
111			}
112			target := filepath.Join(base, Name)
113			if existing, err := os.Readlink(target); err == nil {
114				if resolveLink(base, existing) == dir {
115					continue // already correct
116				}
117				os.Remove(target)
118			} else if _, err := os.Stat(target); err == nil {
119				// A real directory, not our symlink: never clobber it.
120				continue
121			}
122			if err := os.Symlink(dir, target); err != nil {
123				return res, fmt.Errorf("link %s: %w", target, err)
124			}
125			res.Links = append(res.Links, target)
126		}
127		return res, nil
128	}
129	
130	func resolveLink(base, link string) string {
131		if filepath.IsAbs(link) {
132			return filepath.Clean(link)
133		}
134		return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(base, link))
135	}
136
```

diff --git a/internal/cli/skill.go b/internal/cli/skill.go
index 014fc4c..c7c1720 100644
--- a/internal/cli/skill.go
+++ b/internal/cli/skill.go
@@ -89,61 +89,61 @@ func newSkillSyncCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
 	var check bool
 	cmd := &cobra.Command{
 		Use:   "sync",
 		Short: "Regenerate the skill's command reference from the live command tree",
 		Long: `Rewrite the generated section of the skill's command reference from this
 binary's actual command tree, so the documented flags can never drift from the
 implemented ones.
 
 With --check, report drift and exit non-zero instead of writing — the form to
 wire into CI or a pre-push hook.`,
 		Args: cobra.NoArgs,
 		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
 			generated := generateCommandReference(cmd.Root())
 			return syncCommandReference(app, generated, check)
 		},
 	}
 	cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&check, "check", false, "report drift and exit non-zero instead of writing")
 	return cmd
 }
 
 // generateCommandReference renders the whole command tree as markdown. This is
 // the single source of truth for what the skill tells an agent dev can do.
 func generateCommandReference(root *cobra.Command) string {
 	var b strings.Builder
 	b.WriteString("<!-- generated by `dev skill sync`; do not edit by hand -->\n\n")
 	writeCommand(&b, root, 0)
 	return b.String()
 }
 
 func writeCommand(b *strings.Builder, c *cobra.Command, depth int) {
-	if c.Hidden || c.Name() == "no-help" || c.Name() == "completion" {
+	if c.Hidden || c.Name() == "no-help" {
 		return
 	}
 	if depth > 0 {
 		fmt.Fprintf(b, "### `%s`\n\n%s\n\n", c.CommandPath(), firstLine(c.Short))
 		if usage := c.UseLine(); usage != "" {
 			fmt.Fprintf(b, "```\n%s\n```\n\n", usage)
 		}
 		if flags := renderFlags(c); flags != "" {
 			b.WriteString(flags)
 			b.WriteString("\n")
 		}
 	}
 	for _, sub := range c.Commands() {
 		writeCommand(b, sub, depth+1)
 	}
 }
 
 func renderFlags(c *cobra.Command) string {
 	var b strings.Builder
 	c.LocalNonPersistentFlags().VisitAll(func(f *pflag.Flag) {
 		if f.Hidden {
 			return
 		}
 		name := "--" + f.Name
 		if f.Shorthand != "" {
 			name = "-" + f.Shorthand + ", " + name
 		}
 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` — %s\n", name, f.Usage)
 	})
 	return b.String()

```text
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}

181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
```

```text
15	func newParkCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

17			next   string
18			note   string
19			wip    bool
20			push   bool
21			cold   bool
22			keepRT bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "park [task]",
26			Short: "Stop working on a task without losing the thread",
27			Long: `Park the current task (or the one named) so its runtime session can close.
28	
29	Parking is the missing move that makes a crowded sidebar shrink. It records
30	what to do next, optionally checkpoints uncommitted work, and closes the
31	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
32	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.
33	
34	  warm (default)  worktree and branch stay; session closes. Back within days.
35	  cold (--cold)   work is committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstruct
36	                  it anywhere later with dev resume.
37	
38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
41			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
42			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
43				ctx := ctxOf()
44				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
45				if err != nil {
46					return err
47				}
48	
49				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
50				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
51					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
52						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
53				}
54				target := task.Warm
55				if cold {
56					target = task.Cold
57				}
58				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
59	
60				if next != "" {
61					t.Next = next
62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69	
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97	
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114	
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}
124	
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes

134					t.WorktreePath = ""

136				if cold && mode == task.ModeBranch {

139					base := t.Base
140					if base == "" {
141						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
142					}
143					if base == "" {
144						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but its base branch is unknown")
145					}
146					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
147						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
148							base, err)
149					}
150				}
151	
152				t.State = target
153				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
154				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
155					return err
156				}
157				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
158				if t.Next != "" {
159					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
160				}
161				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
162				return nil

164		}

171		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
172		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app, task.Hot, task.Warm)
173		return cmd
174	}

176	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
177	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
178		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
179			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
180		}
181		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
182		return nil
183	}
184	
185	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
186	// directory when no argument is given.
187	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
188		if len(args) == 1 {
189			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
190		}
191		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
196		if err != nil {
197			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
198				config.Contract(cwd))
199		}
200		return t, nil
201	}
```

```text
272	// parseSince accepts a relative window ("30d", "6mo", "1y") or an absolute
273	// date. Relative is what people actually type; absolute is what scripts want.
274	func parseSince(s string, now time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
275		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
276		if s == "" {
277			return now.AddDate(-1, 0, 0), nil
278		}
279		if d, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", s, time.Local); err == nil {
280			return d, nil
281		}
282		var n int
283		var unit string
284		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(s, "%d%s", &n, &unit); err != nil || n <= 0 {
285			return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot parse --since %q: want 30d, 6mo, 1y or YYYY-MM-DD", s)
286		}
287		switch strings.ToLower(unit) {
288		case "d", "day", "days":
289			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n), nil
290		case "w", "week", "weeks":
291			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n*7), nil
292		case "mo", "month", "months":
293			return now.AddDate(0, -n, 0), nil
294		case "y", "yr", "year", "years":
295			return now.AddDate(-n, 0, 0), nil
296		}
297		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown unit %q in --since: want d, w, mo or y", unit)
298	}
```

```text
1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11		"strconv"
12	
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16	)
17	
18	// App is the state shared by every command.
19	type App struct {
20		Cfg   config.Config
21		Tasks *task.Store
22	
23		Out io.Writer
24		Err io.Writer
25	
26		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
27		configPath string
28		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
29		runtimeOverride string
30		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
31		noRuntime bool
32	}
33	
34	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
35	func (a *App) Load() error {
36		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
37		if err != nil {
38			return err
39		}
40		a.Cfg = cfg
41		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
42		if a.Out == nil {
43			a.Out = os.Stdout
44		}
45		if a.Err == nil {
46			a.Err = os.Stderr
47		}
48		return nil
49	}
50	
51	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
52	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
53	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
54		if a.noRuntime {
55			return runtime.None{}
56		}
57		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
58		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
59			backend = a.runtimeOverride
60		}
61		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
62		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
63			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
64		}
65		return rt
66	}
67	
68	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
69	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
70		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
71	}
72	
73	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
74	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
76	}
77	
78	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
79	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
80	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
81	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
82	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
83	// integrations.
84	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
85		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
86			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
87			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
88				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
89			}
90			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
91			if file == nil {
92				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
93			}
94			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
95				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
96			}
97			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
98				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
99			}
100			return nil
101		}
102		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
103		return err
104	}
105	
106	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
107	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
108
```

```text
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)

142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}

183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
```

```text
1	// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
18	type Session struct {
19		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
20		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
21		Handle string
22		Label  string
23		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
24		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
25		// value.
26		Dirs []string
27		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
28		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
29		AgentStatus string
30		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
31		AgentSessions []string
32		Focused       bool
33	}
34	
35	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
36	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
37		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
38			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
39			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
40			// $HOME active.
41			if d == dir || strings.HasPrefix(d, dir+"/") {
42				return true
43			}
44		}
45		return false
46	}
47	
48	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
49	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
50	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
51	type Runtime interface {
52		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
53		Name() string
54		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
55		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
56		Available() bool
57		// Open makes dir live and returns a handle. Opening something already open
58		// focuses it rather than duplicating it.
59		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error)
60		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
61		// task entry.
62		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
63		// List enumerates live sessions.
64		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
65		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
66		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
67		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
68	}
69	
70	// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
71	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
72	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
73	type WorktreeOpener interface {
74		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error)
75	}
76	
77	// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
78	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
79	
80	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
81		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
82	}
83	
84	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
85	//
86	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
87	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then None.
88	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
89	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
90		herdr, tmux, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}
91		switch backend {
92		case "herdr":
93			return herdr
94		case "tmux":
95			return tmux
96		case "none":
97			return none
98		case "", "auto":
99			if herdr.Available() {
100				return herdr
101			}
102			if tmux.Available() {
103				return tmux
104			}
105			return none
106		}
107		return none
108	}
109	
110	// All returns every backend, for `dev doctor` to report on.
111	func All() []Runtime { return []Runtime{NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}} }
112	
113	// haveBinary reports whether name is on PATH.
114	func haveBinary(name string) bool {
115		_, err := exec.LookPath(name)
116		return err == nil
117	}
```

```text
1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11		"strconv"
12	
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16	)
17	
18	// App is the state shared by every command.
19	type App struct {
20		Cfg   config.Config
21		Tasks *task.Store
22	
23		Out io.Writer
24		Err io.Writer
25	
26		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
27		configPath string
28		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
29		runtimeOverride string
30		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
31		noRuntime bool
32	}
33	
34	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
35	func (a *App) Load() error {
36		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
37		if err != nil {
38			return err
39		}
40		a.Cfg = cfg
41		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
42		if a.Out == nil {
43			a.Out = os.Stdout
44		}
45		if a.Err == nil {
46			a.Err = os.Stderr
47		}
48		return nil
49	}
50	
51	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
52	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
53	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
54		if a.noRuntime {
55			return runtime.None{}
56		}
57		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
58		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
59			backend = a.runtimeOverride
60		}
61		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
62		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
63			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
64		}
65		return rt
66	}
67	
68	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
69	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
70		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
71	}
72	
73	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
74	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
76	}
77	
78	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
79	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
80	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
81	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
82	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
83	// integrations.
84	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
85		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
86			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
87			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
88				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
89			}
90			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
91			if file == nil {
92				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
93			}
94			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
95				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
96			}
97			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
98				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
99			}
100			return nil
101		}
102		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
103		return err
104	}
105	
106	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
107	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
```

```text
56	func runList(app *App, o listOptions) error {

74

97				if r.Session.AgentStatus != "" {

105			case !r.CheckoutExists:

107			}

110				truncate(r.Task.Title(), 28),
```

```text
1	// Package inventory joins the three sources that describe work in progress:
2	// the task registry (human intent), git (durable code state) and the runtime
3	// (what is live right now). It is the single code path behind `dev ls`,
4	// `dev status`, `dev sweep` and the TUI, so all four can never disagree.
5	package inventory
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"os"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"sync"
13		"time"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
18	)
19	
20	// Row is one task enriched with everything derived live.
21	type Row struct {
22		Task *task.Task
23	
24		// Checkout is where the task's code currently lives: its worktree if it
25		// has one, else the repo. Empty when nothing exists on disk.
26		Checkout string
27		// CheckoutExists reports whether that directory is actually present. A
28		// cold task, or one whose worktree was removed behind dev's back, is not.
29		CheckoutExists bool
30		// WorktreeMissing flags a task that records a worktree path which is no
31		// longer a registered git worktree — the drift `dev sweep` reports.
32		WorktreeMissing bool
33	
34		// Status is the live git status of Checkout. Zero when there is nothing
35		// on disk to inspect.
36		Status    gitx.Status
37		StatusErr error
38	
39		// LastCommit is the author time of HEAD, used to age a task.
40		LastCommit time.Time
41	
42		// Session is the live runtime session hosting this checkout, if any.
43		Session *runtime.Session
44		// sessionsTracked reports whether the runtime can observe sessions at all.
45		// With the "none" backend it cannot, so "hot but nothing live" is not
46		// drift — it is the only state that backend can ever produce.
47		sessionsTracked bool
48	}
49	
50	// Live reports whether a runtime session is currently hosting this task.
51	func (r Row) Live() bool { return r.Session != nil }
52	
53	// StateDrift reports a task whose recorded state disagrees with reality:
54	// hot with no live session, or warm/cold with one. It is what `dev sweep`
55	// turns into suggestions — dev reports drift and never silently rewrites it.
56	func (r Row) StateDrift() string {
57		if r.sessionsTracked {
58			switch r.Task.State {
59			case task.Hot:
60				if !r.Live() {
61					return "no live session"
62				}
63			case task.Warm, task.Cold:
64				if r.Live() {
65					return "session is live"
66				}
67			}
68		}
69		if r.Task.State == task.Cold && r.CheckoutExists && r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
70			return "worktree still on disk"
71		}
72		if r.WorktreeMissing {
73			return "worktree is gone"
74		}
75		return ""
76	}
77	
78	// Age is how long since the task's last commit, falling back to when the entry
79	// was last written for a task with no commits of its own.
80	func (r Row) Age() time.Duration {
81		ref := r.LastCommit
82		if ref.IsZero() || r.Task.Updated.After(ref) {
83			ref = r.Task.Updated
84		}
85		if ref.IsZero() {
86			return 0
87		}
88		return time.Since(ref)
89	}
90	
91	// Options tunes what a Collect call spends time on.
92	type Options struct {
93		// SkipRuntime avoids querying the multiplexer, for callers that only need
94		// git facts (and for tests).
95		SkipRuntime bool
96		// SkipGit avoids running git per task, for a fast listing.
97		SkipGit bool
98	}
99	
100	// Collect builds the enriched inventory. Git probes run concurrently: each is
101	// a handful of process spawns, and a machine with dozens of tasks would
102	// otherwise make `dev ls` feel slow.
103	func Collect(ctx context.Context, tasks []*task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opts Options) []Row {
104		rows := make([]Row, len(tasks))
105	
106		var sessions []runtime.Session
107		tracked := false
108		if !opts.SkipRuntime && rt != nil && rt.Name() != "none" {
109			if s, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
110				sessions, tracked = s, true
111			}
112		}
113	
114		var wg sync.WaitGroup
115		// Bound concurrency: git is process-heavy and an unbounded fan-out over a
116		// large inventory would thrash.
117		sem := make(chan struct{}, 8)
118	
119		for i, t := range tasks {
120			rows[i].Task = t
121			rows[i].Checkout = checkoutOf(t)
122	
123			if opts.SkipGit || rows[i].Checkout == "" {
124				continue
125			}
126			wg.Add(1)
127			go func(i int) {
128				defer wg.Done()
129				sem <- struct{}{}
130				defer func() { <-sem }()
131				enrich(ctx, &rows[i])
132			}(i)
133		}
134		wg.Wait()
135	
136		for i := range rows {
137			rows[i].Session = matchSession(sessions, rows[i])
138			rows[i].sessionsTracked = tracked
139		}
140		return rows
141	}
142	
143	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
144		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
145			return t.WorktreePath
146		}
147		return t.RepoPath
148	}
149	
150	func enrich(ctx context.Context, r *Row) {
151		info, err := os.Stat(r.Checkout)
152		r.CheckoutExists = err == nil && info.IsDir()
153		if !r.CheckoutExists {
154			if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
155				r.WorktreeMissing = true
156			}
157			return
158		}
159		if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Checkout); err != nil {
160			r.StatusErr = err
161		} else {
162			r.Status = st
163		}
164		if unix, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, r.Checkout); err == nil && unix > 0 {
165			r.LastCommit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
166		}
167		// A recorded worktree that git no longer knows about is drift worth
168		// surfacing: the directory may exist while the administrative entry is gone.
169		if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
170			if _, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, r.Task.RepoPath, r.Task.Branch); err == nil && !ok {
171				r.WorktreeMissing = true
172			}
173		}
174	}
175	
176	// matchSession picks the runtime session hosting a row's checkout. An exact
177	// directory match is preferred over a containing one, so a worktree's own
178	// session always wins over the parent repo's.
179	func matchSession(sessions []runtime.Session, r Row) *runtime.Session {
180		if r.Checkout == "" {
181			return nil
182		}
183		var contains *runtime.Session
184		for i := range sessions {
185			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
186				if d == r.Checkout {
187					return &sessions[i]
188				}
189				if strings.HasPrefix(d, r.Checkout+"/") && contains == nil {
190					contains = &sessions[i]
191				}
192			}
193		}
194		return contains
195	}
196	
197	// Filter narrows rows by state and repo. An empty filter matches everything.
198	type Filter struct {
199		States []task.State
200		Repo   string
201		// LiveOnly keeps only tasks with a runtime session.
202		LiveOnly bool
203		// DirtyOnly keeps only tasks with uncommitted work.
204		DirtyOnly bool
205	}
206	
207	// Apply returns the rows matching f.
208	func (f Filter) Apply(rows []Row) []Row {
209		out := rows[:0:0]
210		for _, r := range rows {
211			if len(f.States) > 0 && !containsState(f.States, r.Task.State) {
212				continue
213			}
214			if f.Repo != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Task.Repo), strings.ToLower(f.Repo)) {
215				continue
216			}
217			if f.LiveOnly && !r.Live() {
218				continue
219			}
220			if f.DirtyOnly && !r.Status.Dirty() {
221				continue
222			}
223			out = append(out, r)
224		}
225		return out
226	}
227	
228	func containsState(list []task.State, s task.State) bool {
229		for _, v := range list {
230			if v == s {
231				return true
232			}
233		}
234		return false
235	}
236	
237	// Orphans reports live runtime sessions that no task claims — the "I opened
238	// this and never wrote it down" case that makes a sidebar grow without bound.
239	func Orphans(sessions []runtime.Session, rows []Row) []runtime.Session {
240		claimed := map[string]bool{}
241		for _, r := range rows {
242			if r.Session != nil {
243				claimed[r.Session.Handle] = true
244			}
245		}
246		var out []runtime.Session
247		for _, s := range sessions {
248			if !claimed[s.Handle] {
249				out = append(out, s)
250			}
251		}
252		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Label < out[j].Label })
253		return out
254	}
```

```text
1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123	
124		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
125		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
126	}
127	
128	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}
141	
142	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}
174
```

 `./internal/runtime/runtime.go`

```text
1	// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
18	type Session struct {
19		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
20		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
21		Handle string
22		Label  string
23		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
24		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
25		// value.
26		Dirs []string
27		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
28		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
29		AgentStatus string
30		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
31		AgentSessions []string
32		Focused       bool
33	}
34	
35	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
36	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
37		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
38			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
39			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
40			// $HOME active.
41			if d == dir || strings.HasPrefix(d, dir+"/") {
42				return true
43			}
44		}
45		return false
46	}
47	
48	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
49	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
50	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
51	type Runtime interface {
52		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
53		Name() string
54		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
55		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
56		Available() bool
57		// Open makes dir live and returns a handle. Opening something already open
58		// focuses it rather than duplicating it.
59		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error)
60		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
61		// task entry.
62		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
63		// List enumerates live sessions.
64		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
65		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
66		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
67		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
68	}
69	
70	// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
71	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
72	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
73	type WorktreeOpener interface {
74		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error)
75	}
76	
77	// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
78	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
79	
80	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
81		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
82	}
83	
84	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
85	//
86	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
87	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then None.
88	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
89	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
90		herdr, tmux, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}
91		switch backend {
92		case "herdr":
93			return herdr
94		case "tmux":
95			return tmux
96		case "none":
97			return none
98		case "", "auto":
99			if herdr.Available() {
100				return herdr
101			}
102			if tmux.Available() {
103				return tmux
104			}
105			return none
106		}
107		return none
108	}
109	
110	// All returns every backend, for `dev doctor` to report on.
111	func All() []Runtime { return []Runtime{NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}} }
112	
113	// haveBinary reports whether name is on PATH.
114	func haveBinary(name string) bool {
115		_, err := exec.LookPath(name)
116		return err == nil
117	}
118
```

```text
package cobra // import "github.com/spf13/cobra"

type ShellCompDirective int
    ShellCompDirective is a bit map representing the different behaviors the
    shell can be instructed to have once completions have been provided.

const ShellCompDirectiveError ShellCompDirective = 1 << iota ...
package pflag // import "github.com/spf13/pflag"

func (f *FlagSet) StringSliceVar(p *[]string, name string, value []string, usage string)
    StringSliceVar defines a string flag with specified name, default value,
    and usage string. The argument p points to a []string variable in which to
    store the value of the flag. Compared to StringArray flags, StringSlice
    flags take comma-separated value as arguments and split them accordingly.
    For example:

        --ss="v1,v2" --ss="v3"

    will result in

        []string{"v1", "v2", "v3"}
```

```text
273			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
274			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
```

```text
8	all: fmt vet test build
```

```text
260	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
261		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
262			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
263			for _, value := range values {
264				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
265			}
266			return out, noFileCompletion
267		}
268	}
269	
270	func commaSeparatedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
271		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
272			prefix, current := "", toComplete
273			if i := strings.LastIndexByte(toComplete, ','); i >= 0 {
274				prefix, current = toComplete[:i+1], toComplete[i+1:]
275			}
276			used := make(map[string]bool)
277			for _, value := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(prefix, ","), ",") {
278				used[value] = value != ""
279			}
280			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
281			for _, value := range values {
282				candidate := prefix + value
283				if !used[value] && strings.HasPrefix(value, current) {
284					out = append(out, candidate)
285				}
286			}
287			return out, noFileCompletion
288		}
289	}
```

```text
21		}

23			return info.Main.Version
24		}
25		return Version
26	}

28	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
29	
30	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
31	
32	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
33	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
34	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
35	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
36	
37	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
38	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
39	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`
40	
41	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
42	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
43		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
44	}
45	
46	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
47	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
48	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
49	// descriptors.
50	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
51		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
52	
53		root := &cobra.Command{

57			Version:       versionFromBuild(),
58			SilenceUsage:  true,
59			SilenceErrors: true,
60			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
61			// exists to answer.
62			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
63				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
64					out, err := skill.Render()
65					if err != nil {
66						return err
67					}
68					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
69					return nil
70				}
71				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
72				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
73				if interactive() {
74					return runTUI(app)
75				}
76				return runList(app, listOptions{})
77			},
78			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
79				if completionInvocation(cmd) {
80					return nil
81				}
82				return app.Load()
83			},
84		}
85	
86		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
```

```text
18	const noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
19	
20	var completionDescriptionSanitizer = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ")
21	
22	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
23	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
24	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
25	// persistent flags (notably --config).
26	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
27		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd || cmd.CalledAs() == cobra.ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd {
28			return true
29		}
30		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
31			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
32				return true
33			}
34		}
35		return false
36	}
37	
38	// loadCompletion prepares local providers after Cobra has parsed the command
39	// line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break command and
40	// flag completion entirely. Cobra invokes one custom provider per request, so
41	// loading here avoids state leaking when a command tree is reused.
42	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool { return a.Load() == nil }
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App, states ...task.State) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		allowed := make(map[task.State]bool, len(states))
46		for _, state := range states {
47			allowed[state] = true
48		}
49		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
50			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
54			if err != nil {
55				return nil, noFileCompletion
56			}
57			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
58			for _, t := range tasks {
59				if !allowed[t.State] {
60					continue
61				}
62				value := t.ID
63				if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
64					for _, ref := range []string{t.Title(), t.Branch} {
65						if candidate, ok := taskCompletionRef(tasks, t, ref, toComplete); ok {
66							value = candidate
67							break
68						}
69					}
70				}
71				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.ID)
72				out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
73			}
74			return out, noFileCompletion
75		}
76	}

78	func taskCompletionRef(all []*task.Task, target *task.Task, ref, typed string) (string, bool) {
79		if len(typed) > len(ref) || !strings.EqualFold(ref[:len(typed)], typed) {
80			return "", false
81		}
82		candidate := typed + ref[len(typed):]
83		var exact []*task.Task
84		for _, t := range all {
85			if t.ID == candidate || t.Branch == candidate {
86				exact = append(exact, t)
87			}
88		}
89		if len(exact) > 0 {
90			return candidate, len(exact) == 1 && exact[0].ID == target.ID
91		}
92		needle := strings.ToLower(candidate)
93		var match *task.Task
94		for _, t := range all {
95			haystack := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
96			if !strings.Contains(haystack, needle) {
97				continue
98			}
99			if match != nil {
100				return "", false
101			}
102			match = t
103		}
104		return candidate, match != nil && match.ID == target.ID
105	}
106	
107	// completeRepos supplies positional repository references. Commands resolve a
108	// unique display name, while duplicate displays use their absolute path so the
109	// selected token still identifies exactly one checkout.
110	func completeRepos(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
111		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
112			if len(args) > 0 {
113				return nil, noFileCompletion
114			}
115			return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, false)
116		}
117	}
118	
119	// completeRepoFlag is the same domain without a positional-argument guard: a
120	// flag may legally appear after another argument, e.g. wt open branch --repo.
121	func completeRepoFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
122		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
123			return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, false)
124		}
125	}
126	
127	// completeRepoNameFlag returns the name stored in tasks and stats, not the
128	// Category/Name display reference used by repository commands.
129	func completeRepoNameFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
130		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
131			return repositoryCompletions(app, toComplete, true)
132		}
133	}
134	
135	func completeTaskRepoNameFlag(app *App) cobra.CompletionFunc {
136		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
137			if !app.loadCompletion() {
138				return nil, noFileCompletion
139			}
140			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
141			if err != nil {
142				return nil, noFileCompletion
143			}
144			seen := make(map[string]bool, len(tasks))
145			var out []string
146			for _, t := range tasks {
147				if !seen[t.Repo] {
148					seen[t.Repo] = true
149					out = addCompletion(out, t.Repo, "tracked task repository", toComplete)
150				}
151			}
152			return out, noFileCompletion
153		}
154	}
155	
156	func repositoryCompletions(app *App, toComplete string, namesOnly bool) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
157		if !app.loadCompletion() {
158			return nil, noFileCompletion
159		}
160		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.CompletionOptions())
161		if err != nil {
162			return nil, noFileCompletion
163		}
164		displayCount := make(map[string]int, len(repos))
165		for _, r := range repos {
166			displayCount[r.Display()]++
167		}
168		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(repos))
169		out := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
170		for _, r := range repos {
171			value := r.Display()
172			description := config.Contract(r.Path)
173			switch {
174			case namesOnly:
175				value = r.Name
176				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
177			case displayCount[value] > 1:
178				value = r.Path
179				description = r.Display() + " · " + description
180			}
181			if seen[value] {
182				continue
183			}
184			seen[value] = true
185			out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
186		}
187		return out, noFileCompletion
188	}
189	
190	func completeWorktrees(app *App, includeMain bool) cobra.CompletionFunc {
191		return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
192			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
193				return nil, noFileCompletion
194			}
195			repoRef, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("repo")
196			var repoPath string
197			if repoRef == "" {
198				var err error
199				repoPath, _, err = repoContext(app, "")
200				if err != nil {
201					return nil, noFileCompletion
202				}
203			} else {
204				r, _, err := repo.ResolveCompletion(ctxOf(), app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repoRef)
205				if err != nil {
206					return nil, noFileCompletion
207				}
208				repoPath = r.Path
209			}
210			worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctxOf(), repoPath)
211			if err != nil {
212				return nil, noFileCompletion
213			}
214			out := make([]string, 0, len(worktrees))
215			for _, wt := range worktrees {
216				if wt.Branch == "" || wt.Detached || wt.Bare || (!includeMain && wt.Main) {
217					continue
218				}
219				description := config.Contract(wt.Path)
220				if wt.Main {
221					description += " (main checkout)"
222				}
223				out = addCompletion(out, wt.Branch, description, toComplete)
224			}
225			return out, noFileCompletion
226		}
227	}
228	
229	func completeHelpTopics(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
230		if len(args) > 0 {
231			return nil, noFileCompletion
232		}
233		topics, err := help.List()
234		if err != nil {
235			return nil, noFileCompletion
236		}
237		out := make([]string, 0, len(topics))
238		for _, topic := range topics {
239			out = addCompletion(out, topic.Name, topic.Summary, toComplete)
240		}
241		return out, noFileCompletion
242	}
243	
244	func completeGitignoreNames(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
245		used := make(map[string]bool, len(args))
246		for _, name := range args {
247			used[strings.ToLower(name)] = true
248		}
249		names := ignore.BundledNames()
250		out := make([]string, 0, len(names))
251		for _, name := range names {
252			value := strings.ToLower(name)
253			if !used[value] {
254				out = addCompletion(out, value, name+" bundled template", toComplete)
255			}
256		}
257		return out, noFileCompletion
258	}
259	
260	func fixedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
261		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
262			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
263			for _, value := range values {
264				out = addCompletion(out, value, "", toComplete)
265			}
266			return out, noFileCompletion
267		}
268	}
269	
270	func commaSeparatedCompletions(values ...string) cobra.CompletionFunc {
271		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
272			prefix, current := "", toComplete
273			if i := strings.LastIndexByte(toComplete, ','); i >= 0 {
274				prefix, current = toComplete[:i+1], toComplete[i+1:]
275			}
276			used := make(map[string]bool)
277			for _, value := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(prefix, ","), ",") {
278				used[value] = value != ""
279			}
280			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
281			for _, value := range values {
282				candidate := prefix + value
283				if !used[value] && strings.HasPrefix(value, current) {
284					out = append(out, candidate)
285				}
286			}
287			return out, noFileCompletion
288		}
289	}
290	
291	func runtimeCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
292		backends := runtime.All()
293		values := make([]string, 1, len(backends)+1)
294		values[0] = "auto"
295		for _, backend := range backends {
296			values = append(values, backend.Name())
297		}
298		return fixedCompletions(values...)
299	}
300	
301	func taskStateNames() []string {
302		values := make([]string, len(task.States))
303		for i, state := range task.States {
304			values[i] = string(state)
305		}
306		return values
307	}
308	
309	func taskStateCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
310		return fixedCompletions(taskStateNames()...)
311	}
312	
313	func taskStateSliceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
314		return commaSeparatedCompletions(taskStateNames()...)
315	}
316	
317	func statsSourceCompletions() cobra.CompletionFunc {
318		return commaSeparatedCompletions(
319			string(stats.SourceSession), string(stats.SourceGit), string(stats.SourceWakaTime),
320		)
321	}
322	
323	func registerFlagCompletion(cmd *cobra.Command, name string, fn cobra.CompletionFunc) {
324		if err := cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(name, fn); err != nil {
325			panic(err)
326		}
327	}
328	
329	func addCompletion(out []string, value, description, toComplete string) []string {
330		if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
331			return out
332		}
333		if description != "" {
334			description = completionDescriptionSanitizer.Replace(description)
335			value = cobra.CompletionWithDesc(value, description)
336		}
337		return append(out, value)
338	}
```

```text
18	const noFileCompletion = cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
19	
20	var completionDescriptionSanitizer = strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ")
21	
22	// completionInvocation reports commands that build or serve completion data.
23	// Neither path should run the normal eager App.Load: script generation needs no
24	// config, while __complete must wait until Cobra has parsed the target command's
25	// persistent flags (notably --config).
26	func completionInvocation(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
27		if cmd.Name() == cobra.ShellCompRequestCmd || cmd.CalledAs() == cobra.ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd {
28			return true
29		}
30		for cur := cmd; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {
31			if cur.Name() == "completion" {
32				return true
33			}
34		}
35		return false
36	}
37	
38	// loadCompletion prepares local providers after Cobra has parsed the command
39	// line. Invalid config should remove dynamic candidates, not break command and
40	// flag completion entirely. Cobra invokes one custom provider per request, so
41	// loading here avoids state leaking when a command tree is reused.
42	func (a *App) loadCompletion() bool { return a.Load() == nil }
43	
44	func completeTasks(app *App, states ...task.State) cobra.CompletionFunc {
45		allowed := make(map[task.State]bool, len(states))
46		for _, state := range states {
47			allowed[state] = true
48		}
49		return func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
50			if len(args) > 0 || !app.loadCompletion() {
51				return nil, noFileCompletion
52			}
53			tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
54			if err != nil {
55				return nil, noFileCompletion
56			}
57			out := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
58			for _, t := range tasks {
59				if !allowed[t.State] {
60					continue
61				}
62				value := t.ID
63				if toComplete != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(value, toComplete) {
64					for _, ref := range []string{t.Title(), t.Branch} {
65						if candidate, ok := taskCompletionRef(tasks, t, ref, toComplete); ok {
66							value = candidate
67							break
68						}
69					}
70				}
71				description := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s · %s · %s · %s", t.State, t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.ID)
72				out = addCompletion(out, value, description, toComplete)
73			}
74			return out, noFileCompletion
75		}
76	}
77	
78	func taskCompletionRef(all []*task.Task, target *task.Task, ref, typed string) (string, bool) {
79		if len(typed) > len(ref) || !strings.EqualFold(ref[:len(typed)], typed) {
80			return "", false
81		}
82		candidate := typed + ref[len(typed):]
83		var exact []*task.Task
84		for _, t := range all {
85			if t.ID == candidate || t.Branch == candidate {
86				exact = append(exact, t)
87			}
88		}
89		if len(exact) > 0 {
90			return candidate, len(exact) == 1 && exact[0].ID == target.ID
```
