1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123	
124		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
125		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
126	}
127	
128	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}
141	
142	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}

1	package task
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"io/fs"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"regexp"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	
14		"github.com/BurntSushi/toml"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}

35	  default        create a branch + linked worktree, provision it, open a

218	
219	// annotate pushes the task's state and next action into the runtime as
220	// display-only metadata, so a sidebar can show why a session is open without
221	// anyone having to ask dev.
222	//
223	// For herdr this lands as workspace metadata tokens. A token only renders if
224	// the sidebar row layout in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g.
225	//
226	//	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
227	//	rows = [["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"], ["branch", "git_status"], ["$next"]]
228	//
229	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds and shows nothing,
230	// which is why dev never treats a failure here as an error.
231	func annotate(app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, t *task.Task) {
232		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
233			return
234		}
235		kv := map[string]string{
236			"stage": t.State.Label(),
237			"next":  t.Next,
238		}
239		if err := rt.Annotate(ctxOf(), t.RuntimeHandle, kv); err != nil {
240			app.warnf("could not annotate the runtime session: %v", err)
241		}
242	}
243	
244	func reportProvision(app *App, res *wt.CreateResult) {
245		p := res.Provision
246		if n := len(p.Copied); n > 0 {
247			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   copied    %d gitignored file(s): %s\n", n, strings.Join(p.Copied, ", "))
248		}
249		if n := len(p.Linked); n > 0 {
250			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   linked    %s\n", strings.Join(p.Linked, ", "))
251		}
252		for _, e := range p.Failures {
253			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   warning   %v\n", e)
254		}
255	}

25	func newAdoptCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
26		var (
27			apply       bool
28			yes         bool
29			noWorktrees bool
30			noSessions  bool
31			noBranches  bool
32			state       string

34		cmd := &cobra.Command{
35			Use:   "adopt",
36			Short: "Import existing worktrees, sessions and branches as tasks",
37			Long: `Bring what is already on this machine under dev's inventory.
38	
39	There is nothing to migrate to start using dev — repositories are discovered
40	wherever your scan roots point, and no directory is moved or renamed. What is
41	worth importing is the work already in flight: linked worktrees created by
42	hand or by another tool, runtime sessions sitting in a repo, and local
43	branches that are ahead of their base.
44	
45	Reports by default. Nothing is created without --apply, and nothing on disk is
46	ever moved, renamed or deleted by this command.`,
47			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
48			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
49				ctx := ctxOf()
50	
51				target, err := task.ParseState(state)
52				if err != nil {
53					return err
54				}
55	
56				repos, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
57				if err != nil {
58					return err
59				}
60				existing, err := app.Tasks.List()
61				if err != nil {
62					return err
63				}
64				known := map[string]bool{}
65				for _, t := range existing {
66					known[t.ID] = true
67				}
68	
69				rt := app.Runtime()
70				var sessions []runtime.Session
71				if !noSessions {
72					sessions, _ = rt.List(ctx)
73				}
74

79					}

81						!noWorktrees, !noSessions, !noBranches)...)

87				}

89				sort.Slice(found, func(i, j int) bool {

91						return found[i].Task.Repo < found[j].Task.Repo
92					}
93					return found[i].Task.Branch < found[j].Task.Branch
94				})
95

97				t := NewTable("REPO", "BRANCH", "STATE", "WHY", "CHECKOUT")
98				for _, c := range found {

101				}

140	// scanRepo collects everything in one repository that looks like work in
141	// flight but is not yet recorded.
142	func scanRepo(ctx context.Context, app *App, r repo.Repo, sessions []runtime.Session,
143		known map[string]bool, target task.State, doWorktrees, doSessions, doBranches bool) []candidate {
144	
145		var out []candidate
146		seen := map[string]bool{}
147	
148		add := func(branch, worktree, reason string, state task.State) {
149			if branch == "" || seen[branch] {
150				return
151			}
152			id := task.MakeID(r.Name, branch)
153			if known[id] {
154				return
155			}
156			seen[branch] = true
157			out = append(out, candidate{
158				Reason: reason,
159				Task: &task.Task{
160					ID:           id,
161					Name:         branch,
162					Repo:         r.Name,
163					RepoPath:     r.Path,
164					Branch:       branch,
165					Base:         gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, r.Path),
166					WorktreePath: worktree,
167					State:        state,
168					Owner:        config.Hostname(),
169				},
170			})
171		}
172	
173		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path)
174		if err != nil {
175			return nil
176		}
177	
178		if doWorktrees {
179			for _, w := range worktrees {
180				if w.Main || w.Branch == "" || w.Prunable {
181					continue
182				}
183				// A harness's turn-scoped worktree is not a change stream a human
184				// tracks; adopting those would fill the inventory with noise that
185				// the harness will delete on its own.
186				if isEphemeralWorktree(w.Path, w.Branch) {
187					continue
188				}
189				state := target
190				reason := "existing worktree"
191				if sessionAt(sessions, w.Path) != nil {
192					state, reason = task.Hot, "worktree with a live session"
193				}
194				add(w.Branch, w.Path, reason, state)
195			}
196		}
197	
198		if doSessions {
199			for i := range sessions {
200				for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
201					if d != r.Path {
202						continue
203					}
204					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
205					if err != nil || st.Branch == "" {
206						continue
207					}
208					add(st.Branch, "", "live session in the main checkout", task.Hot)
209				}
210			}
211		}
212	
213		if doBranches {
214			for _, branch := range unmergedBranches(ctx, r.Path) {
215				add(branch, worktreePathFor(worktrees, branch), "branch ahead of the base", target)
216			}
217		}
218		return out
219	}
220	
221	// isEphemeralWorktree recognises the checkouts an agent harness creates and
222	// cleans up itself.
223	func isEphemeralWorktree(path, branch string) bool {
224		return strings.Contains(path, "/.claude/worktrees/") ||
225			strings.HasPrefix(branch, "worktree-")
226	}
227	
228	func sessionAt(sessions []runtime.Session, dir string) *runtime.Session {
229		for i := range sessions {
230			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
231				if d == dir {
232					return &sessions[i]
233				}
234			}
235		}
236		return nil
237	}
238	
239	func worktreePathFor(worktrees []gitx.Worktree, branch string) string {
240		for _, w := range worktrees {
241			if w.Branch == branch && !w.Main {
242				return w.Path
243			}
244		}
245		return ""
246	}
247	
248	// unmergedBranches lists local branches carrying commits the default branch
249	// does not — unfinished work that would otherwise be invisible to dev.
250	func unmergedBranches(ctx context.Context, repoPath string) []string {
251		base := gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
252		if base == "" {
253			return nil
254		}
255		out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname:short)", "refs/heads/")
256		if err != nil {
257			return nil
258		}
259		var branches []string
260		for _, b := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
261			b = strings.TrimSpace(b)
262			if b == "" || b == base || isEphemeralWorktree("", b) {
263				continue
264			}
265			// Contained in the base means the work has already landed.
266			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", b, base); err == nil {
267				continue
268			}
269			branches = append(branches, b)
270		}
271		return branches
272	}

Cobra v1.10.2 defines `NoSpace` specifically to suppress the shell’s usual post-completion space and implements it independently in all three generators: bash enables `compopt -o nospace`, zsh passes `_describe -S ''`, and fish applies its no-space workaround. Since the provider currently emits directive `4` (`NoFileComp`) rather than combined `6`, the report is not refuted by framework semantics; I’m now validating the project’s generated scripts and focused test output.

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-27 19:15:34Z)**_

Cobra v1.10.2 makes the protocol failure concrete: completion-with-description is `choice + "\t" + description`; `__completeNoDesc` discards everything after the first tab, and all completion output discards everything after the first newline before printing one record per line. A raw tab therefore reclassifies part of the title as description, while a newline truncates the candidate before any shell even parses it.

14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16	)
17	
18	// App is the state shared by every command.
19	type App struct {
20		Cfg   config.Config
21		Tasks *task.Store
22	
23		Out io.Writer
24		Err io.Writer
25	
26		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
27		configPath string
28		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
29		runtimeOverride string
30		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
31		noRuntime bool
32	}
33	
34	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
35	func (a *App) Load() error {
36		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
37		if err != nil {
38			return err
39		}
40		a.Cfg = cfg
41		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
42		if a.Out == nil {
43			a.Out = os.Stdout
44		}
45		if a.Err == nil {
46			a.Err = os.Stderr
47		}
48		return nil
49	}
50	
51	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
52	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
53	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
54		if a.noRuntime {
55			return runtime.None{}
56		}
57		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
58		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
59			backend = a.runtimeOverride
60		}
61		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
62		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
63			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
64		}
65		return rt
66	}
67	
68	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
69	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
70		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
71	}
72	
73	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
74	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
75		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
76	}
77	
78	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
79	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
80	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
81	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
82	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
83	// integrations.
84	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
85		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
86			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
87			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
88				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
89			}
90			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
91			if file == nil {
92				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
93			}
94			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
95				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
96			}
97			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
98				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
99			}
100			return nil
101		}
102		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
103		return err
104	}
105	
106	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
107	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
108

25			Use:   "try [name]",

27			Long: `Create (or jump to) a dated experiment directory under paths.tries_root.
28	
29	Experiments need a home that is neither /tmp (where they vanish) nor your
30	projects directory (where they accumulate as clutter you are afraid to delete).
31	A try is date-prefixed, disposable by default, and promotable with
32	"dev graduate" when it turns out to be real.
33	
34	  dev try                    list what is there
35	  dev try redis-streams      jump to a matching try, or create 2026-08-27-redis-streams

39				ctx := ctxOf()
40				root := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot)
41				if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o755); err != nil {
42					return err
43				}
44	
45				if list || (len(args) == 0 && clone == "") {
46					return listTries(app, root)
47				}
48	
49				name := ""
50				if len(args) == 1 {
51					name = args[0]
52				}
53				if clone != "" && name == "" {
54					name = repoNameFromRef(clone)
55				}
56				slug := config.Slug(strings.ReplaceAll(name, " ", "-"))
57	
58				// An existing try wins over creating a near-duplicate: the whole
59				// point is to stop accumulating test/test2/test-actually.
60				if match := findTry(root, slug); match != "" && clone == "" {
61					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(match))
62					return openOrCD(app, ctx, match, filepath.Base(match))
63				}
64	
65				dir := filepath.Join(root, time.Now().Format("2006-01-02")+"-"+slug)
66				if _, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil {
67					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(dir))
68					return openOrCD(app, ctx, dir, filepath.Base(dir))
69				}
70	
71				if clone != "" {
72					url := clone
73					if k := forge.FromURL(clone); k != forge.Unknown {
74						if f, err := forge.For(k); err == nil {

104	// tryEntry is one scratch directory with the facts needed to rank it.
105	type tryEntry struct {
106		name     string
107		path     string
108		modified time.Time
109		isRepo   bool
110		dirty    bool
111	}
112	
113	func listTries(app *App, root string) error {
114		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
115		if err != nil {
116			return err
117		}
118		var tries []tryEntry
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			if !e.IsDir() || strings.HasPrefix(e.Name(), ".") {
121				continue
122			}
123			info, err := e.Info()
124			if err != nil {
125				continue
126			}
127			path := filepath.Join(root, e.Name())
128			t := tryEntry{name: e.Name(), path: path, modified: info.ModTime()}
129			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
130				t.isRepo = true
131				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctxOf(), path); err == nil {
132					t.dirty = st.Dirty()
133				}
134			}
135			tries = append(tries, t)
136		}
137		if len(tries) == 0 {
138			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "No tries yet under %s\n", config.Contract(root))
139			return nil
140		}
141		// Most recently touched first: "what was I doing yesterday?" is the
142		// question a list of experiments actually gets asked.
143		sort.Slice(tries, func(i, j int) bool { return tries[i].modified.After(tries[j].modified) })
144	
145		tbl := NewTable("TRY", "AGE", "GIT")
146		for _, t := range tries {
147			gitCol := "—"
148			switch {
149			case t.isRepo && t.dirty:
150				gitCol = "repo ●"
151			case t.isRepo:
152				gitCol = "repo"
153			}
154			tbl.Add(truncate(t.name, 44), humanAge(time.Since(t.modified)), gitCol)
155		}
156		tbl.Render(app.Out)
157		fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\n%d tries under %s — promote one with `dev graduate <try>`\n",
158			len(tries), config.Contract(root))
159		return nil
160	}
161	
162	// findTry locates an existing try whose name contains the slug, preferring the
163	// most recent when several match.
164	func findTry(root, slug string) string {
165		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
166		if err != nil {
167			return ""
168		}
169		var best string
170		var bestTime time.Time
171		for _, e := range entries {
172			if !e.IsDir() || !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(e.Name()), strings.ToLower(slug)) {
173				continue
174			}
175			info, err := e.Info()
176			if err != nil {
177				continue
178			}
179			if info.ModTime().After(bestTime) {
180				best, bestTime = filepath.Join(root, e.Name()), info.ModTime()
181			}
182		}
183		return best
184	}
185	
186	func openOrCD(app *App, ctx context.Context, dir, label string) error {
187		rt := app.Runtime()
188		if rt.Name() == "none" {
189			return app.cdDirective(dir)
190		}
191		if _, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, dir, label); err != nil {
192			app.warnf("could not open a session: %v", err)
193		}
194		return nil
195	}

51				}
52				if name == "" {
53					name = datePrefix.ReplaceAllString(filepath.Base(src), "")
54				}
55				if name == "" {
56					return fmt.Errorf("could not derive a project name from %s — pass --name", src)
57				}
58	
59				dest := filepath.Join(config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot), category, name)
60				if _, err := os.Stat(dest); err == nil {
61					return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists", config.Contract(dest))
62				}
63	
64				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "graduate  %s\n", config.Contract(src))
65				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "       →  %s\n", config.Contract(dest))
66				if dryRun {
67					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\n(dry run — nothing moved)")
68					return nil
69				}
70	
71				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dest), 0o755); err != nil {
72					return err
73				}
74				// Rename first: it is atomic within a filesystem and leaves
75				// nothing half-copied if it fails.
76				if err := os.Rename(src, dest); err != nil {
77					return fmt.Errorf("move %s: %w\n"+
78						"If the projects root is on another filesystem, copy it by hand and remove the try",
79						config.Contract(src), err)
80				}
81	
82				if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dest, ".git")); err != nil {
83					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dest, "init", "-b", "main"); err != nil {
84						return err
85					}
86					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   git init")
87				}
88				// An experiment usually has files but no commit. A project needs
89				// one: without a HEAD there is no default branch, so `dev start`
90				// would have nothing to base a worktree on.
91				if made, err := ensureInitialCommit(ctx, dest, name); err != nil {
92					app.warnf("could not make an initial commit: %v", err)
93				} else if made {
94					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   committed the existing work")
95				}
96	
97				if remote {
98					f, err := forge.Preferred()
99					if err != nil {
100						app.warnf("%v — the project is in place; add a remote by hand", err)
101					} else {
102						url, err := f.CreateRepo(ctx, dest, forge.RepoRequest{
103							Name: name, Private: private, Push: push,
104						})
105						if err != nil {
106							app.warnf("could not create the remote: %v", err)
107						} else {
108							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   remote    %s\n", url)
109						}
110					}
111				}
112	
113				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%s is now a project. Start work on it with:\n  dev start %s --task <name>\n",
114					name, name)
115				return openOrCD(app, ctx, dest, name)
116			},
117		}
118		f := cmd.Flags()
119		f.StringVarP(&category, "category", "c", "", "category subdirectory under project_root")
120		f.StringVar(&name, "name", "", "project name (default: the try name without its date prefix)")
121		f.BoolVar(&private, "private", true, "create the remote as private")
122		f.BoolVar(&remote, "remote", false, "create a remote repository with gh or glab")
123		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", true, "push after creating the remote")
124		f.BoolVar(&dryRun, "dry-run", false, "show what would happen without moving anything")
125		return cmd
126	}
127	
128	// resolveTry finds the try directory to graduate: an explicit reference, or
129	// the try containing the current directory.
130	func resolveTry(app *App, triesRoot string, args []string) (string, error) {
131		if len(args) == 1 {
132			ref := args[0]
133			if abs := config.Expand(ref); isDir(abs) {
134				return abs, nil
135			}
136			direct := filepath.Join(triesRoot, ref)
137			if isDir(direct) {
138				return direct, nil
139			}
140			if match := findTry(triesRoot, ref); match != "" {
141				return match, nil
142			}
143			return "", fmt.Errorf("no try matching %q under %s", ref, config.Contract(triesRoot))
144		}
145	
146		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
147		if err != nil {
148			return "", err
149		}
150		if !strings.HasPrefix(cwd, triesRoot+string(filepath.Separator)) {
151			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s is not inside %s — name the try to graduate",
152				config.Contract(cwd), config.Contract(triesRoot))
153		}
154		// Walk up to the try's own top-level directory, so running this from a
155		// subdirectory still graduates the whole experiment.
156		rel, _ := filepath.Rel(triesRoot, cwd)
157		first := strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator))[0]
158		return filepath.Join(triesRoot, first), nil
159	}
160	
161	func isDir(p string) bool {
162		info, err := os.Stat(p)
163		return err == nil && info.IsDir()
164	}
165	
166	// ensureInitialCommit gives a repository a first commit if it has none,
167	// seeding a README when the tree is otherwise empty. Reports whether it made
168	// one.
169	func ensureInitialCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) (bool, error) {
170		if _, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, dir); err == nil {
171			return false, nil // already has history
172		}
173		if empty, err := isEmptyTree(dir); err != nil {
174			return false, err
175		} else if empty {
176			readme := filepath.Join(dir, "README.md")
177			if err := os.WriteFile(readme, []byte("# "+name+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
178				return false, err
179			}
180		}
181		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
182			return false, err
183		}
184		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "commit", "-m", "chore: graduate experiment into a project"); err != nil {
185			return false, err
186		}
187		return true, nil
188	}
189	
190	// isEmptyTree reports a directory with nothing in it but git's own metadata.
191	func isEmptyTree(dir string) (bool, error) {
192		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
193		if err != nil {
194			return false, err
195		}
196		for _, e := range entries {
197			if e.Name() != ".git" {
198				return false, nil
199			}
200		}
201		return true, nil
202	}
